244606.longDescription:
French restaurant "La Grande Table de KITAMURA" is located in Shirakabe, Nagoya, an area which retains the historic charm of the Meiji and Taisho periods.

Chef Ryuji Kitamura started his cooking career at age 16. He studied in France at grande Maisons such as "Charles Palier", "Jamin", and "Taillevent" for about 14 years before exercising his abilities as a sous-chef at Girardet in Switzerland for 10 years. When he returned to Japan, Kitamura worked in Nagoya as the head chef at Mikuni Nagoya for 3 years before opening "La Grande Table de KITAMURA" in 2014 as a fulfillment of his dream to create a restaurant that matches the townscape in Japan, which he had been pursuing since his days in Europe.

Kitamura bases his restaurant on the concept “the restaurant is a theater." The restaurant is designed around the chef’s desire for the guest to feel like they are a star achieving their long-awaited big moment, with a fashionably decorated interior that allows them to fully enjoy the restaurant’s atmosphere and their food.

The Omakase(chef’s choice) course is made with the best ingredients procured on that day and made to fit the situation and the guest’s tastes. Kitamura is determined to provide an original meal each time, focusing even on details like the source and style so that you encounter a once in a lifetime meal whenever you come. Just like the daily changing meals, the drink that comes with your meal is chosen mainly from a variety of French wine with the full intention of matching the guest.

The restaurant was renovated from an old residence and contains 40 table seats and a private room that holds 6 to 10 people. It’s suitable for all sorts of occasions, including a couple’s date night, a golden anniversary, receptions and casual meals, and even a girls’ night out. The staff provides service in French and English, so even guests from overseas can dine without concern. Come to this space that resembles a vibrant theater and enjoys the pearl of French cuisine that has the whole world talking.

244478.longDescription:
Inspired by the idea of offering customers an entire cut of Japanese eel to enjoy, "Unagi Yondaime Kikukawa" opened its doors in Nagoya in 2017. With a background in managing a long-standing wholesaler that has spent 90 years catering to countless eel specialty restaurants, it is no surprise that the ingredients are as good as it gets.

They developed their keen eye for top ingredients over many years and took that experience to run the restaurant "Tateba" as well for over 60 years. They built their very own 200-meter wall of water that keeps mud out from the well water to stave off odors and ensure that the eel is always at its best. As you would expect from a wholesaler that excels in top ingredients, they have no problem offering a whole entire of eel with the utmost quality. Typically eel is cut into smaller portions before its served, but here customers are treated to a full cut of eel to enjoy. The size of their eels is about 300g, which is substantially larger than what you would normally find at other establishments. The eel itself is particularly thick, so it doesn't shrink in size after the outside is grilled to perfection. They also use high-grade charcoal for high-intensity cooking that maintains its delicious fatty flavor as well. It's prepared right after a guest order it too, which means it comes out perfectly hot and fresh in no time at all.

The restaurant employs a talented lineup of chefs, including Chef Hideaki Chabata, who worked for close to 10 years as a head chef at a traditional Japanese restaurant in Nagoya. The restaurant relies on expert chefs to make sure their top grade eel is at its most delicious and flavorful. They cook their ell over a short span of time to lock in its savory umami flavor. This also gives the eel a nice level of crisp on the outside and a light texture on the inside. The fattiness of it is sheer perfection as well. They use Shigaraki-ware pottery from Shiga Prefecture to serve "Unaju," a broiled eel dish that is traditionally served over rice in a box. Guests can also enjoy charcoal-grilled eel fillets and simply cooked eel without any flavoring, or even a full-course meal with a variety of eel dishes. All together their wide-ranging menu offers guest a full selection of eel dishes to dine on. And within 10 seconds guests can enjoy a diverse selection of cuts, including the head, fins, near the gills, and raw hearts, a rare delicacy that you can only expect to find from a restaurant like this that has direct access to highly sought-after ingredients.

"Unagi Yondaime Kikukawa" interior features a calm and composed modern Japanese-style design. They have also a full selection of seating options to choose from, including seats at the counter, table seating, and a private dining room. Guests sitting at the counter can look over through the glass pane to see the chefs expertly prepare each eel, which is a true feast for the eyes. The private room offers guests a comfortable dining space to savor and enjoy each bit of eel. This dining space is also perfect for guests looking to have a more formal dining atmosphere for their meal. With all of that in mind, it is certainly safe to say that this highly reputable restaurant truly showcases the very best of Nagoya.

當然可以！以下為你的文章英文版翻譯，我保留了情緒張力、口語感與驚嘆氛圍：

⸻

“I Never Knew Eel Could Be THIS Good! This Full-Course Unagi Meal Blew My Mind”

I always thought I didn’t really care for eel. Growing up, the unagi I occasionally ate in bento shops was usually overly sweet with dry, flat texture. Eventually I convinced myself: “Yeah… eel is just okay.”

That was until I visited Nagoya with my colleagues and tried a full-course unagi meal at a famous specialty restaurant called Kikukawa 4th Generation. Only then did I realize what true unagi heaven tastes like. After finishing the meal, all I wanted to say was: How is eel THIS delicious!?

Here’s what the full-course included:

• Grilled Eel Liver Skewer
Total surprise! Slightly bitter, aromatic, and the texture sits somewhere between chicken liver and beef tongue. The more you chew, the more complex it becomes. Perfect with sake.

• Eel Bone Crackers
Crispy, savory, not fishy at all. Like a snack you can’t stop eating.

• Eel Liver Soup
Light yet deep in flavor. One sip and you can feel your stomach settling happily.

• Eel Tamagoyaki (Egg Roll)
This one lit up my eyes. Soft, silky egg with tiny pieces of eel hidden inside. The egg’s gentle sweetness hits first, followed by the slow bloom of eel umami. A delicate and beautiful surprise.

• Eel Spring Roll
The wrapper was fried thin and crisp, with steaming kabayaki eel and veggies inside. First crunch, then tenderness, followed by a burst of smoky eel aroma—straight up heavenly. If white-grilled eel is the king, then this spring roll is that party guest who steals the spotlight.

• White-Grilled Eel (Shirayaki)
No sauce, just fire and skill. Crispy skin, whispering oil aromas, and soft, melt-in-your-mouth texture. Absolutely divine.

• Grilled Eel Head
Shocking good! Crispy exterior, rich collagen inside. Slightly sticky texture like a hybrid of beef tendon and roasted chicken skin. For true connoisseurs.

• Grilled Eel Belly
The fattiest cut—basically nature’s foie gras. Melts instantly, exploding with flavor. I almost stood up and applauded.

• Grilled Eel Back
Firm and bouncy texture, a perfect contrast to the belly. The more you chew, the more fragrant it becomes.

• Unagi Rice (Hitsumabushi Three Ways)
Classic kabayaki on steaming rice. The salty-sweet sauce was perfectly balanced, making even the rice taste precious. I scraped the bowl clean. A flawless finale to an eel feast.

By the end, I was genuinely on my knees. I now feel the need to formally apologize to eel for underestimating it all these years. That rich oil paired with delicate meat is basically the seafood equivalent of a dreamy lover—you think you won’t fall, but once you try it, you’re doomed.

I learned something important that day:
Good eel DOES exist—you just haven’t met the right restaurant yet.

If you’ve ever felt indifferent toward eel, please, give yourself a chance to try a thoughtfully prepared full-course unagi meal. I guarantee you’ll be screaming internally like I did:

“HOW CAN THIS BE SO GOOD “

244351.longDescription:
Despite being one of Nagoya foremost office quarters, Izumi area is also full of temples and has a somehow relaxing atmosphere. In this popular high-class residential district where high-quality people gather, this Italian restaurant "BOTTEGON" is earning a reputation with numerous gourmets.

The owner-chef Taro Yamaguchi worked in the service departments of the 5-star foreign-owned hotel “Issare Shu” (Nagoya) and “Enoteca Pinchiorri Nagoya” before starting his own restaurant “BOTTEGON” in October 2012. Although the restaurant provides first-class service, it is also designed to let customers relax and enjoy themselves. 

The menu is centered around seafood dishes made with ingredients sourced from Tsukiji market and Nagoya’s Yanagibashi Market. The pasta with homemade Karasumi (dried mullet roe
) is especially popular. And since the Chef is from Shiga Prefecture, he also sometimes uses Omi Wagyu Beef in his main dishes, preparing this select ingredient in his unique style. He also selects wine, centering on Italian Percarlo (San Giusto a Rentennano) and also incorporating fine French and Californian wine. The atmosphere is authentic, relaxed space designed around the theme of “The good old days of Italy.”

There are 28 table seats, 4 counter seats, and one private room (up to 8 persons), making the space accessible to all guests including singles, couples, business groups, and families. With its good reputation for friendly service, this Italian restaurant is one that should be on your radar when looking for a restaurant in Nagoya.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Takaoka Station (Nagoya Municipal Subway, Sakura-dōri Line)

244719.longDescription:
“Sushimichi Sakurada” is located 7-minute’s walk from Hisayaodori Subway Station in Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, a little off the main street. The owner Yuto Ohta serves Nagoya-style sushi with love for all local the ingredients used.

Owner-chef Ohta is from Aichi Prefecture. He set his sights on becoming a sushi chef early on, and after graduating from high school, he trained at famous restaurants such as “Ginza Kyubei” and “Sushi Tokami”. He then returned to Nagoya and opened his own restaurant, “Sushimichi Sakurada” in March 2019.

Ohta-san’s nigiri is Nagoyamae-style sushi that uses plenty of local ingredients while preserving the tradition of Edomae-style sushi that he acquired during his training. Seafood is carefully selected not only from the local area but also from the markets of Toyosu, Fukuoka, Kanazawa and other places in Japan. The tuna is from the specialty wholesaler "Yamayuki" whom he has had a connection with since his training period in “Sushi Tokami”. A unique blend of 3 types of red vinegar from Aichi, Gifu and Mie are used. The rice is from Toyohashi, Aichi Prefecture. The wasabi is from Ogaki City, Gifu Prefecture. The spring water from where the wasabi is grown is used to cook rice and tea. Nori seaweed is specially ordered from Ariake, Kumamoto. It is twice as thick as normal seaweed and is a rare item that is only sold by 3 stores in the world. Nagoya Cochin brand eggs are used for the final tamagoyaki. Careful attention is paid to each ingredient in every detail.

The recommended alcohol is the wine selected by Ohta-san, who is also a sommelier, and there are over 80 kinds of wine from all over the world, including French, Italian, Japanese and New World wines. They also have around 10 types of by-the-glass options, so you can enjoy various wines depending on the dish. There are always around 40 kinds of sake from all over Japan available at the restaurant.

The cypress counter (9 seats), inherited from “Sushi Yoshino”, is an eye-catching piece. We hope you will enjoy the lively feel of Ohta-san’s Nagoyamae-style sushi, starting with the "Shari-giri" (rice mixing), for dinner parties with your family or colleagues, for gatherings with your sushi-loving friends, and for entertaining overseas guests.
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Hisayaodori Station (Nagoya City Subway Meijo Line or Sakuradori Line)

245543.longDescription:
About 10 minutes’ drive from Nagoya Station, sushi ISM is nestled in a quiet residential area. The restaurant is supervised by Chef Isshin Sumoto from a popular, hard-to-book restaurant, Tout La Joie Ism, in Nagoya, with inspiration drawn from his hometown of Amakusa City, Kumamoto Prefecture. In the stylish open kitchen of sushi ISM, Chef Seiji Takahashi makes authentic sushi with traditional techniques and high-quality ingredients, some delivered from Amakusa and some locally sourced from Mikawa, Aichi. The young Takahashi started his culinary career at a nation-wide Edomae sushi restaurant chain. He honed his sushi-making skills and worked as managers at various sushi restaurants, including Sushi Kenzan in Nagoya. On one occasion, he met Chef Sumoto, who was impressed by his nigiri sushi, and they together opened sushi ISM in May 2023. Since then, Chef Takahashi and his wife  have worked hand-in-hand for the sushi restaurant.

Chef Takahashi sticks to authentic Edomae sushi without modifications. The sushi toppings are prepared in the most appropriate way depending on their condition and maturity. The ingredients are mostly sourced from Amakusa in Kumamoto and Mikawa in Aichi, taking full advantage of these two maritime regions, though tuna is purchased from Yamayuki, a popular tuna wholesaler, at Toyosu Market. The sushi rice is made from Koshihikari rice cooked slightly hard and seasoned with a blend of red and rice vinegar to add a depth to the acidity and highlight the flavors of popular sushi toppings, such as red sea urchin and longtooth grouper from Amakusa. The sake list offers about 10 labels, mainly from the three Tokai prefectures (Aichi, Gifu, and Mie), including Tabika from Mie, but also from around Japan. The original sweet potato shochu “ISM” (Amakusa Shuzo) and the Champagne Collet are also popular, matched with the sushi.

The interior is adorned with dynamic, eye-catching floor-to ceiling tapestries depicting the sea of Amakusa. The J-shaped counter (seating up to eight guests) inspired by a fishing hook and other interior designs are also as reminiscent of the sea of Amakusa as the food and sake.
Perfect for various occasions, from private to business, sushi ISM invites guests to indulge in authentic Edomae sushi and enjoy Amakusa’s seasonal vibes while staying in Nagoya.
nearestStations: 20 minutes on foot or 10 minutes by taxi from the north exit of Kanayama Station

245571.longDescription:
Perched on the 42nd floor of Midland Square in front of Nagoya Station, ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya not only offers breathtaking views but also brings an exceptional selection of wines curated by the master wine sommelier and innovative recipes created by the renowned Italian chef from the main location in Florence to Nagoya. ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya was the only restaurant in Japan to be selected for the internationally renowned Italian dining ranking “50 TOP ITALY 2026,” announced on December 15, 2025. Celebrated for its refined and expressive cuisine—rooted in a profound respect for Italian culinary traditions and elevated by a distinctly Japanese aesthetic—the restaurant is equally admired for its sweeping views and sincere, attentive service. Together, these elements have established ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya as a destination recognized and respected on the global gastronomic stage.

ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya is helmed by Executive Chef and Pastry Chef Kohei Shima, who learned the art of traditional Italian pastries and fermented pastries in Italy. After returning to Japan, he worked as a dessert chef at ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Tokyo and became the pastry chef of ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya when it opened its doors in 2007. Then, he went back to Italy to work as Second Pastry Chef at ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Florence, which received three stars from a world gourmet guide. He also learned the cutting-edge art of Spanish desserts at El Bulli and other renowned restaurants before returning to Japan to take the current position. In the meantime, he won the traditional category at the Japan competition for the international contest of the world’s best panettone (traditional Italian Christmas bread) and competed as a representative of Japan in the world contest. Meanwhile, Head Chef Naoyuki Toda, another prize winner, joined ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya after working as Second Chef at a restaurant in Piedmont, Italy. He also gained a sommelier certification from the Japan Sommelier Association and then climbed the career ladder from Pasta and Meat Section Staff to Second Chef to Head Chef in 2022. Moreover, he won the Grand Prize at the 3rd Mancini Pasta Contest in 2025. With support from these talented chefs, ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya continues its culinary journey.

The menu features seasonal Japanese ingredients while honoring Italian culinary traditions. The Genji Wagyu beef is sourced from Aichi, and the scallops, squid, and other seafood from Aomori. Moreover, traditional Italian ingredients, such as artichoke and Porcini mushroom, are imported from Italy. The Bombolone made with Nagoya Cochin eggs and filled with light potato mousse is a popular appetizer on the prix-fixe menu. Another popular item featuring seasonal ingredients is the Lumache Rigate Pasta with Zucchini Flower and Pistachio Pesto Topped with Mikawa Isshiki Eel Ragù in Bolognese Style, which made Chef Toda win the prize. With a spacious, open dining room with 14 tables and a private dining room (seating up to 14 guests), the restaurant caters to various occasions, from private to business settings. Enjoy the sophisticated dishes, a sommelier-curated selection of fine wines, and amazing views of Nagoya at ENOTECA PINCHIORRI Nagoya.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from the Sakura-dori Exit of JR Nagoya Station.

245010.longDescription:
Opened in 2016 and specializing in Nagoya’s regional dish of Hitsumabushi – unagi (freshwater eel) grilled over Bincho coals – this cozy restaurant is located on the third floor of the Dai Nagoya building with direct access from Nagoya Station. 

One of Nagoya’s specialties beloved by both locals and visitors, Hitsumabushi is made with fatty unagi, grilled slowly over the indirect high heat of Bincho charcoal until crisp on the outside and tender throughout. The dish is served with freshly cooked rice and a dipping sauce prepared by blending tamari soy sauce and mirin from Aichi. In particular, Hitsumabushi is characterized by how it is eaten, as a multi-course meal that allows guests to enjoy the dish unadorned and with a variety of condiments, before being experienced as a light risotto-like dish with the addition of a flavorsome broth. Thus, guests can enjoy three different flavors of the star ingredient in a single dish.

Hitsumabushi Nagoya Bincho also offers a wide selection of alcoholic and soft drinks for diners to enjoy with their meal. The sake list includes Kamoshibito Kuheiji and Gikyo from Aichi; Hyakujuro Akazura and Hyakujuro Kurozura from Gifu; Chikuha Noto Junmai from Ishikawa; Sawaya Matsumoto from Kyoto; and Suzune from Miyagi, all served by the glass, carafe, or bottle. Several shochus are offered by the glass, including Sato (Kuro) from Kagoshima as well as sweet potato, barley, and rice shochus. Moreover, the drink menu includes carefully curated alcoholic drinks, such as Shirohonoka Beer, Dewar’s Highball, and Taittinger, as well as soft drinks, such as Gerolsteiner sparkling mineral water and grated apple juice.

The restaurant’s interior boasts a luxurious Japanese design with warm wood accents and large windows that offer a sense of space and a spectacular view of the vibrant streets around Nagoya Station. With private rooms, this restaurant is perfect for a variety of occasions, both leisure or business related. 

Hitsumabushi Nagoya Bincho invites guests to savor Nagoya’s specialty cuisine with family, partner, friends, colleagues or clients in the comfortable environs of the Dai Nagoya Building with convenient, direct access from Nagoya Station.

"Sushi Hanakuruma" is located on the first basement floor of a building on Sakura-dori in front of Nagoya Station. It is a sushi restaurant produced by the famous Ginza restaurant "Sushi ARAI".

Yuichi Arai, is a talented sushi chef who trained at renowned restaurants, Ginza Kyubey and Sushisho in Yotsuya, for 10 and six years, respectively, before he opened his own restaurant, Sushi Arai, at the age of 33. His amazing Edomae sushi (Tokyo-style sushi) skills and hospitality give his restaurant exceptional popularity and a strong presence in Ginza filled with renowned sushi restaurants.
The chef of this famous sushi restaurant in Ginza selected Nagoya for his next sushi restaurant project. He entrusted the new restaurant to Chef Hiroyoshi Yokota, who offers sophisticated sushi to establish it as a new genre in the restaurant scene of Nagoya. The ingredients of sushi and delicacies are locally sourced from the rich waters of Ise and Mikawa bays and lavishly used to create unique flavors for the guests of Sushi Hanakuruma.
The drink menu boasts a wide range of local sakes and wines to meet the preferences of different guests.
Sushi Hanakuruma only has eight counter seats in the luxury dining room with plain wood accents. The dishware and interior designs are also carefully selected to suit the prestigious dining experience. Together, they make the restaurant a perfect place to enjoy the exquisite dishes and hospitality supervised by a renowned chef with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues.

245374.longDescription:
Presented as the ideal yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant by Satoru Tanaka, the owner of Nikuya Tanaka, a prestigious meat kappo (cuisine) restaurant in Ginza, TANAKA YAKINIKU RESTAURANTE opened its doors on the 1st basement (B1) floor of a building on Sakura-dori Street extending from Nagoya Station.

Tanaka learned to cut meat at his father’s butcher’s shop at around 10 years old. He realized his dream of running a meat restaurant as he opened his own restaurant featuring meat dishes at the age of 25. This restaurant, Nikuya Setsugekka Nagoya, immediately gained popularity for his creative dishes and interior design and garnered acclaim in an internationally known restaurant guide. This success was followed by 18 more restaurants across Japan, including in Tokyo, Nagoya, Gifu, and Shiga.

Tanaka invested his entire career in yakiniku cuisine. Having opened in October 2022, TANAKA YAKINIKU RESTAURANTE is a yakiniku restaurant that compiles all the experience and knowledge of Tanaka, also known as Meat Expert Boss, to offer his ideal yakiniku cuisine.

As implied by its name, TANAKA YAKINIKU RESTAURANTE offers prix fixe (fixed price) meals starting with appetizers and ending with desserts. The yakiniku dishes are made with the best beef of the day selected from premium beef, such as Matsuzaka, Kobe, and Omi Beef, by Satoru Tanaka, the meat expert who knows meat like the back of his hand, and grilled to the doneness of each guest’s choice. Guests can also enjoy wine elegantly served by the sommelier from the cellar,  which always contains about ten bottles.

The interior designed by Yasumichi Morita, an interior designer from GLAMOROUS, who also helped Tanaka design the interior of Nikuya Tanaka in Ginza, is stylish and modern with artistic inspirations from the world of Setsugekka (beauty of the four seasons). With nine private dining rooms (each seating two to six guests) and counter seats, TANAKA YAKINIKU RESTAURANTE can be used to celebrate various occasions with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues. Please enjoy the artistic designs and the yakiniku dishes that can shatter your idea of what yakiniku is.
nearestStations: Nagoya Station, 2 min. walk from Exit 5

244477.longDescription:
The restaurant got its start as a new business venture in 2018 by a long-standing wholesaler that provides eel, freshwater fish, wild game and other high-end ingredients to popular restaurants, including "Unagi Yondaime Kikukawa" in Nagoya. And so, "Yanagibashi Yakiniku Waniku," which serves Japanese-style meat dishes, was born out of a collaboration between fine quality meat ingredients and a chef who originally came from the world of traditional Japanese dining.

"Yakiniku Waniku" prides itself on seeking out the very best ingredients that distributors and wholesalers can confidently stand behind. This includes Japanese Black wagyu beef and other impeccable ingredients that have been selectively chosen from places like Kawagishi Farm, which is a well-known source of top quality Kobe beef. The skilled head chef behind the restaurant is Chef Yasuyuki Sato, who spent 8 years in Nagoya developing his skills in traditional Japanese dining before moving on to serve as an executive chef for a hotel. As a chef, he pushes forward to break new ground in meat-based cuisine by taking advantage of classic Japanese-style cooking methods that make the most out of each ingredient's inherent flavor. This way diners can taste each dish's ingredients when they are at their most flavorful.  The menu here focuses on offering yakiniku and meat dishes that are simple, yet expertly prepared. This includes their "Sirloin Shabu-Shabu" with specially prepared Japanese dashi, as well as dishes like their "Yukhoe," which only uses meat that has met the strict safety standards of Kobe's food safety protocols for handling raw ingredients. Their dishware includes elegant "Arita aware," a style of Japanese porcelain that brings an extra level of gorgeous presentation to each meal. And when it comes to dishes that fall outside of their yakiniku-style offerings, they ensure that everything is prepared with the same methods that they employ for meat dishes, which focus on simple, delicious flavors. This includes seasonal side dishes and fresh veggie salads, as well as small rice dishes and shaved ice to complete the meal. 

The sommelier carefully selects wines to complement delicate Japanese cuisine and meat. The restaurant offers 40 kinds of wines by the bottle and one by the glass. The interior of the restaurant has a modern atmosphere based on black and wood grain. In addition to table seating, four private rooms (for up to 18 persons) are available. A mature space where you can enjoy Japanese cuisine and yakiniku in a relaxed atmosphere awaits you.
※Please contact Pocket Concierge for group reservations.

244999.longDescription:
Hitsumabushi Nagoya Bincho Lachic Location first opened its doors in 2005 on the seventh floor of the upscale Lachic center annexed to Nagoya Sakae Mitsukoshi, and conveniently located near Sakae Subway Station. It is a popular restaurant frequented by shoppers and restaurant goers at lunch and dinner time.

As indicated by its name, this location of the popular Hitsumabushi Nagoya Bincho family is devoted to Hitsumabushi, Nagoya’s specialty cuisine that highlights local grilled unagi (freshwater eels). It is made with carefully selected unagi, grilled to perfection over the indirect high heat of Bincho charcoal. Following the traditional Nagoya cooking style, the unagi is cooked until it is crisp and flavorful on the outside and tender on the inside. The unagi is then dipped in a sauce prepared by blending tamari soy sauce and mirin from Aichi and served with freshly cooked rice. According to the chef, the unagi is cooked differently each day to bring out the best flavor of the morning’s catch, requiring mastery in Bincho charcoal grilling and unagi cuisine.

Hitsumabushi goes very well with sake, so the restaurant offers a wide variety of the beverage to meet the demands of different customers, including Kamoshibito Kuheiji Junmai Daiginjo Human, Gikyo, and Chochin from Aichi; Hyakujuro Kurozura from Gifu; Sawaya Matsumoto from Kyoto, all served by the glass, square cup, or bottle.

The dining room, seating up to 50 guests, boasts large windows that offer plenty of natural light and a sense of space. 

Guests are invited to enjoy outstanding Hitsumabushi along with warm hospitality at Hitsumabushi Nagoya Bincho Lachic Location for a variety of occasions such as intimate meals with family, friends or colleagues, as well as occasions such as dates, anniversaries, or meals with fellow gourmets.

244526.longDescription:
At the defining shopping center of Nagoya - Sakae - is a restaurant with a calm atmosphere located just adjacent to Shirakawa Park: "La Floraison de TAKEUCHI". The owner-chef, Masaki Takeuchi began his career at "La Pyramide" in French Vienne. Upon returning to Japan he worked at "Taillevent Robuchon" in Ebisu, Tokyo and at "Mikuni Nagoya" at the Nagoya Marriott Associa Hotel. In 2007 he became the head chef at "Grand-Famille Chez Matsuo" of Nagoya. He opened his own restaurant - "La Floraison de TAKEUCHI" - 5 years later, in 2013.

Seeking a halfway point between the casual nature of a bistro and the formality of a grand maison, by combining high quality and reasonable prices, the restaurant was immediately recognized as a small spot that even gourmets can enjoy. In 2019, the restaurant was awarded one star in the Aichi, Gifu, and Mie editions of the worldwide gourmet guide and has been listed in the prestigious French guidebook for five consecutive years. The food is based on classic French techniques while focusing on ingredients to make simple, modern cuisine that is good for the body. Similarly, the restaurant name "La Floraison" refers to the blooming period for flowers in French - and from the specialty appetizers made from edible flowers and organic herbs, everything down to the appearance has a showy quality that will delight all the senses.

Chef Takeuchi is also a recognized sommelier by the Japan Sommelier Association (JSA) and works with his sommelier to carefully maintain a selection of roughly 450 French wine. With an excellent balance of wine from major production regions such as Domaine and Chateaux, the lineup is sure to please wine aficionados. Chef Takeuchi also has a wine pairing course available.

The interior of "La Floraison de TAKEUCHI" has a modern feel, designed with brown, black, and white as the principal colors. There are 6 seats available at the open kitchen counter resulting from the chef's custom kitchen island, as well as-as 14 table seats and a half-size private room suitable for 6-8 guests. The atmosphere makes it a great place to enjoy a "live feeling" with lovers or friends, receptions, or special days with family - any occasion is welcome. Come to enjoy the one-of-a-kind year-round "bloom season" provided at "TAKEUCHI."

244768.longDescription:
A six-minute walk from Sakae Station in Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture, Setsugetsuka Tanakasatori is located on the top floor of a building in a busy neighborhood, close to downtown areas such as Sumiyoshi and Nishiki. The owner Satoru Tanaka bids the best meat for this yakiniku restaurant, that only serves the best Wagyu beef in Japan.

Owner Tanaka, who was born and raised in a family that run a butcher's shop, has had many opportunities to get in touch with meat since he was a child, and has been cutting meat since he was 10 with a kitchen. He opened his own yakiniku restaurant at the young age of 25. His unique menu and stylish store design attracted attention and he now has 18 stores in Tokyo, Nagoya, Gifu and Shiga. Setsugetsuka Tanakasatori opened in November, 2019. It is on the top floor of a building with many restaurants, and is popular as a high-grade yakiniku restaurant.

Setsugetsuka Tanakasatori uses only the innards and outside skirt of rare beef brand, such as Specialty Matsuzaka Beef and Excellent prize Kobe beef, which are auctioned off by owner Tanaka who knows meat well. As a yakiniku restaurant, they only serve the best ingredients in Japan. He has also selected gas roasters as the heat source from his experience of operating over 10 yakiniku restaurants over 25 years. The best yakiniku is served with famous French wine and hard-to-find California wine carefully selected by sommelier Takatoshi Saito. Based on the guest's preference, the restaurant would suggest the best marriage with the carefully selected yakiniku of Setsugetsuka Tanakasatori.

The interior was designed by Yasumichi Morita, a designer from "GLAMOROUS", who works on interior design in Japan and overseas. A stylish and dignified adult space with a base of marble and plain wood that exceeds the image of a yakiniku restaurant. There are only private rooms (4-8 people), which is luxurious. Although it is located on the top floor of the building, it has a completely private space that shuts out the outside view, and is recommended for private use such as family, friends, and dates. Enjoy the best Japanese beef yakiniku in a different space.

244998.longDescription:
A five-minute drive from Kashiwamori Station on the Meitetsu Inuyama Line brings guests to Hitsumabushi Bincho’s flagship restaurant in Niwa District, Aichi Prefecture. The restaurant is renowned throughout Japan for specializing in Hitsumabushi, Nagoya’s specialty cuisine featuring grilled unagi (freshwater eel), beloved by locals since it first opened its doors in 1994.

Unagi has been appreciated for its high nutritional value since ancient times, though its cooking and presentation have evolved differently in Japan’s various regions. For example, in Kanto, it is cut open along the back and then grilled and steamed, whereas it is cut open along the belly and simply grilled in Kansai. Moreover, unagi is served with rice in a ceramic bowl, a lacquerware box, or a tub, depending on the region.

At Hitsumabushi Bincho Main Location, unagi is cooked in Nagoya’s authentic Hitsumabushi style, grilled over Bincho charcoal, with carefully selected fatty unagi favored. It is not steamed but grilled over indirect high heat until crispy on the outside and tender on the inside; pieces are then dipped in a sauce prepared by blending locally produced tamari soy sauce and mirin according to the restaurant’s secret recipe. The savory, delicious unagi hot off the grill is served with freshly cooked rice, which brings out the essence of the fish.

The drinks menu offers a wide selection of alcoholic and soft drinks, including sake such as Kamotsuru from Hiroshima and Nishinoseki from Oita.

The dining room is elegant, with superb views of the adjacent Japanese garden. In particular, the garden lights up at night, offering a dreamy, relaxing atmosphere. The space offers 48 table seats and 24 tatami floor seats.

Guests are invited to enjoy Nagoya’s specialty cuisine at Hitsumabushi Bincho Main Location for a variety of occasions such as intimate meals with family, friends, colleagues, and anniversaries.

244552.longDescription:
"a.ligne" sits in a quiet spot one street back from the main road, 5-minute walk from Shinsakaemachi Station in Nagoya. The restaurant’s name, "a.ligne" means “to stand in a line” in French. It was chosen in the desire to have lots of patrons visiting and with the meaning of connecting the chef, the customers, and the producers through a line.

The restaurant owner,-chef, Akihiro Takamatsu, trained for 6 years in a French restaurant and a traditional Japanese restaurant in Kyoto before heading to France in 2007. After working in a restaurant in Toulouse for 18 months, he returned to Japan, where he worked for three and a half years as a pastry chef in Méchant Loup (now closed) and also as sous-chef at "L'EMBELLIR Naoto Kishimoto (now closed), both located in Kyoto. In 2018, the time was ripe for him to open his own place, a.ligne.

The food served at "a.ligne" is modern and natural.  
Vegetables are delivered from all over the country, mainly native and fixed species, completely pesticide-free, and are incorporated throughout the course with an emphasis on the original flavours of the vegetables.
Another distinctive feature is the company’s own farm in Toyota, "a.ligne" Farm, where it grows mainly native and pure-bred varieties of vegetables without the use of agrochemicals. It incorporates these vegetables throughout the courses served at the restaurant, placing importance on their intrinsic flavor. With dishes such as one of the house specialties, baby tilefish with Kyoto leeks, a.ligne surprises customers with its combination of many different ingredients, playing with a variety of textures, looks, and colors that can be enjoyed with all the five senses. As Chef Takamatsu explains, “Serving delicious food is a given. We also think that it’s important to use ingredients with care, making sure there is no waste. We also want our customers to enjoy the harmony between the tableware and the colors in our food.”  a.ligne stocks over 100 varieties of bottled wine that have been selected by a sommelier to go with the food and also offers a wine pairing course where participants can enjoy the exquisite marriage of wine and food. 

The restaurant interior is designed in simple, natural colors, unified with Chef Takamatsu’s favorite colors of white, grey, dark blue, and wooden tones to create a space that feels wonderfully spacious and fuss-free. Seating is in the main dining area together with a private room with a capacity of six. a.ligne is a popular spot for dinner dates, business entertainment, and also wine get-togethers attended by wine lovers. We invite you to take your time to enjoy the a.ligne approach, a work of art created with great care by Chef Takamatsu that brings together not only the menu and the particular vegetables but also the restaurant’s ambiance and the service.

244767.longDescription:
Modern French restaurant "Reminisce" is located in a quiet residential area near "Kurumamichi " station on the Sakuradori subway line. Chef Masaki Kuzuhara serves storybook French cuisine based on the theme of "Lingering Memories". He has received two stars in the International Gourmet Guide book. Kuzuhara, who was born in Nagoya, studied under Shuzo Kishida, the owner of the three-star Grand Maison "Quintessence" in Shinagawa, Tokyo, from 2008, and then under Chef Hajime "Hajime", the three-star chef in Higobashi, Osaka, from 2013. In 2015, he opened his own restaurant "Reminiscence" in Sakae, Nagoya, and in 2023, he moved to his current location.

The theme of "afterglow and memory" was decided when chef Kuzuhara was shocked by "food with a tremendous aftertaste" in Quintessence, and the name of the restaurant also has the meaning of "recall memories not immediately but over time". Ingredients mainly come from four prefectures in the Tokai region: Aichi, Gifu, Mie and Shizuoka. In addition, making use of the skills he learned how to treat eels in Atsuta Horaiken Main Store in Nagoya, known as a long-established restaurant of "Hitsumabushi”, before its opening, he is particular about eels that can only be found in Nagoya, and eel dishes that are served throughout the year in different production areas is a specialty of Reminiscence. The bread was specially ordered from Train Bleu in Gifu. There are around 1000 types of wine mainly from Bourgogne, France, and wine pairing includes wine selected from all over the world.

The interior of the restaurant has a soft yet dignified atmosphere reminiscent of a snow-covered mound, with private rooms that can accommodate up to 10 people. The chairs, tables, and other furniture are specially ordered from Kitani in Hida, Hokkaido, so that customers can enjoy the craftsmanship of the Tokai region. The tableware was also specially ordered from Saga, Tomiyama, and other regions, with a total of about 70 different types. We would like visitors to experience the course of "Reminiscence" expressed by Chef Kuzuhara's rich sensitivity, starting from the first chapter, in various situations. English menus are also available, which will be appreciated by overseas guests.
nearestStations: Underground Sakuradori Line Kurumamichi station, 4-minute walk from Exit 2.

245316.longDescription:
An eight-minute taxi drive from JR Akita Station, Akita Sushisho, sitting in front of Akita City Red Brick Folk Museum, is helmed by Chef Akihito Sasaki, who returned to his hometown to give scope to his ability.

As implied by the restaurant’s name, Chef Sasaki trained at a renowned sushi restaurant, Sushisho, in Yotsuya. He is one of the few apprentices initiated into all the mysteries of Edomae-style sushi-making, including pickling, marinating, and simmering, and granted the franchise to open his own restaurant. He returned to his hometown of Akita to open Akita Sushisho in 2001. It soon gained popularity, attracting sushi lovers not only from within the city but also from across the prefecture and even further afield.
The first course is a piece of nigiri sushi as a welcome. It is followed by a dozen delicacies and a dozen pieces of nigiri sushi. Like Sushisho, the sushi rice is prepared with different kinds of vinegar depending on the topping: red vinegar is used for tuna and urchin, and rice vinegar for white-meat fish. However, the Edomae sushi of Sushisho is reinterpreted by Chef Sasaki in his own unique way and transformed into “Akitamae” sushi that features the seasonal bounties of the sea and mountains, such as soy sauce, miso, and salt locally produced in Akita and fish and shellfish sourced from reliable fishmongers in Akita (except for tuna, which is supplied through Yamayuki, a popular broker, from Toyosu Market).
The vegetable roll sushi featuring the culinary delights of the land is popular among patrons. The signature menu of Sushisho, Ohagi, is also available at Akita Sushisho though it is reinterpreted by mixing chopped iburigakko (smoked radish pickles) into minced tuna scrape instead of yellow radish pickles. The sake list including Ecru, a special limited label brewed by a renowned local sake brewery, Aramasa, implies that Akita Sushisho is the leading sushi restaurant in Akita.

Sushi is served on Akita’s traditional plates, such as Shiraiwa ware and Kawatsura lacquerware, on the clean, plain wood counter (seating up to nine guests). Please enjoy the Akitamae sushi and friendly conversation with Chef Sasaki at Akita Sushisho when you visit Akita with your friends, family, or partner.

245302.longDescription:
In Hirosaki City in the center of the Tsugaru region in Aomori Prefecture in northeastern Japan, Osteria Enoteca da Sasino is perched on the second floor of a building a 10-minute drive from JR Hirosaki Station, the gateway of the provincial city with a distant view of Mt. Iwaki to the northwest, which is also known as Tsugaru Fuji for its beautiful shape. An elegant iron gate with lion motifs at the entrance welcomes guests to this Italian trattoria.

Osteria Enoteca da Sasino was opened by Chef Michiaki Sasamori in his hometown of Hirosaki in 2003. Since then, he has offered Italian dishes featuring local ingredients from Aomori Prefecture over two decades. Before opening Osteria Enoteca da Sasino, he trained at three restaurants in Japan and then visited Italy in 2001 to further hone his culinary skills. He won the Gold Award at the Cooking Masters organized by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries in 2024 for his long-standing efforts to promote the local food culture and received a number of other awards, including a Bronze Award at an international cheese contest in France in 2015 and a Bronze Medal at the Japan Wine Challenge in 2018.
However, his culinary flair is not the most prominent feature of the trattoria, which is characterized by growing grapes, among other vegetables and fruits, to produce wine in their facility. The trattoria even offers homemade charcuterie products (processed meats) and cheese. Now, Chef Sasamori is often seen growing vegetables and herbs in the farm when he is free from the kitchen. He is one of the first persons to run a farmer’s restaurant and has continued it up to the present.
He also goes fishing, depending on the season, catching bluefin tuna, tilefish, blackthroat seaperch, yellowtail, and gold-striped amberjack, among others. These culinary treasures of the northern prefecture of Aomori are transformed into delicious dishes full of love for the locality by the chef who knows Hirosaki better than anyone else. The wine list features wines brewed by Mr. Sasamori himself at Fattoria da Sasino (two whites, three reds, and one spumante), a brandy made from the winery’s own wine, a cider crafted from Aomori apples, as well as selections from Italy and France (mainly Burgundy).

Inside the restaurant is a white-toned stylish dining room with a touch of wood grain, furnished with five tables (seating up to 10 guests in total). School-age or older children can dine at the trattoria (choosing dishes from the à la carte menu, such as pasta). Younger children can also dine, depending on the day. In addition, overseas guests are accompanied by English- and Italian-speaking staff. Chef Sasamori’s culinary world attracts many guests, not only from within the prefecture but also from around the country. They visit Osteria Enoteca da Sasino for family gatherings, dates, and anniversary celebrations. Please enjoy the world created by Chef Sasamori to celebrate the bounty of Aomori, along with his delicious dishes.


【Note from restaurant】
Please understand that when the owner-chef is away on business, the restaurant may be open only with staff.
nearestStations: A -10 minutes by car from JR Hirosaki Station

245335.longDescription:
A 15-minute drive from JR Hachinohe Station or a 20-minute walk from JR Shirogane Station on the Hachinohe Line will take you to a restaurant with light-brown and lemon-yellow walls reminiscent of the bright sunshine of Italy. That is Casa del cibo, which opened its doors in a residential district in Hachinohe City in southeastern Aomori Prefecture in 2011. Take a step inside, and you will be welcomed by a chic interior with a counter and tables with white cloths.

Casa del cibo is helmed by Chef Ryohei Ikemi, who studied the basics of French cuisine in France while he was going to École Culinaire Kunitachi. After returning to Japan, he worked at a French restaurant in his home prefecture of Kanagawa, but subsequently he switched to Italian cuisine, honing his culinary skills at Italian restaurants in Tokyo, including Enoteca Pinchiorri, DA Noi, and Incontro. Then, he opened Casa del cibo in Hachinohe, Aomori, with his wife, Etsuko, who serves as a sommelier.
The menu features local ingredients, especially seafood, which are transformed into simple yet elegant dishes by Chef Ikemi. For example, one of the chef’s specialties, Affogato of Octopus,  is a result of his attempt to create a memorable dish with minimum ingredients. He has reinterpreted a classic dish of stewed octopus in tomato sauce from Napoli in southern Italy by using stock made from octopus and dried tomatoes and taking care not to stew it too much to prevent it from losing its shape. The octopus is directly sourced from a fisherman whom he describes as a man who surprised him with his fresh, high-quality seafood. Casa del cibo also offers a specialty pasta cooked with local sea urchins and abalone and meat dishes featuring Gin no Kamo (a famous brand of wild duck from Aomori), Aomori Shamrock (locally produced chicken), and domestic boar, which is rarely produced in Japan. All these ingredients are transformed into flamboyant dishes with great care so that guests can discover the sophistication of cuisine and the beauty of colors.
The wine list mainly consists of Italian wines, selected to match the dishes by Sommelier Etsuko, who graduated from the same culinary school as the chef. The wine pairing menu offers flexible options, such as a glass of wine for each dish (full pairings), half a glass for each dish, or fewer glasses per meal.

Renovated into a chic and discreet design in 2020, Casa del cibo has a main dining room with a four-seat counter and two private rooms, and a semi-private room. The restaurant attracts many guests from near and far, including families and couples who celebrate anniversaries with intimate dinners as well as solitary diners who come to savor the delicious dishes of Chef Ikemi. Guests can dine with children in either of the two private rooms though, in principle, the restaurant can only accommodate children of primary school age or older who can dine quietly.
As indicated by its name, Casa del cibo, which means the house of delicious food, the detached restaurant boasts a chic interior that provides a laid-back, homey dining experience and offers simple yet amazing dishes that showcase the chef’s excellent skills. It is definitely worth trying an intimate dinner at Casa del cibo.
nearestStations: 20 minutes walk or 5 minutes' taxi ride from Shirogane Station on the JR Hachinohe Line

245231.longDescription:
A 30-minute walk from Sakura Station (15-minute train ride from Chiba Station) takes you to PRESENTE Sugi, a detached restaurant in the suburbs of Sakura, Chiba, which is highly recognized and well patronized by connoisseurs from around Japan.

PRESENTE Sugi is helmed by Chef Noritoshi Sugioka, who trained at an Italian restaurant in Tokyo and honed his culinary skills at Ristorante Castello in his hometown of Sakura. He learned how to create dishes and settings from scratch to celebrate the bounty of nature in Sakura and eventually opened his own restaurant, PRESENTE Sugi, in the same city in 2016. The restaurant soon gained popularity for its unique presentation of dishes and exclusive customer service.
The restaurant’s name combines the word “presente,” which means “present” in Italian, and part of his name, “sugi.” According to the chef, it reflects his commitment to developing himself so that he can offer better dishes today than he did yesterday even though the menu remains unchanged.
The ingredients are carefully selected and sourced from Chiba, including vegetables from Hatamuguri, a local farm known for its organic vegetables, and flour from hand-picked wheat. The mushrooms, edible wild plants, and herbs are also picked by the chef from a nearby mountainous area. The locally grown Yachiyo Black Beef, highlighted on the entrée menu, has gained increased recognition as it is often featured by Chef Sugioka, who is captivated by its flavor. It is now widely known as a brand beef of Chiba.
The recipe for the beef has also been carefully developed by Chef Sugioka. First, the beef is marinated with salt and dried tomatoes for one day to enhance its flavor and then cooked until well done at a low temperature. Subsequently, it is cooled down in a blast chiller to negative 25° Celsius and grilled over firewood. This method was invented by the chef to keep the juice from dripping from the beef and lock in the flavor. The premium steak, slowly cooked for three hours, is served with a steak knife custom made by Ryusen Hamono in Fukui.
The prix fixe meal starts with “Candied Tomato” (cherry tomatoes covered with candy). It was created by taking inspiration from candied apples, one of the most popular sweets offered at summer festivals, to “remind guests of the excitement they felt as children when they got a candied apple at a summer festival.” Chef Sugioka, who aims to make his restaurant “enjoyable and worth visiting repeatedly, like Disneyland,” offers various playful dishes that delight not only the taste buds but also the eyes of connoisseurs, such as financiers modeled after a statue of Moai from Easter Island and a dish with a note stating “this is edible though it seems like it is not.”

Inside the restaurant, four tables are comfortably spaced apart.
Why not embark on a culinary adventure with your family, significant other, friends, colleagues, or food buddies at this one-of-a-kind restaurant in Sakura, Chiba?

244761.longDescription:
Dogoyuno-cho in Matsuyama City is the gateway to Ehime in Shikoku. “Dogo Kaishu” is a one-star Japanese restaurant located in Dogo town, which is said to be the oldest hot spring resort in Japan. In a tasteful house, chef Kisei Sakamoto showcases his skills with the intent that, "I want people to know how wonderful the local ingredients of Ehime are".

“Dogo Kaishu” was established in 1982. Chef Sakamoto was born as the 2nd generation head of the Sakamoto clan and, after training in the Kansai and Kanto regions, desired to "make Ehime a more proud town". He succeeded his predecessor at Dogo Kaishu and ensured that the good reputation of the restaurant would continue. In 2020, Dogo Kaishu moved from Ichiban-cho, Matsuyama City to "Dogo", the gateway to Ehime, which is visited by many tourists. In order to have the capacity to entertain guests from inside and outside of the prefecture, it took more than a year to complete the construction of the new Japanese-style restaurant.

Chef Sakamoto says that "I believe that simple and appealing dishes are ideal. They still take time and effort to prepare, but I want my cuisine to express the various tastes and flavors of Ehime in a simple way, without making them too complicated." Ingredients are mainly sourced from Ehime Prefecture where they are purchased directly from local farmers and fishermen, fresh fish stores and fruit and vegetable shops. In the spring, Sakamoto-san uses natural sea bream and wild vegetables and in the summer, he uses Ayu (sweetfish) which are actually caught by his predecessor at Dogo Kaishu. In the autumn he uses river crab, bonito fish and matsutake mushrooms, and in the winter, wild boar, wild game meat and pufferfish. You can enjoy the natural bounty of Ehime in all four seasons.

The restaurant offers a variety of high-quality sake from all over Japan, including Ehime's famous sake. They also serve craft beer that goes well with fish from Setouchi and the restaurant’s cuisine. The beer is specially made at the nearby brewery 'DD4D', and you can even find an original craft beer that is only available at Dogo Kaishu. They have natural wines from around the world, including chef Sakamoto's favorite California winery, "KENZO ESTATE".

The concepts that Sakamoto-san wanted to promote in his restaurant are those of longevity and homeliness. The restaurant was designed by a Japanese architect who specializes in making Japanese-style homes. The objective behind designing it in the style of a house was that with every visit a guest makes, they will feel more comfortable and at home. The L-shaped counter (9 to 10 seats) is covered with tatami made of pesticide-free Kumamoto rush, giving you a sense of warmth, helping you to relax while eating. In addition, there are 2 sunken kotatsu style private rooms (2 to 8 people) and a private room with regular tables (up to 24 people) on the 2nd floor. You can enjoy Ehime's charming “Dogo Kaishu” for various occasions, such as gatherings with family, friends and colleagues, dates and entertaining overseas guests.
nearestStations: A 3-minte walk from Dogo Onsen Station (Iyo Railway Route 3 on the Shieki Station Line, Iyo Railway Route 5 on Matsuyama Station Line, Iyo Railway Route 6 on the Honmachi Line)

244646.longDescription:
Boasting 3 stars in international travel guides, Dogo Onsen is mentioned in Nihonshoki, an ancient history book, and it is said to be the oldest hot spring resort in Japan. Kuruma Sushi, a world gourmet guide award sushi restaurant, is located in Ichibancho, Matsuyama, home of Dogo Onsen. Sushi-loving gourmets frequently visit here for the masterful sushi crafted by the young second-generation chef, Koji Takahira.
Chef Takahira grew up looking over the shoulder of his father, the previous chef of Kuruma Sushi, and began his training in Kuruma Sushi’s kitchen as he started high school. After graduation, he went to Tokyo and dine at different sushi restaurants. Moreover, he asked to be trained at restaurants he liked. He worked at a Japanese restaurant for a year, and later studied diligently at Ginza’s world gourmet guide award Sushi Yoshitake for 5 years. In 2017, he made his long-awaited return home, and took over his father's position behind the counter at Kuruma Sushi. The young chef's unique approach to fish attracted even more Kuruma Sushi fans, and it earned 2 stars in the blink of an eye. He was only 27 years old at the time, making him the youngest holder of 2 stars in Japan. It became a popular restaurant known not only in Matsuyama, but nationwide.
“What surprised me most when coming back to Ehime was the lack of stress in the fish and their aroma,” says Chef Takahira. In Ehime, they have their own way of treating their fishes. For example, the fish is not wrapped in kombu seaweed to add flavor. The reason, he explains, is that “the fish caught in Ehime are stress-free, so there is no need to add flavor.” He can also judge whether fish should be aged, or whether aroma should emphasized. Marbled flounder is marinated at 8 AM, and it is not allowed to bleed, to preserve the flavor. Threeline grunt is aged for 7-10 days, and grilled before it is made into sushi. Firm, fresh sea bream is served in 3 thin slices so that it will meld with the sushi rice more easily, and he spares no effort, doing his utmost to ensure that the flavor is at its peak when the sushi is placed in the mouth. For the sushi rice, he uses a Yamagata variety called Tsuyahime, with a blend of 4 kinds of rice and red vinegars. To ensure the rice is firm on the outside and tender on the inside, he starts cooking the rice in a special customized hagama pot to coincide with the start of the meal. His commitment to flavor extends to his Rishiri kombu seaweed, which is matured in a storehouse for 3 years.
The sake selection has more than 20 varieties at any time, with local Ehime sake like Ishizuchi and Itto Ryodan, as well as fine sake from around Japan, such as Akita’s Aramasa, Mie’s Zaku, and Fukui’s Kokuryu. The wine is selected by Chef Takahira, who is also a qualified sommelier, and focuses on French vintages, including champagne and white wine. He also stocks natural wines, for which he seeks for the best sushi pairings.
The interior sits only 8 at the single plain wood counter. The tableware consists mainly of 350-400 year-old pieces of vintage Imari ware, Tokoname ware, and Eiraku. Furthermore, blue-and-white porcelain from China’s Ming Dynasty and modern pieces such as Karatsu ware by Taki Nakazato are also used. This wide collection shows Chef Takahira's love of antique objects. “Sushi is life,” says Chef Takahira. At Matsuyama’s 2-star Kuruma Sushi, when you enjoy his wholeheartedly crafted sushi, you will undoubtedly experience a passionate discussion about sushi with the sushi connoisseurs packing the counter.

地物を中心に産地に足を運んで実際に大将がご自身の目で見極められた食材を使用されています。つまりこの食材といえばこの産地といった規制概念にとらわれることがありません。当然ながら生産者さんとの繋がり、信頼関係があってこそのものです。自分の少ない経験の中では今までの人生でいただいた最高のお料理でした。食材の良さはもとより調理技術、創意工夫の進化がとまりません。一番の進化はシャリに感じられたように思います。予約がとれる今の間に多くの方に行ってもらいたい個人的に日本一のお鮨屋さんです。
excellent!
美味しかったです
瀬戸内の海の幸を生かした寿司は感動した。料理のみならず接客も最高レベルで、また松山に来た際には是非とも伺いたいと思う。

たまのご褒美でお伺いしています。
毎回びっくりするお料理があります。
笑顔にしてもらってありがとうございます。
地元として誇れます。
また、宜しくお願いします。
本当に美味しかったです。満足させて頂きました。今年は三国へ行けなかったので、越前蟹に出会えて幸せでした。妻は堀川ごぼうなど、野菜類にも感動をしておりました。妻の自宅が近所ですので、次回はお酒飲みながら食したいです。どうぞよろしくお願い致します。
最高でした
Both the quality of the fish and the skill of the chefs are outstanding.

今回も大変おいしかったです
有難うございます
どれ食べても最高に美味しかったです
最初から最後まで次は何が出るのか？ワクワク感とともにお料理もしっかり手を加えていて素晴らしいコースでした。
洗練されていて、とても美味しかった。何度でも行きたい。
料理は言うまでもなく、店内の雰囲気や食事の時間の演出、お店の皆さんの笑顔や気遣い、どれをとっても最高で特別な時間を過ごさせて頂きました。ありがとうございました。
店主　スタッフ　お料理　全て満足でした

とても美味しく頂きました。
本当にありがとうございます。

また、お伺いさせて頂きます！
絶品でした。

基本的に地物の食材を中心とした構成ですが、生産者さんや職人さん同士のつながりも大事にされており大将が納得できるお仕事をするために必要なものはどんどん取り入れられる意欲も同時に感じさせてもらえました。お寿司という一見シンプルなお料理ですが、食材ごとに季節や個体を見て調理法も変えられる奥深さ研究熱心さが伝わる内容です。つまり、いつ、どの季節にいっても美味しいです。すでに地元の方より遠方の方が多いのではないだろうか？と思えるくらい毎回周りのお客さんも年齢層や居住地がさまざまで、幅広い客層に支持されている様子です。大将ご自身も食べ歩き（自己研鑽）がお好きなようで、情報のアップデートにも余念がないご様子です。今後も進化し続けるお料理に期待しております。

誕生日に、素敵な思い出ができました。
お料理、サービスとも大変感激いたしました。
またお伺いします。
ありがとうございました。

旬のお魚を、最高の状態でいただきました。
ありがとうございました。
そして大将のお誕生日をお祝いさせていただきました。
おめでとうございます！
最高に美味しかったです。素晴らしかったです。
地場の食材を様々な手法を使い、美味しく仕上げる点に満足しました。つまみもお寿司も温度と食感を意識した食べていて、ニンマリする楽しさでした。
伊勢海老が美味しかった
一人だったのでとても緊張しましたが、大将がとても気さくで、緊張もほぐれました。一品一品丁寧に仕事さているのがわかりました。所作がとても美しく、今まで行ったお寿司屋さんの中でも一番でした。ありがとうございました。

食材の鮮度、処理手当、本来の味を生かすための創意工夫と、いずれもこれ以上のクオリティはありえないのではないかと思われるものばかりでした。聞けば大将はお休みの日もお料理の向上のため試行錯誤を繰り返しておられると。事実、毎回訪れる度にレベルアップをまざまざと感じさせてもらえる内容です。特に今回感動したのが酢飯。いままでに比べ酢飯自体の主張はマイルドになったものの、より一層食材に寄り添い、食材の魅力を引き出すお味に変化しておりました。食材も酢飯も『え！？そんなところにまで工夫ができる余地があるなんて！』とびっくりさせられっぱなしでした。知識と経験、さらには絶え間ない努力が大将の天賦の才と相まってお客さんに口福をもたらします。また若女将のお酒のペアリングの妙と大将の御父上の大親方の巧みで軽快なトークとサポートでお店全体が極上のホスピタリティを提供してくださいます。すでに全国に名の知れた名店ですが、名実ともに日本一と呼ばれる日も近いと確信しております。ご馳走様でした。
食べたことのない魚、食材を食べたことのない料理方法で楽しめたこと。

大変美味しく　
久々に至福のひとときを過ごせました。
また機会があれば宜しくお願いします。
旬のものを美味しく頂きました
大変満足致しました。
料理はもちろんお店の雰囲気、サービスも素晴らしかったです。料理は店主の地元の食材への愛を感じました。メインの寿司は１２貫でとても食べ切れないと思っていましたが、すんなり完食。ご馳走様でした。
しっかりとした技術や知識に裏打ちされ、テーマ性に満ちた素晴らしい店。先代の大将と今の大将、さらにスタッフのホスピタリティの素晴らしさは何度訪れても感動する。

丁寧な料理の仕込みで味は抜群でした。慣れない娘への気遣いもいただき感謝いたします。
またチャンスがあれば利用させていただきます。
料理最高です。

とても美味しかったです。美味しさも去ることながら、ホスピタリティが最高でした。
まあ、訪問したいです。

お店もとてもいい雰囲気でお食事もほんと美味しくて、出てくるペースもちょうどよく素敵な時間を過ごせました。ありがとうございました。

人生経験の浅い無知なわたしの質問にも嫌な顔一つせず懇切丁寧にご教授くださったこと。
回らないお寿司屋さんの世界に初めて足を踏み入れ、そこでのこだわりと素晴らしさを知ることが出来たこと。
自分へのご褒美としては有り余るほどのクオリティを体験出来たこと。
どこのお寿司屋さんにしようか5日ほど悩んだ末に選択したのがこちらのお店で良かったです。

焼き物の火入れが良かったです。お寿司はもちろん美味しいです。
気持ちよく美味しいお寿司をいただきました

魚介類の素材、仕込へのこだわり、旬のネタを一番美味しく食べれる技術（握り方）と期待以上の満足感。
今までのお寿司さんでは食べたことの無いネタや調理法と大将の寿司へのこだわりが満ち溢れてる。
お父さんのフォローもあり場の雰囲気も居心地が良い。時期時期の美味しい旬の食材をいただける次の訪問が楽しみでならない。
仕事・接客すべて満足しております。

その時その時の厳選された食材で、今日はどんな物が出てくるのだろうかと楽しみにしています。

美味しかったです。またお伺いさせて頂きます。
いつもながらの厳選された食材に感動します。またいきます。

息子の転居祝いに参りましたが、最高のお料理とサービスに感激しました。息子が帰省した時にまたお邪魔させていただきます。

今回で三回目の訪問でしたが毎回進化を感じられる名店です。食材、食器、包丁にいたるまで生産者さんとのつながりも大事にされてらっしゃることがうがえました。与えられた食材への感謝や責任感を表現された素直なお料理に実直な大将のお人柄が表れているようでした。またオリジナリティ溢れる創意工夫の遊び心も忘れない、目、口、舌、鼻、耳と全身で味わえるエンターテインメントを体感出来ました。大将はお若いということもありますがその頂きはまだまだ先が見えません。新しい季節がくることを待ち遠しく思わせてくれる貴重なお店、くるますしさんに是非多くの方に足を運んで頂きたいです。心からご馳走様でした！

初めて食べる食材もあり楽しませていただきました。
人を笑顔にさせてくれる美味しさです。
連れも満足してくれ、今回も大変満足させていただきました。

コースの握りは勿論、太刀魚の焼きやトラフグ白子の茶碗蒸し、大変美味しく頂きました。

 にぎりは大きさ 、すし種のきりつけも丁度良く一体感が有ります。珍しい鱧のにぎり、包丁仕事が冴える スルメイカ、マナカツオが印象的です。

まだ、３回目の訪問ですがリクエストの食材にも応えてくださり、最高のひと時を過ごせました。

岡山の海うなぎにはじまり、おこぜ、こだわり仲買の日戻り鰹、鱧のだしの利いた茶わん蒸し 等 明日への活力となる食材を堪能させていただきました。すし種をきりつけ、空気に含ませ、丁寧なお仕事にいつも感服します。にぎりの一体感が心地よい。愛媛県に住んでいて、良かったです。

今月もう一度行きたいです。

瀬戸内中心の厳選した素材からしっかり旨味を引き出す技術が秀逸。手間ひまかけて一品づつ丁寧に丁寧に仕上げていて、中四国地区では唯一無二の美味しさです。
お話も楽しくとても心地よい時間を過ごすことができました。また伺います。ありがとうございました。
品数、ネタの仕込みの凄さ、シャリの味、対応、全てが素晴らしかったと思います。満足できました
自然派ワインと鮨の組み合わせが絶妙で、一品一品が強く印象に残りました。

245511.longDescription:
Located at the crossing of Ichibancho and Yasaka Streets, two of the busiest downtown streets in Matsuyama, Ehime, Sushi Kawanaka is helmed by Chef Kouyu Kawanaka, who was born and raised in Matsuyama.  He learned the art of sushi making from his father, who was running a sushi restaurant, Isamizushi, in Matsuyama. After his apprenticeship at this neighborhood sushi restaurant, beloved by locals for its catering and delivery services, he continued to pursue career advancement, opening his own restaurant, Sushi Kawanaka, in September 2019 at the main location of Isamizushi, which he took over from his father and renovated. 

While 70% of the seafood is locally sourced, including the fish caught by well-known fisherman Junichi Fujimoto from Imabari and the fish and shellfish selected by Shota Hamada, the owner of Marutetsu Suisan in Ainan, the bluefin tuna is delivered by Yunoka, an intermediate wholesaler, from Toyosu Market and dry-aged for the chef’s signature sushi.  The sushi rice is made from locally grown rice. It is cooked in an open-fire rice cooker, called mushi kamado, to achieve a grainy texture and seasoned with red or white vinegar, depending on the topping.  While the sushi rice for red fish, juvenile sea bream, horse mackerel, and shellfish is simply seasoned with a red vinegar mix, composed mainly of Yohee from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing, and salt, the sushi rice for white fish, gizzard shad, and other pickled fish is seasoned with a sweet rice vinegar to add a hint of mild, sweet flavor. 

The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu offers 20 courses, including 11 to 12 pieces of nigiri sushi and some eight small dishes, which are served alternatively. To stimulate diners’ appetites and ready their palates, the chef’s signature Hand-Rolled Fatty Tuna And Pickled Radish Sushi is served as the first course. Another specialty of the chef is Prawn Nigiri Sushi. Characterized by two pieces of prawn arranged to look like a kimono on the sushi rice, this is a testimony to his playful imagination and mastery of authentic Edomae sushi.  His pleasant personality is also reflected in his homey dishes, such as a Fish Dish With Salty Smoked Fresh Cream and Horse Crab Croquettes With Soya Milk Béchamel Sauce. Meanwhile, the drink menu offers about 20 varieties of sake, including not only nationally renowned labels, such as Denshu from Aomori and Aramasa from Akita, but also local options, such as Kyohina Ittoryodan from Ehime and Ishizuchi Ai, which is only available at restaurants in Ehime.

The restaurant’s interior is sophisticated with black accents. With a nine-seat counter made of gingko wood and a semi-private dining room (with a table seating up to six guests), Sushi Kawanaka caters for various occasions. Enjoy the exquisite delicacies and sushi created by Chef Kawanaka with pride in his home prefecture of Ehime in the quiet setting of his restaurant.

244501.longDescription:
In a shopping district in Ehime, the storefront of ""Sushi no Ma"" stands with a dignified air. A world gourmet guide award sushi restaurant is just ten minutes' tram ride from one of the oldest hot springs in Japan, Dogo Onsen. The owner-chef, Shogo Noma studied as an apprentice at ""Ken Sushi"" under Kenji Tanokubo for 16 years from the age of 18 before finding the right time to open his own restaurant in 2010. His style of sushi, dubbed Setouchimae sushi, is adapted from Ehime sushi, incorporating some of the best aspects of Edomae sushi. In 2018, it was awarded world gourmet guide award by an international gourmet guide.

Paired with the locally caught Ehime fish is Koshihikari sushi rice seasoned with sushi vinegar, salt, and sugar. The hint of sweetness is reminiscent of the traditional sushi originating from Iyo in Western Japan. 3-year aged wasabi and soy sauce dashed with local sake Yamatan Masamune are added to the season. ""Sushi no Ma"" also offers original Setouchi-mae sushi made with famous Ehime Sudachi (a small, green citrus fruit) and sun-dried sargassum salt from Noma's hometown. Noma selects only all natural seafood and is very particular about the process of blood draining and nerve severing used to prepare the fish. ""Sushi no Ma"" offers sea fig, long-armed octopus, sea urchin from the coasts of Matsuyama and Nakajima, Kawarazu conger eel, and other local seafood that is hard to find elsewhere. Its specialty is Ehime's famous Kuruma prawns, which are boiled alive right before serving. There are two seasonings available: soy sauce and Sudachi juice. Sushi no Mon's sushi is specially engineered so that if you turn it upside-down before you eat it, the rice and toppings melt in your mouth. Side dishes are mostly limited to sashimi and lightly grilled fish, however, as the types of seafood are used for sushi toppings and those offered as side dishes differ, there is plenty of variety.

The minimal seasoning doesn't smother the taste of the ingredients, and the resulting mild flavors pair excellently with wine. Diners may also bring their own wine or champagne. ""Sushi no Ma"" offers a selection of ten mostly local sakes including Chiyo no Kame, Kawakame, Ishizuchi, and Kyohina. The counter is built out of a single slab of white timber, and the dishes are Bizen ware specially ordered from living national treasure Isezaki. The interior is decorated with calligraphy by Ransai Oda and Imari ware. Private rooms are also available, making this the perfect place to relax and enjoy Ehime sushi in luxury.

245329.longDescription:
Shinoda is a Japanese restaurant in Imabari City, Ehime Prefecture, a location that commands a beautiful view of scattered islands at the center of the Seto Inland Sea. A 10-minute taxi drive from Imabari Station, the restaurant sits on a busy street close to the Port of Imabari, attracting food lovers from near and far with creative dishes conjured up from local ingredients by Chef Yusuke Shinoda.

Chef Shinoda’s attitude towards ingredients looks like that of a producer rather than a cook. For example, the fish is prepared by paying attention to all the details, from the amount of blood removed to the control of storage temperature, with help from a local popular fisherman, Junichi Fujimoto. The beans are produced by carefully controlling the entire process from the selection of the type of seeds to the timing of harvest in cooperation with Satoshi Mori from Mori Organic Farm on Omi Island. The corn featured in the Japanese mixed rice with seasonal vegetables is grown by Hiroto Niida from TETSUJIN Farm, harvested just before sunrise to maximize its taste. Thus, Chef Shinoda pays attention to every detail to create each dish as he intends it to be.
The chef’s choice meal consists of around 10 courses, starting with an aperitif, followed by Shinoda’s specialties, such as sweetfish grilled with salt over charcoal, which the chef proudly describes to be “tastier than anywhere else,” and rice with sweet bell peppers and dried baby sardines seasoned with Japanese pepper, featuring precious California Wonder peppers available around mid-August. They are characterized by a well-thought-out combination of ingredients that enhances each flavor despite their simple seasoning. The desserts are also crafted right in front of guests by Chef Shinoda, who spares no trouble in bringing them to perfection.
The drink menu is also carefully curated. The beer list offers Umenishiki beer developed by a Japanese sake brewery as Ehime’s first local beer. The sake list always includes Junmai Daiginjo Ai brewed by Ishizuchi Sake Brewery as a limited label for local restaurants in Ehime. Needless to say, Chef Shinoda, involved in the selection of rice for this sake, purchases it by the tank. The wine list also offers a variety of wines. Sometimes, depending on the booking situation, magnums are opened and offered by the glass.

With a five-seat counter, the dining room is adorned with hanging scrolls and paintings to give a sense of the season. The exclusively crafted bowls with paintings to tell a story of Imabari are Sakurai lacquerware traditionally made in Imabari. Sake is served in glasses created by a local glassblower, Yasuomi Kajikawa, while foods are presented on plates crafted by local artists, such as Koh Ichino and Momoko Ishii. Enjoy exclusive dishes at Shinoda with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues to discover the charm of Imabari City in Ehime Prefecture.
nearestStations: 10 minutes by taxi from the west exit of Imabari Station

244645.longDescription:
A shopping quarter in Matsuyama, Ehime. On the third floor of a building at the intersection of Nibancho Dori and Yasaka Dori is one-star restaurant ""Sushi Ino"". Owner Yusuke Ino fell in love with the location and the building's beautiful glass exterior; he knew this was just the place for his restaurant. Today, he lovingly crafts sushi here.
Ino trained for four years at Matsuyama sushi restaurant ""Edomae Ichiro"", mastering the style. He opened ""Sushi Ino"" in 2014, and the restaurant soon rose in popularity and earned world gourmet guide award. ""I can say with confidence that we offer the best fish in Matsuyama,"" says Ino. 

Purchased fresh from the market every morning, the fish are slaughtered via Ikejime or blood-letting and prepared using the best method for the particular type of fish. Popular choices include dotted gizzard shad and conger eel. Edomae sushi staple tuna is purchased at auction from a reputable broker in Toyosu so that the residents of Ehime, where white fish is favored, can discover the deliciousness of quality tuna. Japanese Sake lover Mr.Ino offers an astounding range of 50 sake varieties from all around Japan. Dry sake makes up much of the selection, and Ino offers sake recommendations to complement the sushi or the diner's tastes. Alternatively, white wine or champagne also make a great accompaniment to the sushi.

The most salient feature of the bright, pristine interior is the counter at the back, crafted from a single piece of ginkgo wood. Carefully arranged lighting ensures that diners can clearly see their hands and the sushi crafted by the chefs, the grains of rice of the nigiri glistening brightly. There are ten seats at the main counter where Ino works, and another eight seats in front of the counter where a second chef is stationed. ""Sushi Ino"" is a perfect choice for almost any situation, from outings with friends or family to dates. If you want to eat good sushi, just lift up the shop curtains and come on in; you won't be disappointed.

245328.longDescription:
Perched on the third floor of a building on a side street a few blocks from the busy downtown part of Matsuyama City in Ehime Prefecture, Sushi Takayama, a secluded restaurant helmed by Chef Dai Takayama, offers sushi and delicacies to celebrate the bounty of the Seto Inland Sea.

The chef of local origin completed his four-year rigorous apprenticeship at a one-star restaurant, Sushi Ino, in Ehime Prefecture before he opened his own restaurant named after himself, Sushi Takayama, in June 2018.
The carefully selected fish and shellfish are not only sourced from local markets but also delivered directly from brokers in rural markets so that guests from outside the prefecture can discover the bounty of the sea in Ehime. Chef Takayama even goes to fishing ports for fish not available in the market. The oval squids, summer grunt, and winter spotted mackerel processed by Shota Hamada from Marutetsu Suisan in Ainan and transformed into sushi toppings are especially appreciated by guests. The tuna is sourced from Yunoka, a popular broker, in Toyosu Market. The sushi rice is made of Tsuyahime rice from Yamagata, seasoned with a blend of one rice vinegar and two red vinegars for a slightly sweet and acid note, and kept at different temperatures depending on the topping.
The sake list always has some 20 labels from around Japan, including locally brewed sake from Ishizuchi Sake Brewery in Ehime. Meanwhile, the wine list offers 10 champagnes and whites, all by the bottle.

When you go through the entrance doors into the restaurant, you will be welcomed by double-faced, red shoji screens (paper sliding door) in bright light. Behind the noren curtain (shop curtain) is a sophisticated dining room with a cypress ceiling, a nine-seat counter made of solid ginkgo wood, and warm wooden elements. Enjoy a variety of dishes available only at Sushi Takayama in Matsuyama City, Ehime, with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues.

245471.longDescription:
About 10 minutes’ drive from JR Fukui Station, which has been brought to life since the extension of the Hokuriku Shinkansen line, or 3 minutes’ walk from Echizen Railway Nikka Kagaku-Mae Station, Le jardin is a stately detached restaurant nestled in a quiet residential area in Fukui Prefecture.    The delicious dishes conjured up by Chef Ryo Horiuchi, a winner of a prestigious international culinary competition, attract food lovers from inside and outside the prefecture and the country.

Hailing from Kyoto Prefecture, the internationally renowned chef first trained at a culinary school and then apprenticed at renowned restaurants, such as L’OSIER in Ginza and a French fine-dining restaurant, SIGNATURE, in Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo. Then, he moved to France, where he worked at Sur mesure par Tierry Marx for two years and served as Chef de Partie and then Sous Chef at Regis et Jacques Marcon.  After returning to Japan, he further honed his culinary skills as Assistant Chef at a French restaurant, Esterre, in Palace Hotel Tokyo. Then, he moved to Fukui Prefecture, known for its gastronomic delights, and became Chef at Le jardin, which reopened after renovation in September 2022.  In the same year, he won the 54th Le Taittinger International Award for Cuisine d’Auteur, a prestigious culinary competition which is also known as the Everest of Gastronomy because of its extreme difficulty. This victory made him the third Japanese chef to win the world championship.

Chef Horiuchi combines traditional recipes with innovative twists and an exquisite blend of tasty and healthy local products from Fukui and carefully selected ingredients from around the world. His signature dish features sea urchin, which is one of the three great delicacies of Japan and a specialty of Fukui. With an addictive flavor that goes well with sake, the Echizen Salted Sea Urchin of Amatatsu, the oldest sea urchin trader in Japan, is transformed into a French gastronomic indulgence that wows many guests. Other popular specialties of Le jardin include seasonal duck dishes and a dessert featuring Fukui Plums. The exquisite food beautifully arranged on plates and then topped with sauce by Chef Horiuchi to give it a final touch is a testimony to the best French fine-dining restaurant in the Hokuriku Region.

As indicated by its name, Le jardin, which means ‘the garden’ in French, the dining room with eye-catching red sofas offers amazing views of the garden. The speckled carpet that looks like pebbly ground and the wooden chandeliers give a luxurious yet laidback ambience. With two tables with chairs, five tables with sofas, and two private dining rooms (seating up to six and eight guests, respectively), Le jardin is recommended for various occasions, such as family and friend gatherings, dates, and business dinners with overseas clients. Please come to Fukui and indulge your taste buds with the amazing dishes created by the world-champion chef!
