244318.longDescription:
Opened in December 2012 as a branch of Restaurant Georges Marceau, one of the best French restaurants in Hakata, by its owner-chef Koji Konishi, Défi Georges Marceau is located in Nishi Nakasu, the highest-end streets in downtown Fukuoka lined with a row of fine restaurants.  Perched on the second floor of a building adjacent to Tenjin Chuo Park (on the Kihinkan Hall side), the restaurant is cozy and comfortable with views of greenery and warm sunshine coming through the large windows.

Défi is helmed by Chef Mami Hakoda, who worked as Sous Chef under Owner-Chef Konishi at Restaurant Georges Marceau for 11 years. 

The word ‘Défi’ in the restaurant’s name means ‘challenge’ in French. Chef Hakoda was committed to become a chef who can empathize with guests and make them feel at home when she was appointed as the chef of Défi.  She is especially keen to surprise guests with extraordinary dishes they would not encounter in their daily lives. She takes on challenges day by day and pushes her sense of balance and creativity to the limit, exploring new French recipes no one has tasted before. However, her ambition is not only to tingle the palate of guests but goes even further. She tries to satisfy their hearts as well as their stomachs. To this end, she directly interacts with diners to capture their thoughts and feelings, earnestly faces each guest, and offers personalized dishes and services.  If it heals their minds and strikes a chord in their hearts, nothing could please her more than that. Bringing smiles and comfort to all guests at Défi is also a ‘défi’ (challenge) for Chef Hakoda.

The dining room feels warm with woody accents. The show plats, butter knives, and chopstick rests are also made of wood. Coupled with them, the cutlery created by Toshihiro Kozuma, a woodcarver from Tamana County, Kumamoto Prefecture, and the chopsticks by Ichihara Heibei Shoten in Kyoto further elevate the dining experience.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Exit 1 of Nakasu-Kawabata Station on the Fukuoka City Subway Airport line

245006.localizedAddress: 3F, Ren Round Building, 3-20, Nishinakasu, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka
245006.longDescription: Gahoujin is located on the third floor of a building in the high-end commercial district of Nishinakasu in Fukuoka, a short eight-minute walk from Nakasukawabata Station next to Fukuoka Station. The restaurant is a second location of the three-star Sushi Sakai and led by chef-owner Daigo Sakai, who trained at a sushi-kappo restaurant in Fukuoka, honed his culinary skills at a two-star restaurant, Sushidokoro Umi, in Aoyama, before launching Sushi Sakai in 2013. Gahoujin finally opened seven years later, in August 2020. The sushi served at Gahoujin is prepared by his apprentices who learned to make sushi from the heart. The restaurant takes its name from a Zen concept that refers to the importance of encounters with people. This reflects the wish of chef Sakai to express his gratitude to both customers and apprentices for their support. The ingredients are sourced not directly from producers but from trusted brokers in Fukuoka City Central Wholesale Market, Yanagibashi Rengo Market, and Toyosu Market, a sign of Sakai’s confidence in his partners. The sushi rice is prepared by seasoning rice with a blend of two varieties of red vinegar, with a flavor exemplified by the restaurant’s nigiri sushi with tuna. The most popular dish is one of sliced raw puffer fish dressed in anglerfish liver sauce, a delicacy served only between October and March. Reminiscent of foie gras, the sauce’s flavor is very rich and creamy, and is a favorite of connoisseurs. In addition, the restaurant offers more than 15 varieties of sake from across Japan, selected according to the season and month, as well as an extensive selection of white wines, Champagne, and red wines, including rare labels. Like Sushi Sakai, the interior at Gahoujin is elegant and understated, with a sukiya-style structure designed by Shinji Maeda, a first-rate architect in the style. With only six counter seats, the small space creates an intimate and relaxing atmosphere and encourages conversations between the owner and guests. The dinnerware is mostly made up of Karatsu ware and also includes handmade pieces by local artisans. These features make Gahoujin perfect for dinners with clients, date nights, birthdays, and other occasions. Please enjoy excellent sushi made by chef Sakai’s trusted apprentices. Click here to go to the Sushi Sakai website. Click here to go to the Zaisho website.
nearestStations: 8-minute walk from Fukuoka City Subway Kūkō Line Nakasu-Kawabata Station Exit 1

244267.localizedAddress: 2F, Rin First, 4-4, Nishinakasu, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka
244267.longDescription:
Located on the 2nd floor of a building in Nishi Nakasu that is facing the Nakagawa River, which flows through downtown Hakata, is the French cuisine restaurant L'eau Blanche. L'eau Blanche means "white water" in French.
 
Chef Teppei Shiromizu decided from an early age to become a cook, and after graduating from a vocational school, he went to France after spending time at Hotel de Mikuni (Yotsuya, Tokyo) and Au goût du jour merveille in Nihonbashi, Tokyo. After returning to Japan, he served as the chef of Ogu de Jules Meruveiyu Hakata for 4 years. By exploring "What we can offer because we live in Fukuoka", and by going to various places in Kyushu and meeting producers in person, he is able to sublimate to the best dish in which they can feel the vitality of the carefully selected ingredients.

"L'eau Blanche" is an open kitchen theater which expresses the way of life and the way of cooking of chefs.

What supports the Teppei Shiromizu cuisine that is not bound by the French concept is the refined space and the calm time that flows comfortably. And the wine makes the food more attractive. They always have domestic wine, French wine, and the pairing for each plate is one of the fun. It is a simple and high quality space created by designer Gaku Takasu. 244533.longDescription:
Located in the busiest shopping district, Nishinakasu, Hakata. In 2016, "Nihon Ryori Nagaoka" relocated to this bustling area where the streets are lined with famous restaurants.

Head chef Shugo Nagaoka honed his skills for 4 years at Hotel Okura Amersterdam's Japanese restaurant Yamasato and then a Japanese restaurant in Nakasu before opening his own restaurant, "Otona no Gochiso," in 2010. In 2015, he participated in the Milano universal exposition, where he became interested in sharing Japanese food culture with visitors from abroad. Nagaoka then relocated to his current premises—located 5-minute from the station and easily accessible from the airport—reopening his restaurant under the new name Nagaoka Japanese Cuisine.

Nagaoka has also worked with 'Slow Food Nippon,' and he recognizes the importance of knowing the faces and the feelings of the producers. He visits farmers and fishermen in person, incorporating the producers' feelings into his cuisine to deliver them to his customers. Nagaoka uses fresh seafood and vegetables sourced primarily from his hometown of Yamaguchi and nearby Kyushu, not adding too much so as to let the natural flavors of the ingredients shine. Nagaoka's true skill lies in his ability to use simple methods to bring out the deliciousness of the ingredients.

There is only one course on offer. First, in typical kaiseki style, diners are served a small bowl of warm rice porridge. Once their stomachs and hearts have been thoroughly warmed up, a selection of dishes incorporating seasonal ingredients follows. Finally, each diner is served his or her own earthen pot of steamed rice. Eight dishes such as home-style pollack roe, miso, and ground meat, rolled omelet, pickles, and Japanese yam accompany the white rice, so diners can enjoy a little bit of everything. The restaurant is also famous for its dried mullet roe, made with painstaking care, which can be ordered separately.
There is a 15-range of Japanese sake, mostly crisp and dry varieties which pair excellently with the food. 10 kinds of Japanese sake are always available, while the other 5 change according to the seasons. There is also plenty of local Kyushu sake. In addition to sake, a range of Burgundy and other wine and shochu are also available.

"Nihon Ryori Nagaoka" luxurious interior makes ample use of wood and stone; it is often chosen for business dinners for its elegant atmosphere. Seating consists of ten seats around an L-shaped ginkgo table, as well as private rooms seating four and 6-diner respectively. Service in English is available, making the restaurant an attractive choice for visitors from outside Japan. Offering traditional yet innovative Japanese cuisine, Nagaoka Japanese Cuisine is well worth traveling for, whether you're coming from outside Fukuoka or abroad.


【Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available?】
Children are welcome to come to the restaurant, but only those who can eat the same course as adults at the counter and in the private rooms.

244286.longDescription:
French restaurant Raisin d’Or locates in a relaxed area in Nishi Nakasu in Fukuoka, where many high-end restaurants are located. Opened with the concept of creating “a restaurant that is made to provide good service”, all of the service staffs are qualified with sommelier certificates. While the dishes are authentic French cuisine, their originality has attracted many guests and they were awarded 1-star in 2014.
 
Leading the entire staff and consistently providing high-quality service is the owner and sommelier Hideki Ishii. After working at Hotel Nikko Fukuoka for 13 years and La Table de Provence at Akasaka, he opened Raisin d’Or in 2007. He was able to make the restaurant one of Fukuoka’s leading grand maisons, with the desire to create a restaurant that provides fulfilling service. 

Over 400 types of mainly French wine are stocked in the best conditions. There is a large collection of glass wines as well, including top-quality and precious wine like Château d'Yquem. You will be able to see the true value of the entire service staff that are also sommeliers during the wine pairing.

To match with the restaurant name "Raisin d’Or" (golden grapes), the interior of the restaurant is decorated with gold in various places, creating a sense of relaxed luxury. There is also a private room that can seat up to 4 guests, which is ideal for business entertainment, anniversaries and dates. We would like you to experience  elegant dishes and the heartfelt hospitality from the staffs.

244394.longDescription:
""Restaurant Aréna"" opened its doors in July 2016 on a corner of Nakasu area just a 4-minute walk from Tenjin-Minami Station. Fate brought Tokyo chef Ryo Arima to Fukuoka where he gained valuable experience in hotels and restaurants throughout the city. After that, he went through two and a half years of training at several French restaurants including world gourmet guide award restaurant ""Passage 53"" and ""Sur Mesure"" in Paris and Burgundy's world gourmet guide award ""Maison Lameloise"" before returning to Japan to open ""Restaurant Aréna"".

The food is prepared as the chef's choice (omakase) courses, and the menu showcases only the theme of each plate and the ingredients used. The first thing that guests can salivate at in anticipation is the chef's signature dish ""Rum Raisin"". This sweet, cutely presented, desert-like hors d'oeuvre consists of French foie gras, rum raisin sauce, and an almond-based crust. It is an exquisite finger food and a great companion to a glass of champagne. After that, guests can look forward to a cavalcade of rich and innovative dishes arranged from a mix of seasonal ingredients to fit into the theme the chef has chosen. For example, the theme of one day's main dish might be ""Arpeggio."" It's a musical term for a type of broken chord. This earthy ensemble featured ingredients like oysters, Charolais beef from France, small turnips, herbs, and other ingredients with varying flavors and aftertaste durations. Each dish invites guests on a stimulating journey that tickles the senses in its own unique way. The wine cellar is stocked with an impressive variety of over 300 different hand-selected AOC wines from the best vineyards. 10 different wine and champagne are kept ready to order by the glass at all times.

Seating is limited to just ten guests at a time to emphasize a private dining experience. The restaurant works well as a venue for a variety of occasions including anniversaries, dates, and entertaining clients. The restaurant has English-speaking staff, so foreign guests need not worry about communicating. The restaurant's name, ""Aréna,"" evokes images of a sports stadium or stage, or, more broadly, a facing of one another. The decor is white and silver, unadorned with flowers, paintings, or other decorations. The elegant white ""stage"" allows you to focus on the food, the wine, and, most importantly, your companions without distraction.

244247.longDescription: Sushi Sakai opens its doors in Nishi-Nakasu, an area known to be a very high class in Fukuoka city. Many fans visit this popular restaurant from near and far, and it is the place to go in Fukuoka for authentic Edo-mae style sushi. Restaurant owner Daigo Sakai trained for 3 years at a sushi restaurant, after which he moved to Tokyo and trained for 7 years at two-star restaurant Sushi Umi. In 2013 he became independent and opened Sushi Sakai, and earned one star in 2014 and 3 stars in 2019. The menu is “omakase(Chef's choice) course” only, with about 8 otsumami (small dish) and about 12 nigiri sushi. In addition, sake, champagne, and wine are recommended for pairing by sommelier. For the ingredients, they use fresh fish caught in the outskirts, and high-grade seafood from all over the country which was caught and transported by air on the same day. “Blowfish sashimi with liver sauce”, served only between October and March, is a very popular otsumami dish. With recommended sushi like the “Pickled Akami”, a small nigiri that is slightly dyed red from the red vinegar used, you can always enjoy a continuously evolving Edo-mae style sushi here. The restaurant has 12 counter seats, and the interior is based on a design using Kyoto Kitayama cedar by Shinji Maeda, the foremost figure of traditional Sukiya architecture. You can enjoy your meal in a relaxing and calm atmosphere, whether it be during a business dinner, date, family event, or a wide range of scenes. We would like you to come and experience a taste and atmosphere that you can only find here at Sushi Sakai. Click here to go to the Gahoujin website. Click here to go to the Zaisho website. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? とっても美味しく、また大将の心遣いが嬉しかったです。
遠方ではありますがまた是非とも再訪したいと思いました。

大将、ひとつひとつ、どんな状態でどういうおいしさがあるのか、丁寧に説明してくださる。どういうおいしさかってところ、私には正直半分程度しかわからなった。お寿司ってほんと奥が深い。そんな私でも、感動は十二分。

245492.longDescription: Located in Nishinakasu, one of Fukuoka’s most vibrant dining districts, “Zaisho” stands as a sister restaurant of the three-star sushi restaurant “Sushi Sakai.” Following its second branch “Gahojin,” it marks the third location, opening in July 2024 on the same floor and in the same building as “Sushi Sakai.” At the counter, apprentices entrusted with their own stations—having honed their skills at “Sushi Sakai” under master chef Daigo Sakai—carry forward his philosophy of “sushi shaped with the heart.” They inherit not only technique but also a refined sense of hospitality, while expressing their own craftsmanship as the next generation. Seafood is sourced through the same trusted channels as “Sushi Sakai,” including the Fukuoka City Central Wholesale Market, Yanagibashi Rengo Market, and Toyosu Market, along with select markets in Kyoto, Hokkaido, and Kanazawa in Ishikawa. Carefully selected by expert intermediate wholesalers, the finest seasonal seafood is delivered. Tuna from the renowned Toyosu wholesaler “Yamayuki” remains a highlight. The rice, seasoned with a blend of two types of akazu (red vinegar), is precisely balanced to complement the tuna, making the signature “maguro nigiri” something to be savored slowly. A wide range of beverages is available, from sake and Champagne to red and white wines, whisky, and non-alcoholic options including Royal Blue Tea, with pairing selections curated by a sommelier. The course is set at approximately half the price of “Sushi Sakai,” reflecting the intention to make Edomae sushi more approachable. The interior, designed by first-class architect Shinji Maeda, presents a contemporary sukiya-style space with a relaxed atmosphere. At the single slab cedar counter, guests are invited not only to experience the evolving craft of these emerging sushi chefs, but also to watch over their journey and share in the path they continue to carve forward. * Click HERE to check the sister restaurant, Sushi Sakai. * Click HERE to check the sister restaurant, Gahoujin.

244440.longDescription:
Located 3-minute on foot from Ohorikoen Station is ""TTOAHISU"" in Fukuoka. This restaurant curtains draping down from the wooden entrance and ceiling make this stylish eatery look like a traditional Japanese style restaurant.

The owner-chef, Taishi Yamashita, after working in a French restaurant of Hotel in Nagasaki, he honed his skills in French cuisine working in places such as world gourmet guide award restaurant ""Joel Robuchon"" and ""AMOUR"" in Tokyo. In 2016, he opened ""TTOAHISU"" in Fukuoka, his hometown. 

""TTOAHISU"" only offers the chef’s selected course, under the theme 'Japanese culture x French cuisine'. Serving dishes such as ""Vichyssoise"" made with almond and dried mullet roe. Its specialty, the double consommé made with whole chicken, pork bones, and a dried flying dish is available all year round. The line up of alcohol includes Japanese sake and shochu, as well as wine. Even guests from overseas can enjoy the unique pairing of Japanese alcohol with French cuisine. To make the most of a visit to ""TTOAHISU,"" it would be best to request a drink that matches with the dishes. 

Upon entering the restaurant, the first thing that catches the eye is the artistically rendered Japanese paper. All around, space is designed so that guests from abroad can enjoy Japanese elements, and local guests can enjoy the touches of French fusion. It exudes Chef Yamashita’s unique tastes. The tables are arranged to give a sense of spaciousness; there are 10 seats in the main dining area for families to use. The kitchen is surrounded by glass, designed to face the customers. Come here for a date, a special occasion or just a casual meal and enjoy a fusion of Japanese culture and French cuisine.

和と洋のテイストがミックスされた独創的な料理で大変美味しかったです。また訪問したいお店でした。

熱い料理は熱く、料理人の気持ちの入ったお皿に感動しました。
親切な接客にも癒されました。
また伺わせて頂きたいと思います。
Great food and service

一皿一皿、山下シェフのオリジナリティーが感じられる工夫のあるお料理でした。どの料理もお繊細な味わいで美味しく、イノベーティブ・和食フレンチという感じでした。
スタッフのサービスも気配り、心配りが素晴らしく、お料理の説明だけでなく、気さくにお声をかけて下さり、くつろいで食事を楽しめました。お招きしたお客様もとても喜んで下さいました。本当に至福のお料理、サービスを提供下さり、豊かな時間を過ごせました。
初めてご利用させていただきました。外観からは想像できない店内の雰囲気に一度圧倒されるような感覚がありましたが、料理の提供へのこだわり・器の質の良さ・お客様へのホスピタリティ全てが良く、終わってみるとまた行きたいと感じました。また機会を見つけ伺います。良い時間をありがとうございました。
雰囲気やインテリアなど、新しい感覚を楽しめました。接客も大変丁寧でした。特に、最後の肉料理は焼き加減、付け合わせ、と圧巻の出来でした。これからも繊細かつ大胆な料理を期待しています。ありがとうございました。
初めてお食事させていただきましたが、接客、雰囲気はフレンチを気軽に楽しめる素晴らしいものであり、お料理は想像のひとつ上をいくものばかりでした。次回は今回以上に楽しめそうな、そんな気のするお店でした。
紹介した方が喜んてくれてよかったです。

一品一品丁寧なお料理と丁度よい接客、意外とリーズナブルばドリンク代。
素晴らしいと思います。
全てのお料理が素晴らしく美味しかったです。特に前菜のフォアグラが感動でした。

料理が美味しく、接客も丁寧でした。
メインのお肉が抜群でしたが、鰹といちじくに新鮮な驚きと美味しさがありました。
シェフが見えなくなるまで、見送ってくださったのも嬉しく思いました。

特にいちじくは甘味と塩味のバランスが絶妙で、感動しました。お肉やお魚の火の入り方も絶妙で、柔らかく、旨味が引き出されていてもう一皿ずつ食べたいくらいでした。

うまい

予約させて頂いたＣＣＢも楽しみですし、また11月に予約したので次回はどんな料理が出てくるか楽しみにしております。
本日はありがとうございました。どの料理もとても美味しかったです。
それぞれの料理がとても美味しく、驚きも与えてくれました。デザートも充実しており、満足度も高かったです。ソムリエの方も話しやすく、楽しく食事ができました。

ほんとうに素晴らしい夜でした。
いつか行きたい、絶対行きたいお店に行くことができて幸せです。予約とれないだろうと、諦めてました。
おもいたったのも遅かったのでキャンセル待ちになって
、、無理なら福岡には行かなかったので。
ちょうどひと席空いたそうで幸運でした。
沢山ききたいことや、お話ししたいことありましたが
料理をいただいてコースを通して会話できました。
それだけで十分です。山下シェフ
写真を撮っていただけたり
Ｔシャツもありがとうございました！
必ずまたＴシャツを着て伺います。

すごく楽しい時間をありがとうございました。

接客してくださった方もとてもフレンドリーで和やかな時間を過ごすことができました。

244319.longDescription:
Restaurant Georges Marceau is within walking distance from downtown Tenjin in a tranquil area of Akasaka. It is located on the 1st floor of a modern stone building.

The owner chef, Konishi Koji, trained at Bistrot d’Anjou (Aoyama, Tokyo) and Restaurant Perignon (Ginza, Tokyo). He also worked as assistant head chef at Georges Marceau (Kokubunji, Tokyo), and as head chef at Bleu Clair (Fukuoka, Momochi). In 1998, he opened his own restaurant called BistroEn in Kego, Fukuoka. After operating for 6 years, he closed the restaurant and moved the restaurant, creating a new French restaurant called Restaurant Georges Marceau, which portrays Kyushu through food. At present, they have opened a total of 3 restaurants, including Défi Georges Marceau and Patisserie Georges Marceau and since August 2014 to February 2020 they had been providing meals on the luxury train Seven Stars in Kyushu. This restaurant is known as a French restaurant that represents Kyushu. 

Since Chef Konishi knows well the charm of the ingredients from his hometown of Nagasaki, he offers French cuisine which specialized in ingredients from Kyushu. Vegetables are sourced from contract- farmers such as Farmers in Yatsushiro, Kumamoto and other parts of Kyushu. The seafood is Shimazaki fresh fish sourced from the Karatsu Market in Saga Prefecture, the chef personally applies a technique to provide them in the best condition. Beef used is Japanese black wagyu beef. All of these materials are sourced from suppliers who have built a strong relationship with the chef and his staffs, and they made dishes that bring out the flavors of each ingredient. There are always 150 kinds of wine available, mainly French, and they also serve wine from the Ajimu Winery. 

The restaurant's interior has a warm, modern atmosphere created by blending stone and wood in the theme of nature. It is a spacious establishment where customers can make reservations for parties and weddings. There are many fans who travel from outside the prefecture and abroad, fascinated by not only the ingredients Kyushu has to offer, but also the food Chef Konishi creates.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Exit 1 of Akasaka Station on Fukuoka City Subway Airport Line

244405.longDescription:
A 10-minute walk from JR Kokura Station in Kitakyushu, "Saint-Emilion" is a hideaway restaurant tucked away in a quiet location, one street away from the main road. The name "Saint-Emilion" is borrowed from the name a small hilltop town in south-west France that is celebrated for its famous wineries.

Chef Iichiro Watanabe traveled to France in 1995 and trained in famous restaurants in France and Italy such as Patrick Jeffroy in Brittany and Chateau Grande Barail in Bordeaux. After returning to Japan, he created a brilliant career for himself working at La Suite in Roppongi and as head chef at the Austrian Embassy. He went independent in 2007, opening "Saint-Emilion" in his hometown of Kokura, Fukuoka. In the desire to offer dishes that can only be experienced at "Saint-Emilion," Chef Watanabe is proactive about incorporating local ingredients and developing his menu. He spares no pains in incorporating ingredients that can only be sourced in the local area. For example, vegetables are delivered directly from farms working without agro-chemicals in Fukuoka, and water is sourced by visiting the famous spring of Ouma twice a week to collect natural water. Taking advantage of his geographical location in Kitakyushu, which is blessed with great seafood, Chef Watanabe works with each season’s best offerings of local seafood—tilefish from Tsunoshima, Yamaguchi in the spring; sea urchin from Aino Island in Kokura in the summer; and black throat seaperch from Iki, Nagasaki, in the fall, for example. He uses these to create seafood dishes that can be considered one of Saint-Emilion’s specialties.

In terms of cooking methods, Chef Watanabe places importance on fundamentals, keeping in mind the idea of learning new ideas based on a study of the past. On the other hand, it is not easy to recreate international cuisine exactly as it is, because he is mainly working with Japanese ingredients. For example, even with potatoes, those grown in France have different characteristics to those grown in Japan, and so dishes much be reconstructed based on the ingredients used, all the while making changes to the cooking method and incorporating the methods and philosophy of Japanese cuisine, to some extent. Even though he may use the traditional Japanese technique of seasoning ingredients by soaking them in stock, with his experience and marvelous skills, Chef Watanabe will turn these ingredients into dishes of outstanding French cuisine. Guests can enjoy a perfect pairing of wine and food, with Saint-Emilion's selection of some 100 varieties of wine, mostly produced in France.

We welcome you to a restaurant with a subdued atmosphere, a warm space decorated here and there with ikebana of seasonal flowers. Seating is available in tables for two, four, or six patrons. "Saint-Emilion" is a spot you will want to visit in each season of the year so as to enjoy dishes unique to this restaurant and this region.

245028.longDescription: Located on the second floor of Hakata Riverain near Nakasukawabata Station in Hakata, Fukuoka,where he creates fine French cuisine unique to his restaurant by showcasing the best flavors from local ingredients from his home region of Kyushu. Ingredients are carefully selected from some of the best local producers, such as ripened longtooth grouper from one of the three master fishermen in Fukuoka, and black figs from a producer in Saga who succeeded in growing the species in Japan. Vegetables are also selected with exquisite care, including Shiroishi lotus roots from Saga and Sadowara eggplants from Miyazaki. In addition, sustainable ingredients with their own stories to tell are incorporated into the dishes served at the restaurant. Citrus fruits are featured on many of the menu choices, taking advantage of Restaurant Hiramatsu Hakata’s deep knowledge of the many fruits grown in Kyushu. The ingredients are sourced not only from France and Kyushu, but also from around Europe and Japan, to offer the best-quality seasonal variety with the effect of helping diners feel as if they were traveling the world through cuisine. This adventure of flavors is complemented by wines selected from some 1,000 bottles stored in the restaurant’s cave. The interior is classic and modern. Guests can enjoy excellent food in an extraordinary setting adorned with flower vases by Émile Gallé and antique tables and furniture, whether dining in the main dining room at one of 10 tables, or in one of the private rooms (accommodating 2 to 30 people). While the restaurant is perfect for celebrating special anniversaries with loved ones, guests are also invited to enjoy exquisite food and service at Restaurant Hiramatsu Hakata for a wide variety of occasions. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.

244263.longDescription:
Teruzushi opened in Tobata-ku, Kitakyushu City in 1964. The second-generation owner developed Teruzushi, the city's sushi restaurant, into a large restaurant of the region, and now it is undergoing a major transformation under the third-generation owner, Takayoshi Watanabe. Watanabe became owner at the young age of 28, and is pursuing "a time that can only be had at Teruzushi" even as he carries on the tradition of Edo-sushi from his predecessors. This space, known as "sushi theater", gained popularity in the blink of an eye, and now draws many guests not only from within the country but from outside as well.

The special ingredients, purchased through Watanabe's passion and communication skills, are what creates the charm of Teruzushi. Acting as mediator with the fishermen, Watanabe has been able to develop a technique for keeping seafood fresh, with results like unbelievably fresh sea urchin, black abalone weighing over 600g, large tiger prawns, and other ingredients that you can't see anywhere else. In addition to that, Watanabe freely brings in other top-quality ingredients such as high-quality tuna from Tsukiji and grouper airlifted from the Goto Islands. The vinegar used for the sushi rice is specially made by Fukuoka's Shoubunsu Vinegar just for Teruzushi, which gently flows through the mouth and leaves a deep aftertaste. Teruzushi is also known for its bold, jaw-dropping performances. With its eel burgers, which have become synonymous with Teruzushi, and cooking skills displayed in front of you, this restaurant draws guests in with its atmosphere of a production.

"I want to create an environment where the fishermen and those who produce the ingredients profit from the fame of the restaurant", says Watanabe. With ingredients that come with a story and dishes that stimulate the five senses, Teruzushi has captured the hearts of gourmands around the world.

244544.longDescription:
"Oryori Furukawa" is located not far from Hakata- Tenjin area in Fukuoka, perhaps the most lively downtown areas on the whole island of Kyushu. The owner-chef, Makoto Furukawa is originally from Fukuoka and has accumulated considerable culinary experience from 13 years working at the famous Japanese cuisine restaurant "Aji Kitcho" in Osaka. He refined his skills for a further four years at a restaurant back in Fukuoka, before opening his own in 2018. 

Talking about his culinary craft, Chef Furukawa explains, "I keep the classic Kaiseki cuisine that I was taught at the core of what I do, but I like to explore ways of presenting dishes that are possible thanks to being located in Fukuoka." Chef Furukawa is not only prodigious in his use of the finest local ingredients, such as seasonal produce sourced from Yanagibashi Market, but also in his use of local crafts at the restaurant, such as Arita-ware porcelain, woven Hakata-ori fabrics, decorative Okawa fretwork, Kurume lacquered baskets, and Hakata circular boxes. He aims to develop a restaurant that promotes the culture of traditional crafts, not just in Fukuoka but all of Kyushu, and the thoughts of the craftspeople through food. One of the culinary delights, that appears in the progression of dishes served as part of a multi-course meal, is the "Hassun," an assortment bite-sized delicacies arranged on a plate. Ever since his day's training at "Aji Kitcho," Chef Furukawa has enjoyed assembling these visually pleasing dishes, as much a feast for the eyes as for the palate. Dashi stock is very important in Japanese cuisine, and at "Oryori Furukawa" it is no exception; Chef Furukawa prepares his stock using top grade kelp from Shirakuchihama, Hokkaido, that he procures from a specialist kelp store in Osaka, and bonito flakes from Makurazaki. The final dish of rice served in an earthenware pot at the end of a meal is prepared using rice that Furukawa grows at home in Dazaifu, and he cooks it fresh for each and every customer. This level of attention to detail and the quality of the carefully selected ingredients really shine through in the food. Chef Furukawa usually has over 18 varieties of seasonal Japanese sake on offer, all of which perfectly match his cooking, and are instilled with the thoughts of the brewers.

"Oryori Furukawa" has a pure, Japanese-style interior, evoked by the beautiful counter made from single piece of cherry wood, made by Moriyama-Meiboku in Fukuoka. Chef Furukawa wanted to create an atmosphere that was not too formal, in which he could enjoy being together with his customers, and so he achieved a design with a real sense of presence, where the charcoal grill is visible across the counter. There are 6 seats at the counter and a further 2 private rooms, and children are welcome. Chef Furukawa always does his best to satisfy customer requests, whatever the occasion. Therefore customers can relax and enjoy the attentive entertaining characteristic of a Japanese dining experience while being wowed by the exceptional food and absorbing the local culture.

244973.longDescription: Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Fukuoka is located inside the five-star Grand Hyatt Fukuoka, just 15 minutes by car from Fukuoka Airport and a 10-minute walk from Hakata Station. The restaurant serves USDA Prime beef — the highest grade awarded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, certified for only about three percent of all beef — prepared with uncompromising cooking techniques. Founded in New York in 2004 by Wolfgang Zwiener, Wolfgang’s Steakhouse opened its Fukuoka branch, the fourth location in Japan, in 2016. Today, the brand continues to attract devoted fans not only across Japan, but also in China, Hong Kong, the Philippines, Singapore, and other parts of the world. The hallmark of Wolfgang’s Steakhouse is its dedicated dry-aging process. Carefully selected prime cuts are aged for 28 days at strictly controlled temperatures and humidity levels. This long aging deepens flavor and enhances tenderness. The meat is then seared in a 900°C broiler, creating a crisp, aromatic crust that contrasts beautifully with its soft, juicy interior — resulting in an exceptional steak unlike any other. The most popular cut is the Prime Steak (T-bone steak), which allows diners to enjoy two distinct textures at once: the richly marbled and flavorful sirloin, and the tender, lighter fillet. For seasoning, guests may enjoy the restaurant’s original sauces, simple salt and pepper, or classic steakhouse side dishes such as mashed potatoes and creamed spinach, both of which pair wonderfully with the meat and can even serve as alternative sauces. The glass-enclosed walk-in wine cellar houses more than 1,000 bottles from around the world, allowing guests to savor the exquisite pairing of fine steak and wine to their heart’s content. The refined, classic interior features 98 table seats, 9 bar counter seats, and private dining accommodating up to 24 guests. With its generously spaced seating and attentive service, the elegant atmosphere is ideal for business lunches. As the only Wolfgang’s Steakhouse in Kyushu, the Fukuoka branch is perfect for a variety of occasions — from leisure and business trips to gatherings with friends, colleagues, or romantic evenings. The finest steaks promise to provide an experience that satisfies both body and soul. 〈Group Restaurant Information〉 Wolfgang's Steakhouse Signature Aoyama Wolfgang's Steakhouse Roppongi Wolfgang's Steakhouse Osaka Wolfgang’s Steakhouse TEPPAN Wolfgang's Steakhouse Marunouchi Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa

Enjoy a savory plate featuring mini burgers made with America’s highest-quality USDA Prime dry-aged beef, roast beef sandwiches, and other popular items from our restaurant, along with a two-tiered cake stand showcasing six varieties of our house-made desserts.

A ten-minute taxi ride from Hakata Station, the gateway to Kyushu, brings you to a quiet residential neighborhood where a small illuminated sign reading “Kyodo Ryori Tsugumi” marks the restaurant’s presence. The modern entrance, set against a gray wall, offers a calm introduction to the experience inside.
Kyushu is a region blessed with outstanding ingredients in every season. Inspired by encounters with local producers, the restaurant was named Tsugumi with the intention of cooking in a way that moves beyond conventional boundaries of Japanese cuisine while remaining rooted in the land. The name reflects a desire to carry forward the flavors and character of Kyushu through each dish.

The cuisine is built around ingredients sourced from Fukuoka and across Kyushu, with menus that vary widely in composition and technique depending on the season. A signature course available year-round is dedicated entirely to longtooth grouper. Large specimens caught in the waters from the Genkai Sea to Nagasaki are purchased alive at port, rested in tanks to regain strength, and then prepared with care. According to the time of year, the fish is served as sashimi, grilled, deep-fried, or in shabu-shabu, allowing its qualities to be appreciated through different preparations.
From January through March, the restaurant offers a natural tiger pufferfish course using large fish of around five kilograms, sourced from Haedomari Fishing Port in Shimonoseki, a well-known producing area. The size of the fish brings a depth of flavor and texture that can be fully enjoyed. From April through December, courses featuring seasonal ingredients from northern Kyushu are also available, including wild eel from the Ariake Sea, red sea urchin, and net-caught wild duck, highlighting ingredients that reflect both season and place.

Champagne is offered by the glass, while wines are served by the bottle, including selections from Kyushu producers such as Kikuka Winery in Kumamoto and Ajimu Budoshu Kobo in Ajimu, Oita. Japanese sake focuses primarily on Kyushu, with six to seven seasonal selections, alongside shochu from Miyazaki, Kumamoto, and Kagoshima. Non-alcoholic options include locally sourced teas such as Yame tea. The experience is further enriched by the use of fine ceramics from renowned kilns including Arita, Imari, and Karatsu.

The interior features a modern design with eight counter seats. From any seat, guests can enjoy watching each dish come together right before their eyes. At Kyodo Ryori Tsugumi, guests are invited to spend a moment savoring Kyushu’s ingredients to their fullest.

*Please note that ingredients and menu content may change depending on weather conditions and availability.

245111.longDescription:
Praised for inventive food that combines classic Kyushu fare with a contemporary New Nordic approach, restaurant Snow can be found in Fukuoka City, the gateway of Kyushu. A ten-minute drive from Hakata Station brings guests to the restaurant, located on the first floor of a building in the residential area adjacent to Tenjin, the busiest and largest downtown in Hakata. The restaurant is also seven to eight minutes’ walk from Yakuin and Watanabe-dori Stations on the Fukuoka City Subway Line.

The restaurant is helmed by chef Genki Unno, who was born in 1984 in Fukuoka Prefecture. After graduating from culinary school, he trained at renowned restaurants, including a restaurant of the three-star chef Michel Guérard in France, Barbizon in Belgium, and Søllerød Kro in Denmark. Then, he returned to Japan and opened his own restaurant in his hometown of Fukuoka, in July 2020.

Taking inspiration from the traditional dishes of Kyushu, chef Unno has created a unique cuisine that combines Kyushu’s traditions with French and New Nordic influences. For him, Kyushu’s seven prefectures, each with their own unique food culture, is not only his birthplace but also a great source of inspiration.

The cuisine reinterpreted by chef Unno reveals fascinating aspects of the local food culture, including forgotten recipes and a dessert enjoyed as a kind of soul food by locals in Northern Kyushu. Most of his dishes highlight local ingredients. He also purchases domestic wines and cheese from local producers in Kyushu.

Meanwhile, most of the wines paired with dishes of the chef’s choice are imported from France. The wine list also includes natural wines as well as domestic wines, all sourced from Kyushu. In addition, the restaurant offers a choice of three drinks pairings, which can be increased or reduced depending on the guest’s preference. The non-alcoholic drink menu includes four beverages that feature fruits from Kyushu.

With a five-seat counter, a three-seat semicircle counter, and a six-seat table, Restaurant Snow is the perfect place to dine with friends, loved ones, or fellow food lovers. Children of any age are welcomed to the restaurant during lunchtime or when it is booked for exclusive use (available only to groups of six guests or more). Non-Japanese speaking guests are also welcomed by chef Unno, who is fluent in English and French.

The restaurant features exposed concrete walls with wood, glass, and ceramic accents in warm shades to contrast with the vivid colors of chef Unno’s inventive dishes. The large Nordic-inspired pendant lights that hang from the ceiling, as well as wooden butter knives, are produced by a furniture maker from Okawa City, Fukuoka Prefecture, which is famed for its furniture craftsmen. The table is set with Koishiwara dishware and napkins made of Kokura-ori fabric. Thus, Restaurant Snow also showcases the splendor of Kyushu not only through recipes but also through the tiniest design details.

Restaurant Snow is perfect for international guests to discover the bounty of the area, while allowing locals to rediscover their home region.

244433.longDescription:
For customers who would like to reserve this restaurant, please join the waiting list system. We will send you an email when there is vacancy. 
Located a 2-minute walk from Hanabatacho station on the Kumamoto City Tram line, at the end of a basement hallway in a building filled with restaurants and bars, tucked away like a hideout, is “Sushi Senpachi"". The owner-chef, Takashi Nakahara, was born into a family of sushi chefs that spans four generations, and he himself decided on a career in cuisine as well. After honing his skills at famous sushi restaurants such as Fukuoka’s world gourmet guide award “Tokimune,” and the 1-star “Sushi Shin” in Nishi Azabu in Tokyo, he set off on his own at age 28 and opened “Sushi Sempachi” in his native Kumamoto. In the world gourmet guide Kumamoto edition, he earned award in July 2018.

Mr.Nakahara begins the reception of his diners from the selection of ingredients. Traveling to the Tasaki Market – known as “Kumamoto’s kitchen” – he selects seafood not by region or brand, but with his eye for quality, and takes his time to prepare them carefully and precisely. While such natural ingredients are often at the mercy of the seasons and the weather, Nakahara serves several specialties which diners should feel fortunate to be served. While the oval squid is outstandingly fresh, as are all the other seasonal sushi dishes, “Sushi Sempachi” is highly acclaimed for its creative and original lineup of “Tsumami (hors-d'oeuvres)”. Here, you will encounter dishes that, once eaten, you will never forget – such as nigiri (sushi topped with seafood) of smoked tuna head seasoned with soy sauce, or a creamy and thick abalone risotto made with abalone liver and vinegared rice. Alcoholic beverage offerings are mainly Japanese sake, which includes sakes from Kyoto (which Mr. Nakahara fell in love with when he trained in that city), as well as sakes from his native Kumamoto, created by up-and-coming brewers, with such brands carefully selected to pair perfectly with seafood and sushi.

Mr. Nakahara has always prioritized seafood from Kumamoto and Kyushu and paired the skills in Edomae-sushi he acquired during his training to create sushi that is unique to this region. His philosophy is “to preserve that which must be preserved, but to break through barriers which must be broken,” and those words continue to guide the evolution of “Sushi Sempachi"". The restaurant seats 12 at the counter and has a private room which seats 4. It is perfect not only for entertaining clients or special meals but also for family get-togethers and even dates, making this restaurant appropriate for a wide range of situations. “Sushi Sempachi” enjoys the patronage of many regulars who have been mesmerized by its cuisine, and often visit daily. It must be exciting to imagine what kind of sushi the chef may recommend today.

244316.longDescription:
Kaiseki cuisine that can only be crafted in Kyushu. With 30 years of experience, this restaurant combines the bounty of Kyushu's seafood and meat with carefully selected ingredients from all over Japan to create perfect dishes. The beverage menu features 20 carefully selected premium selections that can be enjoyed in conjunction with the cuisine. The dashi, a cornerstone of the menu, is made with Japan's finest soft water, katsuo-bushi, and kombu from Rishiri Island to achieve a harmonious balance. Here, you can immerse yourself in a holistic experience where cuisine, ambiance and scenery come together seamlessly. This is one of the rare two-star establishments in Fukuoka.

The owner, Akira Nakamura, trained at restaurants in Kikusuiro and Unoan in Nara Prefecture for 7 years after graduating from Tsuji Culinary School, then he returned to his hometown in north Kyushu. In order to understand more about the local ingredients, he worked in a fishery's wholesale market for one year and then at a fresh fish marketplace for two years. With a different viewpoint from that of a chef, he discovered a way of handling and purchasing seafood. In 2002, he opened Chisou Nakamura in north Kyushu at the age of 30.

The current restaurant was designed by Akira Sugihara, an architect from Kyoto, and when you enter from the stone path at the entrance, you feel a reminiscence of a Kyoto teahouse. It is an authentic Sukiya-style building (tea ceremony house), which beautifully expresses the restaurant's concept of "a house in the mountains made in the city".

The landlady presents each guest with a hand-written menu at the beginning of the course. An English hand-written menu is provided for guests from overseas. The meal starts with a seasonal appetizer, followed by a bowl dish harmonizing dashi and seasonal ingredients, and a visually stunning hassun platter. The course continues with freshly cooked rice prepared in a traditional kamado, concluding with matcha tea. Rather than featuring one standout dish, every element of the meal is meticulously balanced at the highest level, embodying Chef Nakamura’s vision of ideal kaiseki cuisine. And he expresses everything about Japanese cuisine with the menu and interior decorations that change every month.

The restaurant accommodates just 14 guests, with seven counter seats and two private rooms. It is a distinguished establishment that not only showcases the depth of kaiseki cuisine but also rekindles appreciation for Japanese traditions and culture, including seasonal festivals and customs that are often overlooked in modern times.
nearestStations: 8-minute walk from Exit 7 of Nakasu-Kawabata Station on the Fukuoka city subway Kūkō Line

244494.longDescription:
Bekk stands with a small sign in a quiet area off the main street in Kokura, Fukuoka. Owner-chef Koji Suganuma gained experience in Italian cuisine in Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, and Kyoto, and opened the restaurant in 2012 in his hometown of Kokura, Fukuoka. Since its opening, the restaurant has been listed in international gourmet guides as "Bisteria Bekk" based on the concept of a casual Italian restaurant, but in November 2022, 10 years after its opening, the restaurant reopened under the new name "Bekk. The restaurant was renamed Bekk and reopened in November 2022, 10 years after its opening.

Chef Suganuma says, The course is characterized by the "four seasons of Kyushu" and the "thoughts of the producers". The courses are composed mainly of ingredients purchased from producers in Kyushu, using "ingredients that are gentle to the body and mind" grown in their natural environment. Vegetables are grown using native and fixed varieties grown in a natural environment with no pesticides or fertilizers, meat is Yazaki beef from Kagamiyama Farm, known for its naturally pastured Japanese black beef, and seafood is carefully selected from trusted producers, mainly wild caught in the seas around Kyushu. The restaurant is also particular about pasta dishes, which was the starting point for Mr. Suganuma's Italian cuisine. Chef Suganuma says, "We offer two types of pasta in each course so that our customers can enjoy a different flavor each time they visit.The chef offers a wide variety of pasta dishes, including handmade pasta, wrapped pasta, long pasta, and short pasta, all with his own unique flair.

The wine, one of the restaurant's specialties, is mainly Italian wines, and a variety of aperitifs and after-dinner drinks are available, offering pairing suggestions according to customers' tastes and dishes. The restaurant's interior can be used for a variety of situations, from anniversaries and celebrations to casual everyday dining, with counter seating with a sense of presence and table seating that can be enjoyed in a private space.

For those who are interested in food and those who genuinely love to eat, we hope you will enjoy the "flavors of the four seasons" that can only be experienced in Kyushu, and the "thoughts of the producers" that can be felt through chef Suganuma.

■Please call the restaurant if you wish to order lunch.
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Tangae Station on the Kitakyushu Monorail

244499.longDescription:
"Sushi Tsubasa" is an intimate sushi restaurant consisting of just 8 counter seats, located in Kitakyushu right by Heiwadori Station, and just an 8-minute walk from Kokura Station. Set foot in the restaurant and the bustle of the shopping arcade outside immediately melts away as you enter an entirely different world where a calm and refreshing atmosphere hangs in the air. The tea house-style interior of the restaurant employs plenty of Yoshino cedar in its design, and the counter itself is made from a single board of ginkgo wood. The owner-chef, Tsubasa Otan carried out the interior design together with a carpenter of tea houses who trained in Kyoto. Together they have managed to execute a consummate design that, while elaborate, leaves a sober and refined impression overall. The interior plays a key supporting role in showing off the gorgeous sushi and other dishes served at the restaurant.

Originally opened in 2012, "Sushi Tsubasa" moved to its present location in 2016. Chef Otan explains the reason behind the move was because the restaurant was a bit out of town, and he wanted to make it easier for people to visit. Another reason might be because it brings him back closer to "Morita," the sushi restaurant where he trained for 8 years, and Otan still stays in touch with his master. Both "Morita" and "Tenzushi," where the chef of "Morita" trained, are leading restaurants for Kokura-sushi. "Sushi Tsubasa" follows on in that lineage, serving 4-5 small dishes first before moving on to the nigiri sushi, in a style typical to the region's sushi restaurants. Amongst the dishes served, the decoratively sliced squid is synonymous with Kokura-sushi. Furthermore, the chef's selection courses feature fish caught in the deep seas off Yamaguchi, such as grunt, as the main dish.

Alcoholic beverages at "Sushi Tsubasa" are centered around Japanese sake that has a clean, crisp, and dry flavor. In addition to staples such as Daishichi from Fukushima, and Shimeharitsuru and Tsurunotomo from Niigata, Tsubasa also stocks seasonal and local sake, and usually has around 30 varieties available. Whether it is wine, shochu, highballs, or plum wine, Chef Otan's policy is to serve drinks that suit sushi. The hope that customers who have simply come to enjoy some sushi will go home a little more knowledgeable about sushi in Kitakyushu is an idea that is catching hold not only among the locals, but also sushi lovers from other regions, including overseas. Every piece of sushi at "Sushi Tsubasa" contains hidden things designed to delight and provide new discoveries with each and every bite. It is worth a visit even if you are coming from afar.
nearestStations: An 8-minute walk from Kokura Station(JR Nippou Honsen)

244704.longDescription:
Away from the center of Tenjin, one of the most popular downtown areas in Fukuoka "Ura Tenjin Street," there are many long-established stores. Located at a street with a Showa atmosphere is Kappou Murakawa. The owner Koji Murakawa under the influence of his father, who is a Japanese cuisine chef, and decided to become a chef when he was an elementary school student. After graduating from the cooking school, he trained at the Tokyo branch of Kikunoi, a famous restaurant in Kyoto, and then he brushed up at the world gourmet guide award Gensai in Kobe and sushi restaurant. He became independent in his hometown Fukuoka in June 2016.

The concept is "Japanese sake and seasonal dishes." They serve seasonal Kaiseki courses and daily à la carte dishes made with Kyushu ingredients and sake. The particular fish is the seafood that is caught in the Kyushu area such as Genkai, Oita and Nagasaki that is purchased directly from the market every morning. They serve the fresh fish like the natural white fish with sashimi, bowls and grilled dishes to enjoy the seasonal flavor. In addition, high quality meat from Kyushu such as Saga beef and Hanamidori Akadori chicken from Fukuoka are carefully selected. Underpinning the flavor of these carefully selected ingredients is the best stock from "Tennen Dounansan Itto Makonbu" (kelp) and "dried bonito flakes". The meticulous work shows the delicate skills of the famous shop. The other specialty is the local sake that is directly purchased from the local brewery. They also have sake that is recommended for each season. The pairing that is unique to local production for local consumption is also special.

There are 8 counter seats and a private room (6 people) in the space where you can feel the warmth of the wood like the counter top plate with a single plate of Katsura. The bamboo chopsticks used were also made by owner-chef Murakawa's father. The cheerful atmosphere of the owner and the landlady is full of warm hospitality. The restaurant is mainly for calm guests and has an atmosphere where even a single guest can relax, so please use it not only for daily use but also for various occasions such as dining together, anniversaries and business entertainment.

244496.longDescription:
Ischia, an island in the Gulf of Naples, is said to be the birthplace of pizza. A resort spot famous for its hot springs, the island is home to a 3-generation Neapolitan pizzeria, "Pizzeria Da Gaetano." The only pizzeria in the world allowed to adopt the same name is located in Fukuoka.

The owner-chef Tomohide "Tommy" Shitama moved to Italy in 2004, where he studied under expert pizza chef Gaetano Fazio for 6 years. He obtained permission from Gaetano to establish his own branch of the original "Pizzeria Da Gaetano" and set up shop in his native Fukuoka in 2011. He wanted to share the fun of Neapolitan pizza and pizzerias with people in Kyushu, aiming to create a restaurant with a Neapolitan atmosphere where young and old alike could discover how fun it is to visit a pizzeria.

Of the range of pizzas on offer, one we would like to particularly recommend is the "Pizza Gaetano," which is topped with rocket and smoked cheese. This unique specialty is only available at "Pizzeria Da Gaetano." The pizzeria welcomes many patrons from outside Fukuoka, and it offers a range of items made using local ingredients, including Fukuoka grown Neopolitan vegetables and Kyushu fish and meat. There is wine from all parts of Italy, but we recommend trying Ischian liqueur Rucolino. In order to share Ischian food culture with the world, "Pizzeria Da Gaetano" became the first business to import this rare liqueur. While it is traditionally enjoyed after a meal, Pizzeria Da Gaetano also offers Rucolino with soda or over ice cream as an affogato style dessert.

Everything from the pizza oven in the back of the kitchen to the Ischian ceramics and pots and the books and decorations adorning the restaurant interior is made in Italy. There are 48 seats, and the heat that flows out onto the street is evidence of the restaurant's popularity. It was included in a selection of the world's top 70 pizza restaurants published by an Italian restaurant magazine this year and is one of the most authentically Italian pizzerias in Japan.

245234.longDescription: The Yakuin area, a 6-minute walk from Yakuin-odori Station on the Fukuoka City Subway, or a 10-minute drive from Hakata Station, is a quiet residential area with many trendy stores. One street over from Josui-dori, Imoto's is tucked away behind a white noren curtain with the name of the restaurant dyed around it. Head Chef Tatsuya Imoto was born in 1986. After graduating from a culinary school in his hometown of Fukuoka, he trained at a Japanese restaurant in Kyoto for seven years. In 2015, at the age of 29, he opened Imoto, and five years later, the restaurant was awarded two stars in a global gourmet guide book. What Chef Imoto values most in his cooking is the "dashi" (soup stock) made from Rishiri konbu (kelp). As dashi is the beginning of everything, he uses ichiban dashi (first stock) in all of his dishes. Ichiban dashi is also used in the mixed stewed vegetables. Dried bonito and tuna flakes are not steamed, but shaved to retain their aroma and flavor. He also uses natural spring water from Aso. It is soft and helps bring out the flavor of konbu. For ingredients, he asks suppliers he has known since his apprentice days in Kyoto, as well as trusted local suppliers in Fukuoka, to create courses with a balance of seasonal fish and vegetables. For example, in the summer, eel and pike conger are featured. The intention is to make the best use of the ingredients and create a dish that one never tires of eating. The sake list features about 15 kinds from all over Japan. Sake is served according to the guest's preference and the cuisine of the moment and includes local Fukuoka varieties as well as Chef Imoto's favorite label. Many guests enjoy a variety of brands, one glass at a time. There is also a wide selection of wines, mainly reds and whites from Burgundy, as well as eight kinds of Champagne. The restaurant has only 11 seats at a neat L-shaped counter that makes the most of the warmth of the wood, and every seat offers a perfect view of Imoto's skills on display right in front of you. The bowls are all Wajima-nuri lacquerware, the tableware is mainly Kyo-yaki and blue-and-white and Nankin Akae porcelain and other antiques, and the glassware is from Baccarat and Lalique. Imoto's sense of aesthetics can also be felt in the vessels used to serve the dishes. The restaurant does not disappoint when it comes to family gatherings, anniversaries, intimate dinners, and entertaining important guests. Visitors from outside of the prefecture also can't miss the convenience of access, considering how close it is to Hakata Station by car. Imoto says he wants guests relax with food and sake, and talk with them about the tableware and drinks. Such warm hospitality will surely make your time at Imoto unforgettable. ■About the Cruise Train “Seven Stars in Kyushu” The “Seven Stars in Kyushu,” Japan’s first luxury sleeper train, offers an exclusive journey around various parts of Kyushu. The train itself serves as a luxurious hotel on wheels, where passengers can fully enjoy the charm of Kyushu through exquisite dishes prepared onboard using carefully selected ingredients from the regions along the route. Some of these dishes are supervised by our restaurant. Each delicately crafted plate, designed to bring out the natural flavors of the ingredients, adds richness to your travel experience even while in transit. For more information, please click here for details.

245435.longDescription:
A 15-minute drive from Koriyama Station on the JR Tohoku Shinkansen line or a five- to six-minute walk from Koriyama Tomita Station on the JR Banetsusai Line will take you to Rantei Bibian, which is located in a residential area in Koriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture.
 Helmed by Chef Isao Igarashi, this Japanese kappo restaurant features local ingredients from Fukushima, which is known as a treasure trove of food, and its neighboring prefectures that are blessed with bountiful harvests from the land and sea.
　
Hailing from Sukagawa City, Fukushima Prefecture, Chef Igarashi was born to a family of chefs. After graduating from university, he apprenticed at Gion Kawakami in Kyoto and then took over his family’s restaurant, Kamebachi, as the fourth-generation owner-chef. In 1981, he opened a new restaurant, Kappo Rantei, in front of Koriyama Station (The restaurant relocated to the Namiki District and was renamed Namiki Rantei in 1991).  He then opened another restaurant, Rantei Bibian, in 2004.

The prix-fixe menu, usually consisting of seven courses, including an appetizer, rice, and dessert, features seasonal ingredients, which are all selected with care and prepared with passion. The autumn prix-fixe meal, “Asadori Matsutake Zanmai,” invites guests to discover the savory flavors of matsutake mushrooms, which are freshly picked in the morning from Fukushima, Iwate, and Aomori and prepared in various ways, such as charcoal grilling and sukiyaki, while the winter prix-fixe meal, “Ikejime Tennen Torafugu,” features seasonal wild pufferfish prepared using the ikejime technique. These seasonal full course menus are the true specialties of Rantei Bibian. Each meal includes different varieties of local rice from Fukushima, which is also known as the best rice-producing prefecture in the Tohoku Region, including “Fuku, Warai” and “Tennotsubu” from Aizu, Fukushima. Notably, “Truffle Rice,” which features Japanese-grown truffles picked in autumn, pairs well with local soy sauce aged in wooden barrels and free-range eggs. The nigiri sushi offered on an irregular basis is called “Ranteimae” and tempts quite a few guests to book counter seats to witness the delicacies conjured up by Chef Igarashi right in front of them.

The drink menu offers a curated selection of Japanese sake and shochu, mainly from Fukushima, such as Tenmei from Aizu Bange, Sasanokawa from Sasanokawa Shuzo, a sake brewery in Koriyama that also distills shochu and whiskey, Niidashizenshu from Niida Honke, and Nekka rice shochu made from rice grown in Aizu-Tadami, as well as a wide variety of non-alcoholic options, such as original herbal tea.

While the exterior of the restaurant is stylish in black tone, the interior behind the noren curtains is designed in a modern Japanese style to create a cozy, relaxing vibe. With a main dining room with a counter that seats between two and four guests and three private dining rooms, either with a dining table and chairs or with a low horigotatsu table, the restaurant is the perfect place for intimate meals with your family, date, friends, coworkers, or international guests. Come and discover the charm of Fukushima at Rantei Bibian!
nearestStations: 5 min. walk from Tomita Sta. on the Ban-Etsu-Nishi Line via Koriyama Sta. on the Tohoku Honsen.

244426.longDescription:
Located 10 minutes by car from Iwaki station, nestled atop a low hill in a residential area of south-east Fukushima, HAGI is a tiny home-turned-restaurant with an outsize reputation. The cozy restaurant is in fact the chef's own home.

The owner-chef Harutomo Hagi is a renowned far and wide, having been invited personally to Europe to cook for a group including the French President and the Prince of Monaco in 2013. The following year, he was one of 7 recipients awarded the bronze in the fifth rendition of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries sponsored ""Cuisine Masters", which seeks to honor outstanding chefs.

HAGI offers only a chef's course; chef Hagi personally sources his ingredients from contacts across Fukushima, and constructs a unique course to showcase their beauty every day. He proudly represents the locale, which with fruitful landscape offers ample and quality produce, seafood, and meats. His herbs and greens are worth special mention, as he obtains the best of the morning's harvest every day directly from neighboring farmers; sometimes, it is through his daily interactions with his sources that he finds inspiration for new and fascinating recipes.

The wine and sake selection, a source for his well-regarded pairing menu, can be ordered a la carte from a single glass as well; given his attachment to home, perhaps it is only natural that guests are commonly delighted to find rare and prized local liquors not yet available on the open market.

The dining hall, placed adjacent to the kitchen, is reminiscent of home; the proximity and ability to watch chef Hagi prepare the courses makes for a cozy mood, as if you are at the home of a friend that happens to be a chef. If you look outside, the home garden is a further treat, enhancing the notion that you may be back in your own dining room. At this tiny outpost to which gourmet-lovers across Japan pilgrimage to, pay homage to chef Hagi's reputation, and enjoy the best of Fukushima in a fun and relaxing meal!
nearestStations: 10-minutes by car from Iwaki Station (JR Joban Line)

地産地消に拘った料理は、マスターの技術と薪によって、更に素晴らしい料理となります。
その季節により、一番美味しい物を出してくれるのは、季節を感じられない今、とても大事なことと思います。
ワインや日本酒とのペアリングは、素晴らしいラインナップで、セラーの方にも素晴らしいワインを所蔵しているのに、地産地消を心掛けている感じが、とても好印象でした。

シンプルでワイルドな調理法を、一流の料理を学んだシェフが本気で取り組むという、全く他にない独自のレストランだと思う。

全料理美味しく頂きました。次に何が出てくるのか、ワクワクして楽しみというのは、久しぶりです。
フレンチのフルコースでよくあるのが、メインにたどり着くころのは、お腹いっぱいで、食べきれない、
最後は食いしごき状態になることですが、今回は全員がデザートまで完食出来ました。味が変化に富んで飽きさせない、美味しいものをちょっとずつで、ヴォリュームも絶妙だったと思います。

244815.longDescription:
A 7-minute walk from JR Ogaki Station in Ogaki City, Gifu Prefecture, 1-star Italian restaurant “CUCINA” is located quietly on the 1st floor of the building. Chef Terumichi Tanaka who was born and raised in Gifu, will show his skills.

Chef Tanaka entered a cooking school officially recognized by the Italian state of Piedmont to pursue his culinary career. After graduation, he began training at “Paulo e Barbara” in Sanremo, Italy, and then studied under Mr. Massimiliano Alajmo, chef of 3-star ristorante “Le Calandre” in Venice. After returning to Japan, he opened his own restaurant “CUCINA” in 2007. In 2008, he created a new style of "大垣リトルイタリアン" (Ogaki Little Italian) with the designer Yasumichi Morita, who is active both in Japan and overseas. In 2014, he entered the wedding market and worked as a grand chef at “THE GRAND TIARA GUEST HOUSE MONTRESOR” in Ogaki. In 2019, “CUCINA” became a popular 1-star restaurant.

At “CUCINA”, there is a casual a la carte menu arranged with local dishes, and an innovative Italian course where you can enjoy the unique combination of ingredients, that can make you laugh by stimulating your sixth sense. For example, "Roasted duck" is a surprising combination of French duck marinated in miso from Gifu's Gujo and Takayama city, adding a local flavor. "Orange and strawberry gelato" surprises the senses of sight and taste with its contrasting concept of orange-colored strawberries and red-colored oranges. In addition, there is a playful spirit in the arrangement of the presentation, as sea urchin dishes are served in a glass bowl shaped like a sea urchin shell, and egg dishes are served in a bowl shaped like an egg shell. There is various wine available from natural to vintage, with a wide range of drinks from classic to original drinks, such as smoked and spicy mixed cocktails.

“CUCINA” is located at a three-story structure with a casual counter Italian restaurant on the 1st floor, an elegant ristorante on the 2nd floor and a bar lounge on the 3rd floor. The interior was designed by designer Yasumichi Morita. The theme and atmosphere are different on each floor. You can enjoy various gastronomic experiences in various occasions, from private situations such as dining with family and friends or dating, to business situations such as welcoming overseas guests.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Ogaki Station (JR Tokaido Main Line (Gifu - Mino Akasaka/Maibara))

244649.longDescription:
A five-minute drive from JR Gifu Station, Takada Hassho is located in an administrative district in Gifu. It is a leading Japanese restaurant known for producing top chefs, including the head chefs from world gourmet guide award Seizan in Mita and Nishiasabu Otake. Here in the restaurant, Chef Haruyuki Takada—the dream mentor to many young chefs—presents his talents.
Chef Takada was born in Gifu Prefecture. He trained in Osaka for seven years before returning home. When he was appointed as the head chef of a leading Gifu Japanese restaurant, he made use of his past experiences in Osaka where he worked so hard that he sacrificed his sleep, and the result was doubling the restaurant's profits and improving its reputation. Seven years later, he became the head chef of the entire group. He succeeded in opening a new branch before he went independent. In 1989, he opened his Japanese restaurant, Takada Hassho. Due to his skill as a chef and his attentive care, Takada has often been asked to teach classes at cooking schools and accept apprentices. In order to reach out to more people, he expanded his restaurant group to five restaurants.
Chef Takada's motto is to always welcome new challenges. "Of course you can't go wrong with traditional cuisine; however, even though you might fail, it is important to challenge yourself and not get restricted with fixed concept. I create new things by combining my inspiration from young people's new perspectives and my years of experience." Chef Takada never stop improving, he adopted sous-vide cooking and low temperature cooking techniques early on. His cooking is also not bounded by the standard definition of Japanese cuisine. Because of his wide circle of acquaintances—which includes the leaders of several cooking associations and chefs active in various genres, from French to Chinese to Italian to Spanish, he is well versed in various genres of cuisine. His signature dishes include thinly shredded potato and raw nori seaweed chazuke. He offers a selection of sake consists of local Gifu offerings as well as some of the best sakes from around Japan, and top quality wines.
The restaurant welcomes guests with the warmth of the wood and seasonal scenery. Chef Takada regularly visits the head of the Urasenke school of tea ceremony in Kyoto to develop his senses. The restaurant has eight rooms of various sizes, including one annex. It accepts a group of up to 60 people and reservations for formal tea parties in the annex. This Japanese restaurant is perfect for family and friend gatherings, business dinners, or whenever you want to enjoy a special night out with a touch of luxury.

244599.longDescription:
"Kaikatei" is a Chinese restaurant located near the Yanagase shopping area in the government office quarters of Gifu City, Gifu Prefecture. This is where second-generation owner Takamichi Furuta, who has inherited the will of his father, practices his culinary skills. 

"Kaikatei" was originally opened by Takamichi's father, Hitoshi Furuta, in 1978. It soon attracted attention for its exquisitely original dishes that pushed the boundaries of Chinese cuisine and became well known both inside and outside of Japan. In 2014, Hitoshi Furuta decided that the time was ripe to open a new Chinese restaurant in Ginza, Tokyo. He named this restaurant "Furuta" after himself. He entrusted "Kaikatei" to his oldest son, Takamichi. His second son, Satoshi, opened a French restaurant called Restaurant "Satoshi.F." in Gifu. In 2016, Satoshi also moved to Ginza to open "CHIUnE", a highly popular restaurant that has drawn the attention of many gourmets. It seems that both sons inherited their father's culinary talent. 

When it comes to Kaikatei's dishes, Takamichi Furuta explains that "First, I imagine the most delicious way of eating whichever ingredient I'm working with, then I try to create that image." Rather than limiting himself to local produce, he also includes seafood from Hokkaido and western produce such as vegetables from France. The standard menu features cold rice noodles with caviar, shark fin with Shantung soup, and abalone liver with oyster sauce and Chinese white cabbage cream. In addition to the seasonal dishes inherited from his father, he continues to create his own specialties, including sweetfish spring rolls for summer and tofu using tiger pufferfish roe for winter. To complement the food, he keeps a selection of 6 types of Shaoxing wine, ranging from 5 to 30 years old, a wide range of wine from Champagne, California, Australia, France and Italy, as well as sake, shochu, whiskey, and beer, allowing him to flexibly respond to customer requests.

The restaurant features a modern béton brut exterior that foreign customers will be instantly familiar with. The first floor has 8 counter seats in front of the open kitchen. The second floor has table seats for a maximum of 16. Those who want to converse with the lively chef should head to the first floor, while those who want to entertain guests or celebrate anniversaries should head to the second. Both local regulars and foreign tourists agree that Chinese food at "Kaikatei" will not betray your expectations.

245322.longDescription:
A 15-minute drive from JR Takasaki Station in Takasaki City, Gunma Prefecture, Tempura Mokkosu sits in a quiet, lush residential neighborhood, helmed by Owner-Chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi.

Chef Yamaguchi trained at Tempura Shinjuku Tsunahachi, a long-established restaurant, for eight years and further honed his culinary skills at Keyaki Kurosawa, a Japanese restaurant renowned for its soba noodles and kappo cuisine, in Roppongi for two years. Then, in 2006, he opened his own restaurant, Tempura Mokkosu, in Takasaki City. The word “Mokkosu” in the restaurant’s name is derived from the dialect of his home prefecture of Kumamoto, where local stubborn men are called “Higo Mokkosu.” It reflects his commitment to being stubbornly obsessed with offering tasty tempura.
One of the obsessions is about the oil used for tempura. In order to prevent a heavy feeling in the stomach after eating, 100% Taihaku Sesame Oil (vegetable oil) is used to deep-fry tempura. The flour is a blend of Shiroganetsuru Flour, locally grown in Gunma, and Super Violet Flour. The water is sourced from Kamihira, famous for its mineral water, in the neighboring Fujioka City.
The fish and shellfish are supplied through Uoichi, a local broker in Takasaki City that goes to Toyosu Market every day for wholesale purchase. The vegetables are selected and directly purchased by the chef himself from local farms. Thus, all the ingredients of tempura are carefully selected by the chef, who says “I would like to get spinach with thick roots in winter so that guests can enjoy their flaky texture and natural sweetness.”
The prix-fixe (fixed-price) meal starts with appetizers, salad, and sashimi, followed by 10 pieces of tempura. The sashimi also includes raw horsemeat delivered fresh from the chef’s home prefecture of Kumamoto. It is served with soy sauce that is also delivered from Kumamoto. All the other pieces of sashimi are accompanied with additive-free homemade soy sauce pressed from moromi (fermenting mash used in the production of sake or soy sauce) aged for one year. The tempura is offered with tempura sauce and salt for guests to choose from. The salt is sourced from the Himalayas and freshly ground in front of guests.
The Sushi Tempura of Urchin, the signature of the restaurant, features one of the first five urchins of the day on the market, served on deep-fried sushi rice seasoned with red vinegar and wrapped with nori seaweed.
The sake list offers a variety of sake, mainly from Gunma and Kumamoto but also from around Japan. The wine list mainly features Champagne wines that go well with tempura. The list of wines by the bottle even includes Champagne Salon, a precious wine craved by wine lovers. Some Champagne wines are also available by the glass.

Marked by an owl motif created by a local artist, the restaurant has a large eye-catching air duct. The main dining room is furnished with a counter and eight chairs. There is also a private room (seating up to two to five guests) with a separate entrance. It is definitely worth visiting with your family, partner, friends, and coworkers. Please enjoy the seasonal bounty of Gunma here at Tempura Mokkosu.
nearestStations: 15 minutes by taxi from the east exit of Takasaki Station

244818.longDescription:
In Tatebayashi City in the southeastern part of Gunma Prefecture, a 15-minute walk from Tatebayashi Station on the Tobu Railway, is the famous “Sushi Obana” that attracts sushi fans from all over Japan. The restaurant is located in Otemachi, Tatebayashi City, a quiet residential area that retains the atmosphere of a castle town near the ruins of Tatebayashi Castle, which was once a key point toward Tohoku. The nearby castle pond with a circumference of 5km is popular as a place to relax with the azaleas of the adjacent "Tsutsujigaoka Park" in spring and the lotus flowers in summer.

Chef Terukuni Obana is from Gunma Prefecture. Since his father was a sushi chef, he went on to become a sushi chef. After studying in Tokyo, he returned to his local area, Tatebayashi, to take over his father's position. Later, he changed the name to the present “Sushi Obana”. Chef Obana's ability to select ingredients and to make sushi are the most distinctive features of “Sushi Obana”. Chef Obana will travel from Tatebayashi, where the restaurant is located, to Toyosu Market in Tokyo to purchase the ingredients. Regardless of the production area, he purchases the best fish of the time from a long-term trusted broker, and he has a reputation for his good judgment.

One of the most popular ingredients is the rare nigiri "salmon roe" that can only be found during the spawning season. The rich salmon roe that is emphasized by each grain goes well with vinegared rice made with fragrant red vinegar. The "Shrimp bowl" is a luxurious dish made with fresh meat mixed with a rich homemade sauce made from the shell and the soup stock taken from the head. You will be able to enjoy the charm of the taste of shrimp. There are about 30 kinds of Japanese sake for drinks. The local sake from Tatebayashi and other Japanese sake that goes well with the sushi, are selected by the proprietress, who is a kikizake-shi (sake sommelier). They also have a wide variety of champagne, wine, shochu and beer.

The restaurant features 9 counter seats made of Japanese cypress from Kiso that accentuates chef Obana's hand-shaped sushi, a semi-private room with a table for 4 and a private tatami room for 6. The counter is for junior high school students and older, and private rooms and tables are available for guests with children. Enjoy sushi with your close friends to your heart's content at “Sushi Obana”, which is filled with Mr. Obana's desire to let all guests enjoy the deliciousness and enjoyment of sushi.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Tatebayashi Station (Tobu Isesaki Line) (Within basic fare by taxi)
