245321.longDescription:
Located in a convenient place a 10-minute walk or a base-fare taxi ride from JR Takasaki Station, one of the hubs of the Northern Kanto’s transport system, FAN×DALCUORE sits in a tranquil residential area. Take a step into the restaurant, and you will find yourself in an extraordinary, modern space.

FAN×DALCUORE is helmed by two chefs, Hiroaki Hoshino and Nobutomo Suzuki. Chef Hoshino returned to Japan in 2020 after training at Din Tai Fung, a world-renowned Taiwanese restaurant famous for its soup dumplings, and serving as a chef at CHINESE FAN, a casual restaurant offering dim sum (a large range of small Chinese dishes) including soup dumplings, in Barcelona, Spain. He was reunited with Chef Suzuki, who worked as a chef at an Italian restaurant called Dalcuore, and together they opened the restaurant. To offer a rare combination of Chinese and Italian cuisine, the two chefs went through numerous instances of trial and error, such as incorporating Italian ingredients (e.g., tomatoes) into Shangtang (luxury soup made from meat and bones as an essential part of Cantonese and Taiwanese cuisine) before they created original dishes only available at FAN×DALCUORE.
As one of the specialties offered from June to September, the Confit of Sweetfish with Homemade Uruka Sauce and Fermented Tomato and Watermelon Sauce features wild sweetfish caught by Chef Hoshino, who is a sweetfish angler traveling around Japan when he is not occupied by work at the restaurant during the fishing season. While his fishing friends sell their catch to renowned restaurants in Tokyo, Chef Hoshino uses all his fish at his own restaurant. The homemade uruka (salted entrails and roe of sweetfish) is enriched with tomato to add an Italian flavor to the exclusive sauce of FAN×DALCUORE. In winter, the restaurant also offers Shanghai crab pasta and gratin, bringing a smile to every diner’s face.
The drink menu offers wines, mostly from Italy and France, to be paired with the dishes as well as Japanese sake locally brewed in Gunma. The paring menu includes both alcoholic and non-alcoholic (tea) options. The non-alcoholic drink menu mainly consists of organic Japanese green and smoked teas from the Tea Company.

In the modern, monotonous dining room dimly lit with indirect light to set a chic mood, there are two tables with four seats each. In addition, the restaurant has a private dining room seating up to six guests. This private dining room can be reserved for ordinary meals with children and infants. A special menu for pre-school children is available if asked for in advance.
FAN×DALCUORE is perfect for special occasions, such as wedding anniversary and birthday celebrations, as well as family gatherings, business dinners, and dates, but recently the reputation of the two chefs has also attracted an increasing number of food lovers. One thing for sure is that the fusion of Chinese and Italian cuisine only available at FAN×DALCUORE makes the restaurant worth a visit.
nearestStations: 10 minutes walk from the west exit of Takasaki Station

245433.longDescription:
CHILAN opened its doors in Hatsukaichi City, Hiroshima Prefecture, known as home to a world heritage site of Itsukushima Shrine. A 20-minute walk from JR Hiroshima Station and a six-minute walk from JR Ajina Station, the restaurant is situated on the ground floor, transformed from a detached house, on a residential hill that commands a fine view.

Chef Chilan Donguyen is born in Tokyo. Raised by Vietnamese parents in Japan, she set her mind on becoming a chef as a high school student. While working in the restaurant industry, she developed an interest in natural wines and got trained at wineries in Australia and New Zealand, where she learned the lifestyles and philosophies of producers who were confronting nature head-on.

“Human beings and their lives and deaths are part of nature. We cannot live without nature.” That is why she respects producers who continue fighting against the ruthless forces of nature, as well as their products and wines. In order to express her deep respect through dishes, she makes regular visits to those producers to get inspiration. In 2019, Chef Chilan moved to Hiroshima, the hometown of her husband, Sommelier Chiaki Fujii, to work more closely with producers while seeking a balance between work and child-rearing. They opened a restaurant, CHILAN, in 2020, and Chef Chilan made the list of finalists for RED U-35, a culinary competition for young chefs under 35, and won the Kishi Asako Award as the most promising female chef in 2021.
nearestStations: 6 minutes walk from JR Hiroshima Electric Railway Ajina Station

244714.longDescription:
A street south of Peace Boulevard that crosses the center of Hiroshima City. Chisou Sottakuito is a Japanese restaurant located in a corner of an area with famous French and sushi restaurants. When you open the door, the proprietress, Emika Ueda, and the chef, Hisama Hirano, welcome you gently.

In order to remain a high-level restaurant, Mr. Hirano continues to pursue deep and genuine ingredients. He does business with SASUE MAEDA Fish store from Yaizu City of Shizuoka Prefecture, which is popular among famous chefs of the world, due to his reliable judgment. Together with the Hiroshima Prefectural Central Wholesale Market "Yoshifumi", they search for a better method of exsanguination. The most important thing is dashi (soup stock). "In Hiroshima Prefecture, there is a world-famous soft spring water everywhere that brings out the flavor of kelp in soup stock. We want to entertain guests with "Dashi no Itteki" in Hiroshima, which has many visitors from home and abroad. I want to make a city where I can do that," chef Hirano said. They go to the spring water in Hiroshima every day and serve the best dashi that shines in the golden color taken from the vintage taste of Fukui prefecture "Okui Kaiseido", such as natural Rishiri kelp and natural Rausu kelp. When you eat the fish placed in front of you and smell the broth, you can immediately feel the difference in taste and flavor. If you try it along with chef Hirano's explanation of the ingredients and cooking, your palate will be enriched and you will be able to enjoy the meal more. The drinks are selected by the proprietress who is well versed in Japanese sake as she goes directly to the brewery. There are 10 - 12 kinds of local sake of the season purchased not only from Hiroshima but also from all over Japan. Considering the dishes served just before the meal, the restaurant would recommend the sake that goes best with the dish. Bottled beer, wine (5 - 6 kinds of red and white), shochu, and soft drinks are also available.

In the interior where you can feel the warmth of the wood, there are counter seats (9 seats) and private rooms (4 people). You can enjoy the real taste of Hiroshima at a leisurely pace at a dinner party with your family, friends, business guests and dates.


■ You cannot choose to be seated at counter or private room. Even if you make a reservation at the counter, we may take you to a private room depending on the reservation status on the day. Please make the reservation with this understanding.
nearestStations: A 8-minute walk from Chuden-mae Station (Hiroden Route 1 (Ujina Line))

244439.longDescription:
""hiroto"" is a French restaurant situated in the town of Fujimi, Hiroshima’s Jizo-dori street popularly known as the “adult’s fashion street.” It is the only world gourmet guide award restaurant of the Western-style restaurants in the Chugoku and Shikoku regions of Japan. After graduating from the Tsuji Culinary Institute, the owner and head chef, Yoshiyuki Hiroto, worked in Hiroshima and Tokyo restaurants prior to working as the sous-chef under Claude Bosi at the world gourmet guide awarded English restaurant, Hibiscus.

Yoshiyuki Hiroto’s style of meals involves small quantities of a large number of dishes, combining over 50 ingredients. Mr. Hiroto states, “This is simple cuisine with no excess, expressing only the flavors I want.” Bearing in mind the concept of “One plate = one dish,” he does not, for example, sprinkle on herbs that serve solely as decoration; only those that are indispensable components of the flavor of the dish. Using a wide variety of forms of ingredients such as purées, homemade flavored oils, charred garlic and hibiscus powder, he melds the five tastes, heat, aroma and mouthfeel on a single plate. For example, his tomato taste combines salted frozen yogurt, dry-cured ham from black Iberian pig, homemade ricotta, lemon basil, black pepper and basil oil into a presentation designed to combine all the flavors in a single mouthful. As the flavors of each of the ingredients combine to play an exquisite harmony within the mouth, diners will come to appreciate this unparalleled understanding of cuisine.

Our wine of the highest-class offerings of the Burgundy region, with over 2,000 bottles of 400 varieties in stock, from winemakers such as DRC and Armand Rousseau. The premium wine such as Meursault 1er Cru “Charmes,” Chassagne-Montrachet, Château Grand Puy Ducasse, and Pernand-Vergelesses are also offered as single glasses. The luxury extends to our interior, with our tables and bar made from single planks of pure Bubinga wood, our Kai Kristiansen No. 42 chairs, and tableware consisting of Limoges porcelain and Lobmeyr and Riedel Black Tie wine glasses, making us Hiroshima’s most perfectly coordinated restaurant.

244571.longDescription:
After heading west from the Hiroshima city center towards Miyajima, the world gourmet guide award French restaurant ""Le Jardin Gourmand"" appears out of the midst of a quiet residential area about 5-minute on foot from Furue Station. The restaurant stands alone surrounded by greenery, and Chef Kenichi Koyama and the restaurant's madame welcome customers as if into their own home.

Chef Koyama is originally from Hiroshima. After graduating from high school, he came across genuine French cuisine while working for his uncle at a restaurant in Fukuoka and was deeply moved by the experience. He then resolved to become a chef of French cuisine and moved to Europe in 1986. He began his training first at Hotel Penta in Swiss Geneva and Bern's Restaurant Pune. He then moved to France to work at ""l'Auberge"" de l'Eridan, owned by Marc Veyrat who had just obtained world gourmet guide award and was moving forward with good momentum. Afterward, Chef Koyama moved on to the location which would have a profound influence on his career, ""Le Jardin Gourmand"". In addition to French cooking techniques, he also learned everything from obtaining ingredients to purchasing wine at the giant market and a wide range of knowledge required for French cuisine from Pierre Bouzereau. He finally returned to Japan after serving for a time at the member's only hotel restaurant Saint James Club. To show respect to the original restaurant to which he was most indebted from his time training in Europe, he received permission to open a restaurant with the same name, and, in 1990 in his hometown of Hiroshima, he opened Japan's Le Jardin Gourmand. He now continues to fascinate the gourmands (gourmets) of the area as Hiroshima's leading world gourmet guide award French restaurant.

Chef Koyama's personal style is to use the classics as a base to create modern cuisine with his own unique essence. For example, if he should find any seasonable shoots sprouting up in his private vegetable garden which he tends to each morning, he begins to think how he might use that in his cuisine. It is a spontaneous style which seeks to find the joy in expressing the discovery of the day on a plate. He is particular about his ingredients, including pesticide-free white corn from Onan, Shimane; wild eels from Yoshinogawa; Miura Farm's Kuroge-Wagyu Beef from Akiota; shiitake mushrooms, citrus fruit, and soy sauce from Osakikamijima; Amakusa aka-uni; passion fruit from Niigata; and more, and brings them in from not only the local area but the whole country. Being deeply impressed by the passion the producers have for their ingredients, and in order to hold dear the connections he makes with those producers, any ingredient he uses once in the restaurant goes on to become a lasting staple in the cuisine of Le Jardin Gourmand. What's more, he stamps black pepper, roses, and other ingredients at Kure, Hiroshima's Seto Tekko to be used in his cuisine and is wholly devoted to his pursuit of the modern. He purchases his hand-picked wine selection using the methods he learned at restaurants in France and allows them to mature in the restaurant. These fine wine, stored in great condition in the wine cellar, each await their turn to appear in the restaurant in perfect drinking condition.

The dining area is an open space which also allows customers to gaze out on the private vegetable garden which runs from the gate to the restaurant's entrance. This Hiroshima' world gourmet guide award French restaurant provides a perfect spot for both dates and dinner parties with friends and family and is great for those who wish to dress up just a little more than usual and have an elegant experience.

244438.localizedAddress: TOHAKU Building, 10-4, Higashihakushimacho, Naka-ku, Hiroshima-shi, Hiroshima
244438.longDescription: 【 Important Notice Regarding Reservation Dates】 Available reservation dates are displayed with a gold circle as the seats available on the calendar. Please select your desired reservation date from those marked in gold. ※Dates shaded in gray are available for registration on the "Waiting List". Please refer to this page for information about the waiting list feature. Reservation time is only acceptable at 6:30 pm since it is simultaneous start. Note that this is only applicable if a seat becomes available on the specified date, in which case we will prioritize your reservation. A confirmation email will be sent upon reservation confirmation, but if you do not receive the email by the waiting deadline, please check your Reservations. It is only fitting that Kisetsu Ryori Nakashima, Hiroshima's only restaurant with world gourmet guide award, resides within the Hakushima district, an elegant and affluent residential neighborhood. Owner-chef Tetsuo Nakashima is an alumni of the Osaka Tsuji Culinary Institute, and began his career at a traditional Japanese restaurant in Osaka. Returning to his hometown to further hone his skills, he continued to excel at his craft until in 2006 he opened his own shop; ever since, he has gained nothing but love and adulation from fans around the world. ""I want each and every one of my guests to think; choosing 'Nakashima' was the right choice"" says our chef, who toils daily with his staff honing their mantra of ""delivering the finest food, in the finest mood, in order to create the joy and wonder of our guests"". This is the 'Nakashima'-style of service, and it shows in the restaurant's specialite; it is transient, using the best of the day's catch, broth simmered painstakingly from Kagoshima's Makurazaki Chiainuki high-quality bonito flakes, and Natural Kelp from Hokkaido's Rausu. Similarly, one day's sashimi appetizer might include Sea Bream from Yamaguchi's Suo-Oshima, Bonito from Kochi, Oval Squid from Shimane, but the next day it could be wildly different; such is chef Nakashima's selectivity regarding fresh-caught natural seafood. It's partner, soy sauce, is not an afterthought either; Hiroshima Mukaigahara's Wadaka-brand sauce, bonito-broth, and natural wasabi from Hiroshima's Yoshiwa combine to make a wonderfully succulent dip for the finest of the ocean's fruits. 'Nakashima''s cellar is not to be forgotten either; with a selection centered on sake of the Chugoku-region with 60% coming from local Hiroshima, the staff changes their selection with the seasons; ""Ugonnotsuki Jungin Koiomachi Special"", ""Horaitsuru Jungin Kanade"", and ""Kirei Nyukon Junmai Yama"" are just 3 of their many delicious pairings available. The interior a piece of art unto itself; a counter of Yoshino Cypress, tabletop of Japanese Zelkova, earthen walls designed by Kenichi Nagumo, and a hand-carved adze finish complete a environment as astounding as the food. The 200 year old Imari-ware, century old Wajimanuri antique lacquer, and artful white porcelain made by ""Living National Treasure"" Manji Inoue all serve to complete the sublime mood worthy of a would-be fourth world gourmet guide award. Sit back in this unforgettable atmosphere; basking in the hall of 'Nakashima' is an experience unto itself, an achievement to attain in life. Now add the chef's timeless culinary mastery, and you will find yourself lost in the silky depths of umami and sake, speaking on the deepest levels with the food and what originated them, nature. Best to bring along another, one with which you would not shy away from conversing deeply and squarely with and regarding the finest of nature's gifts. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- *All seats at this restaurant are reserved by waiting list. Available dates are not made public. First, register the date you want to reserve on the waiting list. The concierge will confirm availability and contact you to let you know if you can make a reservation. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. Please note that we request that everyone including children to respect dining experience of others. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customization on our course offers or offer a la carte option. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals. We request that you do not wear strong scent or perfume when dining with us.

とても感じのよい接客で気持ちよく過ごせました。

より引き立ちました。
四季折々伺いたいお店だと思いました。

心も体も、元気になっていくのを感じました。
ありがとうございました。
料理は自然な出汁の旨味で味わう最高のものでしたし、、接客は自然で大将のこだわりをしっかり教えていただけて、共に大変満足しました。

予想を超える美味しさに感動しました。ペアリングも最高でした。いつかまた機会があれば伺いたいと思います。
結婚記念日ということで今回初めて利用させていただきましたが、料理が素晴らしいのは勿論のこと、器へのこだわり、行き届いたおもてなしと全て堪能させていただきました。ありがとうございました。

The sushi quality was exceptional—one of the finest dining experiences I’ve ever had, with exquisite flavors and unparalleled freshness. The restaurant’s ambiance exudes elegance and sophistication, offering a tranquil hideaway from the bustling city. The location adds to its charm, creating an exclusive and serene dining retreat.
料理もお店の方の接客も最高でした
白子入りの茶碗蒸し、ハゲ肝の和え物など、初めて食べました。どれも、美味しく頂きました。また、近いうちに行きたいと思います。
お客様をお連れしての会食でしたが、お料理が美味しいのはもちろん、大将や女将さんには気さくで優しい対応をしていただき、満足できる会食となりました。
非常に美味しかったです
とても美味しかったです

一品一品とても美味しく頂きました。
特に土瓶蒸しと猪肉は超絶品でした。
土瓶蒸しは秋鱧と立派な松茸がゴロゴロ入っていて秋鱧からいいお出汁が出て松茸の薫りが漂いひと口呑むと一瞬我を忘れボーッとしてしまいました。
途中でスダチを搾ると清涼感が増してまた新しい味わいで頂けました。
今年はもう終わりみたいなので是非来年も土瓶蒸し目掛けても行きたいと思います。
猪肉は本当に超絶感動で、シンプルに炭で塩焼きにされてましたが、変なにおい等は全く皆無で旨味しかなかったです。
脂は必要最少限で旨味しかなく、脂と言うよりも肉自体がとてもジューシーで味わい深く、敢えて例えるならとても美味しい豚肉にとても美味しい鴨肉の深み・コクを足した様な味でした(あくまで個人の主観です)。
猪肉を美味しく調理するには、そもそも熟練の猟師さんで仕留め方や血抜きの仕方含め処理が完璧でないと、ここまで美味しい猪肉にはならないとの事。
良い状態のものがたまたま入らないと巡り会えないひと品らしく御縁に感謝し、美味しく頂きました。
他にもクエのお粥仕立てはお米とお出汁の塩梅が絶妙で、クエの美味しさを上手く引立てられてましたし、カワハギの肝和えも雑味なく濃厚まろやかで自家製ポン酢の美味しさと相まって感動的に美味しかったです。
料理や器の説明についても、女将さんは元より従業員さん全員の説明が素晴らしく、大将と女将さんの従業員さんへの教育指導の素晴らしさも際立ち、飲食店に限らずサービス業に従事している全ての経営者の模範となるお店だと感じました。
個人的には経済的に許される限り(笑)、何度でも通いたいと思える数少ないお店さんの一つになりました。

とても美味しくいただきました。
ご丁寧な対応をしていただき、ありがとうございました。
どの料理も細やかな手間が感じられ、とても美味しくいただきました。また、料理の内容や器についても丁寧に説明いただき、より一層関心を持って味わうことができました。おかげさまで私も妻も大満足で、銀婚式の祝い膳に相応しい内容でした。また、大事な人を連れて食べに伺いたいと思います。ありがとうございました。
今回は緊急事態宣言下でノンアルコール飲料しか頂けなくて残念でしたが、時間内にしっかりとお料理を出されて感心しました。器もお料理も楽しみながら本当に美味しくいただきました。また伺います。

美味しいお料理に、美しい器と空間。
とても素敵な時間を過ごさせていただきました。

大満足です。

Excellent dinner at Nakashima.  The staff were wonderful, incredibly gracious, and went the extra mile to communicate with us despite the language barrier.  Fantastic seasonal kaiseki dinner.  Highly recommended.

特に白焼きが美味しかったと夫が言ってました！
ここまでのクオリティなのに広島だからこの金額だなって思いました。

料理全般が素晴らしかったです。
特に、鱧の炙りたたきとお吸い物が気に入りました。
また、今回は丁度緊急事態宣言中だったということもあり、人生で初めてノンアルコール飲料を飲んだのですが、(ノンアルコール)白ワインとハイボールが非常に良く、銘柄を教えて貰うべきだったと少し後悔しています。

とても美味しかったです。
また料理はもちろん、接客、店の雰囲気、カウンター、料理の器など細部までこだわりが感じられて素晴らしいと思いました。
お酒が飲めなかったのが残念ですが、また世情が落ち着いたら是非お邪魔させていただきたいと思います。素敵な時間をありがとうございました。

初めて伺わせて頂きましたが、店の雰囲気は
やわらかく、初めてでも心地よく過ごさせて頂きました。
それがお料理を口に運ぶ事にも大きく影響されると
信じているのですが、それが見事に融合しました。
目にも楽しかったです。

ご馳走様でした。

記念日ということもあり、いろいろとご配慮いただき、感激しました。
お料理はとても美味しく、前回とメニューが被っていないものが多かったので驚きでした。

食材や食器の説明等、丁寧でとても良かったです。

また、来週お伺いします。

誕生日のお祝いにパートナーに連れてきていただきました。
お店の佇まいに少し緊張しましたが、扉を開けると女将さんと仲居さんが温かい笑顔でお出迎えしてくださり緊張が解けました。
カウンターから見える厨房にはお料理に対する真剣さが伝わってくる大将の調理姿、拘りの食材それぞれの背景やお料理に華を添える人間国宝や古伊万里、輪島塗などの器を丁寧に説明してくださる女将さんや仲居さんの接客。
そして、お料理の味。ジビエが全く臭みもなく甘くて美味しいこと。フグの皮は3種類あって、それぞれ食感が異なること。白子がこんなにクリーミーで美味しいこと。今まで知りませんでした。

244683.longDescription:
About ten-minute walk from Fukuyama Station in the eastern part of Hiroshima Prefecture, a short distance from the shopping district, “Chinese Cuisine Renka” is located along a quiet street in the neighborhood of a park and kindergarten. The owner-chef Rintaro Ogawa cooks the best ingredients of the day and serves simply in the best way.

Owner-chef Ogawa is from Fukuyama City, Hiroshima Prefecture. When he was in high school, he wanted to become a chef and he encountered the Japan-China Friendship Association, and after graduation he went to China. He learned Cantonese cuisine in the kitchen of a hotel in Guangzhou City for half a year, and after returning to Japan, he trained for 12 years in Yuraiken, a major Chinese restaurant in Fukuyama. Later, he became independent and opened 蓮花(Renka). In addition, in order to secure a space where you can cook as you like, the restaurant was relocated and renamed 蓮華(Renka) in 2007. It has become a restaurant that is introduced in the world-renown gourmet guide.

Chinese Cuisine Renka is really a maniac restaurant. There is no fixed menu, only omakase course by Chef Ogawa. The menu only has a brief description on the ingredients of the day (seafood includes sea bream, sea bass, flounder, meat includes duck, acorn black pork, deer, etc., and vegetable includes bok-choy, bamboo shoot, yellow chive, Chinese arrowhead, etc.) and the recipe (stir-fried seasonal vegetables in soup, stir-fried seafood and vegetables, black vinegar sauce for meat, etc.). "If you request the main ingredients and how to taste them, we will provide the best cuisine for you. So to speak, improvisation. There will never be the same thing again," says owner-chef Ogawa.

Vegetables are purchased from Kajitani Farm in Mihara, Kodawari Farm with organically grown in Kamiishikogen-cho, Mitsuboshi Seika Midori in Fukuyama, etc. Seafood from Shimada Sengyo and pork from Nakai Seiniku Shokai, both in Fukuyama, and chicken from Nakabayashi Chicken Shop in Fuchu, are all sourced from reliable local producers and traders. The seasonings used are kept to a minimum, no garlic or sesame oil is used, no decoration is used, and the original taste of carefully selected ingredients is not spoiled, and finished simply. The drink menu is overwhelmingly rich in Chinese tea. There are over 20 kinds of tea such as green tea, white tea, yellow tea, dark tea, black tea, etc., and they are selected according to the season and diner’s physical condition. In addition, instead of pairing with each dish, it is a style that you can enjoy with the change of expression of Chinese tea where the intensity peaks in the middle of the meal to match with the course composition of Chinese cuisine, where the main dish comes in the middle. The restaurant also has beer, Shaoxing rice wine, shochu, Japanese sake and wine available.

The restaurant has 4 counter seats and tables (6 people for round table, 12 people for table). Owner-chef Ogawa says, "Eating is a tool that creates a get-together and conversation. I hope you will feel energetic tomorrow. It's about choosing ingredients and cooking methods". Enjoy the simple and flavorful Chinese cuisine of Chef Ogawa in various occasions such as celebrating anniversaries and special occasions with family and couples, dining together with friends and foodies, and with business guests.


■Access
A 10-minute walk or 5-minute by taxi from Shinkansen Fukuyama Station
A 10-minute walk or 5-minute by taxi from Fukuyama Station (JR Sanyo Main Line (Okayama - Mihara))
*This restaurant is located at Fukuyama Station, Fukuyama City, Hiroshima. It takes about 30 minutes from Hiroshima Station by bullet train. The fare for a one-way trip on the bullet train is about 5,000 yen.
Please check the transportation information before making a reservation.

244369.longDescription:
A 15-minute walk from JR Onomichi Station, situated near ""Shimanami Kaido (※),"" the long-established world gourmet guide awarded Japanese cuisine restaurant “Kappo Higashiyama.” After studying under the founder, Mr. Masashi Yokoyama was appointed the second generation master in 1981. With a wide outlook that is the result of over 15 years studying Urasenke (tea ceremony) and Onomichi yaki (ceramic art ceramics), Mr. Yokoyama offers “Japanese cuisine worthy of Onomichi.” Since its inception in 1962, it has been a well-known restaurant that continues to be loved by its many guests. They can speak English, Italian and Chinese.

Using seasonal fish and vegetables from Onomichi, and starting with only the highest quality ingredients, including edible wild vegetables and greens harvested by himself. With staple dishes such as sashimi and Takiawase (fish and vegetables cooked separately but served together), the cuisine is orthodox Japanese cooking that makes use of ingredients in a simple manner, but isn’t tied down by the classics, and is a production directed according to modern taste. In addition, the third generation of the family, Mr. Daijiro Yokoyama, currently the sous chef, has been studying at the Japan branch of Milan’s world gourmet guide awardred, “Ristorante Sadler” as well as other famous Italian restaurants in Tokyo, and makes use of the unique Italian fire pan technique in grilled and fried dishes. 

The Japanese sake selection centers around Hiroshima-distilled favorites such as “Kamotsuru,” “Zuikan,” and “Kirei,” and the “Hire sake” which makes use of puffer fins processed and dried in-store is also recommended. The restaurant is well-suited to foreign tourists and their families; dishes can be changed according to individual likes and dislikes, and a kids menu consultation is also possible. 

The interior features counter seating, recessed-floor tables, and standard tables, as well as 4 private tatami rooms.  The ceilings of the private rooms are decorated with lucky “good fortune” and “sea bream” motifs, painted by Onomichi’s famous painter, Toyotaro Mizoue, making them well-suited for occasions of celebration. By all means, we urge you to come and taste the seasons of Onomichi at a famous restaurant that has brought guests from all over the country for many years.


*It takes 2-hour train ride from the following locations: ""RIHGA Royal Hotel Hiroshima "", ""Grand Prince Hotel Hiroshima"", ""Sheraton Grand Hotel Hiroshima"", and ""Hiroshima  Station"" .
nearestStations: A 15-minute walk from Onomichi Station (East Exit), JR Sanyo Line

244684.longDescription: In Hatsukaichi City, Hiroshima Prefecture, there is an area called Miyajimaguchi, where ferries come and go to Miyajima, home to the World Heritage Site Itsukushima Shrine. Located about an eight-minute walk from Miyajimaguchi, AKAI is situated on a hill slightly away from the hustle and bustle of the touristic area. This restaurant is set in a renovated private house that is more than 80 years old. Here, Chef Kenji Akai serves simple and heartwarming dishes made with plenty of local ingredients. Chef Akai is from Hiroshima City. After working at Italian restaurants in Hiroshima and Fukuoka, he served as the head chef at a wine bar in Hiroshima. At that time, he was attracted by the compositional power found within French cuisine, which led him to travel to France. He studied for about one and a half years at Le Relais Louis XIII in Paris, and was selected as one of the top performers in the Hiroshima Chef Contest hosted by Hiroshima Prefecture, through which he began to stand out as a chef of French cuisine. For his third trip to France, he trained at the three-starred restaurant Maison Pic in Valence, where he was entrusted with grilling meat. In 2017, he won the top prize at a chef competition dedicated to discovering young culinary talent, and attracted widespread attention. After further refining his skills at wedding venues and other establishments, he returned to his hometown, and in May 2019, he opened his own restaurant, AKAI, in Hiroshima.His culinary world received an enthusiastic welcome from foodies, and the new restaurant became a popular destination for food lovers from across Japan and all over the world. “I simply named my restaurant after my family name because I wanted it to represent my culinary philosophy and my idea of living a simple and modest life,” says Chef Akai. The AKAI cuisine is characterized by its live dining experience, where dishes are served hot and fresh right in front of guests. The menu varies day by day, taking inspiration from the best ingredients available on the day. The prix-fixe menu, consisting of approximately 10 courses, is the same for both lunch and dinner. The ingredients are carefully selected. Most of the other ingredients are sourced from local markets within reach. Seasonal ingredients are elevated into exquisite dishes that celebrate the four seasons. For example, the spring menu features edible wild plants, spring vegetables, beans, and oysters. In summer, sweetfish is exclusively sourced from a professional fisherman. The sweetfish caught in the Usa River in Yamaguchi Prefecture is retrieved every morning and transformed into delicious dishes, ranging from sashimi to sweetfish rice. In autumn, the restaurant is filled with the flavors of wild mushrooms. The natural mushrooms rarely found in markets are delivered from Shobara City in northern Hiroshima Prefecture. The winter menu spotlights game meats, such as wild boar and Japanese badger from Shobara, net-caught wild duck from Kagoshima, and black bear from Akita and Iwate. The menu offers detailed descriptions, including the origins and producers of ingredients, tableware, furniture, and decorations. The wine list offers a variety of options, mostly from France but also from Italy, Australia, and Japan. The pairing menu includes not only wines but also sake that goes well with AKAI’s dishes. The restaurant only has counter seating (for up to eight guests), which is spaciously set out. Enjoy AKAI’s simple dishes made from only the essential ingredients to highlight the seasonal flavors of Hiroshima, Setouchi, and other parts of Japan. *Please note that the location of the restaurant may be slightly difficult to find. While it is shown correctly on Google Maps, the restaurant is housed in a traditional Japanese building located at the top of a small hill, and the entrance will not be visible until you reach the top. *For inquiries, please contact the restaurant directly at 070-2662-1329.​
nearestStations: A 8-minute walk from Miyajimaguchi Station (JR Sanyo Main Line)

245205.longDescription:
Miyoshi City, located in the northern part of Hiroshima Prefecture and bordering Shimane Prefecture, has historically developed as a cultural and economic center and a transport hub connecting the Sanin and Sanyo regions. The city is also blessed with water resources and solely depends on groundwater for all its needs. Meanwhile, it is locally known as a foggy city because fog occurs frequently at the meeting of the waters. In this city, the restaurant “muk” is set on the former main street lined with old merchant houses. Renovated from a closed sake brewery, it is atmospheric as if it had stood there for decades. It is a 120-minute drive from Hiroshima City, or 2 km away from Miyoshi Station on the Geibi Line, and a 5-minute walk away from the local landmark of Miyoshi Mononoke Museum.

The restaurant was opened by a couple when they got married, selling pastries in the daytime and serving French cuisine at night. The husband, Daichi Fukuma, honed his cooking and baking skills at some restaurants in Tokyo, including the two-star restaurant ÉdiTioN Koji Shimomura. Now he works as a pastry chef and a sommelier at muk while his wife, Kayo, serves as a chef.
The food menu only offers prix fixe (fixed price) options. The ingredients are directly sourced from producers, mainly in Miyoshi and Fukuma’s home district of Kawanishi. In particular, the eggs are purchased from the Fumichan Family’s Eggs, which offers specially designed eggs for making cakes. Laid by hens on special feed, they are extremely rich in flavor and used to make meals, flans, and cream puffs at muk. Some specialties of the restaurant are inspired by pastries, such as “Terrine de Foie Gras,” with foie gras sandwiched by slices of pound cake and topped with seasonal fruits.
The drink menu mainly features wines, gins, and whiskies. The wines are sourced from vineyards in Miyoshi as well as France and Italy, while the whiskies come from Islay. The pairing menu offers both alcoholic and nonalcoholic options so that many guests who come by car can enjoy drinks as much as non-drivers do.

The restaurant name “muk” is derived from a comma-shaped bead which is the symbol of the neighborhood (one of the Chinese characters for the word consists of two Japanese characters that read “mu” and “ku”) as well as muku tree and solid natural wood (also pronounced as “muku” in Japanese) which symbolize a storehouse. As indicated by the name, the restaurant renovated from an old building preserves the charm of the original structure, equipped with two tables and a private room.
It is the perfect place for anniversaries, celebrations, and other family gatherings. Please enjoy a relaxing time with your significant others in a cozy setting at muk.
nearestStations: From Miyoshi Station, take a bus to the Mononoke Museum. A 5-minute walk from the Mononoke Museum

244550.longDescription:
Situated about 20 minutes by car from Fukuyama Station in eastern Hiroshima prefecture, ""L’ardoise"" is a French restaurant operated in a house nestled in the woods. Its name can be found in 'Gault et Millau' 2018 and other renowned 'world gourmet guide Hiroshima Ehime'2018, and the cuisine is prepared by the skilled hand of Chef Fumio Fujii.

After graduating high school, Fujii studied under Chef Tsuyoshi Miki of restaurant ""Jean Moulin"" in Kobe before working at his father’s French restaurant in Fukuyama and subsequently traveling to France. Having worked at ""Le Petit Nice"", a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Marseille, Fujii moved to Paris, where he worked at a bistro ""L’ardoise"" under Chef Pierre Jay.

In addition to food, Fujii has always been an avid student of wine, and in this respect, the experiences of his year and a half in Paris have had a lasting influence on Chef Fujii since his return to Japan. Returning to Fukuyama in 2007, Fujii was entrusted by Chef Pierre Jay with the ""L’ardoise"" name in opening his own restaurant. It has not only developed the local following but also earned a place in world-class gourmet guides.

“My goal is for this to be a local restaurant favored by local patrons,” says Fujii.

He travels in the mountains, by the sea and upriver, seeking out and enjoying his encounters with local ingredients in the pursuit of a concept of cuisine that is both French and local. He says that his first desire is to have local people enjoy a cuisine in which he manages to maximize the potential of local ingredients by applying the techniques of French cuisine.

Examples include the game meats supplied by ""Iwataya"" in Hiroshima’s Sera district, lamb from ""Farm Mae"" in the town of Kitahiroshima, and the cheeses of ""Mirasaka Fromage"" in Miyoshi. Fujii sources his red sea urchin and other ingredients from Miyakubo in Japan's Setonai inland sea region. He ventures to the morning seafood markets himself every morning to make strict selections using his keen eye for quality. He buys his vegetables directly from the farmers, often making the purchases himself at local morning produce markets.

Seasonal dishes include springtime white asparagus and ice cream made from fukinoto. In summer, he prepares summer roast venison and peach desserts. His fall dishes include lamb, as well as kotake and matsutake mushrooms. Winter offerings feature game meats and oysters with apple desserts. The result is an ability to partake of the freshest local ingredients season by season, which is the essence of Fujii’s “local French” concept.

For guests wondering which wine to select, pairings chosen by the sommelier are recommended. Those who prefer sake can choose from selections only available from Hiroshima brewers, including labels such as Tenpoichi of Fukuyama and Kirei of Higashi-hiroshima.

The restaurant’s interior décor is based on the appointments observed during a visit to Chef Pierre Jay’s family home in the city of Mâcon. Cutlery and tableware ordered from local artisans blend well with the white-and-red color scheme of the interior, enabling guests to relax as they enjoy their meal. Dining tables seat a total of 32. This unique “local French” cuisine, and an ambiance overflowing with love of the local landscape, assures an enjoyable dining experience for meals with family, with friends, or on a date.

244368.longDescription:
Surrounded by the bountiful sea and numerous islands, the unassuming French restaurant ""Amiral"" lies hidden within Kure City, Hiroshima Prefecture.  The concept is to ""prepare cuisine exclusively for the guests of the day,” welcoming in just 1 group of guests for lunch and dinner each day.  The owner-chef Shigeaki Nagashima prepares cuisine and serves his guests, making for a unique experience that has put ""Amiral"" on the map.

Chef Nagashima completed his culinary training at a restaurant in Hiroshima City, after which he worked as the resident head chef for ambassadors at the Japanese embassy in Morocco.  Demonstrating his French cooking to the many foreign guests who visited, he was awarded the status of “exemplary resident head chef for ambassadors” by the minister of foreign affairs.  Then, after returning to Japan in March of 2013, he opened ""Amiral"".  He is the only chef in the Seto inland received the "Promising Young Chef Award" from the World Gourmet Guide and has been awarded one star by the famous gourmet guide.

A distinct feature of the cuisine is its use of simple dishes that focus on one ingredient.  It may appear simple, but once it’s in your mouth a multitude of flavors explode.  The wine selection centers on France, but there is a wide variety including wines from countries like Argentina and Romania, and suggestions are made based on the preferences of guests. The only Japanese sake they have is the local ""Hanahato""; they also have a good selection of digestifs such as cognac, Calvados, pomace brandy, and whiskey.

As you open the wood patterned sliding door with a Japanese feel to it, you would enter a space that feels chic and classy; there is a counter at the kitchen that seats 6 and a table that also seats 6.  Guests might sit at either the counter or table and because you’ll have the place to yourself you do not need to worry about other customers; it is perfect for special occasions or a date.  They also accommodate halal and vegetarian needs.  When you make a reservation at ""Amiral"", you are guaranteed a truly special experience for that day.

244417.longDescription:
On the 2nd floor of a building in Noborimachi, an upper-class residential area of Hiroshima, one can find “le triskel”, a restaurant which led the way for French cuisine in Hiroshima in the 2000s. This famous old French restaurant is known to any and all gourmets in Hiroshima.

The owner-chef Motohiro Yuzaki, trained at world gourmet guide award restaurants in France, Italy, and Switzerland from the late 1970s to the 1980s. At the IKA Culinary Olympics in 2000, he led the Hiroshima team to a bronze medal. That the same year, he opened “le triskel”. The one to name the restaurant was Patrick Joffroy, who is still close with Chef Yuzaki. The restaurant hosts visiting artists and musicians from around the world, and it plays the role of a salon for the businesspeople and politicians of Hiroshima. Chef Yuzaki also judges chef competitions held in Hiroshima, whence young chefs fly off to France’s world gourmet guide award restaurants.

Since the 1970s, Chef Yuzaki has followed the context of French cuisine earnestly, approaching food which is “properly delicious.” His specialty dishes—such as his lobster terrine and his foie gras beignet inspired by Chef Gille Epié of Miravile in Paris—which he has improved upon for 18 years, convey the chef’s sincerity towards food. His lobster dishes, which have carried on the esprit of Patrick Joffroy, are particularly fine dishes worth tasting. His dishes are also well-balanced in their use of many local terroir ingredients, such as Hiroshima beef, fresh sweetfish from the Otagawa River, and ""Mirasaka Fromage"". 

“le triskel” stores approximately 200 types of wine in its own cellar. The majority are Bordeaux and Bourgogne, with wine from the 5 premier chateaux (Lafite-Rothschild, Margaux, Latour, Mouton-Rothschild, and Haut-Brion) and DRC also available. The restaurant also has carefully stored old wine, so the oenophile should inquire about making a reservation. With private rooms, vegetarian, kid, and low-calorie menu options available, prior consultation can help the restaurant fulfill many requests. Come to experience the historical cuisine of Hiroshima’s master chef.

244765.longDescription:
A 10-minute walk from Saijo Station in Higashihiroshima City, Hiroshima Prefecture, “Ryoriya Sobiki” is located in Saijo town which is known as one of the three most famous brewing districts in Japan. It is a Japanese restaurant where customers from inside and outside of the prefecture come looking for dishes made with seasonal ingredients.

Chef Yasumasa Sobiki became independent after studying Japanese cooking for 8 years in Hiroshima. “Ryoriya Sobiki”, opened in March 2017 with the thought of "will open a Japanese restaurant someday", became the 4th store of Sobiki. "I didn't know there was such a restaurant in Saijo," gradually spread from customers who were looking forward to authentic Japanese cuisine, and in 2018, the restaurant acquired its first two stars in Higashihiroshima.

Reservations are limited to a total of 10 groups, including 5 groups for lunch and 5 groups for dinner, and 1-day advance reservation is required. Ingredients are taken not only from local area but from all over Japan, and they are purchased from producers whom Sobiki trusts himself, such as Junichi Fujimoto who is known as a charismatic fisherman in Imabari, Ehime Prefecture, "Sakai Sengyo" from Hakodate City, Hokkaido, and wasabi from the oldest wasabi farm in Japan, "Wasabi Monzen" in Shizuoka Prefecture.

There are several types of sake available, including local sake as well as recommended sake from outside the prefecture that changes regularly. Summer sake in summer, hiyaoroshi in autumn, new sake in winter, and sake that goes well with the cuisine are served. The restaurant mainly serves Japanese wine, along with wine from southern France and Burgundy, with a light nuance that goes well with Japanese dishes.

The restaurant uses lots of Japanese cedar, and the counter made of Japanese cypress (7 seats) is elaborately designed so that customers can stay comfortably. The 2 private rooms (up to 6 people each) uses Nara wood for the tables. You can feel the seasonal features not only from the ingredients but also from the arrangements such as the Hassun that changes with the season and the dinnerware that goes with it. For people who enjoy eating, please experience chef Sobiki’s "delicious" in "Ryoriya Sobiki".
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Saijo Station, South exit (JR Shinonoi Line, JR Sanyo Main Line (Mihara - Iwakuni))
*A limousine bus is available from Hiroshima Airport to Saijo Station. (Time required: approx. 35 minutes)

244549.longDescription:
The city of Fukuyama in Hiroshima Prefecture has a sightseeing spot called Tomonoura which was made famous by becoming the backdrop for the Studio Ghibli animated film Ponyo, directed by Hayao Miyazaki. A 7-minute walk from Fukuyama Station—the gateway to the city—is ""Miroir"", a long-established restaurant that represents the best of Fukuyama. The owner-chef Takao Nakayama trained in different places before going independent and opening the business in 2003. He is a skilled chef who has received a one-star rating two times in a row, no doubt due to the self-study he has done by poring over books and the journeys he has had and people he has met during his frequent travels to France.

The seafood at ""Miroir"" is sourced from the Kasaoka Islands in the Seto Inland Sea, with Manabeshima—an island made famous by a book by Florent Chavouet—supplying ingredients such as squilla, Japanese blue crab, ""aka-ashi ebi"" prawns, and Japanese sea fig. Vegetables are special Fukuyama products such as spinach, aodai, cucumbers, and figs. By purchasing local products that are in season during different times of the year, Miroir offers French cuisine of the kind that is unique to Fukuyama. The restaurant is particular about salt and the way that the food is heated. With these 2 simple elements, ""Miroir"" is able to draw out the best of the ingredients to the ultimate degree. For example, butterfish that has simply been salted and baked/pan-fried or lobster that is simply boiled in water with salt have a sensual aroma and texture and are bursting with deep, rich flavor. Chef Nakayama’s style with his main ingredients is to combine elements inspired by natural scenes on the plate. For example, a dish based on his image of “the scent of the sea and grass” expresses this idea through baked/pan-fried butterfish with a tarragon sauce with a garnish of boiled beans. He explains the inspiration for a dish such as this as coming from the “empty space” of his inner world. Chef Nakamura used to read books by/about the chef Georges Auguste Escoffier during his teens and has made over a dozen trips to different parts of France since he was in his early 20s. The inner world that he has built up through his encounters with a range of different ingredients and people is reflected in his cooking as if it was a mirror (Miroir, the restaurant name, being the French for “mirror”), to become a highly distinctive group of dishes that could be called “a fusion with Nakayama.”

""Miroir"" has only 3 tables and a private room. Antique furniture gives the space a subdued ambiance. The service continues the traditional style of service in French restaurants, carving dishes and lifting off the cloche tableware cover in front of the customer’s table in an all-around orchestration of “a space for enjoying French cuisine.” The elegant ambiance of Miroir is perfect for anniversaries and business entertainment. The wine is a lineup of mostly Bordeaux and Burgundy vintages that will make for a blissful time enjoyed at a slow pace with the cuisine. We do hope that you will make your way to Fukuyama so that you may enjoy ""Miroir"", a renowned establishment located in regional Japan.

244355.longDescription:
"Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" opened in April 2014 in Nakanotana, the heart of Hiroshima’s busy downtown area. The business can trace its origins back to before the Edo period, as Hiroshima’s very first fish market. "Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" is famous for being the hardest sushi restaurant to get a reservation in these days in Hiroshima Prefecture.

The chef of "Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" is Mr. Soshi Satani. Soshi started work at a sushi restaurant after graduating cooking school, but later changed occupations to work as a marine products wholesaler in order to be able to pursue his passion for fish. He worked in the industry for 17 years and then opened "Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" when he felt the time was ripe. The restaurant has become popular for the individuality of its dishes, which are not limited by the typical sushi restaurant concept.

To source fish, Soshi visits the fish market each morning. He assesses the quality of the fish himself, drawing on his experience from the time he worked selling marine products. For the vinegared rice, he uses Akisakari rice grown in Hiroshima. To create the vinegar, he blends red vinegar with premium rice vinegar made from eight times the standard amount of rice. He also chooses wasabi grown in Hiroshima, thus unifying the sense of terroir. Food can only be ordered as “Setouchi-Mae” in Japan’s Omakase (Chef's Selection) style, which leaves all food item selections up to the chef. First to be served will be 6 or 7 seasonal hors d'oeuvres. This will be followed by about 10 pieces of sushi. "Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" stocks about 20 different kinds of sake, chiefly local sake produced in places such as Hiroshima, Yamaguchi, and Shimane in the Chugoku region. 

The entrance to "Sakana Kui Kiri Soshi" is through an antique English door hidden in the dark in a corner of a shop that has its shutter/shutters drawn. The restaurant has only 14 counter seats, and with low lighting, is designed to be an atmospheric space. Soshi strives to be one of a kind in Hiroshima. We invite you to visit and enjoy his sushi.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Tatemachi Station of Hiroshima Electric Railway

244698.longDescription:
“Wagyu and Wine Fuoco” is located on the 1st basement floor of a building in Tatemachi, downtown Hiroshima. It is a yakiniku restaurant that serves rare meat, carefully-selected by the owner-chef Takashi Hiromoto, at reasonable prices along with wine. “Fuoco” means ‘fire’ in Italian.

After graduating from Hattori Nutrition College in Tokyo, Chef Hiromoto, who grew up with his parents running a ryokan business in Yamaguchi Prefecture, trained at Italian restaurants in Tokyo and Hiroshima. Later, while studying in Italy, he was attracted by the appeal of beef while dining at various restaurants, and after returning to Japan, devoted himself to studying at a famous yakiniku restaurant in Tokyo. He returned to the familiar city of Hiroshima, and opened “Wagyu and Wine Fuoco” in March 2016. The restaurant serves Wagyu beef that is all A5-grade. The signature dish, “Grilled Fuoco,” is an elegant sukiyaki-like dish where Hiroshima rib roast is dipped in a special warishita (sukiyaki sauce), grilled in a roaster, and enjoyed with specially prepared egg mousse. There are six kinds of rare parts among the “Assorted Rare Cuts,” which change daily. You can enjoy the different flavors of each part, such as the dipping sauce or rose rock salt. Also, a portion of Hiroshima’s rare shoulder rib meat, “Koune,” is a must try. You can enjoy carefully-selected Japanese beef from the Chuo-Shikoku region, such as “Hiroshima Japanese Beef,” which is not widely distributed outside of Hiroshima, as well as Kagawa “Olive beef,” and “Tottori Japanese Beef Olein 55.” In the Omakase course, the Fuoco style is to serve fatty meat first so that the flavor won’t be overpowering.

The restaurant’s concept is to “enjoy good meat at reasonable prices,” while presenting rare parts of carefully-selected Japanese beef. Other than fillet and sirloin, the beef is purchased directly from a trustworthy wholesaler run by Chef Hiromoto’s childhood friend, allowing diners to enjoy the beef at a reasonable price. They also use a no-duct roaster that doesn’t emit any smoke, eliminating the smell of yakiniku from guests’ clothing – another reason for the restaurant’s popularity. Also, for celebrations, you can order the “meat cake,” which is made from slices of meat and arranged like flower petals, making it a popular dish for its playful presentation. They also have a variety of drinks on the menu. There are more than 100 varieties of wine that match well with yakiniku, from casual-drinking to California-cult wines and five large Bordeaux Chateaux wines, all in the cellar waiting for you.

The interior has a stylish design in red, based on the fuoco (flame) image. There are 12 counter seats, table seats and semi-private rooms. Enjoy the flavor of Japanese beef with family, friends, and colleagues, or guests from overseas.

244685.longDescription:
Tempura restaurant “Tenyoshi” which reopened on May 18, 2024 is located in Yoshijima-cho, about 5 minutes by car, south of the Peace Memorial Park in the center of Hiroshima City. You will be welcomed by the chef Masahiro Ishihiro and the proprietress as you pass through the “noren” (shop curtain). The restaurant’s name, “Tenyoshi”, is derived from the word “tempura” and the town’s name, Yoshijima. It is a popular restaurant loved by locals.

Chef Ishihiro trained at Japanese restaurants in his hometown of Hiroshima, as well as at sushi and soba restaurants. He decided to open a tempura restaurant because there are not many opportunities for people to make tempura at home and there are only a few restaurants specializing in tempura in Hiroshima. He visited famous restaurants in various places around Japan, self-learned the technique of making tempura, and opened “Tenyoshi” in February, 2015.

The tempura at “Tenyoshi” is fried in a 
 rapeseed oil and a thin, delicate batter is used so that the true flavor of the ingredients can be enjoyed. “You can enjoy freshly made tempura one piece at a time. You can enjoy not only seafood, but also vegetable tempura. I want to dispel the image that tempura is heavy”, says chef Ishihiro. He is particular about the ingredients, and the seafood is sourced from “Yoshibun” at Hiroshima Central Wholesale Market, which has a nationwide network. The vegetables are ordered directly from reliable producers and grocers. The vegetables are selected so that diners can enjoy seasonal ingredients. The “Omakase Course” is a combination of simple tempura and the chef’s original tempura to ensure that visitors can enjoy a variety of dishes.

Drinks are selected by the proprietress who is a licensed sake taster. In addition to sake from Hiroshima and other parts of Japan, the restaurant also focuses on wine. They have around 30 types of champagne and 50 types of white and red wine mainly from Bourgogne.

There are only 8 counter seats. In addition to the calm interior, the restaurant also uses “Miyajima’s Osuna pottery”, from Hatsukaichi, Hiroshima Prefecture, on which the tempura is served, allowing visitors from outside of the prefecture or overseas to feel the true sense of Hiroshima. Enjoy dining with family, friends, and colleagues at “Tenyoshi”by Mr. and Mrs. Ishihiro, who “want tempura culture to take root in Hiroshima.”

245398.longDescription:
Takashi Anezaki, owner of Ryouriya So, a Japanese restaurant in Sapporo City, Hokkaido, opened KOUUNRYUUSUI NISEKO in response to guests’ requests to offer sushi and fresh ingredients only in winter. 
To satisfy guests visiting Niseko, he closed Ryouriya So in winter and started a pop-up restaurant in Niseko in winter from 2018. From 2019, he has stayed in Niseko for a limited time from December to early spring every year to entertain guests from Japan and all over the world.

The cuisine offered is centered on Hokkaido ingredients, with one carefully selected course, the "Sushi Course 36,300 yen (including tax and service charge).  KOUUNRYUUSUI NISEKO definitely encourages you to try dishes using the popular live crabs, which can be included in the courses. Depending on the day, it is also possible to savor King crabs, Snow crabs, and Blue King (Hanasaki) crabs (advance reservations required).

The restaurant has a counter seating six guests and table seating four. It also features a large aquarium with seasonal crab and shellfish.
The restaurant’s name, KOUUNRYUUSUI, comes from an ancient idiom describing the way clouds move by letting nature take its course. When you are in Niseko, be sure to visit KOUUNRYUUSUI NISEKO, where you can fully enjoy the blessings of the seas while in the mountains with the owner’s creative cooking, and enjoy a blissful time.
nearestStations: A sister restaurant of Ryouriya So in the Niseko area where you can enjoy sushi with fresh ingredients.

244632.longDescription:
World gourmet guide award Japanese cuisine restaurant ""Ryoriya So"" is located on the Maruyama Park side of Sapporo City, Hokkaido. Keeping true to the restaurant name, the Owner Mr. Takashi Anezaki treats his guests to ""cuisine that makes the most out of the deliciousness of raw ingredients"".

Mr. Anezaki was born and raised in Hokkaido. After training for 9 years in Kyoto and 4 years in Kagawa, he returned to Hokkaido and opened ""Ryoriya So"" in Sapporo in 2005. Its motto - To use the best ingredients of the day no matter what. Personally picking mushrooms and mountain vegetables from the mountains and combining them with pesticide-free vegetables purchased from local farmers, Mr. Anezaki assembles the menu for the day, producing food through which diners can ""taste the deliciousness of the raw ingredients"". For ""Ryoriya So"", 2 other important keywords are ""seasons"" and ""customer preferences"". 

Every season, Mr. Anezaki picks and chooses ingredients from different regions depending on where his guests hail from, and their preferences - allowing guests from Honshu to sample local terroir, while providing local guests with a taste of Honshu ingredients. During the game season from autumn to winter, the venison yu-tofu, grilled venison and other dishes that feature the meat of the Ezo deer receive great reviews. As for Japanese sake to go with the food, in addition to the classics such as Horai from Gifu and Suigei from Kochi, we have also prepared a variety of different types of Japanese sake from all over the country, that will go with any kind of food. The tableware and liquor are all artisanal pieces, serving as an excellent foil to the food and sake. 

""Ryoriya So"" is located in an old but renovated the freestanding building, with a modern atmosphere. The interior of the restaurant is completely Japanese-style, with 5 counter seats. Reservations for a party of  5 may book the entire premises. Children are welcome, making ""Ryoriya So"" a great venue for family gatherings and kids' birthdays. In winter, a private chef service that serves the Niseko region is also available, so please contact us if you would like to enjoy fine dining in the comfort of your resort.

244408.longDescription:
Sapporo’s Maruyama area is a town with a quiet, elegant atmosphere. Standing along a peaceful lane is a Japanese restaurant ""Wada."" Since opening in 2009 it has been endorsed by gourmet guests, and in 2017 it received one world gourmet guide award, showing its strength as a Japanese restaurant.

Chef Hayato Wada comes from Okushiri Island, known for being a treasure trove of ingredients in Hokkaido. To share the delicious ingredients of his childhood with his guests, he includes many seasonal specialties in the menu, such as Okushiri Island’s wild plants, mushrooms, and sea urchin. Additionally, he conveys the abundance of ingredients to be found in this region by procuring vegetables from farms around the outskirts of Sapporo and buying only fresh Hokkaido seafood from a local brokerage every day.

The 10-dish banquet course meal, overflowing with fresh seasonal ingredients, is particularly popular. The chef is meticulous about his stock, using 2 types of kombu from Rausu and Osatsube as well as bonito flakes to carefully take the stock before adding subtle flavoring. While the stock appears elegant and pale, it has a thick umami and sweetness which act as a linchpin to support the flavors of the dishes. The guests are particularly fond of the sushi which combines red vinegared rice and fresh seafood and ties together the course meal. The selection of wine is extensive and includes many labels from Hokkaido and Okushiri.

""Wada"" is located in a renovated home built more than 50 years ago. Its stylish impression is given by its uniform whiteness, connoting the snows of Hokkaido. Consisting of 7 counter and table seats and a semi-private room (6 seats), it is perfect for anniversaries and business entertainment. This famous northern restaurant allows you to experience the abundance of Hokkaido and the craft of a Japanese master in a relaxed atmosphere. It is certainly worth a visit.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Maruyama koen Station(Sapporo Municipal subway Tozai Line)

244983.longDescription:
Sushi Tanabe is located on the 9th floor of the Rokkatei Building near Sapporo Station. 

Originally from Eniwa, chef Masashi Watanabe set his sights on becoming a sushi chef at the age of 15 and began training in his hometown and Tokyo. He became independent at the age of 22 and opened a sushi restaurant in Susukino. In 2002, when The Windsor Hotel Toya Resort & Spa was established, he was appointed as the owner of a sushi restaurant there, and five years later, he opened Sushi Tanabe. Surrounded by the sea, the restaurant's particular style of sushi and sophisticated hospitality made the most of Hokkaido's natural features, and it became a popular three-star restaurant in 2012 before being relocated to its current location in 2015.

The sushi at Sushi Tanabe specialises in the familiar Edomae-style sushi from Tokyo, as well as the distinctive Ezomae-style, an approach specific to the northern region that maximizes the use of Hokkaido’s terroir. 

To make the most of the area’s famed ingredients, Watanabe and his team put their heart and soul into their preparation; marinating, simmering, grilling, and pickling all bring out their flavour. Each ingredient is carefully selected so that guests can enjoy Hokkaido’s fresh seafood, and the sushi rice and accompaniments. 

Sushi connoisseurs particularly appreciate the Tsuri-kinki (idiot fish) in Abashiri, sea urchin, and raw oysters. Milt from tiger pufferfish caught in Hokkaido is harvested from spring to early summer, while the milt of Pacific cod is gathered from autumn to winter. 

The restaurant also offers a variety of sake, for guests’ pleasure -- this includes Japanese sake from Kuniki Shuzo Sake Brewery, the northernmost brewery in Japan, as well as rare bottles selected by sake specialists. In addition, there are always 5 Hokkaido wines (Furano City Furano Wine, Chitose City Chitose Winery, Otaru City Osa Winery, Toyako Town Tsukiura Winery, Yoichi Town Hirakawa Winery), including the Champagne Salon carefully selected by the sommelier. Wines such as from other countries, California’s Kenzo Estate, and Burgundy Grand Cru are also offered, and oenophiles have been known to search this wine list to reserve bottles.

The understated interior boasts a minimal design created using materials such as cypress, cedar and bamboo. The restaurant is particular about using famous trees such as Yoshino cypress. Sake cups and bowls such as Tin Chirori from Seikado in Kyoto, and Ryuta Kiln from Saga add to the dining experience. 

A counter (11 seats and 13 seats) and semi-private table (2 rooms for 6 people) are available. The restaurant is ideal for occasions with loved ones, family, and friends.

244749.longDescription:
15 minutes by car from Maruyama in Sapporo City. Once you pass through the Obetsuzawa tunnel, you can enjoy rich nature. “AGRISCAPE” stands within the farmland. It is a sister store of the popular restaurant “Restaurant SIO” in Sapporo, and opened in April 2019 in the place where it was originally an onion farm. In addition to the restaurant business, it also produces vegetables, poultry and pork. This is a circular agriculture restaurant with the thought of "I want to start cooking by going back to making ingredients".

Chef Kaori Yoshida has gained experience in “Le Musee” and “Restaurant SIO” in Sapporo since 2010. “AGRISCAPE” uses vegetables carefully-selected from seeds, safe and secure chicken, eggs and pork raised without antibiotics or hormones to create "Caramelized Sapporo Yellow Roast" "Moist Roast Black Chicken" and other creative dishes following the example of nature. The scent of fresh seasonal vegetables is striking. One of the characteristics of “AGRISCAPE” is that, unlike most of the farm restaurant in Japan, it uses not only vegetables, but also freshly picked chicken and eggs from the farm. The concept of considering all aspects of food production, breeding, processing and cooking as part of the cooking process can be said to be one of the great attractions of the “AGRISCAPE” that live side by side with the strict but rich four seasons in Hokkaido. The restaurant mainly serves wine and has around 20 types of sake from Hokkaido and France. The selection goes well with the cuisine.

The restaurant makes use of the warmth of wood, and the simple white space brings out the colors of vegetables. There is a main dining room for 14 people and 2 private rooms for 2 - 4 people. You can enjoy the scenery of the four seasons from the large window of the dining room, and you can experience the taste of Hokkaido throughout the meal time. As staff who can speak English is available, overseas guests are welcome. There is also a direct sales area in the restaurant, where you can find freshly picked vegetables and fruits, as well as homemade products such as tomato juice made by a producer who is close to the chef. You will want to enjoy an extraordinary time enjoying the vegetables grown in Hokkaido, in the land convenient for transportation from Sapporo city.
nearestStations: 15 minutes by taxi from Maruyama Koen Station (Sapporo City Subway Tozai Line)

245593.longDescription:
本文	美酒美食の町として知られる北海道西部、余市町の余市駅前に店を構えるのが『Yoichi LOOP（ヨイチ ループ）』。ホテルを併設するオーベルジュのレストランとして、国内外から日々多くのゲストを迎える。厨房を任されるのは、札幌市出身のシェフ、成田 汐哉(なりた せきや)氏。ニセコ『KAMIMURA』（閉店）、北品川『カンテサンス』、札幌『Le Musée』といった名店で研鑽を積み、札幌『Le Musée CONCEPT-C』のシェフを務めた後、2020年オープンの『Yoichi LOOP』に、2025年より二代目シェフとして就任。余市の豊かなテロワールを一皿に描き出す。

 9品で繰り広げるコース料理のアミューズは、成田氏のスペシャリテ。生産者の元に足を運び仕入れる食材や、自らが山に入って採取する山菜など、季節の食材3種を盛り合わせ、葉や枝、松ぼっくりなどをデコレーション。まるで余市の森に誘われるような最初の一品だ。釧路・白糠町の敏腕ジビエハンターより届く鹿肉や、帯広の牛肉は薪焼きされ、オープンキッチンからこぼれる薪火の暖かさが店内を包む。ホタテ、ホッキ貝、牡蠣、エビといった魚介はもちろん、「けいら農園」（余市・仁木町）の肉厚なシイタケや、「しあわせチーズ工房」（北海道足寄町）のチーズをアクセントに、夏のウニ、秋冬はキンキのウロコ焼き等、シーズナルメニューも豊富にそろう。

さらに『Yoichi LOOP』の魅力は、いま国内外から人気沸騰中の余市ワインをメインに、フランスやスペイン他、各国の厳選ワインを堪能できること。中でも、余市ワインを知り尽くすサービスマネージャー・ソムリエの倉富 宗（くらとみ そう）氏セレクトのワインペアリングは圧巻。自社の余市ワインをはじめ、「ドメーヌ・タカヒコ」、「平川ワイナリー」、「ランセッカ」、「ドメーヌ･ブレス」等、余市や近郊・北海道の希少なワインをスパークリングからデザートワインまで、コース9品に寄り添う少量9杯をペアリング。ワインペアリングをオーダーして“余市ガストロノミー”体験を完結させることをおすすめしたい。

ダイニングでは、インテリアのように置かれたワインセラーから鮮やかなワインボトルとエチケットが顔をのぞかせ、ゲストをお出迎え。テーブル席（20席）と8名までの個室1室も用意される。プラーベートでもビジネスシーンでもさまざまなシチュエーションで訪れ、極上の余市料理とワインのLOOP＝輪で、美酒美食を楽しまれてはいかがだろうか。	Located opposite Yoichi Station in Yoichi Town, known for its excellent food and wine, in western Hokkaido, Yoichi LOOP is a popular auberge (restaurant with lodging) that attracts guests from across Japan and overseas. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Sekiya Narita. Hailing from Sapporo City, he trained at renowned restaurants, including KAMIMURA (permanently closed) in Niseko, Quintessence in Kitashinagawa, and Le Musée in Sapporo, and worked his way up to Chef at Le Musée CONCEPT-C in Sapporo. Then, in 2025, he took over as the second-generation chef of Yoichi LOOP, which opened its doors in 2020 to celebrate the exquisite wines and rich terroir of Yoichi.

 The nine-course menu starts with the chef’s signature amuse-bouche. Made of three seasonal ingredients, including produce sourced from producers with whom the chef has forged personal ties and edible wild plants picked by the chef himself from the mountains, and decorated with leaves, twigs, and cones, this starter invites diners to the forests of Yoichi. Meanwhile, wild venison hunted by experienced hunters in Kushiro and Shiranuka and beef sourced from Obihiro are wood-fired in the open kitchen, filling the air with a comforting warmth. The menu also features a variety of seafood options, such as scallops, Sakhalin surf clams, oysters, and shrimps, as well as thick shiitake mushrooms from Keira Farm (Niki, Yoichi), flavorful cheeses from Shiawase Cheese Factory (Ashoro, Hokkaido), and various other seasonal flavors, such as sea urchin in summer and Kichiji rockfish cooked with its scales on in autumn and winter.

Another hallmark of Yoichi LOOP is its excellent wine list, mostly consisting of Yoichi wines that have taken the Japanese and international wine markets by storm, but also including international selections from France, Spain, and beyond. However, the most surprising is the list of wine pairings curated by So Kuratomi, Service Manager and Sommelier, who knows Yoichi wines like the back of his hand. The nine small glasses of wine selected to match the nine courses of the meal, ranging from sparkling to dessert wine, sourced from the in-house vineyards as well as Domaine Takahiko, Hirakawa Winery, Lan Seqqua, Domaine Bless, and other wineries across Yoichi and Hokkaido, are the perfect final touches to your gastronomic journey of Yoichi.

Entering the main dining space, guests are welcomed by an interior design-like wine cellar filled with different bottles of wine with different labels on each one. In addition to the main dining room with table seating for up to 20 guests, there is a private dining room seating up to eight guests, making the restaurant ideal for both personal and business occasions. Stay in the loop and enjoy the best of what Yoichi LOOP offers!
nearestStations: 1-minute walk from Yoichi Station on the JR Hokkaido Hakodate Main Line

245424.localizedAddress: 4F, International Passenger Terminal, New Chitose Airport, Mimi, Chitose-shi, Hokkaido
245424.longDescription:
New Chitose Airport, a gateway to Hokkaido, has not only handled a large number of domestic flights but recently also received an increasing number of international flights. Conveniently located with direct access to the international terminal and connected to the domestic terminal by a walkway protected from rain, Hotel Portom International Hokkaido opened in February 2020.

The main restaurant of the hotel, Tateru Yoshino Portom International Hokkaido, boasts a captivating, spacious dining area with a high ceiling. At the center of the dining room, guests are welcomed by four artworks of Hikoju Makie inspired by nature in Hokkaido.

Supervised by Grand Chef Tateru Yoshino, who visits the restaurant every month, the food menu features specialties, such as Tourte (pies), as well as seasonal dishes made with locally grown ingredients.  Located in Hokkaido, rich with all kinds of ingredients, ranging from vegetables and marine products to livestock and dairy products, the restaurant offers entree and homemade seasoning recipes featuring special local products, such as mayonnaise and sabayon sauce made from local passion fruits, and venison tourte made with Ezo deer meat hunted by Matsuno, a hunter from Shiranuka. They are complemented by marine products, including surf clams and whelks from Tomakomai, sea urchins from Shakotan, and abalone from Hiyama.

The drink selection includes a rich collection of French wines, characteristic of Tateru Yoshino. We also offer Japanese wines that are gaining global attention. Additionally, you can enjoy Hokkaido-produced fromage, such as “Fromage de Biei” from Biei Farm, paired with wine.

The main dining room with a modern interior in monochromatic tones seats up to 86 guests, complemented by a private room seating up to 12 guests.  Ready as an air gateway for travelers of different ages and nationalities, it is perfect not only for gourmet gatherings but also for meals with international guests.

The beautiful interiors of the hotel reminiscent of an art museum also makes the restaurant worth visiting. Adorned with ukiyo-e paintings by renowned painters, such as Katsushika Hokusai and Utagawa Hiroshige, and artworks and installations created using plastering and dyeing techniques, Portom International Hokkaido offers art tours for diners before and after their meals on prior request to hotel staff. Enjoy French dishes made with rich local ingredients and artful cooking techniques to delight your eyes and palates at Tateru Yoshino Portom International Hokkaido.


■To guests arriving by car
Please use the airport parking lot as the hotel parking lot is for "Guests only".

244733.longDescription:
“Shinonome” is located in a quiet residential area just outside the downtown area, close to Maruyama Park in Sapporo City, Hokkaido. Chef Wataru Nakahara, who is a local, serves Hokkaido  Edomae-style sushi.

The name of the restaurant comes from chef Nakahara's hometown of Shinonome, Higashikawa-cho, Hokkaido. Shinonome means ‘dawn’, and the wish that we do not forget our original intention. Chef Nakahara has a unique background in his previous job at a special effects company for movies and commercials. However, he felt that he could not directly see the audience's reaction to his work. Through his interest in fish and hobby of fishing, he entered the world of cooking where he knew he would be able to see customers’ reactions to the dishes he had created. After training at a sushi restaurant in Tokyo for five years and practicing the techniques and knowledge of sushi, he returned home. In 2016, he opened “Shinonome”.

The nigiri of “Shinonome” is a unique sushi that uses lots of ingredients from Hokkaido and is based on chef Nakahara's own interpretation of Edomae sushi techniques. For example, taking a hint from the kelp that sea urchins eat, making homemade salted kelp, and mixing it with additive-free sea urchins. His trick of adding special touches and twists for each ingredient is a similar approach to that which he used in his previous job when creating special effects and the result is a type of sushi that is truly unique. His vinegared rice is a blend of "Nanaboshi" rice made in Higashikawa-cho and "Yumepirika" old rice. The water used is "Asahidake Gensui", from the highest peak in the Daisetsuzan mountain range in Higashikawa-cho where rice is able to grow. The vinegar is based on the premium red vinegar matured for 10 years by Iio Jozo of Tango, Kyoto, and is blended with 2 kinds of rice vinegar made by the company. "Our first priority is vinegared rice. The brown rice we receive is only polished on the same day. The entire process is carefully timed and cooked in a rice-cooker so that the rice has a nice outline. I want to make sushi with a ratio of 6:4 so that the impression of the vinegared rice is strong and the flavor is a rich explosion when both are mixed in the mouth" said chef Nakahara. The soy sauce used is from Kajita Shoten "Tatsumi Soy sauce" in Ehime Prefecture which is additive-free and has been matured for a long time.

There are usually 8 kinds of Japanese sake available, including hot sake and also those that are not on the menu, so please request your favorite. They also have wine, shochu and whiskey. The glasses and bowls that the drinks are served in are mainly those that have been made by artists from Hokkaido, such as Iwamizawa "Kobushiyaki” and from Mawatari Shinpei in Yoichi.

The L-shaped counter (8 seats) in the restaurant uses Tenryu cypress from Shizuoka. Seating for 9-10 people is also available upon reservation. Please enjoy chef Nakahara's original sushi with your family, close friends and colleagues.

244580.longDescription:
""Nukumi"" is located right in the heart of Sapporo, a Japanese city in Hokkaido. This world gourmet guide award Japanese cuisine restaurant is located near Nakajima Park in an area lush with greenery. Take one step from the concrete exterior of the restaurant and you will find chef and owner Masaki Yamamoto showing off his craft in a warm restaurant atmosphere furnished with wood befitting the name Nukumi, meaning warmth.

Chef Yamamoto was born in Sapporo. Determined to become a chef, he trained at ""Koya,"" a famous Japanese restaurant in Sapporo, become an executive chef after five years.  He then trained at ""Kagaman"" in Osaka before moving to Hong Kong as a chef at the Consulate-General of Japan in Hong Kong. After returning to Japan he became executive chef at the Japanese restaurant in The Windsor Hotel TOYA before opening the Nukumi Japanese restaurant in 2006. He was awarded world gourmet guide award in 2012. This outstanding restaurant moved to its current premises in 2016 and was awarded world gourmet guide award the following year.

The owner-Chef Yamamoto has a strong belief in being faithful to the fundamentals. In addition, ""Nukumi"" cuisine is made with love, while at the same time always on the cutting edge of cuisine. Yamamoto explains, ""Rather than simply coasting reputation alone, I have a fresh desire each day to provide guests with delicious food using ingredients carefully selected and prepared with love."" These delicious in-season and high-quality ingredients naturally include those locally sourced from Hokkaido, as well as ingredients from across Japan, such as snow crab and Kagayasai from Kanazawa, puffer fish from Kyushu, and Kyoyasai from Kyoto.

There is also a special focus on the dashi stock, the essence of Japanese cuisine. Ichiban dashi, the first brew of the stock, uses top-quality natural Rishiri Kombu. The niban dashi, the second brew of the stock, uses the finest Rausu kombu. The bonito is sourced from different regions depending on the season, and a supplier that carries Sapporo dried bonito provides daily deliveries of freshly shaved Hongarebushi bonito. The restaurant is dedicated to preparing dashi stock with only the finest flavor and umami. 

An array of Japanese sake to pair with the dishes is available, including junmai, junmai daiginjo, and daiginjo, each with its own charm. In addition to 6 types of main menu selections, there are 2 to 3 recommended seasonal selections. In addition, there are 2 to 3 selections of specialty sake for those who have their own preferences, all sure to consistently entice any fancier of Japanese sake.

The first floor of the restaurant interior features 6 private rooms, while the second floor is equipped with table seats as well as four counter seats. The bright restaurant space gives a clear view of the colorful abundance of food on your plate. The relaxed environment furnished with natural wood allows for a leisurely meal, perfect for couples, family dining, or dining with friends in private. This cozy Japanese restaurant is also well suited for business interactions, such as dining with colleagues or entertaining guests.
