244637.longDescription:
Approximately 3-minute on foot from Susukino Station in the heart of Sapporo, on a side street in the bustling downtown area, stands a world gourmet guide award French restaurant where Sapporo-born chef Akihiro Nagao displays his global culinary skills, ""Aki Nagao"".

Chef Nagao moved to Tokyo when he was 19 and trained for 5 years at a French restaurant there. When he was 26, he moved to France to train in the homeland of French cuisine. He returned to his homeland after mastering classical French cuisine with 3 years of diligent training at a world gourmet guide award ""Relais Louis XIII"", Hotel Prieure in Avignon of Southern France, and ""La Maison de la Lozère"" in Montpellier of Southern France. He opened ""Aki Nagao"" in 2010 after further polishing his skills at restaurants such as ""MARU:NI"" in Maruyama, Sapporo.

Chef Nagao aims to present the essence of Hokkaido using the ingredients brought forth by the wonderful producers all around the country. From amuse-bouche to dessert, he uses his own inspiration to top each plate with the best of the season so that guests can take in the four seasons of Hokkaido from course to course. He focuses not only on local production for local consumption but has widened his view to include great ingredients from the whole country. He does this because he believes his home to be not Hokkaido but, looking from a global point of view, all of Japan. ""Noma, which has been crowned the best restaurant in the world 4 times, is said to practice local production for local consumption. However, they actually use not only ingredients from Copenhagen but from all of Northern Europe. In other words, from a global point of view, whether the restaurant is in Sapporo or anywhere else in the country, using Japanese ingredients is what local production for local consumption means for a restaurant in Japan. Precisely because I am Japanese myself, I would like to express the beauty of this 'hometown = Japan' concept,"" says Chef Nagao.
His specialty is his oyster cuisine. Many guests visit the restaurant hoping to partake of his dishes prepared using deep-sea water with seasonable oysters from all over Japan, including Akkeshi, Hokkaido. The restaurant's Wine selections are carefully chosen not only by the sommelier, but also by the chef and other kitchen staff. The selection focuses on French wine and includes plenty of Hokkaido wines from excellent producers gathered in the local area as well. The restaurant also opens up a new world for guests with their Vin Naturel Pairing which pairs natural wines from around the world based on flavor regardless of production area.

The restaurant's exterior is the blue walls often seen in Europe. The interior walls are made of antique bricks imported from Europe and create a beautiful contrast with the 360° all stainless steel kitchen. The restaurant's make-up closely reflects Chef Nagao's culinary concept of having something new placed in the midst of the old. A dining room with table seating as well as private rooms (for 2 – 8 guests), which can accommodate guests in strollers and wheelchairs as well, are available here. Guests here can enjoy the cuisine which embodies Chef Nagao's worldview on any occasion, including with friends and family, together with co-workers, or on dates.

I can see the whole team’s efforts and the chef’s thoughtfulness. We kindly ask that guests refrain from visiting if they are wearing strong fragrances such as perfume or hair products.
Our cuisine is carefully prepared by the chef to highlight its delicate aromas and flavors, and strong scents may compromise not only your own experience but also that of other guests.
Fragrances can permeate the air, interfering with the aromas of the dishes and affecting the overall dining environment.
Should a strong scent significantly impact the restaurant atmosphere, we may, with regret, ask for your cooperation in adjusting reservation times or relocating seats.
We sincerely appreciate your understanding and cooperation so that all of our guests may enjoy a comfortable dining experience.

【Attention】Due to the snow in the center of Sapporo, it will be hard to get a taxi. Traffic jam is also expected. Please use public transportation and arrive the restaurant with time to spare.
■Important Information for Guests Visiting in Winter
During the winter season, heavy snowfall in central Sapporo may make it difficult to find taxis, and traffic congestion may also delay your arrival at the restaurant.
We kindly recommend using public transportation and allowing sufficient time when planning your visit.

244742.longDescription:
1-minute walk from Hosui Susukino Station on the Toho Subway Line, “TATEOKA TAKESHI” is a 1-star French restaurant in a convenient location near Susuki, the busiest area in Sapporo.


Owner-chef, Takeshi Tateoka is from Otaru-city, Hokkaido. He went to France at the age of 24, and trained in "Les Templiers” in Vence, Southern France, "Restaurant du Palais Royal" and "Au Bon Accueil" in Paris. He also worked at a 1-star restaurant "Passiflore" and "NAMIKI" in Southern France. He was then entrusted with the role of Poisson Chef (fish chef) for 1 year at the 3-star restaurant "Maison Troisgros" in Roanne. After returning to Japan at the age of 31, he worked as a chef at the restaurant where he is now, and after that, he changed the name and concept of the restaurant and re-opened it as “TATEOKA TAKESHI”, in November 2016. In April 2017, just six months after its opening, it received one star in a world-renowned gourmet guide. The restaurant also won the 17th Toque d’Or Contest in the Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Awards.

We offer omakase courses using the best ingredients of the season, focusing on seafood and vegetables, in the hope that you will experience the natural aroma, taste, and essence of Hokkaido's ingredients. We hope you will enjoy our dishes with natural wines and the flavor and aroma of Japan's unique climate. Mr. Tateoka focuses on the "sense of ingredients”. The combination of ingredients, cooking methods, and temperatures are used to create a dish with a rich taste. This is a special dish created here in Hokkaido with Japanese ingredients and Tateoka's French experience. Using ingredients he makes himself (Hokkaido pickled plums, koji miso made from Tokachi soybeans, tomato seasoning made from Yoichi Amakko, and homemade seasoning fermented from ginger, radish, tomatoes, etc.), Tateoka's cuisine provides "a sense of ingredients”. Ingredients are purchased directly from trusted farmers and fishermen. We hope you will enjoy Mr. Tateoka's world view, in which he continues to consider the essence of ingredients on a daily basis.

The dishes at the restaurant were designed based on the image of the colors and shapes of Mr. Tateoka's cuisine and were custom made by artists and pottery artisans several years before the restaurant opened. There are about 500 kinds of wine on the drinks menu. They have a large selection of natural wines mainly from France, Hokkaido and around the world. In addition, they brew tea such as genmaicha and bancha every day, so that guests who do not drink wine can can enjoy it.  The combination of the cuisine, dishes, bowls and drinks married together, complete a memorable gourmet experience for any guest that visits Tateoka.


A modern restaurant in white decor, with a spacious dining room and large tables that are well-spaced out meaning that you can relax quietly without worrying about other guests. In addition, 1 private room is available to reserve for 2 to 8 people and 3 seats at the counter. You can rest assured that an English menu will be prepared for foreign guests. Visit Tateoka to enjoy the taste of the four seasons of Hokkaido on your plate, when celebrating family anniversaries, on a date or entertaining overseas guests.
nearestStations: A 1-minute walk from Hosui Susukino Station, Exit 2, (Sapporo City Subway Toho Line)

244508.longDescription:
Chef Masaya Miyashita stayed on a single course of the trajectory to gain his culinary know-how by training for 20 years in traditional Japanese cuisine at Japanese-style restaurants in Hokkaido. As a first-rate sushi chef, he took his firm understanding of the basic tenets of classic Japanese food to open up his own sushi restaurant, "Takuzushi," which won further validation after earning a star. The restaurant opened its doors in Sapporo in 2010, and then later it relocated to a quieter neighborhood in 2013. Today it continues to serve the "best sushi made from the day's freshest ingredients."

Chef Miyashita is extremely particular when it comes to his ingredients. His fastidiousness and desire to always search for the best led him to assemble trusted relationships with fresh fish distributors at Tsukiji Fish Market. These connections give him access to fresh, seasonal ingredients that he uses to build up a first class menu of food. Chef Miyashita's penchant for fine quality ingredients isn't just limited to the selection at Tsukiji Fish Market either. Even if it's a just a minor difference that separates one ingredient's quality from another, he will nonetheless search locally in Sapporo and across Japan if he has to in order to find the very best selection available. After searching for top seafood ingredients like these that are unparalleled in quality, Chef Miyashita uses his culinary dexterity to elevate the ingredients even further and create the sublime sushi that "Takuzushi" is known for. Their sushi starts with white rice that is patiently cooked with an earthenware pot in order to condense the rice's inherently savory umami flavor. The rice is then combined with fermented red vinegar, which has a mellow acidity and rich flavor. Their sushi rice's high quality shines through while also highlighting the seafood's own inherent flavors. The sushi rice, toppings, wasabi, and soy sauce all work together like a golden ratio to achieve a perfect balance. Chef Miyashita is indeed the only one who can create these finely crafted culinary works that represent the menu at "Takuzushi." The sushi here is further complemented by drinks as well, including refreshingly smooth Japanese sake, as well as Burgundy wine, champagne, and other French wines with delicate, subtle flavors.

Inside guests will find counter seating along with private dining rooms that can accommodate 8 and 2 guests respectively. To ensure that guests can enjoy the restaurant's high-end sushi in the best setting possible, they offer a calm and composed Japanese-style dining space that is also chic and modern at the same time. This includes their selection of ceramics, black lacquerware, and other tableware pieces. When guests dine at "Takuzushi" they are sure to have a remarkable time as they dine on top-class sushi prepared by Chef Miyashita. A memorable dining experience like this is the perfect addition to any trip to Hokkaido.

244515.longDescription:
1-star French Restaurant Banquet is located in a quiet residential area somewhat away from the city center, 10-minute walk from Nishi-18chome Station in Sapporo, Hokkaido. Hokkaido-born the owner-chef Kohei Wakasugi trained in 1-star restaurant Vivarois in Paris before moving on to 3-star restaurant Guerard in Landes, where he refined his skills further in his position as the chef in charge of fish dishes. He then gained experience in numerous starred restaurants before going independent. Chef Wakasugi is a talented player in the world of French cuisine, with achievements such as coming runner-up in 2002 in the All Japan French Food Contest, presented by the French Food Culture Center (FFCC).

For Chef Wakasugi, it is important to be a high-quality “petit maison,” an intimate restaurant where he can interact with each customer individually and have them enjoy the best of French cuisine with roots in the local area. He incorporates the rich range of ingredients—agricultural produce, livestock products, and seafood—offered by Hokkaido’s blessed natural environment into all of his dishes. The French cuisine that can only be enjoyed in Banquet comes into being through a combination of 3 ingredients with the techniques that Chef Wakasugi acquired in France. Each and every dish is finished by carefully attending to the various details that are involved to create a result that is a supreme dish, unique to the day on which it is served. In particular, Chef Wakasugi signature dish is Blue Lobster: a Homage to Michel Guerard, which is created using the finest blue lobster. The dish expresses his warm sentiments for Michel Guerard and is a masterpiece that every customer must try. In the fall, we recommend the varied dishes created from deer, the game that Chef Wakasugi commissions local hunters to hunt. Wine on offer is the focus on a selection of French and Hokkaido vintages that go well with Chef Wakasugi’s cuisine.

French Restaurant Banquet offers a limited of 1 table seating (up to 8 people) and a private room (up to 6 people) a day. Sitting at the tables, customers can view the chef cooking and also enjoy how the food is being prepared. Whether you are a food connoisseur living in Hokkaido or are from another part of Japan or some other place in the world, if you wish to truly savor genuine French cuisine created from the abundant ingredients found in Hokkaido, this is a restaurant that we recommend you visit.

※The meal tickets listed on the restaurant's official website cannot be used if you make a reservation through Pocket Concierge. Thank you for your understanding.

244374.longDescription:
Susukino Naniwatei is located at the center of Susukino, a premier shopping district in Hokkaido. It is conveniently located close to Susukino metro station. The first generation of owners, a husband, and wife from Osaka moved to Hokkaido and opened for business in 1962, establishing a restaurant which is popular among a wide range of people, from the selective palates of locals to visiting tourists.

The original owners have tried to recreate the familiar tastes of Kansai in Hokkaido. Starting with the procurement of ingredients, they buy both the abundant local ingredients of Hokkaido as well as those of Kansai, garnering them a reputation for providing nostalgic tastes of home. Currently, a new generation has taken over, with the original owners’ sons, Koji and Takeshi Murai, handling the management of the restaurant. Each of them has trained at restaurants on the main island of Japan, bringing back with them the lessons they have absorbed and adding new layers of attraction atop a foundation of tradition.

The theme of their cuisine is fresh ingredients, and they use their own expertise to gather the rare bounties from the mountains and seas of Hokkaido and the rest of Japan. Using their creativity, they then carefully draw out the delicious flavors of each ingredient. For example, after serving salted and grilled kichiji rockfish from Abashiri, the bones are broiled and made into a clear broth. Rank A4-A5 Hokkaido wagyu beef fillet is made into a Japanese style steak using the sauce made with red wine and tamari soy sauce—a specialty since the restaurant’s founding—and finished by making a fried rice which allows the diner to enjoy the food without wasting a bite. In addition to these specialty dishes, the restaurant provides plenty of local Hokkaido flavors every day for guests to enjoy, such as fresh asparagus and Sakhalin surf clam or Japanese scallop grilled in butter. With both a la carte and course meal options available, the restaurant responds flexibly to guests’ requests, from ingredients from across Hokkaido to seasonal ingredients such as natural puffer fish or soft-shelled turtle courses. Alcoholic beverages available include sake from Hokkaido breweries as well as brands from across Japan.

Guests can sit at the 14 seats before the white cypress wood counter or in the private room. The restaurant is suitable for business entertainment or special celebrations, and recently overseas visitors have been increasing. To experience the first-rate cuisine and hospitality offered by Susukino Naniwatei, it is worth coming to the Susukino area to visit this venerable Japanese restaurant.

245381.localizedAddress: Matsuoka Bldg. 1F (in Susukino Naniwatei), 4-7, Minami4-jonishi, Chuo-ku, Sapporo-shi, Hokkaido
245381.longDescription:
--
Before making a reservation, please be sure to read the “Reservation Policy” in the middle of this page.
--
Having opened its doors in Sapporo in 1962, the long-established Japanese restaurant, Susukino Naniwatei, shares its entrance with another restaurant, Tempura Masa, where Chef Masayuki Murai offers what he calls “Ezomae” tempura.

Born as the third generation of Susukino Naniwatei, Murai trained for seven years at Kikunoi, a long-established Japanese restaurant in Kyoto. Then, following the advice of his father, who was running Susukino Naniwatei as the second-generation owner at the time, he moved to Tokyo to learn tempura cooking techniques at a renowned restaurant, Tempura Kondo. In April 2021, he returned to his hometown to open Tempura Masa. The kanji character for “Masa” in the restaurant’s logo was handwritten by his father with a mixture of black ink and oil and flour from Tempura Kondo. This implies his father’s high expectations for the third-generation owner of the tempura restaurant.

Tempura Masa only offers prix-fixe menus, each consisting of a couple of seasonal dishes and some 10 pieces of tempura made with local seafood and vegetables to celebrate the seasonal bounty of Hokkaido. For example, in the spring, tempura made from edible wild plants picked by Chef Murai is served with a story about how he collected the plants. His seasonal menus include not only local specialties, such as scallops and sea urchins, but also other local products, such as mackerel and sailfin sandfish, so that guests can explore the diverse flavors of Hokkaido.

The tempura is deep-fried in a blend of untoasted and lightly toasted sesame oil. The flour is dehydrated in the fridge for three days until it becomes dry and smooth like powdered snow. His perfectionism extends to the iron pots that he asked a professor at Muroran Institute of Technology to make for cooking rice, which he uses to cook a local brand of rice called Yumepirika. Served as the last course of a meal, the rice cooked with a lavish amount of seasonal seafood and stock in these iron pots is a special treat only available at this restaurant.

The wine and sake lists also feature local specialties. Among them, Nanatsumori Pinot Noir from Domaine Takahiko pairs perfectly with the Shiitake Tempura offered by Chef Murai, as guaranteed by the owner of the winery.

The restaurant’s interior also uses many local materials, as exemplified by the walls partly covered with soft stone from Sapporo and the eight-seat counter made of oak from Asahikawa. Please enjoy the “Ezomae” tempura cooked by Chef Murai with respect and affection for local products to your heart’s content with your family, friends, colleagues or partner.
nearestStations: 2 minutes walk from Exit 2 of Susukino Station on Namboku Line

244744.longDescription:
“Sushi Watanabe Sapporo” is located just a 4 minute-walk from Susukino Station in Sapporo City, Hokkaido. It is on the 6th floor of the building. In downtown Sapporo, which is visited by many tourists from Japan and abroad, chef Tomohito Watanabe creates the "Ezomae Sushi".

Born in Hokkaido, chef Watanabe trained at famous Japanese restaurants and sushi restaurants in Tokyo and worked as a chef from an early age. With the "Edomae techniques" he cultivated in Tokyo, he returned to his hometown, Nakashibetsu and became independent. Later, it became known as the first "Ezomae Sushi" in the Doto area, and continues to operate to this day. While working as a sushi chef, he also devoted himself to training young people. He left the Nakashibetsu main restaurant to his young protege, who had trained under him for 10 years and became his right-hand man. In 2018, he opened his 2nd store in Susukino, the busiest district in Hokkaido, where he stands at the counter and serves the guests himself.

“Sushi Watanabe Sapporo” uses ingredients from Hokkaido (especially from eastern Hokkaido where Nakashibetsu is located) and uses Edomae techniques to make "Ezomae Sushi". Hokkaido "Yumepirika" rice and a blend of red vinegar and rice vinegar is used to make their vinegared rice. The signature dish is the "abalone". After steaming the abalone, liver sauce made from abalone liver, sea urchin and seaweed is mixed with vinegared rice. In addition, they also offer abalone soup, and even "Abalone sake (with dashi)", a luxurious dish where guests can enjoy three levels of flavors. The homemade tofu, which uses premium soybeans from Nakashibetsu, is also popular. The town of Nakashibetsu, which produces high-quality milk, has adopted a "be filled with milk" campaign and guests at the restaurant are welcomed with a cup of milk. They have 70 ~ 80 kinds of sake from around the country to pair with the dishes and various preferences of their customers. There are also 10 types of champagne available. The bowls are mainly made by local artists, and some of them are plates that Mr. Watanabe has made himself.

The restaurant has 8 L-shaped counter seats, table seats (up to 4 people) and 2 private rooms with a sunken kotatsu (up to 6 people). We would like you to enjoy Mr. Watanabe's "Ezomae Sushi" when dining and dating with family and friends, business events, such as entertaining clients, and welcoming guests from overseas.


■Notes
This restaurant is the Sapporo branch of the main store “Sushi Watanabe” located in Nakashibetsu, Hokkaido.
Please be aware that this restaurant has no affiliation with the restaurant of the same name, “Sushi Watanabe” based in Tokyo.
nearestStations: A 4-minute walk from Susukino Station on the Sapporo Municipal Subway Namboku Line

245463.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from the intersection of Susukino in downtown Sapporo, Matsukura is hidden in the basement of a building, offering an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. Established in 1962, the restaurant has been passed down through three generations.

“We carry on the passion of our founder, stay curious, and keep exploring the potential of local ingredients,” said Kazuaki Matsukura, who has inherited the passion of his predecessors and taken over the restaurant as the third-generation owner after apprenticing at renowned restaurants in Kyoto and Kamakura.  He applies his sincere passion for cooking and his knowledge and skills acquired through his training and experience to create his own Hokkaido cuisine featuring local ingredients from the rich nature found in the region.

Matsukura offers an elaborate prix-fixe menu, in which each course gradually becomes more and more flavorful as the meal proceeds, allowing diners to enjoy the true flavors and aromas of seasonal ingredients.
The seasonal soup is made with a broth made from kombu seaweed from Hokkaido, spring water from Mt. Yotei, and dried bonito flakes shaved by the owner-chef right in front of guests. This entire cooking process will engage all five senses.

The subtly flavored courses end with Matsukura Potato, the specialty of the restaurant passed down from the founder. Made by slowly and carefully steaming locally grown potatoes with local butter, spring water, natural salt, and wild honey, the melt-in-your-mouth potato and butter represents the taste of traditional Hokkaido cuisine.  As exemplified by this dish, the third-generation owner-chef continues to delight the taste buds of guests by recreating the recipes and passion of his grandfather.

To satisfy the appetite of each guest, the meal ends with a grain dish, which can be chosen from three options. Among these popular items, the salt ramen served in a simple yet rich broth made from local fish bones, locally brewed sake, and natural salt especially represents the taste of Hokkaido cuisine.
Matsukura always keeps about 20 varieties of sake in stock, including not only bottles from Hokkaido but also from around Japan, to pair with seasonal dishes. The restaurant also offers fine wines that pair well with Japanese dishes.

The restaurant’s interior is cozy with wood accents. In addition to the main dining room with a seven-seat counter, there is a semi-private room with a table and four chairs. In principle, the restaurant can only accommodate children who can eat the same meals as adults, but younger children are also welcomed when it is booked exclusively. Owner-chef Matsukura explains his dishes in English to guests from abroad. These features make the restaurant the perfect place to celebrate a special occasion or make your trip to Hokkaido memorable.

With easy access to quality ingredients from around Hokkaido, Matsukura offers Hokkaido cuisine featuring local vegetables, edible wild plants, and seafood. Please come and enjoy seasonal flavors from the fertile lands of Hokkaido.

244491.longDescription:
“Sushi Himeshara”, a two star sushi restaurant, moved from Susukino in Hokkaido to the Maruyama Park area in December 2017. The owner, Akira Tanaka, was highly praised for his skill as a sushi chef during his training in Japanese cuisine and sushi. He went independent in 2003 after gaining experience in many different sushi restaurants. With its well-earned two star rating, Sushi Himeshara has a reputation as one of the finest sushi restaurants in Hokkaido, drawing many guests, both Japanese and international, to the restaurant.

The kanji for "sushi" combines the characters of "fish" and "delicious." Based on that same idea, "Sushi Himeshara" uses the written characters of "fish", "rice", and "delicious", to conceptualize its own sushi. The idea is that fish combined with rice is what makes sushi taste delicious. "Sushi is prepared inside the mouth," Tanaka said. Sushi is the synergy created by its elements of vinegared rice and seafood mixing together in the mouth, while experiencing the aroma coming out through the nose. Two types of red vinegar are used for vinegared rice at Sushi Himeshara. The course menu consists of sushi, assorted appetizers, and then a final round of sushi at the end, attracting guests with its unique style. 

Tanaka-san is a veteran chef and when asked about how he developed his course menu concept, he explains that it was born from his idea of sushi throughout the season. At the beginning of the season, when sake is not ready yet, he wants the taste of the sushi to be clear. Then when the sake is ready in the middle of the season, it can be enjoyed with snacks that he carefully selects to pair with the sake. Finally at the end, he wants his guests to feel moved by the sushi again. One of our specialties, "Topped with all shrimp" is a beautiful and luxurious dish with vinegared rice, using Botan shrimp, shrimp miso and shrimp eggs layered in a mille-feuille style. The freshly prepared sushi is handed over the counter for guests to enjoy its rich flavor and they will savor every single bite of this truly superb sushi, without leaving so much as a crumb on their plates.

Tanaka-san deliberately designed his restaurant to be a simple space so that guests can enjoy the experience of watching the sushi being prepared impeccably in front of them and savoring its delicious taste without distractions. The interior of the restaurant is simple with a basic black base and without any hints of excess or unnecessary flashiness in the design. The counter is made of Japanese cypress and the specially made ice room, which only two woodworkers in Japan have the skill to make, provides a strong presence in the space, contributing to an extraordinary atmosphere. Enjoy Edomae style sushi made with the very best ingredients in the ever-evolving sushi scene in Hokkaido at Sushi Himeshara.

244674.longDescription:
Shimoyami Tenaeizuru is a restaurant located in downtown Sapporo near Nakajima Park, not far from Susukino. The fine cuisine by Chef Hikaru Igarashi, known as ""the Genius of Sapporo,"" is enough to impress even the most discerning of gourmands. After graduating from high school, Chef Igarashi was working at a hotel before leaving for France at age 24. There he worked at a world gourmet guide award restaurant for 3 years. After returning to Japan, he honed his skills at several Sapporo restaurants before going independent. In 2013, he opened his own restaurant, Igarashi. The restaurant soon became very popular, but closed after five years. Chef Igarashi established his restaurant with the intention of offering French cuisine, but he then undergone a change in heart, and was inspired to strip away the unnecessary elements from his cooking. He decided to create minimalist cuisine that defies genre conventions. Seeking a fresh start, he opened Shimoyami Tenaeizuru in 2019.
The restaurant name Shimoyami Tenaeizuru is a seasonal word referring to one of Japan's 72 microseasons. It describes the time in late April when the frost recedes and the rice plants begin to sprout. At this time, Hokkaido's natural scenery turns lush with greenery. ""In line with this natural image, I don't use chemical seasonings in my cooking,"" says Chef Igarashi. There is a reason why he chose a Japanese name. ""My cooking is categorized as 'French,' but it no longer fits neatly within that category."" He incorporates French tastes into his cooking while emphasizing originality. Because Hokkaido is known for its high quality fish, the star ingredient of many of his dishes is fish caught off the shores of the prefecture. Many regulars are drawn back again and again for his specialty, dotted gizzard shad terrine. Of course, he also serves excellent quality meat. The course consists of 15-20 dishes. Chef Igarashi explains that ""I want diners to enjoy cuisine that's Japanese but not Japanese in style, here at a restaurant in Japan."" For drinks, in addition to shochu and sake, a selection of French natural wines is on offer. Chef Igarashi stays in constant contact with the producers, exchanging information to ensure he has the choicest wines on his shelves. The unbeatable combination of delicious food and wine is something you won't find anywhere else.
The restaurant interior showcases Japanese tastes. The doors open with a clatter, and when you step across a courtyard and onto a platform where you remove your shoes, you are greeted with the pleasant aroma of tatami mats. There are six sunken kotatsu counter seats. ""Genius of Sapporo"" Chef Igarashi's cuisine is a great choice for a sit-down meal with family, friends, colleagues, or fellow food lovers.

244892.longDescription:
Five minutes by car from JR Hakodate Station or the Shiden Jujigai Station, and then a five-minute walk up to the Nijukenzaka, you will find Maison FUJIYA Hakodate. In Motomachi, Hakodate’s most iconic tourist destination, second-generation chef Yuki Ito showcases his culinary talent.

Chef Ito was selected as the "Focus Chef" at Japan's largest French cuisine event, "France Restaurant Week 2024," from among more than 500 participating restaurants nationwide. This honor is reserved for promising chefs expected to earn Michelin stars in the future. Born in Kutchan, Hokkaido, Chef Ito crafts dishes that celebrate not only the rich ingredients of Hokkaido but also the seasonal produce of Hakodate and the southern Hokkaido region. His cuisine is designed to be a feast for all five senses—flavor, texture, aroma, and visual appeal.

He mainly uses ingredients from Donan, Hokkaido, including Shinai oysters, local masu salmon, Hakodate's various squids, hairy crabs, conger eels, scallops, surf clams, and king shiitake mushrooms from Nanae Town. He makes the best use of the finest ingredients to build dishes that are sure to be remembered by diners.
The wine pairings that accompany the cuisine also reflect a strong desire to share “Made in Hakodate” with the world. With deep passion, the team curates wines ranging from classic French selections to locally produced wines from Hokkaido. These include bottles from the renowned Norakura Winery near Hakodate, as well as grapes grown in the Kikyo area of Hakodate by Étienne de Montille, the owner of the famed Domaine de Montille in Burgundy. Sommeliers from maison FUJIYA Hakodate even assist in the vineyard work. In addition to wine, sake brewed in Donan is also thoughtfully selected to complement the dishes.

The interior of the restaurant, which has an open, light feeling, has wooden chairs from Carl Hansen & Søn and tables with white crosses, creating a natural atmosphere where the food and the superb view blend together. The dishes are accentuated by a wide variety of dinnerware, such as those ordered from glass artists in Otaru and Toyako, Arita-ware, and J.L Coquet from France. There are 30 seats in total, with table seats and semi-private rooms for up to 10 people. A casual bistro is on the first floor. For special occasions such as anniversaries and celebrations, please visit Maison FUJIYA Hakodate with your family, friends and colleagues, and enjoy the idea of "Made in Hakodate."
nearestStations: A 10-minute by bus or tram from Hakodate Station (JR Hakodate Main Line (Hakodate - Oshamanbe), JR Esashi Line)

どの料理も非常に美味しかった。地元の食材の魅力をふんだんに引き出していて本当に素晴らしい体験になった。カスベのボールは何度食べてもいいくらい好きだし、だけど今回一番驚いたのはエイヒレ。あんなにビネガーが香るのに混ぜて食べてみるとアクセントとしての酸味だけで、エイの旨みをまったく邪魔せず引き出していたのが良かった。ホタテも分厚さを活かして外は香ばしく、中は絶妙なレアな火加減がまさに職人技。ぜひまた食べに行きたいと思いました。

結婚一周年記念日に利用させてもらいました。
昨年のプロポーズの際に利用させてもらったときもそうでしたが、藤谷シェフがつくるフレンチのコースは見た目ももちろん味もとても素晴らしくて感動しました。特に豊富なアイデアがつまったアラカルトやメインのお肉料理は絶品でした。それに加えてスタッフの方々のおもてなしがとても良かったです。料理に合うドリンクを丁寧に説明してくださったりお腹がいっぱいで食べれなかったデザートを包んでいただいたりと対応が素晴らしく、また絶対にきたいなと思わせてもらえるお店でした。
ありがとうございました。

旅の締めくくりにMaison Fujiyaで最高の体験ができ、心に残る函館旅行となりました。
怪我の同行者に配慮下さり感謝します。
違う季節ではどんなお料理がでてくるのか、再訪が今から待ち遠しいです。

実は今日、一緒に行く予定の人がキャンセルとなり、予定外の人、しかも偶然誕生日という人をお連れしました。「誕生日おめでとう。乾杯」っていうのをお店の人が聞いててくれたみたいで、蝋燭を立てたケーキが振舞われました。私も事前に行ってたわけじゃないので、ほんとにビックリしました。そのケーキのプレートのデコレーションも美しかったです。やられました。借りができた感じです。誰か美しい人がセットできたら、また予約したいと思います。今日はありがとうございました。

味はもちろんですが、道南を中心とした道産食材にこだわり、雰囲気、ロケーションも素晴らしく、また、高級でありながらも、リラックスできる接客サービス。
とても心地よいあっという間の2時間30分時間でした。

記念日にまた、利用させていただきたいです。
量も満足！

いつも、お料理はもちろんとても美味しく、スタッフの皆様にとても暖かくお迎え頂き、更に素敵な景色を眺めながら食事が出来て、全て全てのおもてなしが素敵で幸せな気持ちにさせて頂きました。
いつもありがとうございます。
感謝しております。

全てのお料理が美味しく、常に気持ちの良い応対をしてくれたので最高のディナーになりました。

ありがとうございました。
前回同様、お料理も美味しく、接客も素敵でまた伺いたいと思えるお店です。母も大変喜んでおりました。ありがとうございました。ごちそうさまでした。

I am very satisfied with the food, customer service, and atmosphere of the restaurant.  In particular, the dishes were traditional French with a slight twist, and I think they were harmonious and made the best use of Japanese ingredients.  Also, if you have a chance to visit Hakodate, I would like to visit you.
とても美味しかったです。

今日は、本当にありがとうございました。お料理も接客も大変素晴らしく、美味しかったです。サプライズのバースデープレートケーキも本当にありがとうございました。ひとつ質問ですが、サーモンのアミューズは、鮮やかな花びらなどをを散りばめたイクラののったものでしたでしょうか？お料理がたくさんでてきたので、どれかわからなくなってしまいまして。
また伺いたいと思います。ありがとうございました。
ひと品の量が適切で、多くの料理を楽しめました。ほぼ道南の食材を使って、創意工夫された本物の料理を堪能しました。

今回は結婚記念日で伺わせていただきました。
来店前からお電話をくださったり、お店でも細やかな気遣いが素晴らしく、ストレスなくお食事を楽しませていただきました。
お料理もとても美味しく、楽しいものでした。
チーズの盛り合わせは、様々なチーズの味を知ることができ、驚きや面白さもあり大変楽しませていただきました。配膳してくださる方も皆さま気さくで、お料理の説明など細やかでとても満足しました。
良い結婚記念日と函館旅行のスタートをきれました。
記念日のプレートと焼き菓子もとても嬉しく、良いお土産になりました！今から食べます！笑
また、函館に来た際にはお食事に行かせていただきたいと思います。
ありがとうございました。

料理も美味しあのはもちろん、支配人とソムリエの方の接客が何より素晴らしかったです。
今回ランチを利用したので、またディナーに来たいと思いました。
北海道の食材が使われており、函館旅行の方にぜひおすすめしたいレストランです。
スタッフの意思統一が見事でした。追加料理にも快く応じていただきました。

素敵なお料理と暖かい接客素晴らしい眺望にとても満足いたしました。
カトラリーが使いやすく良かったです。
お皿のデザインが良かったです。
一口で食べれるアミューズが新鮮でした。
柔らかめのマカロンが美味しかったです。

一つ一つの料理が、とても美味しく、料理の説明も分かりやすくかったです。
コミュニケーションもよく取れたので、是非またお邪魔させて頂きたいです。
楽しい思い出になりました。ご馳走様でした。
道南愛がたっぷり詰まったお食事、最高に美味しかったです。初めての本格フレンチでしたがお店の方全員とても親切で安心して頂くことが出来ました。予定時間より早めに着きましたが、全てとても丁寧な対応で大満足です！

初めてディナーを頂きました。
地元の食材を使った料理最高でした。ワインのセレクトも料理に合ったものを
出して頂き美味しかったです。
また来年の結婚記念日に利用させて頂きます。
ごちそうさまでした！

どれも、見た目もインパクトがあり大変おいしく、楽しませていただきました。妻も喜んでおりました。
関東からの移動日当日で、思ったより疲労がたまっていたようで、大変失礼しました。
料理、サービス、どちらも完璧でした。またよろしくお願いいたします。

春から東京への転職が決まり、その前に…と以前から気になっていたメゾンフジヤさんに母とお伺いしました。
最初から最後まで、とても素敵なひとときを過ごさせていただきました。
繊細で素材の味を活かしたお料理は見た目も華やかで、目でも舌でも楽しむことができました。
スタッフの皆さまのお心遣いも大変温かく、特にソムリエの男性のお人柄が記憶に残りました。
ぜひまたお伺いしたいです。
本当にありがとうございました。
食べる速度が遅く、御迷惑を御掛けしたかもしれませんが、お料理のサーブタイミングもバッチリでした。お心遣い頂き有り難うございました。

料理の味も、見た目の美しさも、スタッフのサービスも全て素晴らしいもので、大変満足でした。
季節毎に伺って、旬のものをどのような形で出していただけるかを楽しみたいと思うお店でした。
ごちそうさまでした。次は雪どけ後に是非。
素材を生かしたオリジナリティの高い料理の数々はフレンドリーなスタッフとともに、お客様を必ず満足させると思います。ほんとうに美味しくいただきました。ありがとうございました。

どのお料理も見た目、お味も大満足でした。

器もどれも素敵でした。
オニオンパイちょっと真似したいなあと…
あのオニオンでグラタンスープ飲みたいなあ…

とても至福の時間を過ごせました。しばらく思い出して幸せに暮らせそうです。
また伺えたらいいなあ…
結婚記念日で利用しました。一つ一つの料理が丁寧で上品な感じがして、良い記念日となりました。スタッフの方もとても親切で気さくな方が多く、気持ちよく過ごすことができました。

地元・北海道の食材を使った東京では味わえない料理が味わえて良かった。
フランス料理らしく、おいしいチーズが用意されていてうれしかった。
シェフもあいさつに出てきてくれて、スタッフの方々がホスピタリティーを持って接してくだしました。

また、伺いたいと思いました。

母を連れて行きました！
お店の雰囲気も食事も
サービスも最高でした♡
母にも喜んでもらえました。
大満足でした。
また来月伺います！

今回もとても美味しいお料理をご馳走様でした。
眺めが最高の席やお祝いのケーキもご用意して頂き、先輩に大変感激してもらいました。
おかげさまで素敵で幸せな時間を過ごす事ができました。
また利用させて頂きます。

緊急事態宣言下でも普段と変わらない、お店の雰囲気、スタッフの対応、何よりお料理とワインのペアリングのマッチ度全て良かったです。

途中でオーナーシェフが料理に白トリフをスライスするために、突然現れ、突然帰って行くのも楽しい演出でした。

家族が亡くなり、住居も処分した私には、もう法事等でしか、帰省する事はなくなりましたが、帰る居場所がある様感じでした。

暖かい「おもてなし」感謝致します。

美味しかったです。
スタッフの方の対応も素晴らしいです？

私達にとってはラッキーでお店にとっては残念でしたが私達1組だけの贅沢なディナーを楽しませていただきました。最初から最後まで素晴らしい美味しいお料理で妻共々大満足でした。特にシェフやスタッフの気さくな接客が気取らず楽しめたと思います。ルビー婚記念で出していただいたチョコレートケーキは妻が感動してました。マカロンタワーやおまけ的なサプライズも嬉しかったです。
本当に素晴らしい時間をありがとうございました。

どの料理も初めて食べる味で、とても美味しく大満足でした。
接客も大変あたたかみがあって素晴らしく、あの値段であの内容は、凄いです。
何度も行きたいお店でした。

新婚旅行で食事する場所を探している時に、偶然テレビで貴店をお見かけしHPを拝見したところ、きちんとコストと時間のかけられたHPでしたので、これは信頼できると、今回お邪魔させていただきました。
景色がたいへんよく、また建物も綺麗で清潔感があり、スタッフの皆様も素敵なお召し物で洗練された立ち振る舞いをされていて、まずそこで素晴らしいと感じました。
お料理も北海道ならではの食材をとても美味しく調理されていて、その上しっかりとディスプレイにも工夫があり、味と見た目でお食事を楽しむことができました。当日はデザートに妻へのメッセージを依頼したのですが、その他にも実に多くのサービスをしていただき、追加のお支払い等必要ではなかったのかと店を出てから些か心配をしてしまいました。大丈夫でしたでしょうか。

今回は新婚旅行の日程上、ランチで参りましたが、次回はディナーでゆっくりお邪魔したいと、強く思いました。こんなご時世にも関わらず、温かくお迎えいただきありがとうございました。たいへん嬉しゅうございました。
スタッフの皆様も体調など崩されませんよう、どうかご自愛くださいませ。

また函館に来たいと思わせてくれる非常に素晴らしいお店でした。ありがとうございました。

お料理がとっても美味しかったです。
ロケーションも素敵でスタッフの方々の対応も良かったです。

とてもゆっくりランチをいただきました。
お店の雰囲気も良く、ワインペアリングも各料理にあった美味しいワインでした。
どの料理もとても美味しかったんですが、一番驚いたのは付け合せのジャガイモでした。
サツマイモと間違えるほどの甘さ驚きました。
今度はディナーをいただきたいと思います。服装は着物でも大丈夫でしょうか？
本当に美味しい料理ありがとうございました。良い結婚記念日になりました。

料理もとても美味しかったです。
ソムリエの石川さんの、ワイン選びも、とてもよかった。
大満足です。

沢山の旬の食材を最高の調理で見た目味共に大満足のコースでした。
また景観も良く、今回はディナーで利用しましたがランチのコースの景色もまた素晴らしいと思うので行ってみたいと思いました。

とても満足しました。
料理は盛り付けもきれいでおいしくいただきました。
スタッフ様の対応も良く、窓からのロケーションもきれいで楽しく時間を過ごさせてもらいました。
また機会があれば利用したいと思います。
お料理も景色も素晴らしかったです。全員が満足した時間を過ごせたので、よかったです。

期待以上のお料理、盛り付けや食器も素敵でした。料金的にも大満足。
サービスの方もスマートながらも、感じかよかったです。
又函館を訪れるときは、絶対行きたいとおもいます。

接客が素晴らしかったです。
お料理の説明もわかりやすかったので、味をより美味しくいただくことができました。
一皿一皿の綺麗さに、これは食べていいのかなと思うほど惹き付けられました。
両親も、こんなに美味しい料理を食べたことがないと、とても喜んでいて、素敵な１日になりました。
また、来店させていただきたいと思います。
ありがとうございました。

地元の旬の食材を大変美味しく頂き、
ごちそうさまでした。

今回もお料理、スタッフの皆様、お店の雰囲気どれも大変素晴らしく、幸せなランチタイムを過ごさせて頂きました。

また、よろしくお願いいたします。

お食事の内容、ボリューム共に想像以上でした。
スタッフもみなさん人柄も良く、とても丁寧に対応してくださいました。
とても素敵な時間を過ごさせていただき、ありがとうございます。

お料理の一つ一つがとても繊細かつ豪快で、力の入っているものでした。ランチのコスパ良すぎる感じで申し訳ないような気がしました。函館のフラッグとして、引き続き頑張っていただきたく思います。デセールも美味しく美しく。いろいろビックリがありました！

定年退職のお祝いに利用させて頂きました。

コース料理を食べたことがない2人でしたが
緊張も最初だけでおいしい料理に
スタッフの皆さんのおもてなしに和んだようです。
とても喜んでもらえました。

料理もソースがとてもおいしく
見た目でも味でも楽しませて頂きました。

また特別な日に利用させて頂きます。
ありがとうございました。

courses.summary: This elegant single-family restaurant is located on Nijukken-zaka Slope, which goes up to Mt. Hakodate. The "Neo-classical" is based on classical French cuisine, but it also combines modern light taste and deliciousness. They are particular about the ingredients produced in Donan, and their specialties include crab and sea urchin from Funka Bay, abalone, oysters from Shiriuchi Town, and neuroroshi sakura masu from Esashi Town. It is a perfect location overlooking the stone-paved slope, and you can enjoy a luxurious moment.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
【Regarding Reservations】
Reservations are available for 1-6 people.
If you are unable to enter the requested number of guests, please contact us directly at the email address below:
Contact: toraya-sapporo@outlook.jp

Please include your requested reservation date and arrival time in your email.
Dinner (Tue-Sun): Please specify either 18:00, 18:30, or 19:00.
Lunch (Saturday and Sunday): Please specify either 12:30 or 13:00.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Located along a road near Maruyama-Koen Station, a little way from the center of Sapporo, ""Nihon Ryori Toraya"" is eye-catching with its mustard-yellow walls. This quaint Japanese restaurant is run by Satoshi Maruyama and his wife and has world gourmet guide award.

Chef Maruyama is originally from the city of Kitami in Hokkaido. His parents run a tempura restaurant, an influence that saw Satoshi naturally enter the culinary profession. He worked as the head chef at ""Tokyo Chikuyotei"" (Sapporo location), a restaurant specializing in eel and Japanese cuisine, for 5 years before going independent in 1996 and establishing his own restaurant, Toraya. Later, in 2024, the 30th anniversary of the opening of the restaurant, it was reopened as "Eel and Seasonal Cuisine Toraya".

Speaking about his cooking, Maruyama says, ""The menu is decided by the seasons. As a chef, I find great joy in selecting the best ingredients of the season."" The majority of the ingredients used at the restaurant are from Hokkaido, including the vegetables that Maruyama grows himself. Meals at Toraya typically comprise of carefully selected seafood and plenty of seasonal vegetables. Toraya is also known for being one of the few restaurants in Hokkaido that specialize in eel, a in particular, many diners come to the restaurant with the aim of trying the fantastic eel Kaiseki cuisine made with eel from Kagoshima throughout the year. There is a selection of 6-7 Japanese sake to accompany a meal, all of which are light, easy-sipping offerings that have been selected to go well with the vegetables. 

The warmth of the wood in the restaurant is created in cooperation with "Kono Meikiten" in Toyohira-ku, Sapporo, using rich Hokkaido trees such as sen, yew, ash, oak, chestnut, walnut, ezo spruce, itaya, birch, and red spruce. Original artworks and tableware have slowly been collected over time to cement Toraya's image as a restaurant, creating a space that is packed with thought and affection. The first floor has a one private room; the second floor has three private rooms with table chairs in a Japanese-style room. Toraya not only enjoys the patronage of tourists, both Japanese and from overseas, but many families also come here to celebrate special moments in their children's lives, such as birthdays or the weaning ceremony, which is just one of the reasons why it has remained one of the area's most beloved restaurants for such a long time. Chef Maruyama says, ""When you're tired and want to be restored by cuisine that features ample vegetables, I'd be delighted if you came to Toraya. No matter how much you eat here, your body will feel lighter the next day."" Toraya's approach is to express the bounties of Hokkaido through vegetables, and diners will enjoy the authentic Japanese cuisine and the sense of relaxation offered at the restaurant.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Maruyama Koen Station(Sapporo Municipal Subway Line)

■ Notice of Temporary Relocation Due to Renovation Work
Thank you very much for your continued patronage.
Due to upcoming renovation work, we will be temporarily operating at the neighboring “Sushidokoro Kitano Hana – Counter Seating” until the renovation is completed.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your kind understanding and cooperation.

[Renovation Period]
February 1, 2026 – Late November 2026 (scheduled)
Guests with reservations during this period are kindly requested to visit the neighboring “Sushidokoro Kitano Hana.”
Information regarding the completion of the renovation will be updated at a later date.

[Access Information]
1-1 Saiwai-cho, Chitose-shi, Hokkaido
(Same address as “Kitanohana Hayashi”)

Please take care to ensure you arrive at the correct location.
--

Located 10 minutes by car from the “Gateway to the Northern Skies” as New Chitose Airport is referred to, or 15 minutes by foot from Chitose Station, ""Kitanohana Hayashi"" is a sushi restaurant whose quality is reflected by the world gourmet guide award it received in 2017. This restaurant is headed by Naokazu Hayashi, a native of Chitose who spent 10 years refining his skills in one of Sapporo’s famed restaurants before returning home to open Sushidokoro Kitanohana in 1996. Although this restaurant gained significant popularity over the years, what he truly wanted was a place where he could give his customers his undivided attention, assuring the best possible service. Kitanohana Hayashi, a reservation-only restaurant with a counter that seats only eight, was born from this desire, opening in 2013 adjacent to the original Kitanohana.

Utilizing the locational advantages of this well-situated restaurant, as well as the personal connections he has fostered since opening Kitanohana, Hayashi is able to procure the best natural seafood products from throughout Japan. He is very particular when it comes to selecting ingredients, purchasing his bluefin tuna from Yamayuki, a specialty Maguro broker at the famous Tsukiji fish market in Tokyo, due to a belief that tuna from Tokyo is unrivaled. This meticulous selection process, combined with a thorough approach to work produces a delectable Tokyo-style sushi with red vinegar sushi rice that holds together firmly and contains no sugar.

The other source of acclaim for Kitanohana Hayashi is its selection of regional sake assembled by the proprietress, Ms. Yayoi. Featuring breweries from Hokkaido, such as Nisekoshuzo and Kobayashishuzo, it is stocked with seasonal varieties such as Hiyaoroshi in the fall and Shiboritate in the winter. There are also suggested pairings that complement the cuisine, as well as an abundance of bar snacks made with seasonal ingredients that will make the drinks flow freely.

The single counter stands out attractively in the interior that Mr. Hayashi designed himself. The subdued atmosphere is what you would expect from a sushi restaurant, evoking Japanese sophistication. The experience isn’t limited to just business entertainment, group dining, and dates, however; the restaurant is also loved by guests visiting from overseas. We hope you will come to experience the finest sushi and service Hokkaido has to offer.

245330.longDescription:
An eight-minute walk from Himeji Station, Tanryu is surrounded by attractions of Himeji, including Himeji Castle within walking distance. Helmed by Chef Hisafumi Nakae, Tanryu offers Japanese dishes featuring local ingredients from Banshu, Hyogo Prefecture.

Hailing from Takasago City, Hyogo Prefecture, Chef Nakae honed his cooking skills at Japanese restaurants in Australia and Dubai to start his culinary career and then returned to Japan to learn Japanese cuisine all over again from ingredients to tableware. He started serving as a chef at Ginza Kojyu. After working at this two-star restaurant for five and a half years, he returned to his home prefecture with an eye toward opening his own restaurant. He further honed his skills at hotels and Japanese inns and even worked as a brewer at Okada Honke, a Japanese sake brewery, in Kakogawa City to learn more about sake for his future career. Then, he finally opened his own restaurant, Tanryu, in 2019.
The restaurant’s name, Tanryu, is derived from the concept of “smoothly flowing like water” as proposed by the Omote Senke School of Tea Ceremony, where the chef is engaged as an instructor. As indicated by its name, the restaurant offers simple dishes without any twist or flashy performance to make diners feel like coming back again and again.
Featuring seafood and vegetables mostly sourced from local waters and farms, the dishes tell stories learned from producers the chef knows in person. He also drives two hours every morning to fetch sweetfish from contract fishermen in the Ibo River during the fishing season. In addition, he collects edible wild plants as well as bamboo shoots by himself. “I would like to purchase a bamboo forest someday to offer guests bamboo shoots I grow by myself,” the chef says.
Chef Nakae sources wild abalone from Ako, eels from the Chikusa River, and watershields from Sanda, as well as Japanese chestnuts from Sanda and swimming crabs from Setouchi in autumn. These seasonal ingredients are simply grilled, steamed, stewed, and turned into the chef’s specialties. Tanryu also offers a 10-course prix-fixe (fixed-price) menu inspired by the spirit of the tea ceremony. The meal starts with one to two appetizers, followed by soup, sashimi, and grill courses and a bowl of rice, and ends with a bowl of matcha tea made by Chef Nakae right in front of the guests.
The drink menu offers Japanese sake, all from breweries in Banshu, including Seiten from Okada Honke. As a former brewer working there, he describes the sake by saying, “It is a must-try that reflects the kind character of the chief brewer,” the chef recommends.

In the sukiya-style (tea-ceremony room) dining room with Juraku (grey wall covering) walls and a bamboo wickerwork ceiling, there is an eye-catching L-shaped counter (seating up to eight guests) made of Yoshino hinoki cypress. The tableware is also carefully selected, including long-cherished plates crafted by Mr. Akinori Bonde, a ceramicist secluded in the mountains in Kazusa, Chiba Prefecture. With a comfy private dining room (seating up to six guests), Tanryu is perfect for different occasions. Please enjoy excellent dishes and beautiful tableware at Tanryu with your family, partner, colleagues, and gastronomic friends.
nearestStations: 10 minutes walk from Himeji Station

244802.longDescription:
“Sushi Ueda” is located on the 1st floor of a building in a quiet town near Motomachi Station in Kobe. Chef Masamichi Ueda makes sushi with the thought of "I want people to feel the life of the local Hyogo land".

Chef Ueda, who is from Awaji Island, started cooking at the age of 16. He was trained at Japanese restaurants and sushi restaurants for 8 years, and gradually became fascinated with sushi. In order to get to know the starting point, he experienced the life of a fisherman for a month. After training at various restaurants, he opened his own sushi restaurant “Sushi Ueda” in November 2018. At that time, the sushi prepared by the stable master, who was only 25 years old, was so popular that he was chosen as "2020 Young Chef of the Year" on one of the world's best gourmet guides.

The decision to open the restaurant in Hyogo, chef Ueda explained that "in addition to being home, Setouchi also has fishing ports on the Sea of Japan side, and is a treasure house full of ingredients. I think that "it can only be done here"". Most ingredients, besides tuna, are carefully purchased from Hyogo Prefecture, such as from Awaji-shima Island, Akashi Strait, Harima-nada Sea, Hamasaka fishing port on the Sea of Japan side and Kasumi port. Aging of fish and shellfish is not considered. "There are professionals all over the place. I want to make dishes that bring out the local scenery and show the face of the producer of each ingredient," he said.

The first sushi is "fresh conger eel" nigiri. "You can say that raw conger eel tastes good as it is. A piece of work that is completed thanks to fishermen and broker who take care of it," chef Ueda said. "Egg from Awaji Island and Onion Chawanmushi" and "Steamed Abalone from Hamasaka Port, Hyogo" are also popular. The abalone is picked by veteran divers, and it arrives either on the day or next after they are caught. The abalone is steamed without any seasonings. You can enjoy the taste of the kelp and seaweed that the abalone ate, as well as the saltiness of the sea water. This is another dish where you can enjoy the teamwork with fishermen.

There are 20 kinds of Japanese sake, including local sake. Chef Ueda, who is also qualified as a Kikisake-Shi (sake taster), makes suggestions based on the food and your preferences. As for wine, there are many natural wines that can be enjoyed by glass, such as those from Austria.

The counter of the local Hyogo "Tajima Hinoki" is eye-catching. The walls are covered with soil from chef Ueda's hometown, Awaji Island, and are designed so that people can enjoy the local atmosphere. The restaurant is also particular about the dinnerware, the sushi table by the creator of Hyogo, Masahiko Ichino, and the glassware by traditional craftsman of Edo Kiriko, Toshio Takizawa. The dishes are decorated with specially ordered plates of “Sushi Ueda”. You can enjoy the counter (8 seats) of “Sushi Ueda” with colleagues, friends and family, or even with oversea guests. You will want to spend a special time relaxing and feeling the wonders of Hyogo with your eyes and tongue.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Motomachi Station (JR Tokaido Main Line (Kobe Line) (Osaka - Kobe))

245396.longDescription:
In Sannomiya, the political and economic hub of the port city of Kobe and the seat of the Hyogo Prefectural Office, a building facing Yamate Kansen Street houses a French restaurant, entre nous, on its second floor. The restaurant is located just a 10-minute walk from Sannomiya Station, and once inside, you will see the cozy interior with traditional clay walls and light-colored wood accents. The restaurant’s name, given by renowned French chef Régis Marcon, means “between us” in French. It was named with the wish that the restaurant would become a place where the chef and guests could enjoy a good time together and build rapport through sharing gastronomic experiences.

Chef Hideki Takayama entered the culinary world at the age of 18. After an eight-year apprenticeship at Chez Inno in Kyobashi, Tokyo, he went to France and refined his skills at three-star restaurants, including Lameloise and Régis et Jacques Marcon. Eventually, he returned to Japan and worked as the head chef at Maison de Gill Ashiya, which was later renamed Maison de Taka Ashiya. He then opened entre nous in Sannomiya, Kobe, in October 2022. While developing his career as a chef, he has demonstrated his culinary talent by coming in fifth place twice at an international gastronomic competition, Bocuse d'Or, in 2015 and 2019. Moreover, under his supervision, Paris 1930 de Hideki Takayama in Taipei has been listed as a one-star restaurant in a world-renowned restaurant guidebook.

Chef Takayama is known for his Japanese-inspired French cuisine. Sourcing more than ninety percent of his ingredients from local suppliers, he creates dishes that celebrate the terroir (which means the natural environment and character of the land informed by its climate and landscape) of Japan. He embraces ingredients from around the country, including sea bream from Akashi, Hyogo, chestnuts from Tamba, and other specialties from neighboring regions. One of his signature dishes, “Origami” mousseline, is a cake-like dish made from two varieties of carrots. With their beautiful bright orange and yellow colors, the carrots are layered alternatively to make a traditional Japanese-style imbricated pattern and topped with a meringue formed into a miniature Japanese garden.

With a cellar holding some 7,000 bottles of wine, mainly from France, entre nous offers three options for food and alcohol pairings, including a pairing with Grand Vin. It also offers a note-worthy pairing with Taiwanese tea.

The restaurant boasts a private dining room seating up to six guests, as well as a main dining room with a 16-seat U-shaped counter. All the counter seats provide a good view of the chef’s kitchen, which serves as a stage for his live performance. Chef Takayama’s delicious dishes make the restaurant a popular place for intimate meals and gourmet gatherings. However, please note that while the restaurant can accommodate children of any age in the private dining room, only those in upper elementary or higher grade levels are allowed in the main dining room (a children’s menu is also available if requested in advance).

Please enjoy delicious flavors from the terroir of Japan at entre nous with your friends and family.
nearestStations: 6 minutes walk from JR Sannomiya Station

245530.longDescription:
About 15 minutes’ drive from Tsukuba Station in Ibaraki Prefecture, Nonna Nietta is a house restaurant nestled in a residential area lined with leafy trees in the lush green city of Tsukuba. Hailing from Tsuchiura City, Ibaraki Prefecture, Chef Kenji Kawamura tackles local ingredients head-on with the authentic techniques he learned in Italy. He first trained at an Italian restaurant in Tokyo and then further honed his culinary skills over six years at starred restaurants in Puglia, Naples, Calabria, Bologna, Piemonte, and other Italian regions. After returning to Japan, he continued to sharpen his skills at an Italian restaurant in Tokyo and eventually opened his own restaurant, Nonna Nietta, in 2021. Naming it after his wife’s grandma, Nietta, from Piemonte, Italy, to pay tribute to her delicious homemade dishes, the Italian-trained chef elevates exquisite local ingredients from Ibaraki, a treasure trove of food, to refined Italian dishes.

The prix-fixe menu offers a dozen courses, starting with antipasti (five courses), followed by pasta and risotto dishes (two to three courses) and meat and fish dishes, and ending with desserts. The menu proudly features local ingredients, such as net-hunted Hitachi-no-Kuni Wild Duck, slow-fattened, tasty Hitachi Beef “Kirameki,” flavorful Hitachi-no-Kagayaki Pork, marine fishes caught off Ibaraki, and freshwater fishes from Kasumigaura Lake, and brings out their natural flavors. The hams and cheeses are all homemade. Among them, one of the most popular is the mozzarella cheese, which is made right in front of diners. The handmade pastas are combined with the best ingredients of the day, inviting guests to indulge in once-in-a-lifetime flavors. For example, one day wood-grilled lobster is featured along with tagliolini pasta topped with citrus-flavored ricotta, and another day homegrown zucchini is tossed with tagliatelle pasta and a ragout sauce made with Hitachi Beef “Kirameki.” Anyway, all these dishes showcase the simple, dynamic flavors stemming from the restaurant’s commitment to homemade excellence.

The wine cellar stores about 250 bottles of wine, mainly from Italy, including Valpolicella from Verona, Veneto, Northern Italy, and wines produced by a friend of the wife in Piemonte. Don’t overlook the wine paring featuring excellent Italian wines that perfectly complement the prix-fixe menu. The restaurant’s design is inspired by an Italian mountain restaurant. All the three tables, eight chairs, and windows are imported from Italy to create an authentic Italian vibe. Please visit Nonna Nietta for various occasions, including family and friend gatherings, date nights, and dinners with international guests, and indulge in Italian dishes that can only be found in Ibaraki.

245312.longDescription:
Take a one-hour express train ride on the JR Joban Line from Ueno Station in Tokyo to Katsuta Station, one stop beyond Mito, and then an eight-minute drive from Katsuta Station, and you will find Kyoyuzen Hanamiyako secluded in a residential neighborhood. Kyoyuzen Hanamiyako opened its doors in 1993 and was renovated into a sukiya-style (style of a tea-ceremony room) restaurant in 2008. The interior was renovated again shortly before its 30th anniversary in 2023 in order to welcome guests with a renewed vigor.

The restaurant is owned by Mr. Masami Nishino, who was born in 1965 as the eldest son of a family running a greengrocer’s shop for generations. After getting his own knife at the age of eight, he learned culinary skills by himself. Then, after graduating from high school, he entered Tsuji Culinary Institute in Osaka to make his dream come true. Subsequently, he graduated from the Institute and started to work at Nishijin Uoshin in Kyoto. While working at this renowned Japanese restaurant that offers Yusoku cuisine (Imperial court cuisine prepared in accordance with the practices of court nobles), he was promoted to Sous Chef. Then, he took the position of Chef at Japanese Restaurant Inagaki in Yanagibashi, Taito Ward, Tokyo, and, in 1993, returned to his home prefecture of Ibaraki to open Kyoyuzen Hanamiyako. He displays his incredible culinary skills, as evidenced by a number of awards and recognitions bestowed on him, including listings in internationally acclaimed restaurant guides, the Bronze Award and Silver Award at the Cooking Masters held by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries in 2018 and 2023, and the three-star rating given to only one restaurant in the Ibaraki Food Selection 2022.
Chef Nishino’s Japanese cuisine is grounded in traditional Kyoto cuisine. In fact, the word “Kyoyuzen” in the restaurant’s name is coined by the chef to mean a fusion of Kyoto vegetables and ingredients locally produced in Ibaraki. Also serving as Ibaraki Food Ambassador, Chef Nishino offers sensible and flavorful dishes to fulfill his mission of conveying the bounties of the sea and land in Ibaraki as a pioneer of inseparability of body/mind and geographical circumstances. 

The wine list offers a variety of wines that go well with the dishes, selected by Ms. Masako Nishino, the sommelier and proprietress, from inside and outside the country. The sake list includes Kokuryu, which is only available at this restaurant run by the one and only Kokuryu Ambassador in Ibaraki. The pairing menu includes both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options.

The sukiya-style building has three dining rooms (seating up to 12 guests), all furnished with tables and mahogany chairs, and a tearoom with made-to-order hinoki cypress trays coated with precious Daigo lacquer from Ibaraki using a traditional method called “Mehajiki-nuri.” The long-cherished menu books made of Nasu mulberry paper, called Nishinouchi-gami, an intangible cultural asset with a history of 350 years, give a traditional feeling of the Japanese culture.
Kyoyuzen Hanamiyako is not only patronized by locals who have been coming for years but also swarmed with gourmets from around Japan. It is definitely worth visiting Kyoyuzen Hanamiyako and trying Chef Nishino’s dishes that reflect his ambition to discover and spread the delights of local gastronomy from Ibaraki.

244639.longDescription:
Omicho Market is one of the most popular spots in the ancient city of Kanazawa. Right next to this bustling market stands A two-star Spanish restaurant, "respiracion". Taking up the whole of a 140-year-old townhouse that has been lovingly restored, and blending harmoniously with the atmospheric old streets, "respiracion" is also just a 5-minute walk from the Higashi Chaya entertainment district. The entrance is marked only by a small gold plate bearing the name of the restaurant, so you can't help but wonder what kind of experience is waiting on the other side of the door before you go inside.

There are three chefs at "respiracion": head chef Tatsuro Ume, Keisuke Yagi, and Yusuke Kitagawa. All three chefs hail from Ishikawa prefecture and have been friends since childhood; Chefs Ume and Yagi have spent time honing their culinary skills in Barcelona, Spain. In addition to the three chefs, there is sommelier Toshihiro Kanemura, and this 4-person team is devoted to bringing the world of modern Spanish cuisine to the Hokuriku region of Japan. The dishes served at "respiracion" is modern, and each dish contains inviting flavors as well as novelty. For example, the dish that is always served at the beginning of a set meal is the "Reconstructed Sweet Shrimp". This brightly colored little ball looks like a confection but is actually created using every part of the shrimp: the tomalley from inside the shrimp is made into a wrapper into which the meat is stuffed, while the shell is turned into a tart. With an unexpected presentation like this, the three chefs draw you into their culinary world. Also, no meal here would be complete without paella, and the paella served at "respiracion" really proves their credentials as a Spanish restaurant. As for wine, Sommelier Kanemura has assembled a selection of French and Spanish offerings to pair with the food, as well as a number of local Japanese wine, such as Says Farm and Noto Wine.

As soon as you set foot inside the elegant townhouse setting of "respiracion," you'll be struck by the refined interior, and would be forgiven for mistaking it for an art gallery. The restaurant has 20 tables, and it is the perfect setting to enjoy a special day with family or friends. The restaurant name, "respiracion," comes from the Spanish word for breathing, and, as an anchor connected to the breath of life from producers, Chefs Ume, Yagi, and Kitagawa believed it to be a fitting name for the unique dining space that they have created. Charmed by the exciting space, more and more people are traveling from afar to sample the delights at this restaurant.

245598.longDescription:
About a 10-minute drive from Kanazawa Station in Ishikawa Prefecture, Higashiyama Shinnei is nestled in the elegant Higashi Chaya District lined with geisha houses dating back to the early modern Edo period. Stepping inside, guests are welcomed by Chef Atsushi Kanata with warm greetings. Hailing from Osaka, he is devoted to the art of Japanese cuisine and honed his culinary skills at renowned Japanese restaurants, such as Nishitenma Iwasaki in Osaka and Gion Owatari in Kyoto, and worked his way up to chef at Kappo Kagamasa (permanently closed) in Kanazawa. He made it grow in popularity and won a star in a well-known restaurant guide before setting up his own business. Opening its doors in October 2022, the restaurant takes its name from Jinen Shinneido, a metaphysical text from the Edo period that inspired Mr. Kaneda to pursue a career in the culinary world. The name also reflects his desire to stay grounded and work with his feet firmly on the ground.

Higashiyama Shinnei offers authentic Japanese cuisine inspired by the spirit of tea ceremony and chakaiseki cuisine of Kanazawa and local ingredients from Kanazawa and Hokuriku. Following the traditions of chakaiseki cuisine, the prix-fixe menu offers 9 to 10 courses, starting with an amuse-bouche and appetizers, followed by soup, sake accompaniments, a grilled dish, an assortment of seasonal delicacies, a hotpot dish, rice, and ending with desserts and matcha. The soup made from a rich broth slowly simmered over three days with spring water from the sacred Mt. Hakusan and the Clay Pot Rice (organic Koshihikari rice cooked in a clay pot over high heat) are a testament to the chef’s pride and devotion to Japanese cuisine. Other dishes also feature high-quality local ingredients from the land and sea, some sourced through Omicho Market, also known as “Kanazawa’s Kitchen,” and some directly from producers. A wide variety of seasonal fish and shellfish, such as giant conger eel, cherry salmon, and wild blowfish from Noto in spring, pike conger, egg cockles, and rock oysters from Noto and neon flying squid from Kaga in summer, Japanese abalone, horse crabs, and sweet shrimp from Wajima in autumn, and winter yellowtail, milt, Kano crabs, and female snow crabs from Noto in winter, are prepared with simple techniques rooted in chakaiseki cuisine, such as slicing, grilling, steaming, and deep-frying, to create exquisite flavors available only at Higashiyama Shinnei.

The drink menu offers about 20 varieties of sake, mainly from Hokuriku, such as Kagatobi and Tengumai from Ishikawa Prefecture, and a great selection of wines curated by Chef Kanata to match his Japanese courses, including whites from Meursault, Chablis, and Montrachet in France and reds from Burgundy and Switzerland.

Rebuilt from a more than 100-year-old Japanese-style house designated for conservation by the Kanazawa City Government, the interior is designed by Chef Kanata to create a space that harmonizes with his dishes. The dining space is furnished with a table (seating up to five guests) and a counter (seating up to six guests), made from bog zelkova wood believed to date back 2,000 years. Seating is by reservation only and limited to two groups per day, one each for the table and counter seating. In addition, an amazing selection of art pieces and antiques that captivates even the most discerning eyes, including hanging scrolls from the medieval Kamakura period, folding screens by Kano School painters in the early modern Edo period, and vintage ceramics, such as Japanese Kutani, Mino, Kenzan, and Koimari ware, Chinese antique blue and white porcelain, Thai Sukhothai ware, and Korean and Southeast Asian ceramics, elevate dining experiences, embodying the hospitality of tea ceremony culture, where dinnerware is considered an essential part of any dining experience. The discreet setting and authentic Japanese cuisine makes the restaurant ideal for both personal and business occasions. Please enjoy the exquisite dishes and relaxing time at Higashiyama Shinnei.

A one-star restaurant “Kyomi Kai” is a quaint machiya-style restaurant located in "Higashi-Chaya district", one of the three Chaya districts in Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture's old capital. The name of the restaurant "Kai (paddle)" reflects the desire to create a warm and pleasant restaurant with dishes and hospitality as mixing with a kai tool in sake making, and the desire to treat customers step by step as rowing a boat. Chef Jun Tajiri and his wife warmly and gently welcomes the guests.

Chef Tajiri is from Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture. His father, a food connoisseur, took him around from an early age to eat, and he started to stay in the kitchen often at home. He then aspired to become a professional chef and entered “L'Ecole Culinaire Kunitachi (L'Ecole Tsuji)”. After graduation, he trained at a long-established soba restaurant in Yamagata Prefecture. Back in Tokyo, he went to the famous “Soba Kaiseki Muan” in Tachikawa. He worked hard as a chef and became independent in 2015. Since his wife's hometown was Kanazawa, he decided to set up his restaurant “Kyomi Kai” here, also because "Kanazawa is an ideal place for chefs as it is close to the seas and mountains, and has a lot of ingredients". The reputation of the homemade soba and dishes made with ingredients from the Hokuriku region spread outside the prefecture and became a popular restaurant that was introduced in a worldwide gourmet guidebook.


Most of the ingredients used are local, Chef Tajiri visits the market every day and get good quality ingredients due to his connections with producers and farmers. Seafood is from Kanazawa Bay, Nanao Bay in Noto, Wajima Bay, etc. Vegetables are delivered from farmers in Kanazawa. The soba that they are proud of is made with homemade buckwheat that uses local ingredients from Fukui and Toyama. The grains are small, strong and fragrant. The buckwheat is ground by hand using restaurant's millstone. The production method is to use "grinder" in which each layer of buckwheat seed is not separated, until number 3rd ~ 4th flour is ground, and the mixture is "Sotoji ". The soba goes down smoothly, and you can feel the roughness and flavor of the coarse-ground soba.

In addition, the soup stock is made of matured rishiri-konbu kelp and Hon-karebushi, and the lacquered bowls of Wajima are changed from season to season to express different phases. The ingredients, bowls, and the beautiful aroma and appearance convey the charm of Kanazawa's nature. The sake is carefully-selected from three prefectures in the Hokuriku region, Ishikawa, Toyama and Fukui, and it has a light taste and matches well with the food. The restaurant mainly has domestic wine that goes well with the gentle broth.


The building was built around 100 years ago in the early Taisho period. The characteristic lattice of the machiya "Kinusuko" in Kanazawa is beautiful, leaving the appearance of the Kanazawa-machiya unchanged. There is only table seating in the restaurant. Enjoy cuisine, sake and soba noodles at “Kyomi Kai”. Please have a relaxing meal with family, friends and guests from overseas.

244952.longDescription:
Located in Kanazawa City, Ishikawa Prefecture, known as a castle town, the Higashi Chaya District preserves the ancient streets to this day. 

In the castle town of Kanazawa City, Ishikawa Prefecture, local districts act to preserve the ancient streets to this day. The Sushi Mitsukawa finds itself in the heart of nostalgic surroundings, with chef Koji Mitsukawa crafting sushi that uses Kanazawa’s famed ingredients. 

Mitsukawa studied at a famous sushi restaurant in Ginza for five years. After moving to Germany, he worked in sushi restaurants overseas for three years in Dusseldorf. After returning to Japan, he opened his own sushi restaurant, Sushi Mitsukawa, two years later in 2005. News spread quickly about his nigiri and delicate side dishes, and the restaurant became popular. Afterward, he opened Sushi Mitsukawa Roppongi Hills in 2019, followed by Sushi Mitsukawa Niseko in 2020, determined to share the taste of his sushi.

The sushi at Sushi Mitsukawa uses Kanazawa's bounty of ingredients in classic Edomae-style. "We provided seared blackthroat seaperch before anyone else," says Mitsukawa, who maintains tradition but never forgets evolution. "Listening to the expressions of ingredients and customer feedback, we are working hard to improve ourselves," he said. As for seafood and vegetables, in addition to buying fresh from the local Omi Market, the restaurant skillfully also uses produce sent directly from Nanao Port in Ishikawa Prefecture and Toyosu Market. 

The restaurant’s vinegared rice is made from two different varieties of rice from Ishikawa Prefecture, while the vinegar is sourced from Kyoto and the salt from Noto. Favourites included the blackthroat seaperch hand roll, available year-round, plus the Kobako crab chirashi sushi, which is only available for two months from November. 

For sake, Kagatobi, Tengumai and other styles from Kanazawa account for two-thirds of the restaurant’s offering. There are usually about 10 other kinds available, including the Dassai in Yamaguchi, Mitsukawa's hometown. There is an original collaboration with a local sake brewery, and its refreshing taste pairs well with sushi.

Housed in a renovated 100-year old building, the restaurant possesses an understated, tasteful appearance. Inside the restaurant is an L-shape counter for up to eight guests, carved from a 200-year old Japanese cypress from Tono, Gifu Prefecture. “The counter is like a stage with customers sitting in the audience seats,” he says. Guests can enjoy Sushi Mitsukawa with family, friends, and colleagues, enjoying the dinner performance in front of them while absorbing the history of Kanazawa.

245319.longDescription:
Located in the heart of Kanazawa’s Higashi Chaya District, one of the city’s three historic teahouse quarters, Tempura Matoba welcomes guests amidst the flow of travelers exploring this ancient capital of Ishikawa. Chef Hiroki Matoba honed his craft for more than a decade at the two-star Tokyo establishment Tempura Motoyoshi in Minami-Aoyama, where he rose to the position of second-in-command. Captivated by Ishikawa’s abundance of ingredients—discovered through more than 100 visits during his career—he resolved to put down roots here in May 2025.

Guided by the words of his mentor, “The batter is light, but the spirit is weighty,” Matoba continues to pursue the essence of tempura. Within the deceptively simple framework of “ingredients, oil, and batter,” he explores how best to reflect the fleeting expressions of the seasons—early, peak, and late harvests. With this philosophy, he embraces Ishikawa’s bounty: Kaga vegetables, seafood sourced daily from Nanao Port, and other treasures unique to the Hokuriku region. His course menu is composed entirely of local Kanazawa ingredients, and in a deliberate departure from convention, shrimp is not served. Instead, seasonal mountain vegetables, mushrooms, and in winter, delicacies such as Kano crab and buri (yellowtail) take center stage.

The restaurant is housed in a renovated machiya townhouse, more than 200 years old, offering a serene Japanese atmosphere. The six-seat counter on the first floor allows guests to share in the immediacy and anticipation of freshly fried tempura. The décor reflects the seasonal calendar, mirroring the changing scenery so that dining becomes part of the landscape itself. Ishikawa’s rich natural blessings, combined with techniques refined in Tokyo, give rise to a new and memorable tempura experience.
