244562.longDescription:
Approximately 10 minutes by car from Kanazawa Station in Ishikawa Prefecture, A one-star "Sushi Kibatani" is located near an elegant teahouse district. The owner, Mitsuhiro Kibatani, has a passion for Hokuriku fish and provides a chef's choice course consisting of a combination of tsumami(appetizers) and nigiri sushi. 

Mr. Kibatani learned the Edo-style of sushi making in distinguished restaurants such as "Yoshiura"—whose owner studied with Jiro Ono of Ginza "Sukiyabashi Jiro"—in Funabashi and "Sushi Aoki" in Ginza. After completing his training, he returned to his hometown of Toyama, where he helped out at his family's fishmonger business and polished his skills by traveling to different restaurants and providing his services. Then, in 2016, he opened "Sushi Kibatani" in Kanazawa. When asked why he opened his restaurant in this area, which is known for its fierce competition, he explains, "I was often dispatched to a nearby geisha house, and I developed a fondness for the traditional feel of the neighborhood."
Apart from tuna, Mr. Kibatani uses almost exclusively local fish. "Hokuriku is known for its abundance of fish species and excellent seasonal variety. I want people outside of Ishikawa Prefecture to know more about the goodness of the fish in this region." Every morning at 5 o’clock, he heads out to one of the fishing ports in Himi or Shinminato and picks out the very best fish with his sharp eye. Highly knowledgeable about fish, Mr. Kibatani explains, "The fish in Wajima, Noto, and Toyama bay are all completely different, so I can get a good mix. Also, many of the local fish have strong flavors, so instead of expending a lot of time and effort in preparing them, I simply serve them with a little twist." He's also well known for his skill in fish aging techniques, and the exquisite way that he prepares white-fleshed fish like tuna, squid, and sea bream leave his discerning regulars groaning with pleasure. When making vinegared rice, he uses a blend of red vinegar and rice vinegar to strike a perfect balance with the taste of the fish. 

For alcohol, Mr. Kibatani keeps a selection of Ishikawa Prefecture sake brands, including Shiragiku and Gorin, as well as wine made on "Says Farm" in Himi. The store interior features traditional earthen walls, which Mr. Kibatani says is to create a warm atmosphere similar to that of "Soba Kyobun" in Takaoka, where he worked for 5 years. In addition to his use of local fish, small touches like the restaurant banner, which was drawn by a local calligrapher, proclaim his love for the Hokuriku region. With his warm personality and lively conversation skills, Mr. Kibatani draws sushi lovers from not only Hokuriku but also from Tokyo and the rest of the country. There are 9 seats at his counter, from which his regulars delight in the sublime taste of Hokuriku fish all year round.

244605.longDescription: ""Paul Bocuse"" is a world-class French restaurant in Lyon, France that has maintained award rating in cuisine guidebooks around the world for more than 50 years. The only other restaurants in the world that carry on the cuisine of legendary chef Paul Bocuse are ""Maison Paul Bocuse"" in Daikanyama, Tokyo and ""Jardin Paul Bocuse"" in Kanazawa, Ishikawa. ""Jardin Paul Bocuse,"" the head restaurant in Japan, has stood calmly in Shiinoki Cultural Complex at the center of the ancient city of Kanazawa, surrounded by the blessings of the sea and the mountains, since 2010. In addition to the specialties passed down from the head restaurant in Lyon, at ""Jardin Paul Bocuse,"" you can enjoy first-rate French cuisine overflowing in the sense of the seasons, made using the natural blessings of Ishikawa. They want their guests to experience a taste of Lyon through the traditional cuisine that has been loved for many years, including the truffle soup served to V.G.E. at Elysee Palace in 1975, sea bass in pastry with Sauce Choron and the fillet of beef Rossini with Sauce Périgueux. The wine served with the meals is carefully selected from among wines imported directly from winemakers at Chateaus and Domaines across France with which the restaurant has built a relationship of mutual trust over many years. You can have your fill of the feeling put into the wine and the wonderful ""marriage"" enabled by the sommelier, who knows when it is just right to drink. The brick building has been standing since the Taisho period and portrays the traditional cultural materials and motifs of Kanazawa through gilding and Yukitsuri across the exterior. It is protected by a tree known as the ""Temple-shaped Chinquapin,"" a nationally designated natural monument said to be 300 years old. The reverse side is an all-glass surface through which you can see the rich greenery and wide stone walls of Kenroku-en and Kanazawa Castle Park. The design of this space allows guests to feel the vibrancy of the ancient city of Kanazawa and the atmosphere of France, closely resembling the spirit of French cuisine, which respects culture while also respecting tradition. The main dining hall seats 50, and there are two private rooms that seat 30 guests between them, so feel free to ask about them when making a reservation. Menus in Chinese, French, and English are provided to cater to guest from overseas. Have a taste of the capital of gourmet Lyon and the food culture of Kanazawa, and enjoy the heavenly collaborations that fuse the blessings of the Mediterranean and the Sea of Japan while surrounded by the rich nature of Kanazawa. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.

244750.longDescription:
“Installation Table ENSO L'asymetrie du calme” is a restaurant in Ikeda-cho, which is close to downtown Katamachi, Kanazawa. The long name of the restaurant reflects the passion of owner-chef Makoto Doi. "Installation" is a term used to describe the art of experiencing an entire space as a work. "ENSO" means "seasoning only with salt" in Japanese cuisine, " L'asymetrie" is asymmetrical, and "Calm" is silent. In the quiet environment of Kanazawa, it expresses the desire to serve the simple and pure taste of the dishes that make full use of all the techniques within oneself.

Owner-chef Doi, a native of Aichi Prefecture, came to Tokyo to become a washi craftsman. At the same time, he encountered Japanese cuisine through a part-time job, and trained at Japanese restaurants in the Kanto and Kansai areas. Later, he started to also enjoy western cuisine and discovered a deep passion for French dishes, stronger than that he felt for cuisine from any other country. After working as a chef at a French restaurant in Ginza, he went to Europe. He studied hard in Switzerland, Northern Europe, France and other countries for about four years before returning to Japan and opening his own restaurant in 2016.

Owner-chef Doi chose Kanazawa because of the pleasant environment and abundance of local ingredients. He mainly uses ingredients from the Hokuriku region and is a strong believer in the value of visiting the local producers to deepen relationships. The ingredients used in cooking are first introduced as illustrations to the guests. "You should be particular about tableware because the food arrives first with its smell and then with its appearance before guests begin eating." he said. There are many authors in Ishikawa, and most of the tableware are the works of those local authors, companies and artisans living in the area, such as Masaki SUSODA for the glass items, Akihiko SUGITA for the lacquer items, Yuichi TAKEMATA for the cutlery, and so on.

Since the restaurant was originally a dressmaking school built in the Meiji period, while making the most of the original design, there are tables and other objects made of wood from the Hokuriku region, chairs from Spain, and other objects made by artists from Belgium, which harmonize the warmth of wood with its retro feel. The dining room has 14 tables and a private room (2 ~ 4 people), and as it is an open kitchen, you can see the chefs’ cooking styles and enjoy the aromas of the dishes as they are prepared. Visit Installation Table ENSO L'asymetrie du calm and enjoy this unique food and space filled with the charm of Hokuriku and Kanazawa for private occasions such as with family and friends, dates, as well as hospitality for overseas guests.

244944.longDescription:
【Temporarily closed due to The 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake】

Ipponsugi Kawashima is a one-star Japanese restaurant in Nanao City, located almost in the center of Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture. 

Hailing from Nanao City, Chef Toru Kawashima recreates the energy of historical Ipponsugi Street through his food. Born into a culinary family, Kawashima attended and graduated from Tsuji Culinary Institute in Osaka, continuing his studies in Osaka and Kyoto. “I learned the basics of Japanese cuisine thoroughly, and acquired an obsession with dashi (soup stock), learned about Japanese sake and dinnerware, management and service”, he says. During his apprenticeship, he won the Grand Prize at the Osaka Grand Prix in 2013, before being chosen as a finalist at RED U-35, one of Japan’s largest contests for young cooks. He was also awarded a GOLD EGG. 

Returning to his hometown, he experienced heading up a large-scale restaurant kitchen as head chef of Kappo Yoimachi in Wakura Onsen Nihon no Yado Notoraku, before striking out on his own and opening Ipponsugi Kawashima in July 2020. “I want to cherish the relationship between people, as Ipponsugi Street that used to be crowded with people is close to the port,” Kawashima says. 

He also uses local ingredients from Noto: “The seafood from Noto is wonderful. The vegetables and seafood from Noto have such great potential that they were designated as a World Agricultural Heritage Site in 2011. I try to make simple dishes so that I can bring out the best in addition to telling the good things,” he explains.

The key ingredient is bonito flakes which, while produced in Makurazaki in Kagoshima Prefecture, are smelted locally by specialty stores and Noto’s soft, clear water. There are 6 to 7 types of local sake such as Kawashima’s favorite, Ishikawa Tedori-gawa, Noto’s Izumi Tani-zumi and several varieties of seasonal sake from around the country.

The restaurant was formerly an 80-year-old fountain pen shop, an elegant building that has been designated as a tangible cultural property. There are 7 seats at a counter crafted from 250 year old Japanese Manchurian ash. Both the table seats (4 and 6 people) and the chairs were handmade by craftsmen. 

Please enjoy the charm of Noto through Ipponsugi Kawashima, a Japanese restaurant rich with details, and worth a special trip. Ideal for meals with family, friends, colleagues, and dates.

245263.longDescription:
Budoonomori, a pioneer French restaurant in Ishikawa Prefecture, has its main location in Iwademachi, Kanazawa City, a 20-minute drive from JR Kanazawa Station. Restaurant  Budoonomori Les Tonnelles is located on the premises of the main location, along with a wedding chapel, a coffee shop, a pastry factory, vineyards and plantations, to allow visitors of all ages and for all purposes enjoy food together. In particular, Restaurant  Budoonomori Les Tonnelles plays a core role, characterized by its unique architecture converted from a greenhouse with a domed roof made of paper tubes by a renowned architect, Shigeru Ban. Inside the greenhouse, the ceiling is covered with real vine leaves, through which bright sunshine pours in to add a sense of openness.

The chef is Marco Santoscoy. Born in Mexico, he gained experience at restaurants in Argentina, Napa Valley, Scottsdale, and other places in the United States, where he developed an interest in Japan. His desire to "see Japan with my own eyes, where there are many things that resonate with my own sensibilities" grew stronger, and he moved to Japan in 2016. He was fascinated by the abundance of food, beautiful nature, and warm-hearted people, and later moved to Ishikawa Prefecture. He is now pursuing a new style of French cuisine that weaves together inspiration from his own culture and the bounty of nature in this region.
Meanwhile, the drink menu curated by Chef Sommelier Daigo Fukushima to match the food is immensely popular. In particular, food and soft drink pairings are highly recommended by various sources.

The spacious greenhouse is comfortably furnished with eight tables and allows guests to enjoy walking around. They are offered an amuse-bouche and a beverage at the entrance and another delicacy at the chef’s counter before they are seated at the table to start their meals. It is the perfect place for gourmet gatherings, date nights, and catching up with friends.
Please enjoy the one-of-a-kind dining experience at Restaurant  Budoonomori Les Tonnelles, which offers not only food but also a variety of entertainment.

245444.longDescription:
Komatsu City, Ishikawa Prefecture, known as the air gateway to the prefecture, has been directly connected to Tokyo via the Hokuriku Shinkansen Line, in addition to flight routes, since the spring of 2024. This accessible city is home to Auberge eaufeu, which is a 30-minute drive from Komatsu Airport. It was converted from a closed elementary school in Kanagaso with minimal modifications, and the restaurant is also open to non-overnight guests. Nestled against the backdrop of Japanese satoyama and rice terraces, the restaurant boasts scenic views of cliffs with quarries producing Nikka stone.

Born in 1992, Chef Shota Itoi trained at a renowned restaurant in L’Auberge de l’Ill in Alsace, France, and further honed his culinary skills at Maison de Gill Ashiya (renamed Maison de Taka Ashiya in 2016) after returning to Japan. In 2018, at the age of 26, the talented chef became the youngest Red Egg (grand prix) winner of the RED U-35 competition for young chefs under the age of 35. In 2023, he was also featured in the Japanese edition of one of the most famous gourmet guides in France.

His dishes are inspired by French cuisine and arranged with local ingredients to share stories of nature in Kanagaso. The amuse bouche of fritters features loach and crabs caught by the chef and other staff in local rivers. Prepared with snowmelt water flowing from the sacred Mt. Hakusan to take advantage of its incredible softness, the dishes highlight seasonal ingredients, such as edible wild plants in the spring and wild herbs in the summer. The bounty of nature and the proximity to communities of producers bring a hint of freshness and a touch of storytelling to the dishes.
Adjacent to the auberge is Noguchi Naohiko Sake Institute, a notable brewery and tasting room run by Sake Brewer Naohiko Noguchi, who is also known as the patron saint of sake makers. Under his guidance, Chef Itoi uses koji (malted rice) and sake lees sourced from the brewer in his cooking and explores the culinary magic of fermentation by fermenting different varieties of mushrooms and creating homemade fish sauce from sweetfish and other fish. Their sense of solidarity as members of the same local community enhances the mutual appeal of their products even more.

Auberge eaufeu offers a selection of wines, mainly natural wines, from around the world. The restaurant also boasts a wide variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks to pair with the dishes, including Japanese sake brewed by Brewer Noguchi and original mocktails featuring local wild herbs and fruits.

The dining room, converted from a faculty room on the first floor of the three-story former school building, has eight counter seats and 20 table seats, which can be combined to seat small or large parties (groups of two, four, or eight guests). The simple, stylish, and modern room with a hint of its former self, ample space, and large windows that provide views of the old schoolyard invites guests to allow their imaginations to wander back to the times when the building was used as an elementary school. The private dining room, which was transformed from the principal’s office, seats two to 10 guests. Please note that the restaurant does not accept children under the age of 10. English-speaking staff are available for assistance. In addition, the French-speaking chef can also explain the dishes if time permits.

Please visit Auberge eaufeu and enjoy the bounty of nature in Kanagaso and the unique dining experience only offered at the restaurant converted from an old elementary school.

245194.longDescription:
Sushi Nao is located across from Chuo Mishoku-Gai Street, a road lined with food stands, in Katamachi, the downtown area of Kanazawa, a locale blessed with the bounty of the sea. The restaurant’s owner, Naoki Arakawa, trained at Suehiro Sushi in his hometown of Shizuoka, honing his culinary skills while working at the one-star restaurant Sushi-Ichi and at two-star Shoukouwa in Singapore, before returning to Japan and opening Sushi Nao in 2019.

Sushi Nao serves fish and shellfish sourced from Kanazawa, Toyama, and Shizuoka, but chooses to specifically highlight southern bluefin tuna from Shimizu, Shizuoka Prefecture. Chef Arakawa purchases the best-quality whole bluefin tuna from one of Japan’s leading tuna brokers before they are shipped to Toyosu Market. Each tuna is delicately thawed by the skilled chef using his elaborate techniques, and is as fresh as if it was just caught from the sea. 

Each tuna is cut into parts so that four to five different cuts can be featured in a multi-course meal, such as lean, fatty back, fatty belly, hagashi (tail), and lightly charcoal-grilled meat. Besides bluefin tuna, a dish of rice topped with the highest-quality sea urchin and salmon roe is also popular among the guests. The sushi rice, made with a mix of new and aged Koshihikari rice from Oku-Noto and original rice vinegar, demonstrates impressive flavor, falling apart as soon as it touches the tongue and pairing extremely well with the rich, distinct flavors of the fish and shellfish.
The drinks menu always has 10 labels of Japanese sake, mainly from Toyama, Kanazawa, and Shizuoka. Tea is exclusively prepared by a tea shop in Shizuoka which the chef has partnered with for years. Different tea leaves are blended, roasted, and crafted into tea in a way to ensure that it matches well with sushi.

Inside the restaurant, guests are warmly welcomed by the chef behind the U-shaped counter, which seats up to nine people. Diners are treated to a display of the highly skilled chef conjuring up sushi in front of them. The sushi is served on Kutani ware and Wajima lacquerware. Sushi Nao is perfect for all occasions, including date nights, business meetings, family gatherings, and solo meals, as well as entertaining guests from abroad.

Guests are invited to enjoy the delicious flavors of southern bluefin tuna in all its glory, an experience only available at Sushi Nao.

244197.longDescription:
A 3-minute walk from Kanazawa’s Katamachi intersection, and just a street away from Saigawa River, Nihonryori Zeniya holds world gourmet guide award and is a “must-visit” in the area. Kanazawa is an area of Japan blessed with an abundance of natural ingredients which allows Nihonryori Zeniya to offer a truly seasonal experience - for lunch or dinner - all year round.

Zeniya’s owner-chef, Mr Shinichiro Takagi, personally visits the local markets to ensure that only the highest quality ingredients reach his tables. While the menu retains an air of tradition throughout, dishes also incorporate innovative ideas and approaches to ensure that they match what customers are looking for.

In order to further enrich the traditional feeling within the restaurant, local wares such as Wajima lacquered goods and Kutani-yaki porcelain are used. Along with the inclusion of local art pieces, guests can feel Kanazawa’s cultural importance emanating from all around them.

Zeniya’s signature dish is without a doubt the abalone steak based on a recipe passed down from the previous generation. The abalone is stewed for at least 10 hours to create a uniquely soft texture in this specialty dish. Please be aware that advance reservations are required to have this included within your meal. 

The restaurant has 6 private rooms of various sizes with several different seating options including regular western-style chairs and traditional “Horigotatsu” sunken-floor options. It is possible to host small groups up to a maximum of 25 members. One of the most popular booking options, however, is the counter seats which allows diners to converse with Chef Takagi while watching him work his magic.

After training at the prestigious Kyoto Kitcho restaurant, Chef Shinichiro Takagi returned home to take over Nihonryouri Zeniya from his parents along with younger brother, and current general chef, Jiro Takagi. Chef Shinichiro Takagi is often invited to restaurants and hotels around the world to introduce his unique style of Kanazawa-cuisine and takes great pride in seeing people from all around the world appreciate his dishes. Chef Takagi strongly believes that keeping a primary focus on locally-sourced ingredients from around Kanazawa helps to keep a consistent link to both traditional and quality. He hopes that everyone who encounters this unique cuisine will feel the same way.

接客も女将さんの細やかな気遣いが良かったです。

Chef Takagi is very friendly and speaks fluent English.

正直、斬新さには欠けるものの、良質な旬の食材を五感で堪能できて、まさに和食の王道をいくような保守本流の料理を味わうことができました。お土産まで付いてきて大満足でした。

お祝いで用意していただいたキャビアのせお赤飯や碗の心配りも嬉しかったです。

仲居さんも丁寧ながらきさくな方でかしこまりすぎずに楽しめました。
このご時世で旅行などもできないし、と奮発しましたが、とても満足できました。

料理、サービス全てに大満足でした。
また伺います。

金沢には3度目でしたが、今までで1番美味しかったです。
親切におにぎりまでご用意いただいて嬉しかったです。
ありがとうございました。
40年来の願いが叶い、想像以上の時間でした。

新鮮な食材のお味を損なわないように繊細な味付けと調理で最後まで大満足な構成でございました。
貴重な松茸を惜しみなく駆使して百変化。久々に松茸の価値を再認識いたしました。

料理・接客・店の雰囲気を満喫させて貰いました。
機会があればまたお邪魔したいと思います。
美味しかった。それ以外にない。良かった。１０月にまた金沢に行く予定なので行けたら行きたい
サービス、料理内容、大変満足です。
We had an amazing time - excellent food and Chef Takagi  was friendly and engaging throughout and made us feel very welcome.
物超所值！

国外、県外のお客様に石川県の郷土料理あり、海山の幸等を楽しんでいただきました。
大変満足して帰られました。
ありがとうございました。


今後も利用させていただきます。

蟹しんじょうのお椀、蒸鮑、鰤なども、大変美味しくいただけました。
ありがとうございました。

This is an exceptional dining experience. Our menu featured Kanazawa specialties, in particular much seasonal fish and vegetables. Each course was stunning to the eye and to the palate, including the dishware, crockery and lacquerware.  The owner and head chef Shin was so gracious, and he explained each course to us in perfect English. His wife is front of house and is equally delightful. 
I recommend Zeniya heartily.
おいしかった。

旅行で初めて金沢”を訪問しました。
お店の情報がなかなかなく、ガイドブックで見た中から調べ、思いきって予約してみましたら、大当たりでした。お店の品格、従業員の方々皆さん、とても丁寧でありつつ気さくな対応で畏まらずリラックスして頂くことが出来ました。どのお料理もとても丁寧な下拵えのおかげで、素材を格上げするお味付け、見た目も美しく季節を謳歌出来ました。

どうもありがとうございました。

先日は美味しくお料理をいただくことができ、妻ともども大変満足しております。
盛り付けや料理に使われた器も綺麗で楽しませていただきました。

Highly recommended!

どの料理も大変美味しくいただくことができたのと、個室も落ち着く雰囲気でよかったです。

244759.longDescription:
At the northern part of Ishikawa Prefecture, Wajima City is located in Okunoto on the Noto Peninsula, which protrudes into the Sea of Japan. A one-star restaurant “L'Atelier de NOTO” is located in the center of this town, rich in nature, known for its Wajima-nuri lacquerware and morning market. Chef Toshiya Ikehata, who fell in love with the ingredients of Noto, brings out the charm of Noto to its fullest.

Chef Ikehata was born in Wajima City, Ishikawa Prefecture. He graduated from Tsuji Culinary School in Osaka and trained at the French restaurant “Calendrier”. He went to France in 2006 and studied at a starred restaurant for about 5 years. After returning to Japan, he thought of opening a restaurant in Osaka, a place he was familiar with, but while mastering cooking, he rediscovered the wonderful ingredients of his home town of Noto. He then decided to set up his own business in his hometown instead. In 2014, he opened “L'Atelier de NOTO” and it became a popular restaurant listed in the world famous gourmet guidebook.

Chef Ikehata said, "The more I live in Noto, the more I realize the charm of Noto", "Noto's treasures include its lively vegetables, fresh and beautiful seafood, and the wonderful products and crafts that its people produce. We want customers to feel it." In addition, because it is a production area of high-quality natural mushrooms and also because of the vertical topography of the inland sea, even if the sea is rough, it is possible to go out for fishing, so it has many advantages as a treasure house of ingredients. Chef Ikehata's specialty is "Noto 115 confit with the charcoal scent," which uses the Noto shiitake mushroom "Noto 115", also known as "mountain abalone". This is a dish where you can feel the season when the flavor of the shiitake mushroom and the texture of the confit are mixed with the charcoal scent on the table. The restaurant is particular about Japanese sake. They have around 12 to 13 types, focusing on Japanese sake from Noto, including famous sake made with super soft water. There are 200 varieties of wine, mainly from Burgundy, which chef Ikehata has been familiar with since his training in France.

The tasteful building is a renovated building that used to be a Wajima-nuriya. The doors and ceiling of the storehouse are left as they were, and you can feel the glory of the past. The dinnerware is made of lacquer, tin ware, glass, etc. The dining room has 14 seats, and there are private rooms (4-6 people) and semi-private rooms (4 -6 people). “L'Atelier de NOTO” is where you can relax and enjoy your meal around the courtyard, is recommended for various occasions, such as with family, friends, dates, and overseas guests. Please enjoy the gastronomy that is unique to chef Ikehata, who is full of love for Noto.
nearestStations: Take the JR Hokuriku Main Line to “Kanazawa Station”, then take a limited express bus to “Wajima Marintown Station” and walk for 7 minutes or take the Noto Railway Nanao Line to “Anamizu Station” and then take a route bus to “Wajima Station” (Maibara - Toyama) and walk for 10 minutes.

245437.longDescription:
Conveniently located seven minutes on foot from the West Exit of JR Kanazawa Station, ecoutieres is located in a residential alley off a bustling street. Passing by a small signboard bearing the restaurant’s name in front of a detached house, guests are greeted with a light noren curtain with the restaurant’s name on it.

Chef Norio Kawamoto, born in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, in 1964, opened his own restaurant, Preeminence, in Kanazawa to fulfill his dream of opening a three-star French restaurant in his hometown and received the Chevalier de l'ordre du Merite Agricole (Knight of the Order of Agricultural Merit) from the French government. He was also awarded one star in 2021. Subsequently, the renowned chef, who represents the French gastronomic scene of Ishikawa, opened a new restaurant, ecoutieres.
The restaurant’s name is a coined term that means “listening to the voice of ingredients.” Taken over from his previous restaurant, the idea of listening to the voice of ingredients to wow guests is now more explicitly articulated by showing guests how ingredients are transformed into culinary masterpieces right in front of their eyes.
The food menu of ecoutieres features locally produced, seasonal ingredients from around Ishikawa Prefecture and the Hokuriku Region, such as Noto brand beef produced in Ishikawa Prefecture, vegetables from Noto Island, and seafood from Ushitsu, Nanao, and Kanazawa Ports and Toyama Bay. The best ingredients of the day are supplied by producers with whom Chef Kawamoto has built strong relationships through in-person interactions. Wild game meat, such as boar and bear, is also delivered by Hakusan Fumoto Kai in Ishikawa during the game season. In addition, edible wild plants from the sacred Mt. Hakusan, such as wasabi, wild parsley, and spicebush, are essential ingredients that add depth to dishes. To celebrate the natural bounty of the Hokuriku Region, the wild plants from the community forests are powdered or infused in oil to add flavor.

About 80% of the wines on the menu are imported from France, including 25 Champagne wines. There is also a list of French wines, Japanese sakes, and non-alcoholic drinks, such as teas and mixed juices from Shikoku, to pair with dishes.

The dining room and kitchen with a wood-fired oven at the center are furnished and equipped by the chef himself with all his heart and soul. The oven is powered by wood and charcoal. With an L-shaped counter table that seats nine and a dining table that seats four,  ecoutieres is the perfect place for small business gatherings, intimate dinners, and anniversary celebrations. In addition, Chef Kawamoto’s elaborate dishes make the restaurant a gourmet hotspot. The restaurant only accommodates children of school age and older who can eat the same meals as adults, but when it is booked exclusively, children of any age are welcome. Moreover, the restaurant also has a simple English menu for guests from overseas.

Upon arrival, guests are first greeted by a large, gilded painting of Kaga Umebachi crests and cherry blossoms, with a height of two meters and a width of five meters, which engraves the image of Kanazawa into their minds. Enjoy dishes at ecoutieres, the ideal destination for all occasions, including personal celebrations, social events, friend gatherings, and trips.
nearestStations: 7 minutes walk from Kanazawa Station West Exit

courses.name: Gastronomique course
courses.summary:
We are committed to local production for local consumption in the Hokuriku region. Our seafood is sourced directly from local fishing ports, and our chef personally visits the ports to select the finest seasonal ingredients.

Each dish is presented on tableware crafted by Hokuriku artisans, expressing the character of the region through both cuisine and ceramics.

Centering on wood-fire cooking, we carefully control the embers to enhance each ingredient, applying refined French techniques to bring out their full flavor.

Our seafood comes primarily from Toyama and Noto, while our vegetables are sourced from nearby farmers, including producers on Notojima. We prepare our dishes using the finest seasonal ingredients from Hokuriku.

This course is crafted with the finest ingredients from Noto.
It features black abalone from Uzu Fishing Port, Noto Premium beef fillet—often called the “phantom wagyu” for its rarity—grilled over a wood fire, along with thick Noto 115 shiitake mushrooms.

Seasonal dishes include a gargouillou-style vegetable course made with organic produce from Takano Farm in Notojima, and a buckwheat galette using Noto-grown soba flour.
These exceptional local ingredients are presented through contemporary French cuisine.

244573.longDescription:
On the banks of the Sai River as it flows through Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture, a world gourmet guide award ""Ryōtei Suginoi Honami"" is about 100 years mansion that has been converted into a ryōtei with tatami rooms built in the styles of the tea ceremony room and the traditional Japanese room with tokonoma alcove. Customers are welcomed by second-generation proprietor Mr. Koichiro Koshizawa, who hopes that they will enjoy Kanazawa food culture and ryōtei culture to the utmost.

Born as son and heir to ""Suginoi Honami,"" Mr. Koshikawa joined leading beer manufacturers Sapporo Breweries in 1980, after graduating from Waseda University. He worked there for 10 years, before returning to ""Suginoi Honami"" in 1990, managing the luxury restaurant as second-generation proprietor since 2012. Mr. Koshikawa speaks of his desire ""to communicate the essence of enjoying authentic food in an authentic place that retains the format of an original ryōtei."" While setting a high value on the traditional formalities, he took hints from resorts both at home and abroad, and, in search of the true value of relaxation and new hospitality styles, opened ""Tsubomi"" in 2004. In 2017, next to the ryōtei, he opened the ""Suginoi Honami Annex,"" where guests can enjoy lunch and a Japanese sake bar, and there pursues a new style of ryōtei.

Kanazawa: blessed with the fruits of the seas and the mountains, and fresh, seasonal ingredients. The cuisine of ""Suginoi Honami"" allows enjoyment of the delicious flavors of the ingredients: flavorfulness is a matter of course, and, prioritizing the relaxation of the ryōtei, excessive seasoning and heating are avoided, in order that guests may delight in the delicacy of the ingredients. As with the kudzu noodles in syrup, which continue to be beloved of long-time guests and are made only with genuine kudzu root from Yoshino in Nara Prefecture, a particularity about ingredients down to the last detail enhances every specialty dish of ""Suginoi Honami"". With a focus on a local brewery with whom they have a long familiarity, they usually offer 20 varieties of Japanese sake. Available wines include Katsunuma Winery ""Arugabranca"".

When you have followed the stone-flagged path and passed from the entrance hall to a room, a stunning Japanese garden of over 5,300 square feet opens before your eyes. This construction, where wild grasses and flowers can appreciate in every season, was another of Mr. Koshikawa's ideas. In addition, as Kanazawa escaped the destruction and disasters of wartime, implements and dishes from older times (such as hanging scrolls, doors, windows, and screens) remain, and the highly atmospheric space can be enjoyed to the full. Every aspect — garden, furnishings, hospitality, dishes, and more — welcomes the guest in the ""Suginoi Honami"" way. The 6 private rooms of varying sizes can be used by 2–30+ guests. This richly historied world gourmet guide award luxury restaurant is delighted to receive couples, families, and work parties, at those moments in life that lend themselves to being enjoyed at a ryōtei.

245036.localizedAddress: Otsu Ha Bu 26-1, Nakajimamachishiotsu, Nanao-shi, Ishikawa
245036.longDescription:
A short 20-minute drive from the center of Nanao City in Ishikawa Prefecture transports visitors to Villa della Pace, a one-star Italian trattoria nestled in a tranquil grove near the seashore of the Noto Peninsula. Chef Meiju Hirata, who has fallen in love with the nature of Noto and the flavors of its mountains and surrounding sea, offers dishes to celebrate the bounty of the region.

Chef Hirata trained at several Italian restaurants in Tokyo for a total of eight years and established relationships with producers around Japan. In September 2016, he opened Villa della Pace in Nanao, Ishikawa, in the Noto Peninsula, which he selected for its unmatched bounty of natural produce including meat, fish, and vegetables. Then, in 2020, he fulfilled his long-cherished dream of opening an auberge as he relocated the trattoria to a nearby location while retaining its name.

“I would like to open an auberge so that our guests can enjoy the nature and food of Noto to their heart’s content,” he says. Located at the head of the Gulf of Nanao, Villa della Pace boasts a 180-degree panoramic view of the sea which appears as still as a lake. Guests visiting the auberge have this spectacular view all to themselves as the beach, previously crowded with bathers 30 years ago, is now secluded without any buildings as far as the eye can see.

A 30-minute drive away from the auberge is the fishing port of Nanao, where fish are sold straight from the catch every morning. At the port, chef Hirata often sees chef Takayoshi Yamaguchi from Sushidokoro Mekumi, a two-star sushi restaurant in Nonoichi, whom he consults for advice on local marine products, fishermen, and the fishing port. In addition to the fish purchased at the port, Hirata also uses vegetables grown in his kitchen garden, edible wild mushrooms and plants collected in the hilly groves behind the establishment, and other locally sourced, natural ingredients to prepare dishes.

Chef Hirata has developed his own original Noto cuisine, which is based on Italian cuisine but features salt and water to highlight the flavors of ingredients and celebrates the bounty of the region’s natural larder. His simple dishes, beautifully executed dishes are best appreciated when paired with wines and sake selected by the sommelier.

Take a trip with family, close friends, or food friends to feel the unique ambience of Noto and explore local flavors through the scenic vistas and delicious dishes offered by chef Hirata to share his love for its natural surroundings.

244500.longDescription: A two-star Japanese cuisine restaurant ""Kataori"" opened in 2018 alongside the Asano River, about 10 minutes by car from Hokutetsu-Kanazawa. In this location, rich with the old Edo atmosphere of the Higashi Chaya District that stretches along the opposite bank of the river, ""Kataori"" serves Japanese cuisine that highlights the tastes of local ingredients, along with a sense of the transition of seasons. The owner-chef, Takuya Kataori established KATAORI after working as the sous chef at Tsuruko, a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Kanazawa(Tsuruko is schedule to be closed in November 2018) then as the chef at a ryotei restaurant in the city. With ""Simple dishes, pared down and scrutinized, highlighting the ingredients of Hokuriku"" as his motto, he is devoted to the connoisseurship and purchasing of ingredients. Takuya shops every day to obtain fresh natural ingredients. He heads to Nanao every morning to examine the morning's catch of fish, then returns to the restaurant with the live catch for marinating and filleting. On the way back from Nanao he stops at Tatsuruhama to collect Fujinose sacred water for use in dishes and in the broth that forms their base. He buys vegetables directly from farmers, listening to growers' ideas and helping them harvest while procuring pure, natural goods and the season's highest-grade ingredients. In autumn, he makes 6-hour round trips to Suzu from late September through October to pick matsutake mushrooms. (In Kanazawa, the taste of matsutake picked that morning is a special treat to be found only at ""Kataori"") Takuya also directly purchases select winter crab and the country's top morning-catch Japanese pufferfish at fishing harbors. The broth that brings out these wonderful, top-class ingredients of Hokuriku is made with bonito shavings that are a special-order item from Makurazaki in Kagoshima. The bonito used are only those caught in the most stress-free way, without contacting the fishing net. Kelp from Rishiri and the spring water of Fujinose also go into the broth. The soy sauce is made with 100% domestic soybeans. Only the best ingredients of Kanazawa come together to create dishes only found at ""Kataori"". 5 selections of Japanese sake are always on offer, centered on local creations. French wine, champagne, and Noto wine are also available. Takuya Kataori's commitment extends to local utensils and interior furnishings by ""sukiya"" architecture carpenters. The 8-seat counter is a single plank of wood from ""ate,"" the prefectural tree of Ishikawa, while the floor is ""tomuro"" stone also used in the stone walls of Kanazawa Castle. The wild grasses decorating spaces in the floor were picked among the mountains by Takuya Kataori on the return from morning purchasing trips to Noto. The dining utensils, collected for over a decade by Takuya and his wife, feature antiques by artists with connections to Ishikawa Prefecture, including works by Rosanjin and by Kutani ware artists Seika Suda and Eiju Yaguchi. ""Kataori"" hopes that you will enjoy the deep flavors of chef Kataori's dishes, together with the ingredients and the stories they weave, such as the specially selected chairs repaired from antiques. ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. Please include your child(ren)'s information in your reservation. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible and we will be happy to assist as needed. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customization on our course offers or offer a la carte option. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals. We request that you do not wear strong scent or perfume when dining with us.

244819.longDescription:
Located in a convenient downtown area for sightseeing in Takaoka-cho, A one-star Japanese restaurant “Kanazawa Setsuri” is a 5-minute walk from “Omicho Market” which supports Ishikawa and Kanazawa food. The chef, Yasuo Kawada, is known as the second-generation chef of Kanazawa's long-established restaurant “Kaiseki Tsuruko”.

After training in “Ajikitcho” in Osaka, chef Kawada returned to his parents' home, “Kaiseki Tsuruko” at the age of 25. In the TV program "Iron Chef" he showed his remarkable talent by competing with Rokusaburo Michiba in "Monkfish Contest". He became the head chef at the age of 33 and was awarded two stars by world famous gourmet guide. In January 2016, he appeared on a TV program called "Jonetsu Tairiku". However, in ryotei, there was a reality that warm dishes cooled down before they were brought to the customers from the kitchen. With the thought of "nothing beats the persuasive power of a cook to cook in front of customer", “Kaiseki Tsuruko” temporarily closed in 2018, and in November 2019, opened again as “Kanazawa Setsuri”, which serves mainly counter seats.

The ingredients are purchased from reliable brokers in “Omicho Market” with long-standing relationships. And chef Kawada is very thorough in incorporating what he wants to eat at that time and what he wants to eat on that day into the menu, and never provides thing he doesn't like. In “Kanazawa Setsuri”, "Blackthroat seaperch shabu-shabu" and "Steamed egg with crab miso sherbet" are popular. The proprietress selects about 15 kinds of sake from all over Japan, including local sake.

There are 7 counter seats and private room with 4 table seats. One of the features of “Kanazawa Setsuri” is that a large monitor in front of the counter shows the scenery of Kanazawa and you can enjoy your meal while feeling the climate of Kanazawa. The dinnerware and sake cups are decorated with Kanazawa-style Kutani-ware. “Kanazawa Setsuri”, which is full of the charm of Kanazawa and chef Kawada's passion, is loved by local people, and is a good restaurant that even guests from outside the prefecture can enjoy the charm of Kanazawa. We hope you will enjoy the authentic Japanese cuisine of chef Kawada that is backed by his career.

245572.longDescription:
About five minutes’ drive from Kanazawa Station in Ishikawa Prefecture, Tsuruko Chishinan is situated in Takaokacho at the center of Kanazawa City. Conveniently located within walking distances to Omicho Market and Kenrokuen Garden, this kaiseki restaurant had its grand opening in November 2025 after a full renovation of Kaiseki Tsuruko, a long-established restaurant loved by locals. Founded in 1965, Kaiseki Tsuruko was a renowned popular restaurant offering traditional cuisine originating from the flourishing feudal domain of Kaga. Combining the name of the original restaurant with that of the attached tea room, the new restaurant was renamed “Tsuruko Chishinan.”

The kitchen is helmed by Chef Keisuke Takemoto. He worked at Kyoto Kitcho for a dozen years from 1998 and further honed his culinary skills at renowned restaurants, including Mizai in Kyoto. Making a name for himself while working at a Japanese restaurant in Fujian, China, and at Taka-an in Aman Kyoto, he was appointed as the chef of Tsuruko Chishinan in 2025.

Inheriting the essence of Kaga kaiseki cuisine from Kaiseki Tsuruko, where tradition meets innovation, Tsuruko Chishinan offers exquisite dishes prepared with meticulous care and fresh ingredients from the land and sea of Noto and Kaga. In addition to the carefully selected ingredients, such as fish from the rough Sea of Japan and seasonal vegetables and edible wild plants, the water obtained from the deep ocean off Noto to prepare and cook ingredients and make dashi stock is a testament to the chef’s commitment to quality. The mineral-rich water allows rice to cook until it is fluffy and glossy and brings out and balances the natural flavors of any ingredients.

The curated prix-fixe menu features top-quality seasonal ingredients, such as matsutake mushrooms in autumn and Kano crabs (snow crabs caught off the coasts of Ishikawa Prefecture and named from the initial Chinese characters of Kaga and Noto) in winter. They are complemented by a rich selection of sake and wines. While the sake list offers carefully selected premium labels from renowned sake-making regions around Ishikawa Prefecture, such as Kikuhime Tori, Kokuryu Muni, Kokuryu Ishidaya, Kokuryu Nizaemon, and Juyondai Tatsu no Otoshigo, the wine list offers over 150 French wines curated by the sommelier to cater to the tastes of wine enthusiasts and connoisseurs, including Grand Cru wines from Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and Leroy in Burgundy, Chateau Petrus in Bordeaux, Jacques Selosse in Champagne, and Screaming Eagle in Napa, California.

Designed as a Japanese auberge, the inn features natural materials that exude grace and style. The Japanese-style lamps along the approach to the entrance invite guests and also create a fantastic atmosphere. The main dining room with a counter (seating up to eight guests) and private dining room (seating up to six guests) are adorned with Wajima lacquerware and Kutani ware that evoke the elegance of Kaga and the dynamism of Noto. When you visit Kanazawa, indulge in the charm of Kaga cuisine at Tsuruko Chishinan, which caters to various occasions, such as family and friend gatherings, date nights, feasts, client dinners, and meals with guests from abroad.
nearestStations: Approximately a 6-minute walk from Kanazawa Station, Kenrokuen Exit (East Exit).

A unique dining experience crafted before your eyes, featuring the finest seasonal ingredients from Kanazawa and Noto.
With precise techniques and careful attention to detail, our chefs bring out the true character of each ingredient.
The aromas, the sound of charcoal, and the colors of the season enhance every moment of the meal.

■ Commitment to Ingredients
We showcase the natural bounty of Noto and Kaga, prioritizing the highest-quality ingredients from Ishikawa.
Local traditions are respected and refined with a modern sensibility, offering dishes that express the flavor of this land and season.

■ Commitment to Water
All water used in our cooking comes from Noto’s deep ocean water or the pure brewing water of Kanazawa, enhancing the clarity and elegance of every dish.

We only accept "waiting list reservations." There may be available days that are not shown on the calendar, so please first register the date you would like to make a reservation on the waiting list. Lunchtime starts from 11:00 to 12:00, and dinnertime starts from 17:00 to 18:00.

If there is a cancellation or a vacancy becomes available on the date and time you requested, and the conditions of your application are met, we will contact you by email to confirm your reservation.

Founded in 1752 (2nd year of the Horeki Era), Tsubajin is the most historically renowned restaurant in Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture. Here, "flavors of satisfaction" and "customer-oriented approach " are philosophies that have been passed down since the restaurant's establishment. This historical restaurant representing Kanazawa, is also popular amongst guests from overseas. 

Prepared in accordance with Kaga Hyakumangoku culture, the Kaga cuisine served here offers an extremely refined style of traditional Japanese Kaiseki dining unique to the area and can be enjoyed with any of the wide selection of handpicked local sakes. 

Relax while admiring the mossy garden from a traditional Japanese-style room, enjoy the mixture of modernity and nostalgia in a Taisho Era western-style room or meet up in a white-plaster conference room suitable for business meetings and events. From weddings to engagement parties, to coming-of-age celebrations, this is the perfect place to celebrate the big moments in life.

The fully-equipped private rooms are suitable for a variety of situations, from entertaining guests to dinner parties and to ceremonial occasions. Come and experience with your own five senses the space with a sense of hospitality unchanged for over 260 years.

244729.longDescription:
A 20-minute drive from Komatsu Airport, a gateway to the Hokuriku region, will take you to SHÓKUDŌ YArn, a one-star restaurant housed in a simple, single-story building in a residential area. Inside the restaurant, there is an aged olive tree in the inner court surrounded by a glass-paned kitchen and dining rooms. The restaurant is run by two chefs: Owner, Chef, and Sommelier Yuji Yoneda, and his wife, Asami Yoneda, who serves as a dessert chef and herb coordinator.

Having trained at starred Spanish restaurants and Italian restaurants, Chefs Yuji and Asami Yoneda opened their own restaurant, SHÓKUDŌ YArn, in 2015 at the site that had formerly been a yarn twisting factory run by Asami’s parents. The restaurant offers a chef’s choice prix-fixe menu informed by modern Spanish techniques the two chefs learned as apprentices and inspired by Japanese home-cooking recipes.

The dining experience starts with Noto Hiba chopsticks placed on the table. The refreshing scent of Hiba (a type of hinoki cypress) drifting from the chopsticks when they are picked up is the cue to start the meal. The majority of the ingredients featured on the chef’s choice menu are sourced locally from Ishikawa Prefecture, especially Komatsu. For example, the water used for cooking is collected by the chef himself from the Yarimizu Kannon Holy Water Shrine in Butsudaiji, Nomi City, Ishikawa Prefecture, designated as one of the Famous Waters of the Heisei Era. The water is soft and adds depth to the taste of konbu stock.

Diners are given a menu in advance, but it is hard to tell what the dishes might be like from their names. They are intentionally named that way to allow guests to enjoy their dining experience without preconceptions. For example, Nikujaga (Simmered Meat and Potatoes), which has been on the menu since day one, may sound familiar to most Japanese guests, but it is reinterpreted with a surprising twist that gives it a unique texture and flavor. Some dishes are given a finishing touch at the table by the chef, filling the dining room with cheerful chatter and laughter.

Attracting guests of all ages, including families, expectant mothers, and seniors, SHÓKUDŌ YArn is perfect for gatherings and parties. The dining room seats up to 14 guests though it is generally equipped with two four-seat tables. The wine list offers some 300 different labels, mainly from France but also from Spain and Italy, while the Japanese sake list has some 10 different choices of local sake. The Japanese-style interior with European influences and woody tones feels warm and cozy, making the dining experience pleasant.
nearestStations: JR Hokuriku Line (Maibara - Toyama) Komatsu Station 10 minutes by cab 15 minutes by cab from Komatsu Airport

245386.longDescription:
Located about a ten-minute drive from Mizusawa Esashi Station on the Tohoku Shinkansen line, Japanese Restaurant SHINCHAYA was established in 1850 at the center of Oshu City in Iwate Prefecture. Inheriting the traditions of the long-established restaurant, the seventh-generation chef, Yasutaka Waga, brings a fresh perspective with a vision ahead of the times.

Born as the seventh generation of the family running Japanese Restaurant SHINCHAYA, Yasutaka attended Osaka Abeno Tsuji Culinary Institute and honed his culinary skills at Hyotei and Hiiragiya Ryokan in Kyoto before returning to Iwate. He joined Japanese Restaurant SHINCHAYA in 2015 and took over as chef in 2018.

The new chef brought new ideas to the restaurant run by his predecessor, making slow but steady changes to the design and menus of the restaurant. Located in Iwate Prefecture, a large prefecture blessed with food resources, the restaurant is particular about its ingredients, such as fish and shellfish sourced directly from rich fishing grounds off Ofunato Fishing Port in Iwate and Shiogama Fishing Port in the neighboring prefecture of Miyagi, among others, as well as edible wild plants and mushrooms picked for the spring and autumn menus, respectively, by the chef himself.

The restaurant’s 12-course meal always includes at least one meat dish, featuring a special product of Iwate, which is noted not only for its seafood but also for its meat products, such as Iwate Short-horned Wagyu Beef, Yanagawa Lamb and Mutton from Esashi, and guinea fowl from Hanamaki. The beef, lamb, and mutton are first grilled in a pan made of Nambu Ironware, another specialty of Iwate, and then cooked on charcoal. The matsutake mushrooms are also steamed in a Nambu Ironware teapot instead of an earthen teapot to reduce cooking time. The appetizers and soups featuring seasonal ingredients are particularly popular due to the dashi stock made from Japanese kelp from Shirokuchihama, Hokkaido, dried bonito and tuna flakes from Ishinomaki, Miyagi.

The sake list offers five to six selected labels from Iwate, including AKABU, as well as the chef’s favorites from all over the Tohoku Region, including Aramasa from Akita. The drink menu also consists of a wide selection of choices, including red and white wines mainly from Bourgogne, beers from Germany, and non-alcoholic drinks.

Walking through a narrow alley, you will be greeted by the elegant façade of Japanese Restaurant SHINCHAYA. Then, stepping across its threshold, you will immediately be greeted by seasonal decorations. The flowers are hand-picked daily by the chef from his garden or nearby mountain meadows. The main dining room with an area of 100 tatami mats (seating up to 50 guests) and the private dining rooms (seating up to two guests) are all equipped with tables and chairs. The chef always seeks to create Japanese dishes that showcase the flavors of Iwate Prefecture. These elaborate dishes and the stylish atmosphere make the long-established Japanese restaurant worth a visit to Iwate, no matter how far away you may live.
nearestStations: 12 minutes by car from Mizusawa Esashi Station on the Tohoku Shinkansen Line

245486.longDescription:
Located in Kawaramachi, downtown Takamatsu, Kagawa Prefecture, at the gateway to the Shikoku Region, Sushitomo is helmed by Chef Yuya Sato, offering exquisite delicacies and sushi made with carefully selected ingredients from local sources and around Japan. 

Chef Sato says he aspired to become a sushi chef because he loved fish and sushi. His Edomae sushi is built around his experience in a fishmonger’s shop and extensive knowledge of fish as well as fresh ingredients sourced from the rich nature of Shikoku and quality ingredients carefully selected from around Japan. He aims at delivering not just good sushi but absolutely delicious sushi as he puts it. In fact, his sushi adds a subtle yet definite kick to each bite. That lingering impression draws sushi lovers to Takamatsu from around Kagawa and Japan.

The sushi rice is made with Hinohikari rice, locally grown in Kagawa Prefecture. It is cooked crispy outside and fluffy inside so that it will taste best when it is turned into sushi. The cooked rice is seasoned with a blend of two red vinegars for a delicate flavor that you will never get enough of. The sushi toppings are also carefully prepared to match the sushi rice. All these steps work together to create Sushitomo-style sushi. Another characteristic of Sushitomo is that the prix-fixe menu of small plates and sushi can be customized for each guest. For example, diners can choose a meal with fewer small plates or a sushi-only meal, depending on their mood that day. The drink menu also offers a wide variety of options, ranging from alcoholic drinks, such as sake, white wine, and champagne, to non-alcoholic drinks, such as Japanese tea, Taiwanese oolong tea, Perrier, and sparkling tea, to satisfy personal tastes and preferences.

The dining room is cozy, only with an L-shaped hinoki cypress counter (seating up to eight guests). The bright lighting allows diners to feast their eyes before their palates. Guests can also enjoy friendly conversations with the chef and proprietress while indulging in the Sushitomo-style sushi and delicacies only found in this sushi restaurant, which makes Takamatsu, Kagawa, a must-visit destination for sushi lovers.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Kotoden Kawaramachi Station

245429.longDescription:
Hakone is a special place for Japanese people. Inspired by the history and memories of countless travelers who have passed through this transit hub located on the historic Tokaido Road running from Nihonbashi Bridge in Edo (Tokyo) to Sanjo Ohashi Bridge in Kyoto, Hakone Honbako has also established its presence as a good transit point for modern-day travelers on the Tokaido Road.

Playing an important role in the gastronomic scene of Hakone, the restaurant, Hakone Honbako, is a four-minute walk from Naka-Gora cable car station and can also be accessed by a 40-minute taxi ride from JR Odawara Station. Converted from a publication distributor’s recreational facility , Hakone Honbako is nicknamed “Book Auberge” as it has installed large bookshelves stretching from the floor to the two-story ceiling on two walls next to the gently rising stairs to pay tribute to its own history.

The restaurant has been helmed since 2023 by Chef Yukihiro Hagiwara, who honed his culinary skills at a restaurant of the Salone Group, headquartered in Yokohama, to run high-end Italian restaurants, and a one-star restaurant in Puglia, Italy, before he joined Hakone Honbako in 2021. He combines his proven culinary skills with local ingredients from Shizuoka and Kanagawa to create innovative dishes that pay tribute to Tokaido.
Sous Chef Aoi Nakano trained at a one-star restaurant in Puglia, Italy, and a three-star restaurant in Denmark, and then joined Hakone Honbako in 2021 and was promoted to Sous Chef in March 2023.

Hakone Honbako features natural ingredients, such as seafood from the long-established Sasue Maeda Fish Shop in Yaizu, Shizuoka, organic vegetables from Kitayama Farm in Fujinomiya, also in Shizuoka, and natural ingredients from Keita Tanida the Natural Ingredients Hunter. All these producers are sought after not only in Kanagawa and Shizuoka but all over Japan. In addition, the restaurant sources ingredients from local producers with whom it has forged close ties. These ingredients are transformed into creative dishes that pay tribute to the location and food culture of the region. For example, “Botamochizaka” is inspired by kuri-botamochi (rice balls covered with chestnut paste), the specialty of Hodogaya, which was one of the 53 Tokaido Stations. Another example is “Yosegizaiku” (which literally means “marquetry” in Japanese). It is a marquetry-like dessert combining a gelato flavored with Japanese cedar from Hakone with other gelatos flavored with spicebush, yabunikkei, and various other native trees of the Hakone mountains.

The beverage menu offers a selection of wines and local Japanese sake. There is also a list of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks to pair with dishes. The menu is updated with new innovative drinks featuring local citrus fruits and wild plants. The modern, open dining room and kitchen are separated by a counter that seats 19. In addition, there are three private dining rooms. One of the walls is adorned with book paintings of food by an Italian-based Russian artist, Ekaterina Panikanova, to add color to the restaurant’s atmosphere.

Hakone Honbako, developed by Jiyujin, which is known for its project, Satoyama Jujo, in Niigata, shares the concept of local gastronomy with that sister project. This concept is also shared with Matsumoto Jujo’s Wood-fired grill restaurant, 367 (Sanrokunana), in Nagano. In principle, Hakone Honbako only accepts children of upper elementary age and older who can eat the same dishes as adults. Meanwhile, the restaurant offers commemorative plates for guests who want to celebrate important life events.

Come and dine at Hakone Honbako to delve into the heritage of Hakone and discover its food culture to satisfy your intellectual curiosity.

244813.longDescription:
8-minute walk from Kamakura Station, when you leave the bustle of the tourist spots, a simple and chic restaurant appears. “Arashida” is a Spanish restaurant and wine restaurant. Owner-chef Norikazu Arashida opened this restaurant in October 2010 in Kamakura, next Zushi.

Owner-chef Arashita learned the basics of cooking at restaurants throughout Japan, including "Sel et Poivre" in Shiga. When he visited the Basque region of Spain, he encountered "the most delicious in one's life" cuisine at the long-established 2-star restaurant “Zuberoa”, and he took this opportunity to learn classic Spanish cuisine under Mr. Hilario of “Zuberoa”. After that, he devoted himself to studying at starred restaurants all over Spain, such as “Azurmendi” and “Casa Marcial”.

Succeeding to the philosophy of his master Mr. Hilario, who valued the taste of food, owner-chef Arashita puts taste first. Arranging, performing, and cooking the food without any unnecessary attention to detail is what owner-chef Arashita does. "Do only what is really necessary" says owner-chef Arashita, whose cooking is supported by his experience and sense of mastery in Spain, on theories of texture and food compatibility. However, it does not stick to the framework of Spanish cuisine, he creates a flavor that goes beyond the fixed concept as a dish made by a Japanese chef using Japanese ingredients.

Specialty is "pitu", a traditional dish from the Asturias region of Spain. The stewed chicken with a rich and burnt onion sauce is one of the specialties of owner-chef Arashita, who says that with the time and effort, only few local people would make it. The traditional dessert, "arroz con leche" is rice simmered in milk for 3 hours. The flavor and richness accentuates it, and the chewy texture is characteristic. The wine is carefully selected by the owner-chef Arashita, who is also a sommelier.

There are 6 counter seats and 12 tables in the restaurant. The calm wood-style interior has a dignified and warm feeling, and is recommended for various situations such as dining with family and friends, dating, and hospitality for overseas guests. After a relaxing trip to Kamakura, please enjoy owner-chef Arashita's original refined Spanish cuisine.


[Notice]
The restaurant at the current location will be open until the end of July 2020 and will be relocated to a nearby location in January 2021.
nearestStations: A 8-minute walk from Kamakura Station, West Exit (JR Yokosuka Line)

recommendations.comment: シェフのこだわりを感じる最高の食事体験でした。

久しぶりに会う友人との再会の場所として、以前から気になっていたArashidaさんを選びました。通りから一本裏に入ったところにあるので隠れ家感満載ですが、その友人がもともとArashidaさんの常連ということもあり、なんとか到着。中に入ると洗練された店内で、とても感じの良いシェフとスタッフに迎えられ、早くも居心地がよくなってしまいました。料理が始まると、これまた洗練されたお料理の数々に襲われ、ペアリングで合わせていただくワインなども相まって、もう立ち上がれません。手の温度で溶けてしまう生ハムやクリスピーながらふわふわのサンマ（これまた食べたい）、凝縮された旨味がしみ込んだパエリアなど、友人に会うのがメインなのか、食事がメインなのか混乱してきます。お話を伺うと、どうやらシェフは理系とのことで、味や食材の組み合わせを考えるときに数学の証明を用いることもあるのだとか。多趣味でいらっしゃるシェフとの世界史の話も盛り上がり、遠方まで来たがために終電を気にしなければならなくなったことを後悔しながら帰路につきました。近所にあればいいのにと思いながら、いっそのこと近所に引っ越してしまおうかなどと、そんな思いを抱かせてくれる最高のお店の一つに出会えました。
素晴らしい料理と演出で大満足でした。また予約させていただきたいです。
とても素晴らしい料理と雰囲気でした。また、伺わせていただきます。

主人の誕生日のお祝いで伺いました。
移転前から存じ上げておりましたが、新しい店舗は落ち着いたトーンでまとめられた一軒家のカウンターキッチンで、シェフが腕を振るう姿を目の前に見ながら、ライヴ感溢れるお料理をいただけます。
より一層パワーアップした嵐田シェフが織りなす旬の一皿と、こだわりのアルコール類とのペアリングで特別な時間を過ごすことが出来ました。特にアルコールは、温度別に備えたテーブル内蔵型の2種のクーラーが興味深いです。
わざわざ遠くへ出かけなくとも、創意工夫に溢れた本格バスク地方料理11品をご近所でいただけるのはありがたい限り。また季節が変わる頃に伺いたい、そう思う貴重なお店です。
クリエイティブで美味な料理が身体を刺激し、料理を彩る数々の器がその刺激を受け止める。落ち着いた白と黒を基調とする石作りの空間の中、目の前で料理を盛り付けするシェフの手さばきとおしゃべり。どれも素晴らしい価値ある時間を演出してくれました。

245392.longDescription:
Jacob Jan Boerma, a three-star chef and one of the most respected chefs in the Netherlands, which has one of the highest gastronomic densities in the world, caused a sensation by opening SMAAK, his first ever restaurant in Asia, on the 46th floor of a building caressed by fresh breezes from the harbor and connected to Bashamichi Station on the Minatomirai Line in Yokohama, a 30-minute train ride from Shibuya, Tokyo.

Born in 1972 in the Netherlands, Director Chef Jacob started his culinary career at a young age. After training at world-renowned restaurants at home and abroad, he opened De Leest (2002-2019) in his home country. This restaurant was awarded its first star only six months after opening and given three stars a decade later. He continues to broaden his range of work, opening restaurants in the Netherlands, Belgium, and other European countries. The newly launched SMAAK is his first opening in Asia. He has entrusted this restaurant to Chef Rob Nollé, who knows his culinary philosophy better than anyone.

SMAAK offers international cuisine with Dutch roots. Director Chef Jacob’s iconic dishes are modern, casual, and sophisticated with multilayer combinations of sour and savory flavors. The beautiful and colorful dishes delight the eyes as well as the taste buds. Most of the ingredients are sourced within Japan. The fish and shellfish come from local waters around Kanagawa.
The wine list curated to match the dishes features European wineries, especially those in Scandinavian countries. The pairing menu offers both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options. Either option invites guests to delve more deeply into the culinary world of Director Chef Jacob.

The bright, modern interior boasts floor-to-ceiling windows on one side that offer stunning views of Yokohama’s bay area. The daytime harbor views and the twinkling city lights at night are equally spectacular. With seating for up to 58 guests, including private dining rooms, the restaurant is an ideal place for dates, anniversaries, intimate meals, and celebrations.

The restaurant’s name, SMAAK, means “taste” in Dutch. Why don’t you taste the modern, casual dishes that contain a complex combination of sour and savory flavors while enjoying the splendid views of Minatomirai in Yokohama?

245555.longDescription:
About seven minutes’ walk from the West Exit of Yokohama Station, ’O Pulecenella faces the peaceful Aratama River. Named after Pulecenella, a character from the traditional Italian masked theater of Commedia dell’Arte, the restaurant has cemented its position since its opening in 2001 , offering Italian dishes crafted by Chef Hiroki Hosokawa, a dedicated professional with over 30 years of experience in Italian cuisine, in an Italian vibe with white stucco walls, an arched ceiling, and a terracotta-tiled floor. He trained at famous restaurants in Italy, such as Ristorante Flipot in Piedmont and Ristorante Paolo Teverini in Emilia-Romagna. After returning to Japan, he further honed his culinary skills at renowned restaurants in Tokyo and became the chef of ’O Pulecenella in 2006.

Chef Hosokawa crafts each dish with meticulous care and heat-control and seasoning skills honed through years of experience. The seven-course dinner menu offers three courses of cold and hot appetizers, two small-portioned pasta courses, an entree, and a dessert, each prepared with an abundance of seasonal ingredients, such as wild bluefin tuna, Maesawa beef from Iwate, mushrooms from Akita, and vegetables from Nagano. Especially popular are the Steamed White Asparagus and Clams with Prosciutto and Gremolata on the spring menu and the Galette with Funghi Porcini Trifolato, Charcoal-boiled Baby Squid, White Beans Purée, and Parmigiano Reggiano on the autumn menu. The wine list offers about 60 selections, mainly from Northern Italy.

The restaurant boasts a spacious dining room with table seating (seven to eight tables) and a semi-private dining room seating up to three guests. Visit ’O Pulecenella for various occasions, from private to business settings, such as family and friend gatherings, client dinners, and meals with guests from abroad. Spend a happy time with delicious Italian dishes and wines.
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Exit 9 of Yokohama Municipal Subway Blue Line Yokohama Station.

244814.longDescription:
Kamakura in Kanagawa Prefecture is a major tourist spot in the Kanto region. Located just a 4-minute walk from JR Kamakura Station, along the bustling main street of Komachi Dori, there is “RISTORANTE IL NODO”, a restaurant where fans come from far away in search of dishes unique to this area. The restaurant is 40 years old and is built with the warmth of wood, like a solitary house in the forest.

The owner-chef, Akinori Matsui, learned the basics of Italian cuisine at “Ristorante Sabatini Aoyama”, a pioneer of authentic Italian cuisine in Tokyo. When going independent, he chose Kamakura as the location because he wanted to use fresh Kamakura vegetables and seafood that he had been using for a long time. This is the ideal place for owner-chef Matsui, who have loved Kamakura vegetables and seafood since his time in Tokyo.

Based on his relationship with reliable producers, he purchases vegetables from Watanabe Farm in Kamakura, seafood from Kazumaru at Kotsubo Fishing Port in Zushi, and also ingredients from all over Kanagawa Prefecture, including Odawara. The freedom to use Kanagawa truffles and various citrus fruits is a privilege of Kamakura's restaurants. Rather than procuring ingredients for cooking, owner-chef Matsui think of cooking as from the goodness of local ingredients. For example, a dish is made of carrots cooked in various ways and fried fish. It is an attractive dish that features the deliciousness of carrots and attracts many fans. He selected wines that go well with the food, mainly Italian and Japanese wines. Pairing is also available. You can also choose from 10 kinds of non-alcoholic drinks, such as Japanese grape juice and tea.

The interior is simple and calm with 6 counter seats and 4 table seats. It is recommended for couples who want to spend their anniversaries leisurely and gatherings with close friends. Please savor the cuisine made by the chef who is particular about the ingredients of Kanagawa and sincerely focuses on each seasonal ingredient here in Kamakura.
nearestStations: A 4-minute walk from Kamakura Station (JR Yokosuka Line, Enoshima Electric Railway Line)

245203.longDescription:
A 15-minute walk from Kamakura Station takes you to the Japanese restaurant Kamakura Kitajima near Ankokuronji Temple. Nestled at the foot of mountains with lush greenery and twittering birds, this townhouse restaurant is helmed by Chef Yasunori Kitajima.

He started his culinary career with training at several locations of WAKUDEN in Kyoto and became Chef at tan, a restaurant affiliated with WAKUDEN. Then, in May 2021, he opened Kamakura Kitajima, named after his family name, in his hometown of Kamakura.
The concept of the restaurant is to “weave.” It is a tapestry for the chef to “translate what he learned in Kyoto for years into his own unique cuisine in a different location with different ingredients” as he says. The fish is caught by fishermen risking their lives, carefully processed, and delivered to the restaurant. The meat and vegetables are also grown in a time- and labor-intensive process. Moreover, the building and tableware are imbued with the souls of their creators. All these elaborate works are inherited and woven into a flavorful dish, together with the thoughts of their creators, by Chef Kitajima so that their stories will be completed when the dish is savored on the tongue.
The fish and shellfish are sourced from a local market in Sagami Bay or a neighboring market in Suruga Bay (in Shizuoka). The vegetables are selected so that only pesticide- and fertilizer-free, healthy vegetables will be delivered. These ingredients are transformed into dishes based on the rustic and cultural cuisine the chef learned in Kyoto. Particular attention is paid to ensure that the seasonal ingredients are delivered in their best condition. In order to highlight their seasonal flavors, the stock is elaborately made with three kinds of ingredients, smoked dried bonito, fermented dried bonito, and dried tuna, which are shaved into 0.01 mm-thick flakes, with a good balance of flavors, just before they are boiled in alkalescent soft water.

The exterior of the restaurant is chic and blends in with the surrounding greenery. The interior is also natural with earthen walls and natural wood accents. The dining space is cozy with a counter seating up to eight guests, and the kitchen is well stocked with vintage and modern tableware, including early Imari ware and antique blue and white china as well as works of Rosanjin Kitaoji, who had a kiln built in Kita-Kamakura, where he played around as a child.
Located in the historic city of Kamakura, Kamakura Kitajima is worth visiting to enjoy the rustic dishes crafted by Chef Kitajima and the stories behind them with your family, partner, or friends to share the pleasure and joy of dining.
nearestStations: Take a bus from JR Kamakura Station, get off at 'Nagoe' and walk for 3 minutes

244942.longDescription:
With its mountains and sea, Chef Yuta Yamamoto says that the environment of Kamakura City, Kanagawa Prefecture, is similar to the environment of Marseille, where he trained. In a picturesque location with a view of the Enoshima Electric Railway, diners will find French restaurant Fierté. 

After graduating from high school, Yamamoto worked for four years at Royal Park Hotel in Nihonbashi Suitengu Shrine before leaving Japan for France. There, he trained at a one-star restaurant in Marseille for a year. After returning to Japan, he studied at acclaimed restaurants such as L’ecrin in Ginza, La Table de Toriumi in Chigasaki, and L’orgueil in Gaienmae. After helping at a restaurant run by his father in his hometown of Fujisawa City, Kanagawa Prefecture, he finally opened Fierté in June 2019. 

The name Fierté denotes pride in French. “We want to provide service with pride, and make our customers smile. Smile with excitement before eating, smile with deliciousness after eating,” Yamamoto says. 

The menu is a combination of the day’s best produce, paired with an ethos to avoid serving the same dishes, a conscious decision made in order to preserve the excitement of everyday life. Yamamoto and his team serve different sauces and textures, even if the ingredients from different regions, such as seafood from Saga and citrus from Kochi, overlap. Dishes with citrus accents are reminiscent of the southern French cuisine that Yamamoto studied, with additional influences from L’ecrin evident.  The restaurant is also proud of its soup de poisson, a classic dish native to southern France that Yamamoto learned to make in country. 

The wine list leans towards France, with French champagne, white, red, rosé offered to guests. While there is no conventional sommelier, the chef will select pairings that match the cuisine after tasting it himself, so guests are recommended to ask for casual suggestions.

With a cool gray interior to match the exterior, the dining room features wood-grain accents to bring out warmth. The restaurant is particular about the plates and glasses, favouring pieces from Bernardaud china to Riedel glassware. In particular, for the glasses for mineral water, Yamamoto scoured the country for glassware that fit the restaurant’s requirements. 

The restaurant is a quiet and calm space located on one of Kamakura's busy streets. Guests can relax at the 7-seat counter and enjoy a date or gathering with friends. A table seats up to 7 diners and benefits from being surrounded by windows, creating a sense of openness during the day and a private room-like intimacy during the evening.

245241.localizedAddress: 2F, Villa Apex Yokohama Kannai, 2-32-1, Otamachi, Naka-ku, Yokohama-shi, Kanagawa
245241.longDescription:
Sushi Hirose, housed in a building downtown, a five-minute walk from JR Kannai Station, is helmed by Chef Junichi Hirose, who trained at Sushidokoro Aizawa, a renowned sushi restaurant in Yokohama, for eight years and further honed his culinary skills at Ginza Kojyu, a two-star Japanese restaurant. Then, in June 2019, he opened his own restaurant in his hometown of Yokohama.

Sushi Hirose offers prix fixe (fixed price) meals that combine exquisite Japanese dishes and sushi made by the chef with innate love for sushi. After an appetizer, four to five Japanese dishes (e.g., grilled dishes) come, followed by several pieces of sushi. These elaborately prepared dishes delight the delicate palate of connoisseurs. Local ingredients, as well as high-quality ingredients sourced from around Japan, are purchased mainly from Toyosu Market but also from Yokohama City Central Wholesale Market. Then, their true flavors are brought out with great care using only natural seasonings such as salt and no excess oil, sugar, or cream. The sushi rice is made from carefully selected Akitakomachi rice. It is cooked just before guests arrive so that they can enjoy its flavor that changes with its temperature. The rice is cooked until tender on the outside but a little firm in the center (al dente) so that it offers a little resistance to the teeth but soon comes loose in the mouth and blends well with the toppings. One of the most popular menus is “Hand-rolled Sushi with Roasted Tuna.” The rich flavor of tuna roasted over charcoal right in front of guests tingle their taste buds. In addition, other popular dishes, such as charcoal grilled sweetfish (offered in summer) and eels, demonstrate the extraordinary skills of the chef, who served as a grill chef at Ginza Kojyu.
The drink menu offers more than 20 labels of red, white, and sparkling wines and more than 10 labels of Japanese sake that go well with the dishes. The food and wine or sake pairings selected by the chef, who is also certified as a sommelier instructor, are also worth trying.

The interior has a bright and elegant atmosphere that highlights the simple beauty of the traditional Japanese-style architecture. It has a main dining room with a seven-seat counter made of hinoki cypress wood and a private room with an L-shaped counter seating up to six people. The chef’s professional sincerity can be seen not only in the dishes but also in the collection of tableware that ranges from ceramics created by Rosanjin Kitaoji to those crafted by contemporary artists.
Thus, Sushi Hirose is suitable for various occasions, such as having a romantic dinner with your partner, eating out with your friends, enjoying your own company, or entertaining your business clients. Please relish the exquisite dishes and comfortable hospitality of this prominent restaurant in Yokohama.
nearestStations: A 5-minutes walk from the north exit of JR Kannai Station
