244240.longDescription:
Vena, an Italian restaurant opened in December 2016 is located in the corner of a residential area a little distance from the center of Kyoto. It was founded by Chef Daiki Hayakawa, who was born and raised in Kyoto, and Sommelier Yoji Ikemoto, with the concept of using only carefully selected ingredients and aged Italian wine. 

Hayakawa began training at IL GHIOTTONE at age 20 and became fast friends with Ikemoto, who was working at BOCCA del VINO nearby. They continued to train with the intent to start their own restaurant, with Hayakawa focusing on cooking and Ikemoto improving his servicing and wine skills. 14 years after they first met, their dream finally became a reality. The restaurant name Vena means a water vein, while also signifying how both the founders’ names have a kanji character meaning water in their name and that the restaurant is located in Kyoto, which is known as the city of water. Only one course is available for lunch and dinner, and is by reservation only. Seasonal ingredients are used, with the focus on the four seasons of Japan. Each dish is prepared with the desire of the chef for the guests to enjoy the ingredients, and flavored to match the various wine. The vegetables used are brought from the Central Market, as well as delivered directly from a contracted farm in Kisshoin, Kyoto. A wide collection of wine is available, starting with old vintage wine from the 1960s. There is a stockpile of over 1000 bottles so that the wine can be served in its best state, taking advantage of the peak of deliciousness. 

The restaurant is designed with a certain elegance as in a hotel while vintage European furniture from Ikemoto’s collection to complete the look of the interior. The lights are industrial designs from Germany, France and America. In the two-floor restaurant, the first floor has 10 counter seats and the second floor has 2 private rooms for up to 8 guests, making it perfect for business entertainment, dates, and anniversary celebrations. Up-and-coming, Italian restaurant from Kyoto. Enjoy the restaurant’s atmosphere which takes in all the good things of the old.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

244030.longDescription:
"Poquito" is well-known as one of the leading Spanish bars in Kyoto. Step through the friendly wooden door and you'll immediately notice the colorful, eye-catching Pinchos(small snack) in a showcase on the other side of the counter. The case is able to slide up and down the bar counter, a novel trick that allows customers to easily choose a snack to accompany their drink. But "Poquito" doesn't just serve bar snacks, what really sets it apart is the fact that you are also able to enjoy a full meal of top-quality food here.

The owner-chef, Kazunori Hirooka originally trained at an Italian restaurant, but after visiting Spain on holiday, he fell in love with the local bars and decided to open the same style of the bar in his native Kyoto. On the blackboard, you will find many examples of food that amply shows off Chef Hirooka's prodigious talents. Plenty of seasonal ingredients go into dishes such as Ajillo and pasta with intricate sauces, and sometimes you'll even find the wild game on the menu. The "Poquito" Salad features 7-8 seasonal vegetables procured from Miyama and Wachi simply dressed with salt and lemon-flavor olive oil, and it has remained a popular choice ever since the bar opened. There is a large selection of wine at the bar, and if you let the chef - who is also a qualified sommelier - know your tastes, then he will pick out something to suit the food.

244280.longDescription: Quietly located on the first floor of an apartment building, a 5-minute walk from Subway Marutamachi Station and close to the Kyoto Imperial Palace, is kaiseki cuisine restaurant Kiyama. Kiyama has drawn attention to itself after earning award from world gourmet guide soon after opening in April 2017. Owner Yoshiro Kiyama is a skilled chef who trained at Wakuden for 16 years from age 19, of which 10 years were spent as head chef. When the restaurant opened, they drilled a well in the garden and began using soft, delicious spring water. Something else that Kiyama is particular about is the basic of Japanese cuisine: dashi stock. As guests enjoy watching the chef shave dried bonito, he uses a fragrant and clear dashi for the soups. Each dried bonito block is tasted, selected by the level of saltiness and acidity, and types of bonito blocks are blended to balance the taste. Courses are on the menu for both lunch and dinner, starting with sayu (water boiled until white), then dish after dish which incorporates seasonal ingredients and the ultimate stock. Guests can look forward to dishes with an interesting twist which change with every visit, like the seasonal egg bowl. Light tea is then served to finish. All the dishes are matched with and served on various wares, from Japanese and Chinese antiques to those by current artists. Chef Kiyama loves alcohol, and keeps a collection of 20 to 30 types of Japanese sake and 80 bottles of wine in the wine cellar at all times. The interior of the restaurant is based on wood, creating a clean and cozy atmosphere. With 9 counter seats, two private rooms which can accommodate 4 to 7 guests and 2 to 6 guests, Kiyama is ideal for dates, business entertainment, dinner parties with friends, and other various settings. Why not come and experience the depth of kaiseki cuisine in a relaxed atmosphere. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023. ■Course serving time table The course needs the following time. If you have a departure time, please let us know in advance. Lunch: about 2.5 hours, Dinner: about 3 hours --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? At the counter seats, we welcome children who can enjoy our standard menu for adults. In our private dining room, everyone is welcome. We are happy to prepare a special menu for children. Please inquire in advance to discuss food preferences and the price. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. If fish-based Dashi stock is acceptable, we are able to offer some customizations. ■ Are menus available in other languages? A simple English menu is available if you prefer. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals. ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Unfortunately, photos or videos are not allowed in the restaurant.

243918.longDescription:
“Tatsuki,” located near Ginkaku-ji Temple in Kyoto, is a French restaurant whose concept is to “serve dishes that leave you with a lasting impression” which expresses the unique sensitivity of chef Fujiwara Tatsuki.
Chef Fujiwara trained at “Restaurant Okumura," “Sanyukyo,” “L’Hotel de Hiei,” and “La Cachette (Valence, France)” and became independent in 2011. The menu continues to evolve as chef Fujiwara adopts new methods whilst maintaining his own bold style, attracting many guests.

The course focuses on the key ingredients of each dish. It consists of 10 dishes made with seasonal ingredients, such as Tamba beef and organic vegetables from Ohara, the quality of which Fujiwara has confirmed by sight and taste from meeting with the producers directly. In addition to the simple dishes, the course also features the “Nigiri Sushi,” which is rare in French cuisine. For vinegared rice, the blend of red vinegar and rice vinegar is adjusted to match the sushi toppings of the day, based on Edomae-style sushi, with different ingredients being used, such as saury, octopus and flounder. You can enjoy dishes simply with salt, lightly kneaded flounder with kelp, or combine tapenade with tuna. It is also interesting to note that the main meat dish comes with rice and chirimen sansho pepper.

The simple and clean interior has only 3 tables in a spacious setting. This is a restaurant spending quality time with special people.
nearestStations: A 2-minute walk from Ginkakuji-dori bus stop. Take the City Bus No. 5 -17 from Demachiyanagi Station (Keihan Main Line)

243991.longDescription:
The restaurant has a modest dining room with a warm and cozy atmosphere, featuring eight counter places and eight table seats. The food is prepared in full view of all the guests.  As the name, "Kyoto Nese," implies, the restaurant serves simple seasonal dishes using ingredients that are unique to the local area. The cuisine is Italian with an authentic Kyoto-style twist.  

The menu focuses on a la carte dishes which usually change every day. For the set menu, the chef puts together a selection of dishes based on the best ingredients available that day.  The restaurant is famous for specialty dishes such as omelet or pasta carbonara made with intensely-flavored eggs from Yamada farm, or giblets of premium chicken, such as Tankai Jidori, lightly smoked on a plate of cherry blossom wood chips. 

Sample unique dishes that can only be found in this restaurant.  Each dish has a story to tell in terms of the ingredients used and the way they are served.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Kyoto Shiyakushomae Station(Kyoto Municipal Subway Tozai Line)
A 3-minute walk from Sanjo Station, Exit 1(KeihanHonsen)

244252.longDescription:
--
Deliver heartfelt moments by connecting creators, ingredients, and guests through a feast of a lifetime.
--

Gion Hanamai is located near the Yasaka Shrine in Gion, Kyoto, just off the road leading from Shijo Street to Maruyama Park. Set in a charming neighborhood of old traditional houses, the restaurant feels like a hidden retreat.

At Gion Hanamai, Japanese cuisine is prepared with carefully selected ingredients, with an emphasis on seasonal flavors. Each dish is crafted with precision to highlight the essence of the seasonal ingredients. In addition to the cuisine, a curated selection of Japanese sake and wines are served in vessels chosen to complement each drink, delighting many gourmet enthusiasts.

With only six seats at the counter, the space exudes a traditional Japanese atmosphere, with a Yoshino cypress counter and a ceiling woven in a traditional Ajiro (wicker) pattern.  Reservations are limited to one group per day, ensuring a quiet and luxurious experience. Inside, guests can forget the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy a peaceful, private Japanese setting. In the historic city of Kyoto, the restaurant emphasizes the fundamentals of classic Kyoto cuisine while showcasing ingredients and craftsmanship. The dining experience is further enhanced by the attentive service characteristic of Japanese hospitality.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from Keihan Main Line Gion-Shijo Station

245105.longDescription:
Shijo Kawaramachi, the center of Kyoto and one of the most popular destinations for history-seeking visitors, is home to Good Nature Station. This new complex, near the Shijo Kawaramachi Crossing and a two-minute walk from the station of the same name, houses a hotel on the upper floors, a market and cafes on the first floor, and restaurants on the second floor. Among these restaurants on the second floor is TAKAYAMA.

Seated at a wide semi-circular counter, diners can enjoy watching the chef and other cooks working in the open kitchen, which adds a theatrical element to an experience here.

This dramatic restaurant is helmed by chef Tadashi Takayama, who trained in Italy for six years before returning to Japan to open TAKAYAMA, his own restaurant, in December 2019. The restaurant was quickly awarded a one-star rating within a year.

TAKAYAMA offers a 20-course Italian tasting menu full of creativity, allowing diners to relax for a few hours while enjoying a variety of sublime dishes. For example, a first course has a 2D barcodes imprinted on top of chocolate that offers a glimpse at the menu ahead. The second course is served in a small box which, when opened, captivates the eyes with the beautiful dish within.

Vegetables are sourced from Kyonoen Yoshida in Keihoku and the morning market in Kyoto Ohara. In addition, bone-in parous beef matured by President Yoshinobu Niiho of Sakaeya, a renowned butcher’s shop in Kusatsu, Shiga, is cooked slowly over charcoal.
The drink menu mainly focuses on wines from Italy, France, and other European bottles, but also includes several kinds of Japanese wines and sake. There is also a choice of two pairings, with either four or eight glasses depending on the guest’s preference.

The minimal all-white interior, furnished only with a 12-seat counter, highlights the beauty of dishes made by chef Takayama with colorful flowers and herbs as well as the liveliness of guests, making the restaurant perfect for gourmet gatherings, dates, and anniversaries. Children are welcome at the restaurant if booked for exclusive use. Non-Japanese speaking guests are also welcomed by chef Takayama and the sommelier, who are both fluent in English and Italian. Guests are kindly advised to contact the restaurant in advance if special accommodations are required.

The concept of TAKAYAMA, “comfort and inspiration lead to happiness,” reflects the desire to entertain guests at the restaurant. The friendly hospitality of chef Takayama is surely one of the attractions of this restaurant.
Guests are invited to enjoy a one-of-a-kind creative experience within the extraordinary world of TAKAYAMA at the center of Kyoto.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 3-minutes walk from Kawaramachi Station on the Hankyu Kyoto Main Line

243870.longDescription:
""Reine des prés"" is a world gourmet guide award French restaurant located near the Kyoto Imperial Palace and only a 3-minute walk from Jingu-Marutamachi Station in Kyoto. Meadowsweet objets d'art can be enjoyed in its stylish interior that has been created with a theme of wood and stones.

The owner chef Mr. Nakahara, received training at restaurants such as ""Arpege"", a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Paris, France. His cooking concept is ""ingredients × heating × simplicity"". Chef Nakahara visits food-producing regions himself to carefully select all the ingredients. Low temperature heating brings out the best of the ingredients, and dishes created in this manner are simple and avoid unnecessary wastage. Surprisingly, just changing the heating process of ingredients creates a different texture and flavor.

Reservations for both the chef's selected lunch and dinner can be made through Pocket Concierge. Enjoy creative dishes that defy the boundaries of French cuisine and that are a great pairing with wine.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

245260.longDescription:
A 2-minute walk from Shijo Station on the Karasuma Line of Kyoto Municipal Subway takes you to Kii, which is located in a narrow alley a few steps away from Bukkoji Street at the center of the historical city of Kyoto. Visitors are welcomed by a wooden signboard bearing the restaurant’s name at the entrance, while the elegant appearance of the hole-in-the-wall restaurant converted from a traditional Japanese house heightens expectations for the world inside.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Teppei Nishiyama, who set his heart on Italy and went to the country to study Italian cuisine. He trained at some of the most renowned restaurants in Italy, including Da Vittorio, a three-star restaurant in Bergamo, and worked at Mugaritz in Basque, Spain, immediately before returning to Japan to open his own restaurant, Semplice, in Chushojima, Fushimi, Kyoto, in 2013. The restaurant was relocated to the current location and renamed Kii in 2019.
Chef Nishiyama’s dishes are grounded in Italian tradition but characterized by bringing out the best in their ingredients in such an innovative way that they can be called “Nishiyama cuisine.” All the ingredients, including vegetables and seafood, are sourced from dedicated vendors with whom the chef has long-lasting ties in order to ensure that only the highest-quality ingredients are delivered. They are cooked in a simple way to enhance their natural flavors. The meat is also carefully selected, including Nanatani duck from Kameoka, Kyoto. Meanwhile, the pasta is handmade every morning and cut into spaghetti. The menu changes from month to month, and the fish menu varies every day depending on the catch and weather conditions because Chef Nishiyama desires to please the taste buds of guests as much as possible.
The wine list includes almost 100 labels of wines, all from Italy except for Champagne. They are also served by the glass. Moreover, food and wine pairings are offered upon request, according to the tastes and desires of each guest, and served in quantities requested by guests or in accordance with their physical condition. Meanwhile, the sake list offers some 10 labels of Japanese sake, which vary depending on the season but all go well with the dishes.

The interior is simple with warm wood accents and furnished with a six-seat counter. The thick countertop is made of soft fir wood grown in Japan.
The restaurant’s name, Kii, means calm, happiness, and gentle pleasure and comes from a book by High Priest Kobo Daishi (Kukai). Staying true to the restaurant’s name, Chef Nishiyama talks to guests over the counter and takes care to ensure they have a pleasant, relaxing time at the restaurant. Seeing his guests leave the restaurant satisfied and happy is what he desires most.
Please enjoy the great dishes and warm service with your food buddies. It will surely be the most relaxing experience you have ever had.
nearestStations: A 1-minute walk from Exit 6 of Shijo Subway Station

243855.longDescription:
Established during the Edo period, this restaurant is a Kyoto fixture with a history of over 250 years, standing strong in its location near Fushimi-Momoyama Station and Momoyama Goryo-mae Station at Kyoto. 

Fushimi is known as a place for sake, and the restaurant uses the local, high-quality natural well water. As for ingredients, they use fresh fish delivered directly every morning from the wholesale market and Akashi, as well as Kyoto vegetables, which guests can enjoy the combination of Kyoto-style Kaiseki course and local Fushimi sake.

When you step through the entrance, which bears the marks of a history dating back to the late Edo period, you will find rooms large and small with a sense of freshness, looking out on the courtyard. The private rooms are fully equipped with sunken kotatsu tables and tatami mats, and are available for events and group meals. This long-standing, traditional Japanese restaurant in Fushimi, Kyoto is a great one to visit on a festive day or special family occasion, as well.

245516.longDescription: Adjacent to Maruyama Park in the atmospheric neighborhood of Higashiyama, Kyoto, Chourakukan is a historic hotel registered as a National Important Cultural Property. Originally built as a guesthouse in the Meiji era (early 20th century) to welcome distinguished guests from around Japan and beyond, the celebrated establishment has now continued to delight guests with exquisite French cuisine at its neo-classic style dining venue, LE CHENE. Since opening its doors in 2008, the restaurant offers creative French cuisine infused with the essence of Kyoto in a luxurious setting reminiscent of the rich heritage of the historic architecture. LE CHENE is helmed by Chef Kazuki Hashimoto. He first trained at french restaurant will in Kyoto and moved to RESTAURANT VITRA NAGOYA in Nagoya in 2008. He also apprenticed under former Executive Chef Hidetoshi Ushimaru from The Westin Tokyo. He joined LE CHENE as Sous Chef in 2010 and got promoted to Executive Chef at the age of 31 in 2013. Since then, he has organized gastronomic events every year to express his gratitude to producers. In 2024, he also held a collaboration dinner with Soujiki Nakahigashi, a two-star restaurant, in Kyoto. Chef Hashimoto starts his morning by driving a three-hour round trip to source fresh vegetables from Ohara and Shizuhara on the northern outskirts of Kyoto. The restaurant’s menu is planned depending on the ingredients delivered each day. The seafood menu featuring fish directly sourced from Maizuru fishing port in Kyoto is always blank. Even the fish course is kept unknown to guests until it arrives at the table. Following the fish course, the entrée is presented in a sophisticated manner that lives up to the high expectations set for the historic dining venue that has served privileged guests for years. For example notable dish is Beurre Noisette Snacké. Served as a hot appetizer, this specialty dish featuring seasonal fish sautéed in brown butter wows the palate of guests with its delightful crispy texture. Nanatani duck, locally raised in Kyoto, dry aged for two weeks, and prepared with ingredients of the day, also enjoys great popularity. The wine cellar of LE CHENE boasts 120 varieties of wine, from casual to grand labels, which mainly come from France, including Champagne, Bordeaux, and Burgundy. The restaurant also offers a wine pairing menu that includes not only wine but also sake options. If you are not sure which drink to choose, ask Sommelier Takumi Suzuki, who also serves as the restaurant’s General Manager. One of the popular choices is a tea paring, for this French restaurant proudly offers a Japanese tea menu (including gyokuro, sencha, and hojicha) worthy of its location in the famous tea producing region of Kyoto. In 2025, Chourakukan became a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, an international collection of independent luxury hotels represented in over 90 countries. It was recognized for its one-of-a-kind space that preserves the architectural details from its founding—an eclectic blend of global design styles—as well as its serene, six-room-only accommodation, attentive hospitality, and a dining experience that harmoniously fuses the traditions of French cuisine with the natural richness of Kyoto. At LE CHENE, guests can enjoy their meals in an elegant setting adorned with French Baccarat chandeliers and plastered walls, either in the main dining space (with 6 tables seating up to a total of 12 guests) or private dining rooms (seating up to 2 to 10 guests). Indulge in the exquisite French cuisine and excellent service, as well as occasional live piano performances, at the historic guesthouse of Kyoto. *Live piano performances are only occasional. 244287.longDescription:
Japanese cuisine restaurant Mizai is located in a quiet corner of Kyoto’s famous Maruyama Park. With award from world gourmet guide, Mizai is well-known to be a place where gourmands from all over the country dream to visit at least once.
 
Owner Hitoshi Ishihara began to journey on the road to cooking at age the age of 15. He entered Osaka Koraibashi Kitcho Honten and studied under Kitcho founder Teiichi Yuki. Ishihara has climbed the ornate staircase to the top, being appointed as Head Chef at Kyoto Kitcho Honten at the young age of 24 and rising to the position of General Head Chef at age 38. 

After he upholded the taste of the famous restaurant for 31 years, he became independent in June 2003. Having inherited the spirit of his prominent tea ceremony master, Ishihara aims to have the heart of “Ichiza Konryu”, which has been treasured in the world of tea ceremony. It is a word that expresses the preparation and hospitality that is put into a single tea ceremony in order to create a sense of unity with guests. At Mizai, the five senses are stimulated not only by the food, but by everything from the wares, the decorated food, flowers and decor of the restaurant, and the scenery of the park towards the restaurant. The four seasons are being expressed in everything. Following the manners of tea kaiseki, a wooden tray with rice, soup, and a side dish is first served, and it is said that over 300 types of carefully selected seasonal ingredients are used daily.
 
The interior of the restaurant has a modern finish of a tea ceremony arbor design, with 14 counter seats and private rooms that can take up to 6 guests. In order to provide the best hospitality, guests are received once a day, all together at 18:00. The restaurant name Mizai means “no limits” in the Zen language, and is a word that Ishihara has carved into his heart as his maxim. Guests are sure to be impressed and touched by Ishihara’s continual desire to aim higher, even as reservations from all over the country flood the restaurant.

* Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Keihin Main Line Gion-Shijo Station Exit 3

243897.longDescription:
Located a short distance from Kyoto's Oike Street, a quiet restaurant with a white curtain is "Ichiko Soden Nakamura". Once you pass through the noren, the atmosphere changes from the bustle outside, and you step on the stone pavement with sprinkled water to the entrance.
The restaurant was established in the early 19th century during the Bunka-Bunsei period (1818-1830), when fresh fish, mackerel, and other seafood from Wakasa Bay were brought to Kyoto via the "Saba Kaido" (mackerel road) and served to court nobles and other court officials. The current owner is the sixth generation, Tomokazu Nakamura. After graduating from university, he studied nutritional science in the master's program at Kyoto University in pursuit of culinary delicacies.
His cuisine focuses on enhancing the taste, color, and aroma of the ingredients, and his "White Miso Zoni," which is prepared without using soup stock or seasonings, and "Guji no Sakeyaki," which is grilled with a layer of sake, are dishes that can only be tasted here.
Along with the meal, we would like you to taste "Soukou" made by Haneda Sake Brewery in Kitayama, Kyoto. The best sake is brewed in a special barrel for "Ichiko Soden Nakamura".
The interior of the restaurant, where you can enjoy your meal and sake, is a purely Japanese building with tatami rooms, horigotatsu (table with a hole in the middle), and tables. We hope you will enjoy not only the food but also the space with those you share it with.

* Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.

245062.longDescription:
A 3-minute walk from Gion Shijo station, in the beating heart of Kyoto, brings guests to Tokiyo, a long-standing restaurant beloved for its home cooking on a narrow street lined with restaurants and pubs. 

The restaurant was opened back in 1985, during the Showa period, by the mother of the owner, Ken Inoue, and now attracts not only local food lovers but also tourists and visitors from abroad. Inoue started his culinary career at the age of 23; after honing his skills at a Japanese restaurant in Kyoto for four years, he made his way back to Tokiyo, where he offers comforting home dishes together with his mother.

At Tokiyo, 10-12 varieties of homestyle dishes featuring seasonal ingredients are available for diners at any time. The daily-changing menu is dependent on the ingredients available, and it’s easy to enjoy new dishes with repeat visits. On-the-spot ordering is quick and easy. “‘Thank you, it was delicious. I enjoyed the meal very much.’ These words are all we need,” the owner says. “Our daily efforts are about offering dishes that live up to these praises.” As indicated by his words, Tokiyo offers familiar, comforting dishes and a warm, homely atmosphere.

The restaurant’s ingredients are sourced from reliable vegetable and butcher shops that the owner visits himself. Popular dishes include a dish of simmered herring and eggplant, and vegetables simmered with beancurd lees. The subtle and well-balanced flavors unique to Kyoto cuisine delight and satisfy and are often described as something only available at Tokiyo.

The drinks menu offers a superb selection of 30 types of locally brewed sake, mainly from Kyoto but also from around Japan. Pairings of food and sake selected by the owner are available, who is committed to offering only sake in which he has full confidence.

The restaurant’s interior is bright and comfortable with warm wood accents that add to the homely feel. In addition to a private room with a low horigotatsu table (seating up to 12 guests), there are 10 counter seats and 8 table seats. Dishes are served on ceramics selected from a ceramic shop where the owner’s father used to work.

Discover delicious food with family, friends, colleagues, business clients, or in the pleasure of one’s own company at Tokiyo.

245074.longDescription:
In a quiet residential area in Higashiyama, Kyoto, surrounded by the iconic Kiyomizudera Temple, Kyoto National Museum, and Sanjusangendo Temple, Higashiyama Yoshihisa was opened by chef Yoshihisa Suzuki in 2018. Since opening, the restaurant has gained popularity, quickly being awarded one star in the world’s leading restaurant guide which it has retained since 2019. 

Higashiyama Yoshihisa has received acclaim for its inventive and exquisite multi-course menus, which change monthly. The restaurant offers creative prix-fixe menus that combine a breathtaking array of cooking techniques and ingredients based on the themes inspired by nature and local terroir, such as “Nagasaki Prefecture,” “sushi x freshness,” “Niigata Prefecture x Shiga Prefecture,” “bamboo shoots x Chinese cuisine,” “Asiatic black bears x wild boars from Tamba Sasayama,” and “meat x mushrooms.” In addition, chef Suzuki, keen to entertain his guests, fills the restaurant with laughter and builds a special bond among guests with engaging conversation while showing his skillful cooking techniques in front of diners at the counter. Each tasting menu uses various ingredients carefully selected by the chef himself or discerning buyers, depending on the theme of the month. In contrast, the chef’s specialties, an assortment of smoked cheeses paired to an original highball, remain the same every month.

The drink menu also changes, depending on the theme of the month, sometimes offering Japanese sake and at other times wines and Shaoxing wines. The chef also suggests food and drink pairings to allow diners to enjoy a marriage of creative dishes matched to rare libations, some of which are so precious that they will impress even the most demanding connoisseurs.

A sophisticated interior blends Japanese and Western influences and allows the cuisine to shine. In addition, foot heaters are installed to protect diners from the cold weather of winter in Kyoto. Both the eight-seat counter in the main dining area and the six-seat table in the private room are set with carefully selected dishware, including Edo-kiriko cut glasses and vintage Baccarat glasses. 

Guests are invited to experience unique, creative dishes prepared by a multitalented chef, as well as an engaging cooking performance at Higashiyama Yoshihisa, perfect for any occasion, such as dining with a partner, entertaining business clients, dining with family, or enjoying one’s own company.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

245515.longDescription:
About seven minutes’ drive from Kyoto Station, Sushi Ginza Onodera at Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto is located on the third floor of Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto, a luxury retreat in the Higashiyama district, dotted with temples and shrines that provide stunning views of the surrounding areas.   Headquartered in Ginza, the renowned restaurant brand brings its authentic Edomae sushi to the historical and gastronomic city of Kyoto.

The kitchen is helmed by Executive Chef Takuya Kubota, who hails from Aomori Prefecture, known for Oma tuna fishing. Raised with fresh seafood from the surrounding waters of the Tsugaru Strait, the Japan Sea, and the Pacific Ocean, he joined Sushi Ginza Onodera in 2018 and worked at overseas locations for years. When serving as Executive Chef at Sushi Ginza Onodera New York, he earned stars from a world-renowned restaurant guide for five consecutive years.  Then, he returned to Japan and worked at Sushi Ginza Onodera Main Location before being appointed as Executive Chef of Sushi Ginza Onodera at Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto, where he combines Edomae culinary techniques with the flavors of Kyoto to delight the taste buds of guests. 

The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu starts with seasonal delicacies, such as sashimi and grilled and simmered delights, followed by about 10 pieces of nigiri sushi. The sushi rice is made from Hitomebore, a brand rice from Akita Prefecture, which is cooked a little hard and seasoned with a blend of red and rice vinegar to add a zesty kick. The first sushi is always whitefish. It is followed by a series of exquisite sushi pieces, such as gizzard shad and baby snapper. In particular, bluefin tuna, known as the star ingredient of Edomae sushi, is a must-try specialty of Sushi Ginza Onodera. The premium tuna delivered by Yamayuki, a popular wholesaler known for making a joint bid with the Onodera Group in the first tuna auction of the year at Toyosu Market, tantalizes the taste buds of sushi connoisseurs. The last course is Matcha Blanc-manger – the signature dessert of the restaurant that perfectly balances the grassy notes of matcha with the natural sweetness of coconut. 

Sushi Ginza Onodera at Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto exclusively offers Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto Cuvée Junmai Daiginjo, brewed from 100% organic Asahi sake rice by Takeno Sake Brewing in Kyotango City to create a slightly sweet, round flavor. The drink menu also features a fine selection of sake from around Japan, such as Kokuryu from Fukui and Katsuyama Akatsuki from Miyagi. The 400-year-old solid hinoki wood counter (seating up to 10 guests) and the view of the renowned Sekisuien garden from the windows make the restaurant a comfortable space that makes you feel like you are in nature, while traditional tableware, such as Bizen ware from Okayama and Shimizu ware from Kyoto, adds a touch of warmth.  There are also 2 private dining rooms (seating up to 4 and 6 guests, respectively) for relaxed meals and conversation, making the restaurant versatile for various occasions, from private to business. Please enjoy seasonal flavors in the traditional Japanese setting of Sushi Ginza Onodera at Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto.

243985.longDescription: A couple was led and settled at a house in the south of the Imperial Palace, where the Japanese Maple, the restaurant symbol, welcomes you. According to the chef, the challenge is bringing out the best of nature of the 4 changing seasons through seasonal ingredients. Every dish born out of these fresh ingredients are seemingly very simple. The balanced flavors and taste easily flow through the body, while allowing you to enjoy the dish with your eyes as well. 244410.longDescription: About a 5-minute walk from Kyoto’s Karasuma Oike Station is the bustling commercial row known as Sakai-machi Dori. This is where you will find "Muromachi Wakuden," a restaurant built in the same style as one of Kyoto’s traditional “Machiya” townhouses. The entrance is wide and expansive, which is a rare sight in the city of Kyoto. The interior is decorated with a painting by Seiji Togo, and there is also a gorgeous courtyard that you can only find in a traditional style building like this one. The restaurant’s ambiance goes a long way to let guests feel completely at ease. Mr. Shinya Matsumoto, who serves as the head chef, highlights each season with delicate flavors that brim with a rustic sense of beauty. Seasonal specialties are prepared throughout the year to give a vivid sense of Japan’s four distinct seasons. This includes well-known seasonal favorites such as Japanese pepper blossom with Wagyu beef shabu-shabu in the spring, sweetfish during the summer, dagger-tooth pike conger eel wrapped in matsutake mushrooms for autumn, and crabs for winter. Situated off in the area known as “Kyoto Tango,” Wakuden has its own private farm used to grow wholly organic rice that is carefully selected to make sake. The restaurant uses a type of rice called “Ise Hikari,” which also serves as special ceremonial rice at Ise Grand Shrine. The Wakuden restaurant group contracts vegetable plots to grow their own ingredients as well. Their impressive counter space is built with wood from Japanese chestnut trees, and guests sitting there can catch an awesome display of seasonal ingredients prepared right before their eyes. This adds a fun first-hand sensibility to the dining experience, and it makes for a perfect setting to enjoy traditional Japanese style cooking. They offer a versatile range of seating options, including 2 wide and spacious counters (15 seats and 7 seats respectively), as well as 4 different large-sized private dining rooms (8 to 20 guests). They also have private rooms that are perfect for families that want to bring their children along, and they even prepare a special selection of dishes for small children to enjoy. Furthermore, the restaurant is close to Kyoto’s business district, which makes it a common spot for co-workers looking for somewhere to dine out. The seasonally inspired menu here offers delicate Kyoto-style cuisine prepared with a vivid selection of ingredients that sure leave a memorable impression on each guest. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023. *Private room can be used. For details, please send your request from inquiry form HERE.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Karasuma Oike Station Exit 3-1(Kyoto Municipal Subway Karasuma Line)

245109.longDescription:
A 5-minute walk from Kyoto Station brings guests to Kyoto Ito. This one-star Japanese restaurant, secluded on the opposite side of the moat of Higashi Honganji Temple, offers creative, one-of-a-kind dishes prepared by chef Shohei Noguchi,

Chef Noguchi trained at a two-star French restaurant in Osaka for seven years; he have created a one-of-a-kind Japanese cuisine inspired by French classics and made his restaurant a popular gourmet destination.

“This restaurant is a place where different genres of cuisines, such as Japanese, European, and Chinese, meet and combine,” says Noguchi. “I also want to make it a place where food meets tableware crafted by artists and where people who pursue a career in cooking can meet and enjoy learning from one another. The word “Ito” in the restaurant name is intentionally spelled in hiragana to represent multiple meanings, such as a string that ties things together, intention, and affection.”

Ingredients, especially vegetables, are carefully selected and directly sourced from farmers in Hokkaido, as well as Nagasawa Noen and other long-acquainted farmers in Kyoto, to offer sublime vegetable dishes. The chef’s specialties include a richly flavored duck rice topped with Kujo scallions, yolk, and black truffles and consommé with locally raised chicken. Bonito flakes are not only used to produce a stock, but also blended with vegetables and used as a seasoning. Thus, a harmonious blend of Japanese and European ingredients and techniques can be found at Kyoto Ito.

The restaurant also offers a wide selection of drinks, including renowned Japanese sake, such as Juyondai from Yamagata, Hakkaisan from Niigata, and Isojiman from Shizuoka, which was offered to world leaders at the Hokkaido Toyako Summit, as well as premium Japanese whiskies, such as 17-year-old Hibiki and 12-year-old Yamazaki, plus rare wines from a small winery in Hokkaido.

Inside the restaurant, there are two private rooms seating up to four guests each on the second floor, and an eight-seat counter on the first floor. Tables are graced with elaborate dishware, ranging from antique china to ceramics crafted by young artists.

Guests are invited to enjoy one-of-a-kind dishes in an extraordinary setting at Kyoto Ito, to create memories and connections with family, a partner, friends, or colleagues.

244753.longDescription:
In Kyoto City, 5 minutes walk from Keage Station on the Tozai Subway Line, located in a quiet residential area just one block from Nanzen-ji Temple on Niomon-dori, is the 3-star restaurant “Hyotei (in the main building)”. If you continue walking about 20 meters past the stately gate you will come to the “Hyotei Annex”.

Hyotei started about 450 years ago as a tea house in the precincts of Nanzen-ji Temple. In 1837, it opened its doors as a Japanese restaurant and became famous as a restaurant that serves Kaiseki cuisine, with its specialties being "Hyotei egg" as well as the seasonal "Morning porridge". “Hyotei Annex” opened in 1972, next to the main building. Hyotei is a long-established Japanese restaurant, and at the Annex, guests can enjoy a unique menu that values the tastes and traditions of Kyoto cuisine. 

The main dish for lunch is the "Shokado bento box". It is offered daily from noon to 4 PM, except on Thursdays. The Shokado bento comes with soup, rice and pickles as well as the famous "Hyotei egg" and grilled dishes made with seasonal ingredients such as takiawase. The ingredients are almost the same as Kaiseki cuisine. The "Morning porridge" is available from March 16th to November 30th and you can order the "Uzura (Quail) porridge" from December 1st until March 15th. Please be aware that the regular holidays and hours of service are different from the Hyotei in the main building.

The dining room has table seats and you can enjoy the distinctive tastes of Kyoto while looking at the elegant garden at this well-established restaurant with family, friends, and colleagues, dates, and guests who are visiting Kyoto from overseas. You can also enjoy the “wabi-sabi” (acceptance of transience and imperfection) culture of Kyoto here.

243932.longDescription: Hyotei's history is long and could track back about four hundred years ago. It is said to have started as a tea ceremony house at Nanzen-ji temple. Since its founding, Hyotei has a thatched roof tea room referred to as ""kuzuya"" greeting guests even to today. Found here are witty epigrams by Aritomo Yamagata and Yajiro Shinagawa, figures active during the Meiji Restoration. There are tea jars at the entrance that also date back. These and other decorations are rich remnants of the restaurant's history. The subtle hospitality and harmony of seasonal cuisine have continued to enchant persons of culture, tea masters, financiers, Kyoto gentlemen, and many more. As represent of Hyotei, “Hyotei Tamago(Egg)” and “Asagayu(Rice Gruel for Breakfast)” are loved by visitors coming all over the world. Not too much, but never too less, the hospitality, dishes and preparations filled with love of four seasons, always supporting, and loved by different peoples in this city. Beyond the reputation of world gourmet guide award, it is the representation of traditional restaurant of Kyoto even Japan. Private rooms, semi-private rooms, Horigotaatsu(low table over a hole in the floor), table seats, and Ozashiki(tatami room) are available for 2 to 28 person to freely enjoy. Also, the garden which showing the changing of for season may also in your sight. Family dinner is also welcome for children elder than 12. For visitors inside or outside Japan, if you would like to enjoy a freely time, please try our restaurant. * Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024. *Please note that Hyotei only accept breakfast reservation through hotel's concierge, you may contact your accommodation for details. 【Access】 ■10 minutes on foot from Kyoto Municipal Subway Tozai Line ""Kegami Station"" Exit 2 ■ About 20 minutes drive from JR Kyoto Station 【Nearby Hotels】 ■ Kyoto Station ""Hotel Granvia Kyoto"" ■ Nijo Ohashi ""The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto"" ■ Shijo Kawaramachi ""Kyoto Hotel Okura"" ■ Shijo Kawaramachi ""Hotel Nikko Princess Kyoto"" ■ Shijo Karasuma ""Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Shinmachi Bettei"" ■ Kyoto Imperial Palace ""Kyoto Brighton Hotel"" ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 2 to 28 people. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? We offer table(s) and chairs (Western style), Ozashiki style (a low table where you sit on a flat Tatami or hardwood floor), and the Horigotatsu style (a low table over a recessed floor where you can sit in the same way you would sit in a western style chair). Please be informed that the seating style is based on availability and it cannot be reserved in advance. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. A vegetarian option may be prepared. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, we do not have staff that speaks English. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available.

   彼がとても喜んでくれたことが、本当に嬉しいです。彼は、お庭の景観が美しいと、お料理が美味しいと喜びました。彼の自分の両親に瓢亭様での夕食をプレゼントしたいと言っています。
   また、今回一時間早く着いてしまいました。それなのに、中に入れて下さり、早速お食事をお出しいただいたことも忘れられません。生姜ご飯のお土産も頂き本当に嬉しいです。
ありがとうございます☺️是非、またお食事させて頂きたいです。
季節の素晴らしい素材を見事に生かしたとても美味しい料理でした。サービスも気が利いていて、気分も良く食事が出来ました。
すばらしい料理と出会いがありました。心から感激しました。一つ一つに心がこもっているばかりか、素材の本来以上のおいしさを最大限引き出していることに、驚きがありました。この特別な料理を作り出し、提供している瓢亭の皆様に心から感謝申し上げます。
Great location, atmosphere and food experience

Incredible experience dining at Hyotei! Best Kaiseki meal in Kyoto! Every course was perfectly prepared! The staff were courteous. The pace of serving each course was nicely timed with the entire meal completed in 2 hours. The environment was great as we sat in a cottage of a few hundreds years of age with a view of a koi pond.
Excellent food and staff. Service was amazing and the ambience was perfect. The private room was much appreciated.

食事の内容から接客サービス、店の外観、内装まですべて
満喫しました。

サービス面で多少問題が有りましたが、すぐにフォロー・改善の連絡をいただき流石と感心いたしました。

Superb environment, impeccable services and every course is delicious. Many thanks!

日本人ですが京都を仕事以外の旅行で訪れたのは数十年ぶりでした。私は関東の人間で、多少緊張してお店に伺いました。京料理の真髄と言える会席料理、お店の佇まい、担当して頂いたスタッフの方のホスプタリティーいずれも最高でした。東京ではこのようなお店はないと思います。
 素晴らしいひと時でした。
また、是非行ってみたいお店です。

お料理はどれも美味しく感激しました。
お部屋も趣きがあり、初めての経験をさせていただきました。
パートナーも大変喜んでいて、是非また行きたいと思います。
ありがとうございました。
２度目の訪問でしたが、初回と変わらぬ素晴らしい体験ができました。季節に一度は訪れたいところですが、それは難しいでしょう。この度、東京の日比谷ミッドタウンに出店するとか。そちらも楽しみです。

存在感のあるお料理、味、素晴らしい器、女将さんと担当の方のおもてなし、すべて満足のいくものでした。
また、約２００年前の茶室に案内されましたが、とても風情があり水の流れる音を聞きながらの食事は心落ち着くものでした。ふっと時代を遡ったような。
また機会がありましたら伺いたいと思います。
一つ一つのお料理が、決して豪華ではありませんが、地域の食材を季節とともに丁寧に提供していただき、大変美味しくいただきました。接客も丁寧で、大変  良かったです。機会があれば再訪したいです。

食事は素朴で洗練されていてとても癒されました。
それ以上にプライベートな空間がとても心地良かったです。
ありがとうございました。
京料理の真髄を見た気がしました。一品一品大変満足しました。

245138.longDescription: Wagokoro Izumi is a two-star Japanese restaurant located in the downtown area of Kyoto near Shijo Subway Station, run by chef Masaki Izumi, who has inherited the spirit of his master, to offer dishes filled with the Japanese spirit of Wa in a place tied to the past. Born in Mie, Izumi trained first at the Japanese restaurant Kase in Nagoya and then at a hotel in Tokyo. After that, he worked at the renowned restaurant Sakurada in Kyoto, where he learned the techniques and spirit of Kyoto’s exquisite cuisine, and then opened his own restaurant in 2006. Later, in 2016, he opened Wagokoro Izumi at the site of Sakurada, which had been closed while being missed by fans. The reputation of his Japanese culinary skills spread by word of mouth, allowing Wagokoro Izumi to quickly expand its clientele and win two stars. His dishes are ordinary but filled with the Japanese spirit of Wa (wagokoro) and packed with seasonal flavors that excite the senses. “I have inherited the spirit of my master, so I will never cut corners,” he says. He visits and consults with producers to purchase ingredients that pair harmoniously together and meet his standards. Needless to say, particular attention is paid to the stock as it is the key to delicious meals – at Wagokoro Izumi it is made with Rishiri kelp purchased exclusively from Kabuka and Funadomari in Rebun Island and precious fermented dried bonito sourced from a producer in Makurazaki that the chef visits to observe the production process. He explains this process to diners while demonstrating how to extract the rich umami flavor of the bonito attributed to that elaborate process in his dishes. The restaurant’s signature dish is Egg Castilla, which is served on a traditional wooden platter with 24-cm sides, the egg and ground fish meat slowly cooked over low heat. The chef also proudly shows off a plate of Sweetfish Grilled with Salt, noting that it “tastes totally different from the one offered by other restaurants.” Grilled using a unique and secret method of his own invention (grilled on upright skewers like it is grilled on a hearth), the fish is so delicious as to be irresistible to the restaurant’s regulars. A sublime selection of Japanese sake is able to meet almost any request. In particular, the original Japanese sake brewed every season by Joyo Shuzo in Kyoto pairs extremely well with the aforementioned sweetfish. The Kyomachiya townhouse-style exterior offers atmosphere, while the dining room offers a serene counter; meanwhile, the Japanese-style private rooms, either with a dining table or a low horigotatsu table (table over a hole in the floor), are adorned with hanging scroll paintings, flower arrangements, and tableware crafted by artists, ranging from living national treasures to contemporary artists, to express the Japanese spirit of Wa in a fashion that changes from season to season. Guests are invited to enjoy the essence of Japanese cuisine at Wagokoro Izumi, either for business meetings with clients or intimate meals with family, partner, or friends. * Awarded two stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024. Access Shijo Station on the Karasuma Subway Line and Karasuma Station on the Hankyu Kyoto Line ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■About Allergies We will do our best to accommodate allergies, likes and dislikes — please let us know in advance.(The day before or the day of the event is not available.)However, please note that we cannot accept reservations for vegetarians and vegans. ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 6 people. Our semi-private dining room can be reserved for a party of 4 to 10 people. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes must be removed in the tatami room. Shoes are not required for table seating. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 6 years of age. We are happy to make our course menu half the size of the adult's. Please inquire. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals.

244839.longDescription:
A three-minute walk from JR Nijo Station in Kyoto, in a residential area close to Nijo-jo Castle, is a building with a mural of an early evening moon and a dramatic entryway. This is Nijo Yamagishi, the sister restaurant of 
one-star Tominokoji Yamagishi, established by chef Takahiro Yamagishi.

"I want to make it a homey place where everyone can gather happily," said chef Yamagishi, whose main restaurant, Tominokoji Yamagishi, is one of the most difficult to reserve in Kyoto. Nijo Yamagishi was opened as a nabe-kaiseki restaurant in October 2019 to serve new dishes centered around the soup stock from the main restaurant. The head chef is Yushi Yokoi, who has trained at a famous restaurant in Kyoto.

Ingredients on the menu are mainly Kyoto vegetables, complemented by fresh ingredients from further afield. The first course is a dashi (soup stock) nabe instead of the typical soup. The restaurant is particular about using the well water from the main restaurant because quality water is essential for its broth. The flavors in the hot pot, which is made in front of the guests by the head chef and the proprietress, are seasonal and change monthly — you may have Szechuan pepper in the spring, or mushrooms during the autumn. To finish the meal, diners can choose zosui (porridge) made with the rice served in prior courses. About 10 kinds of unique sakes are available; the proprietress can suggest a great pairing.

The restaurant is all tatami rooms, with semi-private rooms and hori-gotatsu (sunken kotatsu) with floor heating. The dinnerware is high-quality and chef-endorsed. 

The reason why the restaurant has captured the hearts of diners? It’s the complete package — food, hospitality, and a warm space. This is a restaurant where you can enjoy a heartwarming time while enjoying the soup of a one-star restaurant, be for it a business occasion or a gathering with friends and with family.


■Reservations
For reservations, please join the Waiting List.
We will confirm your reservation once there is availability.

243867.longDescription:
""Sushiiwa"" is a frontier as counter-main sushi place in 1960, the year it opened. Being born by the creative idea from the first owner, not be restrained by traditional, this pioneer is conscious of the new concept of Japanese cuisine, thoroughly utilize seasonal ingredients, to present the basic idea of Japanese cuisine as ""To deliver the difference of Japan's four seasons through food"". The chef's selected course is composed of traditional Kyoto vegetables and seasonal fish, a contemporary cuisine that with a variety of styles to form a well balance. The restaurant became more famous since Steve Jobs visited in 2010.

The head chef, Toshiya Onishi, who had been trained in the world gourmet guide awarded restaurant ""Japanese Cuisine Kitcho"" in Osaka, with holding a qualification of sommelier, chef shows to the guests the new world of sushi pairing with wine and champagne. In addition, more than 50 brands of Japanese sake and “Shochu(Japanese spirits)” provided.

As a foreign-guest-friendly restaurant, not only is Chef Onishi capable of English, English menu and vegetarian menu are also available. The restaurant may be able to correspond to requests made directly at the restaurant. Kid's menu and private room can be prepared with advance request. A must-try when you visit Kyoto.

245376.longDescription:
Nestled beside the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge, a symbol of the ancient capital of Kyoto, stands the small luxury hotel MUNI KYOTO. Perfectly located just a 4-minute walk from Randen Arashiyama Station and about 10 minutes on foot from JR Saga-Arashiyama Station, the property is also accessible from Hankyu Arashiyama Station across the river. From there, guests can enjoy the approach to the restaurant while crossing the bridge itself. The hotel’s refined, minimalist interiors, designed by Yasuda Design Institute, harmonize beautifully with Kyoto’s natural surroundings.
Among its inviting spaces, Riverside Café Muni offers one of the most breathtaking views. Through its expansive glass windows, guests can gaze out over the Katsura River and Togetsukyo Bridge, while savoring meals in a calm atmosphere away from the bustle outside.

Breakfast is served in a full course style and is open not only to hotel guests but also to visitors. Dishes include homemade juices, freshly baked bread, and roast beef crafted by Japan’s most renowned butcher—an array of plates perfectly suited to the refreshing mornings of Kyoto. With a menu rich in seasonal vegetables and fruits, it delights the eyes as well as the body. After an early morning stroll, enjoying breakfast alongside the quiet flow of the river is truly a special experience. At lunchtime, guests can savor course meals prepared with carefully sourced ingredients from trusted producers. The terrace seating invites you to relax while taking in the seasonal beauty of Arashiyama.

Whether for gatherings with friends and family or a romantic date with someone special, Riverside Café Muni offers an unforgettable experience in a setting infused with Kyoto’s natural charm and aesthetic sensibility. Located in one of Kyoto’s most renowned areas yet open to all, the café welcomes every guest to enjoy its terrace as part of their treasured Kyoto memories.

245047.longDescription:
A 3-minute walk from Arashiyama Station in Kyoto, Steak Otsuka is set in a calmer neighborhood in the north of the station compared to the tourist precincts in the south. Here, chef Yoichi Otsuka offers high-quality, authentic Wagyu beef steaks at accessible prices.

Otsuka previously worked at Ginkakuji Onishi for 10 years, a famous butcher shop in Kyoto, cutting beef for sale while serving as shop manager. Gaining a thorough knowledge of Wagyu beef, he opened Steak Otsuka in 2013 to create opportunities for guests to enjoy high-quality, authentic Wagyu beef. The next year, Steak Otsuka became famous nationwide as it was ranked the most popular restaurant for foreign travelers in Japan by the world’s largest travel review site. Then, after the restaurant moved to its current location in 2019, it became even more popular, and is now known for being perpetually booked.

All beef served at Steak Otsuka is sourced from Ginkakuji Onishi, which supplies the restaurant with only the best cuts of premium beef.
A 150-gram cut of premium beef is grilled on an infrared grill until crisp on the outside and tender on the inside, a method that removes excess fat and concentrates the meat’s flavor. Some rare cuts, such as flat iron, flap, and chuck flap, which are usually served in slices at Japanese BBQ restaurants, are exclusively served as thick steaks at Steak Otsuka.

One of the most popular menus is the restaurant’s Murasawa sirloin. Murasawa beef cattle, especially cows, are legendary for their scarcity -- only 80 heads of the cattle are shipped each year from Murasawa Farm in Nagano. Renowned for its tenderness and tastiness, this beef sells out so quickly that the restaurant is only open for lunch. 

The newly renovated restaurant boasts a sophisticated design, with 10 counter seats and 20 table seats.

Steak Otsuka is perfect for intimate meals with family, a partner, friends, or colleagues and parties for meat connoisseurs. The restaurants invites guests to visit the restaurant to enjoy premium Wagyu beef steak at a reasonable price.

245552.longDescription:
Quietly nestled on Nijo Street, about five minutes’ walk from Karasuma Oike Station in Kyoto, Kyoto Gosho Minami Kushikatsu Bon opened on September 4, 2025—Kushi (Skewer) Day in Japan, a wordplay based on the pronunciation of the numbers 9 (ku) and 4 (shi)—as a branch of Kitashinchi Kushikatsu Bon, a popular restaurant offering kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) featuring premium ingredients. The Kyoto location is run by Manager Seiichi Ito, with almost a decade of experience as manager at Kushikatsu Bon Paris after working at the main location. Drawing on his years of overseas experience, he runs the Kyoto branch with focus on the charm of Japanese history and culture rooted in the traditional city.

Executive Chef Masahiro Saneshige also has a strong presence, working in front of the deep fryer. He honed his culinary skills at specialized restaurants, such as sushi, izakaya, and ramen establishments, before joining Kushikatsu Bon to gain experience in counter service. He was appointed as the Executive Chef of Ginza Kushikatsu Bon when it opened in 2014 and then worked at the Paris location before becoming the Executive Chef of the Kyoto location. Mastering the art of deep-frying, he removes excess oil from deep-fried skewers using centrifugal force created by rapidly spinning the skewers.

The Gosho Minami Bon Prix-Fixe Menu offers 13 kushikatsu courses, along with rice/noodle/bread and dessert courses, featuring Kyoto vegetables and other local ingredients, such as Chawanmushi with Cod Milt (a cup-steamed egg custard hotchpotch topped with a deep-fried cod milt skewer) and Kushikatsu Dish (an assortment of deep-fried skewers, including a Japanese Black Beef skewer, served on a dish with the restaurant’s house-made curry sauce brushed in the shape of the kanji character ‘凡’ (Bon), the name of the restaurant). Among them, the Bluefin Tuna Sushikatsu (a deep-fried ball of sushi rice on the skewer topped with raw bluefin tuna from Yamayuki, a popular wholesaler, at Toyosu Market) and the Wagyu Beef Fillet Kushikatsu have gained wide popularity. Following them is the final savory course, which gives the diner three options to choose from: Udon Noodles made from Yoshino Kuzu from Nara, Salmon Belly Rice Pot, and Bluefin Tuna Cutlet Sandwich. The dessert course also offers unique options that would be only available in kushikatsu restaurants, such as Soy-Glazed Dango Kushikatsu, Ice Cream Kushikatsu, and Ice Cream Wafer Sandwich with French Valrhona Chocolate Ganache Kushikatsu.

The drink menu offers about eight varieties of local sake from all over Japan. The restaurant also has an impeccable wine list, mostly from France but also from California and Italy, curated by the group’s sommelier to go with the deep-fried kushikatsu skewers, and a fine selection of high-end beverages, such as Ujien Bottling Tea “Gotas Gyokuro” from Kyoto and Jasmine Tea. The atmospheric interior of the restaurant, which was renovated from an old private house, features a brick wall behind the cooking range and antique cabinets for a touch of modern Japanese flair. The main dining area on the first floor boasts a U-shaped counter (seating up to 14 guests) crafted from a solid piece of plain castor aralia wood grown in Japan. The second floor has a semi-private dining room with two tables (seating up to four and six guests, respectively) and a spacious special dining room (seating up to eight guests) for versatile dining needs, from private to business occasions. Please enjoy deep-fried kushikatsu skewers with premium seasonal flavors at Kyoto Gosho Minami Kushikatsu Bon.

245443.longDescription:
“middle” has a charm of its own, taking you to the intersection between Japanese and foreign cultures. A six-minute walk from Kitaoji Station on the Kyoto Municipal Subway Karasuma Line, the two-story house restaurant on the bank of the Kamogawa river represents the ideal image of a Kyoto restaurant. Converted from an Italian Consul General’s residence , the restaurant is reminiscent of a warehouse and produces feelings of nostalgia even at first sight. The second floor provides amazing views of the busy Kitaoji Bridge and the calming Kamogawa river.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Yasuhiro Fujio, who moved to the UK to study at the age of 15 and was exposed to French cuisine while studying in Paris. While in France, he trained at Passage 53 in Paris and worked at Mirazur in southern France. He then returned to Japan and continued to hone his culinary skills while working as Sous Chef at Restaurant La Cime in Osaka. In 2016, he made the list of Gold Eggs (finalists) for RED U-35, a culinary competition for young chefs in Japan. He also became the first Japanese chef to win the S.Pellegrino Young Chef competition when he took the top prize at the third edition of the world young chef competition in 2018.

Chef Fujio offers French-inspired, innovative dishes with a delicate balance of Japanese and European flavors. The balance between Japanese and European influences varies depending on factors such as where the guest is from. The food menu mostly consists of typical French dishes but also includes French-looking dishes with Japanese flavors. With a sense of belonging to the whole motherland of Japan, the chef sources ingredients from all over the country, such as game fowl chicken from Hasugamine Farm in Ayabe and butterfish and cutlassfish from Ise and Akashi. He also takes advantage of the restaurant’s location to obtain Kyoto vegetables, such as Kamo eggplant and Shogoin radish. However, all meals end with cheese.

The wine list offers a great selection of French and Italian wines (at a ratio of 8:2), including natural and classic wines, and several wines by the glass to pair with dishes. The restaurant also offers Japanese sake, including IWA created by Richard Geoffroy, the cellar master of Dom Pérignon, as well as non-alcoholic options that will pair well with dishes, such as homemade plum juice and black tea-based kelp tea.

Converted from the Italian Consul General’s residence, the restaurant boasts a Japanese-style interior with European elements, such as Italian plastered walls, to represent the image of Japan in the minds of foreigners. About half of the tableware collection consists of European antiques dating back to the 18th-19th century. The spacious dining room, originally a main reception room, is furnished with a two-person table, a four-person table, and an eight-person table as well as partition walls to create a semi-private atmosphere. In addition, guests can dine on the large terrace on sunny days. Combined, these attributes make the restaurant a perfect place for date nights, anniversary celebrations, and intimate dinners, while Chef Fujio’s dishes alone make a trip to Kyoto worthwhile.
nearestStations: 6 min. walk from Exit 3 of Kitaoji Station on the Subway Karasuma Line

244086.longDescription:
Approximately 15 minutes walk from Demachiyanagi station, Keihan Main Line in Kyoto. On the east side of the forest spreading around Kamomioya Jinja(Shimogamo-Jinja),a UNESCO World Heritage Site, there is a long-established store of Kyoto Cuisine Kaiseki called "Shimogamo Saryo".

Founded in 1856, the chef of this venerable restaurant has served in Shimogamo Shrine for few generations. The Sukiya-zukuri style buildings with tells the story of history. When you pass through the entrance curtain, a refined tea room with exquisite furnishing is there welcoming you. The garden which has been maintained for over hundreds of years makes you feel the beauty that only in Kyoto. Spring, summer, Autumn and Winter, a wonderful location where you can see the elegant Takano River under the eyes of "Shimogamo Saryo". A reliable one in Kyoto that meets the needs in every situation such as travel, sightseeing and date. Both lunch and dinner can be booked from the pocket concierge.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

245287.longDescription:
Located on the edge of the Tadasunomori Forest, which spreads around Kamo Mioya Shrine (affectionately known as Shimogamo Shrine), one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto inscribed in the World Cultural Heritage List, Kyokaiseki Kichisen is an old established Kyoto cuisine restaurant awarded two stars by a world-renowned restaurant guide.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Yoshimi Tanigawa, who started his culinary career at the age of 15. He was exceptionally selected as the chef of an acclaimed Japanese restaurant in Saga Arashiyama at the age of 26. Then, he opened his own restaurant in a hotel in 1983, when he was 31 years old, and relocated it to the current location two years later. The sophisticated dishes crafted by the experienced chef who is still active in the kitchen despite being over 70 attract many food lovers from not only around Japan but all over the world.
Kichisen offers traditional feasts derived from chakaiseki cuisine (tea ceremony dishes). It is reinterpreted by Chef Tanigawa in his own innovative way while paying respect to the traditions of the Kyoto cuisine. Not only the selection of ingredients but also the sequence of courses, starting with a cup of Japanese sake (shared as part of an offering to the gods) followed by a mukozuke (side dish) course of sashimi served with Chinese herbal ingredients and comforting refreshments between courses, such as sushi and stewed dishes, is deliberately designed to tingle all the senses with seasonal delights. The ingredients are carefully selected by the chef with a keen eye, who visits local markets early in the mornings, or directly supplied by producers around Japan.
The drink menu offers a popular selection of wines, including original champagne handcrafted from vine to label by a winery with an over 3,000 sq. meter vineyard in Reims, France, as well as Japanese sake selected by the chef from international prize winners.

Decorated with refined furniture and Japanese-style flower arrangements, the restaurant’s interior has a dignified atmosphere comparable to the authentic vibe of Kyoto. Outfitted with a main dining room with a five-seat counter, three private dining rooms (with an area of 10, 18, and 50 sq. meters, respectively), and a traditional Japanese tea room, Kichisen is the perfect place to enjoy the good, old flavors of Kyoto with your friends, business partners, overseas guests, or loved ones.


* Awarded 2 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.
nearestStations: A 10-minutes walk from Keihan Demachiyanagi Station

244937.longDescription:
A 3-minute walk from Gojo Station in Kyoto takes you to Godan Miyazawa, a kaiseki restaurant set in a tranquil residential area down a narrow street from Karasuma Street. The restaurant is run by Chef Masato Miyazawa, who was captivated by the art of the tea ceremony and the charm of tableware and developed his eye and taste for authenticity while learning Japanese cuisine at Kakiden, a renowned cha-kaiseki restaurant (for meals served in the tea ceremony). In 2007, he opened his own restaurant, Jiki Miyazawa, which soon attracted throngs of people from inside and outside Japan. Then, he opened his second restaurant, Godan Miyazawa, in July 2014.

Chef Miyazawa sticks to the principle of doing what he likes to do. For example, he uses ingredients he likes regardless of brands and common values. The dishes and environment created by the skilled and tasteful chef who learned from the best and who sincerely enjoys entertaining guests are pleasant beyond description. In particular, Chef Miyazawa values personal ties. In fact, most of the ingredients are sourced directly from producers with whom he has forged bonds. For example, Koshihikari rice is delivered from a rice farmer in Shiga. The restaurant’s specialties include “Grilled Sesame Tofu of the Season” reinvented from Grilled Sesame Tofu, a signature menu item of Jiki Miyazawa, by mixing in seasonal ingredients, such as grilled eggplant, corn, and burdock. The rich, creamy flavor of the dish captivates the taste buds of patrons. The sake list offers 17 labels of Japanese sake from around the country. Carefully selected by the chef to his taste, they all go well with the dishes. The soft drink menu also offers a wide selection of homemade cold brew tea, such as Himalayan Tea, Yabukita Tea, and Lemon Oolong Tea made with lemongrass, so that guests who do not want to drink alcohol can enjoy food and drink pairings.

With a wickerwork ceiling and natural wood finishes, the main dining room is adorned with minimal decorations to highlight the simple beauty of the design, like a tea house, and furnished with an eight-seat counter. In addition, there is a private room seating up to five people. Families with children are welcomed into the private room. The collection of tableware is selected by Chef Miyazawa, who had been exposed to a wide variety of authentic tableware that laid the foundation for contemporary tableware. Serving the essence of kaiseki cuisine, Godan Miyazawa is suitable for different occasions, such as entertaining your business clients, having a romantic dinner with your partner, eating out with your family, or welcoming guests from abroad.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023
nearestStations: A 3-minutes walk for the Kyoto City Subway Karasuma Line to Gojo Station  from exit 1

244820.localizedAddress: 416, Shinmachidouri Bukkouji Sagaru Iwatoyamacho 416, Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto-shi, Kyoto
244820.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Shijo Station on the Kyoto Municipal Subway, this well-known Japanese restaurant is located in the center of the tourist city of Kyoto, and has been in business for over 80 years. Passing through the noren and through the long stone-paved path sprinkled with water, you will be filled with clean air. Kinobu was opened in 1935 through the good will of ryori-ryokan called Kifuji, a purveyor to the Imperial Palace. The current owner Takuji Takahashi took over the third generation of Kinobu after studying at Tokyo Kitcho for five years.

Chef Takahashi goes to the market every morning to buy seafood. Rice, citrus fruits, spring vegetables and wild grasses are from Aomori and Nagano. Many good ingredients are directly traded with producers across the country.

Shark fin and sesame tofu hot pot is the signature of chef Takahashi. The soft texture of the homemade sesame is similar to shirako and matches the exquisite shark fin. The soup is made with Japanese soup stock, chicken bone and Kinka ham for a rich flavor. It is served throughout the year, and you should definitely try it.

Chef Takahashi, who is also a senior sommelier, is working on new ways of cooking while learning about traditional Japanese cuisine. Here, the world of Japanese cuisine is expanding, seen through the marriage of wine and Japanese cuisine. There are 40 types of wine and about 20 types of sake from all over the country, from Tohoku to Kyushu.

There are only private rooms, including 13 rooms for four or more people. The Komuten (construction firm) that built the Kyoto State Guest House made the entrance. You can relax in the horigotatsu style room, and since English service is available, this restaurant is recommended for foreign guests.

Even if it is your first visit, you can consult in advance according to your request and budget, and in subsequent visits, the restaurant can arrange the next menu based on your past visits. The attraction of Kinobu is that it responds to each guest's requests. By all means, please enjoy the taste and the essence of hospitality unique to Kyoto.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 6-minute walk from Shijo Station (Kyoto City Subway Karasuma Line)

244724.longDescription:
Located 5-minutes walk from Kyoto Subway Gojo Station, “SEN” is a one-star Japanese restaurant, on a quiet street a short distance away from the busy city. Owner Takeshi Sugisawa welcomes you when you pass through the restaurant's entrance curtain.

After training at Tokyo's 2-star “Akasaka Kikunoi” and Kyoto's 1-star “Muromachi Wakuden”, owner Sugisawa served as manager and head chef at a Japanese restaurant in Gion. He worked as a private chef in London for about a year, honing his sensibility and returning home. In March 2018, he opened the long-awaited SEN. The character used in the restaurant's name originates from owner Sugisawa's kanji character and it became a popular restaurant that gained a star in the blink of an eye, with a strong desire to improve itself.

The cuisine at “SEN” uses the best ingredients such as Tamba's Matsutake mushrooms, Matsuba crab and black abalone, and values the sense of the season. Local vegetables, including Kyoto vegetables, are purchased directly from farmers with whom they are connected. Most of the seafood is delivered directly from the fishermen. Using water from Kyoto's Ohara, the local Kyoto produce is made into gem plates with "Grilled milt cooked in a small pot" in winter and "Steamed abalone with vinegared jelly" in early summer. As for Japanese sake, the selection comes from breweries run by young Toji and there are a total of 8 -10 varieties available, mainly from the Tohoku region, especially Fukushima, with the aim of supporting the disaster-stricken area. There are 5 kinds of red and white wine, including champagne.

The building is a Japanese house built by a shrine carpenter. There is a modern Scandinavian counter (8 seats), where you can enjoy your experience with your date, dine with friends, entertain guests from overseas, and even if you are alone, you can enjoy your food in front of the owner as he prepares the next dish. There is also an authentic Japanese style private room (up to 6 people) where you can take off your shoes and relax on special days such as family anniversaries, and business occasions such as entertaining guests. You can choose the type of seat according to the situation.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

※About Reservations
Please register on the “Waiting List”. Pocket Concierge will inform you when there are seats available.
