245453.localizedAddress: 459, Shimokawaracho, Shimogawara-dori, Yasaka Torii-mae,, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto-shi, Kyoto
245453.longDescription:
A 15-minute walk from Higashiyama Station on the Kyoto Municipal Subway Line, Kikunoi Honten is a long-established, iconic restaurant, immersed in the greenery and tranquility of the hill crowned with Kodai-ji Temple and overlooking the emblematic Yasaka-jinja Shrine. Kikunoi’s history as a restaurant dates back to 1912, but its origin can be traced back even further to an old family that for generations had preserved the Kikusui Well, which supplied water for Kitanomandokoro, a wife of Feudal Lord Toyotomi Hideyoshi, to make tea. The Kikusui Well, located on Shimogawara Street in the vicinity of Kikunoi Honten, has survived until today and the restaurant uses the water from its namesake well for cooking.

Kikunoi’s emblematic water is so soft that it can bring out the flavors of ingredients when used in stock-making. In particular, the water drawn up from the Kikusui Well for Kikunoi Honten is known as the highest quality water. Water is an essential ingredient in cooking, especially in Kyoto cuisine, which is closely associated with the water of Kyoto through its water-based cooking methods, such as stewing, steaming, and boiling, as well as its origin lying in the tea ceremony. Taking all these factors together, Kyoto cuisine is dubbed as “composite water art.” It is for this reason that the cuisine of Kikunoi Honten, which is closely associated with water (the symbol of Japanese culture) as its name implies, is called “water cuisine.” It is also recognized internationally, having been awarded three stars in a world-renowned gourmet guide for consecutive years.

Yoshihiro Murata, the third-generation owner of Kikunoi, who runs two more restaurants besides Kikunoi Honten, one in Kiyamachi, Kyoto, and the other in Tokyo, is regularly featured on TV shows and in magazines as one of the most celebrated Japanese chefs in Japan. Renowned not only domestically but also internationally, he devotes his heart and soul to raising the profile of Japanese cuisine outside the country, having established the Japanese Culinary Academy and contributing to the inscription of Japanese cuisine on the UNESCO intangible cultural heritage list. As a result, he received the Person of Cultural Merit in 2018. He also won the American Express Icon Award in the eighth edition of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants in 2020 for his great contribution to the restaurant industry.

Kikunoi’s dishes are distinguished for their “discreet grace and vigorous simplicity” reflecting the art of “kirei-sabi” (the Japanese aesthetics of beauty, elegance, and strength) and the generosity of Kyoto. They are served on various plates and bowls handed down from the former owner, including Oribe ware produced in the Momoyama period in the late 16th century and dozens of works of Kitaoji Rosanjin, to celebrate the bounty of the seasons. The dining rooms are adorned with remarkable artwork, such as paintings by Maruyama Okyo and Ito Jakuchu and flower vases by Kitaoji Rosanjin and the third-generation Sawamura Tosai. The drink menu offers a great selection of Japanese sake and wines from various places, including hard-to-find sake such as Ishidaya and Nizaemon from Kokuryu Sake Brewery in Fukui and Higan from Taiyo Sake Brewery in Niigata.

The sukiya-style building constructed in the end of the Edo period in the mid-18th century only has private dining rooms. Seating between two to 50 guests, each of these 11 rooms provides beautiful views of the Kyoto-style garden. The restaurant accommodates various occasions, from anniversaries and celebrations to intimate dinners and gatherings of Kyoto cuisine fans by offering individually customized services to allow guests to enjoy the special occasions to their heart’s content. In addition, it has English menus for foreign guests. Please note that the restaurant does not accept children under the age of 10, though children’s menus are available if requested in advance. At Kikunoi Honten, guests can enjoy the essence of Kyoto and Japanese culture not only through the dishes but also through the interior décor. Embark on an exciting adventure to the world of this historic restaurant!


* Awarded three stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.
nearestStations: 15 minutes on foot from Kawaramachi Station on the Hankyu Kyoto Main Line

245500.longDescription:
Kikunoi Sushi Ao is a celebrated sushi restaurant with a dignified atmosphere, tucked away in Ishibe Koji Lane, a quiet stone-paved alley lined by traditional townhouses, in Higashiyama, Kyoto.  Opened in 2024 by Kikunoi, a long-established Japanese restaurant awarded three stars by a world-renowned gourmet guide for many consecutive years, this new sushi restaurant has inherited the culinary artistry and tradition of the renowned Kikunoi, which makes it a beloved spot known only to those in the know. The kitchen is entrusted to Chef Eiki Abe, a proud disciple of Yoshihiro Murata, the third-generation owner of Kikunoi, and a former sous chef at Akasaka Kikunoi. Honing his sushi-making skills there, he was appointed as Chef of Kikunoi Sushi Ao at the time of its opening and made it to the list of one-star restaurants just one year later. Particular about his ingredients, the chef deliberately chooses to source fish and shellfish from the neighboring Setouchi region, rather than ordering them from Tokyo, and skillfully combines the local ingredients with traditional culinary techniques from the Kansai Region to create sushi that can only be found at Kikunoi Sushi Ao. “Please enjoy sushi you can only enjoy in Kyoto,” says Chef Abe.

The chef’s choice prix fixe menu consists of 12 to 13 pieces of nigiri sushi, served alternately with Kikunoi’s exquisite Kyoto dishes with seasonal flavors to create a luxurious full-course experience from starter and appetizer to sashimi, soup, grilled fish, simmered dish, and dessert. The sushi rice is prepared with three different blends of vinegar and served in different temperature ranges to match different sushi toppings. The toppings themselves are crafted not just to impress but to bring out their best flavors and textures. In addition, the knowledge and expertise honed at the celebrated Japanese restaurant are applied to creating sushi. For example, the tuna nigiri achieves a balanced harmony of flavors by layering two pieces of lean bluefin tuna – one soy-marinated and the other unmarinated.

Kikunoi Sushi Ao also boasts a great selection of sake from around Japan, including not only renowned labels difficult to find but also Kikunoi’s must-try original sake brewed by Kokuryu Shuzo, a distinguished sake brewery, in Fukui Prefecture. In addition, with a wine cellar made up of Murata’s favorite wines, the restaurant offers Great Wines (Grand Vin) at original prices, despite the recent price rises (this is one of the hidden reasons for its high customer satisfaction). It is also noteworthy that all dishes are served on museum-quality masterpieces crafted by celebrated artists, such as Rosanjin Kitaoji. Guests can pick up their sushi serving stands from the historical tableware collections of the three-generation owners of Kikunoi stacked on the shelves behind the counter.

The restaurant name, Ao, which means blue-green in Japanese,  is derived from the calligraphy of Rosanjin on the wall that features a Zen verse likening enlightenment to blue mountain peaks appearing through the clearing clouds . Enjoy the refined atmosphere of this premium restaurant, with only 10 counter seats, designed by Sotoji Nakamura Builders Office , a master of sukiya-style architecture, who had also designed all the other locations of Kikunoi, and indulge in the beauty of Japanese art and culture with someone who shares your values.

* Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2025.
nearestStations: 15 minutes walk, or 8 minutes  by taxi from Gion-Shijo Station on the Keihan Main Line

245455.longDescription:
Situated in the downtown of Miyazu city in the Tango area of northern Kyoto Prefecture, which is known for the famous Amanohashidate Sandbar and stunning views of Wakasa Bay in the Sea of Japan, Nishiiru is a sushi kappo restaurant helmed by a Portuguese-born chef, Ricardo Komori, with his wife Mio Komori.

Miyazu is admired by sushi chefs as it is home to Iio Jozo, a rice vinegar brewery known for its Fujisu vinegar, which all the renowned sushi chefs use in their kitchens. Chef Komori is among the sushi chefs who gravitated to the city for the precious ingredient. Impressed by the taste and art of Japanese cuisine when he was a cooking student in his hometown of Lisbon, he came to Japan to learn more about it. After honing his culinary skills in tourist destinations in Yamanashi, Shizuoka, and Gunma Prefectures, he learned the art of Edomae sushi at Palace Hotel Tokyo Sushi Kanesaka. He then learned over-the-counter kappo cuisine and vegetable dishes at Mutsukari in Ginza and at Tenoshima in Minami Aoyama and deepened his knowledge of Kyoto cuisine at SEN in Kyoto, establishing the basis for his style of cooking.

He initially considered opening a restaurant in Kyoto, but when he visited Iio Jozo in preparation for his restaurant business, he fell in love at first sight with the sea and mountains of Miyazu and decided to open his restaurant in the city. In June 2022, he made his dream come true by opening his over-the-counter sushi kappo restaurant, Nishiiru, in a warehouse owned by Iio Jozo. He offers Japanese-inspired dishes that reflect his own identity, featuring seafood from the Tango area and fresh local vegetables and showcasing culinary techniques he learned through years of apprenticeship. The dishes are served in courses, starting with appetizers, followed by various exquisite dishes, grilled fish, and about seven pieces of sushi. The exclusive sushi rice made from organic Koshihikari rice grown by farmers under contract with Iio Jozo and seasoned with a blend of three types of Fujisu vinegar brewed from the same rice is particularly noteworthy. The meal ends with pão de ló, a traditional Portuguese cake said to be the forerunner of today’s Castella sponge cake, instead of a Japanese omelet, which is typically served at the end of a sushi meal. The beverage menu mainly offers Japanese sake from the Tango area but also features Portuguese wines, including those that pair well with the pão de ló.

Remodeled from a 100-year-old warehouse, the restaurant has exposed beams with a touch of solidity and an eye-catching counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood (seating up to six guests). Please come to Tango, Kyoto, and enjoy the unique dishes created by a Portuguese-born chef fascinated by Japanese cuisine and Edomae sushi and trained in their birthplace. Needless to say, the restaurant is also a perfect place to entertain overseas guests.

244510.localizedAddress: 4F, Miyuki Building, 80-11, Sueyoshicho, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto-shi, Kyoto
244510.longDescription:
Sushi Nakamura" attracts many food lovers in Roppongi, Tokyo.  Hiroki Wakabayashi, who trained at "Sushi Nakamura," has been working independently in Kyoto since 2023, providing users in Japan and abroad with sushi that can only be tasted here.

The seafood used is the same as in Tokyo. In addition to purchasing seafood from Toyosu, Fish Market such as tuna from “Yamayuki”, Kyoto's unique local fish is also used to create sushi. Sushi rice is also made from Koshihikari rice from Tochio, Niigata Prefecture, and cooked in a Nambu iron pot in Iwate. Kyoto has good water quality, so the same product can be made tastier. The rice is blended with about three different types of vinegar, including red vinegar and rice vinegar, to create a sushi rice that accompanies the seafood and brings out its natural flavor.

When pressing the sushi, Mr. Wakabayashi gives consideration to the sense of unity between the vinegared rice and the sushi toppings. He uses special tricks throughout his work, such as cutting white fish into thin slices and layering it in four layers to create a soft texture.

""Gion Sushi Nakamura"" interior has a Japanese cypress counter that seats 12 patrons. Views of Gion Shirakawa can be enjoyed through the windows. In spring, the sakura blossoms beautifully, giving patrons a feeling of Kyoto-style elegance. The dignified space is overflowing with Japanese-style atmosphere and is frequented by customers on dates and on business entertainment or dinners, as well as being popular among foreign customers.

245422.longDescription:
About a five-minute walk from Kawaramachi Station in Kyoto. Featuring a with a Kyoto-esque atmosphere, Niku Ryouri Yama is located on a backstreet of Ayanokoji Gokomachi. The head chef, Ryuji Yamagishi, is a master of meat cuisine.

His brother is Takahiro Yamagishi of Tominokoji Yamagishi, a hard-to-reserve Japanese restaurant in Kyoto. Following in his brother’s footsteps, he went from being a white-collar worker into the world of chefs. His love of yakiniku (Japanese barbecue) led him to become the head chef of Yakiniku Yama-chan. This later motivated him to open Niku Ryouri Yama in 2022 in the pursuit of further possibilities in meat cuisine. Chef Yamagishi looks up to Chef Takafumi Kayamori of Nidaime Kayamori as his mentor. Since the opening of Yakiniku Yama-chan, Mr. Kayamori, who has been involved in the yakiniku business for many years and knows all about meat, has been teaching him how to make yakiniku and establishing it as a popular restaurant.

The omakase course, is a char-grilled beef course using only female Japanese Black Wagyu beef as the main dish, starts with seasonal appetizers and features original dishes based on char-grilled beef and Japanese cuisine. Tail gyoza, which are wrapped in a rice-flour skins and baked, use tails that have been simmered for 6 to 8 hours and are crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. The niku somen, which is a dish of finely sliced beef and mountain yam savored with a broth, is also a popular gem. For the yakiniku portion, Chef Yamagishi lets diners compare the taste of three types of tan-shio, or salted grilled tongue— tongue underside platter, tongue base, and tongue midsection—which are char-grilled with perfect timing in front of them. The yakiniku features five different top-quality cuts, including skirt steak, cheek meat, and flap meat. Each cut is accompanied by its own condiments, such as Romaine lettuce, sesame leaves, and rough grated daikon with ponzu dressing.

The second half of the course is a Chateaubriand katsu sandwich that wows guests with its tender mouthfeel. In addition, the beef tongue curry and cold noodles to finish off the meal, as well as the 100% sirloin shigureni dashi chazuke (stewed beef over rice with dashi broth) that can be encountered if you are lucky, have received rave reviews. The drink menu ranges from highballs made from Yamazaki, Hakushu, Taketsuru, and Hibiki Japanese whiskies to red and white wines and SALON champagne to suit guests’ tastes.

The interior, inspired by a Kyomachiya, or traditional wooden townhouse in Kyoto, has a laid-back and relaxed atmosphere. The L-shaped counter with six seats (can seat seven when fully reserved) and the table seat for four are cozy with the aroma of char-grilled food and the calming voice of Chef Yamagishi, creating a space that will surely make you want to return. Families, friends, business associates, and couples are invited to visit and enjoy the cuisine of Niku Ryouri Yama.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi.

244025.longDescription:
Odaidokoro Roji is located in the Uji bridge shopping street, five minutes on foot from the Byodo-In Temple World Heritage Site. In this snug, relaxing venue, guests enjoy dishes carefully prepared by a proprietor who previously trained in Kyoto's well-known restaurant.

The ingredients used are carefully selected and include natural fish delivered directly from the Tango seaside region of northern Kyoto, Kyoto Beef, Kyoto vegetables and "Koshihikari" rice. The innate qualities of the ingredients are given full play, and incredible knife techniques and a keen chef's sensibility attract not only local guests but sightseers visiting from afar as well.

After a sightseeing adventure among Uji's historic buildings and natural beauty, a visit to Odaidokoro Roji to enjoy the seasonal flavors of Kyoto is the perfect way to round out a day packed with the essence of Kyoto's four seasons for the five senses. With separate table seating for parties of up to 10, this Japanese restaurant is the perfect place to take the children along for a family meal and a meaningful experience.

244024.longDescription:
From Kyoto Station, it takes 17 minutes by JR Nara express to the nearest station-Uji. It is approximately 9 minutes on foot from JR Uji Station and 6 minutes on foot from Keihan Uji Station. "Chikurin" was founded by Mr. Shimoguchi who has had experienced at a long-established restaurant "Kikunoi" in Kyoto. Located on the banks of the Uji River, next to the World Heritage- Byodoin Hoo-do. Since it is possible to enjoy meals while watching spring cherry blossom and red leave in autumn, not only local people but tourists visit here. At "Chikurin" , you could taste authentic Kyoto dishes. It is a sister store of a caterer's shop called "Chikurin" which is loved by Uji local people.

Mr. Shimoguchi says that the charming point of Kyoto cuisine is considering the connections between culture and cuisine. Based on Kyoto's history and culture, the chefs uses a new cooking recipe to head for a constantly evolving restaurant. In addition to the taste of the seasons, you could also enjoy a wide range of Kyoto cuisine with Uji Tea.

Apart from daily life, visit here for a luxurious dine with important person. Vegetarian menu is available (consultation at the time of reservation) , recommended to overseas guest as well.

244026.longDescription:
"Tatsumiya", a traditional Japanese restaurant in Uji,Kyoto, overturning the Concept of “tea”-not only a drink. As a dish, you could taste the real sprit of tea with pleasure at Tatsumiya. It is a 12-minute walk from Keihan Uji Station, a 15-minute walk from JR Uji Station, next to the World Heritage- Byodoin Hoo-do. You can enjoy traditional Kyoto kaiseki using seasonal ingredients. Furthermore, feel free to be refreshed by watching, smelling, tasting the Matcha cuisine.

There are dozens of Matcha teas for different ingredients and recipes, Sencha and Gyokuro are also available. "Matcha tofu" with a vivid green color, takes 3 days to make from Hokkaido soybean(strong sweetness) and the finest Matcha. The sweetness of soybeans,the fragrance of Matcha and a delicious flavor bonito and kelp soup stock have been splendidly harmonized. Serving with original tea-ware beautifully.

Located along the edge of Uji River, Tatsumiya is surrounded by greenery. Here is a great location with the view of the Uji River. You can enjoy delicate delicious cuisine with different events; Cherry blossom in Spring, fishing with cormorants in Summer, autumn leaves and all the beauty of season. The counters on the first floor are horigotatsu-style, and the second floor and the third floor are fully equipped with a private room or a large hall. English menu and vegetarian menu (consultation at the time of reservation) are available, it can be used in various situations, such as family gathering, banquets and sightseeing in Kyoto. Reservations are possible from pocket concierge for both lunch and dinner.

244653.longDescription:
Located about a 15-minute on foot from Gion-Shijo Station in Kyoto. "Kodaiji Wakuden" is situated near Kodaiji Temple and greets visitors with an ambiance of refined elegance. Though Kyoto is packed with venerable restaurants serving Kyoto-style cuisine, "Kodaiji Wakuden" is so famous that it would be no exaggeration to say that everyone knows its name.

Relocated from Kyotango, "Kodaiji Wakuden" was born in 1982. Currently, the main attraction of "Wakuden" is the opportunity to enjoy the very best ingredients in every season. In spring, fans look forward to their Beef and Sansho Flower Hotpot. HAMO(pike conger) and AYU(sweetfish) are summer features. Matsutake is for the autumn ingredient. In winter, Taizagani snow crab is synonymous with Wakuden. Only the snow crabs caught by just 5 small boats sailing from Taiza Port are called “Taizagani,” and these extremely rare crabs are classified in about 50 different grades, despite the extremely small catch. Wakuden uses only the highest grade, allowing customers to savor the very pinnacle of winter delicacies. They also specialize in cuisine with a rich rustic character, serving rare fish, vegetables, and meats such as boar and bear.

As for Japanese sake, they serve their own special Aotake-shu, a sake made with groundwater from Kyotango and served in a green bamboo sake set. It has a clean and refreshing flavor that perfectly complements the cuisine. They also have an abundant selection of wine, whiskey, and shochu, etc., that pairs well with the food. 
The building inherits the tea-arbor style architecture erected by master carpenter Sotoji Nakamura, and it has been renovated in the traditional ryotei restaurant style. The interior has 5 private rooms with sunken hearth and hearth-side seating, plus 4 seats at a counter. The private rooms are perfect for a quiet meal with family or friends, while at the counter, you can enjoy watching the chef grill the food right in front of you sharing the seat with other guest. Enjoy Japanese beauty and refinement to the fullest in a space brimming with Kyoto elegance.


* Awarded two stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.
*Please be aware that we are not a barrier-free restaurant.
nearestStations: A 15-minute walk from Gion Shijo Station(Keihan Honsen)

244936.longDescription:
A 5-minute walk from Shijo Station in Kyoto, Jiki Miyazawa is based on cha-kaiseki and set in a shopping area packed with privately run shops. Chef Takatomo Izumi, who had first trained at Tenki, a traditional Japanese restaurant in Kyoto, was so impressed by the dishes of Chef Masato Miyazawa, the proprietor of Jiki Miyazawa at that time, that he eventually apprenticed himself to the celebrated chef. Then, he was appointed as the chef of Jiki Miyazawa in 2014, when Chef Miyazawa opened a branch location, Godan Miyazawa.

Learning Tenzo Kyokun (Instructions for the Cook) from Chef Miyazawa, Chef Izumi believes that “Ingredients are living things. You should not waste any ingredients” and makes full use of them, including the living things turned into ingredients and people involved in the production of ingredients. Jiki Miyazawa, helmed by Chef Izumi, distinguishes itself with its fermented dishes. He goes beyond the category of traditional Japanese cuisine to explore new flavors, such as fermenting fish to bring out its umami flavor and using lactic acid bacteria to ferment vegetables. The fish is sourced from Nishiki Market, selected by a broker in whom he has confidence, while the vegetables are sourced not from any dedicated Kyoto vegetable shop but from a common greengrocer’s shop. The signature menu is homemade “Grilled Sesame Tofu.” The rich flavor and melting texture of sesame tofu are brought out by adding twice the normal amount of kudzu starch and mixing all ingredients with the utmost care. This is so popular that it is also made available for takeout and online orders. The sake list offers 20 labels of Japanese sake from around the country. In particular, Tenon produced by Itakura Brewery in Shimane with an intention to offer it to a god has a mild flavor that goes very well with the dishes of Chef Izumi. Meanwhile, the wine list mainly features natural wines. The marriage of dishes and wines captivates the taste buds of many guests. On request, Chef Izumi selects food and wine/sake pairings.

The restaurant is furnished with a 10-seat counter. The windows at the opposite side are partly covered with white paper sourced from Karacho in Kyoto to make a sharp contrast with the green background in the garden in the daytime. The carefully selected collection of tableware ranges from antiques to contemporary ceramics by young artisans and is used depending on the dish. The restaurant is suitable for different occasions, such as enjoying your own company, having a romantic dinner with your partner, eating out with your friends or family, and entertaining guests from abroad. It also offers a variety of options for online orders, such as Herbal Hot Pot, Shabu Shabu with Soup Stock, and an Assortment of Five Kinds of Delicacies. Please enjoy the elaborate dishes at Jiki Miyazawa, which fully embraces the practice of eating.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 5-minutes walk from Shijo Station on the Karasuma Line of the Kyoto City Subway

245114.longDescription:
Komada is a three-star sushi restaurant in Ise, Mie Prefecture, a town known for the Ise Shrine and the old streetscapes reminiscent of historic Edo-era neighborhoods. Komada is a popular destination restaurant frequented by sushi lovers from around Japan, with sushi elaborately made by chef Kenri Komada, with great attention paid to the sushi rice and fish.

Komada changed his career from a white-collar worker to a cook at the age of 28. First, he worked at a Japanese restaurant in a hotel, and then, he opened his own sushi restaurant in Ise. In his sixth year there, however, driven by the desire to hone his culinary skills in Tokyo, he asked for an apprenticeship at Araki in Ginza, a renowned sushi restaurant. After two years of apprenticeship, he returned to his home prefecture and opened Komada in its current location in 2013. The reputation of his culinary skills honed at Araki spread by word of mouth, allowing his restaurant to expand its clientele and rapidly win three stars in six years.

“My apprenticeship at Araki changed the way I make sushi,” he says. Although he cannot completely reproduce the master’s sushi-making techniques, he explores his own style using similar techniques. The fish and shellfish are sourced not only from local markets but also from Toyosu Market, which he became familiar with during his apprenticeship in Tokyo. Likewise, the sushi rice is elaborately made with aged rice, and seasoned only with red vinegar and salt before being carefully cooked so that it does not stick together but falls apart. The temperature is carefully controlled to be slightly higher than body temperature.

The drinks menu always consists of seven to eight labels of Japanese sake selected from 30 of the chef’s favorite brands, including Yuki No Bijin from Akita, Shichihonyari from Shiga, and Tanaka Rokujugo from Fukuoka, among others from around Japan. Takasago from Mie, which he describes as “perfect,” stays on the menu year-round. Guests can also ask the chef to recommend Japanese sakes to pair with their sushi.

While the exterior appears historical and atmospheric, inside the restaurant is a calming atmosphere, with guests seated at a six-seat counter made of solid cypress wood. Expect a variety of tableware at meals here, ranging from Iga ware from Mie to Karatsu ware from Saga, Bizen ware from Okayama, and Mino ware from Gifu as well as from antiques to handcrafted works by contemporary artists.

Located in Ise, Komada allows guests to enjoy the sophisticated flavors of sushi with a family, partner, or friends in a relaxing environment.

244806.longDescription:
15 minutes by car from the center of Miyazaki City in Miyazaki Prefecture, “Okibi kawaguchi∴”, a local innovative restaurant focusing on Miyazaki ingredients is located in Awakiharacho, 10 minutes by car from the Resort Hotel “Sheraton Grande Ocean Resort”. The restaurant serves Okibi (charcoal) cuisine with Miyazaki ingredients.

Chef Kawaguchi is from Shintomi-cho, Miyazaki Prefecture. He worked at “PILAW∴”, a French restaurant in Ogikubo, Tokyo, founded in 1958 and studied under chef Takashi Hattori. While still working at the restaurant, he was sent to be trained in the United States and Italy, and established “Miyazaki PILAW∴” in 2001. After training in America and Italy again, it was relocated to the current location in 2010. In 2011, he opened “Okibi kawaguchi∴” in the same building. In 2020, he also served as chef for the "SEVEN STARS in Kyushu", which became Japan's first cruise train based on the concept of "presenting Kyushu to the world".In addition, Recently, he has traveled around the world to Bangkok, Singapore, Hong Kong, New York, and other cities to deepen exchanges with chefs in each region and through his own filters, he has expressed a unique world view that is not just fusion cuisine.

Based on the "Cuisine that takes advantage of the terroir" that the chef learned in Italy, “Okibi kawaguchi∴” focuses on ingredients in Kyushu like Miyazaki, then uses the charcoal to cook. It all started when chef Kawaguchi, who saw someone cooking in the fireplace in a farm in Italy " Agriturismo", and recalled his father grilling a whole fish over a campfire. Inspired by that, Kawaguchi scooped up wood from the pizza oven at “Miyazaki PILAW∴”, which serves Neapolitan pizza, and started cooking over a charcoal brazier.

The restaurant uses reliable ingredients that show the face of the producer, "I want to convey the feelings of producers along with the food". Kawaguchi's father and his friends, who were fishermen, deliver fresh the meat used for the main course is Miyazaki's brand Wagyu beef "Ozaki Beef". It is one of the few restaurants in Japan that can serve it as a designated restaurant. The restaurant also uses vegetables that are separated from the producers in Miyazaki Prefecture and grown in their own farms in Shintomicho.Guests can also enjoy some dishes that replicates the cuisine served on Japan's first cruise train, the "Nanatsuboshi in Kyushu".

For drinks, the restaurant focuses on alcoholic beverages, including wines that match the tone of the bonfire cuisine and shochu brews that have been passed down from generation to generation. They also have tea from “Shinryokuen” in Kawaguchi's hometown, Shintomi-cho, selected by Shingo Kuroki, who is a tea master with title that only around 10 people nationwide has. 

There are only 6 seats at the L-shaped counter in the restaurant, where you can feel a sense of harmony. The interior is decorated with plaster, which is inspired from the layers of Takachiho-kyo over the storehouse door, and there is also "Okudo". Enjoy the cuisine and space of “Okibi kawaguchi∴”, which could only be found in Miyazaki, with family and friends. In addition, it is also recommended for entertaining overseas guests.

244641.longDescription:
"GIGLI" is like a hideaway spot, located one street in from the downtown area of Chuo Dori Street in Miyazaki, Miyazaki Prefecture, Kyushu. The young owner-chef who trained in Tokyo fascinates his customers with authentic Italian cuisine.

Chef Shin Toyama is a graduate of the Cooking Department, Nisshou Gakuen Senior High School, Miyazaki. After graduating, he went on to Darie in Ginza, "Don Sabatini" in Haneda, and "Il Ghiottone Marunouchi", where he trained under owner-chef Yasuhiro Sasajima for four years. Then, in 2011, he opened GIGLI in his hometown of Miyazaki. In 2015, he was awarded the Bronze Egg in RED U-35, Japan’s top culinary competition to discover the young talented chefs of tomorrow. Chef Toyama’s cooking is bursting with originality. His dishes are created with the following idea in mind: “If Miyazaki were in Italy, what kind of food would I be serving?”

Chef Toyama is particular about having a selection of the best meats that are the pride of Miyazaki. For beef, he uses Black Wagyu from Miyazaki and Toman-gyu, which is known as a “phantom Black Wagyu.” For pork, he uses Nobeoka Yotton pork and Miyakonojo Okome pork; for chicken Kuroiwa Tsuchidori chicken, and so on. Popular "GIGLI" dishes are the quick smoked Miyazaki Black Wagyu, the Black Wagyu cheek simmered in red wine, and from fall through winter, deer and wild boar from Morotsuka Village served together with seasonal fruits. Also, the simple tomato sauce spaghetti created in a straightforward way using Miyazaki Momotaro tomatoes together with Italian whole tomatoes is one of the restaurant’s pasta dishes that continues to be loved by customers. With a focus on Italian and Japanese vintages, GIGLI’s wine list has about 100 wine to go with the food. Just let the staff know what your tastes are and they will arrange a pairing for your enjoyment.

Open the restaurant’s warm, order-made wooden door to find two different types of dining areas. One is a dining area for casual enjoyment, with counter seating for four and elegantly hand-carved tables/chairs in the table-seating area. The other is a subdued, quiet space. The tables are covered in tablecloths and are recommended for special occasions such as dates, anniversaries, or business entertainment. Customers in search of Italian cuisine produced with new values include those coming from other parts of Japan and overseas, in addition to local people. We invite you to enjoy exquisite Italian cuisine born from the talents of this young chef and the gifts of Miyazaki produce.

244249.longDescription: -- ■About "Waitlist” The Waitlist can be made for the dates at least two days ahead. (Tomorrow and the day after tomorrow will not be accepted.) ■Dinner Reservations for Counter Seating If you wish to make a reservation for more than 4 persons, please contact the restaurant directly or indicate "Counter Seating Request" in the "Request" column when submitting your reservation. -- Just a 15-minute walk from JR Miyazaki Station, nestled quietly in a serene residential neighborhood with a stone-paved approach, stands a discreet haven. Step through the doors, and you are welcomed into an atmosphere of dignity and grace that cannot be experienced in any city—a true “guesthouse of Miyazaki” that transcends the notion of mere “regional sushi.” This is "Isshin-zushi Koyo".Founded in 1973 by the late Kazutaka Kimiya, the restaurant’s appeal lies not simply in its exquisite taste. Sushi that reflects the local climate, wines aged to perfection, and hospitality that blends refinement with warmth—all come together in harmony to create moments that linger in memory. At the counter stands sushi master Haruyoshi Sorakubo, who joined the restaurant at the age of 18 and has dedicated over 30 years to his craft. Using fish and shellfish sourced mainly from Miyazaki and throughout Kyushu, his hands shape each piece in the restaurant’s distinctive “Miyazaki-mae” style, carrying the weight of time and experience. The sushi rice is accented with rare local honey harvested from Japanese honeybees, imparting a natural sweetness and a lingering finish. With the very first bite, it is not your palate but your heart that stirs. Pairing this cuisine is the work of Kazumitsu Kimiya, a certified sommelier, who carefully selects wine and sake at their peak to complement each dish. The progression of sushi and drink unfolds like a story, with the precision of a stage performance. Guests may choose from several course styles: sushi-only, sushi paired with small plates, or the elaborate Sushi Kaiseki. The pairing course, in particular, is highly regarded among discerning diners. Passing through the stone-paved entrance, guests are greeted by an open and inviting space where a large glass window frames the lush garden. A seven-meter counter crafted from a single slab of cherry wood, together with the interplay of light and greenery, sets the stage for a memorable experience. The restaurant also offers a range of private rooms, from intimate spaces for celebrations, business dinners, or engagements to sunken kotatsu seating, each designed with care that surpasses the boundaries of an ordinary sushi restaurant. At Isshin-zushi Koyo —the guesthouse of Miyazaki—you are invited to experience a truly elevated moment, one that fulfills the human instinct for refined time well spent. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? We have 5 rooms and up to 30 people can be accommodated. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? We ask you to remove shoes in the private dining room(s). ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children of any age. We also have a special menu for children. A crib is also available to use. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? Wheelchairs are welcome and an accessible bathroom is available. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. A vegetarian option or ordering from our a la carte menu may be prepared. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? We do not have a dress code.

245452.longDescription:
A 10-minute walk from Miyazaki Station, Hitotsu is a sushi restaurant set in downtown Miyazaki, which is densely packed with restaurants and bars. Opening its doors in November 2022 as a branch of Isshinzushi Koyo, a popular sushi restaurant attracting sushi lovers from around Japan, Hitotsu immediately took root and became a viral sensation. And in July 2025, the restaurant entered a new chapter under a refreshed vision.

The kitchen is now led by Chef Yuta Kawahara, who first trained in traditional Japanese cuisine at a prestigious ryokan in Yufuin before pursuing the path of sushi under Master Sorakubo of Isshinzushi. Carrying forward the philosophy of Shu-Ha-Ri—to protect, break, and innovate—Chef Kawahara respectfully builds upon his mentor’s guidance while forging his own unique style. Though soft-spoken, his craftsmanship speaks volumes, with each piece of sushi expressing quiet intent and deep care.

In this new chapter, Hitotsu places greater emphasis on precision and mindfulness. A flexible two-part seating style allows for a variety of experiences. The first seating offers a chef’s omakase course, featuring both appetizers and nigiri under the supervision of Isshinzushi. The second seating, starting at 9:00 p.m., is more relaxed and focused on a 10-piece of Sushi  course, with guests welcome to enjoy additional seasonal dishes and sake à la carte.

The interior is awe-inspiring, designed by Tetsu Kijima, a popular architect from Kyoto who is known for his wooden structures and earthen walls. Behind the L-shaped counter (seating up to 10 guests) is a grill station made of bricks that used to surround the historic Windsor Castle in England, and together with it, the made-in-Denmark chairs create a playful combination of Japanese and European designs. At Hitotsu, guests are invited to explore a new expression of sushi culture in Miyazaki. Whether for a quiet evening or a special celebration, enjoy a dining experience that honors tradition while embracing creativity—one piece at a time.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from the west exit of Miyazaki Station on the JR Miyazaki Airport Line

244364.longDescription:
The one place in landlocked Nagano where you can find world-class authentic sushi'; the words of gourmet foodies and master chefs from Tokyo and elsewhere, who pilgrimage to 'Sushi Taka'. Since it's opening in 2008, it has served a never-ending clientele seeking its incredible aged-sushi delicacies, so much that 80% of its visitors are from outside the prefecture. The owner-chef, Takayoshi Kubo, was born in the area before mastering his art over a decade in Tokyo. 

Under his mantra 'Laboring over preparation is key', chef-Kubo painstakingly concocts his creations; from his signature aged-fish, which he lets mature over 2-4 weeks, to his 'kanpyo' gourd shavings, simmered over a day, and his 'tamagoyaki' egg omelette, with shrimp and scallops rolled in, everything he creates is built with zero-compromise. Referring to maximizing the ingredients' sensations as 'treating them in their essences', he lovingly prepares his ingredients through traditional Edomae, or Edo-style sushi techniques. Through his mastery of the simplest of methods, marinating, simmering, and grilling, he brings out the utter best of each contributor, and assembles his top-of-the-line pieces of art.

Kubo sources his seafood from 20 ports rich in heritage, spread throughout Japan from Hokkaido to Kyushu; thanks to his direct channels with his sources, some of his fish arrive as quickly to him as they do to Tsukiji, Tokyo's famous central fish market. Just for an idea of his storied selection, his Spring menu could include Flounder and the rarely-seen 'mystical' delicacy 'budo-ebi' Pandalid Shrimp from Miyagi, Japanese Bluefish from Wakayama, and  Ark Shell from Ehime. With such extraordinary seafood in stock, he then proceeds to conduct age-ing in a temprature-controlled chiller until his ingredients are matured to perfection, a wondrous blend of mellow umami. Of course, 'Taka' is not only about fish; professing that he 'hopes to pass on the passion of producers', chef Kubo buys his rice directly from local Nagano farmers, and has his stock stored chilled with husks on.

Only when necessary does he have them husked, in order to concoct sushi as close to 'live' as possible; to this he ads red sushi vinegar from Kyoto, and blends for a taste most befitting the complexity of his aged seafood. 'Taka' takes pride in its cellar as well, with a seasonal selection of 20-30 bottles for pairing with each piece; chef-Kubo recommends with modesty, thinking of not only the partner in mariage, but also the guest and their preferences.

The interior, with a beautiful Japanese Cedar one-piece counter seating 10, also has a table for 6-10, and a Japanese room for 10. The hostess, chef-Kubo's wife, serves with elegance, completing the revered shop's refined and elegant mood, one that makes one forget the hardships of the long trek there.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Gondou Station (Nagano Dentetsu Nagano Line)

245428.longDescription:
A 20-minute taxi ride from JR Matsumoto Station, 367 (Sanrokunana) is immersed in nature in Shinshu, an easy day trip via Shinkansen bullet train. It is about 70 minutes from Karuizawa Station. The travel time can be reduced to 50 minutes if you rent a car at Ueda Station. The restaurant, 367 (Sanrokunana), is incorporated in Matsumoto Jujo, developed by Jiyujin, which is known for its project, Satoyama Jujo, in Niigata, and represents the concept of local gastronomy.

Matsumoto Jujo is a collective term for a project to restore Koyanagi, a long-established Japanese inn that used to serve as the hub of the Asama Hot Springs in Matsumoto City, Nagano Prefecture, to build Matsumoto Honbako, the hotel where 367 (Sanrokunana) is housed, and to develop shops, cafes, and other small businesses around the hotels. This restaurant is also an integral part of the project to revalue the historic hot spring town of Asama based on modern values. The restaurant’s name, 367, is the sum of 365+2 , which reflects the commitment to representing the natural features of Shinshu, which vary throughout the 365-day year, to allow guests to discover two elements: the culture and history of the region. The number 367 also refers to the total length of the Chikuma and Shinano Rivers, which flow from Nagano through Niigata to the Sea of Japan.

Hailing from Shizuoka, Chef Dai Ishikawa worked at restaurants in Tokyo and then honed his culinary skills at Ristorante Capriccio, a one-star restaurant, in northern Italy. After returning to Japan, he joined Satoyama Jujo, worked as Sous Chef at Hakone Honbako, and became Chef at Matsumoto Jujo in 2021.

The chef offers wood-fired cuisine, using Italian culinary techniques to create unique flavors only found in Shinshu. The ingredients are almost all sourced from local producers. Freshwater fish, known as a specialty of Shinshu cuisine, and young tuna from Sado are served with wasabi sprouts pickled in a vinegar mixture and black garlic sauce. There are also dishes featuring vegetables from SASAKI SEEDS, which is known for growing indigenous vegetables of Matsumoto, Azumino Houbokuton pasture-fed pork from Fujiwara Chikusan, and Sanadamaru free-range chicken. The menu is further enriched with game meat in the winter. Moreover, inheriting the traditional culture of fermented food preservation in Shinshu, homemade miso buckwheat is offered with Sanadamaru free-range chicken grilled over firewood.

The drink menu offers a great selection of local brews, such as Shinshu wines and Shinshu sake. There is also a list of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks to pair with dishes. The non-alcoholic options include original drinks, such as “Tomato + Kyoho” (a mixture of tomato and Kyoho grape juices fermented with lactic acid bacteria), “Gold Crest Wilma Green Tea” (a mixture of two different syrups, one made from Gold Crest Wilma (a variety of cypress) and the other from green tea leaves), blended with soda water), and “Hojicha Kuromoji” (a mixture of cold brewed Hojicha tea and spicebush). Moreover, placing particular emphasis on brewing cider (hard cider), 367 (Sanrokunana) brews its own cider from apples grown with low chemical inputs in a nearby farm under contract with the restaurant. The apple residues are used as feed for Azumino Houbokuton pork to create a virtuous cycle in the community.

The interior is warm with wooden accents. In addition to the main dining room with a counter that seats six and nine dining tables, there are four private dining rooms. The kitchen behind the counter is equipped with a wood-fired oven. In principle, the restaurant only accepts children of upper elementary age and older who can eat the same dishes as adults. In addition, the restaurant has English-speaking staff available to assist guests with menu selection.

Matsumoto Jujo is the perfect place for a day trip around the Asama Hot Springs and exploration of the food culture of Shinshu. Take a walk around the restaurant and discover how tradition and modernity blend together there. It will be an unforgettable experience for you.
nearestStations: Approximately 18 minutes by taxi from Matsumoto Station

244470.longDescription: -- 【About Reservations】 If there are no seats available on your preferred date, please register for the wait list（Not a confirmed reservation）,For more information,Please check the email after application from Pocket Concierge. -- "E.Bu.Ri.Ko" is located in a house in an old district of Karuizawa for holiday villas, and the area itself is full of history and considered one of Japan's premier summer resort destinations. The title "E.Bu.Ri.Ko" comes from the name of a mushroom, and just like its namesake, this restaurant serves French fare that specializes in wild mushrooms picked straight from the forest. The owner-chef Atsushi Uchibori is originally from the city of Umeda in Nagano Prefecture. In his twenties, he served as a chef at an Auberge-style French restaurant in Matsumoto, a city located in Nagano. While he was there he picked up an interest in mushrooms, which led him to study and learn more about mushrooms and plants that grow out in the wild. While he continued to learn as much as he could about cooking with mushrooms, he served as a sous-chef at "La Butte Boisee" in Setagaya, as well as "Mushroom" in Ebisu. From there he moved on to set up his own establishment in 2011. Wild mushrooms are around all year long, but the window to catch them when they are fresh is very narrow. Chef Uchibori ventures out himself to hunt for mushrooms and pick them up when they are at their best. He grabs the freshest mushrooms he can find, and if necessary he uses cold storage to help ripen any type of mushroom that needs it. Every mushroom requires its own specific method of preparation and cooking, and Chef Uchibori is an expert when it comes to figuring out which techniques work best. This way guests can expect that each ingredient on their plate is as fresh as possible. For instance, "Akayamadori," an elusive type of mushroom that only grows in Asia, are gathered up each season and kept in cold storage so they can ripen. This brings out their highly fragrant aroma and deep flavor, which is a perfect finishing touch for potage soup. For main courses, their menu features fresh fish and meat that come paired with mushroom-based sauces and garnishes. Their wine list is also tailored to match their mushroom cuisine, and guests can enjoy local wine made in the surrounding area and Nagano Prefecture. "E.Bu.Ri.Ko" is located in a standalone house with a main dining area split between 2 floors. The atmosphere has a forest-like feel to it that adds an extra layer of comfort. Guest can look out the windows and take in the lush green colors outside, and the interior has a chic ambiance with wood tones running throughout it. The restaurant has table seating with a 8seat total, and for an added bit of charm, there are mushrooms decorated all around the dining area. Chef Uchibori says that "I want our guests to enjoy our fresh, new approach that seeks out the very best flavors that mushrooms have to offer." With his deep love of mushrooms, Chef Uchibori seeks out one-of-a-kind flavors with a dining set to match them, making his restaurant an essential destination for anyone traveling to Karuizawa.
nearestStations: A 15-minute walk from Karuizawa Station, Exit North(hokuriku-shinkansen,Shinano Line)

245420.longDescription: 【Restaurant Information】 When registering for the waiting list, please apply for your preferred time of arrival at 18:00. Situated in Karuizawa, Nagano, Makiyaki Kakehashi, which is a five-minute drive from Karuizawa Station, was opened by Owner-Chef Daisuke Maruyama to bring his culinary flair to this famous highland resort town. When working at a Japanese restaurant in Tokyo, Chef Maruyama came to Nagano and gathered edible wild plants and mushrooms from time to time. In 2019, when the region was hit by Typhoon No. 19, he also participated in volunteer relief work. At that time, hearing about the clearance of all damaged apple trees, he came up with an idea to use the specialty trees as firewood. He then taught himself how to cook with firewood and opened his own restaurant, Makiyaki Kakehashi, in the popular resort town of Karuizawa, Nagano, in 2021. The massive typhoon he witnessed in Nagano Prefecture, usually blessed with mild weather, drew his attention to climate change. “We need to return to the basics,” he said. “Enjoy simply cooked, local food. That is the ideal way to eat.” The restaurant’s name, which means “bridge” in Japanese, reflects his commitment to building a bridge to a better future through food. Makiyaki Kakehashi offers a Japanese-inspired, prix-fixe menu consisting of 10 to 12 courses, from appetizers to desserts, All of the dishes incorporate elements of wood-fired cooking, but the advantages of the technique are most prominent in the beef entrée, which features Tankuro wagyu beef produced by Takashi Ito at Davos Farm in the Sugadaira Highlands, Nagano. At this farm, Tankuro wagyu cattle, a hybrid breed that combines the best of shorthorn cattle, which are known for their tasty, lean meat, and Kuroge wagyu cattle, which are famous for their marbled fat that melts in the mouth, is raised on a 100% chemical-free pasture and fermented feed made of apple and grape lees and tofu refuse to keep their intestines healthy. At Makiyaki Kakehashi, this carefully grown organic meat is placed in the firewood oven while the first course is prepared and cooked slowly on low heat for two hours to make the meat absorb the fragrant scent of burning wood. The restaurant’s specialty, Grilled Turtle, features softshell turtles from Tsumagoi, Gunma. They are kept in spring water from Mt. Asama for two weeks to get rid of mud, grilled over a wood fire, and simply seasoned with salt to bring out their natural flavor. Stating that the Grilled Turtle pairs well with Pinot Noir wines, Chef Maruyama always stocks 40 to 50 varieties of wines, mainly from Bourgogne but also from Funky Chateau in Nagano, which is known for its full-bodied wines that go well with wood-fired dishes. In addition, he has curated a sake list that only consists of local names, such as Shinshu Kirei, Kawanakajima Genbu, and Obuse Winery’s sake. And lest we forget, the apple juice is also popular among diners. In keeping with the concept of returning to the basics, the restaurant’s interior is simple, with plastered walls and a bamboo countertop (seating up to seven guests, or up to eight if fully booked for private dining). Behind the counter, the firewood stove has a strong presence. Located in one of the most popular resorts towns in Japan, Makiyaki Kakehashi is definitely worth visiting. Enjoy tasty dishes there with your friends in a relaxing atmosphere with a crackling fire and fragrant smoke.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Karuizawa Station on the Hokuriku Shinkansen and Shinano Railway.

いつも大変素晴らしい料理をありがとうございます。
ライブ感と仄かなチップの香とお人柄で包まれた温かいお食事でした。
非常に美味

いつものように上質な時間を過ごさせていただきました。　たまたま知り合いの方もいらしていて、話が盛り上がりました。丸山さんの誘導も巧みです。全ての料理が美味しかったですが、初めていただいた締めの蟹雑炊が絶品でした。寒い軽井沢にピッタリでした。また伺います。
どれも美味しかったですが、特にすっぽんの薪焼きは格別でした。次伺うときはダブルを予約しておこうと思います。
どのお料理も工夫されていて、美味しく頂けました。
薪焼に特化された料理とブルゴーニュワインのマリアージュを堪能しました。軽井沢に行く際には必ず伺いたいと思います。

245579.longDescription:
A 20- to 30-minute drive from Karuizawa, Nagano, one of the best highland resorts in Japan, or a 10-minute walk from Komoro Station, Benkeibashi Seki is a Japanese restaurant quietly nestled in Minamicho, Komoro City.  The kitchen is helmed by Chef Hirofumi Seki, who welcomes guests with a delightful menu featuring precious seasonal ingredients. He set up his own business after 14 years of apprenticeship at Azabu Kadowaki, a three-star restaurant famous for its specialty “Truffle Pot Rice,” and fulfilled his long-cherished dream by opening his own restaurant, Benkeibashi Seki, in his hometown in 2017.  Since then, he has strived to establish the refined Tokyo-style Japanese cuisine he learned from years of training in Nagano.

The restaurant’s seafood is sourced from a trusted wholesaler at Toyosu Market. The best seafood of the day is carefully selected within the budget every day. After the market closes at 3 a.m., the chef decides the menu of the day based on the available catch. In addition, seasonal vegetables, such as matsutake mushrooms sourced from local producers, and Minemura Beef and Shinshu Premium Beef from the adjacent city of Tomi are turned into Seasonal Chef’s Choice eight-course meals, from appetizers to desserts.  Precious seasonal ingredients, such as pufferfish, long-tooth grouper, and daggertooth pike, are prepared in a simple way to bring out their best flavors. For example, snow crabs and Japanese pepper flowers are dipped in a shabu shabu hot pot, while wild eels are grilled over charcoal. Minemura Beef is made into steaks, and pufferfish milt is mixed with sake to allow diners to enjoy its rich flavor.  

The sake list offers 30 varieties of premium sake from around Japan, such as locally brewed Shinshu Kirei from Nagano, Juyondai from Yamagata, Kokuryu from Fukui, Hiroki from Fukushima, Kachikoma from Toyama, Jikon from Mie, and Denshu from Aomori. Meanwhile, the wine list offers an excellent selection of wines to meet the tastes and preferences of guests, such as Solaris from Komoro Winery and some labels from Funky Château in Nagano and French wines from Meursault, Burgundy. Open the sliding door behind the noren curtain, and you will be welcomed by a plain wood counter (seating up to seven guests). It is dimensioned to create an intimate atmosphere and encourage lively interactions with the chef. The dining experiences are further elevated by ceramic dishware crafted by Shion Tabata from Shiongama in Karuizawa, arranged to add a seasonal touch. The restaurant also features a semi-private dining room (seating 4 to 10 guests) and a fully private dining room with tatami floor mats (seating up to 4 guests). These spaces cater to various occasions, from private to business situations, such as family and friend gatherings, after-work meals, date nights, and dinners with guests from abroad. Enjoy exquisite Japanese dishes crafted by the skilled chef at Benkeibashi Seki.
nearestStations: An 8-minute walk from Komoro Station.

245409.longDescription:
The Hermitage de Tamura restaurant is a house nestled amidst the greenery of Karuizawa's forests, known as a high-end villa resort. The restaurant's name, "Hermitage," means "hideout" in French, and it exudes a magical atmosphere far removed from the real world. In March 2017, Chef Tetsuya Otsuka took over the restaurant. Chef Otsuka worked at ”Mushroom”” in Ebisu for three years before becoming interested in a restaurant in a land blessed with a natural environment and training at ”Hermitage de Tamura" under Chef Tamura. He has succeeded in further enhancing the restaurant's reputation as the successor to the famous restaurant by maintaining the taste of his mentor and brushing up in many areas.

The restaurant has been attracting many gourmets with the best dishes that bring together the best of the season's bounty from the rich natural surroundings. The restaurant gathers the most delicious ingredients of the season from all over Japan, including local farmers, and serves highly original dishes. For example, the "Cold Peach Soup," a specialty dish served from June to September, combines ripe peaches with consommé to create a clear, clear flavor while bringing out the flavor of the peaches. The flavor can only be achieved with perfectly ripe peaches, which are purchased in season from different regions from south to north, and blended just before serving to preserve their fresh aroma and flavor. The fresh aroma and flavor are preserved by mixing the peaches just before serving. The restaurant has two sommeliers who prepare mainly French wines, but also local wines from Nagano.

The restaurant is not only carrying on the tradition, but also changing some things. The restaurant has also made some changes to its cuisine, such as reviewing the process of cooking to make it more elaborate and flavorful. The restaurant has 23 table seats and two private rooms that can accommodate up to 4-5 people. The private rooms were partially renovated in 2018, and the tableware has been replaced with simple, high-quality items to enhance the cuisine. The restaurant also places importance on teamwork among the staff and fully emphasizes the feeling that everyone is there to entertain guests. The taste and hospitality of a famous restaurant that has been passed down through the generations and continues to be further refined. This is a restaurant you will want to visit in each of the four seasons.
nearestStations: 10 minutes drive or 25 minutes walk from Nakakaruizawa Station

244332.longDescription:
L'ombra will be relocated to the Satoyama area in Karuizawa in July 2020. While keeping the concept of "Local dishes from Italy" from the Roppongi era before the relocation, they use Shinshu's abundant ingredients from organic fields, rivers, and magnificent mountains. At the new L'ombra, you can enjoy authentic Italian cuisine that can only be enjoyed here, as well as the superb view of Mt. Asama.

The chef is Ushio Yutaka. After graduating from high school, he worked for more than 10 years in Italy, focusing on restaurants with stars. After serving as the head chef at Kyoto Art Monzen Hotel, he became the head chef of L'ombra. In addition to the techniques cultivated in Italy, they also add Japanese cuisine, and serve light and beautiful dishes that are comfortable with salt.
As for vegetables, the chef himself goes to a contracted farmer's field to pick chemical-free vegetables. They are more particular than ever about the purchase of meat, and they have various kinds such as Japanese beef, pork and chicken from various places in Shinshu, Joshu beef from Gunma prefecture, Duck meat from Kagoshima prefecture, etc. The fish is selected by the chef's own judgment at the market in Takasaki. The dishes are studded with the skills of the chef who came from a Japanese restaurant with stars, and many customers say, "Another helping!".


The white styled interior is lined with vintage furniture from the 1950's to the 60's and has an atmosphere of a winery in Tuscany or Piemonte in Italy. There are also dishes and cloths with a "RATTA RATTARR" design that warms the body temperature . These products can also be purchased at the shop "NATUR HOME".


There are table seats for 10 people in the well-ventilated room and table seats for 6 people on the deck outside.  The garden, where you can enjoy the flowers and plants of each season, received the Grand Greening Award sponsored by Daiichi Life Insurance Company in 2020. Children and dogs are allowed on the deck seats. Even under the condition of COVID-19, you can enjoy the meal in the well-ventilated indoor seat or the deck seat that is completely outside. It can be reserved for up to 2 - 25 people, and is also recommended for special occasions such as family dinners, birthday parties, and marriage proposals.

244479.longDescription:
"Musaian Ikeda" is located in an elegant, stand-alone house with a glass facade that has been built to be surrounded by the greenery of Karuizawa, a place full of quality vegetables; a place that is nurtured by the abundance of nature.

The owner-chef Masaaki Ikeda’s aspiration to become a chef was influenced by his father’s love of eating out. After graduating the National École Culinaire and the French cooking school Escoffier, Ikeda trained in France for 6 months. Returning to Japan, he honed his skills working in French restaurants in Tokyo and Yokohama, then went on to work at "Musai-an," the sister-restaurant of Hermitage de Tamura in Karuizawa. After serving for seven years as the chef, he opened  "Musai-an Ikeda," a restaurant that bears his own name, in the same resort town.

Bright colors are brought to the plate by ingredients that have been carefully selected by Ikeda, who places great importance on interacting with the producers. Particularly impressive is the generous amounts of Karuizawa vegetables used by the restaurant. Chef Ikeda is particular about using Kitaakari variety of potatoes from Kudo farm in Komoro for the chilled Kitaakari potato potage, which is a specialty dish. He adds truffles and consomme ice to the Kitaakari soup, bringing the dish a greater range of texture and fragrance. Each dish is finished lightly, so you can really sense the vitality of the ingredients. Another characteristic of the restaurant is the way that it casually incorporates a Japanese sensibility into things like the ingredients, seasonings, and cooking methods. "Musai-an Ikeda" stocks Japanee sake made in Nagano Prefecture and shochu, in addition to wine. This is French food that is easy to get used to, and elderly customers will also enjoy eating here. "Musai-an Ikeda" also attracts many customers from outside the prefecture.

Inside the restaurant, guests will find that time passes quietly in this space surrounded by natural light and greenery. Both the counter and table seating is available. Handmade items such as the tables and chairs by the Kiso-based artist Yoshiyuki Hannya and plates and chopstick holders created by ceramic artists add warmth to this stylish interior. Through the food served, "Musai-an Ikeda" allows customers to feel the sentiments of producers and the charms of this place called Nagano. We invited you to visit the restaurant with a sense of calm, so that you may enjoy flavors unique to this restaurant.

244471.longDescription:
At the heart of Karuizawa, a well-known holiday resort destination lies "Restaurant Meli-Melo," a French restaurant surrounded by an expanse of untouched nature. The restaurant itself relocated twice before it moved to its present location near Shiozawa Crossing in the summer of 2017. Chef Keiji Shinohara originally hails from the city of Komoro, which is right beside Karuizawa. He is a veteran chef with a long history of working in the world of French cooking.

Chef Shinohara focuses on local ingredients from Nagano Prefecture and prioritizes fresh local vegetables from Karuizawa when they are in season. He takes advantage of rare and delicate ingredients that are hard to come by elsewhere in the country by procuring from local farms like "Karuizawa Salad Farm," which has access to carefully maintained plots that grow 30 to 40 types of vegetables a year. By taking in local ingredients like this, Chef Shinohara is able to showcase the best of Nagano. Both lunch and dinner consist of omakase courses only. Omakase courses are specially selected by the chef. At the end of the course meal, guests are treated to a rice dish cooked in a Staub iron pot. The dish ingredients change each month, and it's come to be a staple menu item at "Restaurant Meli-Melo". They use rice with large grains and a textured, dense flavor. To accomplish this they purchase a rice brand called "Inochi no Ichi" from Matsukawa in Nagano's Shimoina district. This rice, in particular, is presented to Japan's imperial household as a special ceremonial offering. Their wine list is mainly centered on wine from France and Italy, and they offer a wide selection of bottles that includes everything from vintage bottles to more recent selections that are a bit more casual. The chef also ensures that each wine that comes in meets his personal approval. They also offer soft drinks and handpicked local drinks, including 100% apple juice made from Jonathan apples picked up from Matsuzawa Apple Farm in Komoro. In addition to their local ingredients from Karuizawa, in the future, they plan on branching out even further to take advantage of special local products throughout the surrounding region in Nagano Prefecture.

Inside guests will find a warm and welcoming dining atmosphere with gentle wood tones. Breakfast and lunch can be enjoyed outside on their terrace, and guests are welcome to bring their pets, too. They offer to counter seating with 6 seats and table seating with 16 seats total. This small, quiet hideaway offers guests the best flavors that Nagano has to offer along with the lush natural backdrop of Karuizawa.

245243.longDescription:
A two-hour express train ride from Shinjuku takes you to Mumyo, located close to JR Chino Station in Nagano Prefecture. The dishes made with devotion by Chef Masafumi Karaki to bring out the bounty of nature in Nagano attract throngs of food lovers from inside and outside the prefecture.

Chef Karaki, who trained at a traditional Japanese restaurant in Mejiro, opened his own restaurant, Washoku Karaki, at the current location in 2008. Then, he renamed it to Mumyo (which means “unsung” in Japanese) in 2021 to reflect his determination to go beyond the category of Japanese cuisine and explore the flavors of Nagano. “Nothing is named at its beginning,” he says. “I want to shed light on unacknowledged things rather than acknowledged things.” As indicated by these words, he uses no renowned ingredients but turns common local ingredients into exquisite dishes that celebrate the nature and culture of Nagano.
Chef Karaki goes to get famed natural water called “Obsidian Water” early every morning. He sometimes picks up edible wild plants and mushrooms in the mountains as well and visits local producers when time permits. He literally runs about to get ingredients, as implied by the Japanese word “gochiso” (which means “rushing about to get ingredients and prepare delicious dishes for guests”). The dishes built around the concept of water, seasonality, wind, and soil are simple and natural with flavors reminiscent of the landscape of satoyama (mountain villages). Like the dishes made from ingredients delivered by hunters and farmers with whom the chef has forged relationships, the “White Rice” offered as the last course highlights the appealing features of the restaurant. The carefully selected, locally grown rice is milled at the restaurant every morning and cooked in an earthen pot. First, the rice should be tasted as it is. Then, explore different flavors by pairing it with wasabi from Azumino or egg or ham produced at the foot of the Yatsugatake Mountains.
The wine list offers some 200 labels of wines selected by the chef based on his extensive knowledge about wine, mostly from Nagano but also from other parts of Japan as well as France and Australia. The same list also includes a wide range of carefully selected Japanese sake, mainly from local breweries. In particular, food and drink pairings curated by the chef are strongly recommended. The soft drink menu features natural ingredients, including alcohol-free gin and tonic made with locally grown and brewed organic roses and organic Chinese teas.

Renovated from a traditional Japanese restaurant into a Japanese house-style restaurant, Mumyo has six seats at the counter and boasts a wide collection of tableware, ranging from antiques to ceramics crafted by artists with whom the chef has developed relationships. Despite its name, the restaurant is famous among food lovers. Please enjoy the dishes prepared by Chef Karaki taking inspiration from the nature and culture of Nagano at Mumyo with your family, partner, or friends with whom you can share the pleasure of dining together.
nearestStations: A 2-minute walk from the east exit of JR Chino Station

245464.longDescription:
Situated in Matsumoto, Shinshu, at the foot of the Northern Alps, Hikariya was founded by the Hirabayashi Family, a renowned merchant family in the castle town that is home to the National Treasure Matsumoto Castle. Located 15 minutes on foot or five minutes by car from Matsumoto Railway Station, the restaurant is housed in a 140-year-old building on Zenkoji Street. Remodeled from a stucco warehouse inscribed on the national tangible asset list, the uniquely structured building houses two restaurants (a French restaurant “Nishi” and a Japanese restaurant “Higashi”) on opposite sides of the courtyard. In addition, the fact that Hikariya-Nishi is one of only 10 Japanese members of Relais & Châteaux also makes the restaurant stand out.

Located on the second floor of the warehouse, the spacious dining room with a ceiling that measures nearly five meters high at its highest point boasts white stucco walls and contrasting wide beams, bearing traces of its former use as a rice granary.

Chef Masahiro Tanabe apprenticed under Chef Kazunori Otowa at Auberge in Utsunomiya. While training under the pioneering advocate of local production for local consumption, Chef Tanabe learned the importance of using fresh local agricultural products in his recipes. This basic culinary philosophy has led to his current quest at Hikariya-Nishi for wellness gastronomy (gastronomy for a better life) based on the concept of local production for local consumption. He creates new recipes by taking inspiration from daily activities, such as growing some 50 species of vegetables in the company’s farm and interacting with local producers in Shinshu. For example, he uses yubeshi, sweet citron-flavored dumplings cooked as preserves in Tenryu Village, Nagano Prefecture. With only a few hundred produced each year, this precious ingredient is blended into a sauce for meat to create a unique flavor that can only be produced by the chef who works with local ingredients of Shinshu every day. He was awarded the Bronze Award at the Cooking Masters held by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Japan in 2023.

The wine list offers a wide selection of French, Italian, and Chilean wines as well as local Shinshu wines, which are paired with dishes on the menu upon ordering. The drink menu also includes mocktails made from pomegranate and other homemade syrups. Alcohol-free wine pairing options are also available for guests who prefer non-alcoholic beverages.

With a dining room seating up to 22 guests and three semi-private rooms seating up to two, four, and eight guests, respectively, Hikariya-Nishi is a popular destination for date nights and family celebrations, such as wedding anniversaries and birthdays. It also attracts many tourists who visit the sightseeing city of Matsumoto. In principle, the restaurant accommodates children of third-grade age and older who can eat the same meals as adults but also welcomes younger children if a private room is available. Moreover, English-speaking staff as well as English menus and wine lists are available for overseas guests.
Please enjoy a dramatic dining experience inspired by the bounty of nature in Shinshu at Hikariya-Nishi in a historic building popular among tourists as well as locals in Matsumoto City.
nearestStations: 20 minutes on foot or 10 minutes by cab from the castle exit of Matsumoto Station on the JR Shinonoi Line, Oito Line, or Matsumoto Electric Railway Kamikochi Line.

245253.longDescription:
Located in Iida City, Nagano Prefecture, a city blessed by agricultural bounty, Nihonryori Yukimoto is a three-minute walk from Iida Station, which is directly connected to Tokyo and Nagoya by express bus. The restaurant is helmed by Chef Takayuki Hagiwara, who trained at Shofukuro in Shiga, which is known for fostering young talent, and later returned to work at Nihonryori Yukimoto run by his father. He officially succeeded his father in 2008 and opened a new location in 2016.

In order to deliver the exclusive, fresh and rich flavors of Shinshu to visitors from far away, the restaurant offers dishes featuring local seasonal ingredients. The changing four seasons and their natural beauty are reflected throughout the restaurant, including the dishes, tableware, decorations, and gardens. The vegetables are carefully selected so that only fresh vegetables grown by acquainted farmers and picked in the morning are delivered. The freshwater fish are purchased from reliable fishermen, while the sea fish are sourced from the neighboring prefecture of Aichi every day. The meat dishes feature wild game meat from local hunters, Shinshu beef, and Chiyogenton pork from Iida City, which is known for its meat quality. In particular, as the restaurant is known for its game meat, its seasonal bear meat hotpots are immensely popular, including “Kuma no Kusa Nabe” (a bear meat and edible wild plant hotpot) in the spring, “Tsuki to Suppon Nabe” (a moon bear meat and softshell turtle hotpot) in the summer, “Kuma Kinoko Nabe” (a bear meat and wild mushroom hotpot) in the autumn, and “Kuma no Shirayu Nabe” (hotpot with a moon bear meat and bones) in the winter. In addition, matsutake and other mushroom dishes are offered, sourced locally from Iida, which is known for matsutake mushrooms.
The beverage menu offers 100 labels of wines mainly from Nagano and 30 labels of Japanese sake as well as a variety of soft drinks, including Chinese tea, Taiwanese tea, and fruit juices.

The interior is a combination of elegant simplicity and modernity with furniture created by local artisans. The simple design highlights the beautiful views of the garden and the bounty of nature. With six private rooms and a banquet room (seating up to 50 guests) with a large screen, all of which are wheelchair accessible, the restaurant is suitable for tourists, celebrations, date nights, business dinners, and intimate family meals.
Please enjoy the terroir of Shinshu and the hospitality of Japanese culture at Nihonryori Yukimoto.
nearestStations: A 3-minutes walk from JR Iida Station

244966.longDescription:
Twenty minutes by car from Chino Station in Nagano Prefecture, ca'enne is a restaurant in an idyllic location. Reflecting on the restaurant’s surroundings in Tateshina Kogen at the foot of Mt. Yatsugatake, chef Noriyuki Usui says, "I was excited to see similar scenery to the Italian forest in which I studied," and demonstrates his skills for guests here.

Usui hails from Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture. As a university graduate, he was drawn to Italian cuisine, and after training at several restaurants in Tokyo, left for Italy. There, he studied at a starred restaurant in Piedmont and at a prosciutto workshop in Emilia-Romagna. After returning to Japan, he polished his skills at restaurants in Roppongi and Minami Aoyama before becoming independent. In April of 2020, he opened ca'enne, choosing the Yatsugatake area for its abundance in natural ingredients.

The cuisine at ca'enne is cooked with firewood. Grill ingredients over live fire, as if wrapping them, cooks and adds fragrance without losing moisture. Far from the bustle of the city, the restaurant is located in an expansive area where it can coexist with nature, and also allows for maximum use of live-fire. 

The restaurant’s specialty is their naturally matured "prosciutto", cured by the prosciutto workshop established at the foot of Utsukushigahara Kogen in the neighboring town, making use of the chef’s experience at an authentic Italian prosciutto factory. In addition, vegetables and herbs are grown in the restaurant’s own garden. "I want to present freshly picked ingredients," Usui says. It isn’t uncommon for guests to remark on the aroma of herbs picked minutes before their arrival; in addition, wild plants and mushrooms from the local Satoyama woodland are also superb. 

Popular for its pleasantly chewy texture, the restaurant’s pasta is rolled using a long rolling pin called a matarello instead of a pasta machine. Meanwhile, additional ingredients such as ayu (sweetfish), wild game, meat and eggs, as well as local ingredients from the Yatsugatake area are offered to diners. 

There are a total of 10 seats at the counter, plus tables by an inviting fireplace. Guests can enjoy Italian cuisine as envisioned by chef Usui, served at the highest location at the food of Mt. Yatsugatake, while enjoying the company of family and friends. Truly a Satoyama restaurant worth visiting.
nearestStations: 25 minutes by car from Chino Station (JR Chuo Main Line (Tokyo - Shiojiri)) (Parking available)

また蓼科に出掛けた折には是非食べに伺いますね！

八ヶ岳テロワールを感じるお料理でした。

四季折々に伺いたいと思いました
また、秋に予約いたしました

東京から伺いましたが、決して便の良い立地ではありません。
しかし、時間をかけてもわざわざ伺うべきで、こちらでの食事自体が旅の目的となる価値のあるレストランだと思います。

レストランに入ると、奥様の柔らかい笑顔や厨房の焼き場にくべられた薪のはぜる音や香り、店内奥の暖炉など、癒し要素に襲われます。
そしていざ食事がスタートすると、自家製生ハムや、その土地ならではの素晴らしい食材の数々にも襲われます。
味が素晴らしいのはもちろんですが、料理が提供された際の食材の説明や、生産地のお話などもとても楽しく、あっという間に時間が過ぎてしまいました。

長野への移住すら考えてしまう、季節ごとにお伺いしたくなるレストランでした。

八ヶ岳を中心に信州の素材を巧みに調理される薪料理。
とにかく風味が素晴らしい。そしてどれも地味深く、実に美味しい。
野菜はどれも清冽で深い味わい。ジビエも丹念に薪で調理され旨味が深い。茸もどれも峻烈に味を主張してくる。唯一の海のもの、鰆もシェフのおっしゃる様に薪からの水分を蓄えてとてもフレッシュ。
カウンターで薪火を眺めながら戴いた2時間、とても楽しくお話も伺って満喫至極。
今度はどうにかして夜に伺ってワインとともに戴いきたい。
料理も美味しく、また、シェフとの会話も楽しめたので。

お店の空気から感じ伝わってきて
