244805.longDescription:
Located a short car ride from the Shimabara Railway Tahira Station, villa del nido is surrounded by fields, a reminder of the region’s ingredients, water, and climate that Unzen City-born chef Takafumi Yoshida expresses deliciously on the plate. Expressive of the region’s terroir, the restaurant has earned a coveted star.

Chef Yoshida’s training began in Fukuoka, before he went to Italy at the age of 26. As he refined his skills at a starred restaurant, he became attracted to Piedmont cuisine, and understood the relationship between food and landscape. After returning to Japan, in 2015 he opened villa del nido in his hometown, which reopened in October 2019 after a renovation. 

The ingredients are predominantly sourced from the Shimabara Peninsula; Yoshida frequently meets with producers to plan his menus, with dishes that can be prepared according to the peak season of ingredients in Shimabara Peninsula presented as the specialty of the season. The fields surrounding the restaurant are made up of aibika, okra, borage, and edible flowers that are naturally grown in the area. 

Meanwhile, wines are focused on pairings, with pure wine made naturally from Italy or Japan, as well as seasonal local sakes from local breweries such as Yoshidaya from Minami-Shimabara. For non-alcoholic drinks, homemade fruit sodas made with seasonal ingredients are recommended.

The interiors were designed with the inspiration of dining in a sophisticated forest, in a space close to nature where diners can feel and see the warmth of the trees in the garden. The dinnerware is decorated with pottery made by local craftsmen or Arita-ware. 

Rooted in the area, guests can immediately understand the terroir of Shimabara through Yoshida's cuisine, and enjoy the breath of nature with family, friends, or dates.
nearestStations: A 15-minute walk from Tahiramachi Station (Shimabara Railway)

244404.longDescription:
Originally opened as the 'Benkei' in 1975, 'Le BENKEI' has been pursuing excellence ever since, in the same 6000m²-plus location on the outskirts of Japan's ancient capital, Nara. The grounds originally belonged to a warrior clan serving the lord of Koriyama castle, prior to becoming home to the current western-style villa of magnificent stone-build. From its beginning, it proposed its own unique style, fusing the famous Todaiji temple's lacquered serving trays 'hinomaru-bon' with western course presentation, re-imaging the trays as charger plates. On its 25th anniversary, the restaurant underwent extensive refurbishing, reemerging as a Grande Maison serving authentic and exrtaordinary French cuisine.

Owner-chef Kinji Ogawa, born to a family of traditional Japanese restaurateurs, was nonetheless enchanted by the French counterpart. Naturally, he became an early leader in the visionary movement for Western-Japanese-fusion cuisine, infusing his French menus with traditions of the tea-ceremony and Japanese culinary themes. A heavyweight in Japan's culinary world, chef Ogawa was presented the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport's 'Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays' in 2017 for his contributions regarding local consumption, slow-food-ism, and culinary education, in addition to his achievements in hosting the imperial family and a multitude of distinguished foreign guests.

Chef Ogawa exclusively selects from local Nara produce in constructing his courses; as an authority on the local consumption and slow-food movements, he is also prevalent on the production side as well. His dishes, illuminated by the vibrant 'life' of the fresh ingredients, are created from selected local sources; contract-farmed 'Yamato' greens are supplemented by home-smoked ham, home-grown additive-free vegetables and fruits, and honey from an in-house batch of bees. The expansive cellar shelters over 150 labels of wine, centered on French bottles, but with recent focus on domestic products as well.

Guests lead through the stately gates and marble-lined walkway find a luxuriously-clad interior; an 80-seat main hall looking over the gardens, as well as private rooms small and large on the second floor. Tableware, china and cutlery from the likes of Okura Pottery, Narumi, and Christofle are joined by paintings of eminent artists from home and abroad, antique furnishing, and more, creating a refined and lush atmosphere perfect for hosting others. From business receptions, Family celebrations and get-togethers, anniversaries, and more, 'Le BENKEI' provides an unforgettable memory for guests young and old alike.

245255.longDescription:
Within Niigata Prefecture, a coastal region facing the Sea of Japan and known for its rice production, Sushi Hatakeyama is located in an entertainment district that is a 10-minute taxi ride from Niigata Station. Run by Chef Masayoshi Hatakeyama, who inherited the DNA of a renowned sushi master, the restaurant offers Niigata-mae sushi featuring local ingredients.

Born in Iwate Prefecture, Chef Hatakeyama says he has never thought of pursuing any career other than a sushi chef. This should be expected given that his father, Yoshitomo, trained under one of the apprentices of Shigezo Fujimoto, a legendary sushi master highly acclaimed in the history of sushi. After graduating from high school, Chef Hatakeyama started training at Sushizen, which was opened by his father and his partners in Sapporo, Hokkaido, and later moved to Tokyo when a branch location was opened there. Then, he further honed his skills at other sushi restaurants before opening his own restaurant. Eventually, he moved to his wife’s hometown of Niigata and opened Sushi Hatakeyama in 2017. Meanwhile, his younger brother, Yoshiharu, also runs a kappo restaurant, Yamaji, in Shimbashi, further evidence that culinary DNA is shared within the family.
The prix fixe meal consists of 8-9 pieces of sushi as well as 3-4  dishes. The sushi made by Chef Hatakeyama can be referred to as Niigata-mae sushi as it features local ingredients, such as wild prawns, northern shrimps, snow crab, horsehair crab, blowfish, and abalone. The sushi rice is made from freshly harvested Koshihikari rice from Sado, Niigata. Characterized not only by its large grain size but also by its stickiness, the rice is cooked with close attention paid to the amount of water added. The sushi rice is cooked with great care to enhance its rich flavor and seasoned with precious additive-free red vinegar that is naturally fermented. The meal ends with the chef’s specialty: inari sushi made by rolling Kanpyomaki (dried gourd shavings) around aburaage (deep-fried tofu) cooked in a gentle and elegant broth.
The sake list offers Tsuru no Tomo and Denkara from Niigata, Kintsuru from Sado, Higan from Murakami-city and the lineup of natural wine is the main product.　

The interior is dignified yet comfortable, brightened up by the chef’s smile and furnished with a counter (seating up to six to seven people) and a table (with four chairs).
Please enjoy Niigata-mae sushi with your family, friends, colleagues, or sushi buddies at Sushi Hatakeyama.

245406.longDescription:
It’s located about a 10-minute drive from Niigata Station. Although located in the center of Niigata City, the Traditional Japanese Cuisine Araragi (hereinafter, “Araragi”) quietly stands on the first floor of a building just outside the hustle and bustle of the city. Daisuke Sato, the second-generation owner of the restaurant, displays his skills.

He started his culinary career at the age of 18 and worked at Gion Kawakami and Kikunoi Roan in Kyoto before returning to Niigata at the age of 28 to work at Japanese Cuisine Aragi, where he became the second generation chef in 2006. Inheriting his father's taste but breathing new life into it with his own unique style, his cuisine won a star in the "World Gourmet Guide," was the only recipient of the Chairman's Award in the "Niigata Gastronomy Awards" launched in 2023, and attracted attention when he took charge of in-flight meals for first class domestic flights of major Japanese airlines in January of the same year.

“There is probably nothing I don’t use,” says Sato, who employs a wide variety of seasonal ingredients to create his one-of-a-kind dishes. He also continues to go to learn from Takamitsu Okuda of Umeichi in Osaka to further evolve his traditional “raw ingredient cuisine,” which makes the most of the flavors of the ingredients.

Each guest is presented with a personalized menu written in calligraphy, and the plates are customized according to the guest’s tastes and physical condition. Among the most unwaveringly popular menu items are the steam shrimp dumpling in a starchy sauce made from Artic shrimp and steamed egg custard with mozuku seaweed. The steamed egg custard with mozuku seaweed, which has an exquisite, tender texture, is such a memorable dish that regular customers say they would like to have it as part of their last supper.

Although ingredients vary with the seasons, Sato believes that there are certain encounters that are appropriate for today's occasion, and he hopes that his guests will enjoy these encounters.The restaurant uses ingredients from all over Japan and does not limit itself Niigata. That said, it has been serving Niigata’s Higan sake for over 30 years and actively expresses the charms of hometown Niigata. The restaurant is as particular about the tableware and accoutrements as it is the food, such as the noren curtain by the Textile dyer Yoshioka (Somenotsukasa Yoshioka) in Kyoto and an incense container by artist Kazuo Takiguchi to highlight the changing of the seasons. The restaurant features a counter (6 seats), two tables (4 seats per table), and a 10-mat tatami room (6 seats), so the unique taste of Araragi can be celebrated with family, friends, as a couple, and fellow food adventurers, as well as for entertaining guests from abroad and other business settings.
nearestStations: 8 minutes by cab from Niigata Station on the JR Shinetsu Main Line

“Restaurant UOZEN” is a 2-star modern French restaurant with an authentic Japanese look, located in a rural area a little far from the urban area of Sanjo City, Niigata Prefecture. The outside signboard with “Uozen” in kanji was the name of the Japanese restaurant which was run by the parents of the owner-chef Kazuhiro Inoue’s wife Mariko Inoue, who is also a sommelier. They took over the building and opened “Restaurant UOZEN” in November 2013.

After training at several restaurants in Tokyo and learning about Pacific Rim cuisine and French cuisine, owner-chef Kazuhiro opened “HOKU” (closed) in Ikejiri Ohashi, Tokyo in 2005. After graduating from a culinary school, Sommeliere Ms. Mariko has accumulated experience in Daikanyama’s “Les Comptoirs de la Tour d'Argent” (closed) and “HOKU”. At the peak popularity of “Hoku”, which filled up every night, they opened “Restaurant UOZEN” in Niigata, because they "want to cook in a place with nature".

Based on the concept of "Chasse in the mountains (hunting), Pêche in the sea (fishing), and Nature (nature)", the cuisine makes use of the uniqueness of Niigata. Most of the ingredients carefully-selected for food safety and sustainability are natural. Owner-chef Kazuhiro himself goes hunting in the mountains, fishing in the sea and grows vegetables in the fields. Salt and mushrooms are purchased from reliable local producers. For the specialty, "Sado Botan Shrimp Bouillabaisse" is made of high quality botan shrimp topped with consommé and sprinkled with herbs. It has a superb flavor and taste. During the hunting season, you can also enjoy wild game dishes made with mountain animals. The wines are mainly French, Italian and Japanese, and there are also natural wines such as Gran vin. The wine connoisseur will be amazed by the glass cellar with 3,000 bottles of wine.

Relaxed seating of 10 tables is available in the modern Northern European style restaurant. The dinnerware and cutlery are mainly from Niigata. The restaurant uses things made by artists and craftsmen whom they adore, including those from "Tsubame Sanjo", which is known as the street of craftsmanship. It is a perfect place for traveling and gathering with family and friends, as well as entertaining guests and with overseas guests. We hope you will enjoy the local taste of Niigata together with the culture of "Tsubame Sanjo".


*We often use wild game in our dishes, so please refrain from eating if you are not a fan of wild game.
nearestStations: 20 minutes by taxi from Tsubame-Sanjo Station (JR Yahiko Line)

夫は、イカのお料理がとても気に入ったようです。

私は、最初のマカロンとコロンが印象に残りました。
コンソメが美味しかったです。
ミントのアイスも桃のソースとの相性ばっちり、濃厚でモロッコを思わせました。
また、釣りに狩猟に存分に新潟を楽しまれていらっしゃるご様子に刺激を受けました。70ランクルがあったのも納得です。
ありがとうございました。

店の雰囲気も良く、店員も親切丁寧でした。
お料理も美味しく独創的なものも多く、メニューがないため何が出てくるか楽しみでした。とても良かったです！

全ての料理が大変美味しくとても満足です。
味だけでなく、料理やワインの香り、器や盛り付け、五感全てで食事を楽しめました。普段、味以外のこれらが食後の話題の中心となるなんてことは中々ないですが、どれも強烈な印象ゆえに話に花が咲きました。
とにかくひと皿ひと皿がアートのように驚きと感動に満ちていて、コースの最初から最後まで幸せな、笑顔にあふれた時間を過ごせました。
料理も美味しく、サービスも行き届いており、大変満足致しました。また、宜しくお願い致します。

地産地消の哲学に共感
一品ずつ驚きがあった
ゆっくりくつろげた

意外な素材の組み合わせから、豊かな風味が広がってどれも本当においしかったです。お魚やお肉の火の通し方が絶妙で、素晴らしいと思いました。それ以上に、野菜や山菜の味が生かされ、本当においしかったです。
頻繁にお邪魔することはできないですが、特別な何かの折にはまたお料理を堪能させて頂きたいです。
父の命日であり、結婚30周年の10日前という日に、思い切って出かけて良かったです。ありがとうございました。

自然に敬意を払った盛り付けとお料理に感動しました。
お味もすべて驚くほど美味しかったです
静かな景観、気取らず温かみのあるお部屋、とてもくつろげました
ありがとうございました
是非また伺いたいです

芸術的なお料理でした。どれも美味しくいただきました。
料理が出るタイミングも丁度良く、ゆったりとした時間を過ごすことができました。
春夏秋冬訪れると、その時の旬の食材を楽しめるので、また行きたいと思いました。
美味しいのはもちろん、目で見ても楽しめる料理でした。ワインはおまかせで頼みましたが、料理一品一品に合うワインをいただき、肉さかな料理とも一口目の印象と食べてからの飲み口が全然違うのに、こんなにお互いの良さを高めあっていくもんなんだと感動しました。
コロナの影響で久しぶりに伺いましたが、美味しさがパワーアップしてました。マリアージュしていただいたワインも素晴らしく、希望も聞いて下さったり至福の時を過ごせました。また是非伺いたいです。
素材にこだわりが感じられ、それを生かす調理がなされていて とても満足です。ジビエは今まで苦手でしたが、処理が適切のため とても美味しく頂くことができ、驚きました。ワインも豊富で総合的に満足度が高いです。

お料理の素晴らしいことはもちろん、サービスの丁寧さもお店の雰囲気も、とても居心地がよかったです。
ひと皿毎に感嘆の声が上がり、初めて戴く味や香りを楽しめました。
料理は美味しいしカトラリーや食材なども新潟の物を使っている所もとても良いと思います。

はじめて見る、はじめて口にするお料理ばかりでしたがどれも美味しくて最初から最後まで楽しめました。
今まで食べたお料理の中で1番美味しかったです。
接客もとてもご丁寧で、素敵でした。
ぜひまた伺いたいです。ありがとうございました。
見た目も楽しく、美味。
お料理ひとつひとつに繊細さを感じ、全てが美味でした。品数も充分で大満足です。接客も素晴らしく、素敵な時間を過ごせました。また行きます。
料理・スタッフの皆さん接客・お店の雰囲気、全てが完璧でした。
素晴らしいお料理、心理的安全性を感じさせてくださる気さくなサービス、とても満足できました。ぜひまた伺わせていただきたいです。

新潟産へのこだわりは、新潟にいる方、新潟を訪れる方、どちらにも新鮮な味覚を提供してくれる。東京では味わえない風味や素材も楽しく刺激的でした。
個人的には特に鰆、フライパンでは出せないテクスチャと香りが印象的でしたし、フレンチにはあまりないほぼ透明な見た目のソース。柚子、鰆、昆布という懐石の椀もののような組み合わせだが、フレンチとして新しい味覚になっていたと思いました。
食材の選び方、組み合わせ、味ののせかた、料理の見せ方　全て素晴らしかったです。
以前一年半前くらいにお邪魔しましたが、今回更なる進化を実感しました。シェフの底力、目が離せません。
お店の雰囲気も良く、熟成された高級食材がふんだんに使われた料理が大変美味しかったです。

お料理もお酒も器も箸もどれも素晴らしかったです。
目に映る料理も美しく、大変おいしくいただきました。
最高でした！2回目の利用でしたが、期待を超えて楽しめました。必ずまた伺います。

フレンチのコース料理、ジビエは初めてで、すごく緊張していましたが、お料理ひとつひとつに丁寧な説明をつけてくださり、目でも楽しませていただきました。初めて味わうお料理の味に感動で本当に来てよかったと思えました。また、ゆったりと和やかな空気を感じられる空間で、あっという間に時間が過ぎてしまいました。今度はまた違う季節にお邪魔して、メニューの違いも楽しめたらなぁと思っています。
ごちそうさまでした。
料理がどれも絶品で、接客が素晴らしく、値段以上の満足感が得られたため。
とても美味しくゆっくりと食べられてよかったです。
毎年結婚記念日にお伺いさせていただいており、年に一度大切な時間を過ごさせていただいております。毎回新しいお料理に出会えることは勿論、スタッフの方々が覚えていてくださり苦手な食材など温かい心遣いに感動です。大切な日はまたここで過ごしたいと思っております。いつも素敵な時間をありがとうございます。

初めて来店しました。
お料理、スタッフの人の対応、お店の雰囲気、全てにおいて素晴らしかったです。また、行きたいと思いました。ありがとうございました。

メッセージプレートや記念写真のサービス
をして頂き、とても思い出に残る誕生日になりました。
料理、盛り付け、どれをとっても素晴らしくまた来たいと思います。
シェフ自らがハンティング、フィッシングしてくる地元食材を使ったコースは、全国、いえ、全世界のフーディーズを満足させることでしょう。田んぼを見ながらというロケーションも米所新潟ならでは。
食材からカトラリーまで、シェフのセンスとこだわりが感じられました。大自然の中で、都内の一流店にも引けを取らない食事を楽しめ大満足です。
シェフのクリエイティブなお料理の数々、サーブくださりまた素晴らしい飲み物の提案くださった奥様、大満足でした。ありがとうございました！

料理は見た目も楽しく、味も美味しかったです。
ワインも美味しくて大満足でした。
ジビエが美味しかったです
想像を超える料理とサービスに感動致しました。これからも通わせていただきます！ありがとうございました。
料理人魂とアート魂とおもてなし魂を感じました。

料理、サービスともに最高でした。
また利用したいです。

素材の下拵えから調理、味付け、盛り付け、サーブ…
全てが素晴らしかったです。

盛り付けが斬新で、ワクワクしました！
味も大変満足でした。普段あまりいただかない食材の組み合わせのものもありましたが、上手くマリアージュしていて、感動でした。
美味しい食事に会話もはずみました。
どの料理も美味しかったです。特に肉料理が美味しかったです。
まるで山の中のレストランのにいるような錯覚に陥るような素敵な時間を過ごしました。自然のすべてに感謝をしていただきました。ありがとうございました。
料理を丁寧に説明を受け地元食材豊かさをあらためて知りました、ありがとうございました。そして結婚４１周年楽しく会話し料理も堪能して至福の時間を頂きました、感謝します。

ジビエ料理は初めてだったので、リーズナブルな7,000円のコースをお願いしました。
全然臭みもなく、とても美味しく頂くことが出来て大満足です。
スタッフの方も、とても丁寧に料理について説明して頂けて、ぜひまた伺いたいと思いました。
今度は、13,000円のコースを頂きたいと思います。
素敵な時間を有難うございました。
初めての利用でした。友人たちからも勧められて、新幹線を使っての訪問でした。メニューが無いので、つぎは何が出てくるかとワクワク、ドキドキしましたが、期待以上の味、盛り付け、ワインとのコラボも感動しました。サービスも完璧でした。冬のジビエの頃にまた伺いたいと思います。
料理の味はもちろんですが地元の食材を使い新潟の素晴らしさを演出されていて地元の人間には堪らないと思います。先方も大変満足されていたのでとても助かりました。
お料理大変美味かったです。新潟の様々な食材が工夫されて、一皿ごとに驚きと感動がありました。コロナ禍の中で持病があるため外出して控えておりましたが、伺ってよかったです。子供と良い思い出作りができました。
素晴らしいです。ワインも。今度は、ディナーでゆっくり伺いたいですね。

味、サービス共に非常に満足でした。
初めて猪の肉を食べましたが、想像以上の美味しさでした。

料理はもちろん、器やサービスも素晴らしく、大変満足しました。特に鮎は味わったことのない美味しさでした。
お盆休みは始まったばかりですが、この休みで一番思い出深い時間になりそうです。本当にありがとうございました。近いうちにまたお邪魔したいと思います。
素材の美味しさ、ワインとのベアリング。満足しました。

玄関での挨拶からとても印象的でした。丁寧に迎えていただき、とても大切にされているという印象を受けました。室内の佇まい、ホールのみなさんの洗練された動きに、一同感心いたしました。
　運ばれてくる料理は、驚きの連続でした。アミューズからスープ、メイン等、そしてデザートに至るまで、複雑な味の構成に、まるで花火を見るような感動を味わいました。とてもいい尽くすことができないので、これぐらいにしておきますが、間違いなく異次元の味わいでした。お金を貯めて、また来年お邪魔したいと思います。ごちそうさまでした。

予定よりも到着時間が早かったのですが、丁寧に対応していただけました。

料理やサービスはもちろんとても素晴らしく、
いままで一番充実した記念日を過ごすことが出来ました。

■Cancellation policy ​
Please note that cancellation fees apply as follows if you cancel or change the reservation.​
From 3 business days prior to the date of the reservation: 50% of the total reservation amount ​
From 1 business day prior to the date of the reservation: 100% of the total reservation amount ​
*This also applies in the event of a reduction in the number of guests.

■ The availability of an English version of this page does not guarantee that the restaurant can provide services in English unless otherwise stated. Please be aware that, even if stated, there may still be days when English speaking staff are unavailable.

■ Same-Day Automatic Cancellation
As all guests begin the course at the same time, if you are unable to arrive by the times below, your reservation will be automatically treated as a same-day cancellation, and the cancellation fee will apply.

Lunch: After 12:00
Dinner: After 18:30

 ■ Photography is permitted for the dishes only. Please refrain from taking photos of the interior, other guests, or staff, and ensure they do not appear in your photos.

■ Children Policy
We kindly ask that children refrain from visiting our restaurant.

■ Flow of the Dining Experience
Our restaurant operates on a synchronized start system and the course will begin at a fixed starting time for all guests.
Upon arrival at your reserved time, you will first be seated in the lounge to enjoy an amuse-bouche. Afterward, you will be guided to the restaurant floor, where you will enjoy the course meal at the counter.
Please ensure that you arrive on time.

Lunch:
11:30 Doors open & amuse-bouche served
11:45 Course begins

Dinner:
18:00 Doors open & amuse-bouche served
18:15 Course begins

■ Same-Day Automatic Cancellation
As all guests begin the course at the same time, if you are unable to arrive by the times below, your reservation will be automatically treated as a same-day cancellation, and the cancellation fee will apply.

Lunch: After 12:00
Dinner: After 18:30

■ Food Preferences and Allergies
■ Regarding food preferences and allergies, we kindly ask that guests who are unable to consume meat, game, seafood, vegetables, eggs, wheat, or dairy products refrain from visiting.
If you have any dislikes or food allergies, please indicate them in the “Requests (Allergies)” section when making your reservation.

■ Menu Change Request
We are unable to accommodate menu changes after your arrival due to preparation and cooking requirements.
Please notify us at least three days in advance if any changes are necessary.

■ Dining Duration
The dining experience typically takes 2.5 to 3 hours, depending on the course.
If you cannot allow sufficient time, we kindly ask that you refrain from making a reservation.

■ Special Anniversary Occasions
If you are visiting for a celebration (birthday, anniversary, etc.), please write the details in the Special Requests column when making your reservation.

■ To ensure all guests can enjoy the aromas of the cuisine, please refrain from wearing strong fragrances or heavy perfume.

245405.longDescription:
Iwamuro Onsen is known as the salon of Niigata City. Akari no Shokutei KOKAJIYA is almost in its center. Chef Seinosuke Kumakura shows his skills at this restaurant, which is in a renovated 120-year-old folk house.

Chef Kumakura began his career as a bartender in Okinawa. He won numerous prizes in cocktail competitions sponsored by the Nippon Bartenders’ Association (including second place in the 2006 Prime Minister’s Cup National Awamori Cocktail Competition). After teaching himself how to cook, he moved back to his hometown of Niigata. Following a stint as a catering chef, he opened Akari no Shokutei KOKAJIYA in 2013. In 2022, he opened Iwamuro Hisamoto, a private lodge alongside the restaurant, expanding the scope of his activities.

The name KOKAJIYA comes from the fact that the original hotspring inn of the main family was originally a blacksmith shop. The theme of the restaurant, which is registered as a Tangible Cultural Property of Japan, is “onko chishin,” which means developing new ideas by learning from the past in both the food and the tableware, as well as its refined appearance. The restaurant makes the most of its location, with mountains in the back, the sea beyond the mountains, and plains (rice fields) spreading out around it. Chef Kumakura uses almost 100% local ingredients, while also incorporating plenty of local culture, such as fermented and dried foods born from the harsh winter climate.

During hunting season from November to February, Chef Kumakura, who is a licensed hunter, shoots ducks and pheasants in the fallow rice paddies. Restaurants in Tokyo typically let their ducks age, but at KOKAJIYA can you taste fresh duck shot that morning. The duck course is popular with many repeat customers. A whole duck is roasted on rice straw as a roast duck main dish. Consommé and other dishes using various parts of the duck are served for your enjoyment.

The handmade short pasta is made from stone ground flour produced by a neighboring farmer. Another item is abalone and shiitake mushrooms tossed in a thick, aromatic sauce made from seasonal ingredients. In addition, deserts are a specialty from Kumakura’s bartender days and are highly acclaimed, such as butterbur sprout tiramisu, which pairs well with the bitterness of coffee.

The drink menu also is particular about local products, with white, red, rosé, and orange wines from Niigata wineries such as Cave D’occi Winery, Cantina Zio Setto, Domaine Chaud, Le CINQ Winery, and Fermier. Cave D’occi produces an original blend for the restaurant. Sake is also available from Niigata breweries Abe Shuzo and Sasaiwai Sake Brewery. It is served in wine glasses except when served warm. Also well-regarded is Swan Lake Beer, a mellow craft beer that is easy to drink.

The restaurant is a calm and relaxing place where you can feel its history of 120 years ago while slipping back in time. It features two rooms with two tables that seat four people. There is also be a space for displaying and selling original tableware and antiques. We hope you will enjoy Niigata’s history and cuisine in a space where time flows slowly.
nearestStations: 10 minutes by cab from Iwamuro Station on the Echigo Line

recommendations.comment: 何度訪問しても、素晴らしく居心地よい至福の時間を過ごすことができる。非の打ち所のない完璧な食事。今回は楽しみだった野鴨でなおさらのこと。華やかすぎず退きすぎないワインとのマリアージュ。寛ぎと和らぎをもたらす心配られたスタッフの接客。雰囲気の細部に感じられる詫び寂び。流れる時間の心地よさ。「またここへ帰ってきたい。」唯一無二の名店。
初めてお伺いしましたが、素晴らしいお料理はもとより、皆様ともお話し出来て大変いい思い出ができました。ありがとうございました！
今回もとても美味しかったです。ありがとうございました。
空間、料理、サービスともに期待通りでした。
とても素晴らしい、満足度の高いひと時を過ごさせていただきました。また行きたいと思います。頑張ってください。
どのお皿もとても美味しく、説明も興味深く楽しめました。ごちそうさまでした。
連れて行った家族全員楽しみました。
ペアリング最高でした
新潟に行くことがあれば、また利用したいです
料理がとてもおいしかった。店の雰囲気もよく満足度が高い。また利用したいです。
料理一品一品が美味しくて、感激しました。香りが美味しさに繋がることを実感できました。
料理もスタッフの対応もとても良かったです。
魂のこもった味はもちろん料理の説明、雰囲気、BGMに至るまですべてがパーフェクト。完璧なホスピタリテイ。ゆったり流れる尊い時間、何度でも足を運びたくなる。
友人との旅行時に利用させていただきました。どのお料理も美味しく、素敵な時間になりました。この度はありがとうございました。
スタッフが話しやすく、リラックスして食事を味わうことができました。食事も大変美味しかったです。
今回も美味しくいただきました。ありがとうございました。
お料理はもちろん、お店の皆さんのおもてなしが素晴らしかったです。また行きたいです。
本当に満足できました。料理はどれも美味しく、美しい。また次回が楽しみです。
いつも、美味しい料理と素敵な時間をありがとうございます。また、お邪魔します。
ここでしか食べられないものでありつつ、身近に感じられるような味もあり、楽しめました。静かな時間を過ごせたのも快適でした。
季節の、地元の美味しい食材を、その美味しさを最高に引き出してくださる技術でお料理してくださり、いただけてとても幸せでした
鴨コースありがとうございました！猟の話から食材の話まで、違う土地に来て聞かせていただいた内容はどれもとてもタメになりました。活気のある新潟のシェフさん達の取組を見習って、地域を盛り上げるために尽力したいと思います。またいつかお伺いしますのでよろしくお願いします！
今回はジビエコースをお願いしましたがどのお料理も美味しかったです。子供にもお気遣いありがとうございました。また行きます！
料理の味も、スタッフさんのサービスも非常に満足です、また是非利用したいと思います
ソースがどれも美味しかった。麺も最高。
料理はもちろん、雰囲気もよく、お二人のサービスもとても心地よかったです。子供達もまた行きたいといっていますので、再訪いたします。ありがとうございました
とっても良かったです。
とても楽しくお食事させていただきました。空間やお料理ももちろん最高でしたが、お酒のマリアージュが極上でした。古民家の奥があんなに広くてステキにされていると思わなかったので、早めに来たら古民家の中をうろうろするのをおススメしてもいいかもしれません。酔っぱらう前にうろうろしたほうが危なくないかと思ったもので。
お肉に添えられていた、きりあえ　のソースがとても美味しかったです。
お料理が素晴らしいのはもちろんのこと、器も、店内の様子も素敵でした。ぜひまた伺いたいです。

お料理の味はもちろん器、盛り付けが素晴らしい！
雰囲気、料理、サービス、どれも言うことなしです。

地元の食材を使って、一つ一つ丁寧に作られており、珍しいものをたいへん美味しくいただきました。フレンチなのに薬膳を食べているようで、健康的な感じが更に良かったです。
スタッフの方々もとても感じが良く親切なもてなしを受けました。
ありがとうございました。
お料理はむろんのこと満足感120％。オーナーシェフ熊倉さんとの会話も楽しく、宿に帰った後も翌朝も岩室温泉街にいるあいだ中、余韻に浸っていました。また再来店したいです。

季節感のあるクオリティが高い美味しいお料理でした。コーヒーも珍しい味で美味しくいただきました。器も楽しめました。
お料理の説明も丁寧で、笑顔の接客が大変良かったです。
お手洗いの部屋が暖められていて、ほっこりしました。心遣いが感じられました。

　　ご馳走様でした。
お料理全て、優しい味で美味しかったです。手打ちのパスタが、とても良かったです。お酒のペアリングも勉強になりました。あのような甘めな日本酒は、自分では絶対選ばないのですが、あんなに料理に合うなんてビックリです。美味しい物をたくさん教えていただきました。大満足です。また、お邪魔したいです。本当にありがとうございました。

お料理すべて大変美味しかったです。
接客もとても暖かくて、良い時間を過ごせました。
ごちそうさまでした。また伺います。

高齢の母は最近、食が細くなって…と、外食をしても多くを残す状態でした…なのに、今回は完食。美味しかったと喜んでくれました。それが何より私たちには嬉しかったです。
母のお祝いの席という事で、高齢で好き嫌いのある母のことを考慮した和の食べやすいメニューを考えてくださったのかしら…と、思いましたが、それは私たちにも美味しく、20代の娘にも大好評。美味しいものは誰が頂いても美味しい、ということでしょうね。ありがとうございました。
どれも素晴らしかったですが、とくに鮎のパスタは衝撃でした。こういう驚きのあるお料理は、ほんとうに嬉しい。
何も知らずにネットで検索して見つけて予約させていただいたのですが、じつは前日は南魚沼の里山十帖に宿泊しており、岩佐さんの「新潟美食手帖」が置いてあり、小鍛冶屋さんのシェフについても書かれてあり、たいへん楽しみにしてうかがいました。その高い期待のさらに上をいく満足でした。
急遽、バースディプレートの追加など、あたたかいサービスも、ありがとうございました。ペアリングのワインもいろいろな驚きの出会いもあり、楽しませてもらえました。
ぜひまた違う季節のお料理も楽しませてください。
良い祝いの会になり、心から嬉しく思います。

一品一品、丁寧に趣向を凝らしたお料理で目でも楽しみながら味わうことができました。
野菜が多く、お肉もあっさりとしており、最後のリゾットは少なめにしていただいたことで胃の弱い私も完食できました。

岩室温泉は3度目でしたが、夕飯を宿でなく、こちらで取るプランがベストですね。

シェフのご案内通り、また違う季節にお伺いしたいと思います。

とにかく「美味しかった」
「評価」するということが愚行ではと思えます。
お料理も良かったです、更にゆったりした時間・空間も食することができました。
「評価」よりも「お勧め」です。

美味しかったです！
シェフもお姉さんも素敵でした(^^)
是非リピートしたいと思います(^-^)
素敵な時間をありがとうございました！
食材の組み合わせやお酒との組み合わせも全てよかったです。

245274.longDescription:
It is a 10-minute walk from Niigata Station. Restaurant ISO, a one-star French restaurant, is located in a quiet area a short distance from the bustling streets. Fuyuto Isobe, who is extremely fond of his hometown of Niigata, is the chef.

Chef Isobe hails from Nagaoka City, Niigata Prefecture. After graduating from the Musashino Cooking College, he trained at the Hotel Metropolitan Edmont in Iidabashi, Tokyo, before moving to France. After honing his skills at starred restaurants such as Restaurant Alain Chapel, La Pyramide and Hôtel Martinez, he returned to Japan and became the Head Chef at Tokyo Grinzing in Kojimachi. He then worked as the head chef at Hakuba Resort Hotel La Neige  Higashi-kan in Nagano Prefecture and Ryokan Urashima Restaurant La Plage in Sado City, Niigata Prefecture, before opening Restaurant ISO in 2016.
Chef Isobe's cuisine is a new take on the classic French cuisine he learned in France, mixed with a sensibility unique to the Japanese and of Niigata. As Niigata is strongly associated with the sea, many seafood delights are used in the course dishes. The seafood comes from Sado Island and the vegetables from contracted farmers in Tsubame City.
The roasted abalone, a specialty of the restaurant, is made by steaming abalone for five hours with Japanese sake from Niigata and then roasting it with butter. Served with an abalone liver sauce, French truffles, risotto made with special Uonuma-grown risotto rice, and seasonal vegetables, this dish is a true expression of Restaurant ISO's theme of France plus Japan and Niigata. We hope you will enjoy the marriage with Niigata sake.
Pairings are recommended for the drink menu. Chef Isobe's wife, the service sommelier, provides one drink per plate, interweaving wine and Niigata sake. There is also a wide range of non-alcoholic beverages such as organic grape juice, tea made in Murakami City, and snow-aged coffee.

Formerly a soba shop, this purely Japanese-style building has an inner garden and a cozy space with a modern Japanese feel. The original tableware ordered from OHASHI in Niigata will add color to your meal. The main seating is at the counter (7 seats), which is unusual for a French restaurant, so as to serve hot food while it is still warm and the aroma is at its best. We hope that families, friends, colleagues, and couples will visit Restaurant ISO, which embraces the charm of Niigata in French cuisine, and enjoy the aspirations of Chef Isobe.
nearestStations: A 10-minutes walk from JR Niigata Station

recommendations.comment: 今回も、夫婦で最高の時間を過ごすことが出来ました。初めてこの時期に来店しましたが、春の訪れを感じられる素晴らしいお料理でした。
美味しいお料理にゆっくりくつろげる空間　お祝いの心遣いもありがとうございました。
提供いただいた料理は見た目からして好印象であり、どれも素晴らしいものでした。ドリンクもまた、頼んだ5種類全て美味しくいただけました。また伺うことができれば幸いです。
土曜日はありがとうございました。どれも美味しくて贅沢な時間を過ごす事が出来ました。またお邪魔させて下さい。
お酒もペアリング美味しかった

新しい食材や組み合わせの妙が食材のおいしさを際立たせていると同時にそれぞれ単独で食べるよりも複雑で奥行きのある味わいになっていることに驚かされます。これからもよろしくお願いいたします。
お互いの誕生日のお祝いも兼ねて、訪問させていただきました。今まで、妻とは、誕生日にいろいろなお店に食事にいきましたが、食事、雰囲気、接客すべてで一番！！との妻の感想でした。また必ず訪問させていただきたいとおもいます。ありがとうございました。
またいきたいです。
お料理もペアリングのお酒もいつもながら素晴らしかったです！またよろしくお願いいたします。
凄く美味しかったです。
今回も大変美味しかったです。いつも口福な時間を過ごさせていただいています。
どの料理もとても美味しかったです。
今回はお友達ご夫婦と伺いました。グルメなご夫婦にも喜んでいただけて良かった出す。味も雰囲気も間違いないお店です
いつも結婚記念日に利用させていただいてます。同じ時季に訪れていますが料理は美味しく盛り付けや器も楽しませていただきました。
いつも美味しく、そして楽しい時間をありがとうございました。
常に満足度が高いです。ありがとうございました。
娘の誕生日プレートもとても喜んでました。お料理お酒、おもてなしに全て感動。また必ず伺います
とても美味しかったです。ぜひまた利用したいです
とても美味しかったです。素敵な時間を過ごすことができました。ぜひまた利用させていただきたいです。
雰囲気も味も素晴らしかった
いつも美味しいです

居心地の良いサービスと空間
そして美味しいお料理とお誕生日のサプライズ
大満足です。
素敵な空間とおいしいお料理でした！また季節メニューが変わったらお伺いしたいです！
年1回程度ですが、家族でお食事を楽しませて頂いております。テーブル上のメニューには料理の素材だけ書かれており、毎回どんな料理が来るのか皆で期待に胸を膨らませますが、いつも期待以上の美味しい料理で驚かされます。今回もとても美味しかったです。また、丁寧な接客も有り難うございます。またお伺いできればと思います。
料理が大変美味しいです、素材の味がわかるようにソースなども強すぎず丁度良い感じです。またペアリングのワインも料理に非常に合うものを選んでもらえ有難く、そして美味しいです。いつもありがとうございます。

味もサービスも最高でした。
県内産の食材を使用されていて、その土地の事を思いながら味わう事ができ、より美味しく感じました。
とても満足しました。
また、違う季節に伺いたいです。
美味しい料理をありがとうございました。

今回もお料理はもちろん雰囲気にも癒され、夫婦で幸せな時間を過ごせました！
ありがとうございました♪
We were seated at the counter and had glimpse of the kitchen. We could see the chef at work. Food was well delivered and we totally enjoyed our dining. We enjoyed the mont blanc dessert.

料理の量はちょうどよく、出てくるタイミングも抜群でした。
3組と限らた人数で店内も落ち着いて食事が出来て非常に良かったです。
1つ1つのお料理が繊細なお味で、とても美味しくいただくことができました。記念日に利用させていただいてとても良かったと思います。

食材はどれも魅力的でお料理は全て大変美味しかったです。お酒のペアリングも大変美味しく楽しめました。
接客もとても丁寧で良い時間を過ごせました。
お見送りまでいただきありがとうございました。
帰りの際、お待たせしてしまい申し訳ありませんでした。
是非また伺わせて頂きたいと思います。
予約してからずっと楽しみにしてました。内容は期待通り満足です。見た目の美しさや美味しさは素晴らしく、食感も楽しめました。また記念日に伺います。

妻と2人で結婚記念日で利用させていただきました。はじめから最後まで、料理はもちろん全て満足行くものでしたし、とても素敵な時間を過ごさせていただきました。
　また機会があれば利用させていただきますし、知人にも紹介したいと思いました。素敵な体験をさせていただきありがとうございました。

先日は言葉では到底言い表せないほど、贅沢でゆるやかなお時間を過ごさせて頂きありがとうございました

新潟の美味しい食材とフランスの貴重な食材の熟達と洗練された手の込んだ絶品お料理の数々、、3時間近くがあっという間でした

お食事はもちろんのこと、思い返すと空間やお心遣いなど、五感すべてが心地よく……

興奮のあまり他のお客様がいらっしゃるのに騒がしくしてしまったかもしれません(申し訳ありません)

親友も本当に喜んでいて、お伺いできて本当に良かったです 意外なおもてなしの演出もどうもありがとうございました

贅の欲望は尽きず四季を通して
「またお伺いしたいな」という想いしかありません

寒くなって参りましたのでこれからもお身体にお気をつけください　

おふたりのお店がこれからもご無理なく末長く続いてくださいますように

改めて秋を存分に堪能させていただき、素敵な思い出を本当にありがとうございました！

毎年１回の割合で食事をさせていただいています。
過去の食事写真と比較すると、コースの構成はほぼ変わりませんが、主菜はそのときどきの物を使い、ソースや副菜、食器を主菜に合わせて変えています。
越後牛のグリルは定番のようですが、調理の仕方を毎年変えているようです。
味は当然に申し分ありませんが、目でも楽ませてもらっています。
常に挑戦し続けている姿勢に感心いたします。

ご近所ですがなかなか予約が取れず、ようやく伺う事が出来ました。
お料理はどれも美味しく、娘は南瓜のスープが特に口に合ったようです。パンも美味しく、買って帰りたいと思ったほどです。
奥様の穏やかな接客、堅苦しくなく静かで落ち着いた雰囲気も良かったです。
食事の途中で娘が気分が悪くなった際も優しく対応いただきました。ありがとうございました。
一品毎にシェフの気持ちのこもったお料理にいつも感激します。味だけではなく見た目も、お皿もペアリングして下さるワインも素晴らしいと思います
コース料理やペアリングの素晴らしさは言うまでもありませんが、一つ一つの細やかな配慮の素晴らしさに感動しました。また是非お伺いしたいと思います。ご馳走様でした。

人数の変更ありがとうございました。味はもちろん目にもきれいで、大満足でした。鮑のリゾットが美味しかったです。ブルーチーズの香りがよく、チーズ好きの娘が感動していました。
またよろしくお願いいたします。
料理もおもてなしも大変満足いたしました。また伺います。

質の高いコースでいつも感動します。今回はこちらの都合でワインペアリングができなくて残念でした。また新潟に帰ってきた時はお邪魔したいです。
ありがとうございました。
コンソメが特に美味しかったです。
いつも和食で頂いている本鮪やマハタが、全く別の味と姿かたち、涼しそうな盛り付けで出され感動しました。ワインはいつもお任せで、安心して楽しむ事ができます。ありがとうございました。
お料理はどれも美味しく、きめ細やかなサービスでとても素敵な記念日ディナーになりました。ぜひまた伺いたいと思います。
美味しくて幸せな時間でした！

一品一品がとても丁寧に作られていて、気持ちが困っているのがよく伝わってきたからです。お酒も厳選された感があり、どれも美味しかったです。

当日は、こちらの不手際でグラスを割ってしまい申し訳ございませんでした。
また、バースデープレートをありがとうごさいました。

料理、サービス共に心よい時間を過ごさせて頂きました。

地産地消の新鮮な食材に心うたれました。

また来たい、友達にも薦めたいお店です。
毎回新しいお料理に出会うのが楽しみです。素材の特色を生かした味や香りも最高です。いつも心のこもった対応に、リラックスして時を過ごすことができます。またお世話になります。

雰囲気の良さそしてシェフ＆ソムリエの方の料理を出すタイミング最高でした。
お店の静けさの中にもしっとりとした優越感を齎せてくれました。
またお伺いしたいと思います。
ご馳走さまでした。
良い記念日になりました！
1日目お寿司で2日目に訪問しました。素晴らしい素材、調理法に加えてお店の造りも大変落ち着ける雰囲気だったので心に残る新潟旅行となりました。

美味しくいただきました。
味はもちろんですが、量もちょうど良く大変満足してます。私たちの後にご入店のご夫婦の品の良さに、憧れます。明日は26年目の結婚記念日ですが、あのご夫婦のようになりたいと思いました。
今日は大変お世話になりました。ありがとうございました😊
どのお料理もとてもおいしく、またペアリングのワインと日本酒もよかったです。一緒に伺った全員がとてもおいしかったと言っていました。ぜひまた行きたいと思い、また予約させていただきました。次回もよろしくお願いいたします。
村上岩船地域の食材とお酒も合わせていただき、地元なので感激しました。
いつも本当に美味しくて美しい料理で、最高の時間を過ごさせてもらっています。
料理、接客ともいつも大満足です。またお伺いします

シェフの手の込んだ料理と、和を貴重とした和やかで最高の時間が妻と過ごせてとても満足しました。
デザートのサプライズの提案もとても良かったです。
また大事な日に食べに行きます。
毎回、楽しみにさせていただいてます。出された料理はすべて素晴らしいものでした。また来年楽しみにしてます。年一回ではなくもっと行けるといいのですが。。

野菜、魚、肉の食感、ソースの味、どれも最高でした。
接客も丁寧で過剰過ぎず、好感が持てました。
また、利用したいと思います。

静かに食べようと思っていたのですが、美味しすぎて食べる度に美味しいと大きな声を出してしまいました。

また来年の記念日に行けたらと思っているので、その時はまたよろしくお願いします。

接客も料理も大変満足出来ました。
また利用させて頂きます。
味、見た目も満足しました
お料理も接客も素晴らしいです。とても楽しめました。また利用したいと思います。

全ての料理が美味しく、きれいだった。

Located in the coastal city of Murakami in northern Niigata Prefecture. Blessed with natural ingredients, Kappo Shintaku has a history of more than 150 years since its establishment in 1868. In 2008, this long-established Japanese restaurant was taken over by Owner-Chef Shinsuke Yamagai and his brother, Ryota, who honed their culinary skills at a Japanese restaurant in Kyoto. With these two skillful brothers, the older responsible for sashimi (raw fish) and hassun (appetizers) and the younger for simmered and grilled dishes, the restaurant received one star from an international restaurant guide in 2020.

Kappo Shintaku offers authentic Japanese cuisine mostly made with local ingredients from Murakami City. Known as the city of salmon, it is also blessed with the bounties of the sea and mountains throughout the four seasons, such as cherry salmon and edible wild plants in spring, iwagaki oysters, abalone, blackthroat seaperch, and other prized fish in summer, salmon and Japanese Spanish mackerel in autumn, and cold yellowtail and crabs in winter.  The restaurant’s menu also includes top-prize winning Murakami beef and Japan’s best rice and sake. These ingredients are sourced from long-standing reliable partners as well as new partners who deliver fresh fish that is not on the market. The rich, tasty dishes are accompanied by fruits and other refreshments to reset the palate so that guests can enjoy the meal to the end.
The wine list features local wineries within Niigata Prefecture, such as Fermier and KIYO Wines. The sake list also consists only of local varieties, including Shimeharitsuru from Miyao Sake Brewing and Higan and Muso from Taiyo Sake Brewery. In fact, all the 20-something varieties of sake are sourced from these two breweries in Murakami City. The soft drink menu includes famous spring water and tea from Murakami City, which is known not only as a great source of mineral water but also as the northern limit for tea growing.

Surrounded by black walls with a dignified presence, the exterior of the restaurant has a touch of modernity reminiscent of the Meiji period in the late 19th century. Inside the restaurant, there is a cozy, laid-back dining room furnished with a counter (seating up to six guests) and three tables (each seating up to four guests) as well as a private room separately built in sukiya (tea-ceremony room) style. Kappo Shintaku is worth visiting with your friends, family, or lover on your anniversary or during your trip. Enjoy the culinary delights of Murakami City and Niigata Prefecture known as one of the most blessed places in Japan.
nearestStations: A-20 minutes walk from Murakami Station on the JR Uetsu Main Line

245262.longDescription:
In the Chuetsu region in Niigata Prefecture, known as a rice- and sake-producing area and blessed by the bounty of the land and sea, Restaurant L'armoise is located on the first floor of a condo building that is a 10-minute walk from Nagaoka Station. It is a one-star French restaurant helmed by Chef Ryotaro Tanaka.

Chef Tanaka was born in Nagaoka City. He trained at restaurants in Japan and overseas and returned to his hometown to open Restaurant L'armoise in February 2018. The dishes featuring local flavors soon gained popularity and the restaurant was awarded one star in 2020.
The word “L'armoise” in the restaurant’s name means “mugwort” in French and reflects the desire of the chef to “make guests healthy and happy like mugwort does as a medicine and a protection from evil.” The chef also aims to deliver “dishes not found anywhere else.” The vegetables are picked in the morning from the chef’s garden and his grandparents’ and father-in-law’s farms. The chef’s signature pork dishes feature Tsumari Pork, a brand of pork from Uonuma. The fish is delivered fresh from a fish market in Teradomari, Nagaoka, which is known as a mecca for seafood markets.
The restaurant’s popular dishes include “Jerusalem Artichoke Flan,” which is characterized by its palate-pleasing combination of northern shrimp tartar and bisque from Sado, and “Monkfish Fritters with Spinach,” which is a winter dish that features deep-fried monkfish dressed with monkfish liver sauce and wrapped together with sautéed spinach in crispy spinach. Meanwhile, the chef’s specialty features Tsumari Pork. Pork tenderloin is wrapped in mugwort mousse and roasted over low heat.
The wine list offers a wide selection of more than 170 wines mainly from Burgundy, as well as champagne from RM (Recoltant Manipulant), a small winery that is not yet well known but produces tasty wines with great care. In addition, Rydeen Beer from Hakkaisan, Niigata, is available on the beverage menu. Another popular beverage is homemade ginger ale made from ginger grown in the chef’s garden.

Although it is a French restaurant, the interior is filled with Japanese vibes, such as walls covered with handmade washi paper and Oguni washi paper handed down in Nagaoka City and fretwork created by Sakai Tategu from Niigata City to decorate the glass tables.
Please visit Nagaoka with your family, significant other, friends, or colleagues and enjoy the unique dishes, exclusive setting, and one-of-a-kind experience at Restaurant L'armoise.
nearestStations: A 10-minutes walk from Oteguchi of Nagaoka Station on the Joetsu Shinkansen

245427.longDescription:
Satoyama Jujo is situated in Minamiuonuma, Niigata, one of Japan’s top rice-growing regions, surrounded by rich nature in the form of the Echigo Mountains and the Uonuma Basin, which are blanketed with white snow in the winter. A 20-minute taxi ride from JR Echigo-Yuzawa Station, Satoyama Jujo is immersed in nature yet close enough for a day trip via Shinkansen bullet train from Tokyo. The restaurant’s name, Sanaburi, refers to a ritual banquet to celebrate the successful completion of rice planting and to pray for a good harvest.

Chef Keiko Kuwakino started her career as a beauty therapist but moved to Australia to learn Ayurveda and traveled to Nepal and India to gain knowledge of body-healing spices. After returning to Japan, she started working in the kitchen of Sanaburi in 2014 and was promoted to Chef in 2018. Since writing a graduation thesis on Chinese medicinal herbs, she has continued to delve into the inner health and beauty of human beings, and now she creates dishes to help guests achieve inner health and beauty. In 2022, these efforts earned her the Terroir Award in an international gastronomic guide.

Chef Kuwakino’s dishes reflect her inspirations from the changes of the seasons in Niigata. She sources almost all ingredients from local producers with whom she has forged personal ties and obtains fresh seafood mainly from Sado. She has learned everything about local mountains, including edible wild plants, nature, climate, and ecosystems, from local elders to understand how edible wild plants grow and how traditional food preservation techniques are incorporated into modern culinary art. Her reflective dishes inspired by traditions have the power to heal the bodies and minds of guests.

Sanaburi offers a great selection of local Japanese sake and wines, mainly from Niigata but also from France. The restaurant also suggests food and drink pairings, not only for alcoholic beverages but also carefully selected non-alcoholic options, including Murakami tea, as well as original drinks made with homemade syrups, herbs, edible plants, Satoyama Jujo’s original honey, and other seasonal ingredients to pair with dishes. The organic sparkling spicebush soda, cherry black tea, butterbur green tea, mojito mocktail, fruit-based mocktails , and wild grass teas made with local ingredients also pair well with dishes featuring local ingredients. Guests are attracted to Sanaburi not only because of its dishes but also their marriage with drinks.

Converted from an old house, Sanaburi boasts a cozy dining room with six dining tables and 10-meter-high ceilings that create a spacious feel.

Sanaburi only accommodates children of upper elementary age and older who can eat the same dishes as adults. The restaurant also has English-speaking staff available. Dining at Sanaburi will be an unforgettable experience for guests who like to explore the nature and food culture of Niigata and satisfy their intellectual curiosity. Discover the blessings of the mountains and the power of food at Sanaburi in Satoyama Jujo.

244342.longDescription:
Shibata City is a bustling tourist area where many leading ryokans can be found. It was here that the 1-star restaurant  Tokiwa Sushi was opened in 1954 (Showa 29) and has been loved by local customers ever since. It is currently in the hands of the third generation owner Kosuke Kobayashi. The interior was renovated in May 2017. Unlike other sushi restaurants in the local area which have tatami seating, there are city-style counters, and by improving the sushi and side dishes, he has created a unique restaurant with added urban elements inside a traditional setting. 

From his early childhood, Mr. Kobayashi grew up surrounded by sushi and have been helping the preparation. After graduating high school, he moved to Tokyo with no plans to pursue a career in cooking. However, he later rediscovered the allure of sushi, and gained experience at Sushi Uoshin in Shimo-Kitazawa. In 2010, he returned to Tokiwa Sushi , and after renovating the interior, set forth to improve the business even further. 

What is becoming a well-known type of Sushi is the popular Tokiwa Inari, which hasn’t changed since the restaurant's opening. Tokiwa Inari is a dish of rolled sushi which has been used in Niigata prefecture since ancient times, and is still popular today. It involves boiled chestnuts and walnuts wrapped in vinegared rice and deep-fried tofu. We also recommend the Shiromi and Nodoguro, which is served all year round. Crab is also popular, and there are various kinds for different season, such as Japanese blue crab, queen crab and hairy crab. The restaurant also uses Yamayuki tuna from Tsukiji market. 

They are particularly particular about their vinegared rice. "Toyokoshihikari", which is the only rice produced by Kunio Takahashi in Shibata City, is cooked using spring water from the mountainous Akaya area. The sushi vinegar is a blend of "white diamond", a salt from Sasagawa river, and Murakami Iwafune vinegar and red vinegar, and is adjusted according to seasonal fish. Toyokoshihikari, which is a variant of Koshihikari, has large grains and is "hard", and when the rice is cooked in a rice paddle, vinegared rice with a strong presence each grain is produced. Every time you bite into the vinegared rice, you can feel the strength of Niigata, the rice-producing prefecture.

Inside the long-established building, the renovated interior features 10 seats at the L-shaped counter made of 300 year-old cypress. In addition, there is a wine cellar in the store where you can always enjoy dozens of wines and champagnes, mainly Burgundy, along with Niigata sake. Why not come and enjoy sushi and sake which is unique to Niigata in a setting which blends tradition with innovation.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Shibata Station on the JR Uetsu Main Line

244748.longDescription:
“Aji Arai” is a one-star Japanese restaurant facing the Seto Inland Sea. It is a place where you can truly relax and enjoy your meal as it is located 10-minutes walk away from the busy restaurant district of JR Nakatsu Station in Oita Prefecture. The owner, Tomoyoshi Arai, became independent after training at "Kika" in Nishinaka, Fukuoka for about 9 years, and opened “Aji Arai” in his hometown, Nakatsu City, in 2011. As his grandmother ran a fresh fish shop, owner-Arai came into contact with a lot of high-quality fish during his childhood, and this experience is reflected in the dishes that he serves today.

The restaurant serves an Omakase course with the best ingredients of the season. They have various types of seafood that are unique to Kyushu, such as large abalone from Oita in the summer and grouper in the winter. Because the fishing port is close by, you can buy good fish directly from the local fishermen. Aji Arai also offers the finest seafood from all over Japan such as Matsuba crab and An-Kimo from Yoichi, Hokkaido. Arai-san knows exactly how to cook them to create the most delicious dishes of what could be called, ‘Kyusyu Kappo’, and you can only taste it here. In addition, wild game dishes such as wild boar and deer, as well as beef from Bungo, cannot be missed. Owner Arai's attention to detail is also clear from the plates he serves his dishes on which are decorated with the local Onta-yaki from Oita and the Arita-yaki ware from Saga. There are always 30 different kinds of Japanese sake available to enjoy with your seafood. They mainly use local sake from Kyushu (Oita/Fukuoka) and other famous sakes from across Japan which are carefully selected to pair well with the dishes across every season. 

Aji Arai has a counter with 8 seats and a private room with a sunken kotatsu that can accommodate up to 2 ~ 12 people. Children are also welcome. Near the restaurant is the "Yabakei" which is said to be one of Japan's three most scenic spots, and it is especially crowded during the fall foliage season. Enjoy the best seafood of Kyushu, beautifully prepared for you by owner Arai, for celebrations with family, such as anniversaries, and also for business dinners and gatherings with close friends.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Nakatsu Station, North Exit (JR Nippo Main Line (Mojiko - Saeki))

245254.longDescription:
Okayama City in Okayama Prefecture is a popular tourist destination with a variety of attractions, including Okayama Korakuen Garden, known as one of the three most beautiful gardens in Japan, and Okayama Castle. You will find Kuikiri Ryori Happou, which is located close to Shirosita tram stop that is a 15-minute ride from Okayama Station. The restaurant is helmed by Chef Toshiya Hamura, who is known as a prominent figure in the Japanese culinary world in his hometown of Okayama.

Chef Hamura trained at a Japanese restaurant in Osaka for five years and returned to his hometown, where he opened his first Japanese restaurant, Hinaichi, in 1984. Thereafter, he opened Japanese restaurants around Japan and eventually opened Kuikiri Ryori Happou in 2018 as a compilation of his journey throughout the culinary world and was awarded two stars in a famous restaurant guide.
“Kuikiri ryori is a type of over-the-counter kappo cuisine developed in Osaka and other parts of the Kansai region. It is characterized by serving small portions of simple yet tasty dishes that bring out the true flavors of the ingredients so that guests can eat every bite. We deliver once-in-a-lifetime dishes to our guests while communicating with them over the counter,” says Chef Hamura. His skills honed over a long time and his elaborate dishes fascinate the patrons of the restaurant named after his parents’ restaurant near Saidai-ji Temple.
Many of the ingredients are carefully selected and locally sourced, including Asahi rice from Okayama. The popular homemade fish sauce is made from small fish from the Seto Inland Sea. The precious blue eels, said to have originated from Okayama, are delivered in the best quality and cooked on their firm skin. Rather than being steamed first, they are just grilled over indirect heat from charcoal for 40 minutes until thoroughly heated, though this takes more time and effort.
In addition to these local ingredients, other ingredients sourced from around Japan, including longtooth grouper from the Kyushu region and Kaga vegetables from the Hokuriku region, are also carefully selected, and delivered by producers with whom Chef Hamura has personal ties. The dashi soup stock is made using a generous amount of Japanese kelp from Rishiri, Hokkaido, as it plays an extremely important role in cooking. The Bowl of Softshell Turtle, the restaurant’s signature dish, features turtles fed on tea leaves grown in Nagasaki and cooked to bring out their rich, umami flavor.
The sake list offers a wide selection of high-quality Japanese sake mainly from Okayama, such as Sanzen, Takaji, and Taiten Shiragiku, but also from other parts of Japan, such as Juyondai from Yamagata, Jikon from Mie, and Hiroki from Fukushima.

Behind the counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood is an ice box, which makes this Japanese restaurant look as if it were a sushi restaurant. The collection of tableware selected by Chef Hamura, who says that “tableware is also an important element of a dish,” ranges from antiques to Bizen ceramics from Okayama, Arita ceramics created by Kakiemon and other artists, and blue and white porcelain from China. With an eight-seat counter and a private room (seating up to eight people), this Japanese restaurant is perfect for special celebrations. In fact, it is also a popular place for marriage proposals.
Undoubtedly, the kuikiri dishes and warm service of Happou make the dining experience special and unforgettable.
nearestStations: A 14-minutes walk from Okayama Station

244630.longDescription:
In an unusually quiet part of central Naha, Okinawa, you will find the calm visage of the French restaurant, "UEHARA". The owner-chef, Masaharu Uehara traveled to France when he was just 19, racking up experience at several different restaurants, including a restaurant with world gourmet guide award. At 30, he returned to Japan, setting up a restaurant in his native Okinawa in 2011.

Ingredients at the restaurant include fine quality pork, sea urchin, and lobster from Okinawa, as well as produce imported directly from France, such as foie gras and truffles. Uehara is not fussy about producing areas, carefully selecting and procuring the best of the season from all over Japan. His culinary technique is all about what he omits, rather than what he adds. Chef Uehara's motto is ""simplicity"", and you will find nothing unnecessary in his seasonings or his platings, which allows the flavor and shape of each ingredient to really stand out. His chef's selection dish is composed of seasonal ingredients, so there will always be something new to try whenever you come back to the restaurant. Wine is available by the glass, and there are at least 2-3 kinds of red, white, and champagne on the menu, mostly French in origin. Wines can be recommended according to diners' tastes, or you can try one of the fantastic wine pairings that produce synergy with the food.

Inside ""UEHARA"" is rather sparse, with no paintings or other artworks in sight. Rather, the predominantly white interior design creates a refined and elegant space that perfectly complements Chef Uehara's approach to cooking. There is only table seating at the restaurant, with the space between tables roomy enough for everyone to enjoy a leisurely meal. Chef Uehara serves just three groups a day, allowing him to devote himself totally to entertaining his guests with his finely crafted dishes. As such, ""UEHARA"" makes the perfect setting for anniversaries and other important family celebrations. Having spent a long time in France, Chef Uehara is also proficient at speaking French, which can be handy for guests visiting from abroad. Come to UEHARA and try the amazing French cuisine forged in France and developed in Okinawa.

私は台湾で活体水産卸売業を営んでおり、魚類だけでなく（主にロブスターなど）を扱っています。これまで、ビジネス接待を除いて、味覚の基準を保つために食べ物を原形のまま消費することを好んできました。このレストランで印象的なのは、シェフの料理技術が食材の純粋さを保ちながら、付け合わせが主要な食材を圧倒することなく、複雑な層を与えていることです。この体験は深遠で文化的にも豊かでした。このレストランは派手な盛り付けや食材に頼らず、代わりにお客様が大切な人と共に瞬間を味わうことに集中できるようにしています。シェフのサービス態度は完璧にバランスが取れており、料理の提供ペースも適切で、食事の流れに丁度良いタイミングで間や転換を加え、また顧客の料理に関する質問にも応えてくれます。そのようなプロフェッショナリズムの中に自然に流れる温かさを私は評価しています。心を落ち着かせ、本当に質の高い食事の時間を楽しみたい美食家の方々にこの場所をお勧めします。I am in the live seafood wholesale business in Taiwan. In the past, apart from business entertainment, I've preferred to consume food in its original form to maintain my palate standards. What's impressive about this restaurant is that the chef's culinary skills preserve the food's purity, giving it layers of complexity without letting the accompaniments overshadow the main ingredients. This experience was profound and culturally rich. The restaurant doesn't rely on extravagant plating or ingredients, but instead allows guests to focus on savoring the moment with important people. The chef's service attitude is perfectly balanced, with appropriate pacing of dishes, adding commas or dashes to the meal sequence at just the right moments, while also satisfying customers' culinary inquiries. I appreciate the warmth that flows naturally within such professionalism. I recommend this place to connoisseurs who wish to settle their souls and truly enjoy a moment of quality dining.

245582.longDescription:
About 15 minutes’ drive from Naha Airport or 7 minutes’ walk from Asahibashi Station on the Okinawa Urban Monorail Line, Sushi Dokoro Motoi is discreetly tucked away in an alley off a busy main street in Okinawa Prefecture.   This popular restaurant, situated in one of Japan’s most renowned resort destinations, entices sushi lovers with its traditional Edomae techniques. The kitchen is helmed by the owner and skilled sushi chef, Motoi Matsuda. Hailing from Fukuoka Prefecture, he declared his dream of becoming a sushi chef in his middle school yearbook. The day after graduation, he moved to Tokyo to begin his apprenticeship at a renowned sushi restaurant in Ginza, the mecca of Edomae-style sushi. Then, after mastering the art of sushi-making, a twist of fate brought him to Okinawa, where he opened a restaurant named after himself in 1993.  

The restaurant, Sushi Dokoro Motoi, keeps local regulars and prominent sushi connoisseurs coming back with its truly authentic Edomae-style sushi crafted with traditional techniques the chef learned from his master and senior colleagues. To enhance the flavors of fish and shellfish, he makes full use of the five fundamental techniques of Edomae-style sushi — simmering, boiling, soy sauce marinating, vinegar curing, and kelp wrapping. In fact, he is noted not only for his classic nigiri sushi but also for his artisanal sushi, such as marinated tuna, simmered clam, simmered octopus, pickled gourd, and delicately seasoned fish flakes. To complement these toppings, the rice is sourced from Akita and Niigata prefectures and seasoned with two types of red vinegar mixed in proportions that change twice a year, in summer and winter, to reflect seasonal variations in the fat content of the fish and shellfish. These marine ingredients are sourced from Toyosu Market and fishers across Japan with whom the chef has built trust, picked up every morning at Naha Airport, and turned into exquisite delicacies and sushi toppings. They are accompanied by a wide selection of sake, wines, whiskies, and shochu curated to satisfy the most discerning guests.

The restaurant has no sign but only a small nameplate outside because the chef insists – despite his mastery of the sushi craft – that he is still in training. Inside the restaurant, the interior is adorned with wooden finishes for a touch of warmth and luxury. The main dining area boasts a hinoki cypress wood 10-seat counter elaborately designed as a signature of the sushi restaurant, while the private dining room is arranged to seat up to 6 guests. On the counter and table are Bizen Ware sushi serving plates and Kutani and Mino Ware plates carefully curated to elevate dishes even further. So, why not take a culinary journey to Okinawa with Chef Matsuda? Dive into his exquisite sushi world together with companions who share the joy of good food!
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Asahibashi Station on the Yui Rail monorail.

Japanese Black Wagyu beef ""Chateaubriand,"" topped with Kombu with Pacific herring eggs, sea urchin, and caviar from which wafts the scent of the sea, using fresh foie gras from Hungary, the zucchini and foie gras provide a wonderful performance of texture. This luxurious menu is unexpected for a Kushikatsu restaurant, but from it, one can glimpse the heights of its ambition.

Since earning its the first world gourmet guide award in 2010, ""Kushikatsu Bon Kitashinchi"" has continued to shine with the honor of its 1-star. With the dream of bringing Kushikatsu to the world, it opened its Kitashinchi location in Osaka busiest shopping district as a trial for a top class Kushikatsu restaurant, in preparation for an expansion into Paris. The head chef, Kenji Otani who has trained extensively at Japanese restaurants in Osaka and Himeji as well as Kushikatsu restaurants in Ashiya. He is meticulous about top class ingredients such as those used in the menu above, as well as fresh seafood such as the legendary high-grade fish ""Kue"" (Longtooth Grouper), high-quality vegetables, and even his kitchen utensils and flatware. The antique European furniture blends into space well, the frying pans are made of copper, and the flatware is specially ordered Arita ware. Everything speaks to Mr. Otani's detailed attention to beauty.

Wine offered is mainly French and California selections by a sommelier. Japanese sake and shochu are also available. The interior is divided into 14 counter seats and 2 semi-private rooms (4 seats and 5 seats). On Sundays and holidays, families with children can make use of the semi-private rooms. Customers are mostly business guests, friends, or couples. Overseas business guests enjoy the restaurant, too.

""Kushikatsu Bon Kitashinchi"" has achieved its dream of opening a Paris location and has made great strides toward its goal of bringing Kushikatsu to the world. At the original launch pad, ""Kushikatsu Bon Kitashinchi,"" a traditional common sense is shattered as high-grade ingredients are used without frugality to bring you a new dimension to the true enjoyment of Kushikatsu together with attentive hospitality.

245309.longDescription: -- Our restaurant is Sushi Takeuchi(寿したけうち) located in Kitashinchi(北新地). Please note that some guests mistakenly visit Sushi Takeuchi(鮨たけうち) in Namba(難波). Please check the name and location of the restaurant carefully to avoid any confusion. -- Located on the first underground floor of a building in Kitashinchi, an entertainment district, in Osaka City, Sushi Takeuchi opened its doors in August 2020, helmed by Chef Hideto Takeuchi, who honed his culinary skills at Sushi Ohata, Osaka’s most popular sushi restaurant located in the same building. Guests can enjoy a prix-fixe (fixed-priced) meal (consisting of five to six delicacies and 11 to 12 pieces of nigiri sushi) selected by Chef Takeuchi, who also trained at a Japanese restaurant. He creates Kansai-style sushi he learned while training at the one-star restaurant, Sushi Ohata. The fish and shellfish are delivered fresh every day from Toyosu Market and fishmongers in the Kansai region. They are served on matching sushi rice selected from three varieties (red rice seasoned with red vinegar, white rice seasoned with rice vinegar, and rosé rice seasoned with a blend of red and rice vinegar), as learned during his apprenticeship. The sake list consists of 12 to 13 varieties carefully selected to go well with the sushi of the restaurant. The simple, cozy dining room is only furnished with a counter (seating up to seven people). “Sushi restaurants with counters are often considered to be highbrow, but we would like guests to enjoy our sushi in a relaxing atmosphere,” said Chef Takeuchi. Please enjoy delicious Kansai-style sushi and friendly conversation with Chef Takeuchi at Sushi Takeuchi on various occasions with your friends, family, partner, or coworkers.

244052.longDescription:
HAJIME is a restaurant that has been garnering a great deal of attention from all around the world, by becoming the establishment that has achieved three stars in the shortest time in the history of the world-renowned gourmet guide, and becoming part of the rankings of the Foodie Top 100 and Asia's 50 Best Restaurants. 

Chef Hajime Yoneda —a remarkable individual with an unprecedented professional history, after changing paths from being an electronic components designer to becoming a professional chef— has a truly unique perspective of the world. He prepares dishes that highlight the beauty of regularity in systems, seeking to showcase the equilibrium and harmony that exists within nature, the Earth, and space, always aiming to show his respect and the fragility of these elements, and even going as far as representing life itself. 

Going beyond the framework of cooking, Hajime's perspective stands independently as a form of art, just like music and painting. Guests who enter the world of Hajime do not merely eat food, but it would be fairer to say that they use all their five senses to experience the series of messages and stories conveyed through art.

The full course menu, which includes approximately 17 dishes and lasts about four hours, provides a new gastronomic world in a grand scale, providing a new form of communication with the Earth. Almost as if they were about to embark on a far-away journey, guests will sharpen their five senses to spend a meaningful time immersed in this world with their whole body and soul. All the elements of the dishes prepared by Chef Hajime Yoneda have a specific reason for being there, even the tiniest drops of sauce, changing the expression of the whole dish with their amazingly strong sense of presence. Not only every dish, but also every mouthful, will allow guests to experience great wonder and the deepest of emotions. Chef Hajime Yoneda possesses a true skill that is immeasurable and limitless, with the power to express his unique philosophy and imagination.

The HAJIME team continues to work and evolve every day, as they envelop people from all over Japan, as well as the rest of the world, in a blanket of happiness, amazement, and deep emotions. We hope you will visit HAJIME and use all your five senses to experience this unique world — the ultimate gastronomy.

* Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.

244354.longDescription:
Opened in February 2016, "Evoluer" is a French restaurant located in a quiet backstreet of the Fukushima area in Osaka. The owner-chef Ryujin Ogata is armed with 20-years of experience working for the Madoi Group, which is based in Kyoto and operates French, Italian, and other western-style restaurants. He has also achieved outstanding results in French cooking competitions such as Escoffier and Trophée Jean Schillinger.

Possessing experience in a diverse range of business conditions, exceptional creativity not constrained by genre, and a rich repertoire of techniques, Chef Ogata produces creative French cuisine fused with the essence of Japan. Insisting on domestic produce, he sends for seasonal ingredients from across the country and uses them to create subtle flavors well-suited to the Japanese palate.
For the course menu, in place of an aperitif, he serves Kyoto’s Kanbayashi Sannyu tea, which is only available in certain restaurants. This is followed by an hors-d'oeuvre incorporating seasonal ingredients in a style reminiscent of the Japanese Hassun dish, a specialty combining Shogoin Yatsuhashi and foie gras, and a number of other artistically arranged dishes to tantalize the eyes and the taste buds. These dishes are accompanied by a fine selection of wines, Japanese sake, and liqueurs, and there is an equally wide range of digestifs.

The facilities, including the cutlery and interior, serve to further complement the chef’s culinary vision. The knives are "Aritsugu," the napkins "Musubi," and the lampshades "Hiyoshiya," all fine Kyoto brands. The subtly placed vases and bowls are originals fired in Shimane’s Chikurai kilns, and the traditional Japanese accessories add spots of color to the elegant white toned interior. 244296.longDescription:
Among the many dining areas in Osaka, the Fukushima district stands out for its unique and diverse restaurants. In this vibrant area, Kamoshiya Kusumoto has been a favorite among food lovers since it opened in October 2006.

The owner and chef, Noriyuki Kusumoto, is self-taught and brings his experience as a former bartender to his culinary creations. Driven by a desire to introduce global food cultures to Japan, he creates innovative courses featuring classic and fermented dishes paired with carefully selected fermented beverages. Each month, the restaurant offers a themed course inspired by different regions and cultures, such as "Japan x Edo", "South Korea x Japan", "Taiwan x Hakka", "China x Yunnan", "Former Soviet Union Countries", "Nordic x Baltic Countries", "Northern Italy x Japan", "Germany x Surrounding Countries", "Spain" × France (Basque Country)", "Southern Italy × Spanish Coast", "Greece × Balkan Peninsula", "Indochina Peninsula × France", "Thailand × Malay Peninsula", "India × Surrounding Countries", "Arab Middle East Countries", "Greece × Balkan Peninsula", "Indochina Peninsula × France", "Thailand × Malay Peninsula", "India × Surrounding Countries", "Arab Middle East Countries", "Mexico × Southern United States (New State of Mexico", "Peru x Japan". These courses consist of around 10 dishes, creating a culinary journey across the globe.  

In addition, the name of the restaurant ``Kamoshiya'' means brewed alcohol, and as a restaurant specializing in brewed alcohol, we have about 2000 bottles of wine, about 200 bottles of Japanese sake and other brewed alcohol, and we also have a variety of dishes. The pairing is also attractive. Each pairing is thoughtfully selected to complement the course theme, and a variety of glasses and vessels are used to enhance the experience of each beverage.

The design theme of the restaurant is "chic, modern and simple". It features an elegant combination of materials such as wood, metal and glass to create a cohesive, bar-like ambiance. The space includes six counter seats and is perfect for intimate rendezvous or gatherings of food lovers. With its innovative menu, sophisticated pairings, and inviting atmosphere, Kamoshiya Kusumoto is a "traveling restaurant" that will make you want to come back every month.
nearestStations: A 2-minute walk from Exit 3 of Shin-Fukushima station on the JR Tōzai Line

244738.longDescription:
Summer 2023. The one-star Japanese restaurant "Kyomachi-Ryori Mitsuya" near Utsubo Park was relocated to the town of Gamo in Joto-ku, where an old house still retains the atmosphere of the past, and made a new start as “"Oriyori Matsumura.“”

The owner, Tomonori Matsumura, started his career in the culinary world when he worked at a steakhouse in Kobe. After 10 years at "Uosaburo," a Japanese restaurant in Fushimi, Kyoto, he left for France to further his education and broaden his horizons. There, he worked not at a Japanese restaurant, but at four Parisian bistros and gastronomy restaurants, learning only French cuisine and bringing a new style to his own cooking. After returning to Japan, he opened "Kyomachi-Ryori Mitsuya" in 2014, The restaurant has now moved to this new location, hoping to revitalize the old private house and to make use of the old traditions in cooking new dishes.

Mr. Matsumura's concept is "to be more like the ingredients than the ingredients themselves. He procures the best ingredients from all over Japan and focuses on seasonings. He carefully selects and uses what he believes to be the "real thing," such as soy sauce made from traditional, authentic whole soybeans, mirin (sweet sake) that has been aged for three years, and naturally fermented vinegar. One of the dishes that Mr. Matsumura focuses on the most is "shinjo," a bowl of soup. The lightness of the shinjo, which loosens and cracks the moment one puts one's chopsticks into it, is second to none. The soup is not seasoned in any way so that the flavor of the ingredients comes first, and the flavor of the ingredients can be savored. In the "vegetable shinjo" dish, the white onion is sauteed in oil, cooked with fish ara, and then blended with a blender to create the surimashiri-style dish, which is a technique used in French cuisine.

The tableware is made by Shiro Yoshii, ceramic artists from Kameoka, Kyoto, and is a visual feast.
Sake from Aramasa Sake Brewery and Kuroryu Sake Brewery are also available, as we believe that "Japanese cuisine is only as good as the sake". The restaurant always offers something that can be tasted as a combination of food and sake.

The interior of the restaurant, a renovated Japanese house, has a bare structure with the pillars left standing. The restaurant has a counter and tables that seat eight in an L-shape made of 150-year-old white Nara hinoki cypress with high quality chairs that do not tire. Visit "Oryori Matsumura" for a live-performance atmosphere at the counter, or at the tables for family, friends, business associates, dates, or for entertaining overseas guests.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
（As Kyoryori Mitsuya）
nearestStations: 3 minutes walk from Exit 4 of Gamo 4-chome Station on Osaka Metro Nagahori Tsurumi-ryokuchi Line and Imazatosuji Line

245324.longDescription:
A three-minute walk from Osaka Tenmangu Station, Oryori Miyamoto is located on a side street a few steps from Tenjinbashi-Suji Shopping Street known as the longest shopping street in Japan. Daisuke Miyamoto, the proprietor and chef of the restaurant, studied culinary arts at Nakamura Culinary School and further trained at a Japanese cooking restaurant in Osaka before he opened his own restaurant, Miyamoto, in June 2012 with his wife, Sachiyo, who was his classmate at Nakamura Culinary School. The restaurant attracts food lovers from around Japan with its dishes created based on traditional Japanese cuisine and enhanced with a touch of originality.

As the owner-chef says, “This is a place to enjoy tasty food in a casual atmosphere,” the warm-hearted, friendly proprietor and proprietress will make you feel at ease even at your first visit. The Japanese dishes are created with great care and attention to detail to bring out the flavor of each ingredient and enhanced with a touch of creativity, such as French-inspired Japanese gelée. The chef’s specialty, White Rice Cooked in the Earthen Pot, features Yumetsukushi, chemical-free, organic rice grown by the proprietress’s parents in Kumamoto. The vegetables are also mainly sourced from them, and the beef from a friend who runs an Akaushi cattle farm in Kumamoto. Thus, Miyamoto’s dishes are made in cooperation with those close to the proprietor and proprietress.
The sake is tasted and purchased from a reliable sake shop every day, selected by the proprietress, who is skilled at sake tasting, to fit the foods and the preferences of guests. Miyamoto also offers carefully selected cold-brew Chinese teas.

The interior designed by an architect renowned for his work in the style of sukiya (tea ceremony house) is elegant and classy. The floor under the eight-seat counter made of solid chestnut wood is dug out so that guests can stretch out their legs in it with their shoes off while dining. The plates, bowls, and sake glasses are selected by the owner-chef, ranging from antiques to hand-crafted works by contemporary artists.
Miyamoto is the perfect place to dine with your date, enjoy your own company, and entertain your important guests. Savor the subtle and traditional Japanese dishes in a friendly atmosphere full of smiles there.


* Awarded two stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.

245306.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Yodoyabashi Station on the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line and the Keihan Main Line, Hinabe Mita Yakuzen Natsume Kitahamahonten sits in a busy business district. The restaurant opened its doors in March 2022 as a sister restaurant to hotpot specialty restaurants, Hinabe Mita in Tokyo and Hinabe Seito in Osaka.

Based on the traditional "Masamune Sichuan Hot Pot" handed down from Hinabe Mita and Hinabe Seito, we offer medicinal dishes and medicinal hotpot that are gentle on the body and mind with a medicinal theme. The food and drink menus are deliberately designed to provide energy to busy city dwellers, especially working women.
For example, Yakuzen Natsume offers five hotpot meals designed to promote detoxification, appetite, and recovery from fatigue, such as one featuring shark fins and other collagen-rich ingredients to make the skin healthy and radiant and one featuring mushrooms to enhance the immune system. The ingredients not available in Japan are imported from China. The specialty rice served at lunch is mixed with mannan (the main ingredient of konjac) to reduce the sugar content by 20%.
The drink menu includes jujube wine, as implied by the origin of the restaurant’s name (Natsume means jujube in Japanese). Guests can choose from five different herbal-infused wines, each targeting specific bodily functions. Non-alcoholic options are also plentiful, including artisanal Chinese teas like blooming tea, which unfolds beautifully in the pot for a visual and aromatic delight.

The dining room on the first floor is furnished with a counter (with eight seats), and the dining room on the second floor with 3 tables (seating up to 12 guests). The tableware is selected from the perspective of environmental sustainability, such as 60% recycled plates, bamboo chopsticks, and recyclable paper wet towels. Please enjoy the the meals that promote health and beauty through medicinal cuisine at Hinabe Mita Yakuzen Natsume Kitahamahonten with your family and coworkers. The restaurant is also suitable for dates and girls’ nights out to recharge for tomorrow.
nearestStations: 5 minutes walk from Yodoyabashi Station on the Midosuji Line

French restaurant "La Bécasse" is one of Osaka's gastronomic leader's thanks to owner-chef Mr. Yoshinori Shibuya, who has a wealth of training gained in France's three-star restaurants. His cooking philosophy is the creation of unique and ever-evolving, one-of-a-kind dishes. This is embodied in the sole dishes that are one of the specialties of "La Bécasse." The only rule is that they will be wrapped insole; the wrapped ingredients and the shape are ever-changing. The chef has even turned his inspiration to further developing local staples, with an emphasis on originality. 

"Relais & Châteaux," an association of hotels and restaurants boasting worldwide authority, has admitted only 10 affiliates in Japan. "La Bécasse" has been granted affiliation as a hotel/restaurant with a unique character, able to offer a unique experience.

In order to allow dedication to a limited number of guests, there are only 12 seats. The restaurant's refined interior with its pleasant atmosphere of anticipation presents an ideal space for anniversary dates with loved ones and dinner parties for corporate entertainment, group dining, and similar. We want you to enjoy internationally recognized French cuisine to the utmost.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2023.

244941.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Tenjinbashisuji-rokuchome Station on the Osaka Metro’s Senri Line, this Japanese restaurant is located in a tranquil residential area; the sign is a small light with the name of the Higashichaya Nakamura written on it.

Higashichaya Nakamura was opened in 2019 under chef Manabu Nakamura. Hailing from Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture, he became independent after training in Ryoriya Uemura in Kobe and Oimatsu Kitagawa in Osaka.

Named after the Higashichaya teahouse district in Kanazawa, this area, with its beautiful decorations and stone paved streets, conveys the chef's feelings for his hometown.

Ingredients from Kanazawa account for 90% of the restaurant’s offerings; fresh seafood such as cockles, abalone, and oysters are delivered to the kitchen every day from acquaintances of the chef who run a fish store in Kanazawa, as well as trusted sources in his hometown. 

As with the best chefs, Nakamura has absolute confidence in the quality of his ingredients, striving to pass on as much goodness and flavour to guests as possible. Even for a simple dashi, Rishiri kelp, bonito flakes,  and tuna flakes from Kafuka are used lavishly.

The restaurant always offers around 20 varieties of drinks with Japanese sakes chosen to pair with Chef Nakamura’s elegant dishes. Champagne and white wines are available by the bottle and glass; meanwhile, red wine is available by the bottle. For the full experience, drink pairings are also available upon request. 

Glassware aficionados are well-looked after, with a wide selection of antique dinnerware and sake cups available, such as Baccarat.

The restaurant has 9 seats at its counter, and a private room that seats up to 6 guests. As each room is separate, guests can enter and leave the private room independently, ensuring optimal privacy. Popular with couples, the restaurant is also a favourite with gourmands, who sit at the counter to enjoy the essence of Nakamura’s dishes. 


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Tenjinbashisuji-rokuchome Station (Hankyu Senri Line, Osaka Municipal Subway Tanimachi Line, and Osaka Municipal Subway Sakaisuji Line)
