244336.longDescription:
Presquile is a French restaurant which opened in 2015 on a corner complex building by Midosuji, a main street in Osaka. It is directly connected to the Yodoyabashi subway station. Based on the concept of Basho-style haiku, they offer unique cuisine which preserves the classical style while adopting a new essence of cooking. It is a grande maison which has a reputation for excellent service.

Chef Yasuji Sasaki gained experienced working in the restaurant Trente et Un in Kobe and the world gourmet guide award Alain Chapel in France. Customers can enjoy classical cuisine blended with modern elements and sense the Lyon / French style which he studied, such as the traditional pie dish Duck and foie gras torteau with rouennaise, which he inherited from his teacher Mr. Alan Chapel, or the chicken breast vegetable wrap, a classical dish from Lyon, which he prepares himself in front of guests. The cute sweets that are placed in a jewelry box on the dessert wagon is also very popular, guests are often amazed by the beauty of the small confectionaries. 

Presquile also has the oldest winery in Japan, stocking a large variety including Maruki Grape wine. The restaurants stocks 2000 bottles of Maruki grape and French wine to match with the chef’s cuisine. We also recommend the unique grape, peach and pear wines. 

The restaurant offers 38 table seats, as well as a private room that can accommodate up to 12 guests. The calm and luxurious space, where classic and modern elements are beautifully blended, makes it an ideal choice for business dinners or special anniversaries.
The private rooms, which had been renovated in March 2026, will also be available for families with small children, making this a restaurant you’ll want to remember for special family occasions.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: 2-minute walk from Exit 10 of Yodoyabashi Station on the Osaka Municipal Subway Midosuji Line

244217.longDescription: “Restaurant La Cime” is a refined restaurant set up in Hommachi, known as Osaka’s office district where you can enjoy French cuisine. Chefs and foodies from near and far visit the restaurant to experience the unique, unbridled dishes created by Chef Yusuke Takada, which have earned him award from the world gourmet guide. After graduating from a culinary institute, Chef Takada underwent training at a famous restaurant in Osaka. He independently opened “Restaurant La Cime” in 2010 after continuing his training at three-star restaurant in France. The only specialty is “Boudin Dog”, a dish that combines boudin noir and hot dog. The menu is evolving daily with unique sense, with ideas like a dish created from the thought of scent encountered in daily life, and a dish based on a regional French food. The interior of the restaurant is furnished with wooden floors, creating a warm atmosphere, and makes use of black and white colors, leaving a lasting impression. With private rooms for up to 6 guests, it is perfect not only for business entertainment but also for anniversaries, dates, and spending time with a special someone. 245145.longDescription: -- Notice from the store We will let you know when the restaurant will be open. -- Located near Minami-morimachi Subway Station in Osaka, Sushiyoshi is a two-star sushi restaurant that attracts gourmands from around the world with sushi elaborately made by chef Hiroki Nakanoue to delight and excite. Chef Nakanoue took over the sushi restaurant from his father at the age of 18: Two years later, he relocated it to the current premises, where he established his own culinary style. With the motto “fully devote yourself, give it your all, and give of yourself” as indicated by the calligraphy by Kanjiro Kawai displayed in the restaurant, he put in all his efforts, and the reputation of his sushi spread by word of mouth, allowing his restaurant to expand its clientele and eventually win two stars. He also expanded his business to other countries and opened three restaurants in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Bangkok. Moreover, he is planning to open another restaurant in China in 2021. “I want to eliminate the negative impression of Japanese sushi restaurants, such as being too highbrow, and adopt positive aspects of other restaurants,” he says. While his sushi respects tradition and focuses on classic flavors, playful side dishes served between each piece of sushi have been created to surprise and delight diners. For example, he offers dishes with flavored oil, such as Clams with Butterbur Flower Bud Flavored Oil, and uses French culinary techniques, as exemplified by a dish of sea urchin gougères. His experience in running restaurants abroad is what made him realize that what matters most is his guests’ enjoyment and overall dining experience. The drinks menu has also been carefully curated by the chef to complement the flavors of each dish, including a Bourgogne-leaning selection of wines, as well as Kistler white wines from California and Japanese sake such as Hoken from Hiroshima and Mimurosugi from Nara. Guests can also ask the chef to select drinks for them. Inside the restaurant, the eight-seat counter made of solid cypress wood welcomes guests. The Japanese-style interior is adorned with low chairs imported from a famous foreign brand to lift the room and guests’ spirits. Diners are invited to enjoy chef Nakanoue’s exquisite and exciting sushi with family, partner, friends, or colleagues at Sushiyoshi, which offers never-ending excitement. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 5-minutes walk from Minamimorimachi Station on Tanimachi Line of Osaka Metro Sakaisuji Line

244075.longDescription:
The restaurant was founded by the first generation in Nishitemma, 1947. Koji Azuma, the third generation, trained for 6 years in Akasaka’s Ishingo and 6 years as head chef in  Shinbashi’s Bifun Azuma, after which he opened Chi-Fu in 2012. The name of the restaurant is derived from Chinois-Fumé (the fragrance of China) and Chinois-Futurism (the future of China), to make Chi-Fu. Chef Azuma takes traditional Chinese cuisine inherited from his grandfather and father, and leads us onto a new stage with innovative cooking techniques.

For example, in the hands of the chef, fó tiào quiáng (a type of shark fin soup) – a luxurious soup which uses dashi (soup stock) from top quality dried seafood – becomes a dish which replaces dried seafood with ingredients from the mountains such as Jinhua Chinese ham, shiitake mushrooms and soft-shelled turtle wrapped in wonton, with popular ingredients like beef tendon and dried sour plum. These adventurous dishes are only possible because the chef has properly studied the ABCs of Chinese cuisine passed down from ancient times.

They have 3,000 bottles of wine in the cellar, which is said to be No.1 in Kansai area. One of the enjoyments is the harmony of wine with as much history as the Chinese cuisine, selected by a sommelier. The simple and modern interior of the restaurant exudes a sophisticated atmosphere. This is where you would want to bring that important someone for a meal.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.

*Please note that Hyotei only accept breakfast reservation through hotel's concierge, you may contact your accommodation for details.

244595.longDescription:
Located 10 minutes on foot from Osaka's Sakai Station, the famous sushi shop "Yasuke" is known as the longstanding number-one place for sushi in Sakai. Across from it stands the unassuming building that is home to Sushi Oga. Its owner, Mr. Shinichiro Ohga, has the distinction of being a fourth-generation sushi chef at "Yasuke". After 3 years at "Yasuke," he honed his skills for 10 years at Japanese restaurants before deciding to create his own sushi and opening "Sushi Ohga" in 2018.

At Yasuke, each type of sushi is made with one of 2 varieties of vinegared rice, but Mr. Ohga opted to redesign everything from scratch, entering the ring with a single type of vinegared rice featuring a blend of three different red kinds of vinegar. The pursuit of further heights of flavor while standing on the shoulders of tradition is the essence of Mr. Ohga's craftsmanship. In addition, the sushi topping given center stage by Mr. Ohga is tuna, a rare thing in Japan's western region. He sources a wide variety of carefully-selected ingredients from Yamasachi, a Toyosu (formerly Tsukiji) sushi ingredient supplier counting famous Edomae-style sushi shops among its clients. When particularly high-quality ingredients are available, he even features a seven-part tuna course menu, with each course offering different cuts. He also pursues top quality in his renditions of western Japan's essential whitefish sushi dishes, sourcing ingredients directly from places such as Osaka's Honan Market and Awaji and carefully working them to draw out the maximum amount of flavor. Also, fun is the different and innovative side dishes, created using his experience working at Japanese restaurants, such as Awaji whitefish rolled with pickled sea cucumber ovaries. The venue also gives its guests a visual treat, with antique tableware, such as that of Rosanjin, used everywhere. The selection of Japanese sake features some 10 always-available varieties in addition to seasonal offerings and is centered around select dry and junmai varieties to best complement the sushi.

The relaxed interior features a single counter of Japanese cypress. With only eight seats available in total, it is easy for guests to watch the master at work. In addition to regulars from "Yasuke," there are also many guests who have been attracted directly by Sushi Ohga's new charm. Guests are sure to want to return to keep tasting the continuously-evolving sushi of Mr. Ohga, with his earnest attitude that "sushi is for anyone and everyone who enjoys it."

244634.longDescription:
“Sushi Ikegami,” a hidden gem in the town, is a 3-minute walk from JR Senrioka Station in Settsu City, Osaka Prefecture. The chef, Hidesato Ikegami, is dedicated to Edomae-style sushi.

While still studying at university, chef Ikegami opened a sushi restaurant called “Sushi Restaurant Maruike.” At first, nori and sushi toppings were given to customers and served as temaki (hand-rolled sushi). Later, he learned the art of Edomae-style sushi while washing dishes at a Japanese restaurant on his days off. After three years, he finally became able to make sushi, attracting more customers to the restaurant. Building on that, he helped with food preparation on his days off at a famous restaurant in Kitashinchi. In 2016, the restaurant was renovated and re-opened as “Sushi Ikegami.” Hidesato Ikegami is a chef who has worked hard to achieve the style of restaurant he envisioned after 17 years in the business. For the food, the Omakase course is available by reservation only. The finest fish is delivered directly from the fishing port or purchased from Toyosu Fish Market (previously, Tsukiji Fish Market), and is dipped in salt or vinegar, or left to rest in order to bring out the best flavor. The sushi rice is made with a blend of red vinegar and rice vinegar. The restaurant is particular about matching the temperature between the sushi ingredients and the vinegared rice. To achieve this, the chef uses an icebox refrigerator that does not use electricity, to keep the sushi ingredients from getting too cold.

The centerpiece of the drink menu is local sake. The restaurant serves about 30 kinds of sake to match the food. There are also 10 different kinds of champagne, available by bottle and by the glass. The stylish point of the restaurant Chef Ikegami says, is that you can casually enjoy “Dom Pérignon” at an exceptionally reasonable price. There are only seven seats at the 300 year-old Kiso cypress counter. Guests will want to spend special occasions with friends, colleagues, family, foreign guests and other important people here, enjoying the Edomae-style sushi that is carefully prepared.

244796.longDescription:
“Japanese Cuisine KASHIWAYA” is a 5-minute drive from the west exit of Senriyama Station in Osaka and an 8-minute walk from Kandaimae Station. You will be fascinated by the beauty of the Sukiya-zukuri style exterior and the magnificent decorative frame. When you step into the house with a magnificent gate, you will feel a calm and extraordinary atmosphere.

The owner is Hideaki Matsuo. Originally, “KASHIWAYA” was opened by Matsuo's father about 40 years ago. Owner Matsuo, who studied theoretical physics at university, first encountered the tea ceremony when he was a student. After graduation, he trained at "Shofukuro", a long-established Japanese restaurant in Shiga. At here, he learns how to think about the food for each guest, and the delicate hospitality of the room arrangement and tools.

You can enjoy local cuisine that has been made since the restaurant opened in each of the four seasons. For example, "Shrimp salt-grilled tilefish" is a winter specialty where you can enjoy the smell of shrimp by the shrimp salt before grilling. Also, the "Tender steamed Ise lobster", which is seasoned only with kelp and salt, is made by steaming and frying the whole body of Ise lobster for a long time, and making it into a boiled and seasoned soup. The monthly menu with a seasonal feel is popular among regular customers. There are various drinks from, shochu to wine. The sommelier Masahiro Matsuoka has worked for a long time at a French restaurant, and selects Japanese sake and wine pairing.

The restaurant was designed by Toshinori Nakamura, a master of sukiya architecture. There are 7 private rooms (2 ~ 30 people) with different atmospheres, including tea room. Each of them is made of Japanese paper dyed by Yoshioka Yukio, a famous dyer in Kyoto. There is an English menu for foreign guests and English service is also available. You can enjoy the view of the garden with tatami room, tea room, the moss and the trees. From the time you enter the entrance to the time you leave, the seasonal scenery will make you excited. We hope you will experience the essence of Japanese hospitality in “KASHIWAYA”.


* Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2024.
nearestStations: A 8-minute walk from Kandaimae Station (Hankyu Senri Line)

245049.longDescription:
The upscale neighborhood of Kitashinchi in Osaka is dense with nationally renowned restaurants. Among them, LES SOUVENIRS, an acclaimed French establishment, is conveniently situated a short 10-minute walk from both Osaka and Umeda stations.

Chef Daisuke Kaneko has been engaged in Chef Yasushi Karato who is the owner of Lumiere, which has been awarded a star in the world's gourmet guide over the past nine times. After working on LIAISON, he became a chef at LES SOUVENIRS. Although young, it is an artful dish with solid technique and airiness.The restaurant gained immense popularity among food connoisseurs immediately after it opened in October 2020.

LES SOUVENIRS offers innovative fusion cuisine grounded in French culinary techniques and complemented by a variety of other cooking techniques and ingredients. The restaurant’s name means “memories” in French and reflects its commitment to offering food that is not only delicious but also unforgettable, with warm hospitality, to create fond memories for guests.

The vegetables and fish are selected with extra care from all over Japan to ensure the best quality available. The meat is selected even more carefully as it is prominently featured on the menu, which offers a choice of three meat dishes: Matsusaka beef from Mie, Nanatani duck from Kyoto, and Sheep "Lamb or Hoget" by Sakai from Shiranuka-cho, Hokkaido Sheep Research Institute.

The wine list offers a selection of 80 reds and 80 whites, mainly from France, as well as from Japan, Italy, and the United States. There are also two options of sake brewed with wine yeast. In addition, a wide selection of hard liquors is offered to be enjoyed leisurely with cheese from Fromage-Sen in Chiba after meals. The restaurant also offers food and drink pairings that are curated by the sommelier to create perfect harmony with the restaurant’s innovative French cuisine. For guests avoiding liquor, you can order from the carefully selected soft drink menu, including "Ringomichi" of Mukai Shoten in Aomori and "Gyokuto" of Uji Gyokuro in Kyoto and Bottlegreen, a cordial flavored with herbs and fruit juices.

The moodily lit entrance hall leads to a carpeted dining room adorned by brown shades for a touch of solidity and tranquility.

With carefully curated first-class tableware ordered from famous Japanese designers, LES SOUVENIRS is perfect for business dinners and intimate meals with a partner, friends, and fellow lovers of French cuisine. Guests are invited to enjoy unforgettable, innovative French dishes at this exquisite restaurant.

244210.longDescription: "Kitashinchi" which is said to be a fancy restaurant district alongside Ginza in Tokyo, in Kita, which is Osaka’s leading downtown area around Osaka・Umeda station. On the 3rd floor of a street building crowded with various shops, 7 minutes walk from the station, there is the Edo Sushi restaurant "Sushi Hoshiyama" quietly located with the orthodox store arrangement. It is loved by repeat customers because they can enjoy "Highroad hand-formed sushi" which is quite few in Kansai area and has won one star. The owner-chef Mr. Tadashi Hoshiyama had been training for 7 years at "Tsukiji sushi Kiyoshi Kyoto" and 5 years at “Sushi Matsumoto” which has won one star, the only one in Kyoto. He started the restaurant in his hometown, saying “Kitashinchi is the best in Osaka.”, and he won one star the following year. The owner-chef of "Sushi Matsumoto" comes from a famous restaurant "Shinbashi Shimizu" in Tokyo Shimbashi, Mr. Hoshiyama is his follower, so he provides the genuine Edomae-style sushi with the impressive effect of red vinegar in Osaka. The specialty is “Nigiri” which put together tasty Sushi rice with red vinegar made with only sake less and salt and Sushi topping that is paid a lot of attention from purchasing and cooked very carefully. It's an orthodox style with no creation, but that's why you can enjoy "Highroad Edomae sushi". Sushi rice with special vinegar match tuna and Kohada, although white fish with marinated kelp that is condensed of good flavor, and a natural prawn that puts out good flavor and sweetness by boiling are also good to feel sushi chef’s craftsmanship of use of red vinegar. The inside of the restaurant is only 8 counter seats with plain wood that was well-prepared.You can also enjoy 7-8 kinds of sake by seasons with baccarat antique glasses. A calm space where the eyes of the owner-chef warm-up is a "hideout" loved by sushi chef of the same profession. It is good to go with someone special, or even alone. It is a famous restaurant where you can enjoy the best moment. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customization on our course offers or offer a la carte option. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? We do not have a dress code.

244541.longDescription:
Located a 5-minute walk from JR Sakuranomiya Station. "Hinabe Mita Seito" is a Chinese cuisine restaurant specializing in a hot pot which opened beside the Okawa River in Osaka in 2018. 

The hot pot has various soup recipes in China which is said to be the birthplace. While praying for the eternal youth and longevity of the important guests visiting from all over the world, it has been continued to follow the recipe, which was said to have been created through extensive research and the use of rare and difficult-to-obtain spices that were served at state guesthouses in China. The hot pot is made with more than 25 kinds of spices imported from China, including Chinese ginseng, Chinese pepper, and goji berries, and has been elevated to a dish that is recognized by gourmets.

“Hinabe Mita” is the one which has been inherited this precious historic taste. They offer selected fresh seasonal ingredients from all over Japan every month. Shaoxing wine and wines, which feature a rich aroma developed over 10 years of aging, along with a smooth and mellow taste, are favored in hot pot.

The chic and relaxed interior is all semi-private seating. It can flexibly accommodate parties from 4 to 14 people by rearranging the blinds used as partitions, so it is perfect for group functions like welcoming and retirement parties. Hotpot is eaten with authentic Sichuan mala soup and herbal chicken soup also has detoxifying and beautifying effects, so it is recommended for groups of family and friends.

245488.longDescription:
A seven-minute walk from either Tanimachi 6-chome or 9-chome Station, Yakitori Matsuoka is secluded from the hustle and bustle of Osaka.  Helmed by Chef Hiroki Matsuoka, the restaurant offers exquisite chicken skewers and chicken dishes featuring his recommended Black Satsuma Chicken Kuro-O from Kagoshima.

Chef Matsuoka first learned cooking as a young child from his parents, who ran a Japanese restaurant. Then, with an eye toward opening his own restaurant one day, he learned different culinary techniques, and he was captivated by charcoal grill cuisine when training at a charcoal grill restaurant. In 2013, he went abroad to extend his horizons, and he honed his culinary skills for four years at chicken skewer restaurants in Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.  After returning to Japan, he opened Yakitori Matsuoka in February 2023. His elaborate chicken skewers and chicken dishes caused an instant sensation, and his restaurant made it into a world-renowned restaurant guide for 2024 in just one year of its opening.

Featured as a signature of Yakitori Matsuoka, the Black Satsuma Chicken Kuro-O is a Kagoshima-native breed which Chef Matsuoka encountered while looking around Japan for the best chicken. It is raised with utmost care in a natural, cage-free environment for 150 days, until the meat reaches its pinnacle. Characterized by its chewy texture and rich flavor, the chicken tastes sweeter as you chew it. At Yakitori Matsuoka, every part of this precious chicken is used, including dark meat, tails, hearts, and other organs. They are placed onto skewers and grilled over Kishu Binchotan Charcoal from Wakayama with a pinch of high-quality salt. The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu consists of about 20 dishes, including chicken skewers and chicken dishes. In particular, the 10-hour boiled chicken soup, the chicken tataki lightly grilled to bring out the chewy texture and rich flavor of Kuro-O, and the ramen that guests can choose to add to their meals are highly appreciated. The drink menu offers an exquisite selection of premium sake, such as Juyondai from Yamagata and Aramasa from Akita, and quality wines and whiskeys to meet the preferences of guests.

The restaurant is lively, with an L-shaped, nine-seat counter where guests can witness the chef’s grilling magic up close. The painting on the wall and the beautiful flowers behind the grill station add a dynamic touch to the dining room. The prix-fixe meals prepared by the chef with an extensive international background are highly recommended for those seeking to entertain guests not only from Japan but also from other part of the world.
nearestStations: Approximately a 7-minute walk from Osaka subway stations Tanimachi 6-chome, Tanimachi 9-chome, Kintetsu Osaka Uehonmachi.

244838.longDescription:
Shunsaiten Tsuchiya, renovated from an atmospheric old house in a tranquil residential area, can be found an eight-minute walk from Esaka Station in Suita, Osaka Prefecture. The restaurant was opened in July 2008 by chef-owner Yukihiko Tsuchisaka, who honed his culinary skills at several renowned Japanese restaurants for years, and offers dishes that demonstrate harmony between Japanese cuisine and tempura. Awarded two stars in a world-renowned restaurant guide, the restaurant attracts many guests both within Japan and from abroad.

The restaurant’s name “Shunsaiten” reflects the chef’s commitment to delivering “graceful tempura featuring seasonal ingredients.” The multi-course menu of the chef’s choice combines the delicate seasonal flavors of Japanese cuisine and the robust flavors of tempura to create a unique dining experience found only at the restaurant.

With the belief that the ingredients should be purchased every morning, managed, and cooked by the chef himself, Tsuchisaka purchases the best ingredients from around Japan, including vegetables from local farmers and locally caught fresh fish and shellfish. The tempura is deep-fried using cottonseed oil, an oil that imbues dishes with powerful umami and sweet flavors, and extracted exclusively by Okamura Oil Mill in Kashiwara, Osaka Prefecture, to highlight the flavors of ingredients. 

In order to clarify the characteristics of each ingredient, they are carefully checked, coated with batters of varying thicknesses and water content, and deep-fried at different temperatures for different lengths of time, depending on the cut shape and thickness of the ingredient. Also, the way the tempura is cooked and the temperature it is served at are different, depending on the season. The flavors of elaborately made tempura are further accented by three kinds of dipping salt: rock salt, offering simple saltiness, seaweed salt with a robust umami flavor, and bay salt that blends well with a diverse array of flavors.

The wine list includes 50 to 60 wines, mainly from Europe, the New World, and Japan, as well as a wide selection of wines by the glass. Guests can taste and select wines for their meals. The drinks menu also offers some 20 labels of Japanese sake, sourced from around Japan, but mainly from the Kansai and Kinki regions. Homemade nonalcoholic cocktails and thick grape juice are also recommended.

The restaurant’s exterior is black and white with stucco walls and a tiled roof, reminiscent of a traditional Japanese storehouse. In contrast, the interior is lined with plain wood in natural shades and brown-colored timber to add warmth. The restaurant has a private room with a dining table (seating up to four guests), as well as a counter with 12 seats to allow guests to sit and watch the chef skillfully deep-fry tempura right in front of them. The tableware that gives a feeling of the season is crafted by contemporary artists. 

Guests are invited to enjoy a wonderful dining experience at Shunsaiten Tsuchiya, a perfect place for a girls’ night out, dinners with colleagues, date nights, and meals with friends from overseas.

245510.longDescription:
A seven-minute walk from Temmabashi Station amidst the hustle and bustle of Osaka City, Sushi Hiramatsu is perched on the third floor of a building in Tsuriganecho, named after its symbol, a hanging bell cast as a tribute to Iemitsu, the third Shogun of the Tokugawa Shogunate (hanging bell is “tsurigane” in Japanese).  The restaurant is helmed by Chef Eikichi Hiramatsu, who worked many years at Sakagura Nakayama, a Japanese liquor store, where he amassed a knowledge of Japanese sake, and then trained and mastered the art of sushi at one of the most popular sushi restaurants in Osaka. He continued to work there as Branch Head Chef but eventually opened his own restaurant, Sushi Hiramatsu.  

The fish is sourced from carefully selected suppliers. For example, the common Edomae sushi toppings, such as bluefin tuna, bonito, and gizzard shad, are all transported by air from Toyosu Market, and the white fish for which the Akashi Strait is famous, such as sea bream, Japanese whiting, and squid, is purchased from a fishmonger’s shop in Kobe and turned into Edomae sushi toppings by the Kansai-born chef.  The sushi rice made of Yukiwakamaru, a premium brand rice from Yamagata, comes in three different flavors for different toppings. The white sushi rice for white fish with a mild acidity, a hint of salt, and a natural, sugar-free sweetness is matched up with delicately flavored white fish. The white sushi rice for gizzard shad is specially invented for gizzard shad but actually versatile and compatible with various other fishes, such as medium fatty bluefin tuna, prawn, horse mackerel, and bonito. The rosé sushi rice is mainly seasoned with red vinegar and salt to bring out the best flavors in the richly flavored toppings, such as blackthroat seaperch, sea urchin, conger eel, and clam.
 
The chef’s choice dinner features five small dishes and 10 pieces of nigiri sushi, followed by a Japanese-style omelet, soup, and desserts. Among them, the dry-aged bluefin tuna sushi, made of carefully selected bluefin tuna from Toyosu Market, is the chef’s signature dish, while the gizzard shad sushi, for which the gizzard shad is desalted at an incredibly slow pace, is the chef’s pride that tickles the taste buds of sushi lovers. The prawn sushi is also very popular for its rich flavor enhanced by boiling the prawns in a broth made from their shells. 

Sushi Hiramatsu offers an excellent selection of sake, curated by the chef based on his extensive experience and deep knowledge of sake. The restaurant always stores 20-odd varieties of sake, including Sohomare from Tochigi, Asahikiku from Fukuoka, Kakurei from Niigata, Koganesawa from Miyagi, Yamagata Masamune from Yamagata, Tenon from Shimane, and Kikuhime from Ishikawa, each served in glasses specially designed to unlock their flavors and aromas as intended by the chef. If you are not sure which sake to go with your food, you can ask the chef to choose for you.

Designed after a traditional Japanese-style house, the dining area is cozy with a comfortable counter (seating up to seven guests), as well as oil-filled electric heaters to keep the feet warm in winter.  The Osaka-style Edomae sushi crafted with heart and soul by Chef Hiramatsu makes any occasion unforgettable – whether it is personal or professional.

245460.longDescription:
Located five minutes on foot from Tanimachi Kyuchome Station or Osaka-Uehommachi Station, Teruya, a Japanese restaurant, is situated in a quiet residential area off one of the busiest shopping streets in Osaka and run by Chef Katsunori Teruya together with the proprietress.

Trained in renowned restaurants in Kyoto, such as Kenninji Gion Maruyama, Iida, and Nihon-ryori Sakuragawa, Chef Teruya opened his own restaurant, Teruya, in 2018 to entertain guests with high-end Japanese dishes reinterpreted in his own style. The location was selected so that guests could enjoy the simple dishes that celebrate the natural flavors of ingredients in a quiet setting, away from the hustle and bustle.

The ingredients are sourced from suppliers in Kyoto with whom the chef has maintained strong ties since his apprenticeship or are purchased at a local market where he goes every morning to choose the best ingredients of the day, regardless of the brand or origin. The dashi stock, the essence of Japanese cuisine, is made by slowly simmering Japanese kelp sourced from Hokkaido. The monthly prix fixe menu offers eight- to 10-course meals, starting with appetizers and ending with desserts. The moderate seasoning of the dishes keeps guests from tiring of them. Many diners also comment that Teruya’s dishes do not sit heavy in the stomach the next morning.

The elegant and sleek flavors of the multi-course meals taste even better when accented by the chef’s choice of Japanese sake. In fact, Chef Teruya prepares each dish while considering which sake pairs best with it, and many guests leave the sake pairing to him.

In front of the restaurant, a small alley leads you to the entrance, which is reminiscent of a kappo restaurant in Kyoto. Open the entrance door and you will find yourself immersed in the universe of Teruya. The dining area with an L-shaped, seven-seat counter is stylish like a museum, boasting a wide collection of tableware and sake vessels, ranging from antiques to modern crafts. They are engraved with memories of Chef Teruya. For example, the Sprinkle-lacquered Bowls with Seven Autumn Flowers were purchased when he visited an antique shop for the first time in his life. Though he just tagged along with his senior fellow apprentice to the shop, he soon developed an interest in tableware and dreamed of opening his own restaurant. His dream has come true, and his restaurant has now become popular for various occasions, such as family gatherings, socializing with friends and coworkers, and date nights. The culinary journey of seasonal flavors offered at the restaurant may make you feel like you are deciphering a record of seasonal customs.

245043.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of the Ritz-Carlton, Osaka, the luxury hotel group’s first hotel in Japan, Splendido.

The ingredients are sourced mainly from the Kinki region, including Kumano Jidori chicken from Wakayama, as well as fresh fish and vegetables. Some specialty ingredients, such as a pistachio olive oil used for carpaccio and Buryat cheese, are imported directly from Italy.

Upon entering the dining room, guests are immediately greeted by the sight of an impressive pizza oven in the restaurant’s open kitchen., and authentic Neapolitan pizzas baked in the oven’s roaring flame are particularly popular. Splendido Pizza, named after the restaurant and characterized by its soft crust with plenty of prosciutto and arugula seasoned with truffle oil, enjoys the greatest popularity for its rich flavor.

The Italian-leaning wine list offers a wide selection of wines, including white Pinot Grigio and Ornellaia Bianco, red Chianti Classico and Amarone, and Franciacorta.

Designed after the concept of Splendid (a stylish Tuscan villa), the restaurant consists of three distinct spaces; an elegant main dining room with luxurious red carpet, chandeliers, and decorative artworks. Meanwhile, a marble floored terrace is the perfect place to relax, overlooking flowers and trees in the garden. Last but not least, a former wine bar has been renovated into an intimate dining room, covered with a wood floor to create a homey ambience.

The restaurant offers flexible seating arrangements to suit any occasion, attracting families with children to enjoy pizzas and pastas.

Suitable for various occasions, Splendido is the perfect place to enjoy authentic Italian flavors with family, a partner, friends, or colleagues.

245042.longDescription:
Perched on the fifth floor of the Ritz-Carlton, Osaka, which was opened by the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company as its first hotel in Japan, Xiang Tao serves a fusion of traditional and modern Cantonese cuisine with expertly selected Chinese tea.

Xiang Tao features Cantonese-based Chinese cuisine, mainly offering seafood dishes that highlight ingredients such as dried abalone and fish. The restaurant’s produce is mostly sourced within Japan, such as leopard coral trout from Okinawa, Japanese spiny lobsters, and abalone, but some dried seafood is also imported from China and Hong Kong. The sous chef’s specialty, bird’s nest in egg white with caviar, features swallow's nests from Hong Kong and caviar from France, Russia, or varieties at their seasonal peak. This specialty dish is seasoned simply to enhance the texture of the bird’s nest and the flavor of the caviar. Another popular menu is Peking duck with miso sauce.

At Xiang Tao, three sommeliers are always on-hand to suggest the perfect pairing of food and wine. The restaurant also offers a selection of Shaoxing wines, including exclusive 40-year old pots and 10, 50, and 100 year old bottles. Moreover, A Chinese tea experts, Junya Oda, licensed as Tea Art Specialists and Tea Tasting Specialists, are on hand to assist guests in not only select Chinese tea, but also serve it in a traditional way that befits its artistic heritage.

Designed to represent the Peach Blossom Shangri-La of modern times, each dining room is crowned with pink ceilings to allow diners to feel as if they were feasting beneath peach blossoms. One of the walls is adorned with abstract ceramic mosaic art in different colors, including pink and green shades reminiscent of peach flowers and leaves, to add a modern twist. The rooms are bright by day, filled with plenty of sunlight through the large windows overlooking the courtyard, and lit up romantically at night. The courtyard is also open to diners, depending on the season.

With four private rooms as well as a gallery space to explore artworks, Xiang Tao is the perfect place to enjoy Chinese dishes with family, a partner, friends, or colleagues in beautiful surroundings.

243925.longDescription: The Osaka location of the world-renowned Wolfgang’s Steakhouse is situated on the tenth floor of the commercial complex LUCUA 1100, directly connected to Osaka Station and a five-minute walk from Umeda Station. Since its start in the United States in 2004, Wolfgang’s Steakhouse has captivated countless fans and expanded rapidly. After opening locations abroad, the Osaka restaurant became the brand’s third in Japan when it debuted in 2015. Founder Wolfgang Zwiener, originally a renowned waiter who worked for over 40 years at a prestigious New York steakhouse, has long prioritized the joy of his guests. This philosophy is reflected not only in the uncompromising quality of the meat but also in the attentive service and the extensive menu offerings. The restaurant’s greatest pride—the steak—is defined by its dedication to quality, aging, and preparation. Only rare USDA Prime Grade beef, the highest grade awarded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, is selected and then dry-aged for about 28 days in a specialized aging room with strictly controlled temperature and humidity. The meat is seared at an intense 900°C, creating a beautifully crisp crust while keeping the interior tender and bursting with savory juices. Thick cuts highlight the concentrated flavor of the aged beef, filling the mouth with pure bliss. The signature dish is the Prime Steak (T-bone steak), allowing guests to enjoy both the sirloin and filet in a single cut. Classic accompaniments such as mashed potatoes and creamed spinach pair exceptionally well, and the extensive selection of appetizers and side dishes ensures that every guest can tailor their experience. More than 1,000 bottles of wine from around the world are available, making the restaurant a wonderful destination for wine lovers as well. Inside the spacious dining room, guests will find 90 tables, 12 counter seats, and a private dining room for up to 14 guests. The chic interior, accented with dark brown tones and warm lighting, creates an elegant yet relaxing atmosphere—an ideal setting for enjoying exceptional steaks. With its rare Prime Grade aged beef, diverse wine offerings, and wide array of side dishes, Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Osaka is perfect for dates, gatherings with friends, wine events, and a variety of special occasions. 〈Group Restaurant Information〉 Wolfgang's Steakhouse Signature Aoyama Wolfgang's Steakhouse Roppongi Wolfgang's Steakhouse Fukuoka Wolfgang’s Steakhouse TEPPAN Wolfgang's Steakhouse Marunouchi Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa

245064.longDescription:
XEX WEST, a sophisticated restaurant for socializing, is perched on the seventh floor of Herbis Ent, a commercial complex directly connected to Osaka Station. The restaurant reopened after a renovation in January 2014, with a luxurious space of some 1,300 square meters, including an open terrace with breathtaking views of Osaka’s cityscape and three loosely connected sections that respectively offer Italian cuisine, Japanese cuisine, and bar fare.

At Salvatore Cuomo Bros, Italian cuisine is presented by the world-renowned Salvatore Cuomo Group, offering authentic Neapolitan pizzas as well as premium steaks cooked in a Josper charcoal oven. This chic Italian restaurant also has a prosciutto cellar, a champagne cellar, and a chocolate shop renowned as the only place to sell the acclaimed Le Chocolat de H, crafted by pastry chef Hironobu Tsujiguchi in the Kansai Region. In the Japanese section, aburiyaki & sushi An offers traditional Japanese dishes and Edomae sushi featuring seasonal ingredients. In addition to beloved styles like sukiyaki and shabushabu, the restaurant also offers an à la carte menu with a wide range of dishes, including tempura.

The third section, The Bar, is spacious, with approximately 140 indoor and outdoor terrace seats and live performances by international musical acts. The drinks menu offers a wide selection of tipples, including 200 wines, cognacs, whiskies, and precious Japanese sake.

The interior features distinct designs for each of the three sections. The Italian section offers 110 seats, all at tables; the Japanese section has 12 seats at the counter and 14 table seats; and the bar section offers 140 seats (including 40 outdoor terrace seats). 

Guests are invited to enjoy authentic dishes prepared by talented chefs and excellent hospitality by attentive staff, and to enjoy an extraordinary, romantic experience in stylish settings at XEX WEST while dining with a partner or friends.

245118.longDescription:
Syouroku is a Naniwa kappo (Osaka-style) restaurant located near Utsubo Park, just a 5-minute walk from Hommachi Station in the business district of Osaka. The restaurant was opened in March 2019 by chef Masato Shimoda, who had started his culinary training at a Kyoto cuisine restaurant and further honed his skills at other restaurants including Gensai in Kobe. Kigawa Syouroku (closed),  has been loved by many guests for 33 years, and after a change, Masato fascinates them with his father's craftsmanship.

 As per the saying that “Kyoto cuisine highlights the natural flavors of the ingredients, and Naniwa cuisine delights the palates of diners,” Syouroku explores how to excite his guests’ palates from the first to the last bite.
The menu is characterized by highlighting the natural taste of ingredients, such as the bitterness and sweetness of vegetables, to create flavorful dishes, rather than relying on heavy seasonings. Ingredients are carefully selected by the chef himself, who visits markets daily to gather seasonal local vegetables, such as bamboo shoots from Kishiwada and young burdocks from Yao, and purchases locally caught fish and shellfish. The restaurant’s specialty is the original Crab Cream Croquette that the chef developed by learning from his father about the Japanese-style croquette of Kigawa. It is popular among the restaurant’s regulars for its thick white sauce in an abalone shell singing with the rich flavors of fish and shellfish, accented by the original sauce and crispy exterior. The drink menu always offers six labels of precious sake, carefully selected by the chef from across Japan.
Featuring a pure Japanese design with a hint of modernity, the restaurant places guests at a counter crafted from Japanese horse chestnut with seven seats on the first floor, and a private dining room with a low horigotatsu table (table over a hole in the floor) that seats up to 10 guests on the second floor. 

The restaurant is a perfect setting for various occasions, such as business dinners, date nights, anniversaries, solo meals, and intimate family gatherings with children.
Guests are invited to savor the palate-tingling dishes of Naniwa in a friendly, relaxing atmosphere typical to Osaka at Syouroku, where the refined culinary techniques of the innovative cooking skills of chef is on full display.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Kyoto-Osaka 2023.
nearestStations: A 5-minutes walk from Honmachi Station exit 28, the Osaka Municipal Subway Yotsubashi Line

Reservation Information
We accept waiting list reservations only for bookings several weeks in advance. Although there may be dates with availability, they are not shown on the calendar. Please first register your preferred date on the wait list. Dates shown in gray indicate that registration for the wait list is available. Please check this page for details about how the wait list system works. Kindly note that this system allows us to contact you only if a seat becomes available on your selected date, and priority will be given in order of registration. As all guests start at the same time, the only available reception time is 5:00 PM. Once your reservation is confirmed, you will receive a confirmation email. If you do not see the email by the waiting deadline, please check your Reservations. -- A 40-minute drive from Saga Airport or a 10-minute drive from Hizen-Kashima Station takes you to Hizen Hamashuku, a charming historical district in Kashima City, Saga Prefecture. The place is home to Onyado Fukuchiyo Souan Nabeshima. Onyado Fukuchiyo Souan Nabeshima opened its doors in spring 2021 as the first sake brewery auberge in Japan. As the name shows, this auberge is run by Fukuchiyo Sake Brewery, which is known for Japanese sake “Nabeshima,” with a desire to create drinking opportunities for sake lovers to delve into the secrets and values of sake and enjoy the remarkable marriage of Japanese sake, food, and tableware. Overnight guests at the auberge can also enjoy the profound world of Japanese sake through a brewery tour guided by the brewmaster or brewers to visit places that are usually closed to the public and hear intriguing stories from brewers. The restaurant is helmed by Chef Takuma Nishimura, who trained at Kagurazaka Ishikawa, a three-star restaurant, in Tokyo and then returned to his hometown of Fukuoka to further hone his culinary skills at the one-star Restaurant Sola. When Onyado Fukuchiyo Souan Nabeshima opened in March 2021, he was offered the position of Chef at the restaurant because of his passion and perfection in cookery. The 12-course menu curated by Chef Nishimura features selective ingredients not only from Saga Prefecture but also from all the other prefectures in Kyushu. Other menus also feature local ingredients throughout the four seasons, mostly from devoted producers around Kyushu who have personal ties with Chef Nishimura. The chef-selected menu changes every one and a half months, along with the paired sake menu that features different varieties of Nabeshima. The drink menu is built around Japanese sake. All the seven varieties of Nabeshima, selected from 26 to 27 varieties to make the menu of the month, go well with the dishes. Exclusive varieties of Nabeshima which are not on the market are also available at this restaurant. The collection of tableware deserves special attention, including Arita ware and Karatsu ware crafted by renowned and young ceramic artists, historical old Karatsu ware and old Imari ware originated from Saga, and antique glassware from abroad. They are carefully selected to match the 230-year-old, traditional, elegant building with a thatched roof. The building is shared with an auberge called Onyado Fukuchiyo. It is worth visiting with your friends, family, partner, or coworkers. Please enjoy Japanese sake “Nabeshima” along with delicious dishes and beautiful tableware to celebrate the bounty of Saga Prefecture.

244795.longDescription:
Karatsu City is located in the northern part of Saga Prefecture, facing the Genkai-nada Sea. “Hirata”, a 1-star Japanese restaurant, is quietly located near Karatsu Castle. Chef Tomohaya Hirata, sharpened his skills at famous Japanese restaurants including “Utsuwa Ryori Sano” in Fukuoka Prefecture and 2-star “Miyamaso” in Kyoto, and opened “Hirata” in 2016. It became a popular restaurant that received 1-star for its gentle and courteous cuisine and hospitality.

With an understanding of the tea ceremony, chef Hirata looks for local ingredients just like chakaiseki (tea-ceremony dishes), and completes his dishes with his own thoughts. He is particular about local production and local consumption of seafood and vegetables, and purchases them with his expert judgment. "As a town rich in seafood, not only the fish is delicious, but also the combination with seasonal vegetables which is easy to feel the season is appreciated by customers," chef Hirata said. There are 5 to 6 kinds of Japanese sake, mainly from the local area, as well as wine that goes well with Japanese cuisine. In addition, the homemade enzyme juice made by fermenting vegetables and fruits and other soft drinks are perfect for even non-alcoholic people.

The rounded ceiling and bright white walls create a comfortable interior. 7 seats at the counter and 4 tables are prepared, and the comfortable distance between the customer and the restaurant is considered. "Although the building is simple and not heavy, I would like you to feel the spirit of the tea ceremony that you can see from time to time, and enjoy a quiet and delicious time," chef Hirata said. Various dinnerware is used according to the season, including antiques bought by local artists of Karatsu ware, Kyoto, Kanazawa, etc., from his training period. While enjoying the calm atmosphere of Karatsu, you will want to enjoy a special time spent in “Hirata” with your family, friends and other important people.

Many gourmets from not only Japan, but also overseas would visit “Tokuyamazushi” in search of the taste of "Narezushi (fermented fish sushi)", which is only available here. Nagahama City, Shiga Prefecture is located at the north end of Lake Biwa on the shores of Lake Yogo. In this place, which blends in with the original landscape of Japan, chef Hiroaki Tokuyama welcomes guests with his daughter Mai and her husband Nayuta.

Born in Shiga Prefecture, chef Tokuyama trained at Kyoto's long-established restaurant “Kawashige” after graduating from high school. Later, when he was serving as a chef at a local auberge, he met Professor Takeo Koizumi of Tokyo University of Agriculture, known as Doctor of Fermentation. While chef Tokuyama was trying to do something about fermented food, which he had been watching his father making since his childhood, since it had begun to decline in recent years. As Professor Koizumi said to him, "The time of fermentation is coming", he made up his mind. Focusing on the local cuisine "Narezushi", after much trial and error he came up with a unique "Narezushi" that was easy to eat for many people. The reputation of its taste spread quickly, and in 2004, “Tokuyamazushi” became a popular local restaurant attracting gourmets from local and abroad. “Tokuyamazushi” is also supported by his right-hand man, Mr. Nayuta. While training at 1-star kappo “Gion Kawakami” in Kyoto, he met and married Ms. Mai, the eldest daughter of “Tokuyamazushi”. After that, he studied under his father-in-law, chef Tokuyama, and now he is the sous-chef. Ms. Mai also help with the cooking and service, the whole family supports “Tokuyamazushi”.

"Narezushi", which is fermented with fish, salt and cooked rice by lactic acid, is said to be the origin of sushi, with unique strong flavor. Chef Tokuyama broke the conventional concept and created his own unique way of fermentation to create a "narezushi unique to Tokuyamazushi", that gradually brings out the umami. The course consists of the famous "narezushi", wild edible plants from the mountains in the spring, eel and ayu in the summer, and wild game meat in the winter. The "Kuma-nabe", which appears from winter to May, is served in a secret soup recipe made with vinegared rice from narezushi by chef Tokuyama. In particular, when you enjoy it with the Szechuan pepper, which is only available for a short period from late April to early May, you can enjoy a special flavor that spreads out in the mouth, so reservations rush in at that time.

"We would like our customers who come all the way here to enjoy local produce for local consumption, that is, local ingredients grown within a few kilometers of the restaurant," chef Tokuyama said. As he has the fishery rights, he goes to lakes and rivers to catch pond smelt, carp and eel, catches wild game ducks and boars as much as they need, and grows vegetables in the fields. Wild vegetables are harvested at different locations on a periodic basis, and efforts are being made to protect the natural environment so that they can be preserved for future generations. "To cook deliciously without wasting ingredients harvested by oneself. A sense of responsibility for food has grown more than ever," Mr. Nayuta said.

For Japanese sake, only 4 kinds of Junmaishu of Tomita Shuzo "Shichihonsai", which is located in the next town within 10 minutes by car, are available. This is because the water that is used are same as the one used for sansai (wild vegetables), vegetables grown in their own garden, rice, fish from Lake Yogo, so it goes well with the food. This has been the same obsession since it opened. Wine is also special. The restaurant is so particular that they talked with a New Zealand maker and asked him to make an original Riseling that goes well with "narezushi of Tokuyamazushi". In addition, 10 kinds of champagne, red and white wine are prepared, mainly from Japan and France.

As the restaurant has a view of the lake, the dining room is made with lots of wood and has a natural feel. There are 4 private rooms (2 to 4 people and 6 to 8 people). “Tokuyamazushi” promises special time, special space, special taste and special hospitality at the lakeside of Lake Yogo in Shiga. Spend a relaxing time as an auberge with your family, friends, food lovers, or even on dates.

245156.longDescription:
A 15-minute walk from Nichihara Station on the JR Yamaguchi Line leading to Masuda Station facing the Sea of Japan transports guests to Mikadoya in Nichihara, Tsuwano Town, Kanoashi District, Shimane Prefecture. The long-established restaurant is run by third-generation owner Ichiro Yamane and frequented by gourmands from inside and outside the prefecture.

Beautiful views and delicious cooking that change from season to season brings the restaurant’s clientele back time and again. In particular, Mikadoya is famous in Japan for its seasonal multi-course menus. From mid-April to mid-May, the restaurant features a hotpot of Shimane Wagyu beef and hanazancho (flowers of mountain pepper). Later, from June to late September, the restaurant offers a multi-course meal of natural sweetfish. Likened to the lady of the mountain stream, the highest quality sweetfish that grows in the Takatsu River with clean water features in each course, including an entrée of sweetfish grilled with salt using a secret method, pickled entrails and roe of sweetfish, and sweetfish rice.

October comes with a multi-course meal of slightly roasted sweetfish with roe, which is only available for a few weeks of the year. A 150- to 250-gram sweetfish dense with roe is slowly roasted over charcoal to produce a rich flavor; guests can then eat the fish from the head. The dish is Mikadoya’s specialty, and cannot be found anywhere else. In addition, on request, the dish  can be served with matsutake mushrooms grilled over charcoal by the third-generation chef himself in front of guests. In September, a multi-course meal of natural turtles from the Takatsu River arrives at Mikadoya. Then, December starts with a multi-course meal of pufferfish from Yamaguchi to close the year-round journey of seasonal flavors through kaiseki-style dishes (a simple meal eaten before tea).

The drinks menu features mainly locally produced wines, such as Okuizumo Wine, and locally brewed Japanese sake for guests who travel all the way to Shimane. Among them, sweetfish sake made by soaking sweetfish in Uijin sake from a local brewery in Tsuwano is very popular, winning the hearts of many regular customers.

The building features an eye-catching roof tiled with sekishu gawara (clay roof tiles), recalling its history as a Japanese inn.

With private rooms on the second floor, Mikadoya is the perfect place to spend a relaxing time with a family, partner, friends, or colleagues while enjoying the seasonal flavors of the chef’s simple yet elaborate dishes.

245135.longDescription:
Almost everyone asked to recommend a renowned Japanese restaurant in Shizuoka mentions Cha Kaiseki Onjaku, located in Yaizu. 

The restaurant is quietly set in a residential area, about a 20-minute walk from JR Yaizu Station. Although the restaurant looks like an ordinary house from the outside, once guests pass through the gate with a nameplate that reads “Cha Kaiseki Onjaku” and a noren curtain, they will find themselves in a different world, with a garden path paved with steppingstones and an atmospheric Japanese-style house. 

The second-generation owner, Daigo Sugiyama, took over the restaurant from his father, who transformed it from a soba noodle shop run by his father to a cha-kaiseki restaurant (to offer multi-dish meals followed by tea ceremonies). Seeing his father running the cha-kaiseki restaurant for years, Sugiyama learned the art of tea as a high school student and naturally chose to pursue a career in Japanese cuisine. He spent six years in training at Wako in Mejiro, Tokyo, where his father had also trained, and then took over the restaurant from his father around 2016.

The word “Onjaku” is allegedly the origin of the word “kaiseki cuisine” in Japanese, but when used as the name of this restaurant, it means “heartwarming, happy dishes without elaborate presentation.” The food menu consists of dishes that are not ceremonious like typical cha-kaiseki dishes, but reflect the spirit of cha-kaiseki cuisine, allowing diners to enjoy local fish from Suruga Bay in Yaizu, Shizuoka, to their heart’s content. The fish is sourced from the nationally renowned Sasue Maeda Fish Shop, which has supplied fish to the restaurant since it was run by Sugiyama’s grandfather. The shop owner, Naoki Maeda, worked with Sugiyama to explore the best ways to offer the fish of Yaizu, and their cooperative efforts led to the birth of a dish of Red Snapper Grilled with Scales On, a specialty unique to the restaurant and offered year-round. Onjaku also offers a selection of Japanese sake, among which the renowned Isojiman from Yaizu and other local sakes particularly work well with the restaurant’s cuisine.

The modern interior with warm wood accents was designed by Japanese architect Yukio Hashimoto, known for designing The Peninsula Tokyo. The restaurant used to only have private rooms, but it was renovated in 2019 to add a dining space with a counter seating up to nine guests (or reserved for a group of ten guests) to allow guests to sit and watch the chef grill fish and vegetables in front of them. In addition, there are two private rooms including a tea ceremony room. Guests are invited to enjoy a heartwarming experience at Cha Kaiseki Onjaku, a restaurant worth a special trip.
nearestStations: A 20-minutes walk from Yaizu Station on the JR Tokaido Main Line

245364.longDescription:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
■Information from the restaurant■
New Japanese Cuisine Obune will be open as follows
Lunch: Wednesday through Sunday, Dinner: Tuesday through Sunday
We look forward to serving you.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A five-minute drive from Kikugawa Station or a 15-minute drive from Kakegawa Station will take you to Shin Nihonryouri Obune, located in a tranquil residential neighborhood in Shizuoka Prefecture. Take a step inside and you will be welcomed by Chef Kazuki Takagi with a warm, friendly smile.

Hailing locally from Kikugawa, Takagi apprenticed at Kappo Ohana in Shimizu City, Shizuoka Prefecture, for three years from the age of 15 and then moved to Tokyo to further hone his culinary skills at Washoku Esquire Club’s locations in Sumitomo Building and Aoyama. Subsequently, he worked at Kyuyutei, a long-established Japanese restaurant in Shizuoka City, and served as the chef at Isawa Onsen Hotel Toyo in Yamanashi Prefecture. In 2022, at the age of 33, he opened his dream restaurant after finding an ideal site in his hometown and building his restaurant, Shin Nihonryouri Obune, there.
Committed to offering “new Japanese cuisine,” Chef Takagi creates dishes combining urban twists he learned while working in Tokyo and the natural flavors of local ingredients. He is a local patriot, having been selected as one of 200 cooks who contribute to the food culture of Shizuoka Prefecture and awarded the title of Fujinokuni Food Capital Professional. In addition, he goes to the Omaezaki and Yaizu Fishing Ports to buy seafood and sources vegetables from local farms. He combines these local ingredients with carefully selected seasonal ingredients delivered from around Japan by suppliers with whom he has relationships dating back to his days as an apprentice.
With a good supply chain of quality beef, Shin Nihonryouri Obune has “Enshu Yumesaki Beef Sukiyaki with Truffles” on its specialty menu. Enshu Yumesaki Beef, a type of premium local beef from Shizuoka, is cooked sukiyaki style and topped with sliced truffles in front of diners. The stock made from quality dried bonito and kombu seaweed makes this popular dish even more sought after.
The Japanese sake list has some 10 varieties, including Isojiman from Shizuoka and Juyondai from Yamagata. Meanwhile, the wine list curated by famous Sommelier Shinya Tasaki offers some 50 red and white wines from the top five châteaux of Bordeaux and Kenzo Estate Winery in California, among others.

Imbued with the Chef’s passion, the detached restaurant building is majestic with charred cedar exterior walls. In addition, with counter and horigotatsu table seats as well as private rooms, the restaurant serves a variety of purposes. Recharge yourself at Shin Nihonryouri Obune with your family, friends, colleagues or partner while enjoying the tasty dishes served by Chef Takagi with a friendly smile.
nearestStations: 7~8 minutes by cab from South Exit of Kikugawa Station

244226.longDescription:
French restaurant  "KAWASAKI " which is near JR Shizuoka station, quietly standing on the second floor of a brick building.  There are 10 counter seats in the open kitchen, and 8 tables, even though it is a small restaurant,  some guests visit there from far away. It is hidden gem.

“Wish to have a job to express something creative” by owner-chef Mr. Yoshinori Kawasaki.  He used to go to music school and doing band activities as a guitarist. At the age of 24, changing the way of expression from music to cooking, and getting into a world of cooking. After he worked at “Restaurant Kinoshita” in Yoyogi, “L’AMITIE” in Takadanobaba, and “Brasserie AUX AMIS” in Marunouchi., he became chief of “restaurant BIOS” which is a farm owned restaurant.  In 2014 he set up and opened his own restaurant “Kawasaki”.  

From his thoughts of “Enjoy the seasonal nature, and value for once in a lifetime opportunity.”, he values the connection with local producers and takes very seriously about providing best ingredients in the best recipe.  During the hunting period, the chef himself hunt, and the store also has a dry aging cellar for the storage.  He goes to the farm of a contracted farmer, and harvest every morning. Using local food and cook with thoughts of producers.  That is Kawasaki chef’s way. 

The interior is a chic atmosphere, based on black. Available in a wide range of scenes, such as a reward for yourself, important anniversary, use with friends and couples and so on. The Kawasaki’s dishes that you can only taste in this time and the place, please check it by yourself.
nearestStations: JR Tokaido Main Line (Atami - Hamamatsu) Shizuoka 10 minutes by walk from North exit

245162.longDescription:
Tokushima Prefecture in the Shikoku region, known for its Awa Odori Dance Festival, is home to the restaurant Toraya Kochuan. Located in Sanagochi Village, a 30-minute drive from Tokushima City, the restaurant is run by a parent-child trio: Koji Iwamoto (the proprietor known as a key figure in the Japanese cuisine scene), the proprietress, and the proprietress-to-be.

Born as the third-generation owner of Toraya Ryokan in Sanagochi Village, Tokushima Prefecture, Iwamoto trained under Teiichi Yuki, the founder of the Japanese restaurant Kitcho, and honed his culinary skills while working as a grill chef at the flagship of Kitcho Arashiyama in Kyoto. Then, in 1985, he returned to his hometown and transformed Toraya Ryokan into Toraya Kochuan to face the culinary world head-on. Word of Iwamoto’s simple yet flavorful dishes spread quickly, allowing his restaurant to expand its clientele and attract food lovers from inside and outside Japan.

”I hope the dishes of Toraya Kochuan will resonate with the tastes of our customers,” says Iwamoto. Although cooking is simple, “‘goodies are hidden in the simplicity.’ I want to make dishes like that,” he continued.

The rice and vegetables offered at the restaurant are sourced from local producers. Stock is made with high-quality water to enhance its flavor, while freshwater fish dishes are prepared with fish caught in a local river. As a fisherman, Iwamoto understands the best ways to cook fish. In particular, sweetfish is a specialty on the menu, and the chef makes the three-hour trip to the Yasuda River in Kochi Prefecture to catch it. These carefully selected ingredients are meticulously cooked to create a balanced meal.

The drinks menu offers a selection of Japanese sake with umami flavors, such as Odenden, made with fertilizer-free rice grown in local terraced fields and carefully selected water, Yorokobi Gaijin from Kagawa, and Asahi Wakamatsu from Tokushima.

The restaurant only has private rooms, two on the first floor and one on the second floor.

Blessed with the bounty of the land and sea, Toraya Kochuan is the perfect place to enjoy the rich flavors of nature with friends and to share the joy of dining.
nearestStations: A 30-minutes by car from Tokushima Station on the JR Kotoku, Tokushima, Mugi and Naruto lines

244769.longDescription:
Akasaka, Tokyo is a high-class historic residential area and a busy shopping district filled with gorgeous restaurants. Japanese restaurant “Akasaka Eigetsu” is on the 4th floor of the building, 5 minutes’ walk from both Tokyo Metro Akasaka Station and Akasaka-mitsuke Station. When you get off the elevator and walk forward, you will be greeted by a noren (a short curtain hung at the entrance of a restaurant) with the restaurant name.

The owner is Hidenori Iwasaki. After working at sushi restaurants and Japanese restaurants in Tokyo, he was trained at "Ajihana" and "Sumiya Ryokan Kyoto" in Kyoto. He returned to Tokyo and became independent in September 2010, opening “Akasaka Eigetsu”.

The menu consists of 12 ~ 13 dishes made with seasonal vegetables and fishes that are inspired by Kyoto cuisine, and beautifully reflect the changes of the four seasons in Japan on the plates. For example, he uses ingredients such as bamboo shoots in spring, Kamo eggplant in summer, ebi-imo in autumn, and Shogoin-kabura in winter. Owner Iwasaki uses seasonal ingredients that are purchased daily at Toyosu market and the Kyoto vegetables are purchased directly from the farmers that he has been associated with since his training. His ability to take advantage of the potential of the ingredients and take care of them as if they were children is his charm. There are about 40 kinds of sake to go with the dishes. You can enjoy seasonal Japanese sake from all over Japan, such as summer sake, Hiyaoroshi in autumn and new sake and Origarami in winter. Burgundy and Champagne are also available for wine.

The restaurant has 4 counter seats, 1 table for 4 and 1 table for 2 people, making use of the warmth of wood for the small atmosphere. Owner Iwasaki's strong desire of "providing a space where guests who chose us, among so many restaurants, can relax as if they were back home," is reflected in the interior decoration and the selection of dinnerware and drinking vessels. If there are any food preferences, the restaurant will respond to them as much as possible if inform in advance. The space with a warm image is suitable for various occasions, such as for dating and business gathering. Why not visit “Akasaka Eigetsu” to enjoy the relaxing space and food in the center of the city?
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Akasaka-Mitsuke Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line)

244673.longDescription:
Far from the bustling crowds in the Akasaka district in Tokyo, you can loiter for a moment at a quiet spot called "Akasaka Gosen". The owner-chef is Hayashi Ayumu, who went independent after a long career of working at restaurants in Akasaka and in Paris. He had business in Kenji for 10 years and in Asagaya for 6 years before moving to Akasaka in 2017, a place where mature and sophisticated taste gathers. 

At "Akasaka Gosen", he offers the specialty of Gosen--soft shelled turtle and the high-quality sake Shihihonyari. A delight to both the eyes and the tongue. 

The soft-shelled turtle is stocked year round from the most trustworthy regions and prepared with its natural excellence. "Akasaka Gosen" puts aside the traditional style of simply throwing it into a large pot, but serves it in a small single portion pot for each guest. Applying this clever technique helps bring out the original taste of the turtle, as well as the subtle variations of flavor. 

The second pillar of "Akasaka Gosen" is its Shichihonyari sake, where 6 to 8 varieties are available. There are also 3 to 4 other sake varieties, champagne, and Japanese vintage wine to round out its offerings. The interior of the restaurant, with its warm, choice wood furnishings, has a counter seating for nine, a well as a separate private room for up to 6 people. At the counter, which was constructed from a single board from a magnificent Japanese ceder of 200 to 300 years old, you can enjoy conversation with the owner-chef Hayashi's about these techniques as you watch him at work. Of course you can also relax in the private room with friends. From business meetings, celebrations, to simply dining together with beloved ones, this is a house for all occasions.

244779.longDescription:
Akasaka Misuji is a upscale yakiniku restaurant located 2 minutes on foot from Tokyo
Metro Akasaka-Mitsuke Station.

Opened in 2010 as a sister restaurant of the popular Yoroniku in Minami Aoyama, the restaurant is owned by Tomoaki Handa, who studied at Yakiniku Jumbo Shinozaki restaurant before opening Yoroniku in 2007, and later Akasaka Misuji in 2010. 

In contrast to the set meals at Yoroniku, Misuji offers a more relaxed à la carte of first-rate lean meat sourced from the owner’s own network, with diners able to choose their desired cuts of beef, in the preferred quantities. The restaurant’s speciality is the eponymous top blade, carefully cut to a calculated thickness. Additionally, the standard menu at Yoroniku is also offered, with dishes such as hand-stretched somen noodles and silk roast, bite-sized rice balls wrapped with lightly grilled meat.  

With the ability to accommodate up to 38 guests, including 6 counter seats and luxury semi-private suites for 4 diners, Misuji makes for a sophisticated and high quality dining experience, perfect for entertainment and celebrating with colleagues, friends, family, and dates.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Akasaka-Mitsuke Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line )

244971.longDescription:
Akasaka Ninomae is a classic kaiseki restaurant set in a calm space in Akasaka, a blissful experience that allows diners to forget the bustle of the city. The restaurant specialises in delighting its guests with cuisine, entertainment, and hospitality that cherishes each customer as an individual, with course after course of stunning food prepared from ingredients woven by the four seasons.  

Chef and his deputy visit Toyosu Market each day to create dishes from the ingredients at their peak depending on the time of year. The restaurant’s name, “Ninomae”, expresses a desire to humbly aim for the best. Matsuba crab is popular with guests and a seasonal pleasure when available, with the theatre of handling the crab in front of diners proving especially popular. For drinks, select wines and sakes are preferred; the best seasonal sakes are offered to guests, with styles ranging from the young to the old; traditional to modern, centering on Kuroryu from Fukui. Wines hail mainly from California’s Kenzo Estate, with wines chosen to match dishes. 

Instead of a single dining room, the restaurant offers a series of private rooms that can be customised to the occasion or situation according to each guest and their party, from family gatherings to business entertainment. An English language menu is available for overseas guests, and English-speaking staff are on hand to assist and provide any services according to guests’ wishes by prior consultation.

244945.longDescription:
A two-minute walk from Akasaka Station, Japanese restaurant Akasaka Ogino is located on the first floor of a stylish building, where chef Satoshi Ogino demonstrates his skills. As guests enter the shop through a curtain, the interior is decorated with pictures drawn by artist Tsurutaro Kataoka.

After graduating from high school, Ogino began his training at the three-star Kyoto Kitcho Arashiyama in Kyoto, where he learned the fundamentals of Japanese cookery before progressing to studying at three-star Ginza Koju. There, he distinguished himself for his characteristic taste in cooking, and was selected as the chef for the two-star Ginza Okuda at the young age of 30. After studying hard for three years, he became independent and opened Akasaka Ogino in 2020.

Ogino describes his cuisine as traditional Japanese. Above all, he values the sense of the seasons, and seasonal festivals such as Hina-matsuri and Tanabata are incorporated into the restaurant’s dishes. "These days, when it is difficult to feel the sense of the seasons, it would be nice if we could introduce the season and the Japanese culture even a little with Akasaka Ogino's dishes", he says. To this end, he places particular emphasis on the hassun, the traditional second course of a kaiseki menu, to express the season.

Vegetables are harvested from Higuchi Farm in Kyoto, which Ogino proclaims to be the best; meanwhile, fish and shellfish are purchased from preferred wholesalers in Toyosu Market and nationwide. 

A charcoal burner has been installed in the center of the open kitchen, allowing guests to watch  the cooking process. In addition, the aromas of freshly shaved bonito and roasted sesame drift through the air, characteristics that are unique to an open kitchen. 

The restaurant always offers six to eight types of sake that are served in one “go” (180 ml), including premium sakes like Juyondai. The wine list was selected by Ogino himself, who is a certified sommelier, along with a wide variety of non-alcoholic offerings.

To enhance the ambience further, flowers are arranged in the shop every day, and guests are welcomed with a unique bouquet each day. Notably, most bouquets are one-of-a-kind arrangements by artists. Diners eat from dishes that are themselves ceramic works of Karatsu Doheigama by Yotaro Fujinoki and Mahito Yamaguchi from Aichi, who is famous for Oribe ware, highly reputed by discerning customers.

With just 7 counter seats, Akasaka Ogino is an exceptional place to relax and celebrate with your loved ones, and to savor the heart and soul of Japanese cuisine.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Akasaka Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

245399.longDescription:
A three-minute walk from Tameike-Sanno subway station, Akasaka Sushi Shino is nicely secluded on the third floor of a building off Roppongi Street. It is a cozy restaurant helmed by Chef Koichi Shinohara, who changed his career path and entered the culinary field at the age of 23. Shortly after beginning an apprenticeship with a renowned sushi restaurant in Tokyo, he distinguished himself and opened his own restaurant, Akasaka Sushi Shino, in October 2022.

Based on his belief that “Our guests deserve not only delicious food but also delightful dining experiences,” Chef Shinohara offers a prix fixe meal consisting of 21 pieces in total (eight delicacies and 12 pieces of sushi). He goes to Toyosu Market every morning to personally select the finest ingredients. The bluefin tuna is sourced from a partner broker with whom the chef has a long relationship. The sushi rice is made of aged Nanatsuboshi rice from Hokkaido. Drier and less sticky, this aged rice is cooked until it will fall apart in the mouth in a way the chef deems perfect and seasoned with a blend of three varieties of red vinegar from Yokoi’s Vinegar. The wasabi directly sourced from Utougi, Shizuoka, which is known as the birthplace of wasabi cultivation, is characterized by its sharp pungency and full sweetness.

The summer menu puts the spotlight on gizzard shad, a typical Edomae sushi fish, carefully selected for size and fattiness and pickled to add a refreshing flavor, while a signature dish for the winter months features horsehair crab (or Kobako snow crab in November), whose meat is removed from the shell, mixed with crab innards, topped with gelée made from crab vinegar, and placed back into the shell. The tsume sauce, which is the essence of Edomae sushi, is also made in a unique way, using clam stock to add a discrete touch of sweetness.


The restaurant holds nine regular varieties of Japanese sake, including Kokuryu from Fukui, Hiroki from Fukushima, Zaku from Mie, and Hidakami from Miyagi, as well as five seasonal options. In addition, the wine cellar contains five varieties of champagne, including Deutz, Bollinger, and sparkling wines, as well as red and white wines, including asatsuyu, rindo, ai, and murasaki from KENZO ESTATE in California.

The sukiya-style dining room is cozy with a hinoki cypress counter (seating up to eight guests) and Juraku walls. The plates for serving sushi are made of Shino ware from Gifu, selected for its unique colors as well as its name, which is reminiscent of the restaurant’s name. Please enjoy a special time at Akasaka Sushi Shino, which provides a delicious and delightful dining experience in a relaxing setting.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Tameike-Sanno station on Ginza Line, Exit 11.
