244513.longDescription:
Named after “Elysion,” the earthly paradise of Greek mythology, “Aoyama ELYSION HOUSE” stands as a secluded mansion restaurant in a quiet residential area, just a five-minute walk from Aoyama-itchome Station. Despite its central Tokyo location, the restaurant offers a tranquil retreat within an elegant standalone residence.

Since April 2024, Executive Chef Ken Sasaki has led the kitchen. He honed his skills at award-winning restaurants and luxury hotels in Tokyo, and further refined his sensibility at renowned establishments and wineries in Paris. While serving as head chef at a star-awarded restaurant in Tokyo, he also supervised culinary projects overseas, including in Shanghai. His seasonally inspired course menus unfold like a story, presenting innovative French cuisine that engages all five senses. Carefully selected ingredients from trusted producers are transformed through his creative vision into exquisite plates.

The restaurant’s name, derived from the Greek mythological paradise “ELYSION,” reflects its dreamlike and extraordinary atmosphere. On the first floor, the main dining room features 180-degree glass windows overlooking a beautiful garden; sunlight fills the space with serenity by day, while glittering chandeliers create a luxurious ambiance at night. Five private rooms accommodating 2 to 16 guests offer refined settings for intimate gatherings. Favored by embassy officials from the surrounding area, “Aoyama ELYSION HOUSE” serves as a sophisticated hideaway for discerning adults. 

From important business occasions to proposals in the adjoining chapel and memorable anniversaries, it presents moments of lasting delight.

245472.longDescription:
Just one minute’s walk from Exit 7 of Akasaka metro station, Araki is perched on the second floor of a stylish building. The restaurant was opened in April 2024 by an internationally celebrated sushi chef who had returned to his roots after making a name in London and Hong Kong. Back in Japan, he tingles the taste buds of sushi lovers in Akasaka.

Chef Mitsuhiro Araki stepped into the world of sushi at the age of 25. He first trained at Sushi Izumi in Meguro and then apprenticed to Takeaki Niitsu, the second-generation owner-chef of Kiyota in Ginza. Then, he opened his own restaurant, Araki, in Kaminoge, Setagaya, in 2000. Having relocated to Ginza in 2010, the restaurant won a three-star rating over two consecutive years in 2011 and 2012. However, at the height of his success, Chef Araki decided to break new ground in London. He opened The Araki in the British capital in 2014 and received a two-star rating in 2016. The Araki became the first sushi and Japanese restaurant in Europe and North America to get a three-star rating in 2017 and 2018, respectively. Leaving this celebrated restaurant to his apprentice, he also opened The Araki in Hong Kong in 2019 and won a one-star rating there in 2020 and 2021, setting the world on fire.

Then, in April 2024, he returned to Japan and opened the restaurant Araki again. According to Chef Araki, the restaurant reopened in the original home of Edomae sushi is also intended to serve as a platform for next-generation sushi chefs. He hopes it will “provide a training ground for an increasing number of young apprentices dreaming of becoming sushi chefs around the world.”

Based on the concept of local consumption of local products, Chef Araki features local ingredients, such as caviar and truffles in London and Shanghai crabs and giant clams in Hong Kong. Back in Japan, the ingredients also go back to the roots of Edomae sushi. For example, the prix-fixe menu uses typical Edomae ingredients to create an exquisite full-course meal, consisting of three delicacies and 12 to 13 pieces of nigiri sushi. The series of nigiri sushi features six pieces of sushi with bluefin tuna sourced from a popular tuna broker, Ishiji, including lean, pickled, medium fatty, and fatty tuna pieces, which prove the reputation of Araki for serving exceptional bluefin tuna. In order to bring out the best flavors of the seafood, the temperature of sushi rice, seasoned with red vinegar from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing, is carefully tuned as well.

The sake list only offers six different types of Masu Izumi from a brewery in Toyama with which the chef has forged close ties, though guests are welcome to bring their own favorite bottles. Those who choose to drink something non-alcoholic are offered bottled cold tea from Marushichi Seicha in Shizuoka. The restaurant’s interior, designed by Itai Komuten with experience working for renowned sushi restaurants, is dignified with earthen walls and a solid countertop made of 300-year-old Kiso Hinoki cypress (with nine seats). Bringing the captivating world of Edomae sushi back to Akasaka, Japan, Araki is a definite must-visit!
nearestStations: Just one minute’s walk from Exit 7 of Akasaka metro station

244964.localizedAddress: 1F D-0118, Tokyo Midtown Garden Terrace, 9-7-4, Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244964.longDescription:
Artisan de la Truffe Paris is a restaurant specialising in dishes that focus on the coveted truffle, with an original location at the long-established BHV department store in Paris, France. Like its relative, the restaurant sources selected truffles from all over Europe for each of its memorable dishes. 

The kitchen selects truffles based on their unique aromas and expressions depending on the season each variety is at its peak, with an array on offer including black and white truffles; summer truffles; bloomer truffles; and burgundy truffles. As guests open their menus, the beginning lists each variety of truffle alongside their provenance and a map, with popular dishes including classic pâté de campagne with truffles, a cheese risotto with freshly shaved truffle, poire of beef fillet with fresh truffles, and even ice cream laced with their aroma. 

A stylish dining room in a signature black mirrors the Paris flagship, and is lent warmth with natural wood floors and tables. In addition to a 50-cover dining room, a counter with up to six seats and private rooms hosting up to five diners each are also available. Last but not least, an open terrace seating up to 46 guests is an ideal setting for al fresco occasions. 

The restaurant presents an ideal setting for celebratory occasions, such as belated anniversaries, as well as relaxed gatherings with friends and dates in dazzling surroundings.
nearestStations: A few minutes walk from Roppongi Station

243980.longDescription:
After gaining experience at Tivoli in Ginza, and Mon Finage in Shibuya, owner chef Hisashi Yamashita now manages the French bistro, Bistro Q. With its casual, bistro-style counter and table seating, there are many regular guests who bring their close friends. You can usually catch sight of adults casually chatting with staff members at the counter, just like at a bistro in France.

After starting with an authentic French style aperitif, the thing you will want to order is the hamburg steak that Yamashita has absolute confidence in. Although it features juicy, 100% Japanese Black beef, the real pleasure is the French foie gras that is hidden inside the hamburg steak. The savory foie gras makes a perfect match for the flavorful beef. This is the kind of pleasure that no adult could turn away from. As one would expect, since the bistro only targets stylish adults, each dish is carefully made, one by one.  

Since Chef Yamashita also has experience working at a teppanyaki restaurant, it doesn’t just stop with French cuisine. Many foodies stop by daily to request a dish that gives a glimpse into his playful creativity, which can only be found here. Welcome to the eatery for sophisticated adults.

244828.longDescription:
A three-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Akasaka Station, sushi restaurant Kagami stands like a hideout in a quiet town. Chef Toshio Kagami is an artisan who has devoted his life to sushi. After training in Ginza, Tokyo, he opened a sushi restaurant in his hometown of Yamanashi, a place that became quite popular, even among customers from Tokyo. Later, he met the master of the sushi restaurant Mitani in Yotsuya, and worked as the vice manager of the sister restaurant Kioi-cho Mitani. He spent three years there, before striking out on his own, with the support of the Mitani. In September 2019, he opened Kagami.

At Kagami, seafood is purchased from reliable brokers and fishermen. High-quality Yamanashi rice brand Mukawamai is used, with a blend of three kinds of vinegar: red vinegar made from 15-year aged sake lees, mild black vinegar, and rice vinegar. The Kagami style is to hand over all the sushi with this thought: "Because I hold it with heart, I want to give it with heart".

Along with the omakase menu, a restaurant signature is the beverage pairing, which also pays homage to Mitani. Wine is mainly French, and for Champagne, the restaurant selects wine made by small producers. Seasonal sake is from all over Japan. Chef Kagami says that alcohol is essential to bring out the flavor of food: "Sake with food, sake like seasoning."

There are only six counter seats in the restaurant. From the design drawn by chef Kagami herself to the dignified air created by the craftsmanship of the shrine carpenters, the interior creates a comfortable space. Most of the dinnerware is inherited from Mitani and there are various old and new items such as Kyoyaki-ware. Visit for dinner or a date with family or friends, feel the heartwarming Kagami nigiri, taste it with your palate, and enjoy the alcohol.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Akasaka Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line)

244291.longDescription:
The owner, Hikoaki Tan, works in many fields such as television appearances as well as a vocational school lecturer. His son, Sawaaki, is currently working as head chef of the restaurant, continuing to maintain the restaurant's famed reputation.

Mr. Hikoaki was born in Yokohama's Chinatown district, and has pursued a career in cooking since the age of 16. He has worked as Sous Chef for a number of restaurants, such as Shinbashi Chugoku Meshi, Shibai, and Sendai Hotels Ume Hanazono. From there, he worked as the head chef for the Keio Plaza Hotel Nanen and then as the head chef for the hotel Edmont. He later become the owner of Akasaka Rikyu in 1996. 

Meanwhile, his son (Sawaaki) began his career as a chef in Tokyo Ana Hotel's (currently ANA Intercontinental Hotel) restaurant, Karin. After training there for 5 years, he went on to work at Sairyu, a restaurant at the Yokohama Bay Sheraton Hotel and Towers. Then, at the age of 30, he joined his father at Akasaka Rikyu. He worked as head chef since 2012. 

In Cantonese cuisine, they use delicious ingredients from around the world to express that "Gourmet begins in Guangzhou" which includes dishes that bring out the best flavors of the ingredients. This is taken one step further at Akasaka Rikyu, where they focus on the wonderful ingredients of Japanese cuisine, overflowing with the delicious taste of the four seasons. Without using unnecessary seasoning, spices and oil, the cuisine conveys a graceful and gentle flavor. The restaurants signature dishes include grilled dishes, shark fin dishes and seafood dishes. In particular, the steamed live grouper, simmered shark fin, and homemade roasted pork fillet are true representatives of Cantonese cuisine. Also, the dim sum prepared each day is made with the belief that it conveys the faith, effort and time it took to make it.

The Akasaka Restaurant was relocated to the 2nd and 3rd floors of the Akasaka Biz Tower Atrium in 2008. The 2nd floor has a classical and calm atmosphere, whereas the 3rd floor hosts an open-dining room. There are 4 private rooms which differ in design and appearance. Since the restaurant is located inside the high-rise tower and is connected directly to Akasaka Station, it is easily accessible. The restaurant can also be host to a variety of occasions, such as birthdays, anniversaries and receptions.
nearestStations: 1 minute walk from Akasaka Station on the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line (directly connected to the station)

245587.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Roppongi-itchōme Station, Korean Cuisine NoruraDa is located on the first floor of a building in Akasaka. Since its opening in February 2023, the restaurant has been helmed by Grand Chef Jaesung Shin, who used to work at popular Korean and Korean BBQ restaurants in Tokyo. At NoruraDa, he surprises and excites guests, as indicated by the restaurant’s name, which is derived from a Korean word meaning “surprise,” by offering a variety of innovative small dishes that combine Japanese, Western, Chinese, and Korean flavors.

The prix-fixe menu offers 12 courses, from an Assortment of Korean Banchan Dishes (appetizers) to Bingsu (Korean shaved ice dessert). The menu is characterized by offering one main dish each of vegetables, seafood, and meat (beef and pork). Among them, Ganjang Gejang, a Korean delicacy of soy-marinated crabs, is the restaurant’s specialty. The blue swimmer crabs, sourced directly from contract fishermen in Minamichita, Aichi, and marinated in a soy-based sweet sauce (ganjang) made from fruits, vegetables, and more than 20 kinds of spices, tickle the taste buds of food lovers.  Another must-try, Yukhoe, is made from rump roast. The highly prized beef cut is slow-cooked over a low heat until it is just seared on the outside and further elevated with caviar and Japanese glass shrimp from Toyama. Gyeran Jjim with Snow Crab, a Korean steamed egg dish, is also made from carefully selected ingredients, including high-quality eggs with rich yolks from Aomori. This popular dish can be upgraded to Luxury Gyeran Jjim  by adding optional toppings, such as anglerfish liver, milt, sea urchin, and salmon roe. What is common to these dishes is that they are all full of delightful surprises, and Spicy Grilled Wagyu Oxtail is no exception. Prepared using a special vacuum-cooking process to infuse deep flavors, it is so tender that it can be cut with chopsticks.

The drink menu focuses exclusively on unpasteurized craft makgeolli, a traditional Korean alcoholic beverage. Curated by Service Manager Tomohiro Yoshida, the selection features labels from across Japan such as Boksoondoga Son Makgeolli from Fukuoka, OMONA Makgeolli from Shimane, Craft Makgeolli SOON from Tokyo, and Tora Makgeolli from Fukushima.  There are also food and makgeolli pairing suggestions. The interior is all black with a black L-shaped counter (seating up to eight guests). Although it only has counter seating, the restaurant caters to versatile dining needs, from private to business occasions. Enjoy the innovative Korean dishes full of surprises and unforgettable flavors at NoruraDa!

244080.longDescription:
Nogizaka Shin is a Japanese restaurant that opened in June 2016. The restaurant is a partnership between owner Shinji Ishida, who gained experience at world gourmet guide awarded Japanese restaurants in Ginza and Paris, and maitre d' and sommelier Yasuhide Tobita.

The restaurant serves Japanese cuisine using carefully selected ingredients sourced mainly from Ishida's home town, Tokushima Prefecture on the island of Shikoku. He has particularly strong feelings about sea bream, an indispensable ingredient in Japanese cooking that sourced from Tokushima, which he says will always be the yardstick for his development as a chef and an ingredient he is confident working with. Complementing the cooking is an extensive wine and sake list that draws on sommelier Hida's overseas experience. This is used to create perfectly balanced pairings that open up new frontiers for Japanese cuisine.

The restaurant is compact, with a six-seat counter and three private rooms, and set menus are served for both lunch and dinner. Children are welcome in lunchtime (state during the reservation) and English service is available, making the restaurant suitable for entertaining or meeting with overseas guests.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Nogizaka Station (Exit 1), Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line

244370.localizedAddress: 4F, Tokyo Mid Town Garden Terrace, 9-7-4, Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244370.longDescription:
Philippe Mille, who won the Meilleur Ouvrier de France (M.O.F.), France’s highest professional distinction, at the young age of 38, is the owner-chef of ARBANE, a two star fine dining restaurant in Champagne, France, and has now opened his first restaurant in Roppongi Midtown, Japan.　The restaurant in Japan is supervised by Hiramatsu – which runs restaurants and hotels throughout Japan. The chef is Mr. Tetsuya Nakamura, who learned his skill at restaurants under Hiramatsu.

The concept of Philippe Mille Tokyo is to be "a graceful and elegant champagne salon." Champagne is primarily gathered from the Champagne region, where Mr. Mille is based, but also has over 100 different types of sparkling wine – ranging from major and famous Maisons to small-scale craft houses. The menu offers dishes which bring out the best and true value of champagne - from a Degustation de Champagne course which is designed dish by dish to marry perfectly with champagne, to a monthly "By The Glass" menu, which provides 5 to 6 different types of champagne by the glass each month.

The foundation of Philippe Mille's cuisine is a thorough dedication to selecting the best ingredients, to bring out the absolute best in flavor from each seasonal ingredient. His belief is that "ingredients are a local region's treasures," and he holds Japanese ingredients in the highest regard. For example, he uses ingredients such as carrots from Takashima, Shiga Prefecture, shiitake mushrooms from Atsugi, and Omi Wagyu beef. He has created a menu that emphasizes Japanese ingredients, featuring dishes which display a deep understanding for Japanese chefs, ingredients, and the tastes of the Japanese people. And of course, each dish has been crafted to precisely and superbly pair with champagne.

Philippe Mille Tokyo is designed to be "an urban oasis", with light streaming in from the immense windows to create a bright and cheerful atmosphere, featuring 80 seats, and 4 private dining rooms. Mr. Mille is particularly fond of the outdoor garden terrace where diners can view the Midtown gardens, and enjoy the many expressive transitions of the seasons and time periods - such as the cherry blossoms in spring, the fresh greenery of summer, and illumination displays at night. Diners can surely discover the diverse pleasures of champagne and cuisine, here in this elegant environment, under the secure services of Hiramatsu management.
nearestStations: Connected to Roppongi station of Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line or Toei Ōedo Line

"Restaurant Lyla" is a French restaurant located on the corner of a quiet residential street in Akasaka. "Lyla" is a portmanteau of two French words, meaning "poetic" and "laboratory" respectively. As the restaurant is in a slightly obscure location about 10 minutes on foot from either Nogizaka Station and Akasaka Station on the Chiyoda Line, or Aoyama-itchome Station on the Ginza, Hanzomon, or Oedo Lines, a taxi bounded for Lyla is recommended. The interior is simple but staid, basically white in color. The lighting creates a moody atmosphere.

With using ingredients that can be stocked that very day, and rare ingredients delivered directly from origins, sophisticated and delicate dishes created with unusual combinations of ingredients. Your dishes will be the only one that cannot be reappeared. It's an exceptional experience to savor a meal specially prepared for you. Among the other delights here, wines and champagnes are beautifully paired with the special dishes.

This restaurant is a great place to spend time with your special one, while enjoying the extraordinary, spacious dining room space. For anniversary dates, a Lyla signature cake or a message plate is a must-order.

245553.longDescription:
Nestled in a back alley near Tameike Sanno Station, Sushi Comari is helmed by Chef Satoshi Fukushima. Knowing seafood like the back of his hand, he creates sushi and delicacies by sincerely engaging with top-quality seasonal fish and shellfish. As a self-taught chef, he honed his culinary skills at Japanese and sushi restaurants in Tokyo and around Japan and worked as a fish wholesaler at Toyosu Market before he opened his own restaurant, Sushi Comari, in 2022. The Fukushima-style original sushi and delicacies made the restaurant an immediate hit and a favorite destination for repeat guests.

Chef Fukushima’s days start in the dark, long before sunrise, as he participates in auctions. He brings carefully selected fish and shellfish back to his restaurant and prepares them without taking a rest. They are featured in the curated prix-fixe menu, which consists of about nine small dishes and about 13 pieces of nigiri sushi. The order in which the dishes are served may vary depending on the conversation with the guest. This thoughtful consideration is another reason for the popularity of Sushi Comari. The sushi rice seasoned with a combination of red and rice vinegar packs a punch of savory flavor with the presence of salt. The chef’s skill lies in creating sushi toppings that will not be overpowered by the striking sushi rice. The Gizzard Shad, one of the most important sushi toppings, is marinated in the same vinegar used to season the sushi rice. Another popular topping is Conger Eel, which is cooked so tender that it will melt on the palate and dressed with a mildly sweet sauce made from the cooking broth. The sponge cake-like Egg Omelet is characterized by its fluffy texture. Among the delicacies, the tender Anglerfish Liver topped with a dark molasses syrup like a Japanese confectionery is particularly worth trying. The Bonito topped with soy-marinated green onions is another must-try delicacy that has cemented its position as a specialty of the restaurant since its opening. With a keen eye honed by his experience as a wholesaler and a delicate sense of touch, the chef examines the quality of ingredients not only by seeing their conditions but also, for example, by feeling the sensation transmitted through the knife handle when cutting bluefin tuna.

The sake list offers about 10 varieties that go well with the sushi created by Chef Fukushima, such as Mimurosugi from Nara and Takijiman from Mie. The restaurant’s name, Comari, originates not from the traditional Japanese handcrafted ball called “comari” but from the Japanese term that means “cozy.” This reflects the chef’s commitment to providing each guest with friendly service and personalized dining experiences. Indulge in a premium dining experience with your foodie buddies while enjoying the harmony of sushi toppings and rice crafted by Chef Fukushima in his cozy restaurant with only eight counter seats.

Just removed from the busy Tokyo shopping district lined with television stations and offices is sushi restaurant "Sushi Haru". The owner-chef, Haruhiko Sato is originally from Miyagi prefecture. He decided to become a sushi chef in junior high school, and after learning the ropes at a veteran sushi restaurant for 10 years starting at the age of 18, he further honed his skills working at a Japanese restaurant in Waseda and a sushi restaurant in Nishi-Azabu for 10 more years before finally establishing his own restaurant in 2018.

The reason, Sato chose Asakusa for the location of "Sushi Haru" was that it is a little hidden away, making it the perfect place for small groups of diners to relax and enjoy delicious sushi and drinks. Sato visits Tsukiji Fish market himself every morning to hand-pick the seafood for his restaurant. The tuna is sourced from Yamayuki, one of the most famous tuna brokers of Tsukiji. In summer the "Sushi Haru" serves sea urchin from Hokkaido and the Sanriku Coast, in autumn silver-skinned Pacific saury and mackerel, and in winter leatherfish, milt, and fresh salmon roe. The menu has a strong focus on seasonal ingredients, with courses designed to give diners a sense of the four seasons. Also worth mention is the restaurant's delicious sushi rice. A blend of Toyama Koshihikari and Miyagi Sasanishiki rice is cooked in a traditional Japanese rice cooker. The result is firm grains of rice which retain their original shape and have a brilliant glisten. The best companion for this delicious rice is sake, as it is itself made from rice. Sato offers a range of sake which pairs excellently with the food, including sake from his native Miyagi.

Inside the restaurant, 9 stylish modern seats are arranged around a counter made from a single piece of Japanese cypress. From the comfortable seats with large armrests, one gets a sense of Sato's desire for diners to take the time to enjoy their meals. "Sushi Haru" is the perfect choice for anniversaries, dates, business dinners meetings with important guests, or any other occasion when you have someone you want to impress.

245031.longDescription:
Itamae Sushi, which continues to evolve into "world-class sushi" while preserving the tradition of Edo-mae sushi, opened its first restaurant in Akasaka in 2007 and now operates 10 restaurants throughout Tokyo. The first restaurant, Akasaka restaurant, was relocated and reopened in April 2022. In November 2023, in order to meet the ever-increasing inbound demand, the restaurant was rebranded as "TOKYO SUSHI ITAMAESUSHI" Akasaka, offering sushi unique to Tokyo (=Edo-mae sushi), natural fish caught in the Edo-mae, and sushi that reproduces the artisanal skills inherited from the Edo period.

 The absolute must-try is the "Strongest Tuna Set". This set includes two pieces of fatty tuna, three pieces of medium fatty tuna, five pieces of lean tuna, Negitoro thin roll and Torotaku hand roll, giving you the best of tuna. Hadate sea urchin in a box is a popular a la carte dish. This luxurious dish is served with seaweed and vinegared rice, and the entire box of sea urchin is served. Another attraction of the restaurant is its extensive tuna menu, which includes "Natural Tuna and Avocado Tartar," "Natural Tuna Spring Roll," and "Natural Tuna Kushikatsu," which is made from the rare head meat. 

Premium sake brands are offered at various times of the year in addition to the standard sake menu. An extensive range of shochu, wine, fruit sours and fruit wine is also available.

The interior has a new design that fuses the good old Japanese modern with digital and stylish materials. In addition to counter seats and tables, there are also terrace seats, so it is a spacious space. Itamae Sushi Akasaka is suited for a wealth of occasions, including dinners with a partner, colleagues, or business clients, and parties with friends. The restaurant is also perfect for entertaining guests from abroad.

At Itamae Sushi Akasaka, guests are invited to enjoy a happy time with delicious bluefin tuna in a vibrant setting.

245461.longDescription:
Secluded on Akasaka Street, a three-minute walk from Nogizaka Station, Unotoki is a Japanese Kaiseki restaurant that features eel under the supervision of Nogizaka Shin.  Quietly located next to the one-star restaurant, Unotoki only offers 10 lunch specials per day. Chef Masayuki Goto will serve a wonderful seven-course lunch. All the courses, from starters and appetizers to soup, sashimi, boiled vegetables, rice, and dessert, feature Amakusa Ai Eel, raised in seawater instead of freshwater in Amakusa, Kumamoto. 

Raised in seawater like wild eel, Amakusa Ai Eel is incredibly delicious, characterized by its indigo color and thick layer of flavorful gelatinous material between the skin and the flesh. In fact, it is no exaggeration to say that an encounter with this amazing eel, whose fatty and tender flesh is irresistible once you taste it, gave birth to Unotoki, and that is why Chef Goto focuses on bringing out the best flavor of the exquisite ingredient. The soup made with a broth made from eel bones and loaded with tender chunks of eel also tastes rich and delicious. It should be noted in advance that there are two options of rice dishes to choose from: rice topped with broiled eel and rice served with grilled eel. Moreover, the drink menu curated by Yasuhide Tobita, the owner-sommelier of Nogizaka Shin who has experience at fine restaurants, ranging from French to Japanese, offers a great selection of wines and sake.

The modern sukiya-style interior of Unotoki was designed and created by experts with whom the owners of Nogizaka Shin have developed strong relationships. For example, the design was created by Atelier ÈS, a Paris-based architecture studio headed by Architect Shinku Noda and Interior Designer Eiji Kikkawa, and was realized by Itai Komuten, which is known for its expertise in high-end Japanese and eel restaurant projects.  The walls were plastered by Makoto Kusumi from Kusumi Sakan Kyoto in Kyoto, which has experience repairing the old drawing room of the Katsura Imperial Villa and the Tsukiji walls of the Kyoto Imperial Palace. The countertop is made of a solid piece of over 300-year-old Ise Hinoki cypress wood. The knotty grain of the wood not only captivates Hida but also adds a touch of warmth and elegance to the restaurant.

Served on plates created by contemporary artists to delight the eyes of guests, the full-course meal featuring Amakusa Ai Eel also tingles their taste buds. Please enjoy an extraordinary lunch at Unotoki, a lunch restaurant supervised by Nogizaka Shin.

245520.longDescription:
Perched on the second floor of Akasaka Biz Tower SHOPS & DINING in Akasaka Sacas, a complex that also houses TBS Broadcasting Center, Zakuro TBS is a branch of the Zakuro Group, which opened Tokyo’s first shabu-shabu restaurant in 1955 to introduce the shabu-shabu hotpot dish believed to originate from Kyoto. First opened in the former TBS Building in 1964 and relocated from TBS Garden to Akasaka Sacas in 2008, when the complex opened, Zakuro TBS has remained popular for decades for the distinctive flavors handed down within the Zakuro Group.

The food menu features shabu-shabu and sukiyaki hotpots with Kuroge Wagyu beef carefully selected from around Japan as well as traditional Japanese dishes infused with seasonal flavors. The prix-fixe shabu-shabu meal starts with appetizers, followed by a salad, a shabu-shabu platter, and Chinese noodles, which you will soak in the shabu-shabu soup, and finishes with your choice of desserts from the Group-wide menu, including kudzu kiri (cold kudzu noodles), pudding and tiramisu from an associated Italian restaurant, La Granata, and cheesecake and chocolate cake from another associated restaurant, Top’s. The Matsusaka Beef Shabu-Shabu Platter Meal is especially popular for its spicy sesame sauce. Reputed for its unparalleled flavor and aroma, this original sauce accompanies the shabu-shabu hotpot and the Salad of Crab and 23 Vegetables to enhance the rich flavors of the Matsusaka beef and crab salad.

The sake list offers an exceptional selection of sake, such as Hakkaisan (Niigata), Sawanoi Kou (Tokyo), and Shimeharitsuru Jun (Niigata). Among them, the most popular is Ikkon—Zakuro’s original sake with a dry taste that goes perfectly well with beef and fish (exclusively brewed by Matsunoi Sake Brewery Co., Ltd. in Tokamachi City,  Niigata Prefecture). The menu is completed by a wide selection of wines, shochu, whiskies, and soft drinks to satisfy the tastes and preferences of guests. The restaurant’s interior creates a warm, rustic atmosphere, which is enhanced by handcraft tableware with a touch of natural elegance, such as Mashiko ware (Tochigi) and Onta ware (Hita City, Oita Prefecture). The main dining room is complemented by seven private dining rooms, some with table seating and others with traditional Japanese horigotatsu seating (low tables with recessed floors), allowing the long-established restaurant to cater for any occasion, from personal gatherings to business events, with exceptional food, refined hospitality, and a relaxing ambience. Please enjoy the long-loved shabu-shabu hotpot and seasonal Japanese dishes at Zakuro TBS.

243943.longDescription:
This more than 20-year-old restaurant, located down a little alley in Akasaka, is like a private hideaway. The owner-chef, Mr. Koshimizu, is very inventive with his finest ingredients. The seafood soups are rich and flavorful, as you would expect from an island nation, and the meat dishes, made with premium Sendai Beef or their original brand pork "Kumabuta", bring out all the rich yet delicate flavors of the meat. They also serve a number of other now-famous dishes, such as a homemade smoked cheese bake, Sendai Beef sushi, and omelet risotto with truffle and foie gras (legendary food a former US president admired, saying “Unbelievable”). 

After dinner, the restaurant can be used as a bar. You can enjoy a quality adult time while sipping on whiskies and liqueurs carefully selected by Mr. Koshimizu. (Available only to guests who have dined at the restaurant.)Drinks are chosen specially for each dish by senior sommelier Mr. Miura, with the chef’s wife, Miharu. He is known as a vin jaune expert. Since the course offered is paired with drinks, you can enjoy the marriage of food and drink that goes beyond any one genre. They also have an impressive selection of whiskeys and liquors from the good old days, as well as vintage Madeira wines.

Mr. Koshimizu has his own smokehouse in Karuizawa, and is a pioneer of smoked seasoning. Perfect for entertaining special guests or close friends.

244376.longDescription:
""CRAFTALE"" is the new must-visit restaurant in Nakameguro, Tokyo's heaven for foodies. The name ""CRAFTALE"" is the combination of ""Craft"" (technique) and ""Tale ""(story). The name suggests the notion of food that conjures up the love and passion of its producers as it is served to the customers. 

The chef here is Shinya Otsuchihashi. He worked at ""The Georgian Club"" and ""Joel Robuchon"", and then spent time in France. The fresh and natural style of cooking and organic wine he came across when he worked at ""Saturne"" in Paris made a deep impression on him. These became the principles he wanted to apply in his own restaurant. Upon his return to Japan, Otsuchihashi worked in ""Restaurant Anis"", and in September 2015, he became the chef of ""CRAFTALE"". He has been receiving world gourmet guide award. 

The key characteristic of Otsuchihashi's menu is that each dish has a story behind it.  From 2018, he has increased the number of dishes on the menu compared to when the restaurant first opened. He now uses even better ingredients and has further refined the presentation of the dishes. Meat, fish, and vegetables - each ingredient reflects the sentiments and passion from the producers and plays its part in different dishes in the menu. The chef matches key ingredients and sauces to create a symphony of tastes and flavors.  The menu also features ""bread pairing"", which is serving freshly prepared bread to match with the dishes in order to create a culinary partnership between bread and food. There is further enjoyment to be had by immersing yourself in the stories and descriptions of each dish as your food is served. 

The large windows of the restaurant face out onto the Meguro River. There are six places at the counter and 18 table seats, set out in a natural-looking interior themed in white. Natural materials such as wood and stone add a sense of warmth to the cuisine. Relax and enjoy your meal in simple and elegant surroundings. Please come and experience Chef Otsuchihashi's delightful food stories and creations. 

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Nakameguro Station (Tokyu Toyoko Line and Toky metro Hibiya Line)

243969.longDescription:
Arakicho is located between Akebonobashi Station to the north and Yotsuya-Sanchome Station to the south, and used to be a gorgeous flower district. Arakicho Tenpaku" is located in an elegant area where many restaurants still stand side by side.

The restaurant reopened in September 2022 as "Arakicho Tenpaku" in the hope that more people will come to know the deliciousness of tempura.

The cuisine is prepared with carefully selected seasonal ingredients from all over Japan, and unroasted sesame oil, "Taihaku sesame oil," gives the tempura a light finish while maintaining its delicious flavor. Mr. Takano's tempura, which is a sublimation of the knowledge and techniques he has cultivated through his study at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, is a gem that can only be tasted here. The rice to finish the course meal is a two-tiered dish with the essence of "Japanese cuisine KONDO". After the tenbara rice with shiba shrimp kakiage is served over freshly cooked white rice in an earthenware pot, you can also have tencha, which is made from the best soup stock of bonito and kombu.
Ten varieties of sake are always available, including Gifu's "Reisen" and Fukui's "Kuroryu. The wine cellar at the entrance has a selection of wines from Burgundy, France, Champagne, Tuscany, Italy, and other regions selected by the owner and sommelier, Mr. Kondo, to match the tempura, allowing customers to enjoy a wide range of choices to suit their tastes.

The restaurant has both a counter and a private room, and the warm and emotional atmosphere reflects the owner's desire to create a restaurant that can be used for any occasion without being overbearing. We hope that you will enjoy your time at the restaurant while conversing with the owner over the counter, and savor your gastronomic delights to your heart's content.

243712.longDescription:
Since it opened in 2014, Noyashichi has gained popularity with its own unique Chinese cuisine. The owner-chef Shinya Yamamoto, who became independent after gaining experiences at the world gourmet guide award Mitamachi Momonoki, moved and reopened in Arakicho the restaurant in June 2017, about 2 years after the opening. Thinking that ""we want to improve the quality of each dish and increase customer satisfaction,""they create their own ideal dish and continue to evolve every day.

Owner-chef Yamamoto aims to create ""a dish that gives makes you feel burden-free after the meal while still feeling satisfied that you had the Chinese food."" To achieve this goal, Japanese cooking techniques were used. For example, the soup stock used as a base for cooking is originally made by mixing chicken bones with ground chicken or pork, but in Noyashichi, kelp is used instead of chicken bones to bring out the flavor of the ingredients without the peculiar smell of chicken. Chinese food has 3 basic elements, ""scent, color, and taste,"" which are often expressed with seasonings such as ""jian"" (sauce). While considering the balance of these 3 factors, owner-chef Yamamoto interprets it as ""Bring out the scent of materials,"" especially in terms of aroma, and becoming the Noyashichi style of cooking.

The interior is a Japanese space that uses plenty of tamo with little sound leakage. At the counter seats, there is room between the wooden floor and the seats so you can relax and enjoy the live feeling of owner-chef Yamamoto making the cuisine. The private rooms can accommodate up to 12 people. Please enjoy the new cuisine that brings out the advantages of both Chinese food and Japanese food.

Since opening in Roppongi in 2009, the prestigious Japanese cuisine restaurant Seikakobayashi has relocated to a quiet back alley in Arakicho in 2016.

The owner chef Yuji Kobayashi is extremely particular about the ingredients, believing "there are few things in this world that are truly delicious," and offers a menu centered on fish. Reservations are limited to two parties for a maximum of six people every evening. After taking off their shoes and entering the cozy restaurant, guests can observe the chef carefully preparing the food entirely by himself. 

Here you can spend a wonderful evening filled with a stunning variety of traditional Japanese cuisine and friendly conversation with the chef. The cozy atmosphere will make you feel at home and is recommended for dinner with close friends.

244130.longDescription:
""Tsunokami-zaka Koshiba"" is a Japanese restaurant located in Shinjuku, Tokyo. This restaurant is in a quiet residential area that takes little distance from the hustle and bustle of Shinjuku.

You can enjoy authentic Japanese cuisine, mainly charcoal-grilled dishes, made with fresh seafood and seasonal vegetables.

The chef Mr. Koshiba trained his skills at several Japanese restaurants in Kyoto, Hiroshima and Ginza. After worked as the head chef at the Japanese restaurant in Kagurazaka, he opened ""Tsunokami-zaka Koshiba"" in Akebonobashi (near Shinjuku) in September 2016.

Mr. Koshiba's culinary philosophy is, taking much care of making a wonderful Hassun (八寸). Hassun is the basis of Kyo-ryori (traditional style Japanese cuisine originated in Kyoto) and so refined. He hopes that guests enjoy the feeling of the Japanese seasons and have a happy time.

You can choose for your charcoal-grilled dishes that what seasonal ingredients you are desired to taste. They are all hand-picked by the chef, such as sea bream, soft-shelled turtle and Hida beef. In addition, chef uses ""Bincho-tan"" (the most famous charcoal for cooking in Japan) for charcoal-grilled dishes. You can also choose Oyako-don (rice bowl with chicken and egg) or Takikomi-gohan (rice cooked with various ingredients).

Some dishes are served in antique tableware, you can enjoy not only the taste but also the appearance of your cuisine. 

Pairing sakes are all chosen on the basis of creating a perfect mariage with the dishes. In this restaurant, there are just tables and counter seats made of Yoshino-Hinoki wood. You could feel relaxed and comfortable in the atmosphere based on the bright grain of cedar.

It's suitable for dating at the counter seats and dinner with friends.

■ Akasaka Excel Hotel Tokyu (Akasaka)
■ Shinjuku Prince Hotel (Shinjuku)

This kaiseki restaurant is tucked away in a quiet location like a hidden gem. The atmosphere was comfortable, but the details conveyed discipline and persistence.

The wait staff were very professional and thoughtful. Although they spoke very little English, they did their best to accommodate our every need.

The chef's kaiseki course was truly a unique experience. Each dish was meticulously prepared before us, carefully assembled on beautiful pottery, then served and explained in the best way that he could.

It was worth noting that the flavours were not particularly bold, but unexpectedly subtle, delicate and elegant, prepared in ways that drew out the essence of each ingredient. We were served a good variety of fish and seafood dishes that demonstrated perfect execution, which clearly requires a great level of mastery and effort.

The course left me feeling warm, nourished and satisfied, without the heaviness and glugginess one might feel after a large dinner. I was grateful for having been served such an amazing meal by the chef and his team.

I appreciated the level of detail given to every aspect of his restaurant: the selection of ingredients, elegant flavours, wonderful presentation, beautiful pottery, attentive staff, and comfortable atmosphere. It was a complete experience.

243920.longDescription:
Yotsuya Uemura, a Japanese restaurant in Arakicho, earned a one-star rating in  world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo for ten consecutive years, from 2012 to 2022. The owner trained at famous restaurants in Kyoto and Tokyo.　
Guests can enjoy authentic Japanese cuisine centered on Kyoto-style dishes, crafted with care by a dedicated owner whose expertise promises a truly refined experience. 

Offering nothing but omakase (chef's choice) course, each menu is thoughtfully adjusted for each group, adding a unique and flexible touch to the dining experience—one of the joys of a counter-style kappo restaurant.
Every dish is carefully crafted, from seasonal vegetables and seafood, including Kyoto vegetables, to the finishing touch of house-made desserts, showcasing meticulous attention to detail throughout.
One of the restaurant’s specialties is its exquisite eggplant dishes, particularly the ‘Eggplant with Sea Urchin,’ which attracts many visitors eager to taste the results of the chef’s meticulous preparation and honed skills.

The cozy interior can accommodate 7 guests at the counter seats only. Guests can enjoy a comfortable atmosphere while watching the whole cooking process and the owner-chef’s brilliant knife-handling skills.
Recommended for dates or casual dining.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Yotsuya-sanchome station (Exit 4), Marunouchi Line

244146.longDescription:
Born in Asakusa area, an up-and-coming young soba restaurant “Asakusa 16”. Everyday fresh seasonal ingredients from Tsukiji market, “Two-Eight Soba (20% Udon powder with 80% Soba powder)” homemade by our proprietress, with traditional Japanese Sake, are here ready for you to enjoy and relax.  This is the modern style soba restaurant where you could have a drink before enjoy soba.

The special prepared and selected soba is prepared with soba powder origin in Fukui, Nagano, and Ibaraki. Single soba powder or complicated combination may require depending on the statue of soba powder daily. To create the best taste of soba, instead of 100% soba powder, 20% of Udon powder is added to bring out be best favor. “There is no correct answer for soba. “Providing the stable taste is requiring every day effort, to bring you the best combination” is what our proprietress said.  In our Pocket Concierge Limited Special Course, you could taste the “Soba Mae” Japanese Sake together with seasonal dishes, finally cured by the warm of soba. Soup used in our soba is origin from thick-cut Japanese dry fish, the best company for soba, brining you a modern style Edo soba soup.

8 counter seats and 12 elevated Japanese style podiums are available for your choice. You could enjoy freely and relaxing atmosphere with your companies, and be free to have conversation with our friendly Chef and proprietress. For children, we are able to provide single dish at your choice, a good suggestion also for family dinning. Please visit us if you passed by Asakusa area.
※Japanese style podiums require you to take shoes off.

243687.longDescription: ""Restaurant HOMMAGE"" located in a calm residential area at Asakusa, a downtown of Tokyo. Born and raised in Asakusa, studied at world gourmet guide award restaurant in France, Chef Arai is now the owner chef of this world gourmet guide award French restaurant. Enjoy the refined French cuisine with the taste of JAPAN. ""Hommage"" is the meaning of ""respect, esteem and praise"" in French, what Chef Arai wants to deliver to the natura, producers, staff, families and all the guests. ""Sending the unique French cuisine by myself to the world"" at the capital of culture in Japan, Asakusa, this is the philosophy held by Chef Arai. Chef's selected course for lunch and dinner are reservable on Pocket Concierge. Only the seasonal ingredients picked around the world will be used, to prepare the inoperative dish served to you. Within a stylish building made with concrete, have a casual dining with no pressure. Dating or dinning with families are recommended. Also vegetarian menu is available upon request, foreigners with variable means. Let's visit this signature French restaurant and experience the emotions of Japan. Stylish construction with exterior not concrete standing. The soft drinking air is flowing in the main dining room. Recommended for Asakusa date and important seat with family. Vegetarian menu is also available (consultation required at time of booking), so you can use overseas guests visiting Asakusa safely. Everyone who visits can be regarded as a French restaurant representative of Asakusa who can keep a close eye on Japanese emotions in this town and this restaurant. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 【Kids Day】 · The third Sunday of every month (lunch time) is Kids Day Next Kids Day will be 16 Feb 2019, lunch time. · Children under the 7 are welcomed with ￥3,025 menu. For adult, please order ￥18,150/per person. ※ The date may vary from month to month, please contact us for details -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. A low calorie or vegetarian option may be prepared. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 8 years old. However, this age restriction is waved on our Kids’ day which is over the lunch time on the 3rd Sunday of every month. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, we do not have staff that speaks English. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available.
nearestStations: 12-minute walk from Asakusa Station (Exit 1), Tokyo Metro Ginza Line

ひとつずつが丁寧かつ、とてもとても美味しい。全てが本当に美味しかったですが、アミューズのトリュフオイルが薫るじゃがいものパンケーキと甘鯛の皮の香ばしさは絶品でした。
今日もう一度同じコースを頂きたいくらいです。

お店の佇まいや、店内へ一歩はいったときの雰囲気とても素敵でした。
二階へ案内されてからもとても落ち着いて食事ができ、なによりもとてもおいしかったです。
ありきたりな組み合わせではなく、一品一品説明してくださるたび驚きの連続でした。
スタッフの方々もマニュアル通りではない、親切で気持ちのよい接客で、私が満腹になってきたことに気づいてくださり量をへらし、ほかの同席者のほうへまわしてくれたことには本当に感謝と驚きでした。
細やかな心配りと次のお品がとても楽しみになるお料理、こんなステキなお店に出会えたことに感謝です。
またぜひお願いしたいです。
3度目の訪問です。今回も期待に違わず工夫されたお料理の数々でした。味、盛り付け方、お料理の説明、時間配分、そして帰りのお見送りまで、心のこもった応対で大変満足度の高いお店です。ごちそうさまでした。

どうしても、フレンチが食べたくて伺いました。今回で３回目の来店でした。
卵アレルギーの対応をして頂きありがとうございました。
日本料理店で卵アレルギーを伝えた所、ただの卵抜きで美味しく頂けなかった事があり実は少し不安だったのですが、とても美味しくお腹イッパイに食べれました。
ランチのクオリティーがディナーと変わらないのでは⁉︎とゆう内容とボリュームでとても満足した。
そう！前回、前々回より何か良い感じに変わった感じを受けました。進化してる感じデス。
また、伺いたいと思います。
味もサービスも素晴らしい！
ホスピタリティ溢れる接客に、目でも楽しませて頂いたお食事、大満足でした。漢方牛を初めていただきましたが、脂もさっぱりしていてとても美味しかったです。

ひとつひとつ、想像もできないようなとても凝ったお料理が出てきて、とても楽しめました。
出産前のいい思い出になりました。
フランス料理に興味をもっている息子と娘に食べさせたくて、家族4人で行きました。ジュースを頼む時点で選択肢の多さに喜び、最初のお食事から最後まで、美味しさと見た目の美しさに大喜びでした。お店の方の応対もよくて、また行きたいと思わせてくれるお店です。デザートがまた夏らしくて、冬は何がでるのか楽しみです。

良心的なお値段で、バラエティーに富んだお料理を提供してくださり、おなかも気持ちも大変満足できました。
普段の生活ではできないゆったりとした時間を過ごせ、スタッフの方の対応もよく気持ちがよかったです。
また利用させていただきたいと思います。
食事、サービスともに満点です。
毎回、素材そのものの拘りといい、素材同士のマリアージュといい、盛り付けといい、器といい、すべてにおいて五感を満足させてくれる最高の時間です！

創意工夫が感じられ、味も見た目もすばらいし料理を提供して頂きました。
帰りに玄関でマスターからご挨拶を頂きました。
帰りのタクシーもマナーのよいところを予約して頂きました。
全てが素晴らしかったです。
落ち着く雰囲気、和のニュアンスを取り入れた手の込んだ食事は、プレゼンテーションも味も素晴らしい。ワインペアリングはぜひすべき。
良かったです。
美味しかったのは当然として、食材の組み合わせや調理が、驚きと意外性に富んでいて、一皿一皿が楽しめました。

どのお料理をいただいてもとても美味しく、また見た目も大変美しく大満足です。
食後のデザートも浅草らしい人形焼風のお菓子を出していただき、面白いなと感じました。
食事、サービス共に満足出来たため

今まで食べてきたフランス料理とは違い、味はもちろん格段に美味しく、そして盛り付け方や食器に至るまで全てにおいて
楽しませて頂きました。
また、お料理に合うワインを紹介していただきワインを詳しく知らない私達でもワインも堪能出来ました。
フランス料理と言うとかしこまった印象を持ちますが、気軽にまた立ち寄りたいお店です。

・料理が美味しかった。
・嫁の苦手な食べ物への配慮もばっちり。
・着物の店員さんが優しかった
・花束プレゼントのサポートもばっちり
・美味しい料理、穏やかで温かい雰囲気、気持ちの良い時間を過ごすことが出来ました。
・関係ないですが、帰り道の浅草寺の雰囲気が良く、食事後の余韻を味わえました。素敵な立地です。


ありがとうございます！
また記念日に利用させてください！
文句のつけようがない、素晴らしく美味しいお料理でした。また、常人では思い付かないような独創的な食材の使い方に驚きました。是非また伺いたいと思います。

３度目ですが、相変わらずの美味しさと料理の美しさで大変満足しました。
同伴者が肉を食べられないですが、その辺りも配慮いただき助かります。
また来年も楽しみです。

全ての料理が、完璧でした。
次回はディナーで予約させて頂きます

お店の方の手際もよく、対応も丁寧で素晴らしかった。
去年利用したときはあまり丁寧でないというか、上から目線な接客の方がいたので今回は気持ちよく利用できました！
誕生日のケーキもとても華やかで美味しく、まさに完璧でした。
また利用させていただきます。
お料理の説明もとても丁寧でとても楽しめました。お店の雰囲気も堅苦しくなく、落ち着いて利用できて良かったです。
創意工夫された素晴らしい料理のクオリティー、スタッフの皆さんの温かなおもてなしで楽しめました。

どのお皿の味付けも予想外の美味なる驚きの連続で、それだけでも楽しく会話が弾みました。
また、メッセージプレートにも感激してもらい、記念日として大変素晴らしい時間になりました。

お料理一つ一つが大変美味しく、主人も私も大満足でした。
どれも丁寧に心を込めて作られているのが伝わってきました。
また、スタッフの方々の笑顔が印象的で気持ち良く食事をすることができました。
素敵な時間を過ごすことができました。またぜひ伺いたいです。

素晴らしい食事でした。食べたことのない手の込んだものばかりで非常に美味しかったです。ただ、店内がとても寒くて身体が冷えてしまいました。
次回は席を指定して行きたいと思います。

ひとつ、ひとつの品が、口に入れた瞬間、う〜ん美味しいと言ってしまうような味でした。
微妙な塩味も、プロといった感じ(*^_^*)

一つ一つのお料理が、驚くような組み合わせで、しかも素材の味を生かしながら作られていた。
出てくるスピードもちょうどよかった。

まず、お食事がどれもとても美味しかったです。
グラスワインの銘柄もちゃんとこだわりのあるセレクトになっていたと思いますし、
ホスピタリティに関しても非常に心地良い感覚を受けました。
自宅から5分のお店なので、また是非お邪魔したいと思っております。

とっても美味しく満足できました。
ただ、おすすめの追加料理のお値段が気になりました。
同伴者が会計したため分からないので、次回の参考に知りたかったです。

244261.longDescription: ""Kannonura"", is known as one of the most popular tourist spots in Tokyo is located behind the Senso-ji temple. In this area where the atmosphere of an old-fashioned street remains, it is said that there are many hidden, famous restaurants and eateries. This is where Yakitori TORI bien is located and is a restaurant with rising popularity since opening in August 2012. Restaurant owner Satoshi Handa honed his skills for 9 years at famous world gourmet guide award yakitori restaurant, Birdland. They use Kaiji Shamo chicken from Yamanashi prefecture. Limiting stock to cocks that have a stronger flavor and less fat than a hen, the chicken is purchased as a whole and prepared at the restaurant. The meat is very fresh, with rare parts such as Sori (a ping-pong ball sized muscle inside the pelvis), Tsuru (neck meat), and Kiwa, seasoned and prepared at its optimal state, and also grilled at the optimal temperature. The Omakase Course includes homemade liver pate, 4 types of seasonal appetizers, yakitori and grilled vegetables, salad and chicken soup. Handa himself went through the tasting process and selected Japanese sake and wine that will go well with the exquisite course, which includes originally-arranged liver pate inherited from Birdland and pepper-grilled chicken thigh that goes well with sauce. In addition, the last dish, ramen noodles made with Kaiji Shamo chicken soup, is also popular. Receiving advice from popular ramen shops within the metropolitan area, Handa decided to use homemade noodles. In the vivid store where the wall is painted in a vermillion color, there are 18 counter seats and 4 table seats. Handa’s warm personality while grilling yakitori makes the atmosphere homey and many use this place for a girls’ night out or for dates. The bright and fun atmosphere along with delicious yakitori in an extraordinary space will definitely make your Kannonura night a special one. *The restaurant is available for private dinner and parties (16 -19 guests). For more details, please fill out contact form.
nearestStations: 12-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Ginza Line Asakusa Station Exit 1

recommendations.comment: 確かな技術による絶妙な火入れの串はもちろん、気さくで温かい店主の人柄や居心地の良い雰囲気で満足度が高いです

どの料理も美味しく楽しめました。ありがとうございました。
店員さんがとても丁寧で気持ちよく利用させていただきました。
Very good
今回も美味しくいただきました。苦手な食べ物にも対応いただきありがとうございました。また、お伺いします。
very good experience
I enjoyed all, and they were very patient with me.
We had a great and enjoyable night. Even the portion of each course is small, we were satisfied and very full after the meal. Thank you chef.
とても美味しかったです。スタッフさんの対応も良かったです。
最初から最後まで鶏をここまで美味しく食べることが出来たのは驚きでした。是非また行きたいです。
鶏も美味しかったですが、野菜がとても美味しかったです。
鶏肉を色々な楽しみ方でいただきました。どれも見た目、味共に楽しませていただき大満足です。また訪問したいと思います。
Great yakitori
the chicken breast was absolutely the best. good service. friendly chef.
店主さんやお店の方々の雰囲気がとても優しく明るく、料理も美味しかったです！
大変おいしくいただきました。おすすめの神亀ひやおろしのぬる燗が料理にぴったり、お酒と箸がすすみます
苦手な食材に対応していただき、ありがとうございました。焼鳥もお刺身も前菜もお食事もデザートのプリンも大変おいしく頂きました。焼いている様子を拝見するのも楽しかったです。またお伺いします。
お店の雰囲気もほどよく美味しかったです。
excellent food

早めに到着したため、オーナーの方にもお席の手配を手伝っていただき、大変ありがたかったです
食事もとても美味しかったです
前回と同じコースでしたが、串の種類が違っていて良かったです。
お酒の種類も多くリーズナブルで、非常によかったです。
焼き加減、塩加減、どれも素晴らしく、美味しくいただきました。追加注文したうずらも、とてもよかったです。初めてお伺いしたにもかかわらず、ご主人、スタッフの皆様が、自分の名前を呼んで対応してくださり、嬉しく思いました。ありがとうございました。
焼鳥こそ食の文化遺産と思わせる逸品
Food delicious, excellent service.
ラーメンが美味しかったです。追加で頂いた赤身が好みでした。落ち着いた雰囲気で、ゆったり過ごせました。
雰囲気は落ち着いておりましたが堅苦しくありませんでした、またコース内容もボリュームがあり満足でした。
安定してとても美味しかったです。

お料理もおいしくお店の雰囲気も素晴らしく、店主や店員さんの応対も気持ちよかったです。
薦めていただいたシャンパンもお料理にマッチしていて
夫婦二人とも大変楽しい時間を過ごさせていただきました。
ありがとうございました。
ぜひ機会があればまた伺います。
友人で食べ歩きが趣味の方がいますので紹介させていただきます。
今後ともよろしくお願いいたします。

一つずつ丁寧に焼かれていてとても満足出来ました。
お酒は日本酒よりはワインよりで自分には未知の世界でしたが、また次回はワイン好きな連れと一緒に来たいと思わせてくれるお店でした。
大将はじめ従業員さんたちの人柄も、料理以上に最高でした❗
A nice place for people to have party with friends after one day’s work. The chief is friendly. I will be here again next time.ime.
大変美味しく満足いたしました。
とても美味しかったです。

Plenty of Food to eat was served. Food was great.
Personal attendants were very kind and professional.
They tried to explain about food(not only to me but to other local guest) 
That was a very nice dinner.
Every dish was delicious.

今回、「〆の一品がついたおまかせコース」をいただきましたが、焼鳥だけでなく、初めに出てくるパテと前菜も美味しく、コース全体を通して満足感のある内容でした。

特に、〆のラーメンに関しては、ラーメン屋が開けるのではないかと思うぐらいのクオリティーで、友人も絶賛しておりました。

しっかりと食べたい方は、〆の一品までつけたほうが良いですね。

家路につく際、浅草寺の脇道を通って帰りましたが、右手にはライトアップされた浅草寺、左手には少しスカイツリーも見ることができ、ちょっとした観光気分にも浸ることがでしました。

デートスポットとしても良いですね。

ごちそうさまでした！

244127.longDescription:
Daigo, a famous vegetarian restaurant provides Shojin cuisine(Japanese style vegetarian food) . Founded in 1950, it has specialized in vegetables and tofu dishes, impressed customers' minds and bodies. 

Fresh green in Spring, autumn leaves in Fall, this 1 starred restaurant makes you feel the real beauty of the season in the natural space with garden. Owing by this, you could put all the hustle and bustle of a city behind and enjoy the meal comfortably, even in Ginza and Roppongi area, the city center of Tokyo. 

The cuisine provided by Yusuke Nomura chef, he understands the ingredients deeply and makes maximum use of the gifts from the land. In a rapidly changing society, the chefs would like to make every guest feel the enjoyment, importance and dainties throughout vegetarian cuisines. The menu is changed every 3 weeks, with his astute ability, you could taste the long history of Japanese vegetarian cuisine and enjoy the difference of each season.

Being popular among vegetarian, some of the Shojin restaurants use dash of dried‐bonito or egg. While Daigo could provide the food without any animal products if booked in advance. Even foreign celebrity visits here for vegan diet.

Furthermore, the rooms of Daigo are all private rooms. There is a large private room accommodates a maximum of 58 people and a private tea room. Can be used for any occasions or a tea ceremony. 

Delights you with the food provided with sincerely hospitality. It is a only place makes you feel peaceful in the center of Tokyo without doubt!

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245232.longDescription:
A 10-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Roppongi Itchome Station takes you to Patous, a French restaurant perched on the second floor of a building on Uekizaka Slope, a few steps from Gaien Higashi Street, in Azabudai. Previously located on Nakayamate Street in Kobe, the French restaurant renowned for its exquisite seasonal dishes was relocated from Kobe to Azabudai in August 2020 for a fresh start.

Patous is helmed by Chef Yoshiteru Yamaguchi, who was born in 1967 and trained at Comme Chinois in Kobe, COTE DOR in Hokkaido, COTE DOR in Tokyo, and restaurants in France. Then, he opened his own restaurant, Patous, in Kobe in 1999. The restaurant was relocated first to Nakayamate Street in Kobe in 2003 and eventually to Azabudai in Tokyo.
The restaurant was named after Pyrenean Mountain Dogs, which are bred, originally in the Pyrenees region in France, to protect herds of livestock, shepherds, and their families from predators such as bears and wolves and locally known as “le Patou” (derived from the word for shepherd in old French). The purity and faithfulness of these white dogs represent the culinary world which the chef aims for.
Patous offers French dishes featuring different seasonal ingredients. High-quality and reliable ingredients are delivered by producers with whom the experienced chef has long-standing relationships. The seasonal menus, ranging from white asparagus and lamb in spring to “Soup of Peach and Celery” and “Cutlassfish Grilled with Potatoes and Foie Gras” in summer and game meat in winter, attract connoisseurs every season. The simple yet exquisite dishes meet the expectations of guests looking for authentic French cuisine.
The wine list offers a wide selection of French wines, mostly imported from Burgundy to match the food menu mainly consisting of dishes of the same origin.
All the dishes are served on white plates manufactured by J.L Coquet (in France) to give diners a sense of warm satisfaction after meals.

Designed in a feminine style with white walls, a beautifully grained wooden cupboard, and white tablecloths, the restaurant retains the same atmosphere as it did in Kobe. Its cozy dining area, with three two-seat tables and one four-seat table, is small enough for the chef and proprietress to pay attention to each guest to give them a sense of being looked after. In addition, the restaurant is designed for business dinners, intimate meals with your friends, dates, and gourmet gatherings.
Guests are welcomed by ceramic Pyrenean Mountain Dogs on a lower shelf of the glassware closet.
The excellent dishes of the chef and the warm hospitality of the proprietress will make the experience at Patous even more memorable.

245550.longDescription:
Four minutes’ walk from Tokyo Metro Azabu-juban Station, Yakitori Matsumoto is located on the first floor of a small building in the vibrant neighborhood of Azabu-juban with renowned restaurants of different cuisines including yakitori (Japanese skewered chicken), gaining a lot of attention as a franchise of a popular restaurant, Yakitori Matsumoto Nishinakasu , in Fukuoka. The yakitori grill is entrusted to the skillful hands of Chef Shuto Niizumi, who was apprenticed to Owner-Chef Kojiro  Matsumoto at Yakitori Matsumoto Nishinakasu but singled out for his extraordinary grilling and seasoning techniques and set up in business by his master. Along with Chef Kazuki Hasegawa, who was also appreciated for his skills in preparing à la carte dishes, Chef Niizumi opened a franchise restaurant in Azabu-juban in 2023 to uncover the charm of yakitori.

The premium prix-fixe menu features premium chicken breeds carefully selected from around Japan and grilled on skewers over Tosa Binchotan charcoal (nine to 10 skewers) and seasonal chicken dishes such as braised chicken and chicken liver pâté. What is worth noting about this restaurant is that it offers different cuts of premium breeds from different sources, such as Shikano Jidori chicken thighs from Tottori, Batten chicken tenderloins from Nagasaki, Tamba red chicken gizzard from Hyogo, and Ise red chicken hearts from Mie. In particular, Shikano Jidori chicken from Tottori is rarely seen on the menus of yakitori restaurants in Tokyo. Selected by Chef Niizumi, different cuts of different breeds are prepared in different ways from day to day to ensure that guests can enjoy top-quality flavors whenever they visit the restaurant. All ingredients are carefully selected, including not only chicken but also ginkgo nuts from Aichi, Tenkeiko shiitake mushrooms from Tokushima, and Isa rice from Kagoshima, which is cooked in earthen pots and served as the second-last course . In addition, the yakitori sauce is constantly topped up with additional ingredients, following the secret recipe only known to Chef Niizumi. The sake list is curated to match each chicken skewer, such as Toyo Bijin from Yamaguchi for Tamba red chicken gizzard from Hyogo, Asamayama Junmai Okarakuchi from Gunma for Hinai Jidori chicken tails from Akita, and Koueigiku from Saga for Batten chicken tenderloins from Nagasaki. These selections are all about highlighting the flavors of chicken.

The black interior is elevated by the striking contrast with the U-shaped vermilion counter (seating up to 12 guests), while the bonsai plants and the Tiffany cups used to serve homemade pudding for dessert add an elegant touch to the room. Visit Yakitori Matsumoto for various occasions, from private to business, and enjoy each bite of the luxury chicken dishes.

243683.longDescription:
Elegant French which imaging the quiet and luxurious residential area ""16th arrondissement"", is located 3 minutes on foot from Azabu Juban Station on Tokyo Metro and Toei Oedo Line. ""Alie Blanche""'s chef Mr. Ogawa had been trained at several world gourmet guide awarded restaurants in France. His cuisine is loved by females as the minimum use of butter, cream etc.

Specialty is ""Foie gras poele, Sherry vinegar sauce"". Using the finest duck foie gras brought up carefully in the French land village, the pudding-like texture gives the highest quality of mouth-feel, attracting guests with is dense flavor and sweetness. This """"mysterious foie gras"" as the specialty of Alie Blanche is served in every course.

Warmful lighting makes the dining room a elegant space, reservation for dining with your special one will be a great choice.Enjoying the live cooking at counter seating for members only, will be a unforgettable experience to you for dating and anniversary celebration. Let's have the meaningful dining causally.

courses.summary:
Japanese wine is now attracting attention.
In recent years, Japanese wines have gained worldwide acclaim for their quality and diversity. Wineries throughout Japan are producing excellent wines, and they are now beginning to be recognized to the extent that they have won numerous awards at international competitions and are even on the wine lists of three-star restaurants abroad.

At Alie Blanche, we have prepared a course menu that suggests the best food pairings that highlight the unique characteristics of Japanese wines.

244119.localizedAddress: 1F, Rose House Azabujuban, 2-7-2, Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244119.longDescription: There is a Japanese restaurant awards by world gourmet guide award every year, located at 5 minutes away from Azabu-Juban Station on Tokyo Metro Nanboku Line and Toei Oedo Line. ""Azabu Kadowaki"" offers you cuisine made with seasonal ingredients. A space that have attention to details, from the interior setting to tableware and cookware, dating or dinning with friends are fitted to be held in counters and private room respectively. Owner Kadowaki had worked at the famous ""Tukiji-Uemura"", ""Kasumigaseki Kamogawa"" in Kyoto etc.. Using seasonal ingredients in Japan and from the whole world, serving guests the ""Kadowaki style Japanese"" that leaves memories to its visitors. Specialty is ""Truffle cooked rice"" avaliable for all courses. ""Azabu Kadowaki"" is a originator of truffle rice. To the rice cooked in the pot, extravagant amount of truffle is added , bringing out rich fragrance, encompassing the whole space, favorited by numerous guests. ※ Awarded 3 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 *Children Policy Children over 13-year-old is possible to dine here. Need to choose 1 course as an adult. 【Nearby Hotels】 ■ Nogizaka ""The Ritz-Carlton Tokyo"" ■ Roppongi ""Grand Hyatt Tokyo"" ■ Akasaka ""ANA Intercontinental Hotel Tokyo"" ■ Shibuya ""Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel"" ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Yes, we have private dining room(s). For a party of 3 or more, the private room fee is complimentary. But in case of less than 2 people, an additional private room charge of 12,100 yen (including tax and service charge) will be charged. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can accommodate a party of up to 6 people. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? The private dining room offers table(s) and chairs (Western style). ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room(s). ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 13 years of age or children who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We are happy to assist you. However, please be aware that our English may be limited. ■ Are menus available in other languages? We have a brief description of our food in English. ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Unfortunately, photos or videos are not allowed in the restaurant in general. Photos of food are welcome.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Azabu-Juban Station, Exit 4 (Tokyo Metro Nanboku Line)

本日は本当にありがとうございました。二人ともこれまでで一番の食事だったと感激しております。また何かの機会に食べに行けたらと思います。ありがとうございました。
とても美味しかったです。

Every ingredient is amazing, and the white truffles are handled very well.
One of the favorite dishes is steamed egg with crab meat and crab butter.
I would like to book again and introduce to my friends.
トリュフのお造り、ご飯は噂通り未体験の世界でした。また、他の料理もこれまで経験したことのないような、和を超えた独自の世界感で大変堪能させて頂きました。そして、幾度となくお祝いのお言葉を頂き、初めての訪問でしたが主賓も大変喜んでくれました。また伺いたいと思います。
お料理はどれも美味しく店内の雰囲気も落ち着いていて素敵でした。カウンターでしたが親方の気配りも行き届いておりまた伺いたいと感じさせていただけるお店でした。

彼女の誕生日お祝いで初めてお伺いしましたが、
門脇様に大変お気遣いいただき誠に有難うございました。また、料理を一品一品出すタイミングも絶妙で、大変美味しく楽しい時間を過ごさせていただきました。大変有難うございました。また是非お伺いさせていただきたく思います。

連れて行った人に大変喜ばれ、良かったです。ありがとうございました。
お料理だけでなくお店のしつらえもとても良かったです。
松露超美味
素材もさることながら一品ずつ工夫をこらした料理ばかりで大満足です。
毎年、冬の季節にカニを食べるを楽しみしております。カニ以外にもすずきなど大変美味しく頂きました。ありがとうございます。
この時季、河豚の唐揚げや蟹は絶品でした。河豚の唐揚げの大きさ美味さ、蟹の身の甘みと蟹味噌の美味さ、そしてかどわきと言えばトリュフご飯の〆の美味さ、どれもこれも満足度100％でした。美味しい料理の数々ありがとうございました。
季節野菜と牛肉、フカヒレの唐揚げ、トリュフづくしの料理の数々、美味しかったの一言では言い表せないくらいの満足度でした。また、カウンターとキッチンの調和のとれた作りにも感動させて頂きました。

価格の割に量が少なく、年配の人でも完食できる適量であった。

244119.reservationTerms: ＜Please be sure to read the "Frequently Asked Questions" on the restaurant's reservation page and the following information to the end before submitting your reservation.＞ ■Cancellation policy Please note that cancellation fees apply as follows if you cancel or change the reservation. From 7 business days prior to the date of the reservation: 50% of the total reservation amount From 3 business days prior to the date of the reservation: 100% of the total reservation amount Please understand that no refunds will be given regardless of the reason for cancellation, such as sudden illness, change of itinerary, change of schedule, or change in the number of people. ■ Please note that if more than 30 minutes have passed since your scheduled reservation time, your reservation will be treated as a cancellation. We kindly ask that you arrive with sufficient time to spare. ■Requests for Reservations: Please make sure to confirm the date and time of your reservation before submitting your reservation request. We have received a number of changes to the date of your visit due to a mistake in the date of your reservation request. Please be careful. ■We welcome children aged 13 and above, as long as they can enjoy the same course as adults. ■Restrictions: Please inform us of any food allergies or dietary restrictions when you make the reservation in the "Requests" column in advance with the details. The restaurant only accepts your food restriction request in advance, no same-day request will be accepted. Kindly note that your food restriction items in the course you have selected can not be replaced to other dishes if you inform us on same-day. If you have any restrictions, please advise the details in the "Requests column” for each guests and suggest who/ what you can't eat/ how much the level of restriction. (ex) Guest 1: 〇〇 Guest 2: △△ ※In case you would like to add guests, please indicate food restriction information upon you send the request. (ex) I would like to add one guest. She/he has no food restrictions. ※Please understand in advance it could be charged additional charge to serve the alternative food to accommodate your restriction. ※Kindly understand it could be happen to refuse your request if you have serious combined allergies considering your safety. ■ We regret that we are unable to accommodate vegetarian requests. Please kindly note that even if dashi (broth) is acceptable, we are still unable to accommodate such requests. ■If you have any questions after making a reservation, please contact us through My Page or the "Contact Us" link in the e-mail confirming your reservation. We do not accept inquiries by phone. We may contact you by email or phone to confirm your reservation. Please include an email or phone number where we can contact you to confirm your reservation. If you would like to change the date or time, please check the reservation calendar for the date and time you would like to change and indicate so. ■About proxy reservations: If the person making the reservation and the person visiting the restaurant are different, please select "Reserving for another person" to make a reservation. If a Japanese person is making a reservation on behalf of an overseas guest, please be sure to indicate so in the "Request" column. For likes, dislikes, and allergies, please provide information about the person coming to the restaurant in the form of "Dislikes/allergies of food items" above. ■ Time table: There is 2 rounds with about 2-hour time-limit per round. It might vary according to the reservation situation. For reservation between 5:30pm to 6pm, please finish the meal by 8pm. For reservations between 8:15 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., there is no waiting area, so please arrive on time for your reservation. ■Children policy: Children may come to the restaurant if they are 13 years old or older and eat the same course as adults. ■About private room request: An additional private room charge of 12,100 yen (including tax and service charge) will be charged. However, for a party of 3 or more, the private room fee will not be charged. ■Anniversary service option: You can order a cake with your message with 8,250 yen (tax included). There is no free message plate. If you are visiting for an anniversary occasion, please fill in the following information in the "Requests" column when making a reservation. 1: Details of the anniversary (birthday, wedding anniversary, etc.) 2: Would you like to order a cake 8,250 yen (tax included)? Yes or No. ( If yes, please suggest your request message to put on the cake.) *No same-day request will be accepted. *Flowers cannot be arranged. *Please note that we are unable to temporarily hold any flowers or items that you bring in. ■Drink Corkage: Please refrain from bringing your own beverages. ■ For 1 person dining: For 1 person reservations, please check the calendar, and if you can select 1 person, you can apply on the date. In that case, for 1 person dining, an additional charge of 6,050 yen will be added. ■ Mineral Water or tea(green tea ) is not complimentary. ■If you break anything in the restaurant, you will have to pay for it. ■Please be aware that you may be charged for any damage to glasses or other items during your meal. ■Truffle rice served at the end of the course can be taken home. In this case, a souvenir box fee of 800 yen (tax included) will be charged. ■If you have any comments or suggestions, please use the link in the email from Pocket Concierge after your visit.

244654.longDescription:
Referral-only, "Azabu kumasan " in Osaka's Kita Shinchi district does not publicize its address and phone number. Now, this mysterious yet popular meat kappo cuisine makes its way to Tokyo. The referral only restaurant "Azabu kumasan " opened in 2018 in an area of Azabu Juban known only to those in the know, and has been mesmerizing meat lovers ever since. 
Chef Shota Murakami learned his technique for Japanese cuisine at the Japanese ryotei, "Kioicho Fukudaya," and honed his skills at various restaurants in and around Ginza before becoming chef. The multi-course kaiseki course features Japanese black wagyu, and is a pleasurable feast of Japanese and Western fusion dishes that highlights Chef Murakami's seasoned Japanese cooking artistry. He explains, "We provide a kaiseki style multi-course meal of meat that is neither just grilled meat, nor just steak." And because he uses meat from various places including Hokkaido, Sendai, Kobe and Kagoshima, comparing the different varieties is an experience unique to " Azabukumasan." The cutlet sandwich is a popular dish that can be enjoyed year-round, more specifically, the Chateaubriand Cutlet Sandwich "Kuma Sand" with the logo imprint right on it. For drinks, they offer champagne and old vintage wines. Customers can enjoy pairing their drinks with the kaiseki meat dishes.
As it is a referral and reservation-only restaurant, the entrance has a private stairway, and for the uninitiated it looks like you cannot enter. The interior has a black color scheme, with copper that looks rusted, for a sophisticated and stylish ambience. There are 7 seats at the counter, and a private room with a table for 6. Enjoy a refined meat kaiseki meal with family, friends, or colleagues in a private setting.The restaurant also provide English menus, so foreign guests can feel comfortable tasting the exquisite flavors of Japanese black wagyu.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Azabu Juban Station, Exit 4(Tokyo Metro Namboku Line)

244980.longDescription:
A one-minute walk from the station, Azabujuban Ozaki is located in a quiet area near Azabu Street. Here, chef Ichiro Ozaki, who fell in love with the town of Azabujuban, “where the good old days and the new come and go”, shows off his skills.

He entered the world of cooking at the age of 19, beginning an apprenticeship at a Ginza kappo restaurant and continuing until he was 25. After three years of study at a Japanese eatery, he joined a sushi restaurant run by his parents; seven and a half years later, he became independent and opened Azabujuban Ozaki in 2006.

Ozaki, who developed his skills at both a Japanese restaurant and a sushi restaurant, puts his mark on a cooking style called sushi kappo. While traditional sushi restaurants usually serve appetizers such as sashimi and nigiri sushi, at Azabujuban Ozaki, the chef serves sushi at the end. In his words, "cooking is a once-in-a-lifetime experience," and goes to Toyosu Market every day for the best fish and seafood of the day -- it is no exaggeration to say that the most delicious Japanese ingredients of the season, such as natural eel, sea urchin, shinko, hairy crab and kobako crab are all on the table. Tuna has a special place at this table, and has been used for many years without losing its rank. 

The restaurant offers more than 20 varieties of sake and more than 10 kinds of shochu, as well as about 15 kinds of wine that Ozaki likes, mostly from France. Beer and sake are poured into tin cups from Kyoto Seikado for guests to enjoy; meanwhile, bowls are original pieces ordered from the makers of Bizen and Oribe ware.

Above all, Azabujuban Ozaki is a place where guests can enjoy memorable food in a spacious private room. There are 6 private rooms (hosting up to 5 diners), and 6 counter seats of which 3 can be reserved for private use. Sushi Kappo is where guests can relax and enjoy Japanese refined sushi courses with family, friends, or a date.
