244129.longDescription:
In December 2016, Crony opened along Roppongi Dori in Nishi-Azabu as a co-founded  restaurant by Kazutaka Ozawa, who served for many years as the general manager of the acclaimed fine-dining restaurant Quintessence and in 2025 became the first Japanese recipient of the Best Sommelier Award at a leading Asian restaurant awards program, and Michihiro Haruta, a chef who trained at some of the world’s most renowned starred restaurants. The restaurant’s name means “a lifelong companion to share tea with,” expressing the idea of friends who feel comfortable being together at all times and can enjoy open, unreserved conversation. In February 2021, the restaurant was relocated and renewed in its current location in Higashi-Azabu.  

Chef Michihiro Haruta is a rising culinary talent who combines extensive experience with exceptional skill. He has trained at some of the world’s most renowned restaurants, including Quintessence, the three stars Ledoyen in Paris, the three-star Saison in San Francisco, the three stars MAAEMO in Norway, and the two stars KADEAU in Denmark. Drawing on his extensive experience in French, Nordic, and American cuisines, Chef Haruta creates dishes rich in seasonality, each infused with sincere appreciation for every ingredient and producer. In 2023, the restaurant was also recognized by a world-renowned gourmet guide as a restaurant promoting sustainability.  

The course begins with a cup of tea, followed by a progression of seasonal dishes delicately crafted using ingredients sourced through visits to producers across Japan, with careful consideration given to the global environment. Another defining feature of Crony is its approach to bread—typically something enjoyed between courses—which is instead presented as one of the featured dishes of the course. The San Francisco–style sourdough features an exquisite balance between a fragrant, savory crust and a moist, chewy interior. While it is commonly flavored with beer in its place of origin, at Crony it is infused with sake. In addition, butter is made from sake lees that would otherwise go unused, addressing food loss concerns, and is served as a signature accompaniment to the bread.  
The course menu evolves gradually, with all dishes completely refreshed approximately every two and a half months. The culinary world woven by Crony is so engaging that guests are drawn to witness its subtle evolution without waiting for the seasons to change. The expertly curated pairings by General Manager  Kazutaka  Ozawa further expand this world, and since its opening, Crony has captivated the palates of distinguished guests not only in Japan but from around the world as well.  

The interior is designed with high ceilings and expansive glass windows, earthen walls, and wooden furnishings arranged in an organic style, complemented by comfortable lighting that creates an atmosphere of elegance and warmth. Guests are invited to enjoy the refined culinary experience at Crony in a variety of settings, from date nights and casual dining to private rooms for business occasions.  

※Awarded two stars in the world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025.

245491.longDescription:
A 3-minute walk from Akabanebashi Station, Higashi Azabu Ichikawa sits in a tranquil neighborhood of Higashi Azabu, offering a peaceful retreat despite its location amidst the hustle and bustle of central Tokyo.  Here you are welcomed by Chef Tatsuya Ichikawa with a warm smile, Japanese dishes filled with seasonal flavors, and exquisite wines and sake.

Hailing from Aichi Prefecture, Chef Ichikawa came to Tokyo to master culinary arts, for he had been fascinated by the restaurant industry while serving as the manager of a local chicken skewer restaurant and enjoying first-hand opportunities to listen to the voices of customers.  He worked as a fish broker at the Tsukiji fish market to deepen knowledge about seafood and then joined the opening team of Ebisu Kifu, which immediately won a one-star award. After honing his culinary skills at the restaurant for eight years, he opened Higashi Azabu Ichikawa in September 2023.

The prix-fixe menu consists of 8 to 10 courses, from appetizer to dessert, all of which feature carefully selected seasonal ingredients. The Japanese eels are sourced from Isshiki in the chef’s home prefecture of Aichi. Large eels weighing about 700 g are selected and grilled without being boiled. With a crispy outside and tender and juicy inside, they are turned into a summer specialty. In winter, Gin No Kamo, a branded duck, from Shingo, Aomori, is grilled with a sweet sauce over charcoal. Other high-end seasonal ingredients, such as snow crabs, maitake mushrooms, and puffer fish, are also incorporated to create luxury full-course meals that please the eye as well as the taste buds.

As indicated by its motto, inviting guests to enjoy Japanese cuisine with sake and wines at our restaurant, the drink menu also offers an exquisite selection of sake and wines. The sake cellar has over 30 varieties of famous brands in stock, including Mimurosugi from Nara, Hakurakusei from Miyagi, Kamonishiki from Niigata, Isojiman from Shizuoka, and Aramasa from Akita, to satisfy the tastes and preferences of guests. The unique selection of wines, including champagnes and red and white Bourgogne wines, are curated by the chef, who is also certified as a wine sommelier, to go well with his Japanese dishes.

Transformed from an over-70-year-old historic house, the restaurant looks atmospheric. With an eye-catching hinoki cypress counter (seating up to eight guests), the dining room is woody and comfortable. The historic home-turned Japanese restaurant nestled in the tranquil Higashi Azabu is recommended for various occasions, such as enjoying intimate meals with your family or friends and entertaining overseas visitors with the elegant interior as well as delicious dishes and drinks. Please enjoy seasonal dishes in a relaxing Japanese-style setting at Higashi Azabu Ichikawa.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Nakanobashi Exit of Akabanebashi Station on the Toei Oedo Line

My girlfriend and I are visiting from the U.S. and decided to dine at Higashi Azabu Ichikawa to celebrate our 5-year anniversary. This was our first time experiencing an omakase/kaiseki, and the bar has now been set tremendously high! From the moment we walked in to the cozy 9-person counter restaurant, we were greeted with warmth and a fabulous selection of drinks, including some of the best champagne and sake we've ever had. The 8-dish procession that followed was one triumph after another. Each ingredient was honored to its fullest and often showcased in an artful simplicity. The team's timing was skillfully executed, and though there was a slight language barrier, Chef Ichikawa took extra lengths to explain each dish to us in English, which was very appreciated. Some highlights for us were the deconstructed sushi roll with egg ribbons, the squid cooked on stone, and the anchovy roll. The strawberry mochi nearly had my girlfriend in tears of joy by dessert. Thank you so much for this amazing meal! We'll cherish this experience for a long time.

245404.longDescription:
The Japanese cuisine restaurant Senshin is located along Azabu East Street, near Akabanebashi Station in Tokyo.
Owner-chef Tatsuya Tsushima, approaches his cuisine with great sincerity in helming the restaurant. After working at a famous restaurant in Tokyo, Chef Tsushima honed his skills at the Ginza- Uchiyama, and was also involved in the establishment of Chisou Kouryu. He opened Senshin in July 2022.

The name Senshin comes from a four-character idiom that means single-minded dedication with one’s whole heart.  Rather than simply piling on premium ingredients, each ingredient is carefully and painstakingly finessed to bring out the best flavors. Furthermore, the chef listens to the guests and makes every effort to meet to their needs.

The meticulous workmanship is obvious in the homemade black sesame steamed yokan served as a dessert to close out the meal. The process of roasting, grinding, steaming, and packaging black sesame seeds is done repeatedly, taking two days to complete. The one-of-a-kind dishes that incorporate the ambition “to have customers to eat something made right down to the last bite, and to want to eat it again” make food foodies’ palates sing with delight.

The freshest ingredients are sourced from producers from Hokkaido to Kagoshima as well as from trusted brokers with whom the Chef Tsushima has long-standing partnerships. He always remembers to express his thankfulness to the producers, saying, “I will use what you have made with gratitude.”

The sake list includes 25 to 30 varieties, including Senshin from Niigata’s Asahi Shuzo, which reads phonetically the same as the restaurant’s name; Katsuyama (En and Ken) from Tsushima’s hometown of Sendai; Kakurei from Niigata; and Oyama from Yamagata. The lineup is stocked with a wide variety of dishes created by Chef Tsushima, so we recommend that you convey for likes to the chef and leave it in his hands. There is also be a full array of non-alcoholic beverages, including Royal Blue Tea, a high-end tea served in first class on international flights, and Honki Juice, which is available exclusively at restaurants.

The concept of the interior design is “to let customers enjoy the restaurant as if they were going to a friend’s home”. It features a white-wood L-shaped counter (8 seats) and a private room (2 to 6 people). Enjoy Senshin as a Japanese restaurant where you can enjoy your favorite cuisine, whether for personal occasions with family, friends, or as a couple, or for business entertainment.
nearestStations: About 3 minutes walk from Nakanobashi exit of Akabanebashi station on Toei Oedo line.

244670.longDescription:
Sugaya" was established in 2018 in the Higashi-Azabu area near Akabanebashi Station, close to Tokyo Tower. Chef Takayuki Sugaya, honed his skills for a total of 22 years in "Kazama Sushi Place," "Sushi Shin" in Nishi-Azabu, "Sushi Arai," and "Sushi Shō," which is a group of affiliated restaurants. After gaining experience in several famous restaurants, he achieved independence in Azabu, an area familiar to him from his skill honing days.
The Omakase course consists of 4–5 side dishes and approximately 15 pieces of sushi. "When guests come to my sushi restaurant, I want them to enjoy nigirizushi." With this philosophy, Chef Sugaya focuses only on simple side dishes. Thanks to this simplicity, diners can appreciate the high level skills underpinning the flavors of the seafood with each fish and shellfish sampled, such as the aging and curing of each individual fish and the heating of steamed dishes. The ingredients include tuna from tuna merchant "Yamayuki" and all other seafoods from Toyosu Market. The sushi rice is prepared with a blend of four varieties of "Yokoi's Vinegar" rice vinegars and red vinegars, giving depth while achieving a delicate balance that does not interfere with the flavors of the seafood. The hand shaping that has each grain of rice in its place before it melts in the mouth is also superb. With a wide range of alcoholic beverages, including 10 varieties of sake, 20 varieties of champagne, and 40 varieties of wine, dishes can be enjoyed with the alcohol of your choice.
The restaurant, fitted with a counter of Kiso hinoki cypress with a fresh look, is a luxurious space where Chef Sugaya attentively welcomes only eight guests. The chairs, custom made to allow guests to relax in comfort, are the work of artisan furniture makers from Hida. The mild manners of he and the proprietress's warm service melt away stress completely, allowing guests the leisure to savor the delights of the palate to their hearts' content without even noticing the time. Even after establishing his own restaurant, Chef Sugaya continues to sincerely pursue further sushi knowledge. Tasting his ever evolving sushi, shaped by hand, you are sure to experience the essence of the professional sushi chef.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Akabanebashi Station (Toei-Oedo Line)

245259.longDescription:
Since opening in 2015 as an introduction-only restaurant, Suikouan has steadily built up a track record as a restaurant that values the framework of Japanese cuisine in accordance with the principles of  ”Yusoku kojitsu”.

Suikoan is helmed by Chef Tomohiro Ishida, born in Tokyo in 1979. He worked at Kyoto Kitcho and served as a sous chef at Kitcho Arashiyama Main Location from 2008 to 2014.

Chef Ishida offers Japanese dishes featuring seasonal ingredients to celebrate the seasonal bounty of Japan. With deep respect for the fundamental concepts of Japanese culture, such as the practices of court and samurai culture and the 24 seasonal divisions of the lunar calendar, the chef strives to deliver not only the flavors of the four seasons but also the spirit of Japanese culture through his dishes, such as an assortment of appetizers that changes every month. The menu features seasonal ingredients from around Japan, including bamboo shoots from Yamashiro, Kyoto, in the spring, sweetfish from Kyoto in the summer, and Taiza crab in the winter. As for the rice, Ryu No Hitomi, a brand of rice known for its large grain, is sourced from Gifu and cooked several different ways. First, slightly undercooked rice is served with wet chopsticks made of cedar to show chakaiseki cuisine’s spirit of hospitality.
The sake list offers a wide selection of rare Japanese sake, including Juyondai. In addition, Suiko, a private label sake, is brewed by Hakusen Shuzo, the same brewery as Kitcho’s, in Gifu. The wine list includes 20 to 30 labels of wines selected by the dedicated sommelier, mainly from Burgundy in France.

After the relocation in June 2023, the restaurant will have a new 8-seat counter where diners can enjoy the live cooking experience. Come visit "Suikouan" to enjoy food with friends and the seasons.
nearestStations: 6 minutes on foot from Akabanebashi Station on the Toei Subway Oedo Line

243967.longDescription:
The concept of this restaurant is ""the contrast between classic and modern"". Here guests can enjoy both the ""classic"" main dish and the ""modern"" main dish in one course. ""Restaurant MAY"" is a French restaurant located in Gotanda, 5-minute walk from Gotanda Station on the JR Yamanote Line, the Tokyu Ikegami Line, and the Toei Asakusa Line, or an 8-minute walk from JR Osaki Station. The configuration of the dishes allows guests to experience the ""richness, flavor, and depth"" of classic cuisine and the ""innovation, aroma, and lightness"" of modern cuisine, as well as ""amazement, rediscovery, and the joy of eating"".

Mr. Iwata, the owner and chef, learned his trade in a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Paris, and then worked at ""Restaurant Monna Lisa"", a world gourmet guide award French restaurant in Ebisu. Based on this experience, Mr. Iwata decided to combine elements of his idea of modern and contemporary cuisine with classic French cuisine to create colorful dishes created with Japanese ingredients. His specialty is ""young pigeon breast cooked in a rock salt crust"". Mr. Iwata's vast experience and exceptional technique create delicious dishes with a traditional feel.

This charming restaurant offers guests the opportunity to enjoy meals in various different situations, from group dining in the quiet dining area, to the monthly ""Welcome Child Day"", which allows guests to enjoy eating together as a family.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Gotanda Station (East Exit), JR Yamanote Line

243953.longDescription:
A French restaurant in the upscale residential area of Takanawadai, whose communal cafe space is like that of a restaurant found in a small lane in the South of France.

"Perfume," the name of the　restaurant, comes from the chef's idea of having customers to enjoy the moment when the various fragrances become one.
The dishes of the chef, who studied in Japan and in France under the master Jaques Chibois, are classic yet modern and sophisticated in taste. 
Enjoy dishes made using fragrant ingredients reminiscent of the South of France carefully selected by the chef himself. 

The interior of the restaurant, based in white hues, has been created by art director Fumito Mochizuki.

It is a comforting space, where you feel nostalgic even on your first visit. This is truely a restaurant where you can enjoy a relaxing meal while having conversation with friends or important guests.

4-minute walk from Takanawadai station, Toei Asakusa Line

244589.longDescription:
"Uotoku" is an Edo-style sushi restaurant nearby the Mukojima-Hyakken Garden in Sumida-ku, Tokyo, known for its flowers in bloom every season. The restaurant opened in 1964, the same year as the first Olympics held in Asia - the Tokyo Olympics. The second owner of the restaurant - Kenichi Komiya - trained at the Kyoto Japanese restaurant "Kappo Yamashita" for 2 years after graduating from college. He entered "Uotoku" in 1992.

The restaurant concept is "sushi kaiseki with Kyoto-style cuisine and Edo-style sushi." With Kyoto-style dishes in the beginning and Edo-style sushi at the end, the traditional culinary culture of the major cities of the East and West regions of Japan can be sampled at once. The ingredients are mostly comprised of vegetables from Kyoto, but in autumn, ingredients like high-quality matsutake are sourced directly from a variety of areas including Hiroshima, Nagano, and Shikoku region; the very best of the season is sourced from all over Japan, starting from Toyosu(ex-Tsukiji) and beyond. Chef Komiya's grandfather originally started a seafood retail business and he goes out of his way to ensure particularly good quality.

"Uotoku" is especially good with eel and "osuimono." The eel, rather than being steamed first, is charcoal-grilled directly in the Kansai style. Making Kabayaki or small donburi by adding the eel to rice yields a variety of arrangements not often seen in eel specialty restaurants. The osuimono is the item of which Chef Komiya is most proud. The dashi broth takes 9 hours to make, with a high quality and depth that highlights the ingredients' true character. The decorative sushi at the end of the meal is made simply with fresh seafood and sushi rice made with red vinegar. The sushi that arises from Chef Komiya's technique is ready to be paired with a constant rotation of 10 types of Japanese sake. Among these, "Kamotsuru" from Hiroshima is often used in long-standing restaurants in Tokyo as an accompaniment for sushi and was a personal favorite of Chef Komiya's father, the previous owner.

The interior - made mostly of hinoki - is simply a 6-seat horigotatsu-style counter and a table for 4. In both cases, shoes are removed before seating, creating a pervasively relaxing space for eating. "Uotoku" is a great place to come share a seat with family or friends after a walk in the nearby gardens, experiencing the beauty of the seasons through sushi.

244401.longDescription:
After more than 20 years of honing the skills at the well-established sushi restaurant "Rokubei" in Ningyocho, Mr. Satoshi Ichijo opened his restaurant "Sushi Ichijo" in November 2015. The location he chose for his independent venture used to be the site of Miyakozushi (which has moved and is now called Nihonbashi Kakigaracho Sugita). Mr. Ichijo used to visit the main location of Miyakozushi with his family often when he was in elementary school. At that time he looked up to the sushi artisans there and aspired to become one himself, making this a meaningful place for him. “Without being flashy, doing the basics properly and consistently is important to me,” he says. He procures good fish, keeps his shop clean, and engages with the sushi earnestly. He offers orthodox Edomae-sushi while protecting tradition.

Mr. Ichijo is particular about using natural seafood from the seas around Japan, and he is strict about choosing only those ingredients in season. Seafood which has served traditional roles—such as vinegared Kohada, melt-in-your-mouth cooked clams, and conger eel with sauce and salt—are harmoniously married with vinegared rice which has been given its essential acidity with red vinegar. “I strive to run a sushi restaurant which will stick in your memory and make you want to come again after you finish eating,” says Mr. Ichijo even as he carries out his words by skillfully pressing each and every piece of sushi with all his soul, as though he were facing a real test. The sake is selected not to interfere with the sushi, and seasonal recommendations are offered. In addition to the taste of the sushi, Mr. Ichijo is particular about the restaurant’s interior, making every detail shine with authenticity. The shop’s name, Sushi Ichijo, has an atmosphere about it, and the characters are written by calligrapher Undo Inamura.

The chef is well versed in traditional earthenware and uses dishes of his own taste and choosing, from creations by Japanese living national treasures to works by modern artists such as Ryo Mikami. Experience the quintessence of Edomae-sushi to your heart’s content at one of the only 10 counter seats.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

A 3-minute walk fromHigashi Nihonbashi Station (Exit B2) of Toei Asakusa Line

245539.longDescription:
Yakatabune Sushi Origami is a floating restaurant on a traditional yakatabune houseboat that enchants guests with its Edo-period atmosphere, authentic Edomae sushi, and stunning views of landmarks around the Tokyo Bay area. Setting sail from a pier near Tennozu Isle Station, the boat takes guests on an elegant three-hour gourmet cruise along the Sumida River, offering Edomae sushi and scenic views of landmarks including Tokyo Tower, the Rainbow Bridge, Hama Rikyu Onshi Garden, the Kachidoki Bridge, Tokyo Skytree, Toyosu Market (also known as the Kitchen of Japan), and Odaiba.

The black houseboat moored at the pier just looks like an authentic sushi restaurant. Once you get on board and open the lattice door, you will find a striking 10-meter L-shaped counter made of solid aromatic hinoki cypress wood (with eight seats). The kitchen is helmed by a young sushi chef with excellent skills and extensive knowledge. He prepares seven delicacies and 13 pieces of nigiri sushi on the prix-fixe dinner menu supervised by Chef Daisaku Murayama from the renowned Sushi Murayama in Ginza, making sushi rice with vinegar, grilling fish over charcoal, and shaping sushi with hands just in front of guests. The tuna is sourced from a popular tuna wholesaler, Ishiji, at Toyosu Market and transformed into an exquisite piece of sushi, achieving a perfect balance with the sushi rice, which is seasoned with a blend of red and rice vinegar to bring out the best flavor. The Steamed Abalone, a specialty of Sushi Murayama, is also included in the menu, along with other popular delicacies, such as the Simmered Tender Octopus.

The restaurant offers a great selection of drinks that go perfectly with its sushi and delicacies, including champagne and white wines by the glass and 12 to 14 labels of premium sake from around Japan (e.g., Edo Kaijo from Tokyo). The drink menu also includes highballs, shochu, and whiskies, such as Yamazaki Single Malt Japanese Whiskies (non-vintage / aged 12 years) and Hibiki Japanese Harmony, to meet the diverse tastes of guests.

The simple yet luxurious interior is designed by a construction team involved in numerous renowned restaurant projects in Japan and abroad. The comfortable Japanese-style design is highlighted by the yukimi shoji windows (traditional Japanese paper screens with vertically sliding panels in their lower half). Dress in smart casual attire and immerse yourself in the comfortable multi-sensory experience while enjoying the seasonal views of Tokyo from the river boat and the food culture of Edomae sushi in the extraordinary atmosphere of Yakatabune Sushi Origami.

244810.longDescription:
"Sushi Tsubomi" opened in June 2018, produced by Takashi Saito, the owner of the famous "Sushi Saito.".
Hoping that his disciples would be successful in this world, Saito brought out Sushi Tsubomi to be a place where young craftsmen, who were still buds, could find their dreams through hard training.

In August 2022, it was renewed as a new "Sushi Tsubomi" with "Tsubomi". "Sushi Saito" and fish are bought from the same combs, and the rice that is made from large grains of used rice is only red vinegar and salt. Saito's spirit is also reflected in the meticulous manner in which he cooks food according to the time customers arrive.
The young craftsmen who follow Mr. Saito's wishes come up with a new menu every month that makes use of his fresh sensibility, so that it will be a place where "buds" can bloom.

There is only an L-shaped counter made of Kiso hinoki cypress in the store. The space between seats is wide so that you can relax comfortably.
By all means, please enjoy the polite and beautiful behavior of young craftsmen behind the counter.

244615.longDescription:
Located just 10-minutes on foot from Naka-Meguro Station, "Sushi Tsukiuda" is tucked away like a hideout in a quiet residential area. Here, Proprietor Mitsuhiko Tsukiuda has gone into business for himself after 25 years of training. He is a sushi artisan who carries on Japanese cultural tradition while also incorporating modern culture in taking on the challenge of creating new sushi.

Each of Mr. Tsukiuda's sushi dishes is made with true gratitude toward the cycle of the seasons that created the ingredients, the bounty of the ocean and environment all the people involved in each step of its creation, from fishermen to wholesalers. His commitment and attention to unifying all elements of the experience, from the effort and care put into each dish to the condition of the toppings and their maturity, temperature and visual appeal, as well as the temperature, flavor and volume of the vinegared rice as it dissolves in the mouth, are born from a mission to leave guests with smiles on their faces. Approximately 10 varieties of Japanese sake, carefully selected by the owner from all over Japan, are available for pairing.

Designed to impart a rejuvenating feel, the interior of the shop includes only seating for eight at the tatami-covered counter and a separate room with a sunken-heater table seating four. From the traditional papered entryway to the counter of Japanese cypress and the wooden cutting boards, every corner of the shop features the use of materials produced in Japan, and the space, with its pure Japanese style and notes of wood, provides guests a dignified atmosphere in which to enjoy their sushi experience. Suitable for occasions such as dates and parties, one of the charms of "Sushi Tsukiuda" is how distinctly accessible and accommodating it is for groups of friends and even for single female diners. Whether for ordinary dining occasions or as a reward to oneself for a job well done, guests are invited to let this sushi, expertly made with long-honed skill, put a smile on their faces.

3315.longDescription:
Sangoan, a restaurant located in Shirokane, Tokyo, had once awarded world gourmet guide award for 4 consecutive years. The owner had worked at the famous soba restaurant ""Take-yabu"" that makes Sangoan becomes a popular place serving soba in Tokyo where even attracting celebrities.

The ""Chef's selection course"" with a total of 10 dishes offer you a full experience of Sangoan's cuisine, including the tempura with the use of seasonal fuki and Asparagus. Crispy tempura coating with the crunchy vegetable inside is a wonderful dish you cannot miss. Also the soba noodle as finishing noodle is a gem, thin noodle spreading characteristic soba aroma and smooth texture are excellent. Sake from Niigata Prefecture are handpicked, only those having full body and concentrated flavour are served.

Exterior with a white-wooden door and Noren (Curtain) with light red in colour, pairing with clean and bright interior. Gathering with your special one or dining of foreign guests are recommended.

244830.longDescription: “Sushi Tatsunari”, which has been loved by various guests since it opened in Ginza in February 2017, will relocate to Hiroo, Tokyo and opened on April 21, 2020. The owner Tatsunari Iwama, who trained at sushi restaurants in Akasaka and Ginza, has determined to open also on Saturdays and Sundays. Chef Tatsunari uses seasonal ingredients purchased from Toyosu market with the thought that "I want to make sure that the flavor of the ingredients is not destroyed" and serves only "Omakase course" for both lunch and dinner. Japanese dishes such as sashimi, grilled fish, steamed dishes and stewed dishes are served first, and then around 14 pieces of nigiri sushi that uses two types of vinegared rice. In particular, the chef puts a great deal of effort into tuna sushi, and it has excellent techniques to expand the possibilities of making tuna sushi by changing its resting time depending on its freshness and by using vinegared rice mixed with red vinegar only for tuna. The restaurant has 8 counter seats made of Japanese cypress. It creates an extraordinary space where you can relax comfortably by with enough room between seats. Please use this restaurant for dates, receptions, and dinner gatherings. ※If you make a reservation 2-day in advance before noon, we can serve you the same Omakase course as evening from 12:00pm. ※There is only 1 round per night, but if you don't mind starting after 9pm, we can prepare for you. If you would like to make a reservation for lunches on weekdays or after 9pm, please use the inquiry form here.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Hiroo Station, Exit 2 (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

244206.longDescription:
If you want to enjoy Japanese food calmly at the huge terminal station, Ikebukuro where various people go and go, I want to recommend you to choose “Amenimomakezu" without any questions. In this area where Japanese food is hardly found, value for everyday use and also enjoying the little luxury of a world of “Wa” is extremely special. After passing through a shop curtain, there is Japanese modern space that conscious of “sorrow loneliness” based on the theme of the spirit of a tea ceremony, good calmness atmosphere makes you calm down and forget the bustle of the outside. Good accessibility of the 3-minute walk from the station is also a good point. 

“I want guests to feel more familiar with the full-fledged Japanese food world and have fun," said president Tsuji, who was a chef challenged to make a classy Japanese food restaurant, that is totally different from a public restaurant. The name of a restaurant that is taken from the representative poetry of Kenji Miyazawa, has full of enthusiasm for a new challenge. 

The recommended menu is the monthly course. Every morning, president Tsuji would go to the Toyosu seafood market and purchases natural seasonal ingredients caught in the near-sea. In order to make dishes beautiful, they use plates designed by craftsmen, of course, there are plenty of sake, wine, and shochu chosen for dishes. 

There are counter seats, table seats, and private rooms, so you can enjoy your meals with your friends, family, or business partners in “Amenimomakezu”. The world of “daily fine day”, which is authentic but comfortable, will make you relaxed softly even in a busy city and will make you feel refreshed.

245534.longDescription:
Located in the first basement of a building on Mishuku Street at the midpoint between Ikejiri-Ohashi and Sangen-Jaya stations in Setagaya City, CREATERNA is run by Owner-Chef Tsuneyuki Suwa, who trained at renowned restaurants in Japan and abroad, to spread the charm of gastronomy through his ideal recipes that have evolved from his distinguished culinary experience. 
 
Owner-Chef Suwa first learned the basics of European cuisine at a French restaurant in Tokyo and then went to Europe to expand his culinary horizons. He honed his skills at world-renowned restaurants, such as the three-star Le Petit Nice in France, the three-star Disfrutar (ranked first in the World’s Best 50 Restaurants) and the three-star El Celler de Can Roca in Spain, and the three-star MAAEMO in Norway. After returning to Japan, he served as chef at a two-star restaurant loved by foodies and then opened his own restaurant, CREATERNA, in July 2025.
 
The restaurant’s name, CREATERNA, is coined by combining two Latin words, Creo (which means “create”) and Aeternus (which means “eternal”), to reflect the owner’s eternal commitment to cooking and his ambition to craft unique and extraordinary dishes that not only please the taste buds but also evoke a sense of creativity, sophistication, and artistry.  The ingredients are sourced from around Japan. Some of them are selected for their rarity or seasonality, and others just for their quality, which is checked on the spot by the chef during his visits to the production sites. The prix-fixe menu features the chef’s selection of dishes presented in an artistic way. Among them, Yezo Venison Brioche is especially popular, becoming a regular menu item. It was invented by Chef Suwa, who took inspiration from his apprenticeship days at the three-star Disfrutar in Spain. Presented on a plate gifted by his friend in Portugal, it looks like a museum showpiece. Another popular menu item is an exotic fruit mousse with a decoration that resembles a butterfly spreading its wings. In addition, much to the delight of guests, the restaurant also offers a prix-fixe drink menu, Serenity, which consists of three glasses of wine, a bottle of mineral water, and an after-dinner cup of coffee.
 
With a predominantly white interior and minimal décor that allows guests to relax and enjoy their meals without distractions, CREATERNA has five tables and a counter (seating up to eight guests), where guests can enjoy watching Chef Suwa working in the open kitchen.  Visit CREATERNA on different occasions and indulge in the dishes that sum up the ideals of Chef Suwa, who says he wants to incorporate all his knowledge and experience into his work.
nearestStations: 13 minutes walk from the south exit of Ikejiri-Ohashi Station on the Denentoshi Line

Located in Kagurazaka, "Teppanyaki Iwakura" mainly serving Teppanyaki and Japanese cuisine. Among the world-wide cooking skill "Grilling", this restaurant is specially with the concept to promote Japanese representation cooking style "Teppanyaki", and offering you the best cuisine that not able to be cooked at home.

"Today's Omakase Course" uses seasonal ingredients, develops a great variety of dishes including "appetizers, sashimi, soup-style appetizer, grilled dish, simmered dish, vinegared dish, teppanyaki of meat, seasonal Japanese pepper rice and dessert". Considering the balance of lean meat and fat, A3-grade Omi beef is purchased directly from the farm. Various flavoring items, such as wasabi, salt, and lemon pepper, can let you eat in fresh feeling even at the end of the course. "Sweet rice cake" in dessert is also excellent. Alcohol are carefully selected, to match Japanese cuisines and meat. Over 50 kinds of wine, mainly produced in France, are available always, as well as more than 20 kinds of sake.

Inside, there are a counter seats where you can enjoy the live feeling, watching changing of ingredients by the craftsman. Table seats are also available, where a modern and chic space is waiting for you. You can also choose Semi-private room (up to 10 people), separated by partitions. In addition to entertainment and dinner, here can be used widely according to situations, such as anniversary date or family use (children's menu is also available, please let us know at the time of reservation).

244967.longDescription:
Found on the 10th floor of La Porte Aoyama, a five minute walk from Omotesando Station in Tokyo and ten from Shibuya Station, where upscale boutiques converge along Aoyama-dori Street, Benoit is a French restaurant that showcases the classic cuisine of Paris. 

The original Benoit opened in 1912 in Paris, and is still loved by Parisians and gourmands even now, more than a century later. Later, French star chef Alain Ducasse established the restaurant in Aoyama in 2005, taking over the restaurant’s traditional style. 

In the kitchen, Takahiro Noguchi was appointed Executive Chef in 2011. He trained at Domaine de Beauvois near Luynes and Le Choiseul à Amboise. After returning to Japan, he built his career at Chez Matsuo, inspired by the cuisine and spirit of Alain Ducasse, who places importance on vegetables and focuses on the water content of the ingredients themselves.

As for the produce that forms the heart and soul of the restaurant’s food, he puts his trust in his vegetable and fish suppliers, who deliver traceable, high quality ingredients each morning. With his team, the chef decides the day’s menu at a daily ingredients meeting. 

This attention to detail can be tasted in their cooking. The soup, for example, prepared with seasonal ingredients, variation and careful work, is an impressive mainstay. In the summer, the restaurant serves the classic vichyssoise (chilled potato soup) for guests at lunch, and its specialty soup de poisson at dinner. Salade Benoit is a popular dish that can be eaten in large portions with vegetables, foie gras, bacon, and chicken gizzards. Also a favourite with guests is the prix fixe menu, which allows diners to choose their favorite dish from a concise range of classic or seasonal dishes. 

The restaurant offers a total of 1,400 bottles of wine, including white, red, champagne and rose. Wines by the bottle hail from France, while wines by the glass lean more global. As a bistro, besides classic champagne, Burgundy and Bordeaux, the restaurant also offers a wide selection of independent wines from small producers, allowing guests to discover lesser-known vineyards, with a monthly sommelier-recommended pairing a popular choice. Non-alcoholic cocktails are also available, including Benoit Soleil, a refreshing concoction of orange juice, organic lemonade, and sparkling grape.

Ascending the spiral staircase from the tenth floor entrance to the eleventh floor, the dining room is imbued with a bright, warm atmosphere created with materials brought in from France, such as the Versailles-style oak floor, the cement lattice with an striking motif, and a walnut bistro table, reminiscent of residences in southern France. Vintage details such as old bottles, antique iron boxes, and unglazed pots add an accent to the interior, each hand-selected by Alain Ducasse himself at a French flea market. Tableware, imported from France, was also selected by Ducasse, while ceiling frescoes are reminiscent of the Provence sky.

The restaurant is suitable for entertainment, dates, parties and family gatherings while enjoying fine cuisine, and for those seeking to enjoy authentic French flavours and atmosphere.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Omotesando Station, Exit B2 (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line)

244822.longDescription: 7-minute walk from Gaienmae Station, Japanese restaurant DEN is located on the first floor of a building along Gaiennishi-dori. The owner is Zaisuke Hasegawa. He trained at the well-established Japanese restaurant Uotoku for 5 years and opened DEN in Jinbo-cho, Tokyo in 2008. In December 2016, it was relocated to the present location in Jingumae. Mr. Hasegawa continues to pursue "the act of making someone happy" through food and service. He established a new style of Japanese restaurant with the warmth of home cooking, and it shines as the top Japanese restaurant in the World's and in the Asia’s 50 Best Restaurant. In 2017, it was also awarded with the "Art of Hospitality Awards" for its attitude towards hospitality at the same event, attracting worldwide attention with regard to hospitality and receiving 2 stars from a famous gourmet guide. The Omakase Course consists of specialties such as "DEN monaka", "DEN fried chicken" and "DEN garden salad", as well as various dishes based on traditional Japanese cuisine, such as sashimi, soup and rice in an earthenware pot. Reservations from Pocket Concierge includes pairing, with not only Japanese sake or wine, but also non-alcoholic drinks. There is no nameplate on the outside of the restaurant, and the glass-walled interior is a woody space with the warmth of wood. There is a long table for 14 people, a table for 2 to 4 people and a private room. It is perfect for special days such as anniversaries and dates. Please enjoy the "Hasegawa-style" cuisine and hospitality. [Message from the owner] The taste of home cooking is different for everyone, but yet it is all prepared with the same wish, which is to make others happy. It brings warmth and closeness to one's heart, making us want to eat it every day. Homemade food is food prepared while thinking about others being happy. Every day, I think about the people who come to the restaurant and cook with the ingredients that arrive each day. For a homemade dish that brings a smile. Owner Zaiyu Hasegawa [Regarding the reservation] Please register the waiting list first, we will send you a confirmation email when there is a vacancy. Also, Pocket Concierge will send you a reconfirmation email, please make sure to reply. [Regarding visitors] Please make sure that the person who made the reservation comes to the restaurant. [Allergies and dislike ingredients] As the Omakase Course uses seasonal ingredients, we may decline your reservation if you have an excessive allergy or dislike ingredients. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? 4,400 Yen (tax inclusive) private dining room fee is charged ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? A party of 4 people is welcome in our private dining room. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room(s). ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Photos are allowed; however, we ask you to respect dining experience of others (no flash, no shutter sound, no photos of other guests or our staff, no video). ■ Are menus available in other languages? 244987.longDescription: Located on the B1 floor, a Den Kushi Flori is a five-minute walk from Omotesando Station. Globally acclaimed chefs Zaiyu Hasegawa, awarded two stars at his restaurant DEN in Jingumae, and Hiroyasu Kawate, a chef with two stars at neighbouring restaurant Florilège, have collaborated on the theme of “kushi” (skewer) at this hotly-tipped restaurant. Mr. Hasegawa and Mr. Kawate are two of Japan's most talented chefs whose restaurants have both been selected in the annual Asia’s 50 Best Restaurants list. Both longtime friends and rivals, they joined forces in 2011 to hold collaboration events, a rare occurrence at the time. From these early origins, a seed was planted and from this, an idea finally took shape before the long-anticipated Den Kushi Flori finally opened in October 2020. Both chefs have complimentary and contrasting styles. Mr. Hasegawa, who cooks in a unique, creative Japanese style, and Mr. Kawate, who delivers classical and poetic French cuisine, have collaborated on dishes that emphasise the best qualities of each chef’s style. The menu of exquisite dishes is unique to the collaboration, and distinct from either chef’s individual efforts, bridged by the humble kushi (skewer). As for drinks, just as Florilège is particular about its cocktail pairings, Den Kushi Flori will also use sours, preparing unique pairings for each course. The restaurant has been designed with an open kitchen to create a sense of immediacy, with a traditional kudosan (stove) visible from the 16-seat counter. For cooking, the height of the furnace is adjusted to the height of the earthenware pot used at DEN. Nostalgic and original in equal measure, the interior has been designed to evoke the essence of Japanese culture. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2022 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age. ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Photos are allowed in the restaurant. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customization on our course offers or offer a la carte option. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals. We request that you do not wear strong scent or perfume when dining with us.

245371.longDescription:
A seven-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Meiji-jingumae Station will take you to a traditional two-story house with no signboard on a narrow side street lined with trendy boutiques and modern condominiums. Housed in an over 70-year-old dark brown wooden building with a modern interior that creates a striking contrast with the discreet, classic exterior design, RESTAURANT HYENE strikes a balance between retro and fresh.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Yoko Kimoto. Born in 1991, she worked at L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon in Roppongi and then moved to South Korea, the homeland of one of her ancestors, to further pursue her culinary career at Hanmiri, which is renowned for its traditional Korean court cuisine. While working at Hanmiri, she found that Korean court cuisine, which does not use pepper or garlic, uses meat stock such as beef tail stock, like Japanese kaiseki and French cuisine. Based on her experience in South Korea, she has invented a new dish: Two-year Aged May Queen with Chocolate Fondant Sauce. It is a chef’s specialty that brings out the sweetness of aged potato by reinterpreting Baekseolgi, a popular Korean rice cake, with French culinary techniques. In addition, she offers innovative French dishes, creatively combining three different culinary heritages of South Korea, Japan, and France.
Another feature of RESTAURANT HYENE is its drink menu with a large selection of Japanese sakes. The restaurant also offers a food and alcohol pairing menu, which features Japanese sakes, rather than wines, to pair with dishes. The non-alcoholic drink menu includes a wide selection of homemade beverages, including original teas made with seasonal fruits.

While the original beauty of the exterior is preserved, the modern interior in dark brown tones was redesigned by a relative of Chef Kimoto and won a design award at CAFERES JAPAN 2022, one of the largest trade shows for cafe, bakery, and restaurant professionals in Japan. The main dining room has an eight-seat counter, while the private dining room on the second floor seats up to six guests. The counter has the same height as the worktop, so diners can enjoy watching their food being prepared. As the chef and other staff are close by, diners can share their impressions while tasting their food.
The restaurant’s name, HYENE, means hyena. Hyenas are cooperative as they live in groups. They are also known as voracious eaters who have no likes or dislikes. Chef Kimoto admires these characteristics and uses the name to represent her hope that her guests will enjoy her dishes to their heart’s content. So, why don’t you come to enjoy the exciting dining experience at RESTAURANT HYENE?

245521.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Shinjuku Station, Niku Kappo Niku Kabuku is located on the second floor of a hotel in an entertainment district of Tokyo. The restaurant is popular for its creative kappo dishes showcasing Wagyu beef in different ways. The restaurant’s name, Kabuku, comes not only from a Japanese word “kabuku” (which means “extraordinary”) but also from the name of its location (Kabukicho).

The kitchen is helmed by Chef Masamitsu Yamamoto, who grew up watching his father serve as a chef. Coupled with this, exciting encounters with inspirational recipes propelled him into his father’s footsteps after graduating from high school. He first trained at a long-established hotel restaurant and a renowned Japanese kaiseki restaurant in Ginza and then went abroad to extend his culinary expertise. He worked as a chef in the five locations of India, Hong Kong, Switzerland, Canada, and Thailand. His Japanese dishes featuring local ingredients were highly praised by local foodies. In India, he was even assigned to prepare a buffet breakfast for the Japanese Emperor and Empress during their stay at the hotel. Moreover, in Thailand, he was thrust into the limelight by winning a TV cooking contest. After returning to Japan with this brilliant track record, he was catapulted into the head chef position at the newly opened Niku Kappo Niku Kabuku.

The prix-fixe menu consists of about 10 courses, including five meat dishes featuring carefully selected Wagyu beef from Japan, such as Miyazaki beef, and three seafood dishes. Among them, particularly popular is Mini Rice Bowl with Perla Caviar, Bavette, and Salmon Roe. The bavette of Miyazaki beef, Perla caviar, and salmon roe are drizzled with a sauce of egg yolk and chili oil and served over steamed rice in a caviar can for a playful appearance. It is also accompanied by several sheets of nori seaweed to wrap the bite-size pieces in. Another popular menu is Wagyu Chuck Flap Grilled Tartare Burger with Shaved Truffle, sandwiched between brioche boule buns with cheese and Pecorino Romano sauce. Some guests even insist that this is worth opening a burger shop for. As exemplified by Earthen Pot Cooked Rice featuring seasonal ingredients, each dish is testament to the chef’s mastery of traditional Japanese cuisine and his playful spirit, which he learned from his culinary journey across five locations. All these specialties evolved with insights gained from diners are enhanced by high-quality ingredients and harmonious pairings with fine wines and sake.

Filled with a tranquil and peaceful atmosphere far from the hustle and bustle of the city and equipped with a counter (seating up to five guests), three tables, and four private dining rooms (three semi-private rooms and one completely private room), the restaurant caters for any occasion. Please visit Niku Kappo Niku Kabuku and indulge in Chef Yamamoto’s exquisite meat kappo cuisine only found in this restaurant.
nearestStations: JR Shinjuku Station, Higashi-Shinjuku Station

244576.longDescription:
Located 5-minute walk from Kagurazaka Station in Shinjuku, the Italian restaurant "DIRITTO" is hidden away on the 4th floor of a building. Getting off the elevator and opening the red-colored door, guests are greeted by Chef Masahiro Sakauchi, welcoming them in as though to his own home.

After working with the "AROMA FRESCA" Group for 6 years, Chef Sakauchi went into business on his own, opening "DIRITTO" in 2004. His decision to open a restaurant in Kagurazaka was because Chef Sakauchi originally hails from the Ochanomizu area and had always wanted to open a shop near his original neighborhood. With its venerable eateries set off by the stone pavement and historic language centers and other buildings, the neighborhood has an almost European atmosphere.

The restaurant's name, "DIRITTO," is Italian for "honest," "straight" or "sincere". "Here in Tokyo, a gathering point for all types of high-quality ingredients from all over Japan, I want to create Italian dishes made with the best of these ingredients," says Chef Sakauchi. "I don't want to create dishes that are all flair and no substance, and I don't want to create dishes that one-sidedly force my own personal views." Never forgetting the common-folk flavors he experienced in Italy, he wholeheartedly strives to deliver a unique DIRITTO-style take on Italian cuisine designed to please the palates of his customers.

DIRITTO-style Italian cuisine means using seasonal ingredients and simple preparation and bringing out the innate flavor of each ingredient for guests to enjoy. The seafood comes straight from Toyosu market, while the vegetables come from Ota Market. A Japanese seasonal theme is in full flourish here, with autumn featuring the use of matsutake and porcini mushrooms, Pacific saury pike and Nagano Purple grapes and winter bringing items such as wild game pasta with white truffles. Also　popular meat dish is Tankaku beef from Iwate Prefecture simmered in red wine. For wine pairings, those from Europe and Japan are available to bring out the best in the cuisine on offer, for a full-fledged, uncompromising Italian dining experience.

The interior of "DIRITTO," designed in the image of a hotel where Chef Sakauchi stayed while traveling in Italy, is formal while also retaining a new-feeling, classical atmosphere. The cutlery is provided by Mepra of Italy, while the flatware hails from locations such as Kobe and Niigata is selected to suit the dish being prepared. Excellent for dates, meals with friends or entertaining guests, the relaxed interior is also available to charter for parties of six or more, making the venue an excellent choice for anniversaries and other special occasions as well.

244602.longDescription:
"Chinese Specialty Restaurant Tsurumi" is located behind the Bishamonten Zenkokuji Temple in Kagurazaka, Tokyo. Owner and chef Hideo Tsurumi, who has been in the business for 40 years, creates unique menus inspired by food culture, history, and conversations with guests, and his dishes, which are simple and beautifully flavored, characteristic of Chinese cuisine, have won over many gourmets.

Mr. Tsurumi devoted 12 years to his studies at traditional Chinese restaurant in Tokyo, taking on the role of sous chef at the affiliated restaurant in Shinjuku. Following this, he served as head chef in various enterprises, primarily Chinese restaurants, before setting up independently and opening "Fukuihua" in Ueno, Tokyo. He operated for 5 and half years, before illness obliged him to close shop, but, 4 years and 10 months later, with the impulse to share the things he had learned so far, in order to repay the teachers of court cuisine who taught him the art of cooking during his period of studies, he opened "Chinese Specialty Restaurant Tsurumi" in 2016.

Mr. Tsurumi's cuisine is characterized by the fact that he does not use chemical seasonings, but brings out the maximum potential of natural ingredients, as he noticed since childhood that scientific flavors didn't agree with him and was impressed by natural flavors throughout his cooking career. A particular specialty is the "Six-Stewed Abalone." Salt and Shaoxing rice wine from a traditional ceramic jug are added to water, into which the live abalone are placed, and a process during which they are gradually heated then slightly cooled is carried out at least six times over the course of two to three days. Due to this method of heating, the abalone does not become overly soft, and their distinctive springy mouthfeel can be enjoyed while experiencing the taste of the meat and the scent of the seashore. In addition, his soup dishes are popular with regular guests. In dishes that could only be created by Mr. Tsurumi — who crafts his menus with regards to nutrients and the colors of the ingredients — such as steamed pork spare rib soup, steamed winter melon soup served in the melon, mushroom soup, and Chinese softshell turtle soup, he skillfully uses vegetables, meats, and elements of Chinese herbal medicine, and finishes the dishes with subtle flavors that allow you to experience the taste of the ingredients. In addition, the specialty "original pot soup", which can be said to be the culmination of Mr. Tsurumi's work, is served at irregular intervals and is an exquisite dish that you should try at least once.

The restaurant has a main counter that seats six, and table seating is provided for up to six guests. The counter is a special seating area where you can not only watch Mr. Tsurumi's cooking process but also hear commentary on the cuisine directly from this chef of 30 years. Mr. Tsurumi declares, "My faith is in the creation of a space where people will comment that they were able to have a great time, even more than that it was delicious." This is a Chinese restaurant providing extra satisfaction, such as the delicious, original flavors of ingredients as you have never experienced them before and Chinese food culture that you had never heard of until now.

245311.longDescription:
Set in a tranquil neighborhood in Kagurazaka, known as the mecca for food lovers, Ichiu is a sushi restaurant opened in February 2020 by Chef Koichi Hamano, who had had a desire to have his own restaurant in this neighborhood during his apprenticeship.

Chef Hamano trained at Akasaka Kikunoi and Ginza Kojyu in Tokyo and then at Sushi Sempachi in Kumamoto, filling his résumé with two-star restaurants only. Bringing his culinary experience honed at renowned Japanese restaurants to Ichiu, he offers five courses, including soup, before the entrée course of sushi.
The following sushi course consists of 13 to 14 pieces. The sushi rice is made of Akita Komachi rice from Jindai, Akita, selected through trial and error. It is seasoned with a blend of two red vinegars and a plum vinegar for a touch of freshness. The fresh seafood ingredients for sushi toppings are mostly sourced from Toyosu Market but some ingredients are also delivered from Amakusa, such as red sea urchin, gizzard shad, conger pike, and swimming crabs featured at the restaurant in Kumamoto where the chef trained. Among them, small fish whose true value is really appreciated when the ingredients are used as sushi toppings, such as greeneye, small sea bream and yellow porgy, are also served as sushi toppings in Ichiu.
The drink menu offers 10 labels of monthly featured Japanese sake and 20 labels of wine, mostly from Burgundy, to cater to the different preferences of guests.

As implied by the restaurant’s name, Ichiu, which means a house, the restaurant has a roof-like ceiling so that guests can feel as if they live together under one roof. On the hinoki cypress countertop (seating up to eight guests), the food is served on the chef’s favorite plates crafted by Mr. Ryuta Fukumura, a second-generation ceramicist from Nichigetsu Gama (a chinaware shop and cafe) in Fukuoka.
Chef Hamano’s comforting dishes and sushi, as well as pleasant conversation with him, make Ichiu worth a visit with your family, partner, friends, and colleagues.
nearestStations: A 2 minutes walk from Exit B3 of Iidabashi Station

245569.longDescription:
Located in a quiet alley off Kagurazaka Street, near Iidabashi Station, Jfree is a modern French restaurant run by Chef Tsubasa Jinnai. Hailing from Miyazaki Prefecture, he honed his culinary skills at Quintessence, a three-star French restaurant in Kita Shinagawa, and Florilege, a two-star French restaurant in Jingumae (currently located in Toranomon). Then, he took up the position of Executive Chef at a Japanese restaurant and worked at L’EAU and Hiroya in Minami Aoyama before setting up his own restaurant, Jfree, in January 2023.

The restaurant’s name, Jfree, is coined by combining the letter “J,” taken from the owner-chef’s family name of Jinnai and a French word “Je” (which means “I” in English) with the word “free,” associated with his given name of Tsubasa (which means “wings”). This represents his desire to spread the wings of free imagination to create new flavors and spaces and keep evolving to take guests to new heights together. His multi-course menu is not just a list of modern French dishes that blend French culinary techniques with Japanese influences but a sequence of dishes that combine delicate Japanese flavors with bold French flavors while balancing lightness with depth to keep the palate refreshed. The flavors reminiscent of delicacies from sushi restaurants captivate the taste buds of French food lovers and Japanese food and sushi connoisseurs alike.

Considering producers as Jfree team members, Chef Jinnai sources most of the ingredients directly from their origin, such as bamboo shoots from Kyoto and mushrooms from Iwate. He is also proud to offer Tsuma Jidori Chicken Bone Broth, a signature dish from the very beginning, which highlights the essence of his native Miyazaki. The rich amber soup is made from the bones of Tsuma Jidori chickens raised free-range in Miyazaki and loaded with Tsuma Jidori chicken thighs charcoal-grilled to be crispy outside and tender inside using traditional local techniques. The dish was named by Kundo Koyama, a creator known for his expertise in culinary arts and food culture, as he was thrilled by the rich flavors of the soup. Another must-try is Crêpe Salée, cooked in a three-stage process with generous amounts of Grand Fermage salted and unsalted butters from France. It is a compilation of research by Chef Jinnai, who loves crepes so much that he has been exploring how to make delicious crepes since he started cooking. Needless to say, this signature dessert is included in the multi-course menu.

The drink menu offers an exquisite selection of wines, mainly from France, and about 15 varieties of excellent sake from all over Japan. The wine and sake pairings are also a must-try. The restaurant’s interior features a striking contrast between the monochromatic palette and the warm wood accents. Taking two steps up to the counter (seating up to six guests) in front of the open kitchen feels uplifting – as if standing on the stage of gastronomy. There is also a stylish private dining room seating up to four guests, featuring an India ink artwork by calligrapher Rogen Ebihara on the wall, suitable for a range of occasions from intimate gatherings to business dining. Please enjoy the flavorful dishes created by the chef’s boundless imagination.

245538.longDescription:
About five minutes’ walk from Iidabashi Station, Sushi Mikuni is perched on the second floor of a building in a quiet alley off the main street in Kagurazaka. This sushi restaurant is helmed by Chef Yosuke Mikami, who captivates the taste buds with exquisite dishes that combine the sushi-making techniques he learned from his father and the culinary skills he honed during his apprenticeship at renowned Japanese restaurants.

Following in the footsteps of his father, who was a professional sushi chef, Chef Mikami trained at Isecho, a long-established Japanese restaurant, in Kyoto for four years and at Tokyo Nadaman in the Imperial Hotel Tokyo for five years and further honed his skills at renowned sushi restaurants in Tokyo while learning sushi-making techniques from his father before he opened his own restaurant, Sushi Mikuni, in 2020.

At Sushi Mikuni, fresh seafood is carefully selected and purchased every morning by the Chef himself at Toyosu Market and offered at the right time and at the right temperature. Especially, he is proud of his two signature delicacies, Crab on the Shell and Steamed Abalone. Not only tuna sushi, he also proudly offers sushi with silver-skinned fish such as gizzard shad, horse mackerel, and mackerel. The so-called “white sushi rice,” which is seasoned with white vinegar to add a mild acidity and enhance the flavors of sushi toppings, is kept at body temperature using two rice warmers. The sake list offers approximately 30 selections, including a wide variety of high-quality sake, such as the mellow Kamotsuru Gold from Hiroshima and the refreshing Yuki no Bosha from Akita, to meet different preferences.

The interior is bright with plain wood accents, boasting a prominent counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood (seating up to six guests). With a private dining room (seating up to four guests) inspired by a traditional Japanese tea room, the restaurant caters to various occasions, from business dinners to personal anniversaries, celebrations, and dates. In addition, the restaurant’s multilingual staff makes it a welcoming spot for everyone, including international guests.

244348.longDescription:
In September 2023, the Japanese restaurant Tanimoto, which was located in a corner of Arakicho, moved to Kagurazaka, a city rich in emotions where history and culture intersect. The owner, Seiji Tanimoto, who has worked as a chef in a kaiseki restaurant and is also trained in the tea ceremony, has created this Japanese restaurant where you can enjoy delicate and dignified cuisine. Tanimoto was awarded one star in the 2024 edition of the world-renowned Tokyo Gourmet Guide.

Tanimoto began his career as a chef in sushi restaurants and small restaurants, and began to enjoy tea ceremony in his 20’s. During this time, he decided to specialize in Japanese cuisine after being struck by the superb flavors of the dishes while dining at a certain Japanese restaurant in Kyoto. Afterwards, he worked at cha-kaiseki ryoteis (traditional Japanese restaurants serving meals before tea) in Shiga Prefecture and in Tokyo for a total of 8 years, and worked at a kaiseki restaurant in Minami-aoyama as the head chef for 3 years. He eventually left to open his own restaurant, Tanimoto, in April, 2017.

The course meals consist of appetizing kaiseki dishes made with plenty of seasonal ingredients in Japan. Paying close attention to every single element, the restaurant sources its ingredients from all over Japan, including fish from Seto Inland Sea, and seasonal vegetables mainly from Kyoto. The chef also carefully arranges the food items to highlight the fresh tastes of the ingredients, while making sure that the flavors are presented in an enjoyable variety.

One of the most carefully-crafted dishes is the wan-mono (soup), the flower of Japanese cuisine. The broth is slowly made by infusing rishiri kelp and Japanese kelp in cold water a day in advance, which is then flavored with sliced dried bonito. Other soup ingredients use specially-selected vegetables, etc., which are carefully prepared before using. Matcha, prepared by Tanimoto himself and presented at the last stage of the course, is another charming item you can look forward to. The restaurant has a lineup of Japanese sake to go with the course meals, which has modest yet refreshing rice flavors that do not interfere with the tastes of the dishes.

The simple and neat store has only 8 counter seats. Every day, Tanimoto himself arranges flowers to create a pleasant aroma in the shop, which contributes to its refined atmosphere that resembles a traditional tea room. It is a great choice for treating guests, dining for couples and friends, or even for spending a good time by yourself in the evening. Sit at the counter to treat yourself to authentic kaiseki cuisine crafted by the restaurant’s honest owner.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

243878.longDescription:
Kagurazaka, Tokyo is a place where a lot of traditional Japanese restaurants are gathered. Washoku ONODERA is a Japanese restaurant with lots of traditional mood, which is located on Kagurazaka Street, just a 5-minute walk from Iidabashi Station.

The seasonal course using premium ingredients which are coordinated daily, depending on inspirations of the chef.

The chef's uncompromising preparation and skillful work makes you satisfied with healthy and mild taste. 

Seasonal courses which are composed of a variety of dishes condensed with Japan-ness, always remind you the transformation of four seasons in Japan.

Butterbur sprout and shrimp tempura in Spring, sashimi and grilled river-fish like Ayu in Summer, pacific saury and Matsutake in Autumn, and angelfish in Winter are recommended. Those can only be tasted at ONODERA.

Interior has been decorated with plain wood that creating a clean and pure atmosphere. 2 different types of seating, counter seats let guests can fully enjoy the skills and works of the chef; and sunken kotatsu are a complete private room that requires you take off your shoes and enjoy the Japanese-style dining experience.

Dating or dinner gathering are suitable in this restaurant located in kagurazaka, having a relaxing dining with hospitality only here can offer.

245549.longDescription:
Nestled in a quiet residential lane less than 10 minutes’ walk from Nakameguro Station, Rokusho is an intimate retreat for those who appreciate vintage tequila that represents the passage of time, as well as good food and the best art of the time. Guests can enjoy exquisite cocktails, from classics to original creations, gracefully crafted by the restaurant’s bartender in the artistic setting.

Rokusho is known for offering vintage tequilas of the 1960s onward, chiefly Clase Azul, a premium tequila made from 100% blue agave, which has been drawing increasing attention with the growing popularity of tequila, especially in Asian countries. It is also recognizable for its iconic ceramic bottles hand-painted by Mexican artisans. Especially, the traditional ceramic decanters of Clase Azul Reposado with feathered brushstrokes of cobalt blue are particularly striking. Aged for eight months in bourbon barrels, this aromatic tequila with notes of hazelnut and vanilla goes perfectly with citrus-flavored soda. Rokusho also offers a variety of drink options, such as cocktails made with Clase Azul Reposado, including five low-alcohol options mixing the tequila with premium Taiwanese tea, and 15-ml tasting shots of various grades of Clase Azul and three different Clase Azul Mezcals made from blue agave.
 In addition, the restaurant bar offers eight signature cocktails created based on aroma profiles to invite the guests to discover global trends.

Another highlight of Rokusho is its food menu, which includes not only bar snacks that go well with tequila, such as truffle-flavored potatoes and roast beef, but also satisfying entrées. These original dishes are created by the chef with 10 years of work experience in a sushi restaurant and an excellent eye for fish and the kitchen staff trained at French and Italian restaurants. In addition, the prix-fixe menu offers six courses: Seasonal Fish Tacos with Wasabi Cream, Sushi Cake (a bite-sized piece of cake-like nigiri sushi characterized by its deep-fried sushi rice), Cold Zucchini Soup with Mexican Ratatouille, Perilla Genovese Pasta, A5-rank Wagyu Beef Steak with Cacao Sauce and Mole Negro, and Flan. This multi-course menu is further elevated by vintage tequila pairings.

The dining area is adorned with artworks selected by the restaurant’s owner and manager, as well as unfinished Clase Azul tequila bottles reserved for customers who bought them. The counter (seating up to four guests) is also covered with bottles of all types of Clase Azul and vintage tequilas. In addition, furnished with 2 tables (each seating up to 2 guests) and two sets of sofas (1 seating up to 3 guests and the other up to 6 guests), the dining room offers a luxurious lounging space. It is a must-visit for anyone looking to indulge in art and food while exploring the world of premium tequila.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Nakameguro Station on the Toyoko Line / Hibiya Line.

244202.longDescription:
Nakameguro, next to Shibuya, is not only a residential area but also a popular gourment spot."SteakDiningVitis" guarantees that customers will have a quality time enjoying the Japanese black beef steak grilled by Kishu white charcoal. "Steak is the most delicious if it is grilled by charcoal", said the chef. As a result, there is a special kiln in the restaurant that is made of fire bricks. The restaurant uses Japanese black cow and "Umabejokomaru", which is the best quality of the Kishu white charcoal.The chef grilled the steak directly with the fire, which makes the surface crispy and at the same time keeps the inside moisture. The dripped extra fat of the steak not only makes the steak healthier, but also merges with the smoke of the charcoal, which enhances the taste of the steak. 

Owner chef,Sohei Yuki, worked in the famous charcoal grilled steak restaurant, "Shimbashi Tamura-cho Aragawa" and "Tsukiji Steak Gorio", for seven years and moved to Chinese restaurant "Chi-fu" and yakiniku restaurant before opening this restaurant in 2014.  The speciality includes not only the homemade smoke salmon, but also the sirloin, the top round cap off and the beef tongue. 

The restaurant's name means "mother tree" in Latin.There is a great selection of wine because the owner wants the restaurant to be "the place where the steak grilled by the mother tree matches well with premium wine". The price of this hidden restaurant is reasonable because it is located a little away from the center. Please enjoy spending special anniversary in this restaurant. 

*Private dinner and private party is available. 
For more information, please contact us from the inquiry form.

245562.longDescription:
Perched on the third floor of a building near Nakameguro Station, Sushi Onikai Tasuichi opened in December 2020 as the second location of Sushi Onikai, a hard-to-book popular sushi restaurant. Guests are welcomed with “kuzushi sushi” created by young sushi chefs with traditional Edomae sushi-making techniques and original ideas.

Demonstrating the restaurant’s commitment to offering authentic sushi at reasonable prices, the curated prix-fixe menu consists of 15 pieces of nigiri sushi, three delicacies, a soup, and a Japanese omelet. The menu changes every month, set at monthly tasting sessions held to select items for the menu from the options suggested by the chefs and kitchen staff across the six affiliates of Sushi Onikai. While the sushi toppings and delicacies are prepared with carefully selected high-quality seafood, the sushi rice is also made with meticulous care and top-notch ingredients, such as Koshihikari rice from Fukui and red vinegar from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing. The sushi rice is finished in a large wooden bowl in front of guests and freshly served in small balls before the meal starts. This tasting is intended to allow guests to enjoy the changing flavors over time when it is served as nigiri sushi later in the meal. The Tempura Prawn Wrapped with Nori Seaweed is a specialty created from a recipe of the one-star chef of the affiliated Tempura Miyashiro. The crispy tempura prawn on a bed of sushi rice is wrapped with a crisp sheet of nori seaweed and directly handed over to guests. The year-round menu items are also popular, such as the Bluefin Tuna Hand Roll featuring three different cuts of tuna (fatty, medium fatty, and lean tuna) and the flavorful flash-smoked seafood.

The drink menu offers a great selection of sake, shochu, and beer as well as wines curated by Wine Sommelier and Italian Wine Ambassador Yoshihiro Nagase, who also joined the monthly menu tasting session to select Italian wines that go well with the sushi and delicacies to be added on the menu of Sushi Onikai. The interior is luxurious, with a spacious, L-shaped plain wood counter (seating up to 11 guests). Enjoy the sushi in a casual setting at Sushi Onikai Tasuichi, which satisfies both novice and connoisseur sushi enthusiasts.
nearestStations: 117m from Nakameguro Station

244614.longDescription: The location is a 3-minute walk from Tokyo's Naka-Meguro Station through the Meguro-Ginza shopping district. Entering a narrow alley just beyond the post office in front of Naka-Meguro Station, a 100-year-old tenement, surrounded by sheet metal, comes into view. Inside the entrance is "Tempura Miyashiro," which opened in 2018. The owner-chef, Mr. Naoaki Miyashiro is a talented chef who previously worked at Japanese restaurants in locations such as the Yokohama Royal Park Hotel and the Hilton Tokyo Odaiba. True to Mr. Miyashiro's philosophy of showing "thanks for the ingredients given to us by the four seasons, the producers who bring them to us and our guests who come to enjoy them," the ingredients used and his attitude toward preparing them are full of earnestness. Mr. Miyashiro draws on technique cultivated over long years to deep fry his tempura with impeccable timing in order to maximize the flavor of his ingredients. To say nothing of its visual beauty, the tempura, enveloped in a perfect battering, features the perfect temperature and exquisite locked-in flavor and texture from the first bite. The moment the compressed flavor of the season spreads throughout the mouth is an opportunity for each guest to experience the true depth of tempura. Also not to be missed are the seasonal small bowl and sashimi dishes served between the tempura courses. In particular, the painstakingly-prepared bonito broth is a must-try. The broth is made using only carefully-selected core material from the first-rate bonito from Makurazaki, Kagoshima Prefecture. Combining this with a soup carefully prepared using the bones of the fish used for that day's dishes allows guests to enjoy an unparalleled harmony between ingredients and broth. Mr. Miyashiro himself pairs Japanese sake and wine to fit with each monthly course. In contrast with the tasteful retro appearance, the interior of the shop features a refined design with soft, high-quality wood trim used together with Japanese paper to create a refined, pure Japanese-styled space with a relaxed atmosphere. Only 8 counter seats are available, and since they are located relatively close to Mr. Miyashiro, guests can enjoy not only the light sizzling sounds of the frying tempura but also the proximity to the excitement of Mr. Miyashiro's culinary action. In addition to simply enjoying the food, the shop has a kindness about it that invites the care of its customers. Suitable for meals with friends, dining events and dates, it would also no doubt be an effective place to provide guests with a pleasant culinary surprise. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? Children over the age of 12 are welcome when you reserve the entire restaurant for your private event. Please inquire in advance. Unfortunately, we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals.
