245487.longDescription:
Ideally located in the high-rise business district of Marunouchi at the heart of the Japanese economy, the restaurant Plaiga TOKYO boasts stunning views of the Wadakura Moat surrounding the Outer Gardens of the Imperial Palace. The word ‘Plaiga’ in the restaurant’s name is coined from the words ‘Plaisir’ (which means ‘pleasure’ in French) and ‘Ga’ (which means ‘elegance’ in Japanese). As suggested by the name, Plaiga TOKYO offers exquisite French cuisine and sophisticated service in an elegant setting to bring joy and happiness to guests.

Plaiga TOKYO is helmed by French-trained Chef Shota Ikeda from Fukuoka. After training at restaurants in his hometown of Fukuoka as well as Tokyo, he went to France to hone his culinary skills at starred restaurants, such as the one-star restaurant Loiseau des Vignes in Beaune, Burgundy, and the two-star restaurant Bernard Loiseau in Saulieu.  He was highly acclaimed for combining French culinary techniques with Japanese ingredients and aesthetics, especially at KIGAWA, a Japanese-owned restaurant, in the 14th arrondissement of Paris. After returning to Japan, he won the Bronze Egg at a prestigious competition for young chefs in 2019 and became the chef of Plaiga TOKYO in 2022. 

At Plaiga TOKYO, the best Japanese ingredients that represent the changing seasons are exquisitely presented in the distinctive style of Chef Ikeda. His playful yet classical French dishes are highly appreciated for their mild flavors. Especially, the Yamagata Tsuyahime Rice and Crab with Seasonal Twists, an appetizer served as the first course of a meal, is a true signature dish, combining a mousse of Tsuyahime rice from Sugai Farm in Yamagata with horsehair crab from Nemuro. Interestingly, the dish is presented with a seasonal theme, such as cherry blossoms in spring, sunflowers in summer, gingko in fall, and snow crystals in winter, to invite guests to embark on a gastronomical journey through the changing seasons of Japan.

The wine cellar stores 2,000 to 2,500 bottles of precious, small-lot wine in 800 to 900 varieties selected from around the world, mainly from France, Italy, Spain, the U.S., and Japan. The wine list is complemented by a delightful collection of Japanese sake from renowned breweries, such as Aramasa Brewery in Akita and Shiraito Brewery in Itoshima in the chef’s home prefecture of Fukuoka, and a unique selection of pairings with wines and sake.

The main dining room is spaciously furnished with 6 tables. In addition, there is a private dining room seating up to 12 guests. Please indulge in the seasonal delights of Japan with your loved ones in the exquisite setting of Plaiga TOKYO.

244959.longDescription:
Directly connected to Otemachi Station, Esterre is located on the 6th floor of Palace Hotel Tokyo and welcomes international clientele.

This French fine dining establishment utilizes the terroir (land and sea) of Japan to bring out the best of its seasonal ingredients. The restaurant was founded in partnership with Ducasse Paris, established by world-renowned chef Alain Ducasse. The luxurious dining room offers a commanding view of the Imperial Palace gardens and moats. Each table has a different view, and as the city lights up in the evening, Tokyo Tower glitters in the distance, as well as the lights of skyscrapers and buildings nearby.

The restaurant opened its doors in November 2019 to tell the story of the encounter of land and sea. Esterre welcomes Kei Kojima as new Chef de Cuisine, and Normand Jubin as new Chef Pâtissier from January 2023. Chef Kei is said to be the Japanese chef who understands and carries out Alain Ducasse's culinary philosophies better than any other chef in the world. Chef Kei has been the Executive Chef of "Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo" since 2010. Chef Normand previously worked as a Chef Pâtissier at Pelagos at Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens from 2010. Chef Normand delivers desserts with a sense of art and passion with abundant experience despite his young age. The new duo aims to produce an elevated level of French dining that showcases Japan’s unique terroir.

Chef Kei selects fresh vegetables by himself from Kamakura whrere he grew up, and make the most out of them to his cuisine. As for the wine list, an impressive collection of 600 bottles are available, from Champagne to red, rosé, white and dessert wines; there are about 17 varieties available by the glass and non-alcoholic sparkling wines on the menu.

Meaning ‘mother earth’ in the Occitan dialect spoken in the south west of France where Ducasse was born, guests are welcomed at the restaurant’s entrance by an impressive wooden sculpture symbolizing the blessings of the earth. Stylish black corridors, elegant wooden interiors and brushed metal fittings create a sense of warmth and luxury. The balance of cuisine and space created by a fusion of traditional Japanese and French crafts is designed to enhance the dining room’s sense of relaxation. Plates are made not only in France but also in Japan, and the hospitality that accompanies each meal is as much of a draw as the food itself.

The restaurent is fully equipped with well-appointed private rooms, and is suitable for business gatherings and receptions, not to mention for families, as children over 10 are welcomed.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

244958.longDescription:
Found on the 6th floor of Palace Hotel Tokyo that is an eight-minute walk from Tokyo Station, the restaurant GO is a part of the Japanese restaurant Wadakura having a distinct private space focusing on Japanese teppanyaki, cooked live by skilled chefs over a hot iron plate in front of guests. 

Presented as a prix fixe course, each experience offers high-quality beef and seafood sourced from across Japan, and seasonal vegetables delivered by one of the kitchen’s trusted producers. For example, the best Matsusaka and Ohmi beef of the season are carefully selected and offered to guests, while the exquisite balance of the restaurant’s signature dipping sauce coaxes the flavor from each perfectly grilled ingredient. 

Over 200 varieties of wine are available for guests to enjoy with their meal, with a sommelier on hand to suggest the best pairings. Meanwhile, 40 types of sake from across Japan are offered, while a range of non-alcoholic options from sparkling wine to juice are also available. 

A modern and luxurious space, the restaurant’s dining room subtly conceals a wealth of craftsmanship, including a mirror-finished plaster wall designed by plasterer Naoki Kusumi. Enclosed counter seats offer privacy for groups of up to 6 and 8 guests, ideal for private occasions such as family celebrations, entertainment or dates.

There are 6 restaurants in Tokyo and 3 restaurants overseas in the ""Kanesaka"" group led by Mr. Shinji Kanesaka and this restaurant is the only member who remains the name of ""Sushi Kanesaka"". Besides, the main branch ""Ginza Sushi Kanesaka"" awards world gourmet guide award. Mr.Kikuchi Shunsuke, who has experienced several years in the ""Kanesaka"" group and the main branch, is now responsible for this restaurant. Emphasis on the ingredient quality, following the styles of Edo-mae and determination, Mr.Kanesaka continues to promote Japanese sushi to the world, with the pride of been a Japanese sushi craftsman. The sushi here are provided with Edomae style technique and flexible creativity, which let every guest enjoy to taste the the worldview of Sushi Kanesaka. You could visit here and experience the sushi at both lunch and dinner time. Guest all over Japan and abroad visiting ""Palace Hotel Tokyo"". English menu and English service are also available. Not only counter seats, but also the private rooms (4 to 8 people) are prepared. 244372.longDescription: “Le Jardin des Sens” (Montpellier in southern France) gained attention from the foodies all over the world for receiving a world gourmet guide award rating at the youngest age in 1998. This restaurant belonged to twin chefs, Jacques Pourcel and Laurent Pourcel. “Sens et Saveurs” in Marunouchi, Tokyo was their 1st oversees restaurant. Their cooking style, referred to as the “Pourcel cuisine,” is based on the idea of what would be considered “traditional, 100 years from now,” and redesigns French cuisine according to their unique sense. Their food is characteristically light, being influenced by the warm climate of the Languedoc region and the Mediterranean Sea. They often incorporate fruits in their dishes to create a delicate and light taste through the acidity, sweetness, and fragrance of fruits. “Sucré Salé” is a common technique used by the chefs. By combining a contradictory flavor, like salt, to the tartness or sweetness of fruit, the inherent flavors of the ingredients are multiplied in the mouth. Moreover, they are known for dishes featuring freshness of the ingredients such as “Terre et Mer,” which combines items from the land and sea in one dish. The executive chef, Takanori Suzuki, is in charge of the kitchen. Following the advice from Mr. Pourcel to “create a southern French cuisine with a uniquely Japanese style,” he incorporates Japanese ingredients to create his unique style of southern French food. His specialty dish is “red sea bream with lemon vinegar sauce,” where a perfectly cooked mature red sea bream is served with a sauce featuring seasonal citrus fruits. Sun-soaked fruity wines from southern France pair well with these light dishes. “Sens et Saveurs” offers 200 kinds of wines directly imported by the Hiramatsu group. Moreover, the amazing location of the restaurant, the 35th floor of a building in Marunouchi, adds to the extraordinary food experience at this restaurant. You have the view of the greater Tokyo area through the large windows, and the Imperial Palace is visible from the bar area. “Sens et Saveurs” has the capacity to seat 80 guests, and private rooms are also available. “Sens et Saveurs” is perfect for a variety of occasions including celebrating anniversaries, dates, and business use. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.

244957.longDescription:
The restaurant Tatsumi was opened in May 2012 when the 5-star Palace Hotel Tokyo was rebuilt. At the counter with only 6 seats, you can enjoy the live feeling of the ingredients being fried in front of you, bringing out the rich flavor of each season. Placed in an intimate cozy alcove inside Wadakura’s main dining room in Palace Hotel Tokyo, the restaurant is an eight-minute walk from Tokyo Station.

Seasonal selections delicately prepared by master tempura chefs are served alongside seasonal salt pairings to enhance the natural flavors of the day’s offerings. Finished dishes boast a shatteringly crisp exterior owing to a light, thin coating and a custom safflower and grapeseed oil blend, retaining each ingredient’s freshness and integrity. Bespoke salt blends - including varieties such as Andean rock salt, mild red salt, matcha and buckwheat salt - enhance the flavor of seasonal dishes, such as summer sweetfish from Gifu, autumn sweetfish from Lake Biwa and meltingly soft red eggplant grown in Kumamoto.

Specially made for Palace Hotel Tokyo by Hakkasan group, “Ichi-no-ichi-no-ichi” sake blend acts as a perfect palate cleanser, along with over 40 varieties of sake from across Japan and a wine list of over 200 bottles from mainly France and Italy. And while the prix fixe courses are popular, dishes can also be ordered from the a la carte menu.

The dining room’s luxurious, private feeling is enhanced by a marble countertop and a special tempura table used for serving dishes individually. As such, the restaurant is a perfect fit for low-key dates, celebrations, family gatherings and entertainment.

245532.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Yurakucho Station, Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Marunouchi opened on the first basement floor of a building in Marunouchi in 2018. It is the sixth location of Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime, which was established in Tsukiji in 2004 by a third-generation fish broker, Motonobu Ishikawa, and the chef of Aozora Sushi Sandaime.
The kitchen is helmed by Chef Hisashi Kodama, who used to work at Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Dai Nagoya Building, Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Bettei, and other locations affiliated with Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime. Known as the man who brings smiles to people around Japan, Chef Kodama personally sources marine products from Toyosu Market every morning, turns them into “Tsukiji sushi” by reinterpreting authentic Edomae sushi in a casual way, and serves it to guests with a big smile on his face.

Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime is committed to “not compromising on the quality of ingredients and offering the best sushi at ‘Tsukiji’ prices.” The sourcing processes, preparation techniques, and menu choices vary from location to location as they are determined by each chef. The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu consisting of one or two delicacies and about 10 pieces of nigiri sushi also reflects the personality of Chef Kodama. For example, he chooses to avoid using red vinegar to season sushi rice. In addition, although all the branches feature tuna selected by Hiroki Fujita, also known as the Charisma of Tuna, from Fujita Suisan, Chef Kodama feels especially honored to create delicacies and sushi with this exceptional tuna because it was his predecessor’s passion that persuaded the wholesaler favored not only by sushi chefs but also by sushi lovers to sell their fish to the restaurant. The high-quality tuna is also used to create the popular “Ohagi,” a reinterpretation of Torotaku (sushi with a combination of fatty tuna and pickled radish) inspired by Ohagi (an oval-shaped sweet).

The alcoholic drink menu offers an excellent selection of sake from around Japan, including Hitakami from Miyagi and Kamonishiki from Niigata, as well as Tokyo Craft Pale Ale, which is sourced in barrels. The soft drink menu also offers a wide range of options, such as Hebesu (citrus fruit juice from Hyuga, Miyazaki) with soda. With a counter (seating up to eight guests) and two tables (each seating up to four guests), Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Marunouchi caters to various occasions, including family gatherings, friend hangouts, company outings, date nights, and dinners with international guests. Counter seating is recommended to see the chef’s rhythmical sushi-making skills and charming smile up close.

244956.longDescription:
An eight-minute walk from Tokyo Station, Wadakura is located on the sixth floor of Palace Hotel Tokyo, outlooking the Imperial Palace Outer Gardens.

The restaurant has been known for its kaiseki cuisine since the days of the original Palace Hotel, opened in 1961. When the hotel was rebuilt and reopened in May 2012, Wadakura was also newly reborn. Visitors frequent this time-honored restaurant to savor traditional Japanese cuisine while taking in the scenery of the Imperial Palace gardens―Wadakura Moat and Wadakura Bridge in particular, from which the restaurant takes its name. The scenery, deeply rooted in Japanese aesthetics, offers a sense of harmony with nature that defines the dining experience.

Chef Shingo Izumi joined the culinary team as Assistant Chef upon the hotel’s reopening. After honing his skills for 11 years, he stepped into the role of head chef in 2023. “Honoring Japanese culinary traditions, we strive to provide cuisine and an atmosphere that bring joy to our guests while treating producers and the ingredients they cultivate with sincerity,” Izumi says. Ingredients are carefully selected from trusted producers and through Palace Hotel Tokyo’s own sourcing network, with an emphasis on seasonality and quality. The kaiseki menu changes throughout the year, while the selectable dish of sukiyaki-style hot pot remains particularly popular among guests. The cuisine reflects a balance of tradition and thoughtful refinement.
With a dedicated sommelier on-site, over 200 varieties of wines―mainly from France and Italy―are available, and pairings of Japanese cuisine and wine are offered. The extensive selection of sake is from across the country, with Ichi-no-Ichi-no-Ichi made in collaboration with Niigata Hakkaisan Brewery being a particular recommendation. Non-alcoholic sparkling wine and sparkling juice are offered to accommodate a range of preferences.
The interior, incorporating natural elements such as earth, wood, and water, is by renowned designer Ryu Kosaka. Guests are welcomed by an installation crafted from a 250-year-old Japanese horse chestnut wood at the reception, and the walls leading to the dining hall is created by master plasterer Naoki Kusumi. With three Japanese-style private rooms for six to eight guests, six Western-style private rooms for four to ten guests, as well as 24 tables seats in the main dining area, Wadakura is well suited for any kind of occasion―whether for business dining or celebratory gatherings.

243931.longDescription: Offering the highest quality aged steak from the United States, Wolfgang's Steakhouse Marunouchi is located a five-minute walk from Tokyo Station, in the basement of the nationally designated cultural property of Meiji Seimei Kan, also close to Nijubashi Station. After retiring at the age of 64 from a 40-year career as a waiter, Wolfgang Zwiener opened his first restaurant in the U.S. in 2004, and his Marunouchi branch in Tokyo in 2014. Today, it is a famous steak restaurant with locations and fans around the world, including China and Singapore. Wolfgang's Steakhouse uses prime grade beef, which is rated by the USDA and accounts for only a tiny percentage of U.S. beef. It is then dry-aged for 28 days in a special aging warehouse. Through this maturation process, the finest meat becomes even more delicious and tender, concentrating and intensifying flavors and aromas. Thickly sliced lean meat is grilled in a 900 °C oven with its own plate, and even when brought to the table, the faint sizzle of meat continues for a while, stimulating the appetite. The signature dish is the Prime Steak (T-bone steak) where guests can enjoy both sirloin and fillet. The restaurant offers over 1,000 bottles of wine from across the world, and a pairing is recommended to bring out the flavors of the meat. As guests approach the restaurant, a red carpet surrounding the venue lends it a dignified air. Inside, the dining room’s design is based on handsome dark brown wood panelling, with an eye-catching glass walk-in wine cellar; white tablecloths and leather upholstery create an elegant and inviting ambience. In the dining area, there are 126 tables generously spaced, 14 counter seats, and 4 private rooms accommodating anywhere from 6 to 10 guests. The restaurant is ideal for private engagements with friends and family, entertaining visitors and guests, and sharing the delicious flavor of the finest aged meat in the United States. 〈Group Restaurant Information〉 Wolfgang's Steakhouse Signature Aoyama Wolfgang's Steakhouse Roppongi Wolfgang's Steakhouse Osaka Wolfgang's Steakhouse Fukuoka Wolfgang’s Steakhouse TEPPAN Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa

245546.longDescription:
Located on the first basement floor of the Tokyo Station Hotel within the red-brick Tokyo Station, the gateway to Tokyo, Yakitori Seo is the first branch of Torizen Seo, a popular yakitori restaurant in Azabu Juban. Since its opening in 2012, Yakitori Seo has attracted food lovers from around Japan and abroad. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Yusuke Asagami. Having trained at the main location for years, he learned the art of grilling over strong, close-range fire from Owner-Chef Hiroyuki Seo.

The prix-fixe menu starts with two appetizers, followed by eight chicken skewers, one dish, and a rice course. The exquisite ingredients are sourced from a partner chicken wholesaler, including Shingendori chicken from Yamanashi. In addition, premium Kumano Jidori chicken from Mie and organic vegetables from Nagano are directly purchased from producers and carefully grilled one by one over Kishu Binchotan charcoal produced by the owner’s favorite charcoal burner. The chicken is grilled over a high heat for a crispy exterior and juicy interior and sprinkled with Bolivian salt to bring out the fatty, savory taste of the chicken or brushed with a secret sauce passed down and replenished since the owner’s apprenticeship days. The finished skewers are served on plates crafted by Koichi Uchida, a ceramist from Mie, to add a touch of sophistication. An exquisite rice course can be chosen from six options: rice in chicken soup, rice topped with minced chicken, Inaniwa udon noodles with chicken soup, rice topped with crispy chicken skin and served with dashi broth on the side, and rice topped with specialty chicken. The homemade desserts, such as Chinese-style Almond Jelly and Brown Sugar Sorbet, are also popular among regulars.

The wine list offers about 50 fine labels, mainly from France but also from Italy and the New World.
The sake list consists of four permanent varieties of different characters (Azakura from Akita, Makiri from Yamagata, Kakurei from Niigata, and Sharaku from Fukushima) and three seasonal limited options. Inside the restaurant, the earthen walls create a deep, tranquil atmosphere, with counter seating (for up to 10 guests) and table seating (for two and six guests) that can also be used for semi-private settings. The restaurant caters to various occasions, from private to business situations, such as family and friend gatherings, after-work meals, date nights, and dinners with guests from abroad. Enjoy exquisite yakitori cuisine at Yakitori Seo.

243690.longDescription:
Where a graceful light shining at the end of a alley connecting to the Aoyama Street, Tokyo, there is a Japanese restaurant "Aoyama Jin". Natural wood has been used everywhere, the dining space comforts guests with sunshine passing through the huge windows to all the table, and the view of Japanese garden presenting landscape varies season to season. A place lets you forget the hustle and bustle of the city.

"Seasonal course" served by the chef who had worked in "Ginza Uchi-yama" and "Japanese cuisine Ichirin" at Gaien-mae, which seasonal ingredients are abundantly used. Specialty "Sesame tofu" melts in your mouth, and cuisine can be tasted only at the right season and will never be forgotten, like "Koubako Crab", the red jewelry box in Winter and "Ayu" in the early Summer.

The counter can be reserved for private use like a private room, perfect for business dining or dating. Private room with table can contain a group of up to 10, unforgettable memory is certain for those traveled to Japan with families. Don't forget to make a advanced reservation for requesting dessert for celebration.

245165.longDescription:
An eight-minute walk from Omotesando Station transports guests to Hakuun, a Japanese restaurant set in a tranquil residential area in Minami Aoyama 4-chome, famously known as a gourmet destination packed with renowned restaurants. Hakuun is directed by Shingo Sakamoto, who worked as a head chef at a three-star Japanese restaurant.

A 1-star “Hakuun” is derived from the Zen phrase, “the green mountains do not move, and the white clouds come and go on their own.” While Japanese cuisine is likened to the immovable green mountains, the restaurant staff who work with a flexible attitude are likened to the white clouds that slowly come and go, changing shape by adding the “man” radical (ｲ) to one of the Chinese characters for the word “white clouds” (白雲) to transform it into “Hakuun” (伯雲).

Chef Sakamoto carefully selects ingredients to allow guests to enjoy the seasonal flavors of Japan through its cuisine. He makes every effort to “get the best out of each ingredient for guests” and offers seasonal menus that showcase shellfish and edible wild plants in spring, pike conger and eel in summer, matsutake mushrooms in autumn, and pufferfish and crab in winter. He attains a sublime texture for fish by using the specialized cutting techniques he learned while cutting raw fish for sashimi and preparing pike conger for cooking as an apprentice. Meanwhile, the basic stock that acts as a foundation for many dishes is made from freshly shaved bonito flakes, carefully made with fermented dried bonito from Ibusuki, Kagoshima, Rishiri kelp from Kafuka on Rebun Island, Hokkaido, and extremely soft hot spring water from Tarumizu, Kagoshima, known for its high extracting power. This dashi adds an umami flavor to several courses from appetizers to entrées.

The restaurant modern and stylish design is striking against the backdrop of Minami Aoyama’s streetscape, but a step inside will reveal a pure Japanese-style interior with wood accents and earthen walls; in fact, guests often comment they feel as if they were in Kyoto. The food is served on elegant tableware, mostly antique, collected by chef Sakamoto as an apprentice. The Japanese sake is served in Edo Kiriko glassware created by Edo Kiriko Artist Hidetoshi Tadano. 

The restaurant is an outstanding place to visit with family, a partner, friends, and colleagues in all seasons. Guests are invited to enjoy delicious dishes crafted by a talented chef with proven skills and abundant creativity at this well-regarded restaurant.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245097.longDescription:
Itsuka is located on the second floor of a building a few minutes’ walk from Gaienmae Station in Minami Aoyama. Named after the concept of “valuing ingredients, producers, and dishes,” the restaurant offers Japanese-inspired Chinese dishes created by chef Ryosuke Tamura.

The name ‘Chinese chef Tamura’ will ring a bell for many gourmets as a legendary figure who gained renown while working at the renowned Sichuan restaurant Azabu Choko Kofukuen. Originally, he followed in the footsteps of his father, who ran a Chinese restaurant, to pursue a career in cooking; he trained at Chinese restaurants, including Suikoen in Yokohama Chinatown and Azabu Choko Kofukuen run by chef Matsuo Nagasaka. At Azabu Choko Kofukuen, Tamura became chef in 2006 and chef-owner in 2009. He opened Itsuka in December 2019.

“Itsuka offers Chinese dishes created by a Japanese chef in Minami Aoyama. These Chinese dishes can be found only in this age and in this place, here in Japan,” says chef Tamura. He also cares for the provenance and sustainability of his ingredients, given diminishing marine resources around Japan. To preserve the bounty of the sea for future generations, he sources seafood from producers who share his concerns and ensure careful management of fisheries in Nagasaki (Goto Islands), Kanagawa, Hokkaido (Hakodate), and Wakayama. The ingredients sourced from these sympathetic producers are carefully prepared to bring out their best flavors.

The Fortunate Assortment of Appetizers is a signature dish at Itsuka. Seven or eight seasonal appetizers are vertically arranged to allow guests to savor each, one by one, from the bottom to the top. Like a prologue, this opening course sets the tone for following dishes. Another recommended dish is Longtooth Grouper (or Leopard Coral Trout) from Goto with Potato Scales. Famous for its gelatinous texture, each fish is sourced from a reliable producer in the Goto Islands and carefully cooked to lock in its flavor, and topped with crispy potato slices and traditional Sichuan pepper and sesame oil sauce. In addition, a Hot Pot of Nanatani Duck from Kyoto has also gained popularity for its dynamic flavor, enhanced by a paste made from twenty spices. These dishes are complemented perfectly with a paired wine, Shaoxing wine, or Japanese sake.

The dining room and interior features Japanese-inspired wood and Chinese-inspired stone finishes, creating a relaxed and natural atmosphere. In addition to the main dining room, a private room with a round table is offered. 

Thus, Itsuka offers outstanding cooking and high-quality service in a refined setting, allowing guests to enjoy any occasion, whether dining with family, a partner, friends, or colleagues. 


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245089.longDescription:
Located in Minami-Aoyama, Kirameki is a unique restaurant where guests can enjoy Japanese-style yakiniku with an elegant touch of washoku tradition. Partnering with the 110-year-old establishment Hiyama, the restaurant sources only the finest wagyu, offering a variety of premium Kuroge Wagyu cuts from across Japan. The head chef, carrying on the traditions of Japanese cuisine, carefully crafts each dish to bring out the natural flavors of the ingredients.

Every ingredient is thoughtfully selected through visits to producers nationwide—Niigata rice, Kyoto miso, Saga’s Ariake nori, and more—allowing guests to savor the regional character of Japan. Alongside wagyu, the dining experience becomes a journey into the depth of Japanese food culture.

The restaurant is composed entirely of private and semi-private rooms, creating a serene Japanese atmosphere. Lanterns handcrafted by a fourth-generation Kyoto master, along with Nanbu ironware and Arita porcelain, reflect a deep respect for Japan’s traditional artistry. Highly praised by many guests, Kirameki is often introduced as one of the must-visit yakiniku restaurants in Tokyo.

Set in the sophisticated neighborhood of Aoyama, the restaurant is an ideal choice for anniversaries, dates, and business occasions. It is also a preferred venue for hosting international visitors, offering an authentic experience of Japanese hospitality and the artistry of yakiniku.

※For reservations of private rooms, please contact the restaurant directly.

244629.longDescription:
“L’EAU” is a French restaurant located in Minami Aoyama, Tokyo, a gourmet town full of up-and-coming restaurants. New styles of French cuisine are created by mixing powerful and delicate ingredients, nurtured by the natural elements of Japan, with modern tastes.

Chef Takamitsu Shimizu grew up watching his father run a French restaurant and began his culinary career at “Mikasa Kaikan,” an Italian restaurant in Ginza. After that, he worked as a chef for 15 years at his father’s restaurant, “Restaurant C’EST BIEN” in Higashi Nagasaki, and in November 2018, achieved independence with his wish to spread a new food culture from Tokyo. “L’EAU” is a French word for water. Chef Shimizu’s wish is for “L’EAU” to be a restaurant where the producers, staff, family and guests can have a close relationship, like “People and Water.” The Omakase course for lunch and dinner is made with seasonal ingredients. The wine, that matches well with the food, is mainly from France. You can also enjoy the pairing course selected by the sommelier.

The underground dining space is based on shades of black and features a design made from stones. The calculated lighting creates a relaxed, calm, and sophisticated atmosphere. Diners can experience the food in this inviting space, suitable for a once-in-a-lifetime meeting with their loved one, such as a marriage proposal or an anniversary date.

16027.longDescription:
Minami Aoyama Essence is a Chinese restaurant managed by a chef famous in the world of Chinese medicinal cuisine, who is also a recipient of the Bronze Award of Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries. Tucked away behind Aoyama Street, this restaurant is visited by "people who want to become beautiful through food."
Every dish is free from artificial seasonings. Filled with an array of pesticide-free vegetables and Chinese medicinal cuisine, the menu uses no artificial seasonings and is kind to the body. In dishes that concentrate in the delicious flavors of ingredients such as tender stewed beef and lamb or succulent shrimp and seafood, the chef expresses a modern Chinese style with full-bodied seasonings and beautiful presentation. Of course, his originality and ingenuity lend peerless flavors to the classics, too, including Mapo tofu and Dan Dan noodles. The pleasant marriage between the dishes and the sommelier's carefully selected wines is another of Minami Aoyama Essence's charms enjoyed by female guests.
Table seating and semi-private rooms are available in the neat and casual interior. We recommend this restaurant not only to women, but also to groups of men for a casual meal. We hope you will enjoy every detail of this specialty Chinese cuisine that heals mind and body, and where you can enjoy your meal guilt-free, no matter how much you eat.

244896.longDescription: -- 【Restaurant Information】 Please select your preferred arrival time below when registering for the waitlist. Lunch : 12:00 Dinner : 17:30 -- NARISAWA, in Minami-Aoyama, Tokyo, is well known as a world-class restaurant. Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa has had a celebrated career that, among others honors, has seen his restaurant selected by The World’s 50 Best Restaurants for more than 10 consecutive years. Since its opening in 2003, the restaurant’s creative cuisine has impressed diners both in Japan and abroad. Chef Narisawa's cuisine, which features a unique genre of Satoyama cuisine, has been an innovator for years. His first dish to showcase his talent was the "Soil Soup" served at his previous French restaurant, La Napoule (Kanagawa/Odawara) in 2001. Around this time, he became aware of his responsibility and role in society as a whole, ranging from his relationship with producers to the sustainability of the natural environment in which food is produced. Subsequently, he created the "Charcoal Dish" and "Water Dish" in 2010, which established a unique genre in which rich food culture and the wisdom of Satoyama culture in Japan are respected and expressed through NARISAWA filters. The signature "Satoyama Scenery" course is a dish that symbolizes the entire concept. Satoyama is a place in Japan where people and nature coexist side-by-side, with forests and the sea alongside farms and rice growers. Chef Narisawa learns about the environment in accordance with the change of seasons, and receives only what he needs. This is the "Satoyama culture," an expression of the irreplaceable culture of Japan that is beneficial to the mind and body of Satoyama — and sustainable to the natural environment. The chic interior is impressive, with 20 tables and plenty of space between the seats. It is recommended for special occasions such as dates, anniversaries, and family dinners. Please enjoy the world view of NARISAWA. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age. ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Photos are allowed; however, we ask you to respect dining experience of others (no flash, no shutter sound, no photos of other guests or our staff, no video). ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. A vegetarian option may be prepared. Unfortunately, we are not able to offer a la carte options. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals.

244345.longDescription:
“Nihon Ryori Wakabayashi” opened in November 2017 in Gaienmae, an area with many good restaurants, offers a nice and mature atmosphere. The owner Koji Wakabayashi, worked 12 years at a Japanese restaurant in the Kanto area and 10 years at “Aoyama Esaki,” a famous Japanese cuisine restaurant that maintained a world gourmet guide award for 7 consecutive years. During 7 of his 10 years at this restaurant, he served as the sous-chef to help uphold the standards of the restaurant, and when he was ready for the next step, he decided to open his own restaurant.      

Mr. Wakabayashi not only purchases fish from the vendors he has known since his time at “Aoyama Esaki”, but also goes directly to the farms that use natural farming method for vegetables. In order to keep his food healthy, Mr. Wakabayashi minimizes the use of additives and flavorings and carefully considers the nutritional value of the ingredients. Mr. Wakabayashi incorporates elements from Western cuisine in dishes like yellowtail confit, he also offer a popular dish from“Aoyama Esaki”, the braised ""Kinki (Idiot Fish)”.  As a certified sommelier, Mr. Wakabayashi selects around 6 different wine, including Burgundy and Montrachet. In addition, he offers about 7 kinds of great Sake from all over Japan, which pairs well with food.  
           
“Nihon Ryori Wakabayashi” features wood as the material for the floor and tables. There are 6 tables for 2, and 1 private room (up to 4 guests). “Nihon Ryori Wakabayashi” is perfect for special occasion, dinner meetings, or dates. The chef's refined creations, rooted in his experience at the famous restaurant, are definitely worth trying.

245266.longDescription:
NéMo is located in Minami Aoyama, less than a 10-minute walk from Omotesando Station. Kenichi Nemoto, who wants to "convey something new" in a place that is ahead of its time, is the chef of this restaurant.

He started his career at Les Créations de Narisawa, then trained at Aimee Vibert and Requinquer, before moving to France. A year and a half later, he returned to Japan and refined his skills for six years at the three-star Quintessence before going independent. He opened his own restaurant, NéMo, in June 2021.
The theme is "nature". The sun glistens through the trees in the dining room, making it feel like home. Chef Nemoto says, "I would like people to relax while they enjoy quality food." Reservations are accepted for a minimum of parties of two, with the intention of having conversation during the meal as a part of background music.
Chef Nemoto, who has fished with his grandfather since he was a child, is exceptionally passionate about seafood, and sometimes buys directly from fishermen. The ingredients are so carefully selected that some sashimi is even offered. For cooking, not only seafood, but also meat and vegetables are all carefully cooked over a slow fire. One of the most eye-catching dishes is the conger eel. The most popular dish is the frite of Tsushima (Nagasaki Prefecture) conger eel from Ueken, a popular wholesaler at Toyosu Market who is known for his connoisseurship of these eels, paired with macadamia nuts. The attention to detail in cooking extends to the desserts as well, such as the truffle soufflé and other dishes to finish a meal that can only be enjoyed live in a restaurant.
Wine pairings and tea pairings are also available, and the wines are selected from about 300 varieties from around the world, mainly from France. Manager Yuito Terashima, who served as chef sommelier at the two-star Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo, adeptly proposes pairings to accompany each dish created by Chef Nemoto.

Chef Nemoto also visited the artists and decided on the tableware to decorate the dishes. You will find earthenware by Akio Niisato of Tajimi, Gifu Prefecture, and Narumi Itaya, a native of Tajimi who lives in Kanazawa, as well as wooden tableware by Kenji Usuda of Hokkaido. The cutlery used is exclusively made from materials that have both function and tell a story, such as those by Studio William of the UK and the Perceval 9.47 table knife with a wooden handle. The dining room features 7 tables (18 seats) and a private room (6 people).
We would like to invite you to visit NéMo with your family, friends, business associates, or as a couple, and enjoy the high-quality food while relaxing in the refined service.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: A 9-minute walk from Omotesando Station

243964.longDescription:
This Japanese restaurant, “Oryori Taichi”, was reopened on June 12, 2024, from “Minami Aoyama Ichita”, a famous restaurant that has attracted many gourmets. It is located a short distance from Aoyama Dori's Gaienmae crossing, having moved to Room 102 of the same building as before.

Chef Taichi Sato opened "Minami Aoyama Ichita" on his own in 2014, after honing his skills at the renowned "Okido Yabe" in Shinjuku. In just one year, he has impressed many food connoisseurs with his exceptional skill and passion, and has achieved the remarkable feat of earning a star from a world-renowned gourmet guide. Chef Sato continues to strive for greater heights with his sincere approach to cooking and relentless quest for knowledge. The original fully omakase course from "Minami Aoyama Ichita" has evolved into a new style at "Oryori Taichi". The first half of the meal features a lighter five-course menu, followed by à la carte options in the second half. You can enjoy the aromatic handmade Jyuwari-soba (100% buckwheat flour noodles) that showcase Chef Sato's skill at the end of the meal. From carefully selected buckwheat seeds produced in Japan, he grinds his own buckwheat for daily use only. His meticulous attention to detail in each dish is evident in every one of his creations.

The restaurant is a luxurious space with only 7 seats at the sophisticated counter. It is ideal for dining with casual friends, having a special date, or having a casual yet sophisticated business meeting. We hope you will enjoy the new charm of "Oryori Taichi" to your heart's content.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2022.

244700.longDescription:
Close to Omotesando, one of Tokyo’s leading trend-setting areas, the Gaienmae area has a calm atmosphere. “Prévenance” is located in a quiet back alley, just a short walk from the station. The owner-chef, Hiroki Shizukai,  began learning his culinary art at the age of 19 and was trained at French restaurant, “Sens & Saveurs” in Tokyo, and “Keisuke Matsushima” in Nice, France. He was awarded one star in “Restaurant-I” in Tokyo, where he was the Head Chef for 3 years. As a highly sought after chef, he went independent in November 2013.

The meaning of the restaurant’s name, “Prévenance”, is “attentiveness to act” in French. In addition to its mission of creating and portraying the future of cooking, the restaurant strives to provide service that is a step ahead of what the guest looks for. The base of owner-chef Shizukai’s cuisine, which is full of robust flavor and vitality, is using a variety of ingredients that have been nurtured by nature, as they were meant to be. The ingredients originate from homegrown farms in Ibaraki and from reliable producers all over the country, such as wild mushrooms and edible wild plants that are selected by the chef. “I was deeply impressed by the fact that delicious food can grow on mountain sides without help from anyone. I want to express the splendor of Japanese ingredients on the plate by going to mountains or rivers and understanding natural ingredients,” says owner-chef Shizukai. The restaurant also serves charcoal grilled meat as a main dish.

The wine that matches well with the cuisine ranges from French to Japanese, as well as natural wine. Wine pairing is also available to meet your needs. The combination of the food and wine allows guests to enjoy the flavor of the various combinations on the plate.

The white interior is an elegant space and service is available in English and French.  “Prévenance”, a restaurant to visit with your date, with friends, or for business gatherings and special occasions.

Its food reflects Chef Okamoto's appreciation of his guests and his desire ""to bring happiness to people through food"".

Okamoto has been trained at several world gourmet guide awarded restaurants, including Hotel New Otani, Chez Inno, Troigros, Michel Trama and De ROANNE. 243736.longDescription:
Located a few minutes on foot from Gaienmae Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, this French restaurant stands just off Gaien-Nishi Street in Minami-Aoyama. The interior harmonizes a crisp contrast of white and black with the warmth of natural wood, creating a refined space that feels both serene and removed from the everyday.

Owner-chef Tani trained for four and a half years in France and Switzerland, honing his skills not only in restaurants but also in charcuteries and boulangeries. After returning to Japan, he served as sous-chef at “Restaurant Aladdin” before leading the kitchen for approximately six years at “Yotsuya Maison Cache-Cache.” He opened “Minami-Aoyama Restaurant Tani” in January 2012. His cuisine fuses traditional techniques with regional French gastronomy, drawing out the full character of seasonal ingredients. Careful attention to serving temperature and precise, uncluttered presentation express a sincere and disciplined approach to each dish. In addition to running the restaurant, he serves as an instructor at a Tokyo metropolitan high school culinary program and teaches cooking classes, contributing to the development of future chefs.

Madame Tani, born into a family in the restaurant industry, also brings extensive experience in French dining. She and Chef Tani refined their expertise together at a hotel restaurant in the Loire region of France. A certified sommelier, Madame Tani offers gracious hospitality that enhances the harmony between cuisine and wine, enriching each guest’s experience. The restaurant’s balance of sophistication and warmth makes it an ideal setting for special occasions, anniversaries, and business gatherings, offering moments that linger in memory.
nearestStations: 3 minute walk from Gaienmae Station (Exit 1A), Tokyo Metro Ginza Line

244155.longDescription:
Opened in 1990, “Ristorante ACQUA PAZZA” is a famous restaurant with world gourmet guide award experienced Chef Yoshimi Hidaka which could be the representation of Italian in Tokyo. An Italian restaurant Chef Yoshimi Hidaka present his special skills flexibly using ingredients from Japan. 

Its name “ACQUA PAZZA”, is the traditional dish from Campagna, Italy, stew of the freshest fish with tomato and olive. You would not like to miss this Chef Yoshimi Hidaka’s most impressive one. Started from the 3-star restaurant “Dar Pescatore” and “Enoteca Pinkioli”, Chef Yoshimi Hidaka did his training in 14 different restaurants all over Italian. After coming home to Japan, he supported the restaurant “Ristorante Yamazaki” as chief cook. With the faith of “The charm of Italian dishes is the native dishes”, uses the traditional Japanese ingredients to create a Italian restaurant that roots in Tokyo, a new record in the history or Italian dishes.  

The peaceful lighting and decorations providing a relaxing atmosphere here. You can enjoy your meal accompany with the ample sunlight shine through the window. Semi-private rooms, serving maximum to 8 persons, is a perfect suggestion for welcoming or dinning. We also welcome children elder than 7 (or in primary school) as long as coming together with families. English service and Vegetarian menu (request at time of reservation) are also available for convivence of oversea guests.

244174.longDescription:
This new Japanese style restaurant, that serves "Japanese food that does not limit to one genre", is located on Nisseki street in Minami-Aoyama.

"Sudachi" is its owner Mr. Makoto Okamoto's dream restaurant, where everyone in the restaurant, including the chef and the staffs, believes that meeting every customers is "one chance in a lifetime". In the restaurant’s name “Sudachi", "Su" means “the element of enjoying yourself” and “dachi" means “with friends”. The omakase course that changes seasonally includes 6-7 appetizers. The open kitchen is a live show where customers can enjoy watching the chef making sushi. To match with the cuisine, the restaurant provides a variety of alcohol, especially wine and about 15 seasonal sakes. 

The restaurant is located on the basement floor. There are two different types of seat in the restaurant, the comfortable counter-seat and table-seat that can be partitioned. Customers can enjoy this new Japanese style restaurant in a wide range of situations, such as with guests, family and dates. It is possible for children that are elementary school and above to enter the restaurant and kids menu is available upon advance request. Vegetarian menu is also available for foreign guests upon advance request. Please visit this restaurant with important people.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line “Hiroo Station”

245485.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Omotesando Station, Sushi Masuda is located on the first floor of a building in Minami Aoyama.  Helmed by Chef Rei Masuda, the restaurant captivates sushi lovers with the Masuda-style sushi built around classic sushi-making techniques passed down from renowned sushi chefs.

Hailing from Kokura City, Fukuoka Prefecture, Chef Masuda first trained at Tenzushi Kyomachi, a renowned sushi restaurant in his hometown. Later, on the advice of his master, Koichi Amano, he went to Tokyo, the mecca of Edomae sushi, where he honed his sushi-making skills for nine years at Sukiyabashi Jiro in Ginza. During his apprenticeship to the most inspirational sushi chef he had ever known at the famous sushi restaurant, he learned essential sushi-making techniques, from preparation to shaping. Then, in 2014, he opened Sushi Masuda in Minami Aoyama.   His new restaurant became an instant hit, earning one star within one year of its opening and two stars for the second year in a row in a world-renowned restaurant guide. Although the restaurant closed its doors at its height in 2019 due to the tenancy agreement, he continued playing an active role in the restaurant scene by helping open a new restaurant, Sushi Masuda, in Mandarin Oriental, Taipei, in 2020. Then, he reopened his original restaurant, Sushi Masuda, in Minami Aoyama in 2022. This caused a sensation and a mad rush of sushi lovers who had waited for his return.

Sushi Masuda’s signature prix-fixe menu consists of 6 delicacies and 10 pieces of sushi. The fish and shellfish are sourced through trusted brokers from Toyosu Market, such as the tuna broker Yamayuki and the prawn broker Kamefuku. Combined with strongly vinegared sushi rice, these seafood ingredients transform into captivating artworks. Above all, each piece of sushi is elaborately prepared to meet the preferences of guests. For example, the sushi rice is prepared in the appropriate size and served at the appropriate temperature, according to each guest. This demonstrates the superior craftsmanship of the classically trained chef who created his own style of sushi based on his expertise. The drink menu offers a delightful selection of sake (with 10 varieties always in stock) and red and white wines, and campaigns that go perfectly well with the exquisite sushi and delicacies of Sushi Masuda.

With an eye-catching solid hinoki cypress counter (seating up to eight guests), the dining room is casual yet sophisticated, allowing guests to spend a relaxing time while enjoying conversations over the counter with the friendly chef.  In addition, English-speaking staff are available to help entertain guests from abroad. All this makes Sushi Masuda perfect for different occasions, ranging from business dinners to family and friend gatherings, date nights, and other private moments.
nearestStations: Approximately a five-minute walk from Exit A4 of Omotesando Station on the Ginza, Hanzomon, and Chiyoda lines of the Tokyo Metro.

244483.longDescription:
Hidden door, pass through the restaurant curtain, and you are met with the beautiful 6-meter counter of Japanese Tōnō cypress, sent from Sanchong. And standing behind the owner-chef Riku Ōtomo, who achieved independence at the early age of 33.

For 16 years, the chef Riku built on his passion for sushi through study in the sushi bars of Tokyo from the age of 18. After setting up independently, he continues to make his way to Tsukiji fish market every morning, lay in only those ingredients that meet his standards, check the condition of the fish as he carries out preparation, and serve it as dishes of the highest quality. Painstakingly layering ordinary processes one by one and transforming them into top-quality sushi is Riku’s style - in early summer, Rishiri Island sea urchin at the peak of its pre-spawning deliciousness is transformed into nigiri; splendid alfonsino is grilled and tops rod-shaped sushi; “Toro-taku nigiri” is created using Takuan(radish pickles) marinated in standard tamari soy sauce; and more. Processed toppings are assembled in the ice-filled display case and wooden box facing the customer, and are a visual means of heightening customers’ anticipation. His sincere attitude towards his work extends to his response to customers. Riku wants to face everyone with seriousness and dedication. Even if it is your first time visiting the restaurant, he guarantees that you can spend time in comfort and free from tension.

The collection of alcoholic beverages includes more than 10 kinds of Junmai sake, champagne, wine, and whiskey, chosen with great care and with consideration to sushi pairing. They are reasonably offered by the half-gō (0.9 l) or the glass, tasty bar snacks whet the whistle, and the majority of guests enjoy the pairings. The counter seats eight, and one semi-private room seats up to six. Recommended for corporate entertainment, dates, anniversaries, and also for spending time with family, as children above elementary school age are also welcome.

245507.longDescription:
An eight-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Gaienmae Station, Sushi Rizaki Aoyama is located in the first basement of a building in Minami Aoyama.  This second location of Sushi Rizaki, a hard-to-book restaurant in Shibuya, captures and tantalizes the taste buds of a wide audience, from sushi connoisseurs to young sushi admirers. Sushi Rizaki Aoyama is entrusted to a 20-something young chef, Ren Okizuka, who has spent his whole career at Sushi Rizaki, working at its main location in Shibuya and its other premises in Aoyama, Ebisu, and Nishiazabu. He was appointed as Chef at Rizaki Nishi Aoyama in October 2024. 

Carrying on the Rizaki’s philosophy of “high quality within reach,” the chef is committed to offering the best-quality sushi at more reasonable prices than high-end restaurants.  The seafood ingredients are selected by Chef Okizuka himself, who goes to Toyosu Market almost every morning to source the best quality ingredients available from wholesalers with whom he has built strong ties. The tuna is sourced from Hicho, a popular tuna wholesaler. The flavors of the seafood are highlighted by Mazuma wasabi grown by Koichi Tashiro from Gotemba in Shizuoka, who is known as one of the best wasabi farmers in Japan.

The sushi rice is made with a blend of two varieties of rice, Tohoku No. 194 and Emi no Kizuna, which are different in grain size and hardness. Cooked to the right texture, the rice will fall apart and melt in the mouth with sushi toppings. It is seasoned with a blend of three vinegars: the spirit vinegar Hakuju and the red vinegar Kohaku from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing and Chidorisu from Murayama Zousu. The rice is cooked, cooled to the right temperature, and mixed with the vinegar mixture just before making a piece of tuna nigiri sushi, the signature dish in the prix-fixe menu, which alternatively serves nibbles and nigiri sushi. Among the sushi pieces prepared in authentic Edomae style, fatty sardine, delicately cut squid, and slightly acidic gizzard shad enjoy special popularity.

The drink menu offers a great selection of sake, including 20 seasonal specials and year-round options, such as Juyondai from Yamagata and Aramasa from Akita, as well as a wide selection of wines, including red, white, and Champagne varietals, by the glass and bottle.  Non-alcoholic drinks are also recommended. Especially, Sushi Cider made with vinegar from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing goes well with the sushi. The dining room with an L-shaped hinoki cypress counter (seating up to 10 guests) and two tables (each seating up to two guests) is dignified but filled with casual conversations, which creates an easy-going atmosphere.  Coupled with high-quality Edomae-style sushi, the distinguished yet relaxing setting makes Sushi Rizaki Aoyama perfect for various occasions, from intimate meals with your date, family, friends, or coworkers to entertaining dinners with your guests from around the world.
nearestStations: 8 minutes walk from Gaienmae Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line

244979.longDescription:
About a 6-minute walk from Omotesando Station, the restaurant is located near the Nezu Museum. Although primarily a sushi establishment, Yoshinobu Kimura, a sommelier, has teamed up with Michimasa Nakamura, an Edomae sushi chef, to develop an innovative culinary experience not bound by genre.

Mr. Kimura studied restaurant management at an American university, and after graduating, worked as a sommelier at Japanese restaurant Megu in New York. After returning to Japan, he worked as a sommelier for Aoyama's world beating Narisawa for 10 years, rising to become head sommelier before opening Sushi m in 2019. 

The "m" in the restaurant’s name stands for “marriage”; Enjoying the sake, wine, and cocktail pairing course inspired by Mr. Kimura's extensive overseas experience is the highlight of 'Sushi m'. The “m” is lower case, as a curve, its flowing natural body more familiar to Japanese culture.

Wine is chosen from a walk-in wine cellar housing a collection of 400 bottles. The cellar is set to 0 to -15°C, with around 20 varieties available, including Akita's 'Shinsei,' directly delivered from the brewery, a wide selection of junmai sake, and other rare finds not commonly available in the market. A lineup perfect for pairing awaits its turn for you to enjoy.

244624.longDescription:
The characters for "Tenoshima" make a simple appearance on a two-story building in Minamiaoyama in Tokyo. The restaurant's owner, Ryohei Hayashi, joined Kyoto's venerable three-star restaurant Kikunoi after graduating from university, and studied under Yoshihiro Murata. In addition to serving as the sous-chef at Kikunoi and the head chef at the restaurant's Akasaka branch, he took part in events to promote Japanese cuisine in over 17 countries. In 2018, he opened Tenoshima with okami (female manager) Ms. Sari, a graphic designer-turned-chef who managed a Japanese restaurant in Scandinavia.

The new restaurant takes its name from Kagawa Prefecture's small outlying island of Tenoshima, from which Mr. Hayashi's family hails. The name embodies the wish to widely convey the charms of the island to people in Japan and abroad. Its concept is "Japanese cuisine for all." Says Mr. Hayashi, "I want to make this a restaurant that people can enjoy more freely and casually, not bound by the framework of traditional Japanese cuisine like kaiseki that places importance on form." The restaurant's ingredients embrace the real seasons in Japan and primarily make use of micro-herbs from Takagakari Farm in Hiroshima, and seafood and vegetables from Setouchi. Courses include many dishes that evoke comfort, including the Tenoshima sushi that offers a taste of the seasons, and the nyumen noodles given sophisticated flavor by broth from dried sea cucumber, an ingredient not often used in typical kaiseki restaurants. At the foundation is a wish to hand down the charms of the "authenticity" found in long-traditional ingredients and rustic dishes. This creativity, unbound by conventional wisdom, also appears in the drinks. The restaurant offers a carefully selected lineup that ranges from Japanese sake to ciders, craft beers, and original after-dinner coffees, selected and paired with meals by okami Ms. Sari.
The interior is coordinated by SUPPOSE DESIGN OFFICE on the theme of a dirt floor kitchen. The counter kitchen, finished with mortar imspired by an "okudosan" (hearth), has a floor and walls mixed with soil brought from Tenoshima. The copper in the shelving and the shoji sliding doors harmonize to create a stylish atmosphere. Seating consists of six counter seats and three four-person tables. Tenoshima aims to let guests from around the world enjoy Japanese cuisine in a relaxed and a warm atmosphere. This style brings the seemingly-high hurdle of Japanese cuisine down closer to guests and delivers a fresh impression.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

l'intenporel opened in November 2017 in Minami-Aoyama, one of the most competitive restaurant districts in Tokyo. Based on the concept of "common sense and values change with the times, but the essence of deliciousness and beauty is eternal and constant," it was named l'intimpoel, which means "transitory and eternal" in French.

Owner sommelier Takashi Koga has experience in AU CRIEUR DE VIN in Nagano,  La Blanche in Shibuya, Les enfants gates and Tsuki Sur La Mer, and has become independent. There are more than 200 kinds of wine mainly from France, with pairings that matches the course meal.

Hiroyuki Satake has been the chef since 2024. Based on the classical cuisine he learned in France and Japan, he uses carefully selected ingredients from around the world and Japan to represent the four seasons and regions of origin. He takes great care in the details of his cuisine, and offers dishes that are also very friendly to guests.

The interior is a chic and calm space based on black. In addition to counter seats, there are also table seats and private rooms for various occasions. Please use it as a place to spend an important time such as business entertainment, date and anniversary.

245467.longDescription:
The restaurant, malca, is located near Tokyo Metro Gaienmae Station, a short walk from the Minami Aoyama 3-chome intersection in front of the building that was formerly known as Aoyama Bell Commons. Just walk a few steps down Gaien Nishi Street towards Nishi Azabu and you will find the entrance to the underground restaurant. The modern counter made of wood and undressed concrete enhances the sophisticated atmosphere of the hideaway restaurant in the mature neighborhood of Miyami Aoyama.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Tsukasa Kitano, who hails from Awaji Island, Hyogo Prefecture. After graduating from culinary school, he honed his culinary skills at Italian restaurants, such as Sfida (currently known as “anu”) in Osaka and TACUBO in Daikanyama, Tokyo. He then opened his own restaurant, malca, in the current location in 2022.

Chef Kitano was born to a fishmonger family in Awaji Island. His family’s fishmonger shop was founded by his grandfather and commonly known as “Maruka” in the local market. Named after this nickname, malca is making new history in the restaurant scene of Central Tokyo.

At malca, guests can eat what and as much as they want. To satisfy the appetite of each guest, a large selection of a la carte dishes are offered for dinner, making the restaurant ideal for frequent restaurant-goers and grown-ups who know what they want. The ingredients are sourced from suppliers with whom the chef has forged relationships. For example, a range of seafood is sourced from suppliers that used to supply fish to his family’s shop, and the bluefin tuna is from Yamayuki, one of the most renowned tuna brokers in Japan. In addition, the restaurant purchases Kobe beef (Tajima beef) locally in halves. These ingredients are grilled over charcoal in a brick oven. Though the simple structure of the oven requires the ingredients to be moved back and forth to fine-tune the amount of heat, the oven creates unique dishes where the ingredients are tailored to the mood of each guest at the moment.

Despite being an Italian restaurant, malca offers a wonderful selection of wines from Bourgogne, France, as well as other wine-producing regions all over the world. The restaurant is also known for its original “malca beer.”

malca boasts a main dining room with a large wooden counter that seats up to eight guests and two private dining rooms that seat up to four and six guests, respectively. If you choose to sit at the counter, you can watch the chef and his young team in the open kitchen. The lively kitchen will heighten your expectations for a great dining experience. In addition to fish and meat dishes, several kinds of quality handmade pasta are also available, making the restaurant a popular destination for foodies. In fact, it has already been added to the list of selected restaurants in a world-famous gourmet guide.
At malca, you can eat whatever you may desire at the moment. Enjoy a la carte dining at this exclusive restaurant that offers a wide range of options for guests to choose from.
nearestStations: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line Gaienmae Station, about 3 minutes by walk from Exit 1b

244064.longDescription:
“Even ingredients without a name deserve a frame, creating a new connection between ingredient and diner,” says owner-chef Hideyuki Shibata, a native of Rubeshibe, Hokkaido. He refined his skills at Restaurant Monna Lisa Ebisu from 1999, and in 2006 traveled to France to further his training at several acclaimed three-star establishments. In 2009, he became head chef at Monna Lisa Marunouchi, and in 2016, he opened his own restaurant, La Clairière in Shirokane-Takanawa. With its warm atmosphere and cuisine rooted in nature, the restaurant drew wide attention and earned one star in a world-renowned gourmet guide. In 2025, Shibata unveiled his new venture in Minami-Aoyama: mærge..

The name mærge is born from a blend of the French word “marge” (margin, frame) and the English word “merge.” Shibata personally visits producers across Japan, engaging in direct dialogue to select only the finest ingredients. With this sincere approach, he creates modern French cuisine that shines a spotlight on ingredients sourced from some of Japan’s most exceptional producers. The tasting menu, composed of 11 courses, offers what he calls “truthful cuisine,” closely tied to the rhythms of nature and everyday life.

To complement the food, the restaurant offers around 300 wines from across the globe, with a focus on French bottles. From seasonal selections to rare labels, the curation is wide-ranging. Sommelier Yasuhide Tobita carefully selects each pairing, enhancing the lingering resonance of every dish.

The interior design takes inspiration from the ancient Chinese philosophy of the Five Elements (Wu Xing). Master plasterer Yuki Kizumi crafted the undulating walls to evoke an unfinished, open-ended beauty. The modern, refined space—imbued with the gentle rhythm of nature—provides an elegant setting for business dinners, anniversaries, or romantic occasions. In Tokyo, one of the world’s foremost dining capitals, mærge invites guests to discover dialogue with extraordinary creations.

244774.longDescription:
A 8 minute-walk from Tokyo Metro Azabu-Juban Station, “Azabu Sannohashi Takenami” is located in a quiet area away from the busy station area where people come and go. Chef Suguru Takenami has 25 to 26 years of experience training at Japanese restaurants and sushi restaurants in Tokyo. He became independent in November 2019 and opened his own sushi restaurant “Azabu Sannohashi Takenami”.

In the "Omakase Course", you can fully enjoy dishes made with seasonal ingredients and Edomae-style sushi. Ingredients are from Fukuoka, Hokkaido, Shizuoka, etc. Seafood is purchased daily at Toyosu Market. The vinegared rice, which can be said to be the key to making sushi, is made by cooking the Koshihikari rice, designated by the producer, in a pot and blending it with rice vinegar and red vinegar. The restaurant has a wide variety of wine, such as red, white and champagne, mainly French wine. There is carefully-selected seasonal sake from a reliable sake store regardless of the production area or brand. As for shochu, only rice shochu is available. The dinnerware is mainly works of modern artists, such as Bizen-ware and Kutani-ware.

The restaurant is located in a building with a tasteful appearance. When you pass through the noren, the L-shaped counter (8 seats) made of Japanese cypress stands out in the warm space, unified by wood and mud walls. There is enough space between each seats, so you will be able to relax. You can enjoy not only the food, but also the peaceful space where chef Takenami's spirit reaches together with your family, friends, dates and other important people. It is also recommended for guests from overseas.

245476.longDescription:
About seven minutes on foot from Shirogane Takanawa subway station, the sushi restaurant, Fukasaka, is perched on the 10th floor of a building facing a main road. The restaurant takes its name from its proprietor, Yusuke Fukasaka, who devotes himself every day to creating dishes in his own style to delight guests.

Chef Fukasaka decided to pursue a career as a sushi chef as he was impressed by the cuisine at Sushi Takahashi in Ginza, where he worked a part-time job while attending Hattori Nutrition College in Yoyogi. After graduating from the college, he learned the basics of sushi-making at Sushi Hashimoto in Shintomi for three years. He then joined a team to open a Japanese restaurant, Sowado, in Hiroo, where he worked for two years to broaden his culinary horizons. With an eye toward opening his own restaurant one day, he leased the space of Sushi Ryo in Ginza, run by Chef Ryo Sasaki, who took the same class as him in college, to serve lunch. Then, pursuing his own style of sushi and delicacies, the self-taught chef opened his own restaurant, Fukasaka, in March 2024. 

The restaurant’s name does not include the word ‘sushi’ because the chef intends to offer a unique combination of sushi and delicacies not commonly found at other sushi restaurants. In fact, he desires to make the restaurant genreless in the future. Fukasaka is also known for offering the perfect marriage of dishes and sake selected by Sommelier Mikiko Kido, who jointly runs the restaurant.

Chef Fukasaka visits several brokers in Toyosu Market every morning to source fresh ingredients, which are turned into full-course meals, each consisting of 5 to 6 delicacies and 10 pieces of nigirizushi. Among them, the sushi rice with seasonal fish and vegetables dressed in sticky sauce is particularly popular for the rich flavors offered by the carefully selected ingredients. The sushi rice itself, made with Tsuyahime, a high-end rice brand, from Yamagata and seasoned with a blend of red, rice, and black vinegar, is also appreciated for its punchy flavors that pair well with sake. The drink menu offers a great selection of sake curated by the proprietress from around Japan. Meanwhile, the wine list focuses on natural wines from around the world, including not only France but also Australia, Germany, and the U.S. If you do not know which beverage to choose, ask for recommendations from the proprietress, who is thoroughly familiar with the flavors of Fukasaka.

The luxurious dining area is separated by a modern eight-seat counter that overlooks the open kitchen decorated with light grey Japanese washi paper created by Wataru Hatano, a washi paper craftsman from Kyoto. The brilliantly colored ceramic plates created by artists, including Ryuta Fukumura from Fukuoka, Yu Maruta from Saga, and Nobuhiko Tanaka from Saitama add sophistication that goes beyond regular sushi restaurants, as carefully planned by the proprietor. “I hope our guests will feel at home and enjoy their time at our restaurant” says Chef Fukasaka. So please indulge your palate to your heart’s content at Fukasaka on various occasions, ranging from intimate meals with your friends, family, or date to business dinners with overseas guests.
nearestStations: 7 minutes walk from Shirokane-Takanawa Station on the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line and Toei Mita Line

244695.longDescription:
Established in 1982. The former Grand Maison of Restaurant Hiramatsu Hiroo was "Hiramatsu Tei," a small restaurant in Nishiazabu. It has moved to a place one minute walk from Hiroo Station. Hiroshima-born Hiroki Hiramatsu is the second generation chef.

Chef Hiramatsu trained at Les Prés d'Eugenie-Michel Guérard after graduating from the Tsuji-style group in France as the top of the class. In 2003, he joined Hiramatsu Inc., sharpened his skills in Restaurant Hiramatsu Hiroo, and returned to France. After training at L’Auberge de l’Ill and Paul Bocues, he served as the sous-chef of Restaurant Hiramatsu Paris before becoming the head chef in Restaurant Hiramatsu Hiroo in 2012.

The theme of Chef Hiramatsu's cooking is subtraction, where the basic sauce and garnishes of French cuisine are kept to a minimum, and excessive staging is eliminated. "It's not just simple. When I looked into how I could enhance French culture as a Japanese chef and how I could please and impress customers, it naturally turned into my own French cuisine," says Chef Hiramatsu. The ingredients are sourced from Japan, such as Okamoto Farm in Hiroshima and Kajinami Farm in Miyazaki. They are carefully selected from producers who can be called partners because of the trusted relationship. About 20 types of cheese, mainly from France and Italy, are served on the wagon, including domestic cheese from Hiroshima and other cities. The chef has a close relationship with Hiroshima, his hometown. Also, when it comes to Restaurant Hiramatsu Hiroo, there is a rare and rich wine stock. There are more than 500 brands and a wide range of vintage wines on the wine curve, and about 3,000 wines await their debut. The sommelier will suggest wine that goes well with the cuisine prepared by Chef Hiramatsu.
 
The restaurant is bright and gorgeous with lots of greenery and sunshine during lunch time. The wall is decorated with all the original paintings of the artist, and the first floor is a luxurious private room surrounded by the warm entrance and artworks. On the second floor, there is a semi-private room with a beautiful view of the trees from the large window and a completely private room with a fireplace. The third floor is the main dining area. Luxuriously, there is a private art museum in the basement, and it is an elegant space where you can enjoy food and art. You will want to enjoy the deep French cuisine drawn by the chef Hiramatsu at family gatherings, date, business gatherings, wine gatherings and with guests from overseas.

244148.longDescription: In February 2017, a Chinese restaurant ""Sazenka"" opened in a corner of the high-level residential area around ​​Minami Azabu. Executive Chef Tomoya Kawada's restaurant is cutting-edge in both name and reality, proposing "the best hospitality" and "the best cuisine" as a new Chinese cuisine with a uniquely Japanese spirit and ingredients. After studying Chinese cuisine at Nishiazabu ""Azabu Changjiang"", and Japanese cuisine in ""RyuGin"" , Chef Tomoya participates in the launch of Taiwan ""Shoun RyuGin"" where he served as Chef. Taking advantage of this achievement, he distributed ""Chinese cuisine in Japan"" to the world through seasonal Japanese ingredients along with Chinese cuisine techniques and charcoal grilling skills. Such as special ""two kinds of baby pigeon"", using Ibaraki prefecture's asphyxiant pigeon, including legs cooked by traditional technique unique to Chinese cuisine, and breast cooked by modern charcoal fire, two kinds of tailoring in one dish to enjoy. Alcohol drinks matching with cooking include an alcohol pairing of wine, Japanese sake, Shaoxing wine and many other choices. From the Chef Tomoya's idea that ""customers who are not good at sake may also enjoy pairing with cuisine."" , Tea pairing is also available here. Chinese and Japanese tea with various temperature zones and providing method is all prepared. The chic and luxurious main dining hall on the first floor, and three private rooms in both first and second floor, would be a good suggestion for dinner and dating. Service in two languages ​including ​Japanese, English are all available here, which makes here the best choice welcoming overseas guests. ※ Awarded 3 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 【Nearby Hotels】 ■ Nogizaka ""The Ritz-Carlton Tokyo"" ■ Roppongi ""Grand Hyatt Tokyo"" ■ Akasaka ""ANA Intercontinental Hotel Tokyo"" ■ Shibuya ""Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel""

243776.longDescription:
In July 2017, distinguished sushi restaurant Sushi ICHIKAWA moved from Setagaya district to the center of Tokyo city- Shirokane Takanawa.

The owner chef Katsumi Ichikawa has a 7-year experience of training at a well-known Kyoto cuisine restaurant 'Kikunoi' , later training at a sushi restaurant for 4 years, founding his own Sushi place in 2012.

Ichikawa has a keen interest in tuna so the chef creates special sushi rice to match it; thus his nigiri sushi basically consists of tuna. Performing with traditional Tokyo-style, you could taste the subtle gems of traditional Kyoto cuisine. The reticent chef prepares he sushi with small amount of rice that ladies could enjoy with ease.
Visit here to enjoy Sushi with the finest pairing drinks he recommends.

With the strength of will, the chef starts a new page in Shirokane Takanawa. The restaurant continues to progress, suitable for business dining or ladies gathering. 


* It is located in a small path connected to Azabu street, just behind the "Ai Kindergarten South Azabu".  Since there is no signboards and name outside, please check our exterior photos.
