244644.longDescription:
Located near the Furukawa Bridge in Minami Azabu, between Azabu Juban and Shirokane–Takanawa, Yakitori Shimaya opened in 2017. It is owned by the brothers XX and Kojiro Urashima, whose father used to run a yakitori restaurant in their hometown in Mie Prefecture, leading both the brothers to pursue a career in the food and beverage industry. The brothers trained in separate restaurants before opening Yakitori Shimaya together.

The carefully selected chicken served at Yakitori Shimaya is Kumano jidori, a high-grade brand of chicken from Mie, and jukusei dori, which is Takasaka dori, a rare kind of chicken from Tamba, Kyoto that has been aged for 10 days. Takasaka dori is said to be the only sterile chicken available in the world. Kumano jidori is a hybrid of the Mie Prefecture-produced Yakido game fowl, the prefecture's famous Ise akadori, and the Nagoya cochin. Kumano jidori chickens are raised on specialty citrus fruits, rice harvested from terraces in the Kumano region of Mie Prefecture, and water that flows down from the area around the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage trails. The meat is very red and dense with flavor, with a taste and a full-bodied quality reminiscent of game. Kumano jidori grilled on genuine Kishu Binchotan charcoal and finished with pearl salt from Ise-Shima creates an exquisite dish full of Mie ingredients. Meanwhile, the jukusei dori can be aged from 10 days to 2 weeks. The aging of chicken is generally considered difficult, and the reason why this is possible here is because of the existence of Takasaka dori. The birds are raised on healthy feed and in clean enclosures, and the meat is judged to be sterile. With its rich and delicious flavor, Takasaka dori is a different dimension to your average chicken. Vegetables are mainly sourced from Keiko Kondo, who practices natural farming in Mie. The wonderful thing about Shimaya is its use of these select ingredients to serve customers a wide variety of chicken dishes that includes sashimi, tataki seared chicken, and gut stew, in addition to yakitori. For drinks, about 10 different kinds of sake, mainly produced in Mie Prefecture, are available, together with robust red and white wines that are not overwhelmed by the chicken.

With a five-meter ceiling and a great sense of spaciousness provided by the atrium, Shimaya’s modern, quality interior was designed with “the finest of the everyday” as the concept. Seating focuses on the slab counter of African cherry wood, but private rooms with tables and a 2nd-floor private room are also available. In particular, the private room on the upper floor is limited to one group per day and also has its own bathroom and smoking room. It is recommended for customers who wish to take their time over a course. Shimaya is like a resting place where customers are served yakitori a touch more luxurious than the everyday kind.

244308.longDescription:
Shunkeian Arakaki is located on Shintomichō’s main street. The restaurant Shunkeian, was used by the owner, Kaname Arakaki, to create the feeling of "a small restaurant where you can flavor each season". It is a restaurant where you can enjoy a relaxing meal and palate Japanese cuisine and tempura which use seasonal ingredients.

Mr. Arakaki trained for 10 years in the Japanese restaurant Tsukiji-Edogin, and another Japanese restaurant in Roppongi. From the age of 28 he spent 20 years working as head chef for various Japanese restaurants. Then in 2014, he opened Shunkeian Arakaki in Kachidoki, Tokyo. He relocated the restaurant to Shintomichō and reopened inJuly 2017. 

Since Mr. Arakaki is from Okinawa, dishes use a variety of ingredients from Okinawa, for example, for the a la carte tempura, gourd, green papaya, and Okinawa carrots are used. He also focused on local ingredients like sillago and conger caught in Tokyo bay. The tempura served at the restaurant is made by putting red bream and rockfish on konbu (kelp) and wrap them with yuba, or halfbeak served with pickled plum and Japanese pepper (ume-sansho), dried seaweed. 
　
The course begins with appetizers, a side dish and sake, followed by a dish to clean the palate, then 7 dishes of tempura that are served in 2 parts. There are many fans of the shiba shrimp tempura or tencha (steamed rice topped with kakiage and hot green tea) along with the brown sugar pudding desert. There are 5 kinds of Japanese sake which change depending on the season, 10 kinds of South African wine which pair well with the tempuras, along with whiskey and Awamori.

The restaurant has 7 counter seats made from hinoki cypress, and is a calm setting where you can feel the warmth of wood. It’s a heaven for adults who are looking to kick back and enjoy a meal and alcohol at their own leisure, or in occasions such as casual entertainment, couples' anniversaries, etc.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

*The meal starts all at the same time. The restaurant's opening time will vary depending on the first booking on that day, so operating hours may vary. We ask for your understanding in advance.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Exit 7 of Shintomichō Station on the Tokyo Metro Yurakucho line

I had the pleasure of dining at Shunkeian Arakaki, a 2 Michelin-starred tempura restaurant, and I can confidently say that it was an experience unlike any other. From start to finish, everything about the meal was exceptional.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is also top-notch, with a calm and serene ambiance that is perfect for a special occasion or intimate dinner.

Overall, I would highly recommend Shunkeian Arakaki to anyone looking for an exceptional tempura experience. The food, service, and atmosphere are all exceptional, and it's easy to see why this restaurant has earned its 2 Michelin stars. 244329.longDescription: world gourmet guide award Tempura Shimomura is located in a residential area in Taito ward, about 5-minute walk from Shin-okachimachi Station. The owner, Mitsuhiko Shimomura worked as the assistant head chef for the famous tempura restaurant Tempura to Washoku in Yamanoue for 20 years. Tempura Shimomura opened in September 2017 as a restaurant where customers can enjoy tempura at a reasonable price, in comparison to high-end dining. The seasonal ingredients are chosen by Shimomura himself from Tsukiji Market. From winter to spring, the seasonal courses include puffer fish, fresh sea urchin, carp sprouts, and cod sprouts. In the latter half of the course, a la carte sweet potato tempura is available, it is deep fried for 40 minutes, creating a firm texture and it is as sweet as a dessert. Brandy can be added to upon customer's preference, that has a taste similar to a chestnut glaze. The carefully stocked ingredients are stored in a traditional ice refrigerator which keeps them from drying and remain in the best conditions. Sesame oil is used to fry the tempura. The pot to make the tempura have 2 temperature settings, low and high, to produce an exquisite temperature. A dipping sauce or Okinawa salt is then provided. Alcohol includes seasonal recommended sake, shochu, wine, etc. It’s the home-like hospitality of Tempura Shimomura which complements the tempura and made it a well-known restaurant. This is a restaurant where the proprietress wrote the restaurant’s name plaque herself, and consists of 10 spacious counter seats, as well as table-seat for 4 people. The wood colors add warmth to the restaurant's atmosphere. Customers with babies are also welcome to taste the finest tempura in a warm atmosphere. Word of mouth made this a well-known restaurant and there is an increasing number of people who have traveled from far away to visit. Why not come and experience an innovative tempura restaurant which have the characteristics of the cheerfulness of the downtown with a high-class restaurant? ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2023 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? Children are welcome. Tendon(1,210 Yen/ tax incl.) and other a la carte dishes can be ordered in advance. Children's chairs are also available at tables. Please consult us in advance. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? Wheelchairs are welcome. We recommend our table seats for guests with wheelchairs. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? We can offer a la carte Tempura option. Also, for our vegetarian customers, if egg in the Tempura batter is acceptable, we can offer vegetable Tempura. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, our staff only speak Japanese. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? We do not have a dress code.

243689.longDescription:
At this Kyo-style 'Kaiseki' (traditional Japanese course-based meal) restaurant, the quaint surroundings that you encounter upon arrival will make you feel as if you have stepped into Kyoto. 

Starting with the use of Kyoto-grown vegetables, all of our ingredients - even the most basic elements such as soy sauce and miso - are carefully-selected from Kyoto, and even the tableware designs add to the Kyoto-style atmosphere. Wherever you look, it it easy to see owner Mr. Okada's vision of a space that is "more like Kyoto than Kyoto itself."

You will be served a Kyoto-style course consists of around 10 separate dishes based on 'cha-kaiseki' (a light meal served during tea ceremonies) and vegetarian diet. The rice, served in 'cha-kaiseki' style, is particularly exquisite.

Because of the detailed care we put into meal preparation, we could serve only five parties per day. The seating consists of a counter made from natural wood, which has eight seats, and a private dining room at the back of the restaurant. Enjoy Japanese-style cuisine while relaxing and watching the owner at work preparing your meal. The restaurant is the perfect space to enjoy casual conversation with friends, and dining companions while being mesmerized by the enchanting atmosphere of Kyoto.
nearestStations: 7-minute walk from Ebisu station (East Exit), JR Yamanote Line

18.longDescription: Descend a quiet staircase on Sakurada-dori street down to the basement floor, and you will encounter a subdued, dignified atmosphere hanging above the stone-paved path leading to Japanese Cuisine Seizan. This world gourmet guide awarded restaurant's interior channels a modern Japanese aesthetic. Guests can observe the owner chef's brilliant knife skills up close at counter seats, but the restaurant also has private dining rooms suitable for business meetings and receptions. Seizan incorporates seasonal ingredients in their dishes. Their grilled suzuki (Japanese sea bass) is seasoned with the perfect amount of salt, and the gobo mochi (poppy seed rice cake) on the side quietly yet intensely maximizes the flavors of the dish. Just when you feel that you have tasted all there is to the ingredients, Seizan gives you a glimpse to another flavor that is hidden in them. While savoring the dishes beyond your imagination, you can also take visual pleasure in the elegant tableware. Enjoy the seasonal sensations and forget the hustle and bustle of city life while dining in this oasis in the city. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 3 to 4 people. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room(s). ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customizations for vegetarian, vegan or low calories. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 10 years of age. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? Unfortunately, we do not have staff that speaks English. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? The private dining room offers table(s) and chairs (Western style). ■ Are photos allowed in the restaurant? Photos are allowed; however, we ask you to respect dining experience of others (no flash, no shutter sound, no photos of other guests or our staff, no video).
nearestStations: 8-minute walk from Tamachi station (Mita Exit), JR Yamanote Line

244546.longDescription:
Kiyosumi-Shirakawa in Tokyo has been called an "art town". Opened in 2018, "O2" is a Chinese cuisine restaurant where diners can casually enjoy first-rate dishes along with stylish interior and exterior designs that blend seamlessly into this artistic place.

The owner-chef Kotaro Otsu is a certified Vegetable Sommelier who has become popular for his novel Chinese cuisine unbound by stereotypes. Mr. Otsu spent 15 years training at the Chinese restaurant "Turandot Garyukyo". After serving there as sous chef, he achieved his dream of starting his own restaurant under his name, "O2."

The course options showcase the flavors of ingredients not only from Tsukiji Market but also shipped directly from Taiwan. The main dishes are "boiled shark fin" and the melt-in-your-mouth tender "beef cheek stew." The wine to match is mostly natural wine from France. A full lineup of Chinese teas is also available, so you can enjoy discovering a new favorite drink to go with your meal and mood.

Mr. Otsu's sensibilities are evident not only in his cooking but also in the restaurant itself. Although the interior is small with just tables and 6 counter seats, its high ceiling gives an extraordinary feeling of spaciousness. Space is uniformly colored in dark green and wood tones and decorated all over with the chef's beloved Star Wars memorabilia. Tasteful city pop music plays from order-made amps and speakers, often introducing guests to the music of Mr. Otsu's favorite musician "Rekishi". Add delicious wine and food to the mix, and you can't help but feel joy. Why not come to stylishly gritty Kiyosumi-Shirakawa to have a chat at the counter or socialize with friends over casual, first-rate dining without the pretense?
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Kiyosumishirakawa Station, Exit B2(Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line)

245332.longDescription:
Situated at a convenient location, a few steps from Morishita Station and an eight-minute walk from Kiyosumi Shirakawa Station, in an old neighborhood that retains the friendly atmosphere of the shitamachi area, Nihon Ryori Takahashi is helmed by Chef Tadashi Takahashi, who aims to reproduce the flavors and spirit of Japan.

Chef Takahashi trained at renowned Japanese restaurants, including Wako in Mejiro (permanently closed) and two-starred Kaiseki Komuro in Kagurazaka, and further honed his culinary skills overseas at Nobu London in the UK, Nobu Melbourne in Australia, and a Japanese restaurant in Singapore before he opened his own restaurant, Nihon Ryori Takahashi, in 2020.
As he says that he “wanted to open a restaurant near Toyosu Market,” Chef Takahashi places great emphasis on the freshness of ingredients. He visits Toyosu Market every day to look for the best ingredients of the day while exchanging information with brokers on friendly terms and purchases plum, Japanese pepper, and wild duck from producers introduced to him by his former master at Kaiseki Komuro.
The chef’s choice meals consist of seven to eight courses, starting with appetizers and ending with Japanese mixed rice and desserts. The authentic Japanese dishes are conjured up from carefully selected ingredients by Chef Takahashi in front of guests at the counter.
Nihon Ryori Takahashi always keeps five to six labels of sake in stock, from which the chef selects pairings for guests who ask for suggestions based on their preferences and paces. For example, with a clean flavor, Kamokinshu from Hiroshima is good to start with. AKABU from Iwate, which has been included in the sake list since the chef worked in Singapore, is also worth a try. The plum wine home-brewed from plum directly sourced from the producer enjoys popularity as well.

In the understated dining room with warm wooden elements and vermillion accents, an inspiring painting by Akira Yamaguchi, a contemporary artist, conveys the spirit of Japanese culture. NIIZAWA Junmai Daiginjo, Japanese sake from Niizawa Brewery in Miyagi with a matching label designed by the same artist is also kept in stock.
“Take a step inside, and you will find yourself in another dimension. Enjoy the exciting world like an amusement park,” says Chef Takahashi. Follow his advice and share the amazing experience with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues. Guests from overseas can also enjoy Japanese dishes and friendly conversations with Chef Takahashi, who has extensive overseas experience.
nearestStations: 30 seconds walk from Toei Shinjuku Line Morishita Station Exit A7

245177.longDescription:
A 5-minute walk from Akasaka-mitsuke Station brings guests to Kaiseki Tsujitome, a 1-star restaurant quietly set among office buildings in Motoakasaka. A renowned establishment, Tsujitome is a long-established restaurant specialized in kaiseki cuisine (tea-ceremony dishes).

The first-generation proprietor, Tomejiro Tsuji, learned cha-kaiseki cuisine (a multi-dish meal followed by a tea ceremony) from the 13th head of Urasenke School of Tea in Kyoto and started a catering business to send chefs to prepare kaiseki meals for tea ceremonies. The second-generation proprietor, Kaichi Tsuji, opened a cha-kaiseki restaurant in Tokyo to offer wider awareness to the cuisine. The present third-generation proprietor, Yoshikazu Tsuji, trained under Rosanjin Kitaoji, known as an artist, gastronome, and culinary explorer. His teachings were transferred to chef Tatsumi Fujimoto, who demonstrates his culinary skills for Tsujitome today.

The menu follows the flowing style of cha-kaiseki cuisine, starting with an appetizer of sashimi or vinegared fish or vegetables, followed by simmered fish or chicken with vegetables in clear soup; an assortment of sea and mountain delicacies; an assortment of simmered vegetables; a grilled meat or fish; a delicacy to accompany Japanese sake; a bowl of soup; and a bowl of rice, finishing with seasonal fruits, sweets, and thin matcha tea. 

Each dish is made with seasonal ingredients sourced from suppliers that have worked with the restaurant for years. The ingredients are carefully prepared one-by-one to highlight their natural flavors.

The food menu itself has been adored for years for its seasonal flavors as well as its reminiscence of the great cultural figures of the old days. For example, the pike conger in soup is called “Peony Pike Conger” because Junichiro Tanizaki, a famous Japanese writer, described it as being beautiful as a peony. The “Hamokawa Bowl,” a bowl of rice with pike conger cooked so that it can be eaten whole, was born from the spirit of wasting nothing – an approach the third-generation proprietor learned from Rosanjin Kitaoji. These popular dishes make regulars look forward to the fish’s seasonal window.

The restaurant offers a variety of Japanese sake, among which Kiku-Masamune Taru Sake from Hyogo is recommended for those who enjoy hot sake. Those who prefer cold sake are directed towards Higan Daiginjo (Uchimizu) from Niigata, which was selected by the third-generation proprietor, who traveled around Japan searching for quality Japanese sake with Togo Kobayashi, a Japanese ceramist.

Inside the restaurant, guests are seated within four private rooms with a dining table or a low horigotatsu table (table over a hole in the floor) and a main dining room. One of the private rooms, with an area of approx. 15 m2, can also be used as a tea room by installing a fireplace on the floor.

Adorned with hanging scroll paintings, calligraphic works, and ceramics crafted by Rosanjin Kitaoji, Kaiseki Tsujitome is suitable for various occasions, such as intimate gatherings and business meetings. Guests are invited to enjoy Japanese cuisine and culture at this renowned restaurant.
nearestStations: A 5-minutes on foot from Exit B of Akasaka-mitsuke Station on the Ginza Line and Marunouchi Line

243727.longDescription:
Located right in the center point from the districts of Roppongi, Hiroo, and Azabu-Juban, in Tokyo. Alveare is a hidden gem of an Italian restaurant situated near Roppongi Hills, within 12 to 13 minutes' walk from each respective station, set underground within a quiet residential area. 

On November 18, 2024, our restaurant began a new chapter by welcoming Yuto Kanno, a chef who has honed his skills at renowned establishments throughout Japan, as our chef de cuisine. He values the combination and balance of ingredients, creating flavors that are simple yet profound. Using fresh seafood from fishing ports across Japan and vegetables and meats from Italy and France, he crafts each dish to bring out the unique qualities of each ingredient.

For dinner, in the early hours of the evening, the restaurant serves only a one-course menu, where you can enjoy about 12 dishes, and in the late hours, you can enjoy an a la carte menu, where guests can relax and enjoy. Lunch is only available on Saturdays and is served as a course menu. The restaurant prides itself in sourcing its ingredients directly from the production areas all around Japan, charming its guests with dishes featuring delicate flavors based on the four seasons of Japan. Alveare can also be enjoyed as a wine bar as there are always 10-15 types of glass wine.

This is a restaurant to be visited with your most cherished guests, offering a quiet and relaxing service, either at the counter or table seating, or in a private room. Dessert plates is as a special offer under request alongside a advance reservation, making it a perfect venue to spend a luxurious time on anniversary dates, birthdays, wine gatherings, and more.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Roppongi Station (Exit 3), Toei Oedo Line
15-minute walk from Roppongi Station (Exit 1b), Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line

245442.longDescription:
About a five-minute walk from Azabu Juban subway station, Ippei Hanten is hidden in a back alley away from the hustle and bustle. It is helmed by Chef Ippei Adachi, who trained at different Chinese restaurants, ranging from street food stalls to high-end dining establishments, in Japan and Hong Kong for over two decades before he opened his own restaurant named after himself in 2022. The restaurant, Ippei Hanten, has gained instant popularity and received one star in a gastronomic guide. According to the chef, the location was selected because the contrast of the dark alley with the brightly lit high rises seen through it reminded the chef of his favorite place in Hong Kong.

Chef Adachi offers Hong Kong cuisine featuring seafood. He has also invented original recipes, not from scratch but by reinterpreting Hong Kong culinary techniques and flavors with Japanese ingredients. These dishes show up on the prix-fixe menu that consists of 14 courses, ranging from appetizers to desserts. The perishable and seasonal items, such as vegetables and seafood, are delivered from around Japan, from Hokkaido in the north to Nagasaki in the south, while dried foods, pickles, and seasonings are selected and sourced by the chef himself from Hong Kong every few months.

The restaurant’s specialty, “Steamed Dumplings in (Fotiaoqiang) Soup with Delicacies from the Land and Sea,” is an opulent dish of steamed dumplings with Fotiaoqiang soup (which literally means “Buddha-jumps-over-the-wall soup” in Chinese), a rich traditional soup from Fujiang with a tempting smell that makes a monk jump over the wall of a temple. Another unique feature of the restaurant is that it adopts the concept of chakaiseki cuisine. For example, the full-course meal starts with a small bowl of congee with flavorful seasonal ingredients to warm up the stomach and stimulate the appetite.

The drink menu curated by Manager Shu Nagai offers a great selection of shaoxing, Burgundy, and Champagne wines and beers, but even more recommended is the pairing menu, where a careful selection of 10 brews, mostly wines but also including Japanese sake and other liquors, and one Chinese tea are served in the right amount at the right time to accompany dishes.

The interior is warm with wood fixtures and earthen walls inspired by downtown Hong Kong. The food is served on white china plates created by modern artists, such as Hanako Nakazato and Shinpei Watanabe. With a counter that seats eight and three private dining rooms, the restaurant is the perfect place for private dining experiences, such as family and friend gatherings and date nights, as well as business dinners with overseas customers. Please enjoy Hong Kong cuisine prepared by the Hong Kong-trained chef at Ippei Hanten.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245547.longDescription:
About eight minutes’ walk from Roppongi Station, Taira is an intimate sushi restaurant on the first floor of a condominium building in the quiet residential area of Moto-Azabu.  The kitchen is helmed by Owner-Chef Koichi Taira, who greets guests with a warm smile while showcasing his craftsmanship. Hailing from the remote island of Tokunoshima in the Amami Region of Kagoshima Prefecture, he started his career as a sushi apprentice at a renowned hotel in Osaka.  Then, he honed his culinary skills at sushi and Japanese restaurants in Japan and abroad. He also worked at a distinguished restaurant in Kyoto and served as the fourth-generation chef of a famed restaurant in Minami-Aoyama for three years before setting up in business on his own.  His restaurant, Taira, opened in Moto-Azabu in March 2022.

The restaurant takes pride in its simple delicacies and sushi, crafted using authentic Edomae techniques. The fresh seasonal fish is directly sourced from around Kyushu, such as Amakusa, Yawatahama, and Fukuoka, while tuna is purchased from Yamayuki, a popular wholesaler, in Toyosu Market. The sushi rice is made from an original blend of rice from Miyagi and Iwate prefectures and a blend of three types of Fuji vinegar (red, rice, and pure rice vinegar) from Iio Jozo in Kyoto. The seasonings are also carefully selected, including two varieties of wasabi from two producing areas, Azumino City in Nagano Prefecture and Gotemba City in Shizuoka Prefecture, and the naturally fermented, flavorful Mitsuboshi Soy Sauce from Wakayama. These fine ingredients are incorporated into the chef’s choice prix-fixe menu, which offers 5 to 7 delicacies and 11 to 13 pieces of nigiri sushi. The meal starts with Freshly Cooked Brown Rice, accompanied by homemade dried mullet roe. This is a signature dish of Chef Taira, inspired by the rice that tantalized his taste buds with its springy texture as he was treated to a meal by a farmer.

The sake list offers about 30 varieties, such as Hakurakusei from Miyagi, Azumaichi from Saga, Isojiman from Shizuoka, Nifudazake from Kamonishiki in Niigata, and some seasonal limited options. The drink menu also includes champagnes, white wines, whiskies, shochu, and non-alcoholic options. If you are not sure which drink to try, ask the chef to choose for you. The interior is understated with soft lighting to focus attention on the L-shaped hinoki wood counter (seating up to 9 guests). The internationally experienced Chef Taira explains each piece of sushi in both English and Japanese, making the dining experience comfortable and memorable for any guests, whether they are looking to entertain business clients from around the world or enhance personal celebrations. Please indulge in exquisite delicacies and sushi showcasing the craftsmanship of Edomae techniques.

244333.longDescription:
Located on the eastern bank of the Sumida River, Mukojima is known as the largest geisha district in Tokyo. It boasts numerous well-established restaurants, but among them, Kiyoshi is considered to be a good choice for beginners, due to its balance between tradition and warmth. Established in 1949, the building and premises have remained relatively unchanged for the past 70 years. Its traditional Japanese-style wooden structure exudes a nostalgic Showa period ambiance.

Kiyoshi is currently run by Ms. Ayako Kobayashi, a third generation proprietress. Ms. Kobayashi is highly knowledgeable about traditional neighborhoods (she has even been invited to give lectures at universities) and has protected the traditions and dignity of Kiyoshi over the years. At this establishment, the proprietress and waitresses wear kimonos as they serve customers. It's also possible to arrange a Mukojima geisha, who are known for their pleasant nature, to dance or play a song on the shamisen for you while you dine, allowing you to experience the hospitality of Japanese culture.

While this sort of establishment might seem intimidating, the atmosphere is in fact very friendly, as the residents of Mukojima are not ones to stand on ceremony. The proprietress is very approachable, so this is a good choice for foreigners or those not familiar with geisha districts. The food served at Kiyoshi is made from in-season ingredients gathered from all over the country, including Tsukiji. They serve authentic kaiseki cuisine that allows you to appreciate the different seasonal flavors.

Kiyoshi has 6 private rooms, ranging from a cozy little room for 2-3 people to a large hall for parties of up to 25. All the rooms are Japanese-style with tatami mat flooring, and there are also hori-gotatsu seats, which are favored by foreigners and elderly customers. Some rooms even have karaoke machines, demonstrating flexibility in responding to customer needs. From the rooms to the food and service, everything is exquisite. I highly recommended that you try a traditional restaurant at least once in order to experience the architecture, clothing, and cuisine of traditional Japan.

245401.longDescription:
Tokyo’s Nagatacho district is the center of Japanese politics, lined with such government buildings as the House of Representatives Office and the Official Residence of the Prime Minister. Nagatacho Sushi Kanesaka opened in July 2022 in an elegant house in a prestigious townscape. Owner-chef Toru Osumi served sushi to VIP guests at the Hokkaido Toyako Summit in 2008 and was instrumental in elevating the Kanesaka Group’s Macau restaurant into a star-winning hotspot.

Chef Osumi, who carries on the tradition of Edomae sushi, embodies the philosophy of “changing the taste without changing the form,” or developing new ideas based on studying the past. He carefully scrutinizes and sources the best ingredients every morning at the Toyosu Market to perfect the Osumi style of Edomae. The “omakase” chef’s choice course features of six side dishes and 10 pieces of nigiri. A futomaki roll was added in response to guests’ requests, followed by egg, soup, and dessert to finish the course.

Chef Okuma says, “Above all, I am particular about rice.” He uses the Yukiwakamaru variety from Kurosawa Farm in Yamagata Prefecture. After participating in rice harvesting and seeing the exhausting attention to soil and moisture content, he chose the Yukiwakamaru variety, which is less sticky and sweeter, and matches well with the restaurant’s cuisine. The vinegar for the sushi rice is a blend of five types (4 white and 1 red) from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing. The blend is not changed throughout, but the optimum temperature is sought according to the sushi topping to be served.

Abalone risotto, in which abalone is added to sushi rice and dressed with an abalone liver sauce, is a signature dish. Nigiri of orient clams, simmered at a low temperature to make them tender and bursting with umami, are also popular. Another favorite is conger eel served in the traditional style of steaming in bamboo leaves. Ten labels of sake are always in stock including seasonal offerings. Champagne as well as red and white wines are available by the bottle.

The chic and modern interior was designed by an architect who also created Kanesaka’s Macau branch. Inside the restaurant, Chef Osumi, who holds a master’s license in ikebana (the art of flower arrangement),arranges flowers for the restaurant himself, evoking the changing of the seasons. Chef Osumi says, “I have heard that ikebana dates back to the time of Prince Shotoku (574-622). In Article 1 of Japan’s first constitution, Prince Shotoku stated that the spirit of harmony is to ‘Cherish the harmony among people’ and to live and let live. I started ikebana because I felt that shares something the world of sushi.”  

The sushi serving plates were crafted made by a Mishima ware artist with whom he has close ties. The restaurant’s teacups were made by the 9th Hanshichi Shirai of Imado ware. There are antiques such as early Imari ware, antique Baccarat glasses and French spoons, and other carefully selected items both charming and quaint, from tableware to cutlery. The first floor has a counter with eight seats. On the second floor, an eight-seat, L-shaped counter can be reserved for private functions. We welcome you to enjoy the restaurant in various scenes with family, friends, business colleagues, or as a couple and savor Chef Osumi’s specialties in this unforgettable setting.

245201.longDescription:
Set in a tranquil residential area a five-minute walk from Nakameguro Subway Station, Nihon Ryori Ensui is an elaborate stage for Chef Ryosuke Itou to display his culinary skills.

Nihon Ryori Ensui explores the culinary secrets of charcoal grilling and stock-making as indicated by its name (“En” means flames in Japanese and represents charcoal grilling, while “Sui” means water in Japanese and represents stock-making). The first brewed dashi stock (soup stock made from fish and kelp) is made from freshly shaved bonito flakes every time a new guest or guests arrive. Because stock-making and grilling are simple and basic techniques of Japanese cuisine, “they are the first and most difficult step,” Chef Itou says. “I would like to learn the techniques honed over generations and hand them over to the next generation.” This is the reason why he continues his culinary journey without stopping.
The soup stock is made with great care from fermented bonito slowly dried for half a year by Sakai Shoten in Ibusuki, Kagoshima, Kurai Rishiri kelp harvested in Kafuka Bay, Rebun Island , Hokkaido, and fermented in chambers under carefully controlled temperatures and humidity by Okui Kaiseido in Fukui, and hot spring water from Tarumi, Kagoshima, known for its super-soft water are used to make stock, to enhance the flavors of seasonal ingredients.
The restaurant’s popular specialties cooked with great care over high-quality Kishu Binchotan Charcoal, such as “Charcoal-grilled Red Snapper Fillet” and “Charcoal-grilled Tilefish Fillet with Skin On,” are simple yet elaborate. Nihon Ryori Ensui also offers exclusive à la carte dishes, such as an assortment of boiled foods served on a bamboo skewer like Oden (various ingredients stewed in soy-flavored dashi) and an assortment of fruits sliced using Japanese culinary techniques and arranged to look like a big peony.
The sake list features some 15 labels of Japanese sake, including those not easily available, such as Aramasa from Akita, while the wine list offers a selection of wines, mainly from Burgundy, curated by Chef Itou, who is also certified as a sommelier. The Homemade Cold Brew Tea, made with the same Tarumi hot spring water as for the soup stock, also enjoys great popularity.

Inside the restaurant, there is an eye-catching, 5.3-meter-long counter made of natural hinoki cypress wood from Sekigahara (Gifu Prefecture) (seating up to eight people). The serving stand on the countertop is very low to allow diners to enjoy as much as possible the rich aroma of bonito flakes shaved in the kitchen. The collection of tableware is also impressive, ranging from antiques to modern pieces and from ceramics crafted by ceramic artists in Kyoto to lacquerware manufactured by Yamanaka Shikki in Kaga, Ishikawa. There is also a private room (seating up to six people).
Please enjoy Japanese cuisine made with highly skilled charcoal grilling and stock-making techniques at Nihon Ryori Ensui with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

244427.longDescription:
'Onda Tokyo', located a convenient 7 minutes from Nakameguro station, resides at a stylish riverside location lined with Sakura cherry blossoms that make for an impressive sight come Spring. Chef Keisuke Nakamura, a veteran of 9 years at Shizuoka's 'Villa di Mangia Pesce (currently 'Ristorante Primavera')', honed his craft further during a pilgrimage through the various world gourmet guide awarded restaurants across Italy. 

Now having learnt the variety of local flavors that makes Italian cuisine so vibrant, he proposes an 'Italian-Japonica' cuisine; recognizing the locale-based nature of Italy's various tastes, he promotes utilizing his techniques, but bringing them with a twist that would create dishes not lesser copies but adapted imports. 

Under Nakamura's high-flying banner, a variety of seasoned staff, some of whom Nakamura himself trained alongside, coalesce; thus, with a quartet of expert specialists, 'Onda Tokyo' was born. The name 'Onda' comes from the Italian for 'wave'; the chefs, and their ideals, each a small wave, seek to combine and generate a great tsunami of impression. 

Nakamura, born in Shizuoka and with strong ties to its communities, sources his ingredients from his nature-rich home as well; from contract-farmers in Mishima to fresh-caught seafood from Odawara, he gets the best of every day's produce straight from the source.
 'Onda''s dishes, custom-made Mino-ware, also enhances the beautiful illusory blend of 'Italian-Japonica'. 

For a sensory experience brimming with Nakamura&Co.'s principle, don't miss the specialite 'Bounty of the Seas; Onda-style'. Served on Mino-ware, 6 different seasonal fish are each paired with the perfect sauce and garnish, creating a simple yet deeply satisfying blend of Japan's natural fruit and Italian culinary arts. The wine list at 'Onda Tokyo' is, fittingly, almost exclusively Italian. However their selection is quite the cellar, with bottles picked as much for their affinity to the menu as they are for their fit with the season; during Winter the cave is filled with Northern Italian labels, while as the climes thaw the availability of Southern wines does as well. 

The restaurant, which makes extensive use of wood, including cedar wood doors and counters, gives a feeling of warmth, and offers a single cedar counter seat for a total of 10 people and one private room for two people.
A secretive little hideaway with no signboard, we invite you to enjoy the one and only Italian cuisine born in this region.

244356.longDescription:
Nakameguro is a gourmet town that is attracting a lot of attention from food connoisseurs, with a large number of excellent restaurants opening in the area. In June 2020, the French restaurant Restaurant Re: reopened in the perfect location along the Meguro River, which turns pink during the cherry blossom season. The cherry blossoms in front of the restaurant are "yaezakura" (double-flowered cherry trees), so the best time to see the cherry blossoms is usually around mid-April.

After graduating from a culinary school, Chef Shinya Ueda trained at famous restaurants in Tokyo, including starred restaurants such as "chez tomo" and "le jeu de l'assiette," and worked in a wide range of styles including classical, modern, bistro, and wine restaurants. After working in a wide range of restaurants, including classical, modern, bistro, and wine restaurants, he became the chef of "Restaurant Re:". He says he wants to create a place with customers where they can rediscover the value of local cuisine and ingredients by incorporating ingredients and food culture from all over Japan. 

The monthly course menu features a specialty for each month, so even if you visit every month, you will be able to enjoy a new discovery. The ingredients are carefully selected so that they are not only delicious, but also tell the story and background of their creators. The restaurant also puts as much emphasis on wine as it does on food, with a wide selection of wines from around the world, including Champagne and Burgundy (over 100 varieties) carefully selected by Sommelier Excellence, as well as Japanese sake, shochu, spirits, and more to match the cuisine. The restaurant also offers a wide selection of non-alcoholic beverages, making it ideal for dinners that do not involve alcohol.

Facing a row of cherry blossom trees, the glass-walled restaurant has a 10-seat counter, tables for 4, private rooms for up to 8 persons, and semi-private rooms for up to 4 persons. The restaurant uses Japanese pottery and Nambu ironware for tableware and glasses, and incorporates Japanese elements throughout the restaurant to allow customers to experience the best of Japan. 
The restaurant can be visited on any occasion, including dates, anniversaries, business entertainment, and in the private and semi-private rooms, where you can bring your children. It is a restaurant where you can rediscover the forgotten splendor of the Japan in which you live, and can also use it in your daily life.

245490.longDescription:
Nihonbashi, a neighborhood that retains traces of the Edo period, is home to the Japanese restaurant Waki Shun. Helmed by Chef Shun Miyahara, it highlights the enchantment of Japan through Japanese dishes that allow diners to explore the changing seasons with all five senses.

After graduating from university, Miyahara took an interest in the art of food presentation in Japanese cuisine and decided to pursue a career in this culinary world. He first trained at Rokkon in Nishi-Azabu. Then, in 2008, he moved to Ginza Kojyu, a popular starred Japanese restaurant. In 2011, when its branch, Ginza Okuda, opened, he was assigned to work at the counter of the new restaurant. He was then assigned to France in 2013, serving as Executive Chef at Paris Okuda for five years. After returning to Japan, he worked as Executive Chef at Ginza Okuda. Then, he opened Waki Shun in February 2023.

The reason for opening his restaurant in Nihonbashi was because Chef Miyahara, raised in and familiar with downtown Tokyo, wanted to use this ever-evolving neighborhood at the heart of Tokyo as a foothold to promote the charm of Japan through Japanese dishes. His commitment to this neighborhood is also demonstrated by using Edo Kiriko champagne glasses exclusively created by Kohei Kobayashi, the fourth-generation glass artist of Edo Kiriko Kobayashi. The restaurant’s name, Waki Shun, is a coined word combining ‘waki,’ which represents the peaceful and friendly Japan, and the chef’s given name, Shun, which is a homonym for season.

Chef Miyahara creates Japanese dishes, blending classic ingredients conceptualized, selected, and used as learned from Chef Toru Okuda at Ginza Kojyu with a striking combination of colorful ingredients found in France and a touch of Miyahara style. The prix-fixe menu consists of several courses (about 10 courses for dinner), from appetizers to desserts, but especially highlights charcoal grill dishes, which feature lean instead of marbled meat.  Guests can not only enjoy the aroma while waiting for the meat to be grilled over charcoal in front of them but also indulge in the rich flavor that bursts forth with each chew. The soup has a deep flavor, thanks to the natural water from Kiso, Nagano, which gently permeates the whole body. Last but not least, the rice course featuring playful recipes, such as inari sushi and okowa (rice steamed with seasonal ingredients), and the dessert highlighting vibrant seasonal flavors also stand out as true signatures of Waki Shun.

The dining room (with only eight counter seats) is bright and relaxing with plenty of sunlight from the windows on two sides. The beautifully presented, delicious Japanese dishes are highly recommended for various occasions, from business dinners to intimate meals with your family, friends, date, or coworkers. You can also ask for help from English- and French-speaking staff to entertain your international guests.

244535.longDescription:
＜On the list of selected restaurants in the World Gourmet Guide Tokyo for Third Consecutive Year＞

Nihonbashi is a part of Tokyo that has developed as a center of commerce and culture since Edo period times. “farsi largo!” is located in the heart of Nihonbashi, right by the Coredo Muromachi commercial complex. The owner-chef, Hidenaga Tsuji traveled to Italy after 5 years training in restaurants in Tokyo. There, he studied authentic north Italian cuisine in restaurants such as ""La Contea,"" a province in Piedmont, north-west Italy that boasts white truffles as its specialty product; ""Albergo Ristorante Verbano,"" which specializes in dishes made from fish caught in Lake Maggiore; and the world gourmet guide awarded restaurant ""Da Vittorio"" in Lombardy. After returning to Japan, Chef Tsuji further developed his skills by working in Italian restaurants in Tokyo. The winner of awards such as the Italian Food Championship on the TV Tokyo program TV Champion and the Grand Prix Cooking Award, Dolce division, Italian Chamber of Commerce Japan, he has a dazzling CV. In 2010, he went independent and opened ""farsi largo!"" which saw a refurbishment and re-opening in 2018.

Chef Tsuji feels it is important for his customers to enjoy pairing wines with authentic northern Italian cuisine, food that offers the chance to enjoy seasonality with all the five senses. He devotes himself to the selection of his ingredients. He is especially particular about seafood and vegetables and receives direct deliveries of fresh seafood caught in Suruga Bay from a long-established fishmonger in Yaizu and organic Italian vegetables from a farm in Chiba. The Italian regional cuisine that he creates from these ingredients carries on the traditions of a flavor that would make even Italian customers nicely contented.

The interior of “farsi largo!” features a modern mood with European-style white walls and is unified to create a warm space with wooden chairs tables and wooden tables that were handcrafted by an artist. Both lunch and dinner are limited to 3 to 4 groups of customers, and the restaurant can also be rented out for dinners and business entertainment. It is also suitable for casual meals by groups of female customers. “farsi largo!” means to “clear the way on your own,” so it is also a spot that we would recommend for celebrating a new beginning with that someone special.

244557.longDescription:
Nihonbashi Kabuto-cho is an area 4-minute walk from Nihonbashi Station. Take a stroll down the quiet road leading to the Tokyo Stock Exchange and you will come across ""Asahina Gastornome,"" a restaurant that is attracting the attention of gourmets around the world. This restaurant serves gastronomy by Mr. Satoru Asahina, a favored disciple of Joël Robuchon and the former head chef of ""La Table de Joël Robuchon,"" a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Ebisu. Here, customers are treated to traditional French cuisine with a pinch of modern esprit and carefully selected high-quality wine. 

The late Joël Robuchon, who was named Chef of the Century, was the most starred chef in the world. His disciple Mr. Asahina's illustrious career began when he joined ""L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon"" as deputy head chef in 2004. Within the year, he was promoted to head chef at ""Le Cafe de Joël Robuchon"". In 2007, he traveled to France to study at SAS Ecole Maître Crêpier – Ecoles Treblec in Rennes, Brittany. After graduation, he polished his skills at La Saint Georges, a restaurant specializing in galette and crepes, two foods said to have originated in the Brittany region. After returning to Japan, he supervised two restaurants: ""Le Cafe de Joël Robuchon"" and ""Boutique du Joël Robuchon"". Then, in 2011, he became head chef at ""La Table de Joël Robuchon,"" a world gourmet guide award restaurant. For 7 years, he maintained those 2 stars, demonstrating his astounding culinary skills. In 2016, he was appointed Chairman of Avance no Kai, an association of French culinary contest winners. In 2017, he decided to leave the Robuchon Group, where he had worked for 13 years, and in 2018, he opened ""Asahina Gastornome,"" a restaurant in his own name.

His favorite phrases are Isshoku-Nyukon (""Pouring one's soul into a single meal"") and Issekigan (""A discerning eye""). Chef Asahina makes good use of his discerning eye for people and food as he engages with customers. The concept of his restaurant is based on two keywords: people and food. He explains, ""People refers to taking into account the historical background of food culture to develop a refined taste for the pleasure of dining and to help one's fellow man through food. Food refers to deepening one's understanding of the classics while pursuing modern cuisine to give shape to flashes of inspiration and to unravel the essence of French cuisine. I intend to build up ""Asahina Gastornome"" through these 2 concepts"". Finding the ideal ingredients for French cuisine is also no easy task. Chef Asahina says, ""Ingredients direct from the farm are delicious. Organic vegetables are delicious. However, French cuisine gives you even more than that."" One must imagine the final flavor and search for ingredients that can be deliciously transformed through the techniques of French cooking.

Walking down the dimly lit cobble road, it's easy to imagine that you're visiting a restaurant in Europe. From the glazed entrance doors, you can see a modern and elegant space with a keynote of white and touches of silver and platinum. The cutlery and show plates are by Marcel Wanders, an international art director, and the chandelier is by Moooi, a Dutch interior brand. Designed under the theme of ""not too modern, not too classic"", great attention was paid to the fine details of the interior, making for a stylish yet comfortable space that further enhances the mood of the gourmets who love Chef Asahina's cooking. This is a restaurant where you can have a wonderful time with someone special, savoring world-class cuisine and lavish hospitality in perfect comfort.

※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

甘鯛の鱗焼きが鱗はカリカリなのに身はしっとりしていてすばらしい焼き加減で特に好きでした。
お店の雰囲気、接客、食器、そして料理、全てが素敵でした。ひとつひとつの料理が丁寧で繊細な味で、料理に合わせた食器がさらに料理の味を引き出しているように感じました。また利用させていただきます。ありがとうございました。
サービス、料理共に素晴らしい

扉で外と中を完全に分けていて、扉を開けた瞬間に別世界が広がっていました。
料理はどれもすごく美味しく、盛り付け方も綺麗で運ばれてきた瞬間にワクワクするような料理でした。

サービスも素晴らしく、説明や提案などを気さくに応えていただき、充実した時間を過ごすことができました。
どの料理も洗練されていて非常に美味しかったです。特にデザートのブュッシュ・ド・ノエルが絶品でした。
スタッフ方々のサービス、会話に楽しい時間を過ごせました。

Food was amazing and service was exceptional.

料理の見栄え、味はもちろんのこと、お店やスタッフさんの感じの良さやサービス全てにおいて大満足でした。是非また伺いたいと思います。

友人と共に訪問致しました。レセプションを通り入り口に入った瞬間から清潔感のあるスタイリッシュな空間に圧倒されました。一品目から目にも美しい料理の数々で、連れてきた友人も非常に喜んでおりました。また、ベーシックなフレンチにとどまらず、遊び心のある洗練された一皿一皿に非常に感銘を受けました。サービスの方たちも非常に安定感があり、緊張しすぎずリラックスしながら素晴らしい時間を過ごす事ができました。大切な人を連れていきたくなるレストランがまた増えました。ありがとうございました。

244441.longDescription:
Nihonbashi, Tokyo—a place that has thrived as a castle town from the Edo period, and still to this day has trails from those days here and there. “Sushi Kimura” opened in 2018, in a popular area with a lot of atmospheres. 4 minutes on foot from the Tokyo Metro Suitengumae Station, it quietly lies on a street turned off from the main road.

The owner-chef, Mr. Koji Kimura became independent and opened his restaurant in Nihonbashi after working in a sushi restaurant in New York for 10 years, and practicing under a well-known sushi restaurant in Tokyo. The seafood is direct from the Aomori prefecture, where Mr. Kimura’s hometown belongs to. Being able to enjoy the freshest fish is a rare find in Tokyo. The delicately flavored vinegared rice made from salt, red vinegar made from fermented sake lees, and Koshihikari rice from the Yamagata prefecture, bring out the flavors of the finest sushi toppings. Mr. Kimura’s competent skills backed with his thoroughness, are steadily raising the restaurant’s popularity amongst sushi lovers in Tokyo. The teacups and sake vessels are all fine pieces ordered from directly visiting vessel craftsmen in Kyushu, and play a role in bringing out the flavors of the food and creating the restaurant’s soft atmosphere. Around 8 different types of Japanese sake, that pair perfectly with sushi, are always available, including a couple of seasonal ones.

Starting with the counter made of a single plate of pure white cedar, the interior that is simply put together using a lot of wood creates a calm atmosphere for guests to enjoy their exquisite meal. 9 counter seats are offered for those who wish to enjoy Mr. Kimura’s sushi making right in front of their eyes. Mr. Kimura who has a lot of experience overseas is proficient in English and can explain about the fish to guests from abroad. “I am aiming for a restaurant in which guests say that they can confidently bring along important people,” he remarks, and at his hands, there is no doubt “Sushi Kimura” will be a perfect choice for receptions, anniversaries, and important dinners with clients. We would like you to enjoy an exquisite moment created by a location and atmosphere that allows you to feel Japan’s air and culture, and an owner who also has international experience from New York.


■ This restaurant is Not the branch of Sushi Kimura in Tamagawa, Setagaya District.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Suitengumae Station, Exit 8(Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line)

recommendations.comment: Food was amazing. Chef care about every detail and preparation were sometimes innovative and delicious. Service was superb. It is a 10/10 experience.

This was my first time trying omakase, and it completely exceeded my expectations. The whole experience felt personal and intimate — especially being in Japan, where the tradition runs deep. The staff was incredibly kind and welcoming, which helped ease some of my nervousness as a first-timer.

Watching chef Kimura and his team work right in front of me was absolutely mesmerizing. The precision, care, and artistry that goes into every single piece is something you don’t fully grasp until you see it up close. At first, it felt a little overwhelming having chef Kimura watch me eat — I wasn’t sure if I was doing it “right” — but I quickly realized it didn’t matter. What mattered was enjoying the food, and chef Kimura and his team seemed genuinely happy to see that.

The dishes were phenomenal. I discovered flavors, textures, and ingredients I never imagined I’d enjoy. Every bite was a surprise in the best way. It wasn’t just a meal — it was an experience I’ll never forget.
Perfect as Always, Katadjikenai
料理の出てくるタイミングが非常に良い。良いお酒を飲める。
The experience was fantastic, the meal was excellent. I'd highly recommend this place for anyone who would like to try eating at a sushi master.

Thank you to the chef and the whole team at Sushi Kimura. This was the best sushi experience we had on our trip to Japan. The quality was fresh, the course fulfilling, and most of all - a very innovative and interesting take on the cuisine. It was a pleasure to be welcomed to your restaurant, and we would be happy to return if we visit in the future.
Perfect as always, Katadjikenai

一品一品の仕事が丁寧でとても美味しかったです。
暑かったので錫製の徳利とお猪口でいただいた冷酒が喉に心地よかった。

鰮の巻物や車海老の頭の焼物、甘海老のづけの握りや鰹のづけには辛子など面白いものまで、
どれも美味しかった。
またお伺いしたいです。
接客も心地よく、それぞれにしっかり手が込まれたお料理を大変美味しく頂きました。
丁寧に仕込まれたお鮨のネタと大将のお人柄、素早く黙々と下準備をされていた助手の方、とても良い時間を過ごさせて頂きました。また伺いたいと思います。ありがとうございました。
我々には量が丁度よく、店員の方も丁寧なご対応を頂きました。もちろん味についてはこの上なしでした。工夫により酸味を抑え、旨味を引き出し、生臭さが少ないというポイントで好みの味でございました。様々なお寿司屋さんにて会食をさせていただいておりますが、立地も東京駅からほど近く、味も当然のこと、またお伺いしたいと家内と共に話しておりました。美味しいお寿司をありがとうございました。
食事、雰囲気、おもてなしなどすべてが素晴らしく、感動を覚える時間を過ごすことができました。東京に来る時は再訪したい、接待でも勝負でも使えるお店です。
大将の人柄と気配りが素晴らしかったです。

味よし。
店主の人柄よし。
値段よし。

また行きます。

First visit.

Otsumami: The awabi (abalone) was simmered till meltingly tender. Squid lovers will be delighted with the Hotaru Ika (firefly squid) which was bursting with roe. The Aji rolled with sesame, shiso and ginger was my favourite. 

Sushi: Special mention must be given to Chef Kimura's shari. The temperature and acidity were absolutely on point for every single piece of nigiri. The rice has a more intense flavour and it greatly enhanced the sushi course as a whole.

Kinmedai, Kohada, Maguro-zuke, Chutoro, Anago and his Uni were the standout pieces. The uni was superbly smooth, clean and creamy that I requested for a 2nd piece as the closing for my omakase.

Not cheap, but definitely a wonderful experience with top-notch ingredients meticulously handled by a stellar chef, with warm hospitality from the service staff and fitting amenities.

Worth a visit.

2回目ですが、前回と同じように大満足してます。
また伺います。
二度目の訪問です。つまみの品々に感心しました。ねっとりとしたタコ煮の柔らかさは絶品です。冬の季節、香箱ガニも贅沢でした。鯖は苦手ですが、こちらのお店のミョウガとガリを合わせた海苔巻きは食べやすく好きになりました。今回は満席でしたが、最後までタイミングよく握りを出していただけました。また、訪問したいと思います。

清潔感溢れる店内で、扉を開けた瞬間から期待が高まりました。つまみ、握りともやさしい味わいで、すべてが美味しかったです。特に、車海老の握りと頭の部分の塩焼きは絶品でした。心地良い時間が過ごせるお店で、また訪問したいと思います。

強いて言えば帆立の磯辺焼きができましたが、しっかり焼いていたのには理由があったのでしょうか？
個人的には生でも食べれる岩手産の大きな帆立は半生で食べるのが好みなのですが、硬くて勿体無い感がありました。
まああくまでも私の好みの問題なので、お肉の焼き方の好みと同じなのかもしれません。
また、お伺いしたいと思いました。
ご馳走さまでした。

245431.longDescription:
Located in a narrow back alley leading from Suitengu Shrine in Nihonbashi Kakigara-cho, Takagaki No Sushi is a home-turned-restaurant infused with Taisho-era romance. Helmed by Chef Nobuhide Takagaki, the restaurant has inherited the culture of Edomae sushi.


Chef Takagaki likes the ocean and fish and has been amused himself with fishing since childhood. He became a fisherman at the age of 16, grappling squarely with fish. When he was 19, he was inspired to become a sushi chef by a TV documentary that featured sushi chefs as earnest creators. He started working at a sushi restaurant in his hometown of Fukuoka, but eventually went to Tokyo to work first at a sushi restaurant in Ginza and then at Shimbashi Shimizu, where he learned the traditional art of Edomae sushi for four and a half years before he could walk unaided. In 2018, he opened a restaurant named after him, Takagaki No Sushi. The Edomae sushi he learned from his master captivated the taste buds of sushi connoisseurs, making his restaurant an instant hit and awarding it with one star.


Chef Takagaki tackles sushi every day, saying “I try to create the most delicious sushi without any compromise.” The ingredients are sourced from Toyosu Market through reliable, specialized brokers, including a popular tuna broker “Ishiji” as well as prawn, shellfish, small fish, and fruit brokers. Takagaki No Sushi offers prix-fixe meals consisting of five dishes of delicacies, 10 pieces of nigiri sushi (featuring different ingredients depending on the day), a bowl of soup, some sushi rolls, and Japanese-style egg omelets. The sushi rice is made of different brands of rice blended by Chef Takagaki, cooked in a broad-brimmed cooking pot, and seasoned with two varieties of red vinegar. Prepared in a timely manner for the arrival of guests, it is served at a lukewarm temperature. All the ingredients, from sushi rice and toppings to wasabi, soy sauce, and other seasonings, are well balanced and prepared “with full attention to ensure that the sushi will not cause any discomfort or harm as it progresses from the mouth to the stomach” as stated by the chef.


The ark shell sushi is recognized by sushi connoisseurs as the signature of Takagaki No Sushi. Its delicious flavor is enhanced by its combination with the sushi rice of Takagaki and the soy sauce made by a soy sauce maker established in 1830. In addition to the shellfish, Takagaki No Sushi is proud to offer richly flavored medium fatty and fatty tuna that are selected with care and prepared to perfection. Moreover, six to eight varieties of seasonal Japanese sake selected by Chef Takagaki are kept in stock at the restaurant, while it features only pure natural wines from France that have been his favorites for years.


The impressive, solid wood countertop (seating up to six guests) is designed by Yuki Sakaguchi, a founder of a solid wood table manufacturer called WONDERWOOD Inc. The raised serving platform on the far end of the counter is made of the heartwood of the highest-grade precious Kiso Hinoki cypress cut down by one of the few Japanese loggers and planed by a professional planer. “The carefully selected Kiso Hinoki cypress is another essence of the culture of sushi we have inherited” said Chef Takagaki, who faithfully observes each guest sitting at the six-seater counter and offers sushi with toppings, sushi rice, and soy sauce in a balanced combination depending on the guest. Visit Takagaki No Sushi, either for private or business dining,

and indulge your taste buds with the very best authentic Edomae sushi.
nearestStations: Suitengumae Station, Ningyocho Station

244968.longDescription:
An authentic Italian restaurant found on the 38th floor of the five-star Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, K’shiki is steeped in Japanese tradition and elegance. The restaurant is just 8 minutes from Tokyo Station and is directly connected to the underground passage of Tokyo Metro Mitsukoshimae Station; the Nihonbashi area also offers easy access to Tokyo's famous sightseeing spots such as the Imperial Palace East Garden.

The restaurant’s clientele is well-traveled, with many hailing from overseas. To accommodate this, the restaurant offers more than 800 kinds of wine from all over the world (including New World, South Africa, Oceania and the United States). Oenophiles should not miss out on the 3-Glass Wine Set pairing that matches elegant pours to the classic Italian menu. 

Offering all-day dining, K’shiki can seat up to 60 guests in a dramatic space while offering a panoramic view of Tokyo, the mountains of Hakone and superb views of Mount Fuji. Guests can enjoy traditional dishes made with carefully selected ingredients for entertainment, dates, anniversaries and elegant dinners with family.

Casual gastronomy ""La Bonne Table "" inside COREDO Muromachi 2, Nihonbashi, just next to Mitsukoshimae Station on Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. A literal translation is ""a beautiful dining table."" A new business model of ""L'Effervescence"" which has been selected as world gourmet guide award and ranked 16th on the ""Asia Best restaurants"". Proposing entertaining modern French  prefix course. You can also enjoy natural wine and non alcoholic pairing there.

Inside the restaurant that made the best use of the wide space, there is table and sofa seating that are recommended for casual dating, and there is a chef table for up to 10 people right in front of the open kitchen. It is also recommended for wine party and lunch dining. Guests overseas will be pleased because of the offer of English menu and also service in English. A sophisticated atmosphere with a sense of presence is familiar to Nihonbashi.

243879.longDescription:
""La Paix"", a world gourmet guide award modern French restaurant in Nihonbashi Muromachi, Tokyo, means ""Peace"" in French. It is a  restaurant where guests are welcomed and taken care with warm ""heart"", following the five philosophies of Japan, harmony, mind, connection and five senses.

Owner chef Mr.Ippei Matsumoto used to be a chef at ""Au gout du jour Nouvelle Ere"" in Tokyo and opened ""La Paix"" afterwards. He focus on the traditional French cuisine with modern ingredients in Japan to make the best dishes, which you could taste and experience the four seasons. The must-try specailty ""Nihonbashi Foie gras Gaufre"", a can wrapped by furoshiki (Japanese square cloth), where a Gaufre and foie gras sandwich is inside the can. It is a splendid combination of the tradition of Japan and France.

As for the interior, there are only 20 table-seats and 2 semi-private rooms with a stylish space incorporating Japanese elements. It is also suitable for family gathering, business-use and dates. It is recommended for overseas guests because it is close to Tokyo station and vegetarian menu is also available (upon advance request).

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Exit A1 of Mitsukoshimae Station on Tokyo Metro Ginza Line

245046.longDescription:
An eight-minute walk from Tokyo Station brings guests to Oriental Lounge, located on the 38th floor of the Mandarin Oriental, a five-star luxury hotel in the busy shopping and entertainment district of Nihombashi.

The legendary afternoon tea served at Oriental Lounge is highly regarded not only in Japan but also around the globe, attracting many tea lovers. The tea is served with a three-tiered cake stand, adorned with a selection of seasonal savories, scones, and petite fours. Carefully prepared one by one, each delightful piece tempts guests’ taste buds even before the first bite. Scones are served warm, straight from the oven on a separate plate, which can be topped up on request. These delicacies and sweets are paired with unlimited cups of different teas so that guests can enjoy an idyllic tea time to their heart’s content.
The Oriental Lounge also offers snacks and drinks day and night for any occasion. The lounge also keeps some 6,000 wine bottles available at any time, offering a wide selection of over 800 varieties. As well as bottles from Japan, the wine list also offers bottles from the Old World, including France, plus New World wines to satisfy the preferences of international travelers.

The lounge, seating up to 54 guests, boasts dramatic floor-to-ceiling glass windows overlooking Tokyo’s vibrant cityscapes. Filled with sunlight by day and lit with reflected neon lights at night, the lounge offers a memorable and romantic setting.

The team at Oriental Lounge invites guests to enjoy an unforgettable experience in an elegant setting at Oriental Lounge, with friends or a  partner, for an indulgent solo excursion, or a relaxed business meeting.
nearestStations: Directly connected to the A7 and A8 exits of Mitsukoshimae Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line and Hanzomon Line

245090.longDescription:
An 8-minute drive from JR Tokyo Station, direct connection to Tokyo Metro Mitsukoshimae Station. On the 38th floor of Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, a five-star hotel that stands as a landmark in the Nihonbashi district of Tokyo, where the style and history of the Edo period still lives on, there is a pizzeria with just eight counter seats. The same 38th floor is home to an authentic Italian restaurant called K'shiki where you can tell them the name and they will guide to the pizza bar in the rear. A spectacular view of the city center unfolds, and in front of the L-shaped, glossy marble-topped counter is a cooking area with marble walls. Behind that sits a formidable pizza oven.

The Pizza Bar ON 38TH is led by Executive Chef Daniele Cason. The pizza dough crafted by the Rome native is made with Italian organic flour using just one gram of yeast and 80% water for a slow and gentle 48-hour fermentation to create a light and digestible crust. The specialty is "Truffle Scented Mascarpone Cheese Pizzino". It's a light, bite-sized pizza topped with truffles. Another is the classic "Bufala", a simple but very popular pizza based on from Buffalo mozzarella.  The light texture is the gift of Chef Cason's dough.
For drinks, there is always a selection of over 6,000 bottles of 800 kinds of wines from around the world on hand, including domestic labels. In addition to bottles, there are also sets that include three recommended wines by the glass, so you can enjoy them in a variety of styles. They also have a non-alcoholic wine set prepared by a sommelier.
As a noble dining set in a high-rise hotel, an attraction of The Pizza Bar ON 38TH is the live theater of the master pizzaiolo baking in front of you. The quality of the pizza is also endorsed by Italy, and the restaurant has been awarded three slices in the 2020 edition of the "Top Italian Restaurants", a digital guide for rating Italian restaurants around the world by Gambero Rosso.

Dining with a spectacular view from eight counter seats. Perfect for a date, dinner with friends, or even a gathering of foodies. Your time at The Pizza Bar ON 38TH is sure to be unforgettable.

SENSE Cantonese Dining is an eight-minute drive from JR Tokyo Station and also accessible directly from Tokyo Metro Mitsukoshi-mae Station. Perched on the 37th floor of the Mandarin Oriental in Nihombashi, the cultural and economic center of Tokyo, the restaurant commands dynamic views of the city’s stunning skyline and Tokyo Skytree.

This restaurant offers traditional Cantonese cuisine featuring immaculate ingredients from around the world. Given the exquisite quality of the produce, dishes such as Okinawa star grouper, abalone, and fresh Chinese vegetables offer modern and delicate flavors. Some dishes, such as a platter of Assorted Cantonese Barbeque (consisting of the holy trinity of traditional Hong Kong-style pork delicacies) or Barbecued Kyoto Duck Skin Rolls, are carved tableside for added theatre. 

SENSE Cantonese Dining also keeps some 6,000 bottles available at any time, offering a vast selection of over 800 different kinds of wines, not only from Japan but also from the New World, South Africa, Oceania, the U.S., and other corners of the world, to satisfy the thirst of international travelers. Prestige wine options are also available by the glass. In addition, a wide variety of Chinese tea and Shaoxing wines, including 50-year old Guyue and Longshan, are available.

The restaurant has the ability to accommodate up to 70 guests. Two private rooms with eight seats each can be converted into a single large dining room with 18 seats. As an added plus, the restaurant’s  sophisticated hotel dining service makes it the perfect place to entertain business clients, celebrate anniversaries, and enjoy intimate meals with one’s family and children. The restaurant also offers multilingual services for international guests.

244782.longDescription:
8 minutes by car from JR Tokyo Station, directly connected to Tokyo Metro Mitsukoshimae Station, "Mandarin Oriental Tokyo" is a 5-star luxury hotel located in Nihonbashi, the cultural and economic center of Tokyo. The main dining “SIGNATURE” is located on the 37th floor. It is impressive to see the superb view of Tokyo spread out in front of you when you go up the elevator.

The cuisine is traditional French cuisine, based on the techniques and recipes handed down from generation to generation, with respect for the great classics in the history of French cuisine, and the sensitivity of a chef from Paris. The chef's strong desire is to provide a memorable experience of authentic French cuisine with comfortable service.

There are over 800 kinds of wine and around 6,000 bottles available at any time. The wine is not only from France, but also from all over the world, such as Japan, South Africa, Oceania and America. There are 3 types of wine pairings with 3 to 5 glasses, and non-alcoholic drinks can be served from the Mandarin Bar if you want a cocktail.


There is a main dining room and 1 private room (5 to 10 people). The semi-private space with one side by the window has a private feel and is popular as you can enjoy the view of Tokyo. Soft light pours in during the day and the city skyline shimmers at night. The elegant and modern interior, divided by silver partitions, adds to the gastronomic experience. There are many foreign guests, and English menus and services are available. We hope you will enjoy an unforgettable time at “SIGNATURE” with the beautiful night and day scenery of Tokyo.

244735.longDescription:
“Sushi Shin by Miyakawa” is an Edomae and Ezomae sushi restaurant, located on the 38th floor of the “Mandarin Oriental Tokyo” in Nihonbashi.

This sushi restaurant incorporates the styles of both Edomae and Ezomae, under the supervision of Masaaki Miyakawa, of the three-star “Sushi Miyakawa” restaurant in Hokkaido. You can see the Tokyo Skytree from the large window and enjoy Edomae sushi whilst taking in this superb view.  

Tetsuya Uno is in charge of “Sushi Shin by Miyakawa”. He is a veteran sushi chef with more than 20 years of experience. The seafood used at the restaurant is purchased from markets in Hokkaido and Toyosu in Tokyo. The combination of Edomae-style methods, such as maturing the fish to bring out the flavor, and the Ezomae-style of Hokkaido that uses fresh seafood, make the courses very well-balanced. The vinegared rice is a blend of red vinegar and "Tsukiakari", a new breed of rice from Niigata. For dinner, the Omakase Course consists of 5 appetizers and 10 pieces of nigiri sushi. About 30 kinds of sake, mainly from Hokkaido, Tokyo and Tohoku region, are available, as well as 30 ~ 40 varieties of wine and champagne.

The interior has been decorated with splendid Japanese craftsmanship, including an eye-catching 350 year old cypress counter. The kumikozaiku near the entrance is made by Nobuo Tanihata, a renowned master who specializes in this woodworking technique that is over 1,300 years old. The wall behind the counter is designed by Shuhei Hasado, a master of "tsuichi-kabe" clay craftsmanship .  Please enjoy the atmosphere, hospitality and taste of Edomae sushi from “Sushi Shin by Miyakawa”, with friends, for dates, business gatherings, and entertaining overseas guests.

*Notes*
If you have any allergies or food preferences, please let us know in advance.
Please note that if you let us know on the day, it will not be possible to change the menu as we will not have been able to prepare any alternative ingredients.

245045.longDescription:
Perched on the 38th floor of the five-star Mandarin Oriental hotel in Nihombashi, Tokyo, this modern Spanish restaurant was renowned for receiving a star for six consecutive years. As a pioneer in molecular gastronomy, comparable to El Bulli in Spain, TAPAS MOLECULAR BAR has produced many famous chefs and attracts gourmands for its eye and palate-pleasing gastronomic entertainment that features dazzling use of liquid nitrogen and espuma.

The restaurant can be on the 38th floor via the Oriental Lounge. At the end of the lounge stands a counter with eight seats where guests can enjoy watching the chef performing feats of molecular gastronomy in an open kitchen. The food is artfully served in tapas portions, amounting to almost 20 unique dishes, and enjoyed over two hours. Each dish confounds and astounds, with a dazzling variety of colors, flavors, textures, and aromas that stimulate all five senses.

The wine list consists of more than 800 labels and 6,000 bottles, not only from Japan but also from around the world –– both the Old World including France, and the New World including South Africa and the U.S.

The moodily lit bar is the perfect spot to enjoy food and conversation and share an extraordinary dining experience with a partner, friends, or business clients.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2022

243923.longDescription:
This long-standing restaurant that was founded in 1912 on the site of a famous kabuki theater, Genyadana.

The restaurant allows guests to get a taste of the changing seasons, with the strictly selected seasonal ingredients that arrive every morning, in private rooms looking out on a beautiful garden which color change throughout the year. 

Perhaps the most outstanding characteristic of the establishment is the building's "sukiya" style of architecture, a method of construction that is rarely seen these days involving building multiple floors without use of a single nail. Guests can enjoy the constantly changing scenery of the garden and the quintessentially Japanese building, which are perfect for important business meals and other formal get-togethers.

244697.longDescription:
Ningyocho is located in the center of Tokyo, yet it retains the atmosphere of downtown Tokyo. There are many long-established restaurants in this area, and Kawada opened its door in February 2019. The gentle owner, Haruji Kanata, went independent after 13 years of experience at the famous Japanese restaurant Iyuki.

There are only 6 counter seats. With the desire to provide meticulous services such as serving dishes to each guest with a short distance and preparing the food in front of the guest, this kappo restaurant is in counter-style.

The signature dish is the claypot pot rice served at the end of the seasonal omakase course. It is cooked with the utmost care so that it can be served in the most delicious and hot state. It is served as "takikomi gohan (mixed rice)" or "dried baby sardines with sansho pepper".

The alcohol collection is carefully selected with sake and wine that doesn't interfere with the taste of the food. It is an orthodox Japanese restaurant filled with humble attitude, continuous passion for cooking, and consideration for guests.

243651.longDescription:
Located in Ningyo-cho, in a back alley on Amazake Yokocho, this two-story restaurant devoted to Japanese cuisine was established in 1955. The ground floor features a cypress counter seats and table seating while the top floor is fully set up with table seats and private rooms. The tables for up to 7 diners each offer views of the greenery, allowing guests to enjoy the ambiance, while the private rooms, which accommodate 4 guests max, offer complete privacy.

Selected at the market each day, we bring together a range of in-season ingredients. This allows a glimpse into the spirit of craftsmanship and sincere attitude of the proprietor towards food. With deliberately simple preparation, the dishes that are created bring out the umami flavor of their ingredients to their fullest. From the first mouthful, guests will enjoy both rich flavors and the sense of seasons.
 
Ingredients include but not limited to: Sakura sea bream and Kyoto bamboo shoots in spring; conger pike, wild ayu, and wild eel in summer; matsutake mushrooms and tilefish in autumn; and wild pufferfish, Matsuba crab, soft-shelled turtle, and mallard duck in winter. In a subdued, calm, and harmonious atmosphere, guests can quietly enjoy the mood of the four seasons.
                                     
We offer pleasant service that maintains a proper and reasonable sense of distance, which is perfect for business reception. The proprietress’s friendly, shitamachi Tokyo-style manner with guests embellishes and adds life to the dignified space. You will find us comfortable and convenient even if it's your first visit to us for business reception.
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Ningyocho Station (Exit A1), Hibiya Line
