244340.longDescription: Nihonbashi Sonoji is a world gourmet guide award tempura restaurant which opened in October 2016 after relocating from Shizuoka to Nihonbashi, Ningyōchō, where many popular restaurants are also located. Based on the concept of combining tempura with soba, it is a popular setting for customers to not only enjoy the carefully chosen vegetables and fish tempuras, but also flavor delicious soba noodles in a place where guests and chefs frequently visit from all over the country. The owner, Toshiyuki Suzuki, is the eldest son in a family which owns a soba restaurant called Hosojimaya, in Shimada, Shizuoka Prefecture. After graduating from culinary school, he worked at his family's for 7 years. He then trained at the Japanese restaurant Kakinoki for 2 years, and finally in 2000 he opened Nihonbashi Sonoji. After experiencing for the first time the taste of tempura from the restaurant Mikawa Zezankyo, which is run by the legendary tempura chef Tetsuya Saotome, he wanted to create a restaurant which provides soba with tempuras, and wanted to become a popular restaurant among local customers. Then, with the idea of ""wanting people in Tokyo to also be able to taste the finest vegetables and seafood tempuras which he had been handling in Shizuoka"", he relocated his restaurant to Nihonbashi, Tokyo. The tempura uses venison and ""tendane"", along with Shizuoka's vegetables and mushrooms, and seafood from Suruga Bay. Shizuoka vegetables are hard to find in Tokyo, for example Shizuoka carrots and tamatori mushrooms, which has an abalone-like texture when exposed to heat. Taking advantage of his prior work experience, Ni-hachi soba noodles are also included on the menu, and are handmaded using buckwheat flour from Mashiko and Kawane. The sake is sourced strictly from the Omuraya brewing in his hometown, Shimada. For each season, the restaurant prepares 3-4 kinds of Japanese sake which cannot be easily found in Tokyo, such as Onna Nakase and Jyuubei sake. The dignified interior has an 8 seat counter made from Japanese cypress wood. Compared to other high-class tempura restaurants in Tokyo, customers can enjoy tempura at a reasonable price. This restaurant can also be held for a wide range of events, such as meals with colleagues, entertaining, and anniversaries. This is an exquisite tempura restaurant where customers can enjoy the allure of Shizuoka ingredients in Tokyo. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age or children who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible and we will be happy to assist as needed. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Please inquire in advance. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English on some days. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? We do not have a dress code.

243734.longDescription:
Ningyocho is crowded with shops of various genres, from old shops to new shops. It is truly a new town. In late summer 2022, Oryori Kokoroba, a small kaiseki restaurant run by the owner and the proprietress, opened in a corner of the quaint city.

The idea behind the name of the store, Oryori Kokoroba, is to express the owner's sincerity towards the customers by taking one character from his name and to combine the meanings of Kokoroba, which is the proprietress's favorite word from the Heian period.
While there are many restaurants, I can't express how grateful I am to the customers who come all the way here. That's what Kokoroba is all about.
The owner carefully uses the best ingredients of the day, and serves carefully prepared "food" that looks like a leaf of the heart. It is a place for adults to heal their daily fatigue and lead them to a new strength by spending a rich time.

In the soft yet dignified space of the tea room, there are seven chairs made of carefully designed horseback saddle made of deer colored leather on the Kiso hinoki counter. While enjoying the comfort of the seat, the owner brings his friends and guests with him to taste each and every dish. Also, you should visit Ningyocho in search of new discoveries when you spend time alone and forget everything.

245078.longDescription:
Sukiyaki Kappo Hiyama, found on the second floor of a century-old Japanese-style house located a two-minute walk from Ningyocho Station, is an established restaurant that has been patronized for years by connoisseurs seeking authentic sukiyaki (Japanese beef hot pot). 

Opened in 1935, following the opening of the butcher’s shop in 1912, the restaurant offers the finest beef of the day via discriminating buyers who select meat based not on its grade, brand, or place of origin, but on its essential value. In particular, the specialty dish, sukiyaki, features high-quality Kuroge Wagyu beef, including prized Yonezawa beef as a tribute to the last president’s winning of the first auction of the year at the Tokyo Meat Market. This premium beef is seasoned with homemade sauce, together with matching Edo Yasai vegetables, locally produced ingredients like Ningyocho tofu, and seasonal flavors such as matsutake mushrooms in autumn.

Sukiyaki Kappo Hiyama offers four different prix-fixe options: sukiyaki, oil-fried beef, shabushabu, and beef steak. The drinks menu offers nearly 30 wines, imported from across the world, including Italy, France, and the US, and a carefully curated selection of Japanese sake, such as Kakurei from Aoki Shuzo in Niigata and Hiyama’s collaboration sake, as well as a variety of non-alcoholic beverages such as Setoka, a pure fruit juice from Ehime.

Sukiyaki Kappo Hiyama accommodates guests in private dining rooms only. The flower arrangements and hanging scrolls in the alcoves of these Japanese-style rooms add a touch of elegance that matches the historic building. Each room is furnished with a low table, which can also be replaced by a standard dining table upon request. In addition, each dining room is served by a dedicated waiter or waitress allowing diners to relax and enjoy their meals. 

Thus, Sukiyaki Kappo Hiyama is the perfect place to dine with a partner, family, friends, or colleagues. Guests are invited to enjoy high-quality Wagyu beef cooked to their preferred style.

244752.longDescription:
“Sushi Kakizaki” is located 2 minutes walk from Ningyocho Station in Nihonbashi, an area of the city with a downtown atmosphere. Owner Yuhei Kakizaki, who loves this calm town, focuses on natural Japanese ingredients to make his Edomae sushi.

Owner Kakizaki has studied at many sushi restaurants, including the long-established “Ginza Kyubei”, the sushi section of the Japanese restaurant “Nadaman”, and “Roku Roku” in the Grand Hyatt. He became independent and opened “Sushi Kakizaki” in 2008. At this restaurant, they are particular about using natural Japanese ingredients which are selected by owner Kakizaki himself from Toyosu market, where the best produce from all over Japan can be found. 

The dishes on the menu that go well with alcohol, such as “Salt-grilled cutlass fish” and “Tender simmered octopus”, are popular, as well as the side dishes that can be enjoyed between sushi dishes. Their vinegared sushi rice is made from large grains of less sticky rice, which is cooked hard so that when it is placed in the mouth, it feels like it is crumbling. Their rice vinegar is finished with salt only, without adding any sugar. They have 4 types of dry Japanese sake, which have been carefully selected by owner Kakizaki. He chooses only sake that is unscented and compliments, but does not interfere with, the taste of the sushi. Shochu, champagne or white wine are also available.

The exterior of the restaurant is plastered in the same style as the outer walls, giving it a sense of unity. Inside, it features a wooden counter (8 seats), made of Japanese cypress from Yoshino, Nara Prefecture, which expresses the spirit of owner Kakizaki, and his motto, "treat people with sincerity". Surrounded by wood and plaster walls, you can relax in “Sushi Kakizaki”. You can visit for various occasions, such as special celebrations with family and friends, entertaining guests from overseas, and of course, enjoying Kakizaki-san’s delicious Edomae sushi in the stylish town of Ningyocho.
nearestStations: A 2 minute walk from Ningyocho Station, Exit A3 (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Toei Asakusa Line)

245545.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of a building in Nihonbashi Ningyocho, which retains its nostalgic charm, Sushi Kaminari is headed by Chef Daiki Araki, who is also captivated by the friendly vibe of the old neighborhood lined with long-standing establishments. Growing up seeing his parents running a sushi restaurant in Himeji, Hyogo, he set his heart on becoming a chef himself. He was apprenticed to a renowned chef, Hiroshi Saeki, at Sushi Saeki and immediately distinguished himself. After 10 years of training, he was appointed as Executive Chef at Sushi Shirogane Saeki in Sheraton Miyako Hotel Tokyo under his master’s supervision. Then, in 2024, he opened his own restaurant, Sushi Kaminari, in Nihonbashi Ningyocho.

Naming his restaurant after his parents’ restaurant, Kaminari Zushi, Chef Araki continues refining the techniques of Edomae sushi he learned from his respected master, Saeki, while upholding his father’s legacy of excellence. In fact, he learned his specialty oshizushi (pressed sushi) and the way of entertaining guests from his father, serving sushi one by one to allow guests to indulge in the delicious bites at their own pace.

The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu starts with five courses of delicacies, followed by 10 pieces of nigiri sushi, Torotaku sushi roll (featured as a specialty roll filled with top-quality fatty tuna and pickled radish), and Japanese omelet. The tuna is sourced from Ishiji, a popular tuna wholesaler at Toyosu Market, known for its process that brings out the natural flavor of the fish. The high-quality seasonal seafood sourced from various regions through Toyosu Market, as well as precious ingredients from the waters around the Kansai region through a fishmonger’s shop in the chef’s hometown of Himeji, such as octopus, sea bream, Japanese Spanish mackerel, and red sea urchin, makes the menu diverse and exciting. The sushi rice is made with slightly sweet Sasanishiki rice from Shiga and seasoned with a full-body blend of five different varieties of vinegar, including red and black vinegar, from Kisaichi Brewing in Chiba. In contrast to the classic Edomae sushi, the delicacies showcase the chef’s creativity, such as salted and fermented bonito and sea bream intestines and monkfish liver served with a French-style sauce made from the red vinegar used to season the sushi rice.

The sake list offers some 20 labels from around Japan, including Shirasagi no Shiro from the chef’s hometown of Himeji. They are all delivered in 720ml bottles to keep them fresh after they are opened. The elegant, sukiya-style (based on the tea ceremony) main dining room has an L-shaped hinoki wood counter (seating up to eight guests), topped with sushi stands and coasters made from Awaji Gawara.
Also with a private dining room (seating up to six guests), the restaurant is suitable for various occasions, from business dinners with clients from abroad to family meals, friend and colleague gatherings, date nights, and other personal events. Please enjoy exquisite sushi in a relaxed, casual atmosphere at the sushi restaurant in this historical neighborhood.
nearestStations: 3 minutes walk from Ningyocho A6 exit on the Hibiya Line

243634.longDescription:
Nihonbashi OIKAWA is a Kyoto-style kaiseki restaurant in Nihonbashi that welcomes guests with its modern atmosphere and arrangements.
The restaurant, which was renovated and reopened on 18 July 2023, offers an enjoyable dining experience with witty conversation by the friendly owner.

Nihonbashi OIKAWA offers dishes that feature both Japanese and Western with the use of hand-picked ingredients sourced from Tsukiji every morning, and fresh vegetables from Kyoto. The chef pays great attention to detail by creating a selection of dishes that are especially suited to the tastes of the guests. For example, he prepares special menu for overseas guests, including the popular "grilled black cod in Saikyo Miso" and "Kyoto beef," as well as the rice course "takikomi gohan (seasoned rice)." In addition, as can be expected of traditional Japanese course meals, matcha will be prepared at the end of the meal, also a pot of "closing steamed rice" will be offered to each group of guests.

Private rooms are available for 2-3, 2-6 and 2-8 persons and are suitable for large group dinners. With English-speaking staff, the restaurant is also recommended for inbound guests.
The restaurant is often used for important occasions such as meetings between two families, and is also an ideal space for a relaxed meal with friends or sophisticated business entertainment.
nearestStations: 1 minute walk from Nihonbashi station (D1 Exit), Tokyo Metro Ginza line

244229.longDescription:
In October 2017, in the corner of an apartment building in the quiet residential area of Kagurazaka, the "secret" restaurant SECRETO opened.
 
Chef-owner Akiyoshi Yabunaka dreamed of being a chef from childhood, influenced by his parents who worked in the food industry. He moved to France in 1999, where he worked at “Le Petit Nice", then later moved to Spain to work at “Dos Parillos” and later "El Bulli", the restaurant well known as “the most difficult reservation in the world”. After returning to Japan, he became sous-chef of “Tapas Molecular Bar” in Mandarin Oriental Tokyo before realizing his dream of opening a restaurant of his own.
 
At 19 o'clock every evening, SECRETO provides a course of creative cuisine featuring top-quality ingredients, a menu full of surprises yet also deeply rooted in the seasonality of Japan. A single course menu is featured each night, and drink pairing is included. There are 12 spacious counter seats within the shop’s signature black interior. Within this space, the chefs, staff, and customers can come together for a wonderful evening. SECRETO can be a place to come together as friends or coworkers, a place to celebrate a special birthday or anniversary, or even a delightful experience for a single diner. Let us be your own personal “secret” spot in Kagurazaka

244290.longDescription:
With the concept of "Japanese spirit with Western sensibility," the restaurant opened in Nishiazabu, Tokyo, in March 2017, using the best ingredients from various regions of Japan prepared with French cooking techniques. The restaurant offers creative and high quality cuisine in a warm space inspired by a resort in Provence, southern France.
 
After training in France, Chef Masahito Ueki, who was called the French cuisine genius, worked in several restaurants, such as Restaurant J in Omotesando and MASAA'S in Karuizawa, as executive chef. The restaurant's signatures are the original dishes made with the concept of "Japanese spirit combined with Western skill", which is using French cuisine techniques to prepare Japanese ingredients. The course composed of about 11 dishes, which used abundant ingredients from chef Ueki's hometown in Noto, Kanazawa. The dishes used the five tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami (flavor)), along with Azure Wines' excellent wine, will leave a strong impression on the guests.
 
In addition, traditional crafts and wares such as Kamachi Toho plates, Aizu lacquerware and Tsubame Sanjo wares, which are used by top chefs, are also used here, bringing a modern twist to the traditional style. 

A warm atmosphere is created in the interior of the restaurant, based on the idea of the resort area of Provence in southern France. There are also 3 private rooms, which is ideal not only for business entertainment and dates, but also for guests to bring their children. Come and enjoy delicious cuisine along with the finest wine.

243901.longDescription:
Just six minutes on foot from the Hibiya Line out of Roppongi Station, Asai Azabu is located in a residential district of Nishi-Azabu that is a stone's throw from Roppongi Hills. Head chef Asai trained at restaurants like Kyoto's Gion Maruyama and Restaurant Yonemura and goes beyond the traditional confines of Japanese cuisine to pursue exciting and creative new expressions of flavor.

Seasonal ingredients collected from Tsukiji Market and Kyoto, scrupulously selected and prepared with skills blending the essences of Italian and French cuisine. Present to you the new generation of Japanese cuisine.The combination of classical cuisine and daring new ideas makes Asai's cuisine one that excites guests' refined culinary sensibilities. The omakase course with wine pairing suggests the seasons of Japan while presenting new discoveries each time you visit.

The counter-tops, tables and private room setting, made from single pieces of Northern-European wood. This makes it the perfect place for everything from casual get-together to dates and family reunions. The staff speak English and a English menu is prepared. Vegetarian menu is also available(consult when making your booking), so guests from overseas could enjoy themselves to the fullest.

13101.longDescription:
Comptoir Missago is on Nisseki Street near the Takagicho Intersection in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo. It is a quiet area about a 15 minutes' walk from Omotesando or Hiroo station on Tokyo Metro. Based on the concept of "unpretentious good food", it is a 

Mr. Tsuchikiri, the owner chef, made use of his experience with sushi, California cuisine, French cuisine, and more when opening Comptoir Missago in 2010. Guests can sit at the counter and decide what they'd like to eat, allowing the restaurant to provide good food that doesn't follow convention. The "Raw Sea Urchin and Consomme Jelly Ensemble" is a must-try, and their game meat specialty is "Roasted Wild Duck in Salmis Sauce". The game meat is at its peak in the fall and winter, but guests can enjoy great food here year-round.

The counter is perfect for casual dates and dining alone, while the tables and semi-private room are well-suited for dinner gatherings, wine tastings, and celebrations. Reservations for message plates and dessert assortments are available. Here is the perfect place for the whole family, including children, to enjoy superlative French cuisine.
nearestStations: 15-minute walk from Hiroo Station (Exit 3), Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line

244017.longDescription:
The best local production for local consumption in the big city, evolved further from "erba da nakahigashi", the only vegetable Italian cuisine which can only be eaten here, has started in 2021. Its name is "Cusavilla". Chef Toshifumi Nakahigashi who started this restaurant has inherited the DNA of the famous restaurant "Sojiki  Nakahigashi" in Kyoto. As of March 2024, since Chef Nakahigashi has moved to Tokyo, and Chef Kanae Chochi has been appointed as the new head chef at the Cusavilla. Chef Chochi came to Kyoto in 2021 after being impressed by Cusavilla's cuisine, which explores the flavors of ingredients to the fullest. Learn from the basics under Chef Nakahigashi to learn Italian from the ground up. To bring out the character of the ingredients, she continues to visit the production areas, learning from the producers and evolving to express the natural scenery in his cuisine.

This restaurant, which has been named after vegetables since ancient times in China, offers seasonal vegetable dishes in the traditional Japanese culture of 24 sekki and 72 climates. As the name of the restaurant reads ~ Kusabira ~, it is Cusavilla even in Italian, and we aim to be a place where customers can relax their body and mind with vegetables.
Chef Chochi runs around the mountains of Tokyo every day and collects ingredients to deliver real meals of this season in Nishiazabu. For example, in March she purchase Bamboo Shoots and Wild Mountain Fish, in June she purchase Wild Ayu from Akikawa, in September she purchase Matsutake Mushrooms and White Truffles, and in November she purchase Crabs from Tsuiyama and Fresh ingredients from the producers Mr.Nakahigashi has cultivated.

The counter seats in the open kitchen where you can enjoy the chef's cooking style and light talks are the faces of the restaurant and the deluxe seats of the restaurant. In addition, there is a private room for 6 people and a semi-private room for 2 people, and it can be used in many situations such as entertaining, dating, and dining with friends you don't like. 
"Enjoy the charm of Japanese as Italian food" You will be able to experience a rare meal at this restaurant.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from Hiroo station (Exit 4), Hibiya Line

244901.longDescription:
Edomaezushi Sushi Tsu is located in a back street of Nishiazabu, an eight-minute walk from
Roppongi Station.

Since opening in 2008, this popular sushi restaurant is commonly frequented by sushi tsu, connoisseurs who dedicate themselves to the pursuit of fine sushi. 

Since 2016, Nobutoshi Takahashi has been the chef of Edomaezushi Sushi Tsu. After training at renowned Japanese restaurant Buntokuyama at the Intercontinental Tokyo Bay for 11 years, he went to Korea to work as chef for Lee Jae-yong, the third-generation vice-chairman of the Samsung Group. Training under Mr. Matsumi Morita (of Ginza restaurant Kiyota) he assumed the position of chef at Sushi Tsu when he returned to Japan. A major draw for guests, Chef Takashi’s firm craftsmanship is based on a lifetime of experience. 

Seasonal ingredients are both purchased from Toyosu Market and delivered directly from producers. The nigiri is a matured sushi that uses the traditional Edomae-style rice as the base, and the steeped seafood as the topping — the best examples balancing the sushi ingredients, vinegared rice and boiled soy sauce, impressing even the most experienced sushi connoisseurs. Tuna, a specialty, is usually allowed to mature for over two weeks before being cut for optimal tenderness, creating a sense of unity with the sushi rice. The seasonal sea urchin and conger eel are also popular. 

Sushi Tsu always offers 50 varieties of sake from across the country, regardless of the production area, selected by Takahashi himself. Wine is poured by a sommelier, and pairings are available. Non-alcoholic beer and wine is also offered.

Approaching the restaurant via the basement, an immaculate spot garden greets guests, leading to a dining room that features 12 counter seats and 3 semi-private rooms (seating 4-6 guests). With each seat offering a view of Chef Takahashi gently preparing sushi, the restaurant is ideal for everything from business occasions and entertaining to private occasions with friends and family. 

“I hope diners enjoy sushi at ease”, he says, smiling. “That’s what sushi restaurants are all about.”
nearestStations: An 8-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Exit 1c (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Toei Oedo Line)

244536.longDescription:
In a spot near the Nishi-Azabu intersection in Roppongi, Tokyo is a restaurant called ""FERMiNTXO"". Despite the casual atmosphere, it is a place that offers Spanish cuisine made with no cut corners and the opportunity to experience the complexities of Spanish wine.

The owner-chef, Shinya Sakumoto built his skills at a number of world gourmet guide awarded restaurants such as ""Restaurante Alameda,"" ""Fonda Sala,"" ""Restaurante Neichel,"" and ""El raco de Can Fabes"". Upon returning to Japan, he opened a restaurant in his hometown Ishikawa prefecture and opened ""FERMiNTXO"" in 2011.

Chef Sakumoto is particular about vegetables and uses Ishikawa produce grown at the ""Taka Nouen"" and ""Nishida Nouen farms"". Robust, healthy vegetables are grown in soil enriched using vegetable chips and green manure without chemical fertilizers or pesticides and grass instead of mulch. The skins of the potatoes are particularly beautiful and taste good as well. For example, the ""Galicia-style Octopus"" uses a puréed potato relish that highlights the flavor of the potato; all of the dishes are authentic Spanish recipes that highlight the Japanese ingredients. Sherries chosen by a 'venenciador' (a sherry expert) and red and white wine carefully chosen by a sommelier are on offer as well, with over 300 types of wine and 50 types of sherries. Chef Sakumoto has personally visited the ""Finca San Blas"" winery in Requena, Valencia to create original wine. The dedication is beyond what you would normally encounter. Advice on sherry for before, during, and after the meal is provided, with venenciador-chosen sherries that ""FERMiNTXO"" prides itself on the offering. There are also a variety of cheeses, raw hams, and salamis from all across Spain to match with wine.

""FERMiNTXO"" offers counter seats, sofas, tables, and a private room for up to 16 guests. Families with children are permitted on Saturdays. From light meals to commemorative dinners, business dinners or receptions, ""FERMiNTXO"" will meet the needs of guests.
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Exit A2(Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

244976.longDescription:
Roppongi, Tokyo, is well known as a battleground for famous restaurants. 
Isana, an eight-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Roppongi Station, is a sushi restaurant located on the first floor of a hotel and residential building along Roppongi Street near Roppongi Hills. Entering from the side of the building, guests are presented with a modern glass facade, the soft light from the entrance emanating, and a plate with the restaurant’s name greeting all. 

The owner, Junichi Onuki, has over 10 years of experience in sushi and Japanese restaurants in England after starting his career as a chef in Japan. After working at Zuma, a globally expanding Japanese restaurant, he returned to Japan and opened Isana in October 2012.

Onuki worked at a sushi restaurant in the Grand Hyatt Tokyo in Roppongi Hills before becoming independent after returning to Japan. It’s close to the current location of Isana, which was chosen as a place where Onuki could fully demonstrate his experience abroad. With this location and his background, Isana attracts many overseas clients. Based on his experience, tuna is purchased from one of the top five restaurants in Toyosu Market through a go-between broker, with the intent that his guests will be able to experience real Edomae-style sushi. The vinegared rice is made by using No. 194 rice, which is loosely loosened and has little stickiness, with Chiodi rice vinegar as the base, accented with red vinegar.

The drinks that go with sushi are sake and wine. The restaurants always offer seven to eight varieties of sake, and around 15 kinds including seasonal sake, mainly Tohoku sake, that pairs well with sushi. A full sake pairing is also recommended. For wine, Isana has carefully selected wines, such as Kenzo Estate.

The contemporary interior seats eight guests at the counter, with a table for up to four diners. Ideal for dates and anniversaries, the restaurant is also perfect for entertaining guests and for family gatherings with children. In particular, the service of international guests will be fulfilling, as the owner Onuki's career is fully demonstrated.

The name of the restaurant, “Isana”, means small fish; here, it's fun to share a little happiness with family and close friends. Guests can enjoy authentic Edomae-style sushi in comfortable surroundings at Isana.
nearestStations: An 8-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Nishi-Azabu Crossing (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

244480.longDescription:
"I believe that food is love," says Yosuke Otsuka, the owner of the namesake restaurant "Japanese Cuisine Otsuka Yosuke". Otsuka opened the restaurant in 2015 in Nishi-Azabu, and when he changed premises in 2016, he chose to stay in the same area because he values his regular customers.

Otsuka is originally from Fukuoka. While he is still just 32 years old, he has already earned considerable popularity among local restaurant-goers. Otsuka's biggest goal is to please his customers with cuisine made from fresh seasonal ingredients. He selects ingredients from his native Kyushu; Otsuka has vegetables shipped directly from Fukuoka every day, while for meat he orders Tarama beef raised in the Miyako-Jima region by a veteran farmer there, and for rice, Fukuoka grown Renge rice produced by a friend of his. Otsuka aims to please diners with simple, unflashy seasonal specialties like an unseasoned grilled eel in summer, longtooth grouper hotpot in winter, and rice seasoned and cooked with various ingredients that differ according to the season. Otsuka's cuisine is an expression of his mastery of technique and sincere desire to please his customers. For tableware, he mostly uses Karatsu ware made in Saga. The earthy colors and wonderful texture of the dishes bring out the flavor of the fresh ingredients of the food. "Japanese Cuisine Otsuka Yosuke" offers Japanese sake and a selection of wine, most of which are sourced from France. Their mild flavors pair wonderfully with the cuisine.

Japanese Cuisine Otsuka Yosuke has a private room which seats four and six counter seats. Its design makes ample use of warm wood interiors, which will relax your mind from the moment you step in the door. "Many of my customers recommend my restaurant to their friends, which helps support my business," says Otsuka, and it is certainly the kind of place you will want to introduce your friends to, with its friendly, fun atmosphere. Since Otsuka is fluent in English, oversea guests can also have a great time here. Otsuka's carefully-made Japanese cuisine inspires the kind of trust that normally takes years to build.

recommendations.comment: I was very happy with dinner at Ootsuka, where I have been many times. The fact that he speaks English is not a secondary detail, since accessing true Japanese cuisine is always a problem in Tokyo if you don’t speak Japanese. Anyway, he has a very good canteen with European wines or sake (nihonsyu). As far as the food is concerned, the freshest vegetables cooked the Japanese way (keeping all the flavour), great meat and sashimi (you will get small bites of everything) and some more adventurous dishes not that easy to find like suppon ( turtle’s broth). Don’t miss it!

243922.longDescription:
This world gourmet guide awarded Japanese restaurant is located in an back alley in Nishi-Azabu. 

It serves Kansai-style Japanese cuisine using fresh vegetables, seafood, and Saga beef, all delivered directly from the owner’s homeland, Saga. 
The sake selection also centers on those produced in Saga, and guests can compare ten different kinds of Nabeshima sake, including rare brands. The food is limited to a single omakase (chef's choice) menu, but the owner is able to adapt flexibly to the desire of his guests. 

Customers can enjoy informal conversation with the friendly owner at the counter, and table seating that can accommodate business reception is also available.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

244946.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Kasumitei Matsubara is located on the 3rd floor of a building in Nishi-Azabu, one block away from a busy intersection. Here, the restaurant acts as a hideaway enveloped in calm, where chef Hiroaki Matsubara demonstrates his skills.

Matsubara learned the fundamentals of Japanese cuisine by training at Kappo Minoichi in Ginza and Kanazawa's long-established restaurant Kinjiro. He joined Azabu Kyozen in 1999 and concurrently served as the manager and the chef. After 11 years of intense study, he became independent and opened Kasumitei Matsubara in 2010. The Kasumitei in the name of the restaurant is derived from Kasumi-cho, the former name of Nishiazabu.

While there are many creative variants of Japanese cuisine, Matsubara preserves traditional cooking methods while incorporating innovation into his dishes. For example, seafood is purchased from Toyosu Market -- if there is a change in the fishing schedule due to adverse weather, Matsubara will be informed immediately and plans accordingly. His dedication stems from his philosophy that “life entrusted by producers such as farmers and fishermen must be presented to guests in the best condition, with respect to producers".

The cuisine is prepared at the open kitchen as part of an immersive experience that allows guests to enjoy the food and aroma, but one that entices the other senses. The restaurant specialized in charcoal grilled seafood and meat, and are very particular about the materials of the cooking utensils. Meanwhile, the burning tools and steamer are made by Ippento Nakagawa, an artist based in Shigaraki Kumoi-yaki. "I am happy to see the smiles of the customers coming through the counter," smiles Matsubara.

The restaurant offers guests around 10 kinds of sake such as Tedorigawa from Ishikawa, Kokuryu from Fukui, and Nabeshima from Saga. Matsubara is also keen in his wine selections, recommending Kenzo Estate, and Chardonnay from Misawa Estate Vineyard in Yamanashi.

Stepping into the restaurant, guests are greeted by characters written by female calligrapher, Makiko Kan. There are 7 counter seats and a private room that can accommodate up to 2 to 8 people, which can be used in a variety of situations, from dining out with family, friends and colleagues, dating to business entertainment. Guests are invited to stop the clock for a few hours, and enjoy a quintessential Japanese experience at Kasumitei Matsubara.

244396.longDescription:
"Kawasaki" is a small Japanese cuisine restaurant located in the Nishi Azabu area, where a host of hidden gourmet restaurants huddle together. The owner Masato Kawasaki has built up experience in a number of famous Tokyo restaurants, and from its opening in November 2012, he served as head chef at the specialty live crab restaurant "Akasaka Kitafuku". In April 2018, he set out independently. Because he wants guests to be able to relax and enjoy their meal, the restaurant contains just two private rooms. He devotes himself to providing heartfelt hospitality to the two groups of customers that are permitted in the restaurant each day.

The food consists of a chef's selection of around 15 dishes. Ingredients are ordered in and the meals put together in accordance with the guests. Wagyu Beef, crab, and turtle are incorporated into the course throughout the year. The crab dishes, cooked from live using the knowledge and techniques the chef developed at "Akasaka Kitafuku," is a particular highlight. Crabs including horsehair crab, red king crab, snow crab, Japanese blue crab are used according to the season and can be enjoyed in a number of ways, such as in hotpot or as sashimi. As well as ordering in the finest Matsuzaka Wagyu beef and turtles from the famous Hattori-Nakamura Farm in Shizuoka, high-quality ingredients such as eels and matsutake mushrooms are available when in season. The drinks are also exactingly chosen, with a wine list focused on Burgundies. Around a dozen hand-picked sakes are available, including Senshin, Juyondai, and Kokuryu, while the champagne selection includes premium brands such as Krug, Salon and Dom Perignon. These combine to produce a truly special and refined experience.

The interior furnishings, including large comfortable chairs and tables, are all chosen to match by Mr. Kawasaki himself.  The tableware is 90% antique, featuring mainly late Edo-period plates from old Imari, Eiraku, and Rokubei, while the glasses are old Baccarat. As well as being ideal for entertaining or business meetings, you can also bring children, making it perfect for a special family anniversary. With its elegant interior, genuine antique tableware, and food available only on that day, a visit here will be a superb experience that lives long in the memory.

243677.longDescription:
Having gained experience at world gourmet guide award restaurants such as ""Michel Bras"" in France and ""The Fat Duck"" in England, Chef Namae brings his originality and creativity to his contemporary French restaurant L'Effervescence.

The courses for your meal will be selected by the chef. Contrary to the innovative appearance of his dishes, the fresh aroma of herbs and the flavor of fresh ingredients erupt spectacularly in your mouth. By cooking seasonal ingredients for long periods of time at a low temperature, he brings out their natural flavors. At this restaurant you will encounter foie gras prepared through a special process, pie pastries stuffed with finest ingredients and made to look like apple pies, and other dishes each endowed with the passion and energy of its creator. Enjoy some wine with the cuisine as you sit amidst the relaxed atmosphere for an experience that will exceed your expectations.

--- From L'Effervescence head chef Shinobu Namae, to our most esteemed customers ---

I was born Japanese, and I aim to draw out and enhance the harmonious flavors of this land that I love and other places around the world. My goal is to create a complete dining experience bound by a unity of plates, tables, customers, and myself.

Our restaurant is a true ""retreat within the city."" During your 3–4 hour sojourn here, escape from the hustle and bustle of the city and forget reality for just a while.

With love for the abundant nature of the forest and sea along with deep gratitude for the toil in the fields and pastures and appreciation for the unseen yeast and microbes, our hearts and bodies will be filled with ""effervescence.""

We look forward to seeing you soon.

※ Awarded 3 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

recommendations.comment:
お料理の素晴らしさはもちろんのこと、接したスタッフの方すべてが気持ちの良い対応でリラックスした楽しい時間が過ごせました。
ありがとうございました。

今回、２回目でしたが、
とても満足しました。

季節毎に伺いたいと思います。

久々に直ぐにでも再訪したいと思わせるステキなフレンチでした。
タクシーで近くまで行って、10年くらい前に訪れた記憶がよみがえりましたが、店構えが記憶と違っていたので、勘違いかと思ったら、店名も変わり、店構えも変わったものの同じお店だと言うことでした。味の方の記憶は残っていませんでしたが、ユニークなメニューもさることながら、それ以上に素材を生かし、見た目も楽しませてくれる料理が次々に、見計らったようなここぞと言うタイミングでの出されて、時の経つのを忘れてしまうほどでした。美しくプレゼンされた料理を引き立てるお皿もさることながら、スプーン、ナイフ、フォークもよく吟味され使いやすいものばかりで驚きました。最後に抹茶も美味しく頂戴しました。お店の雰囲気も、料理及び飲み物をサーブしてくれる人達も、気持ちのいい応対でした。

Very delicious especially the ayu, tulips and corn soup. 
However, the veal is a bit let down as it is too fibrous and powdery taste. Guess the veal is to young?
Roland and Zac are very attentive but the rest of the staffs are not as my glass of water was empty without anyone filling it until Zac saw it.
料理がおいしいのは当然の時代、店の雰囲気・ホールスタッフの対応等でのトータル的な食事の場所として満足出来るお店でした。
一人でも安心して食事できる
大変、楽しい時間を過ごさせていただきました。

料理もサービスも大満足でした。
また利用したいと思います。
最初のお皿から最後まで、ハッとする驚きがあり、特にお任せでお願いした各料理とお酒のマリアージュがまた素晴らしい発見でした。これ程5感をフルに刺激され、楽しい食事は久々です。素材選び、火の入れ方、塩加減、様々なアクセント、お酒のセレクト、サービス、全てにおいて一流と感じました。

料理、サービス共に素晴らしく、迷ったもののソムリエの方にお任せしたお酒も、どれも想像と違い(良い意味で)、料理を引き立てる役目があるなぁ、と感心させられました。
機会がありましたら、またお邪魔したいと思います。

まず、冷酒と白ワインを合わせた食前酒を金杯で頂くという驚き。すだちのシャーベットが爽やかでした。スープを味わってから、鮎を食べ尽くす一皿が絶品でした。山椒の香りが良かったです。野辺地の蕪が美味しかったこと。メインの満遍なく程よく火が通った牛肉が美味しく、2枚目を燻製ソースで頂くと全然違う味わいで楽しめました。どんな質問をしても、ギャルソンの方がお料理を知り尽くしてらっしゃるのに感心しました。また、フレンチのお店でお薄のお点前を拝見できるとは驚きでした。初めてお伺いしましたが、大満足です。ご馳走様でした。

素晴らしいお料理、そしてそのお料理に合わせるワインはもちろん、サービスも含めて非常に心地よいひとときを過ごさせていただきました。やはり人気の実力派のレストランだけのことはあると思います。サービスの質も高級店によくありがちな偉そうな振る舞いではなく、フレンドリーかつ親しみやすい感じ（かといって決してくだけすぎることがなく、品が良くてエレガントです！）で、そこがまた此方の持ち味の一つだと思っています。たまたま一人客の方がすぐ近くにいらしたのですが、一人でも寂しくないように、そして食事の邪魔にならないように、適度な距離感をもって話しかけている姿には好感を覚えました。一人でも訪問してみようかなーという勇気が湧いてきました（一人は受け付けていないのでしょうが・笑）。また、お誕生日のサプライズも周囲のテーブルの邪魔になることなく、静かにお祝いされていて良かったです。予約の難易度が高いお店の一つですが、また機会があったら是非利用せさせていただきたいと思います。有難うございました。
料理も素晴らしく、スタッフさんの対応やホスピタリティも最高でした。美味しいことはもちろん、一皿一皿に驚きがあって、とても楽しい時間となりました。また違う季節に是非伺いたいです。今日は本当にごちそうさまでした。

結婚記念日でお伺いしました。
落ち着く席に ご案内いただき、お料理も品数多く いずれもシェフが よくご研究されて、お気持ちが感じられる 大変美味しいものばかりでした。
とても満足し楽しませていただきました。
人気店のため、途中からとても混んだせいか、お料理がサーブされてかなり経ってしまってから、合わせるワインが来るというハプニングもありましたが、ソムリエのかたも気づかれて、恐縮されていらっしゃいました。
全体に、お料理はとても素晴らしく、ソムリエ、フロアースタッフのかたがたも お気遣い下さり、とても素敵な お食事になりました。

244175.longDescription:
"La BOMBANCE”, a hidden gem in Nishi-Azabu, offers new Japanese-style cuisine that does not limit to Japanese genre. The name of the restaurant means "feast" in French.

The owner-chef Makoto Okamoto opened “La BOMBANCE” in 2004 after working in "Japanese Cuisine Kamogawa" and "Kioicho Fukudaya" to polish his skills to extract the essence of Japanese cuisine."We want to create cuisine using seasonal ingredients from Japan that will remain in customers' hearts", said Mr. Okamoto.  Mr. Okamoto said that these sophisticated dishes has the wish for customers “ to enjoy their time with important people and feel satisfied that they have chosen to dine here. I also want to connect people by using amazing ingredients from Japan."

La BOMBANCE has several table settings that can fit to every occasion. Besides the table and counter seats, there is a private rooms (up tp 8 People) that can create an intimate and personalized culinary experience.

244954.longDescription: An eight-minute walk from Roppongi Station, in a quiet neighbourhood just one block from the main street, is the Tokyo branch of L’Auberge de L’ill, a one star French restaurant in Alsace that has been established for over 100 years. Designed and decorated to perfectly capture the spirit of grand European mansions, the establishment was created in collaboration with the Hiramatsu Co, which develops luxury restaurants and hotels in Tokyo and across Japan. Leading the kitchen is chef Yasutaka Sakai, who hails from Niigata Prefecture. He joined Hiramatsu Corporation in 2011. He has worked at "Daikanyama ASO Celeste Futakotamagawa" and "Maison Paul Bocuse" as sous chef before becoming sous chef at "Auberge de l'Ile Tokyo" in February 2019, and in April 2023, he was selected as head chef. The menu is based on the cuisine of the most famous restaurants in Alsace, but makes the most of the excellent Japanese ingredients to create a menu unique to Tokyo. For example, the popular pie-wrapped "Beef Tenderloin with Foie Gras and Truffles" uses local beef rather than the gibier meat found in French recipes. The combination of quality Wagyu beef, French foie gras, and truffles makes this dish one of the restaurant's most confident creations. The Hiramatsu Co. shares the curve of directly importing and storing wine from makers across France, 200 types of wine are always available for guests, such as champagne, red, white and rose. From the entrance, guests ascend a spiral staircase to a beautifully-appointed 40-seat dining room. In addition, a private room that accommodates up to 12 guests is available on the second floor. Diners and epicures are invited to visit this gorgeous restaurant on a special day with family, friends, couples, colleagues, where they will be able to fully enjoy the unusual atmosphere together with traditional, upscale French cuisine. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.
nearestStations: A 5-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Exit 2 (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

244031.longDescription:
Located a few minutes walk from Hiroo Station and near Nishi-Azabu intersection, this exquisite modern French restaurant is a place where the world's finest truffles can be enjoyed in whole.It is almost dream-like restaurant, where guests can select truffles they like from an assortment of fragrant high-quality truffles and use them to season their courses on their own. 

""Truffles,"" one of the world's most sought-after delicacies, are procured from all over the world to get the best ones for each season, and they are offered to guests at special price. Other than ""Margotto e Baciare,"" there are no other restaurants in Japan at which guests can select and slice whole truffles just for themselves. We highly recommend that everyone experience the exquisite delicacies on offer at this hidden gem in Nishi-Azabu.

245366.longDescription:
Nestled in a quiet residential neighborhood just off Roppongi Street, Myoujyaku is a refined Japanese restaurant that embodies the culinary philosophy of Chef Hidetoshi Nakamura. The name “Myoujyaku” itself reflects Chef Nakamura’s guiding concept. The character “Jyaku” (寂) is associated with “Zen” (然)—a notion that expresses the true essence of things and resonates deeply with Japanese aesthetics. 
It represents the ultimate destination of his cuisine. With profound insight into ingredients and a supple, sensitive approach, Chef Nakamura creates dishes that allow each ingredient to appear as it truly should. Guided by the principles of harmony, subtlety, and purity, he engages sincerely with his ingredients, refining his craft through daily trial and contemplation.
Chef Nakamura places particular importance on the idea that emotions and memories can reside in water. 
The opening dish is seasonal vegetables gently simmered in salted water. Using seawater salt from Miyazu, Kyoto, along with carefully selected water, the dish expresses a pure, nourishing flavor that reveals the essential character of the ingredients.

The beverage selection is curated by Sommelier Kibou Ogura. A wide range of sake, distinguished wines, and non-alcoholic beverages is thoughtfully listed to complement and elevate the cuisine of Myoujyaku.
The interior, designed by architect Toru Kijima, who has worked on numerous acclaimed restaurants, welcomes guests with a simple yet dignified and serene atmosphere. The restaurant features an eight-seat counter and two private rooms accommodating four and six guests respectively, allowing it to cater to a variety of dining occasions. 

※ Awarded 3 stars on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2026.
nearestStations: 8 minutes walk from 「Roppongi」 Station on Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line

"Nishi-azabu Kamikura", hidden-gem sushi place located at the Nishi-azabu transaction, about 7 minutes walk walk from Hiroo Station. Head chef Kamikura had worked at famous sushi places at Ginza, his brightness has been affixed to the atmosphere around the counter seats.

Using ingredients stocked at Tsukiji Market, serving only the a alternative style of chef's selected course, that nigiri sushis are served along with alternately. Vinegar rice is prepared by red vinegar, among those representative Edo-mae ingredients like tuna, kohada, urchin, chef especially focuses on the tuna, not only the "red meat, medium fatty tuna and pink fatty tuna" but a lot more rare cuts can be enjoyable here. Pairing alcoholics are also eye-catching, a variety of wine and red wine are attractive to customers.

Both domestic and international guests can enjoy top class sushi in a carefree environment. Definitely perfect for business dining or foreigners traveling to Japan, it is also suitable for dating or friends gathering. Let's enjoy sushi with chic of Edo-mae sushi and elegance of Japanese culture.

244840.longDescription:
Found on the first floor of a building on Gaien-Nishi Street, Nishiazabu Kenshiro is a short 10-minute walk from Roppongi Station. This Japanese BBQ restaurant was opened in 2015 in Nishiazabu, a popular dining destination known for its luxury BBQ restaurants. Here, the restaurant stands out as a genuinely celebratory eatery designed for celebrating special occasions. General chef Taisuke Chikashige trained in French and Japanese cuisine and stepped into the world of BBQ cuisine as he took his current position at Nishiazabu Kenshiro. With a keen eye for spotting meat of outstanding quality, he tackles each ingredient head-on to deliver exceptional cuisine to each guest.

Under the mission of offering Japan’s best festive BBQ, Nishiazabu Kenshiro welcomes each customer with exquisite food prepared with great care in every detail, including ingredients, culinary techniques, and meat cookery, as well as attentive hospitality and a diner-first approach. The meat served at the restaurant is sourced only from producers across Japan who share values and aspirations with chef Chikashige. In particular, full course meals featuring the best-quality meat available on the day are exceptional – the restaurant’s specialty, Kenshiro-style Wagyu Beef Chateaubriand, is cooked at low temperature and smoked instantly to bring out its rich aroma and flavor. A decadent Wagyu Beef and Sea Urchin Tartar Hot Dog is also popular for its combination of precious beef tartar and sea urchin served on toasted nori seaweed. The wine list is curated to feature vintages that pair well with meat, and consists of 50 wines sourced from France, the U.S., and Italy. To assist in choosing the perfect pour, a dedicated sommelier is always on hand to recommend pairings for customers.

As guests step into the restaurant, the Japanese-style entrance hall leads to tearoom-inspired low doors that open into private rooms. There are nine private rooms in total, each with two to eight seats, perfect for dinner with a partner or treasured clients. Book one of these rooms to enjoy exclusive premium beef in a sophisticated setting at Nishiazabu Kenshiro.
nearestStations: A 10 minutes' walk to Hiroo Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line
A 10 minutes' walk to Roppongi Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line

244365.longDescription:
After spending 10 years as an understudy at the renowned "Takada Hassho" in Gifu, followed by 6 years managing the "Kogane" and "Wakamiya Hassho" locations, Mr. Tetsuya Otake decided the time was ripe to start an independent venture in Tokyo. In December 2017 his restaurant, named Nishiazabu Otake, opened its doors. The restaurant won a 1-star in the 2022 edition of the World Gourmet Guide.

"Takada Hasshou" is located on a back street in Nishiazabu, an area with quality restaurants abound. It was founded on the idea of, “offering a compilation of traditional Japanese Kaiseki style banquets to guests in an intimate space.” The focus is on using seasonal ingredients in a single course that changes monthly.

Beginning with Potato Harihari and Turtle Okara, dishes that were popular during his time at "Takada Hassho," and then continuing on to meat dishes cooked over charcoal, a quintessentially Japanese seasonal wan(soup bowl), and a Western-style croquette, the course is organized in an original manner that allows one to fully enjoy the flavors of the season. Mr. Otake’s talent is on full display, utilizing simple ingredients to create highly refined dishes that satisfy on all levels, from the wafting aroma to the extent of the flavor and umami, and finally the profound aftertaste.

Another feature of the restaurant in the unique manner in which the ingredients are procured. The charcoal grilled Duck available during the winter season is wild game served with wild growing plants from the Gifu area, while marine products from the Sea of Japan are shipped directly from the neighboring Fukui Prefecture. Complementing the cuisine is a seasonal menu of choice sake from across Japan that enhances the flavor of the banquet even further.

Takada Hasshou’s interior features a counter made from a single slab of gingko wood and seats eight. There is also a private room that seats four. The counter seats are positioned close enough to enjoy a conversation with the mild-mannered Mr. Otake, a perfect atmosphere for a cheerful dining experience with friends or a lover.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

Located about five minutes from the Nishi-Azabu intersection, the entrance to a quiet residential area on the side of Kogaicho Park, Nishi-Azabu Shangou has made a fresh start. Going up the stairs and through the entrance area from the door, you will find a large single board counter in the main dining area.

Chef Arishima Hiroaki started his training at Keio Plaza Hotel "Nanen" in Shinjuku in 1981. He studied at some of Tokyo's leading hotels including the All Nippon Airways Hotel (currently the Intercontinental Hotel Tokyo) "Karin," and at The Peninsula Hotel Tokyo "Hei Fung Terrace," he became the top Japanese assistant chef and at the time of assuming the position of head chef at Mandarin Oriental, Tokyo "SENSE", he was awarded 1 star as a world class gourmet guide. He later went to Paris, France. In Franklin Roosevelt, he opened a Cantonese dish called "Tong Yen", and he was active not only in Japan, so he opened a new restaurant called "Nishi-Azabu Shangu" as a culmination.
The cuisine was born from Arishima's career, and while the cuisine is centered on Cantonese cuisine, the inspiration and experience of Arishima is interwoven everywhere in this course that can only be enjoyed here. The concept is "Issai Iskon". The specialty uses shark fins, which are rare in Japan "Simmered shark fin.", to capture the hearts of guests. The steamed fish is served with hot fish sauce in front of guests by Arishima himself, using sujiara which is directly delivered from Miyakojima.
The drink will include wine carefully selected by the sommelier, and they will suggest a pairing to match the dish.

The dining room has an open kitchen with a spacious 8-seat counter in front. A counter where you can enjoy the live feeling while watching the movement of kitchen staff. And for the guests who enjoyed the meal in the first part, you can spend a relaxing time in a different atmosphere at the sub-dining in the back. Private rooms for up to 6 people are also available. We hope you will enjoy Mr. Shima's cuisine as a friendly friend, date, entertaining, etc.

243863.longDescription:
""OHARA ET CIE"", a French restaurant located in a residential neighborhood nearby the Nishi-Azabu crossing in Tokyo, and about an eight minute walk from Roppongi Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line or from Roppongi Hills. The restaurant's interior is all white in colour, following the theme of an inorganic feeling of cleanliness, and though it is underground, it features an open space lit by sunlight entering from a wellhole style terrace.

Owner and Chef Ohara opened ""OHARA ET CIE"" in 2000, after eight years of working as the executive chef at ""Q.E.D. CLUB,"" a high-end restaurant in Ebisu, Tokyo. In 2008, the restaurant earned a world gourmet guide award. Over many years, this exquisite cuisine that prioritizes the natural flavor of ingredients has won the hearts of many fans. The wine menu comes mainly from France, and courses featuring glasses of champagne can be reserved for either lunch or dinner using Pocket Concierge. Vegetarian menus can also be prepared upon request during reservation. A recommended restaurant for anniversary dates, family occasions, or a light meal with friends.

244243.longDescription:
Restaurant Kodama on the 2nd floor of a building located in a Nishi Azabu alley, just a short walking distance from the lively main street of Roppongi. It is often touted as new Japanese cuisine or creative Japanese cuisine, but the food, created based on the owner’s conscious effort to serve “pure Japanese cuisine”.
Owner Tsutomu Kodama has experience working in several different types of restaurants such as traditional Japanese, soba, and sushi restaurants. However, his own cooking is based on a foundation of food culture, science, and even physics on books, whereas it was developed through logistics. Kodama’s cooking takes into account not just the shape or taste of the food, but what will make the person eat healthier, using recipes that take into account such things as controlling the amount of heat that is used in order not to cause the food to oxidize. And yet the food is authentic and similar to tea ceremonies and/or flower arrangements, the presentation is a feast for the eyes. Most of Restaurant Kodama’s dishware are original creations by artists; some were created to match the food that will be served in it. The combination of the dishware and the food makes a further impact and transports the eater into the world of the owner’s creations. 

On the menu are omakase courses only. Strong seasoning is avoided in order to bring out the natural flavors of each dish, allowing guests to enjoy a one-of-a-kind cuisine.  
Restaurant Kodama’s original Awabi (Abalone) Soba has taken food lovers captive – many visit the restaurant to enjoy this dish. The alcohol served is centered around Japanese sake, in order to bring out the flavor of the food. Just as for the food, the beverages are carefully selected by the owner, who makes sure that they are healthy, go down smooth and will not cause you to get drunk.  
 
Along with 10 counter seats, a private room that holds up to 8 people is prepared because the owner “wants our customers to be able to relax as if they are coming to my home”. The kitchen is built low, allowing those to view it well and see their food being prepared. There is no age limit and customers with children are valued. Enjoy with us the world of food created by Chef Kodama in a top quality yet relaxed atmosphere.

245052.longDescription:
Without a sign outside, Sushi Kinoshita is hidden away in a condominium complex in Nishiazabu 1-chome. Inside the restaurant, chef Noriaki Nakamura, who honed his culinary skills at renowned sushi and Japanese restaurants, makes sushi with all his heart.

Chef Nakamura first trained at Kyoto Kitcho Arashiyama, which he left for his hometown of Hiroshima to hone his skills at Inasa, a Japanese restaurant run by a junior disciple of renowned chef Rokusaburo Michiba. Then, he worked at Rokusantei helmed by chef Michiba in Ginza. After working there for eight years, he was referred by chef Michiba to the position of chef at Minamitsugaru Kinsui (in Aomori), where he contributed to its first-place ranking in a travel agency’s survey on the best Japanese-style hotel restaurants in the country. 

Afterwards, he learned customer service skills at a French restaurant as well as culinary skills at a Japanese restaurant and took the position of general chef at Kissho Ginza Honten. Then, he was invited by a sushi chef with whom he had been acquainted to learn sushi cuisine at a famous sushi restaurant. In 2018, another twist of fate brought him to Sushi Kinoshita. The restaurant was restructured and reopened in August 2020, where he has since served as its manager.

The seafood is sourced from wherever the best quality is available at that moment, depending on the season. For example, tuna is sourced from Toyosu Market, sea urchin, salmon roe, and angler liver from Hokkaido, snow crabs from Ishikawa, and kelp grouper from Kyushu. The sushi rice is made with a blend of different varieties of rice from Hachidaime Gihei in Kyoto and seasoned with red vinegar and salt from Christmas Island. All sushi is made with the same sushi rice, but the temperature is adjusted to match the pairing. The signature dish is steamed abalone with liver sauce.

The drinks menu offers red, white, and sparkling wines, as well as about 10 kinds of sake, mainly dry ones, such as Hitakami and Hakurakusei from Miyagi, Aramasa from Akita, Toyo Bijin from Yamaguchi, and chef Nakamura’s favorite Hiroki from Fukushima.

Visitors press the intercom button at the entrance of the condo and ascend to the second floor where the sushi restaurant is located. Inside the restaurant, there is a handsome wood counter and a kitchen with an ice fridge and a grill.

The restaurant invites guests to enjoy exquisite delicacies and sushi with their family, a partner, friends, or colleagues at Sushi Kinoshita, designed to delight the palates of casual diners and sushi lovers alike.

244725.longDescription: “Sushi Murase” is located in Roppongi, where there are many popular restaurants. Beyond the restaurant curtain is a dignified space, and from the large window that can be seen from the counter, you can view the courtyard with its changing appearance every season. Chef Nobuyuki Murase went independent after training at a famous sushi restaurant in Tokyo. In 2014, he opened “Sushi Murase”, named after himself. The kanji for “鮓”, stands for "To make sushi with ingredients that go well with vinegared rice, and to make vinegared rice that goes well with the sushi ingredients", which is chef Murase’s strong wish to achieve for all of his sushi. The chef's Omakase Course includes side dishes, nigiri and sushi rolls. "The composition changes from day to day depending on the state of the sushi ingredients," chef Murase said. The seafood for sushi is purchased directly from a reliable vendor. Only salt and vinegar are used for vinegared rice, and red vinegar and rice vinegar are used separately. The restaurant specializes in matured sushi, especially matured Kohada. It is also popular among women because of its beautiful appearance. The recommended alcoholic drink to pair your sushi with is Japanese sake. There are around 35 types from around Tokyo, Tohoku and Mie Prefecture. You can choose the type that goes best with your sushi from dry, medium and sweet tastes. The restaurant has a U-shaped cypress counter (14 -15 seats) and private rooms (up to 8 people, children are allowed). You can enjoy it in various situations such as with friends who like sushi, dates, entertaining guests from overseas, and with family for special occasions. ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 8 people. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? We ask you to remove shoes in the private dining room(s). ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children. However, please be informed that seats by the counter are available only for adult guests. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible and we will be happy to assist as needed. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person.

245454.longDescription:
Located among renowned restaurants in Nishiazabu, Sushi Rizaki Nishiazabu opened in May 2023 as the fourth location of the highly sought-after Sushi Rizaki, following the main location in Shibuya and the two branches in Aoyama and Ebisu. This newest location is helmed by Chef Naoki Shiotani, who has inherited the sushi-making craftsmanship of Sushi Rizaki.

Chef Shiotani developed his career at prestigious restaurants, learning the basics of Japanese cuisine at Kikunoi Honten in Kyoto and gaining experience in French cuisine at Tsubaki in Nishiazabu. He then asked Sushi Rizaki for an apprenticeship to become a sushi chef who can demonstrate his culinary skills right in front of guests. Appreciated for his masterful art of sushi making backed by his honed culinary skills, he was appointed to helm the third location, Sushi Rizaki Ebisu, which opened in 2021. Having made it a popular destination for sushi lovers, he has now been assigned as a chef to the fourth location established near the second location in Aoyama, which has also become highly sought-after. The fourth location is also expected to emerge as a hotspot for sushi lovers.

Continuously seeking to dispel the highbrow image of sushi restaurants, Chef Shiotani keeps prices within reach for young customers. In the meantime, he competes in quality by sourcing ingredients in the same way as the main location to satisfy the most discriminating sushi connoisseurs. He visits the Toyosu Market to source fish and other sushi ingredients from brokers with whom he has forged strong ties while scrutinizing the offerings himself. He orders different sushi ingredients every week to offer some variety for frequent diners — even those who come weekly.

As for wasabi, the Mazuma variety is sourced from Koichi Tashiro in Gotemba, Shizuoka.
The sushi rice is made with a blend of two varieties known as Tohoku No. 194 and Emi no Kizuna, which are different in grain size and hardness, to ensure that it will fall apart in the mouth. It is seasoned with a blend of three varieties of vinegar: the spirit vinegar “Hakuju” and the red vinegar “Kohaku” from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing and “Chidorisu” from Murayama Zousu. The bluefin tuna featured halfway through the multi-course meal is delivered from Hicho, a renowned intermediate wholesaler. This superb tuna sushi is a signature sushi for which the sushi rice is exclusively made by cooking rice in a timely manner, cooling it down to an ideal temperature, and mixing it with vinegar. Meanwhile, the chef’s pride, “Sake-steamed Clams,” which are cooked in stock made by soaking kombu seaweed in sake for one week, demonstrate his masterful skills rooted in his experience in Japanese cuisine.

Sushi Rizaki Nishiazabu offers some 20 labels of sake from across Japan, in addition to options stocked year-round, such as Juyondai from Yamagata and Aramasa from Akita and you may want to ask recommended sake according to sushi toppings and your preferences. Inside the restaurant is a dining hall with an eye-catching L-shaped, solid Hinoki cypress countertop (seating up to 10 guests) and earthen walls as well as a private dining room (seating up to four guests). Relax and enjoy high-quality sushi and delicacies in an elegant yet effortless setting at Sushi Rizaki Nishiazabu.

244183.longDescription:
An Edo-mae Sushi restaurant located in an unique white building opened near the Nishi-Azabu intersection in Tokyo. The signature vinegar rice uses a special "Nagai Sushi Tou Rice" from Kumamoto Prefecture that is only for Sushi Tou. It is a result from a careful discussion between the producer and Sushi Tou. This "hinohikari" rice is special because of the harvest timing and the unique rice polishing process. Two kinds of vinegar, rice vinegar and red vinegar, are used according to the taste of the seafood, to let you hear the story expressed through the balance of the whole. You can enjoy a selection of sake, which changes monthly, and their marriage with sushi.

There is only one counter, made from “Shiraki”(plain wood), in this sushi restaurant. A warm space with the feeling of connection with people. Not only for entertainment and dinner, but also for sushi dates with females, here would be a very good choice. English menu and English service also available, recommended for overseas guests.

245323.longDescription:
About a 10-minute walk from Nogizaka Station, Sushi Yamaguchi sits on a quiet side street near the Nishi-Azabu Crossing. The restaurant is helmed by Yasuhiro Yamaguchi, a faithful chef who gives his all to satisfy guests.

Chef Yamaguchi has been devoted to the art of sushi for his entire career. He trained at renowned sushi restaurants, including Sushisho in Yotsuya and Takumi Shingo in Minami-Aoyama, for a total of 14 years before he opened his own restaurant named after himself in February 2022.
“I always strive to be sincere and honest with each guest, as I was taught during my apprenticeship,” Chef Yamaguchi says. “In the meantime, I am deeply exploring my own style while sticking to the flavors and techniques I learned.”
Like Sushisho in Yotsuya, Sushi Yamaguchi offers a prix-fixe (fixed price) menu consisting of 20 to 22 courses of sushi and delicacies. The fish and shellfish are sourced from a fishmonger at Toyosu Market with whom the chef has had a good relationship since his apprenticeship. The sushi rice is kept at body temperature and seasoned with either white rice or red vinegar, depending on the topping.
Sushi Yamaguchi always keeps 10 labels of sake in stock, including the chef’s favorites such as Hitakami from Miyagi and Nogomi from Saga. A selection of white wines, including SOU from 98 Winery in his home prefecture of Yamanashi, are offered by the bottle or glass. If you do not know which drink you want, you can ask the chef to choose for you.

With a nine-seat counter, Sushi Yamaguchi is the perfect place for intimate meals with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues. Enjoy conversations with Chef Yamaguchi and his ever-evolving sushi and delicacies at Sushi Yamaguchi.
nearestStations: A 10-minute from Nogizaka Station

If you would like to make a new reservation, please contact us separately. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Sushi restaurant Sushi-Sho Masa is located close to Nishi-Azabu Crossing and 10 minutes' walk from Roppongi station. It is distinguished by its bright red doorway curtain. The boss who manages the seven counter seats is Masakatsu Oka, who came from the famous Sushi-Sho in Yotsuya. Masakatsu Oka carries himself with such energy that he has deeply invigorated the atmosphere of the entire restaurant . Following the style of his original restaurant Sushi-Sho, courses of nigiri sushi and side dishes are served alternately. Guests can sample small portions of a rich array of delicious dishes, along with Japanese sake. Committed and uncompromising selection of ingredients are the boss' obsession. Come and experience the menu where every dish is a culinary gem; the product of a chef who has honed his craft and sees being picky naturally creates the true sushi. Being located in the area of town that never sleeps, the restaurant is open until late at night. Guests can stop by for sushi as an after-work reward or a late-night gathering with friends. This taste bud-tantalizing restaurant is for people who want to try the real authentic sushi. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? 244447.longDescription:
Located on the basement floor of a condominium between Nishi-azabu and Hiroo, ""TAIAN"" is a hidden getaway which opened in 2018. In addition to Chef Naoyuki Mori, who spent 20 years training at world gourmet guide award restaurant ""Chateau Restaurant Joel Robson"" in Ebisu, this classical French restaurant employs the cream of the crop coming out of the 'Joel Robuchon 'group.

The restaurant name ""Taian"" comes from the tea room built by 'Sen no Rikyu' which exists today as a Japanese national treasure. The interior is a modern interpretation of the spirit of 'Sen no Rikyo,' who entertained guests in his two-tsubo large tea room; it is simply built with the chef's kitchen installed in the center, giving the feeling of a live performance. The furnishings and equipment—the 105cm walnut countertop, Christofle cutlery, Imari and Arita flatware, ""Koma"" and ""Moctave"" chairs—all shine with authenticity, not having faded at all over the years.

The concept of the cuisine is memorable dishes. The best ingredients of each of the four seasons have their characteristics expressed directly in simple yet profound dishes. The tradition of French cuisine lives in the taste of the sauces, and the French esprit can be felt everywhere. The wine list is mainly Champagne and Burgundy, with many 90s' vintages offered, allowing you to imagine the mellow traditional culinary culture of France. The evening banquet is opened to only 7 at the chef's table and 6 in the private room and is recommended to those who want to experience the essence of French cuisine, which is not bothered by fads or trends.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Exit 4, Hiro-o Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

The Owner Chef Otsuki Takumi training 3 years and 3 month in France to open this restaurant. He started in world gourmet guide award restaurant “Le Petit Nice”, finished in 5-star restaurant. After back to Japan in Nov. 2015, he opened the “Takumi”. He barely have any experience in Japan Restaurants: after finish Bachler degree in Kobe University management direction, he came to France and directly talk with the restaurant he interested in “I want to learn in this restaurant”. During his stay, he tasted over 100 Europe restaurants. His sensitivity learned in France, and the approach of activity of cooking, is the most precious part of this world gourmet guide award “Takumi”. 

Chef Otsuki Takumi believe that the “correct understand creatively coordination makes a joyful restaurant”. Guests always remember “that’s the dish in Takumi style”. “Delicious is without boarder” is what our chef saying. We only offering one course. By deeply understand our guests, we offering each dish with introduction cards explaining its idea and ingredients, and example of materials in little bottle, present you not only tasting but also great vision and smelling experience. 

For simple eating, private room (max.4 person) are available, good selection for lunch or dinner. We have English Menu and we are offering English service, easily access for oversea guests. Selected by our sommelier, the cork tail are valued to have a taste also in our “Takumi”

245299.longDescription:
Perched on the second floor of a building on Seijoki Street in Nishiazabu, the Chinese restaurant, Tsugumi, is helmed by Chef Sho Hama, whose dishes delight the taste buds of connoisseurs that gravitated to prominent restaurants in Nishiazabu.

The restaurant was named Tsugumi (meaning migrant thrush in Japanese), likening guests to migrant birds and the restaurant to a perch that offers them high-quality dishes and services in a relaxing atmosphere, as was the chef’s wish. In fact, the white entrance gate is inspired by a bird’s nest.

Chef Hamasaki’s Chinese cuisine is grounded in Cantonese and Sichuan culinary techniques, though the classical flavors of these cuisines are reinterpreted in an innovative way. In addition, he combines different culinary techniques he learned at other restaurants to fulfill the desires of guests.

The restaurant’s menu includes a number of popular dishes, such as stewed whole abalone, mapo tofu served in an earthen pot, and fried rice with home-roasted Iberico pork cooked over a specially made Chinese stove with a high heat output.
The wine cellar holds more than 600 bottles, mainly from Bourgogne, selected by Mr. Yukihiro Shindo, the manager and sommelier, who worked at a starred restaurant in London, and the Chinese tea list is curated by Ms. Marina Fujimoto, a certified tea art specialist. Remember to try food and drink pairings selected by these two specialists who know Chef’s dishes like the back of their hands.

Inside the restaurant, there is a white-toned main dining room furnished with two modern tables (each seating up to four guests) and a bar counter (seating up to six guests) as well as a private dining room (with four seats). Please enjoy quality dishes and services in a relaxing atmosphere at Tsugumi on various occasions.
nearestStations: A -7 minutes walk from exit 2 of Roppongi Station on Hibiya Line

245529.longDescription:
Located in Nishiazabu, which is now a mecca for yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) lovers, YAKINIKU JINSEKI Nishiazabu offers Jinseki, a mythical Kuroge Wagyu beef, in yakiniku or kaiseki (multi-course) form. While the yakiniku menu offers premium cuts, the kaiseki menu invites guests to enjoy an array of traditional Japanese flavors to their heart’s content. Carefully fattened for a long period of time in Jinsekikogen Town, Hiroshima Prefecture, Jinseki beef was propelled into the spotlight when former Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida offered Grilled Jinseki Beef Tenderloin to the then U.S. President Joe Biden during his visit to Japan in 2022. This legendary beef is quite difficult to find as only 400 heads of cattle are shipped yearly. However, YAKINIKU JINSEKI securely sources the mythical beef from its own ranch in Jinsekikogen Town that is operated as part of the community development project. When it arrives at the restaurant, the beef is first cleaned and trimmed and then processed into cuts, which are all used in different recipes.

The kitchen is helmed by Executive Chef Ren Ishino, who has been devoted to Japanese cuisine for years, serving as chef at Iyuki in Ginza and at Rokkan in Tsukiji. The 10-course prix-fixe menu features beef tenderloin slowly grilled over a low-heat charcoal fire, complemented by seasonal game meat and river fish from Jinsekikogen Town, which is renowned for its mountain delicacies. The menu also includes seasonal kaiseki dishes, such as Matsutake Rice, made with rice and mushrooms from the restaurant’s own farm and mountains, and Super Thin Jinseki Beef Sirloin Shabu-Shabu with Japanese Pepper Flowers. The ingredients are all outstanding, but what is most worth noting is Jinseki beef. The fine texture and rich flavor of A4-ranked lean meat chosen over A5-ranked marbled meat never fails to captivate the taste buds of guests.

The wine list curated by the restaurant’s sommelier from shared wine cellar with an affiliated wine bar offers Italian and French wines, from which the best option is selected for each guest according to their preferences and menu selections. The restaurant also offers a wide selection of sake, including not only Shinrai brewed by Miwa Sake Brewing Co., Ltd. in Jinsekikogen Town but also Ugo no Tsuki and Seikyo Maboroshi from Hiroshima and Aramasa from Akita.

The restaurant’s interior is stylish with Japanese décor, reminiscent of traditional Japanese restaurants. Above the counter is a series of openwork panels meticulously carved with pine and wave motifs that create a serene and peaceful ambience. The spacious counter seating (with eight seats and four roasters), ideal for dates and business entertainment. Also with well-ventilated table seating (two tables, each seating up to four guests) and a private dining room (seating up to six guests), the restaurant serves various purposes, such as entertaining guests from abroad and enjoying family reunions, friend gatherings, and other private events. Please enjoy the exquisite flavor and aroma of Jinseki beef at YAKINIKU JINSEKI Nishiazabu.
nearestStations: 9 minutes walk from Exit 2 of Roppongi Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Toei Oedo Line

This is a value-packed course featuring the rare and elusive "Jinseki Beef," a type of premium Wagyu.

Are you familiar with the difference between "Wagyu" and "domestic beef"? "Domestic beef" can be labeled as such even if it's born overseas, but "Wagyu" must be born and raised in Japan. Among the "Wagyu," the "Jinseki Beef," with only 400 cattle shipped per year, is known as the "phantom Wagyu."

The hallmark of Wagyu is its "tenderness." Jinseki Beef has a low melting point of fat, providing a melt-in-the-mouth texture. The flavor is rich in umami, offering a mellow sweetness akin to milk.

Please indulge in this rare and exquisite Wagyu, "Jinseki Beef"!
