244659.localizedAddress: 1F, La Alta Nishiazabu Building, 1-15-9, Nishiazabu, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244659.longDescription:
Not far from Tokyo's Nishi-Azabu intersection, on the first floor of a building on Gaien-Nishi Dori lies "Yakiniku Komiyama". Owner Hideki Komiyama really knows the wagyu beef, and here he serves up the best cuts, along with his traditional recipe sauce.

Komiyama worked part-time at a butcher's shop during his student days, and in 1997, aged 27, he turned in his white-collar job to become the manager of yakiniku restaurant "La Bouef" in Yoga, Tokyo. He taught himself about the various cuts of meat through a process of trial and error, and the restaurant soon rose to popularity after he began offering then rare A5 grade wagyu beef, which he bought up by the beef.  He then launched A5 grade wagyu beef specialty restaurant "Cossott'e" in Komazawa, followed by a second yakiniku restaurant featuring lavish interiors, "Cossott'e sp", which opened in Azabu-Juban in 2014. Komiyama struck out on his own in 2019 with the opening of "Yakiniku Komiyama".

Komiyama carefully selects the meat himself from a market in Shibaura, where he purchases A5 grade Japanese Black beef by the cow. The beef is then prepared by hand, expertly cut according to how it will be served. While the fillet is a good place to start, we also recommend the yaki-shabu—thinly sliced, grilled sirloin dipped in sauce with egg yolk. The Chateaubriand fillet katsu is another popular choice. There's also a course consisting of a sumptuous line-up of a beef tongue, tongue base, and tongue underside platter; skirt steak, topside and sirloin yaki-shabu, and fillet katsu. Komiyama also puts a lot of thought into his marinades. He uses five different marinades made to compliment the balance of lean meat and fat of various cuts of meat. There is a soy-based sauce with gochujang, Chinese broad bean chili paste, and four kinds of miso; a blend of garlic, ginger, and sesame oil; and a delicious salty-sweet concoction—each perfects the delicate balance between salt and sweetness, bringing out the flavor of the meat. A selection of alcoholic beverages to accompany the meat is available, with 15-16 wines, mostly French, a seasonal rotation of 5 Japanese sake, and 8 whiskies.

The restaurant logo was designed by a famous Japanese rock band. Liberal use of wood gives the interior a warm atmosphere. There is a range of seating arrangements, including eight counter seats that allow staff to interact more closely with patrons and semi-private table booths each seating four. Komiyama's prime cuts are best enjoyed with special sauce and good company, whether that be family, friends, or meat-loving colleagues.

Step into the world of premium Japanese beef with this exclusive lunch course from Komiyama, a renowned yakiniku destination in Nishi-Azabu.
From the rich flavors of our Special Yukhoe and grilled Wagyu Harami to rare cuts wrapped in fresh lettuce, the course offers a variety of textures and expressions of top-grade Wagyu.

Paired with a free-flow drink menu (beer, wine, sake, and soft drinks), this is not just lunch — it’s a destination-worthy Wagyu experience.

244731.longDescription:
“Yakitori Hirako” is located in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, where gourmet lovers often gather. This is the yakitori restaurant where the owner Makoto Takaiwa serves the local chicken that he is proud to have raised himself using his own unique method of heating.

He started raising chickens in Kobayashi City in Miyazaki Prefecture, at the age of 21, in order to provide delicious yakitori. He says "Yakitori is made from 80% ingredients and 20% arms. The grilling technique is meaningless unless you have a good selection of ingredients". After 10 years of trial and error, he created what he deemed to be the perfect recipe for cooking chicken and opened the restaurant “Jidori no Sato” in the city. Later, he opened another restaurant “Soup Egg Rice Specialty Shop Miran” in Miyazaki City. The reputation of the restaurant’s free-range chicken and eggs spread all over the country in no time, and finally they expanded to Tokyo in April 2019. He opened “Yakitori Hirako” in Nishiazabu, where even famous foodies are willing to line up outside and wait to get in.

The free-range chicken served in “Yakitori Hirako” is "Pure blood Nagoya cochin chicken" that is carefully raised by Mr. Takaiwa in Kobayashi City, Miyazaki Prefecture. It takes 400 to 500 days, which is 6 times longer than the usual time and cost, to raise high quality meat with pesticide-free vegetables grown by local farmers using natural farming methods. 

It should be noted that the chicken is grilled over charcoal but is not skewered. Because chickens are polyhedral, they need to be cooked to the center in different ways depending on the part. The appeal of “Yakitori Hirako” is that you can enjoy the different tastes of different parts of the chicken, so the best part is that each part is served one at a time which customers really enjoy. After the chicken has been cooked, it is then seasoned with wasabi soy sauce or salt to your liking.

For drinks, only sake that matches well with yakitori and vegetables is served. There are 30 kinds of sake from all over Japan served at the restaurant. There are 10 types of wine available by the glass and about 40 types of wine available by the bottle, which are mainly older vintages from France and Italy. Shochu produced mainly in Miyazaki Prefecture is also served. They are particular about mineral water, which they source specially from Kobayashi City in Miyazaki Prefecture. It is carbonated water that has a bubbly feel like champagne.

In this small restaurant with only 10 counter seats, only the counter is illuminated so that customers can talk with each other. If your party includes children, a reservation must be made in advance. The conversation will surely be lively whilst you enjoy the yakitori that is so meticulously prepared during celebrations such as family anniversaries, gatherings of gourmet lovers, dates or entertaining overseas guests.

245246.longDescription:
Located on Seijoki Street lined with renowned restaurants in Nishiazabu, Yakitori Shinohara is a yakitori kaiseki (grilled chicken banquet) restaurant featuring "Kokutei", the finest brand of heritage chicken from Kagoshima. This restaurant was opened in January 2021 by Owner-Chef Adore Shinohara, who had trained at famous yakitori and Japanese restaurants, and soon gained popularity among food lovers looking for the best grilled chicken.

At Yakitori Shinohara, the spotlight is on Kokutei, a premium brand of Kuro Satsuma chicken cultivated in Kagoshima. Refined from the “Kokuo” breed, its meat is exceptionally tender, with a deep concentration of flavor. Chef Shinohara is committed to sourcing only what he has personally verified—visiting cheesemakers in Hokkaido, herb growers in Hiroshima, and other producers across Japan to build direct relationships. This dedication extends not only to ingredients but also to the tableware and utensils used in the restaurant.

The wine list features a selection of natural wines, mainly from Burgundy and Italy but also from California, as well as vintage wines. The marriage of premium chicken and wine is definitely worth trying.

Inside the restaurant furnished with warm wood accents, the copper range hood handcrafted by a copper artisan shines brightly over the grill. The main dining room is furnished with an 11-seat counter made of 2000-year-old hinoki cypress wood. In addition, there is a private room seating up to four people. Whether for a date, a business dinner, or a special celebration, Yakitori Shinohara offers an elevated dining experience where guests can savor the very best of premium Japanese chicken.

245333.longDescription:
Take an eight-minute walk from Roppongi Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, and you will find an impressive wooden door on the first floor of a building on a quiet street near the Nishi-Azabu Crossing in the gastronomic neighborhood of Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, with plenty of renowned restaurants. The door leads to merachi, a chic Italian restaurant with a striking combination of stone and wood on the exterior.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Kosuke Sugimoto, who trained at restaurants, both inside and outside of Japan, known for their modern cuisine, such as Ristorante TOKUYOSHI in Milan, Mielcke & Hurtigkarl in Copenhagen, Gaggan in Bangkok, and a one-star restaurant FARO in Ginza, for eight years in total before he opened merachi at the current location in 2021.
Chef Sugimoto creates original dishes by reinterpreting the traditions of Italian cuisine in his own way. He uses different culinary techniques originated from different cultures to offer Italian-inspired dishes only available in Japan. The ingredients are mostly sourced from within Japan, such as mozzarella cheese from KURKKU FIELDS in Kisarazu City, Ashikaga Marc beef from Hasegawa Farm in Tochigi Prefecture, and Mukashi Okina Ariki eggs from Higashi-Matsuyama City in Saitama Prefecture. The eggs delivered fresh with no eggy smell are used to make omelets. Pasta with Brown Mushrooms, made with chicken and mushroom stock and grated mushrooms, is a popular dish that looks simple at a glance but is actually labor- and time-intensive. The pasta menu always has two choices, one of which features fresh pasta handmade right in front of guests.
Chef Sugimoto pours the same enthusiasm into wines as he does into dishes. The wine cellar that guests can enter to select their own drinks is stocked with some 500 bottles of wine, including vintage French wines that are hard to find in Japan and magnum bottles. Wines are paired with dishes, though they are not paired one by one but served at the pace of each guest.

The restaurant boasts tiled walls in a muted shade and a straight counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood. If you take one of the eight seats at the wooden counter in the dining room featuring the warmth of wooden elements, you can watch the chef working in the kitchen. The restaurant is patronized by guests of different ages, ranging from 30-something to 50-something, and often chosen as a place for women to gather and for foodies to enjoy solitary meals.
The restaurant’s name, merachi, is coined from Greek and Italian words to mean “pouring your soul, creativity, love, and passion into something.” There is no way even for professionals who master their field of expertise to enchant their audience without pouring their soul into their works. The word “merachi” describes Chef Sugimoto’s desire for guests to savor the beautiful moments hidden in daily life.
He aims to go beyond offering delicious dishes and make the dining experience at merachi fun and memorable as if at a friend’s home so that he can hear his guests say, “I had a great time!” So, indulge in the dining experience at merachi with your close friends.

245544.longDescription:
A two-minute walk from Gotanda Station, Vierge is a French bistro nestled in a basement in one of Tokyo’s vibrant business districts. The restaurant is helmed by Chef Atsushi Niida, who trained at a renowned restaurant in France. Hailing from Kyoto, he graduated from Tsuji Culinary Institute and went on to study at a satellite campus of the Tsuji Culinary Institute Group in France. He also completed practical training at a renowned three-star restaurant, Georges Blanc, in the eastern French village of Vonnas. After returning to Japan, he further honed his skills under Makoto Mabuchi , the first executive chef of the Westin Osaka, at his restaurant, Gion Carre de M (now permanently closed), and enhanced his career by providing catering for luxury cruise lines and wedding parties and planning afternoon tea menus for hotel guests. Then, in 2024, he opened his own restaurant, Vierge.

Intended to invite guests to enjoy French cuisine in a relaxed, casual atmosphere, Vierge calls itself a bistro, but it is, in fact, much more than that. Especially, the chef’s particularity about ingredients is worth remarking. The vegetables are sourced from Namiki Natural Farm in Katori, Chiba, known for producing special vegetables for chefs, and Ishiwari Farm in Kyoto, which has been visited by many celebrated chefs, including the renowned Chef Alain Ducasse. Among those vegetables, carefully selected seasonal potatoes are featured in the Oeuf Mayonnaise with Truffle, which is a signature dish of Vierge elevated by replacing a boiled egg with a poached egg. The Roasted Inside Round of Yuri Beef is another signature dish featuring a premium beef from Akita, which is famous for its perfect balance of lean meat and savory fat. Not commonly found outside of Akita, this precious meat makes the restaurant a special spot to check out. Another must-try is the Fresh Oysters on the Half Shell, which is available around the year with three sauce options (homemade citrus sauce, cocktail sauce, or original basil mayonnaise).

The wine list offers about 20 labels, including Bordeaux, Bourgogne, Languedoc-Roussillon, and other French wines that captivated the chef during his apprenticeship in France as well as Japanese wines sourced from Tamba Wine (the first winery in Kyoto) and Takahata Winery and Takeda Winery in Yamagata, and popular pairing options (five different Japanese and French wines). The drink menu also offers a wide selection of soft drinks, including homemade ginger ale and grape juice, to meet the different tastes of guests.

The interior is modern with grey and silver tones and yellow accents. The cozy wooden tables (four tables, each seating up to four guests) and counter (seating up to seven guests) in the main dining room and the private dining room (seating up to six guests) make the restaurant a perfect choice for various occasions, from family and friend gatherings and date nights to corporate and business meals and dinners with international guests. Please enjoy exquisite bistro dishes in a relaxed, casual atmosphere at Vierge!

243921.longDescription:
This hidden gem of a Japanese restaurant is nestled in a residential area of Yoyogi-Uehara. The owner, Daisuke Oyaizu, gives warm welcome to every guests and, with his credentials as a Certified Rice Appraiser, pours love beyond measure into his rice dishes.

The main feature of the venue is certainly its rice cooked in earthenware pots, so much so in fact that all of its course menu includes clay pot rice as one of their dishes. Each pot is brought out individually, where it is carefully mixed and served in front of the guests. Of the various types of rice offered, there is one that comes with a particularly high recommendation: ”Milky Queen," a variety created by Showa Imperial Rice Provisioner Koji Aoki. Having been awarded a gold medal in the past in the overall category of the International Contest on Rice Taste Evaluation, this exquisite rice was also awarded a first-place gold medal in the Eighth Annual Japan's Most Delicious Rice Contest. It features an exceptionally good texture when cooked in a clay pot. The moment the lid is opened, the sweet fragrance of the rice spreads with the steam through the air. Coming apart in the mouth with the first bite, the feel of each grain of rice is maintained, resulting in a texture that is eminently pleasant to chew.Taking each and every grain of rice seriously, the preparation done here incorporates modern techniques along with cooking methods in line with centuries of traditional Japanese cuisine. It is the cutting-edge effort of the producer, along with the skill of a rice dealer in rice preparation and management, that makes Okon's clay pot rice what it is. There is an amazing love for Okon's outstanding technique in turning the best of rice into the best of dishes and for the owner's rice that goes into that technique. At Okon, you can find the "real" rice which even the locals rarely get the chance to experience.

The restaurant features a sharply-designed interior with a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. 16 table seats are available in addition to a separate room for eight, and reservations are welcome for larger parties and events. Traditional red rice instead of a cake for special occasions such as family events are special service provided at Okon, the venue is also a great place for a meal to celebrate the precious turning points in your life.

244073.longDescription:
Located in a quiet residential area just three minutes on foot from Yoyogi-Uehara Station on the Odakyu Line, Yoyogi-Uehara Yuu is a Japanese restaurant that specializes in making incredible use of ""now-or-never"" seasonal ingredients. Here is a venue can provide you a calm and relaxing atmosphere, that attracts lots of regular guests from the area and places far away.

The owner, Mr. Imoto, got his start in the cooking world at Ristorante Hamasaki in Minami-Aoyama and went on to learn the arts of Japanese food and sake at Ginza KAN and at Potsura-Potsura in Shibuya. Then, in 2014, he struck out on his own with a strong desire to ""deliver meals with spirits and vegetables carefully selected to embody the philosophy of the chef."" Travelling among a variety of farms, Mr. Imoto listens to the ideas and philosophies behind the vegetables cultivated and selected those that, more than being purely delicious, are also the most authentic. The seasonal ""Chef's Selected Course"" which changes on a weekly basis, makes full use of ""now-or-never"" ingredients taken from the fields to offer a sensory experience of the four seasons.

A further commitment to perfection can be seen in the Japanese sakes storage. Notably, all sakes on offer are of the ""Ouroku"" brand, hailing from Shimane Prefecture. All Ouroku sakes are produced unfiltered and in limited quantities, and Mr. Imoto was fascinated by the philosophy of its creator. Even the same Ouroku exhibits different aspects of its scent and flavor when drunk differently, such as from a sake glass versus a wine glass, giving it incredible versatility and potential.

With both counter and table seating available, the venue allows guests to fully enjoy the cuisine and Japanese sake on offer, whether for group meals with friends, dates, casual dining or business outings.


【Nearby Hotels】
■ Shibuya ""Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel""
■ Shibuya ""Shibuya Excel Hotel Tokyu""
■ Ebisu ""Westin Hotel Tokyo""
■ Futako Tamagawa ""FutakoTamagawa Excel Hotel Tokyu""

-- 【Notice from the restaurant】 We hold pop-ups in Milan several times a year, so there will be days the main chef is not in the store. During lunch time or the period the main chef is in Milan, the 5th generation will be serving. Please confirm the course when making a reservation.

-- A 7-minute walk from Kamata Station in Ota, Tokyo transports diners to Hatsunezushi, a long-established sushi restaurant opened in 1893. It is currently helmed by the fourth generation of the founding family, Chef Katsu Nakaji, who inherited the restaurant after training in Kyoto cuisine and other restaurants for 10 years. His exclusive sushi makes Kamata a hot spot for food connoisseurs. The meal starts with lively introductions by the chef. Regulars have been known to take their seats early to enjoy watching him making sushi rice with vinegar and hot rice straight from the pot cooked over charcoal to prepare for the opening act. The sushi is served in the order that the chef determines to be best, taking into account the temperature of the sushi rice that cools over time to ensure the best harmony between the sushi rice and toppings. The seafood is sourced from a trusted broker who has delivered the best-quality fish and seafood to the restaurant over the past 30 years. The long-standing trust between chef and broker allows the restaurant to offer sushi made with rare and precious seafood, such as wild giant mottled eel and giant abalone. Seasonal specialties are offered, such as sushi topped with soft cod roe and the highest-quality white truffle from Italy (available only in November and December); another popular dish is sushi made with both male and female snow crabs. Guests can also watch the process of live crabs being prepared and then steamed and made into sushi. Hatsunezushi also offers a food and drink pairing menu consisting of seven offerings selected according to the seafood served on the day, mainly featuring a seasonal selection of sake but also including red and white wines. The tea pairing menu is curated in collaboration with a tea roasting master, and includes Yame Gyokuro green tea from Fukuoka as well as Chinese and black teas. The dining space consists of two elegant rooms, each with eight seats. The room “Yama” for dining service features marble, and the room “Umi” for tea service boasts blue stained-glass windows inspired by the ocean. Sushi is served on antique plates dating to the late Edo period in the 19th century, such as Old Imari and Old Kutani ware, as well as handmade pieces by Tomomi Kamoshita, a ceramic artist and a friend of the chef for twenty years. Whether enjoyed with a partner, business clients, or a special solo meal, guests are cordially invited to enjoy exquisite Edomae sushi and a lively performance in the presence of a friendly master chef.
nearestStations: A 7-minute walk from Keikyu Kamata Station on the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line and Keikyu Main Line

245438.longDescription:
In Jinbocho, a neighborhood anchored by office buildings and antique bookstores, Jinbocho Gokita is conveniently located four minutes on foot from Jinbocho Station on the Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and six minutes on foot from JR Suidobashi Station. Hidden in an alley off Suidobashi Nishi-dori Street, this ground-floor restaurant boasts a chic lattice façade to welcome guests.

The restaurant is helmed by Chef Yuto Gokita, whose culinary roots lie in French cuisine. He started his apprenticeship in Japan at the age of 20 and went to France at the age of 25 to hone his culinary skills at restaurants in southern France and Bourgogne. He then returned to Japan in 2012 and became Sous Chef at Chemins in Akasaka and Chef at Cellier and Manoir d'Inno. In 2021, he opened his own restaurant, Jinbocho Gokita, featuring roast chicken, which had been his specialty since he worked at French restaurants.

The kitchen is equipped with two grills, charcoal and wood-fired, to be used for different cooking temperatures. Cooked with a French-inspired sauce created by the experienced French chef and paired with French wines, Jinbocho Gokita’s yakitori (Japanese chicken skewers) are made with Hinai Jidori chicken, which is characterized by its distinctive taste that goes well with any flavor to make a perfect marriage with the sauce. The lean meat skewers are made with squab imported from France. The vegetables are sourced from Karuizawa Salad Farm, which is known for its strongly flavored products.
The prix-fixe menu always includes “Hinai Jidori Chicken Breast with Shrimp Américaine Sauce,” inspired by a traditional French dish of chicken galantine and sauce américaine and reinterpreted in yakitori style. “Tsukune with Bourguignon Butter,” a skewer of ground chicken wrapped with caul fat and grilled with herbal butter, took inspiration from chicken Kiev, a boneless chicken breast rolled with butter and coated with batter consisting of flour, eggs, and breadcrumbs. These combinations of yakitori and French cuisine demonstrate the true talent of Chef Gokita.

The wine list offers some 300 different labels, mainly from France, especially Bourgogne and Bordeaux. The drink menu also includes a versatile selection of Japanese sake that pairs well with the dishes. In addition, prix-fixe meals can be paired with five wines selected to enhance each course.

The Japanese-style wooden interior is adorned with wooden furnishings and a solid cherry countertop. In addition to the eight-seat counter, the main dining room boasts a large dining table that seats up to eight guests. Moreover, there is a private dining room that seats up to six guests. Served on Kutani and antique Imari ware, the food tingles the taste buds of connoisseurs of French cuisine as well as yakitori lovers who want to enjoy great meals with their friends or dates. The private dining room can accommodate children of all ages. A special children’s menu is also available for those reserving in advance. Moreover, English-speaking services are offered by Chef Gokita himself and service staff.
Discover the unique fusion of yakitori and French cuisine and the delightful world of flavors that can be offered only by the experienced French Chef at Jinbocho Gokita!

Located at Jinbo-cho, Tokyo, “Sushi Yoshino” is with a concept of “A Sushi house where you can enjoy both food and dishes”.
Focusing mainly on “Kutani ware”, only using limited instruments such as “Arita-yaki” and “Kyoto-yaki” produce, serving gorgeous cuisine and sushi, together bring you a full-space show.

Chef Keiichi Nishimoto, who graduated in Osaka, got his experiences from training in, Marunouchi and Shimbashi sushi restaurant, finally independent in 2016.
With his perfect skilled craftsmanship, he developed a Chef recommend course with Edo-mae sushi as main, interwoven with original Japanese cuisine.
For example, in the early summer, asparagus would be used as a standard ""Seasonal vegetable slide"", seasonal vegetables are also used in dishes such as ""sesame tofu”.
Sushi vinegar, which can be said the spirits of sushi, are using 7 kinds of blends vinegar from all over the country here, centered on red vinegar, made by Kisaichi brewing in Chiba prefecture. Excellent compatibility with the finish dishes such as Kohada.
Sake cuisine with sushi is sake selected carefully pure rice sake, so you can taste the “pure” in colorful “Kutani” ware.

Inside, there is a single board counter made by Ginkgo wood, and a small area of table seat. A perfect recommended for casual dinner or anniversary celebrations, we could arrange you surprise birthday cake if required.

245423.longDescription:
Located almost in the center of Tokyo, Tachikawa City is an hour’s drive from Haneda Airport. JR Tachikawa Station is a major transportation hub served by many JR lines and a monorail, yet it retains lush landscape including Showa Memorial Park and the Tamagawa River. Just a minute walk from JR Nishi-Kunitachi Station, one stop from JR Tachikawa Station, Auberge TOKITO welcomes guests with the beauty that seems to draw in the surrounding nature as it is.
Mumon-An, the predecessor of Auberge TOKITO, is a long-established ryotei (traditional Japanese restaurant) that was well known in the Tachikawa area. Its history dates back to the early Showa era. As a inn, it offered warm meals and lodging to guests, and after the war, it carved out a long history as a ryotei. Auberge TOKITO, which opened as its successor, retains many of its historic features, including the main gate and garden, while the interior has been modernized and reborn as an auberge. It has a dining room, a tea room, and four guest rooms.
The dining room has 10 counter seats and 22 table seats. The counter offers the dynamism of a chef’s table, and even at the tables, guests receive intimate service as the chefs approach the guests to explain the ingredients. Creating cuisine for both settings are Executive Chef Yoshinori Ishii, General Manager and Head Chef Kenji Okawara, and Head Chef Hiroki Hiyama. A team of seven chefs led by these three prepares the cuisine. After they worked together at a renowned and long-established restaurant in Kyoto, Chef Ishii led the Japanese restaurant UMU London to two stars, while Chef Okawara earned one star for Ito in Kyoto.
“Artisan Cuisine,” Auberge TOKITO’s culinary concept, means that six unique chefs, like a team of artisans, craft the courses. Chefs with a variety of domestic and international careers have assembled to create a novel style of Japanese cuisine that will delight and surprise guests. Chefs take advantage of the relationships they have had with producers and are conscious of capturing the “moments” of the best ingredients available, such as those found in Hokkaido or Kyoto. Furthermore, in cooperation with local producers, a Hokkaido fisherman’s group called Hasshinkai produces kajika-bushi, an alternative to bonito flakes made from typically unused fish that rarely make it to the market. They use such ingredients because they believe “the mission of a restaurant is to create value from things that are not yet known.”
For drinks, sake and wines collected from all over the world are on offer. There is a focus on Japanese producers, not only of sake, but also wine and gin. Alcohol pairings are also on offer. Wineries in Hokkaido, Yamagata, Nagano, and other regions are used extensively by the chefs because of the trust they have built with them.
The dining room, renovated from the Mumon-An days, is modernized with many natural materials, such as wood, stone, and exposed-aggregate plaster walls, while retaining its historical dignity. Most of the pottery was fired by Mr. Ishii using soil from Mumon-An and charcoal ash collected from cooking. The counter is made of Japanese cypress, and the tables in the hall are made of walnut. All are subdued materials whose depth and flavor are enhanced by the changes they undergo. In addition to the counter and hall, there are three private rooms each with space for four guests. Children must be at least 16 years old and must be able to have the same meals as adults. Chef Ishii himself can explain the dishes in English for international guests. It’s suitable for dates and dining with close friends, as well as gatherings of foodies.
“Toki” used in the restaurant's name means time and crested ibis, a bird representative of Japan. Like the feathers of a crested ibis, which shine in a variety of colors and have no fixed color, or like its changing colors, the world view of the restaurant is created by the chefs’ varied aesthetic senses, while embracing constant change. Why not visit the Auberge TOKITO for a taste of that novelty?

244443.longDescription:
Tachikawa is a town in the suburbs of Tokyo lined with commercial facilities and office buildings and crowded with many eating and drinking establishments. A 5-minute walk away from the bustling station, "Sushi Kitamura" sits in a quiet spot. The owner, Mr. Naoki Kitamura, began his training in sushi restaurants at the age of 15, built up experience working in restaurants in Shinjuku and Meguro and as the second-in-command at Conrad Tokyo’s Kazahana until the time was ripe in 2016 to set up on his own. Exquisite sushi made possible by many years of experience have earned him a solid reputation, and sushi lovers from neighboring cities and even the heart of the metropolis seek out this famous yet hidden-away restaurant.

For the vinegared rice that forms the basis of sushi, he uses red Junmai-shu sake vinegar made from an ancient rice variety, which gives it a refreshing taste. The rice is the select "Tsuyahime" variety from Yamagata, with its large, distinct grains that have umami flavor and sweetness. He is very particular about where he buys each and every ingredient, and his tuna is from Hichou, one of the most famous tuna wholesalers at the Tsukiji market. Also, he orders seasonal ingredients directly from suppliers all over the country, such as red sea urchin, bigfin reef squid, and tilefish from Fukuoka, and purple sea urchin and barfin flounder from Hakodate. And to the carefully selected seafood, he adds his personal touch to bring out the deliciousness in his sushi. He also wants his customers to enjoy traditional Edo-mae style sushi, which requires considerable time and effort to produce such specialties as gizzard shad, sea bream, clams, and boiled conger eel.

The Chef’s Choice Course consists of the delicate flavor of white fish sashimi intertwined with the rice and other tidbits to create contrasts. He monitors the speed at which his guests eat and drink and serves them snacks and sushi with perfect timing. There are always about 10 kinds of sake available, served in quantities from as small as 90cc, so that various kinds can be combined with the different dishes. The hostess, who is qualified as a sake sommelier, also makes suggestions tailored to the preferences of the guests. Refreshing white wines such as Chablis and Champagne are available. One of the charms of Sushi Kitamura is that it allows non-drinkers to be able to enjoy their meal without alcohol, such as providing pickled vegetable dishes as snacks rather than the delicacies that go with sake.

The only seating is 6 seats at the counter, which is made of Japanese cypress. The chopping board is placed in a position higher than the counter so that customers can see the chef at work, creating a sense of a live performance. The relaxed configuration of the seating means you can be intoxicated to your heart’s content with Mr. Kitamura’s sushi.

■This restaurant is Not the branch of  "Sushi Kitamura" in Nishi-Azabu.

244326.longDescription:
Approximately 15-minute from Shinjuku, the restaurant is located in Nishi-Ogikubo, in an area that attracts a lot of foodies. Sushi Marafuku is a popular sushi restaurant differs itself from other similar establishments through its unique research into matured sushi. It is a sushi restaurants where you not only can find local customers but also fans from all over the city and surrounding regions. 

Mr. Isayama Yutaka grew up in his parent’s long-established sushi restaurant in Tokyo and Higashi-Nagasaki. At the age of 25 he was trained at a sushi restaurant in Tokyo, and in October 2011, he took over the family business and opened Sushi Marufuku in Nishi-Ogikubo, Tokyo. The restaurant offers not only fish, but also properly prepared sushi, which has been the idea since the restaurant opened, and adds to its original charm. 

The fish that is used for sushi is sourced from a famous fish dealer market in the Goto Islands. Also, depending on the season, a rare sea urchin and a special type of tuna, called Yamako tuna, is delivered directly from fishermen in Hokkaido. Depending on the size and fat content of the fish, the amount of vinegar, salt and the maturing period changes. For example, sliced fishes such as Kohada is often held for 2 to 3 days after being caught, however at Sushi Marufuku, fishes are stored for at least 5 days or more, removing the vinegar and salt, leaving only the good flavor of the fish.  Also, all white fish meat is matured for more than 20 days to a maximum of 1 month, depending on the fish. The sushi rice is a mixture of 2 kinds of rice, Akita and Niigata, and blended with 4 types of red vinegars. 

The menu is made up of recommended courses by the chef, starting with matured sushi, followed by sliced fish. The second half of the course offers a blend of sushi and side dishes with a thick taste, like shellfish.  One of the many pleasures of Sushi Marufuku is that the proprietress, who is qualified as a sommelier, suggests sake that matches well with your dish. There are around 25 kinds of Japanese sake prepared at all times. The Hiroshima Houken is highly recommended. It is also a sake that the general manager likes, and goes well with the food.

The counter, made of hinoki wood from Kyoto, is fitted with seats for up to 10 people. The walls of the restaurant features Toyama craftsmanship, and the ceiling is slightly lowered, creating a calm and relaxing setting. The number of great sushi restaurants in gourmet-rich Tokyo has just increased by one.

244663.longDescription:
“Matsuzaka Ushi (Beef) Kaiseki Shin”, located close to the landmark "Toranomon Hills" in Toranomon, Tokyo, an area currently undergoing redevelopment, reopened on November 16th. The new head chef, Ryushi Yamamoto, has worked at many restaurants in Japan, Europe, America and China. He previously served as head chef at a members-only restaurant, and at a restaurant in Tokyo that is an offshoot of a 3-star restaurant from New York.

They serve "Matsuzaka beef", a top-class brand of Japanese beef, with the theme of "Onkochishin" (old wisdom), expressed in an innovative way, incorporating the essence of traditional Japanese cuisine with French techniques. Chateaubriand and sirloin of Matsuzaka beef are slowly heated at the just the right temperature and grilled over charcoal. Fresh Matsuzaka beef giblets, which are rare in Tokyo, are made into creative Japanese dishes using pure water from the Nobi Plain and pesticide-free vegetables, grown on fertile land. It is innovative, fusion-Japanese cuisine made with the sweetness of Matsuzaka beef, wholesome vegetables, and the seasonal seafood of Edo.

What amplifies the deliciousness of this "beef kaiseki" is the carefully selected sake. They serve French, Italian and American wine by the glass to match the dishes. They also have vintage Japanese whiskeys like "Yamazaki" and "Hakushu", which are difficult to get. Another attraction is the restaurant’s selection of rare sakes which you can enjoy by the glass, such as "Jikon" and "Zaku", ordered from Mie Prefecture, the hometown of Matsuzaka beef. They also have non-alcoholic drinks made by the chef for those who prefer not to drink alcohol.

The interior of the restaurant has an inspiring atmosphere, based on art nouveau. There are 12 counter seats and 3 private rooms that can accommodate 3~12 people. The restaurants aims to meet food preference requests and has services in English and Chinese, to accommodate guests from overseas and for business situations, allowing you to entertain guests with peace of mind. In an international area such as Toranomon, you will definitely want to enjoy the unique Japanese food experience of "Matsuzaka beef x Japanese sake".
nearestStations: 9 min. walk from Toranomon Exit 1 on Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, 7 min. walk from Toranomon Hills Station on Hibiya Line, 7 min. walk from Onarimon Station on Mita Line

Shinbashi Sasada is located on a side street not far from the Toranomon business district. Guests will be greeted warmly in this neat and cozy restaurant which has 8 seats at the counter and two private rooms with tables. 

Every day Chef Sasada purchases quality ingredients from trusted vendors in Tsukiji to prepare culinary masterpieces. Specifically to mention are the vegetables and fish that are cooked in an excellent broth whose subtle flavors leave a lasting impression. The ingredients of each dish are brought to their fullest potential and the rice served at the end is cooked to perfection in an earthenware pot. This restaurant is amazing at any season, with many regular guests from the beginning of the store opening coming back again and again. Sasada is a place to entertain and dine with important clients or visit with your close friends.

245503.longDescription:
Situated in Nishi Shinbashi, Aragawa stands out as one of the best steakhouses in Japan for its supreme charcoal-broiled beefsteak. Founded under the name of Shinbashi Tamura-cho Aragawa in Shinbashi 3-chome in 1967, the steakhouse was relocated to its current location in 2009. This main location is complemented by Gorio, a branch that opened in Ginza 8-chome in 1984, and ARAGAWA, another branch launched in London, the United Kingdom, in 2023 to captivate the taste buds of food lovers around the world with its sophisticated charcoal-broiled beefsteak. 

Aragawa features Tajima beef exclusively raised for the steakhouse by Okazaki Bokujo and Nishizawa Bokujo in Shiga and Hyogo, respectively, where only purebred Tajima cattle are selected for fattening and raised in a strictly controlled environment.  Among them, premium nulliparous heifers fattened for as long as 40 months or more are supplied for processing. Thus, the precious Tajima beef suitable for Aragawa’s signature charcoal-broiled beefsteak is carefully selected taking into account their breed, quality, monthly age, and overall balance.
The specially selected beef is simply seasoned with salt and pepper and broiled in a furnace kiln with the highest quality Kishu Binchotan charcoal to bring out the best flavor in it. This supreme Tajima beefsteak stars in the full course meal where each course, from appetizers to desserts, tells a story of the seasons through flavors curated by a duo of chefs.  The whole salmon slowly smoked over high heat in a kiln has been one of the most popular appetizers since the restaurant’s founding. In addition, as the sizzling aroma of the steak and the elegant flavor of the smoked fish stimulate cravings for wine, Aragawa offers a great selection of 200 to 300 premium wines, mostly from Bourgogne and Bordeaux in France, including Domaine De La Romanée-Conti and First Growth Bordeaux wines.

The dining area, seating up to 22 guests, has maintained its classy design since its inception, with Nishijin-ori tapestries crafted by Tatsumura Art Textile in Kyoto, Swedish chandeliers, substantial cherry wood chairs, and tables set with Noritake tableware. Moreover, the restaurant’s name, Aragawa, taken from a novel by Honoré de Balzac, a brilliant French writer also known for his passion for food, adds an academic touch to the setting. Please visit Aragawa and indulge in its supreme beefsteak and elegant setting with your loved ones.
nearestStations: 1 minute walk from Onarimon Station, A5 exit, Toei Mita Line

243823.longDescription:
“Tempura Osaka,” in Nishi-Shinbashi, is 5-minute walk from “Toranomon station.”  The owner, Mr. Akihiro Osaka, has experiences in “Kanda Sarugakucho, Tenmasa” and “Tempura Tsujimura” before opening “Tempura Osaka” in June, 2001.   

The tempura omakase course, focusing mainly on fishes, is made with the concept of “fry the seasonal ingredient at its best condition.” Mr. Osaka goes to the Toyosu Market every day for the best ingredients, such as shrimps from Nagasaki Prefecture. He not only uses Edomae fishes, including whitings and big-eyed flathead, but also fishes that are rare in Tokyo’s tempura restaurants, such as splendid alfonsino, pufferfish, largehead hairtail, and sea bream. In addition, edible wild plants in Spring, young sweetfish in Summer, and the fried chestnut made with homemade syrup are very popular, many guest would visit every year for these!


The tempura is lightly fried in a mellow blend of cottonseed and sesame oils, making it crispy but not oily. Enjoy the tempura with grated raw Daikon and lemon, along with Pakistani rock salt, which is carefully-selected and recommended by Mr. Osaka. The alcohol selection focuses on white wine and champagne from France and popular sake “Retsu Junmai Ginjo-Shu” and “Kirinzan KARAKUCHI,” all pairs well with the tempura. 

The 9-seat counter is made with the 200-year old cedar wood. The 75cm depth ceiling is wide enough to have a relaxing space. We recommend this tempura restaurant for anniversary celebration and any private use!
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Toranomon station (Exit 1), Ginza Line

244223.longDescription:
In a quiet area near the Tokyo Metropolitan Government building just out of West exit of Shinjuku Station, Edo sushi restaurant Shinjuku Sushi Iwase is located. Drawing inspiration from the famous Sushisho, Chef Kenji Iwase speaks of his enthusiasm for going after the sushi culture of Shinjuku.

Unlike many who aspire to be a sushi chef from a young age, Chef Iwase discovered “sushi” and began his training after the age of 20. He became independent in 2012 after polishing his skills in various well-known restaurants which are part of the Sushisho group, beginning with Sushi Hide in Yotsuya, to Sushisho Masa in Nishi Azabu, and Aoyama’s Sushi-ko. “I want this restaurant to be a fun place. I want guests to enjoy chatting while eating sushi”, says Iwase; his omakase menu style consists of nigiri sushi and a side dish brought out alternately. Many visits to enjoy the Kasugo fish (young seabream) and Anago (salt-water eel) nigiri, which is a staple in the omakase menu.

Rice vinegar or red/plum vinegar is used depending on the seafood used on the sushi, the staple Japanese sake is Koriyama, Fukushima’s Odayaka, as well as 10 other types of sake, to suit the season. The restaurant has a counter made of plain and unfinished wood, with 9 seats, where you can watch Chef Iwase’s skills from all angles. Sushi shared with friends, colleagues and that special someone is exceptional. You can easily spend a blissful time here, and even forget that you are in Shinjuku.

244203.longDescription:
It is relatively hard to have authentic Edomae-style sushi especially in Shinjuku. Usually, customers can only enjoy sushi in hotel restaurants, but Sushi Sagane in Nishi-Shinjuku is an ideal sushi restaurant there. Even though it is a small restaurant with only 6 counter-seats, it is very cozy and neat. There is a refreshing space with sakura motif behind the sliding door. The young chef's sushi making skill is so eye-catching that customers will forget about the hectic city. 

The restaurant was opened in 2011. In spring 2017, Mr. Hideki Yamaguchi took over the restaurant and it was reopened after renewal. After graduated from a culinary institute, Mr. Yamaguchi was trained in a sushi restaurant in Tokyo for ten years. "No music is played in the restaurant because I also want the customers to enjoy the sound of slicing the fish," said Mr. Yamaguchi. He wants to promote the tradition and attractive point of Edo-style sushi to the young generation and foreign guests.

He gets the ingredients from Tsukiji market. The signature dishes are boiled prawn, eel and dry calabash from chef's hometown Tochigi. 
His homemade cuisine matches well with sake.The sushi rice is made right before customers arrive, it is cooked in a traditional rice cooker and mixed with rice vinegar and red vinegar. He uses pesticide-free 「Fuji vinegar」 from Iio Jozo Vinegar Brewery in Kyoto. 
In addition, he also uses dishes that match with the cuisine, such as glass and ceramics. "I want customers to think of our restaurant when they want to have sushi. " said the owner. It is a sushi restaurant with many young sensibilities.

243979.longDescription:
An Italian restaurant located in Koganei, approximately 40 minutes from Shinjuku, featuring a beautiful Japanese building and garden.

This fantastic restaurant was born from the refurbishment of a private Japanese residence located on a vast site of approximately 1,000 square meters — the former home of the Osawa family dating back to approximately 500 years ago across 36 generations. The exterior of the building features a traditional Japanese design. However, once you take a step inside, you will be met by a beautiful interior that blends Japanese and western styles with a wide range of antique furniture — a space of great relaxation for enjoying delicious meal. From the main dining area, you can look across a carefully maintained Japanese garden. The garden has been landscaped to resemble the Tenryuji temple in Kyoto, featuring beautiful plum blossoms from a 300-year-old tree in the spring, colorful hydrangeas in the summer, vividly-colored Japanese maple trees in the fall, and stunning snowy landscapes in the winter, offering truly unique views in every season.

The food is prepared by Yukio Sato, a chef who has trained at renowned restaurants such as the Italian world gourmet guide award restaurant Sadler. His mission is to offer guests highly original dishes based on his much-loved Italian tradition and culture, augmented with a touch of Japanese essence. In recent years, there have been many guests flying here from abroad for special wedding celebrations.
nearestStations: 20-minute walk from Musashi-koganei station, JR Chuo Line

245540.longDescription:
A 10-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Sumiyoshi or Kiyosumi Shirakawa Station, Sushi Kurofune is located on the first floor of a building in the quiet residential area of Ogibashi. Leading the kitchen of the restaurant, Chef Syota Ito offers meticulously crafted seasonal dishes and nigiri sushi. He started his culinary career at a kaiseki restaurant in Mie Prefecture and then moved to Restaurant Yonemura, a renowned French restaurant, to work at its main location in Kyoto. While working at the Ginza location of the same restaurant, he had a life-changing encounter with Edomae sushi, impressed by the meticulous process of aging and curing fish with salt or vinegar. To master the Edomae techniques, he trained at Sushi Ginza Seamon and served as Chef at another sushi restaurant in Akasaka. Then, he finally opened his own restaurant, Sushi Kurofune, in 2021.

The restaurant’s name, Kurofune, which means “black ship” in Japanese, reflects the Chef’s commitment to impressing and wowing food lovers in Ogibashi by delivering exquisite sushi to this untapped neighborhood, like the “Black Ships” of Commodore Matthew Perry, which jolted and opened Japan to the West. The Chef’s choice prix-fixe menu consists of 12 pieces of nigiri sushi, complemented by five to six seasonal dishes and followed by a Japanese omelet, rolled sushi, a bowl of soup, and dessert—each crafted with passion. His commitment to quality is also evident in how each ingredient is sourced. Bluefin tuna is purchased from Hicho, one of Toyosu Market’s most respected tuna wholesalers. The finest fatty tuna, carefully selected by Hicho for its softness, flavor, and fat content, is precisely filleted and turned into nigiri sushi. With a buttery texture, the fatty tuna instantly melts in the mouth together with the sushi rice. It is so delicious that it has even shattered the concept of tuna among the guests. Prawns are sourced from a specialized wholesaler, Kamefuku, at Toyosu Market. Sushi rice is made from Haenuki, a premium rice from Yamagata, which is purchased from Okome no Funakubo in Kiyosumi Shirakawa, a rice shop renowned for its high-quality rice. Delivered ready for sushi, the rice is seasoned with a blend of two varieties of red vinegar from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing and a pinch of salt to cleanse the palate. Nori seaweed is directly delivered from Kuboi Noriten in Omori Higashi, Ota City, and wasabi is shipped from Sugiyama Farm in Umegashima, Shizuoka City. All the other ingredients are also carefully selected for their fine quality.

The sake list offers about 15 selections, including classic options, such as Tanaka Rokugo from Fukuoka and Hakurakusei from Miyagi, among which Chef Ito chooses the best sake for each guest according to their preferences and menu selections. The restaurant also offers sparkling and white wines from Fukagawa Winery Tokyo in neighboring Monzen Nakacho. The plain wooden counter adds a touch of freshness to the cozy, wooden interior of the restaurant, which only has counter seating (seating up to four guests) but caters to various occasions. Please book the premium seats and enjoy the elaborate flavors of Sushi Kurofune with your family or friends.

244011.longDescription:
Ristorante Drammatico is a famous restaurant located 15 minutes from Shinjuku. Thanks to the support of the local residents, it has been based in the area of Ogikubo, on the Chuo Line, for over 20 years. In 2015, the restaurant moved to a residential area closer to the station to embark on a fresh start. As it is set slightly back from the main road, the restaurant offers a bright and comfortable dining space. The first floor is comprised primarily of counter seats, and the second floor offers a comfortable dining area with some private rooms. 

Some guests are even known to have been regulars for 20 years. Its specialty is Seafood. The seafood prepared here is carefully selected by the chef who is known for his love of food markets. The seafood he selects is fresh enough to rival those used at sushi or traditional Japanese kaiseki restaurants. The dish most worthy of mention is the Handmade Pasta with Seasonal Seafood. With this dish, guests are sure to enjoy the greatest happiness, as they experience the perfect combination between Italian food and fresh seafood sourced from Tsukiji. And of course, the best pair for a dish like this is wine. The chef offers a personally-selected range of approximately 300 wines, with a focus on natural ingredients. On special occasions, the restaurant can also provide special surprises like the serving of a whole cake. 

This restaurant is highly recommended for sharing a delicious meal with friends and family, or entertaining important business guests.

245085.longDescription:
Steps from Otemachi Station, easily accessible from Tokyo’s financial district, the Imperial Palace, and commercial facilities, PIGNETO opened in September 2020 atop the Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi, a hotel housed in Otemachi One. This chic Italian restaurant is designed to allow diners to experience the joy of abbondanza (living a life of plenty) in a relaxed atmosphere as if they were at home with family.

Specialty pizza chef Alessandro Luca de Leo, hailing from Naples, brings the traditional art of pizza making, handed down for generations, to the restaurant.

At this stylish restaurant, guests enjoy not only panoramic views of Tokyo’s epicenter, including the Imperial Palace Gardens and distant views of Mt. Fuji on sunny days, but also a dazzling variety of traditional Italian dishes prepared from seasonal ingredients in a relaxed environment. Each authentic Italian dish, such as pizzas by chef Alessandro, and T-bone steak cooked with a Toscana oven, are impressive by any measure. Diners can take a seat beside one of the four open kitchens and enjoy the theatre of the chefs at work.

The Italian-leaning wine list offers wines made from hand-picked grapes at boutique wineries in Italy as well as a selection of free flow drinks, while food and wine pairings elevate the experience further.

PIGNETO has 105 seats in a spacious high-ceilinged dining room with large windows that allow natural light to enter freely, and 40 seats on an outdoor terrace (only available on sunny days from April to October). The discreet monochrome interior invites lingering and intimate conversations. Guests are invited to enjoy seasonal Italian dishes prepared by experienced chefs at PIGNETO, a restaurant perfect for a range of occasions, such as business dinners, dates, and intimate family meals.
nearestStations: Directly connected to the underground passage from the C4 and C5 exits of Otemachi Station on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, Tozai Line, Hanzomon Line and Toei Mita Line

244593.localizedAddress: B1, Otemachi Place West Tower, 2-3-1, Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
244593.longDescription:
The Roppongi bistro "RRR" is known for its top-class Japanese Black Wagyu Beef, including Japan's world-famous Kobe Beef, and premium wine offered at reasonable prices. It is this restaurant that opened a new flagship location, "RRR Otemachi," in 2018. It is located in Otemachi PLACE, a commercial center in Otemachi, one of Japan's leading business districts.

The interior design is inspired by the concept of a Manhattan, New York steakhouse. Guests pass through the entrance and bar into a black-themed, stylish dining atmosphere. In the center of the restaurant is the open kitchen and the Wagyu beef cellar, and behind it is the dining area with table seating and a brick wine cave-style design, offering a sophisticated and classy atmosphere combining bustle and relaxation. 

The venue seats a total of 42 guests, with seating for 38 in the open dining area in addition to a single room seating four and terrace seating as well. Offering pairings of Kobe beef and premium wine ideal for casually enjoying on a nice day, "RRR Otemachi" is perfect not only for business dining but also casual dining with the family, date night, anniversaries or just about any other scenario, promising guests a blissful experience.
nearestStations: A 1-minute walk from Hanzomon Station, Exit A4,A5(Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line)

245084.localizedAddress: 39F, Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo Otemachi, 1-2-1, Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
245084.longDescription:
The Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo Otemachi, a five-star hotel located within a walking distance from Tokyo Station and directly connected to Otemachi Station with easy access to many of the city’s best attractions, houses The Lounge on the 39th floor. This sumptuous establishment offers afternoon tea and sweet treats, in an open space with large windows that provide sweeping views of Tokyo Imperial Palace Gardens.
The Lounge’s popular afternoon tea is served in three courses – savories, sweets, and scones. The afternoon tea menu also includes a selection of traditional Japanese teas, caffeine-free coffees, and original mocktails to meet the preferences of each guest’s mood.
The modern, luxurious space is decorated with artworks created by contemporary Japanese artists and furnished with tables and sofas which collectively seat up to 64 guests in comfort. During the evening’s magic hours, the establishment’s floor-to-ceiling windows offer romantic views that dramatically shift with the passage of time from sunset to night.
Guests are invited to enjoy confections created by a skilled and sophisticated pastry chef in an elegant, relaxed setting at The Lounge, perfect for a variety of occasions including business dinners, dates, and intimate meals with family and friends.
nearestStations: Directly connected to the underground passage from the C4 and C5 exits of Otemachi Station on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, Tozai Line, Hanzomon Line and Toei Mita Line

245083.localizedAddress: 39F, Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo Otemachi, 1-2-1, Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
245083.longDescription:
A contemporary French restaurant, est opened in September 2020 atop the Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi, directly connected to Otemachi Station in Tokyo’s business district. They serve innovative and contemporary French cuisine inspired by their deep knowledge of terroir in Japan.  And in the 2026 edition of the World-renowned Gourmet Guide, for five consecutive years the chef de cuisine of the one-starred est, Guillaume Bracaval, and his team not only provide guests with memorable, high-quality dinners, but also organize and operate menus that are always environmentally conscious.

Born and raised in a small village in northern France, Bracaval was greatly influenced by his garden and farm. From an early age, had a love and respect for food making and was delighted to see mother kneading, mixing, roasting, baking bread and sweets in the kitchen. This became the foundation for his later career. His childhood passion for food and cooking led him to Paris, where today Bracaval serves innovative French cuisine at the "est" of the Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi, inspired by his deep respect for Japanese terroir ingredients. Brakavall himself visits various parts of Japan and does not compromise on the supply of food for his kitchen, including fresh fish caught by fishermen in Kyushu and more than 50 types of citrus grown on farms in Wakayama. The menu at "est" is made with plenty of seafood and mountain produce, and is a wonderful blend of French techniques and Japanese craftsmanship.
The restaurant received the Best of Award of Excellence at Restaurant Awards 2025, presented by globally influential Wine Spectator of the United States. The est offers 530 wines that are strong in Burgundy, Bordeaux and Japanese wines. The sommelier team will select your own special wine according to your taste and food from a wide wine list.

The restaurant's interior is decorated with classic French and Japanese elements, with attention to detail in materials and traditional craftsmanship, creating an elegant and The restaurant offers 72 seats at tables in a refined space.

Perched on the 39th floor with stunning views of the city skyline both day and night, est is a perfect place to enjoy an exceptional time while celebrating anniversaries, dining with a partner, and entertaining both business clients and guests from abroad.
nearestStations: Directly connected to the underground passage from the C4 and C5 exits of Otemachi Station on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, Tozai Line, Hanzomon Line and Toei Mita Line

243929.longDescription: -- We are currently not accepting reservations or waiting lists through Pocket Concierge. Please contact the restaurant directly for reservations and inquiries. -- The popular Yakiniku restaurant "Shichirin" in Minowa reopened in Ichigaya under the name "Sumibi Yakiniku Nakahara." Without being particular about the brand, Sumibi Yakiniku Nakahara selects only the highest quality Japanese Black Wagyu beef and uses only the most delicious parts of each section. The most popular items on the menu is the "Legendary Wagyu tongue". You will be hard pressed to find a restaurant that satisfies meat lovers more than this one. ■Counter Seating A separate seating fee of 4,840 yen (including tax and service charge) will be charged for counter seating. And,Children under 16 years old are not allowed to sit at the counter. ■Some customers have mistakenly come to our restaurant for Sumibi Yakiniku Fuchioka. Please be careful when you visit us. Featured Article: "Sumibi Yakiniku Nakahara" -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 6 to 10 people. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? The private dining room offers table(s) and chairs (Western style). ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room(s). ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customizations for vegetarian, vegan or low calories. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children. Unfortunately, we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Are menus available in other languages? Unfortunately, we only offer our menu in Japanese.

244970.longDescription:
37 Steakhouse & Bar is an authentic steakhouse that offers prime steaks that rival those of steakhouses in New York and other top locations.

The recommended dishes include the thick-cut porterhouse steak from Akagi beef, raised in Gunma Prefecture and aged for 21 days, as well as the ribeye steak from Black Angus cattle, which has a perfect balance of lean meat and fat. You can enjoy these at a reasonable price that breaks the stereotype of what you’d expect to pay at a high-end steakhouse. The wine selection is carefully curated, focusing on wines from California and Australia. The bar area is also available for those who just want to drop in for a drink.

In spring, you can enjoy the cherry blossoms of Roppongi Sakurazaka, and in winter, the illuminations of Roppongi Keyakizaka Street. This has been well received since it opened in 2010. There is one private room available (for 4 to 24 people), making it ideal for family gatherings, meals with friends or colleagues, business meetings, dates, or entertaining clients. You can savor dynamic steaks while experiencing the changing seasons.

244821.localizedAddress: 1F, Roppongi Hills Roppongi Keyakisaka-Street, 6-12-4, Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244821.longDescription:
The original Jean-Georges is an upscale three-star French restaurant opened by famed French chef Jean Georges Vongerichten in New York. The chef’s signature French cuisine is now offered at Jean-Georges Tokyo in Roppongi Hills. Having trained at a three-star restaurant, chef Jean-Georges was inspired by his travels in Asia to open his own restaurant, revolutionizing traditional French cuisine with the aromas and flavors of the East. Subsequently, each of his 39 restaurants worldwide has garnered acclaim from critics and gourmets.

The first Jean-Georges location in Japan is helmed by Executive Chef Ryoichi Mochizuki. Officially appointed as the culinary ambassador to Japan, the former chef of Union Square Tokyo and Terres de Truffes now brings his culinary flair and expertise to Jean-Georges Tokyo, offering refined French cuisine infused with an ingenious blend of spices and herbs. In order to offer dishes of the highest quality, each ingredient is sourced from reliable producers with personal ties to the restaurant. The chef’s most iconic dish, Scramble Egg Caviar, is also served as a specialty at Jean-Georges Tokyo; as with the chef’s New York flagship, the dish features fluffy scrambled eggs served in an eggshell topped with caviar and infused with a hint of vodka. A selection of tasting menus are offered, along with dedicated vegetarian dishes that showcase the finest seasonal Japanese produce. 

The wine list offers 200 bottles from chef Jean-Georges’ home region of Alsace, Champagne, and Bourgogne, as well as New World wines from California and Chile. The soft drink menu includes cold-pressed vegetable juices and home-made cocktails. The restaurant also offers wine pairings and non-alcohol pairing for its flavorful dishes.

The interior is adorned with marble and curtains woven from traditional Japanese paper threads and laces to add a sense of luxury and space. The restaurant has 14 counter seats on the first floor and a private chandelier room with 6 seats on the second floor. The first floor boasts a unique Japanese-style layout with a marble-clad counter facing the open kitchen, which chef Jean-George favors because it allows guests to enjoy watching the food being prepared, further enriching the dining experience. Each beautifully plated dish is presented on original plates as those used at the main location in New York to welcome guests into the world of Jean-Georges.

Explore the renowned chef’s world through his innovative, flavorful French cuisine and wines in an atmospheric modern dining space at Jean-Georges Tokyo, perfect for special date nights, anniversaries, and business dinners.
nearestStations: A 7-minutes walk from Roppongi Station Roppongi Hills Exit of Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line

245506.longDescription:
A five-minute walk from Roppongi-itchome Station, KOBAYASHI is located in the first basement of a building tucked away in a back street, opened by Chef Takeshi Kobayashi, who has stolen the show many times with his innovative Chinese cuisine, to take his culinary exploration to the next level. Graduating from Tsuji Culinary Institute in Osaka, he served as a lecturer at the school for eight years and honed his practical skills at a renowned Chinese restaurant, Chikuro Sanbou, in Kichijoji before he opened Mitamachi Momonoki in Mita, Minato-ku, Tokyo, in 2005.  His unique approach to Chinese cuisine gained attention and popularity and led his restaurant to retain its starred status for years. In 2020, he relocated the restaurant to Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho and renamed it Akasaka Momonoki. Then, he resigned from the restaurant in 2023 and opened a new restaurant named after himself, KOBAYASHI, in June 2024.

Believing in an old Chinese saying that “peaches and plums do not talk, yet a path is formed beneath them” (meaning delicious food naturally attracts people), Chef Kobayashi carries on the culinary journey of evolution and revolution, diving into the history of Chinese cuisine and yet stepping out in pursuit of his own style, which he calls “New KOBAYASHI Chinese cuisine.”  The “ULTRA K” menu, exclusively served at the eight-seat counter, invites guests on a gastronomic journey of evolution, offering multiple courses of pioneering dishes, such as “KOBAYASHI & NUMAMOTO” Sichuan Boiled Beef, featuring Takamori Wagyu Beef from Iwakuni, Yamaguchi, carefully selected by Meat Specialist Akinori Numamoto, and “KOBAYASHI Special XO Sauce ULTRA style” Ajillo, consisting of Ise lobster and clams stir-fried in XO sauce and sizzled in untoasted sesame oil. Meanwhile, the menu exclusive to the private rooms (five rooms) is an invitation to a journey of revolution, offering multi-course meals featuring the chef’s specialty dishes, such as Chinese Fried Rice with Dried Scallops, Chicken Noodles, and Deep-fried Eggplant with Japanese Pepper and Chili. The wine list curated by Chef Kobayashi, who is well versed in wines, offers an excellent selection of 1,000 wines, mainly from France. In particular, wine pairings are recommended for guests looking for a truly special dining experience. There are also tea pairings featuring precious Chinese teas from Taiwan.

The enticingly primitive stone signboard and the roughly hewn staircase descending to the restaurant create an ambience like you were at the entrance of a forest. This restaurant landscape, designed by Landscape Architect Junsuke Masui, truly represents the culinary world of Chef Kobayashi. Please indulge in this enchanted space as well as Chef Kobayashi’s innovative dishes that break free from traditional Chinese cuisine with your friends who share your gastronomic passion.
nearestStations: 5 minutes walk from Roppongi 1-Chome Station on the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line

243780.longDescription:
Odajima, where you can take a step away from the bustling streets of Roppongi and discover the quiet charm of a small Japanese restaurant tucked away in the neighborhood. Behind the curtain of noren is a warm, intimate space run solely by the chef-owner. 

The founder, Minoru Odajima, returned to Japan after three years of training in France to open “Kappo Arisugawa,” eventually relocating to Roppongi in 1998. Challenging the traditional notion of pairing Japanese cuisine solely with sake, he became a pioneer in promoting “Japanese cuisine with wine.” 
In the fall of 1997, Minoru became the first in Japan to receive the prestigious Chevalier du Tastevin from the Burgundy Wine Association.
Today, his son, Daisuke Odajima, has taken the helm, working to spread his father’s concept of pairing Japanese cuisine with wine to the world.

A certified sommelier by the Japan Sommelier Association, Daisuke deepened his knowledge of wine in southern Italy’s Puglia region in 2002 and Burgundy, France, in 2003.
Each morning, he carefully selects seasonal fish and vegetables from markets like Tsukiji, crafting a menu that celebrates the simplicity and freedom of Japanese cuisine. 
His dishes are designed to create a space that guests will want to return to.

Delicate Japanese dishes featuring seasonal ingredients are paired with a curated selection of wines.
According to Daisuke, the key to perfect pairing lies in balancing “aroma and acidity.” The restaurant offers an 8-course omakase menu accompanied by a wine list of over 80 varieties, inviting diners to indulge in the harmonious marriage of Japanese cuisine and wine.

The interior is adorned with paintings by a French artist who was a close friend of Minoru during his time in France, while the placemats feature Minoru’s colorful illustrations of French cityscapes.
While maintaining a homely atmosphere, Odajima offers a uniquely special experience. Conversations with the owner across the counter are an exclusive delight. Perfect for business entertainment, dates, or simply for younger guests seeking new discoveries through wine, Odajima is a must-visit destination for anyone eager to experience the innovative pairing of Japanese cuisine and wine.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Roppongi station (Exit 2), Hibiya Line

April 2016 saw the birth of a new fixture in Chinese cuisine in Tokyo: ""Kohou,"" a counter-style restaurant. 

The menu consists entirely of ""chef's choice"" courses. It is a dazzling gastronomic journey offering the ability to sample carefully-arranged combinations of dishes. The ability of the young chef to blend elements of tradition and innovation is earning the admiration of foodies from all over. The chef's specialty is the pride and joy of Chinese cuisine, the shark's fin. Guests cannot help smiling when they try this dish, with its flavor and texture honed to perfection. The venue is small, with 15 counter seats only. The presence of the chef, the sommelier and the guests together makes a stylish and pleasant atmosphere.

Those hoping to expand their horizons from the old ways of large-served Chinese dishes into this new, delicate and deep world are encouraged to act quickly to make a reservation while they are still available and give this up-and-coming restaurant a try.

244568.longDescription:
The Roppongi branch "Kyoto Hyoki" sits 2-minute by foot from Roppongi Station on Hibiya Line, in a quiet spot a step inside an alley near Roppongi Intersection. Entering the restaurant, one steps out of the urban bustle and is enveloped in the scent of incense and pure air. What's more, the restaurant is particularly equipped to control humidity and keep outside dust from entering. 

The famous menu of "Dashi shabu" served in the traditional dashi broth inherited from Kyoto is offered as a kaiseki course with dishes of the four seasons. We hope you enjoy the sweet and tender pork with a melt-in-your-mouth texture, generously dipped in our deep and proud "dashi" soup broth and served with fragrant leeks. The beautiful and delicious dishes served in a modern Japanese private room are "just right for bringing an important person" and are also suitable for business entertainment, dinners, celebrations and important dates.

The restaurant interior presents a stylish, Japanese-style modern atmosphere, brightened by silver foil. The tasteful furnishings are united by the use of plain wood. All seats are private rooms, so it is recommended for　entertaining, celebrations, and treating guests from overseas. English menus and basic English conversational ability are available. Come and enjoy a relaxed time in a refined private room.

244939.longDescription:
A three-minute walk from Roppongi Station in Tokyo, Miyake Akira is a kaiseki restaurant that encapsulates the best of Japanese cuisine and culture. 

Hailing from Tajimi City in Gifu Prefecture, owner and chef Akira Miyake serves as a proud ambassador of tourism for his hometown, and was given the status of Japanese Cuisine Special Goodwill Ambassador by the nation’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries. In 2014, after a successful stint at the unagi specialist Yuugetsu in Tajimi, Miyake took on the challenge of opening Miyake Akira in Tokyo in August 2020. 

“I want guests to enjoy Japanese cuisine and Minoyaki,” he says, referring to the regional style of pottery found in his home region, used to present dishes to his discerning guests. He also favours Wara River sweetfish and other specialty ingredients from Gifu, carefully selecting high quality ingredients from across Japan. 

The restaurant’s signature dish celebrates Miyazaki caviar, from Japanese sturgeon. The creamy, rounded flavour, distinct from traditional caviar, is a selling point with the restaurant’s loyal following. A dish of grilled eel coated with a rich, traditional sauce used for over 130 years at Yuugetsu, has an exquisite taste. Meanwhile, a 15-strong selection of Japanese sakes complements a meal without overpowering, while a Southern France-leaning wine list also pairs well with the grilled eel. As for alcohol-free options, guests are offered Royal Blue Tea of outstanding quality. 

Guests are offered either one of eight counter seats, or a private room with space for six, imbued with warmth of Gifu; a wooden counter and chairs transported from the region, for example, or Tajimi City tiles that embellish the interior. Additionally, the chef also offers guests dinnerware from Minoyaki to accentuate each dish, carefully designed by Miyake himself. 

With the charm and cuisine of Gifu in a cosmopolitan setting, Miyake Akira makes for an excellent venue for dates and gatherings.

244627.longDescription:
Oryori Mukyu, located in the residential tower of Roppongi Hills, is led by Chef Shotaro Igarashi, who showcases his refined culinary expertise.

Chef Igarashi hails from Fukushima Prefecture. After training at a renowned traditional Japanese restaurant in Kyoto, he returned to his hometown, where he worked as the fifth-generation successor of his family’s long-established Japanese restaurant. In 2017, he was appointed Head Chef for the opening of Saryo Miyasaka. In 2025, he began leading the kitchen at Oryori Mukyu.

The interior design is inspired by the Japanese-Western architectural style of the Taisho to early Showa period (early 20th century), recreating the aesthetics of a time when traditional Japanese sensibilities remained deeply rooted while Western influences were gradually incorporated. The space reflects the spirit of wabi-sabi—an appreciation of understated beauty and imperfection—and a harmonious blending of cultures.

The restaurant features eight counter seats, table seating, and two private rooms accommodating up to four guests each. Within this tranquil setting in the heart of Tokyo, guests are welcomed into an atmosphere reminiscent of “good old Japan.” Although located in central Tokyo, the space evokes the feeling of having wandered into a quiet corner of Kyoto or another historic city. Here, we invite you to savor a once-in-a-lifetime dining experience—ichigo ichie, a Japanese concept that treasures each encounter as unique and never to be repeated.
