244395.longDescription:
In 2016, Restaurant L'aube reunited Hideaki Imahashi, who was the head chef at Keisuke Matsushima in Akabanebashi, Shoko Hirase, who was the chef-pastry chef, and Hiroshi Ishida, who was the chef-sommelier at Akabanebashi. In 2023, the restaurant will move to Kamiyacho and ARK Hills Sengokuyama Mori Tower for a new start.

The three are all giants of their field; chef Imahashi  and patissier Hirase were trained in Paris and Nice, hot-spots in French cuisine, and sommelier Ishida is a former Japanese sommelier contest-champion and a decorated veteran of awards across the globe. This tri-ni-set comes together to produce a harmony of 'L'aube', or 'dawn', of 'birth'. 

Both lunch and dinner offers courses of 5-7 layers. Chef Imahashi, drawing on his past as a farming chef, concocts a course centered on Kamakura vegetables grown on sea-side, nutrient-rich soil. Coupled with fresh-caught fish from Kyushu's Amakusa, and the finest selected meats from both Japan and abroad, 'L'aube' serves a classical yet visionary French cuisine. 

Patissier Hirase too showcases her craft; from live slicing of oven-fresh loaves of  bread at your table-side, to delicate sweets served in exquisite jewelry boxes, 'Laube' brings an exciting approach to presentation sure to make your hear dance. 

Wines selected from new and old world alike, from France but also South Africa, the Americas, Georgia, and others, line 'L'aube''s impressive cellar. From this selection sommelier Ishida proposes wine-pairing options tailored to each guest.

The dining hall, with 32 seats, is illuminated through walls lined with lighting reminiscent of champagne bubbles. The ornate, Möbius strip-themed centerpiece at each table is similarly striking. The hall offers not just a luminescent mood; from the dining guests can gaze into the kitchen, and watch the masters of foods and pastries spin their craft. 

'L'aube' is thoroughly guests-first; with a balanced sense of distancing, they will deliver every time on orchestrating incredible symphonies for your most cherished anniversaries. Do visit this magnificent hall, of extraordinary harmony playing music to the senses, for an experience you will treasure for the ages.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Roppongi-itchome Station Kamiyacho Station 2

recommendations.comment: お料理とワインのペアリングが素晴らしく、スタッフの方々の応対も丁寧で、幸せな時間を過ごすことができました。
とても美味しかったです。また来ます。
お料理が大変美味しく美しく、素敵な時間を過ごせました。食材の組み合わせやソースなども繊細にして鮮烈で食文化を存分に楽しめました。選んでいただいたワインとの相性も良かったですし、サスティナブルな試みやシェフの打ち出したい思いが込められたそれぞれのお皿に感嘆致しました。また是非伺いたいです
素晴らしい時間を過ごすことができました。ありがとうございました。
どの料理もとても美味しかったです。全員とても満足でした。
料理はどれも美味しく、ペアリングの注文は大正解でした。全体的に味がしっかりし、主張は強いもののワインとの相性が良いです。メインの猪と焼立てパンの香りが印象的で、デザートは2品もあり、ついデザートワインまで追加しちゃいました。食器から、オーダーメイドのワインスタンドやメニュー専用のカバーなど、細かいところまでの拘りが素敵です。シェフとスタッフの皆様、ありがとうございました！とても楽しかったです。
どの料理もデザートも、とても美味しかったです。
料理、人、サービス、雰囲気、全てが満足度高く、とても気持ち良く楽しめた。ありがとうございました。

約5年ぶりの来店でしたが、前回にも増して満足致しました。お料理も一品一品丁寧な作りとみためだけではなく素材を活かし、素材の組み合わせも見事で、お腹いっぱいと言いながら飽きのない味にペロリと食べてしまいました。サーブも丁寧な説明はもちろんこちらの会話にも応じて頂き楽しいひと時を過ごせました。ワインのチョイスもさすがという感じで、定番の売れ筋のものというわけでなく、本当にお料理に合わせた素晴らしいマリアージュでした。それなりの対価ではありますが、もっと上でもいいくらいの感じがしました。デザートは言うまでもなく素晴らしい数々でした。本当に素晴らしい時間を過ごすことができました。ありがとうございました！
全てにクオリティの高い技術・味を感じた。ビジュアル的にも非常に良かった。素材を大切にしていると思った。
お料理もサービスもとても満足でした。お店の雰囲気も良かったです。次回は家族と再訪したいです。

243831.longDescription: Restaurant Ryuzu is a world gourmet guide awarded French restaurant located just a five-minute walk away from Roppongi station. Owner chef Ryuta Iizuka served his apprenticeship both in Japan and overseas, and was also the head chef at world gourmet guide awarded L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon in Tokyo. The restaurant offers a variety of dishes that maximize the flavors of seasonal ingredients. One of Ryuzu's popular dishes is the Yairo Shiitake Mushroom Tart. The warm vegetables are served with abalone that is carefully cooked right before it is served. The restaurant has both counter seats and private rooms, which makes it ideal for all kinds of occasions. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 Featured Article: ""Restaurant Ryuzu"" -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? Second time dining at the restaurant.  Both time our wedding anniversary. The staff remembered us and served us with passion and professionalism.  Food was excellent again.  I prefer the relatively smaller number of courses here vs some other more fancy fushion restaurants.  Wine recommendation was also great.  Will definitely come again and recommend to friends.

The service was excellent. The decor was modern and elegant. The sommelier was very knowledgeable. The food was beautiful, seasonal and divine. The location is very convenient and in the heart of Tokyo. It was a lovely meal and experience. Much appreciation to the chef who greeted us as we were leaving.

The following fish was also delicious. The tiramisu was splendid and so was also the rest of the dessert menu. The smoked salmon was also a real treat. It is one of the best meal I have in Tokyo, the choice of ingredients for each dish is matching perfectly.

The fish is the best with the crispy bone and liver paste match perfectly with the fish.

The services is attentive but not intrusive.

Overall, a perfect choice of taste. I definitely will recommend to other, which I already did.

244362.longDescription: “Ryoriya Tachibana” is located 3-5 minutes on foot from Roppongi station, a back alley on Gaien Higashi Dori, after entering an even more secluded place you will find a storefront that is the home of the Japanese restaurant. Based on the concept of “Taste of Japan,” with the idea of “Growing Japanese Culture Through Flavor,” we will accomplish this not only through Japanese culinary culture, but also by creating the restaurant that can spread the ceramics and glass-work of contemporary Japanese artists to the world. The owner-chef is Mr. Kosei Tachibana. After learning the art of sushi and Japanese cooking in his hometown Fukuoka, he traveled to Tokyo. He was trained at several Japanese restaurants in Asakusa, Nihonbashi, and Shinjuku, and also has experience as a head chef. After that, he worked for 13 years at “Kozue” in the Park Hyatt Tokyo, where he was the sous-chef. In November of 2017, he went independent and opened “Ryoriya Tachibana.” With great interest in tea ceremony, Tachibana brings his obsession of “ocha” to all aspects of the course. When guests are seated, they will first be offered an “issen” (the first course in Japanese tea ceremony) of Fukuoka Yame Dento Hongyokuro (known as the “king of green teas”). In a teapot set into the center of the counter, it is brewed with “Ougaku” water from the Tarumizu Kagoshima natural hot springs, for a tea characterized by a deep umami and aroma. In addition, dishes that make use of this tea are also offered, and at the end of the course, Mr. Tachibana’s matcha will be served. The atmosphere of the live performance at the counter is another attraction, and the soup stock used is prepared in front of the guests with shavings from bluefin tuna and two types of bonito so that they can enjoy the unparalleled flavor of the stock when it is freshly prepared. Also, sashimi is offered in an impactful large bowl. Upon a bed of ice,Upon a bed of ice,Seasonal seafood carefully selected from all over Japan are served. The dinnerwares used are mainly works from contemporary artists such as Mr. Sakurei Okamoto. The clean and fresh atmosphere inside the restaurant, with its traditional finished plaster walls, features a chic black cork counter with 8 seats, and a private room for 4 guests. It can be used in a wide variety of settings, including anniversaries, dates, or business dinners. It is a remarkable restaurant, where one can taste Japanese culture in a relaxing space. ※ For reservation of 5 to 8 people, please click here for inquiries. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room is available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No charged. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can accommodate a party of up to 4 people. ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 12 years of age who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. ■ Are menus available in other languages? No menu available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? No English-speaking staff. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We do not accept reservations for one person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals. ■Can I bring my own drinks? Bring your own bottle fee 5500 yen (tax included). Wine, Sake (720ml or less) and Champagne may be brought in. but,Bringing in bottles of whiskey, sake (720ml or more), and shochu is not allowed.

recommendations.comment: 今回も期待以上のお料理とサービスでした。玉露から始まり、お抹茶で終わる最高のおもてなしに感動です。お料理は旬のものを丁寧に調理してくださり、本当に美味しかったです。ご飯の味はどこのお店でも食べられない美味しいご飯で、一口目から違いを感じられました。デザート皿に描いてくださった彼岸花は本当に美しかったです。来れて良かった、そして次回もまた絶対に帰ってきたいと強く思います。素敵な時間をありがとうございました。
最初から最後まで本当に素晴らしい体験をさせていただきました。料理も大変美味しく、接客も素晴らしく、楽しくお話ししながら食事を楽しめました。また料理へのこだわりだけでなく、細部に渡るおもてなしの心遣いが伝わって、感動の連続でした。特にお皿に店主さまが絵を描かれた時の感動はひとしおでした。東京に行った際はぜひ再訪したいと思います。本当にありがとうございました。

We had a great time! The food was delicious and immaculately presented. Every component of the dishes was thoughtful and added to the its taste and texture and our overall enjoyment.

The staff were a bit nervous at first, knowing that we speak only English, but they tried hard to make us feel welcome and to explain as best they could. Luckily we can read Chinese, so we were able to decipher a bit of the menu from the kanji. We left very very happy and with satisfied bellies ¨̮

すべてが素晴らしかった。 それは一生に一度の経験でした。 ありがとうございました。

また伺いたいと思ってます。宜しくお願い致します。
A wonderful meal and in the current climate almost felt like having a private chef for the evening.

素敵な時間を過ごせました！
妻もとても喜んでいました！
また次回お伺いいたします！
とてもおいしかったです。最高です。

初めに出てくる玉露は、今までに味わったことのない旨味があり、驚きました。

食材はかなり厳選されています。

カウンターでの演出が面白く、鰹節を目の前で削っていただいたり、デザートの苺大福の皿には、筆を使って季節の絵を描いていただいたりと、見ていて楽しいです。

海外の方にも喜んでいただけそうですね。

知人にもオススメしたいと思います。

ごちそうさまでした！

245418.longDescription:
With its bright façade facing Gaien Higashi Street in Roppongi, one of the most spectacular neighborhoods in the international city of Tokyo, SeRieUX is conveniently located three minutes on foot from Tokyo Metro Nogizaka Station and five minutes on foot from Roppongi Station. The floor-to-ceiling windows on the façade and the skylights on the ceiling allow soft natural light to enter the dining room during the day and reflect the glowing neon lights of Roppongi at night. These windows also allow diners at the counter to feel the street vibes.

The dining space with a 20-seat counter features a modern, woody decor. The windows on the façade are adorned with impressive square-shaped lattices, along with a touch of greenery, to allow natural light in while shielding guests from unwanted views. The restaurant has English-speaking staff for international guests and can accommodate children above the age of 10 for lunch and 16 for dinner, if requested in advance. In addition, attracting diverse clientele due to its location, the restaurant is also designed for various occasions, such as entertaining dinners with guests from Japan and abroad, dates, intimate meals with friends, and gourmet gatherings.
nearestStations: 3-minute walk from Nogizaka Station on the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line
5-minute walk from Roppongi Station on the Toei Oedo Line and Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line.

245225.longDescription: Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi, which has had its doors open in Roppongi Hills at the center of the redevelopment of the international city since the grand opening of the complex in 2003, is a branch of Sukiyabashi Jiro, a renowned sushi restaurant in Sukiyabashi, Ginza. The Roppongi location, which has been awarded two stars in a restaurant guide, follows the main location’s concept of competing on the quality of its sushi and adheres to the no-longer-popular, restrained practice of offering no dishes other than sushi and beer and Japanese sake (one label each). The branch location is helmed by Chef Takashi Ono, who was born in 1961 as the second son of Owner-Chef Jiro Ono of Sukiyabashi Jiro and apprenticed himself at the age of 19 to his father acclaimed as a sushi chef. During the apprenticeship, he learned not only culinary skills but also attitudes toward sushi from his father. Then, at the age of 42, he was certified to be skilled enough to open his own restaurant. According to Chef Jiro Ono, his second son was “trained stricter than any other apprentice.” The sushi is made exactly to the recipe of the main location. The same goes for the sushi rice, the sourish sushi vinegar, and the temperature controlled to store sushi toppings. The ingredients are also sourced from the same mediator that has procured high-quality ingredients from Toyosu Market for the main location of Sukiyabashi Jiro for years. The fact that only the best ingredients of the day are delivered from all over Japan is proof of the mediator’s good judgment. The mediator delivers the same fish, nori seaweed, tea, and rice to the main and branch locations. The long-standing trust allows the branch location to offer high-quality sushi worthy of the name “Sukiyabashi Jiro.” Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi offers a prix fixe (fixed price) menu where sushi is served in a typical order (starting with lightly flavored seafood, such as flatfish, and followed by shellfish, bluefin tuna, blue-skinned fish, and grilled seafood) so that sushi lovers can focus on the sushi. With warm wood accents, the simple interior designed after the main location also allows diners to focus on the sushi right before their eyes. Any of the eight seats at the counter allows guests to enjoy sushi to their heart’s content. Guests from abroad are also welcomed by the chef, who speaks English and Chinese. Thus, Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi is the perfect place for sushi lovers. Please enjoy their authentic Edomae sushi. Notes for reservations: Please check the cancelation policy in the section “Please refer to the below” in the reservation form before making a reservation. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are not available. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children. Please note that we request that everyone including children to respect dining experience of others. Children are welcome to order from our a la carte menu. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible and we will be happy to assist as needed. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks limited English and Chinese. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Smart Casual. Please refrain from shorts, tank tops or sandals.

244953.longDescription:
Sushi Mitsukawa’s Roppongi location can be found on the 5th floor of Roppongi Hills, a neighbourhood landmark. Based on the ultra-modern West Walk, one-star chef Koji Mitsukawa takes centre stage to offer his best sushi on the Premium Dining Floor, a food hub in Tokyo that has attracted global attention. 

Mitsukawa studied at a famous sushi restaurant in Ginza for five years. After moving to Germany, he worked in sushi restaurants overseas for three years in Dusseldorf. After returning to Japan, he opened his own sushi restaurant, Sushi Mitsukawa, two years later in 2005. News spread quickly about his nigiri and delicate side dishes, and the restaurant became popular, eventually being awarded one star. Afterwards, he opened Sushi Mitsukawa Roppongi Hills in 2019, followed by Sushi Mitsukawa Niseko in 2020, determined to share the taste of his sushi.

"I wanted to try out what possibilities could be found in Toyosu Market, which has the highest volume of distribution in Tokyo," says Mitsukawa, who was awarded one star with local ingredients in Noto. The nigiri sushi concept is based on the same Edomae technique as the flagship in Kanazawa. The strength of the Roppongi store lies in the fact that ingredients can be purchased from three locations: Kanazawa's high-quality ingredients, those from the famed Toyosu market, and Hokkaido, which is connected by the edge of the Niseko store. While preserving tradition, the nigiri sushi and side dishes that are served with ingredients from the 3 treasure boxes of food continue to evolve daily.


Popular with diners, the Nodoguro hand-roll menu, called Mitsukawa's Three Great Specialties, can be enjoyed year-round. Also, it’s common for guests to return frequently for Kobako crab, which is only available for two months from November. 

For sake, Kagatobi, Tengumai and other styles from Kanazawa account for two-thirds of the restaurant’s list. There are usually about 10 other varieties available, including the Dassai in Yamaguchi, Mitsukawa's hometown. After collaborating with a sake brewery in Kanazawa, they also created an original bottle with a refreshing flavour. The restaurant favours wine from Bordeaux growers; for champagne, the owners visit the region every few years, selecting bottles personally chosen by Mitsukawa. 

As diners enter the restaurant through the noren (a short curtain hung at the entrance of a store), a 300-year old cypress counter stands out. An additional counter brings the total to 19 seats for guests. 

In a serene space to make guests forget the chaos of Roppongi, the restaurant is ideal for a visit with friends, couples, or family to enjoy outstanding sushi and side dishes.

244386.longDescription:
""Sushi Nakamura"" locates in Roppongi, an area with many famous restaurants, and aims to establish a new style of Edomae-sushi; using clever techniques and preparation methods, it creates unique sushi and side dishes which are well received, bringing in many sushi fans.

Chef Mr. Masanori Nakamura started training from the age of 19, at Japanese restaurants and sushi restaurants for 10 years before he opened ""Sushi Nakamura"" in April 2000. Although Mr. Nakamura is mostly self-taught in the art of sushi-making, his restaurant has got a world gourmet guide award in 2008.

Mr. Nakamura chooses the best seafood at Tsukiji fish market such as tuna from Fujita Fisheries. Taking into account the marriage of the sushi topping with the vinegar rice, he uses distinctive scoring to bring the sushi together. He devotes himself to devising clever techniques wherever possible, such as slicing white-fleshed fish very thinly and layering 4 slices to give a softer mouthfeel. 

Mr. Nakamura has done various research on preparation methods to pursue a new style of Edomae sushi. For his vinegar rice, he uses Koshihikari rice from Tochio, Niigata, steamed in a Nambu cast iron pot from Iwate prefecture, and combined with a blend of 3 types of red vinegar and rice vinegar. He also is selective with his sakes, stocking brands such as Kokuryu, Juyondai, and Sawaya Matsumoto.

The interior was designed in the image of a Kyoto-style Japanese restaurant, with 11 seats in front of a counter of a Japanese cypress. Much attention and care were given to the chairs and lighting as well. The clean and dignified atmosphere allows everyone to enjoy their meals, it is not only a good choice for business dinners and dates, but also is popular among overseas guests. Please enjoy the sushi prepared by Mr. Nakamura, polished by daily practice and extensive research.

244555.localizedAddress: 5F, Roppongi Hills West Walk , 6-10-1, Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo
244555.longDescription:
Roppongi Hills brings you premium dining with its many renowned restaurants, of which ""Ten Soso"" is the only restaurant specializing in tempura. Head chef Keita Sato trained for 11 years at ""Yamanoue"", a famous restaurant serving tempura and other Japanese cuisines in Yamanoue Hotel (Hilltop Hotel), Ochanomizu. He then joined ""Tempura Kondo"", a world gourmet guide award restaurant that is said to serve the absolute best of tempura. He spent an additional 12 years training there, learning Kondo’s rich range of ideas in the process. Then, in 2011, he joined Kiwa Corporation Co., Ltd., working at Tenmaru in Marunouchi before becoming head chef at ""Ten Soso"" at the time of its opening.

Tempura is the kind of dish where the character of the ingredients comes through directly, and so it is important to first focus on the quality of the ingredients themselves. Fish from the Sasebo–Kujukushima area in Nagasaki Prefecture and oysters from Nagasaki are purchased fresh each day; carefully selected ingredients from around the country such as Kumano Jidori chicken and branded vegetables like Gorojima Kintoki sweet potatoes or Kyoto carrots are also purchased. The ingredients are prepared by either cooking them live, letting them sit for a while, or steaming them in order to bring out each ingredient's flavor to the maximum degree.

Eggs are not used in the tempura batter, and ""Ten Soso"" is also particular about frying its tempura to be light and almost white in color, what Japanese would describe as ""hagoromo."" We especially recommend trying the Edomae no Anago, the conger eel tempura that is one of the numerous tempura dishes available on the menu. First, individual differences in the conger eels, which are prone to fishiness or muddiness, are ascertained. They are then cooked in a highly skilled manner that goes so far as to consider the temperature of the oil, the way of working with the batter, and the deep-frying method, all to transform this ingredient into the absolute finest quality of tempura. To accompany the food, ""Ten Soso"" stocks a wide variety of alcohol, not only Japanese sake and shochu but also wine and champagne.

The interior is decorated in the sukiya style, with a sense of the wabi-sabi aesthetic that is uniquely Japanese. If visiting as a couple or with friends, we recommend sitting at the counter, where you can experience the thrill of watching the tempura being deep-fried right in front of you. ""Ten Soso"" is equipped with tables and private rooms in a relaxed atmosphere. Recommended for business entertainment and meals enjoyed with a small group of people.
nearestStations: Directly connected to Roppongi Station, Exit 1C(Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

243930.longDescription: Wolfgang's Steakhouse Roppongi, from the Roppongi intersection, head in the direction of Itakura Katamachi, turn at Toriizaka and walk a little, you will see a classical appearance with the name of the store hanging in a tent across the red eaves. Founded in the US in 2004, Wolfgang’s quickly attracted a strong following before expanding rapidly. Today, his restaurants can be found in the United States, China, and Singapore, with the Roppongi restaurant the first of its kind in Japan, and the first branch outside the US. Wolfgang Zwiener, the restaurant’s founder, originally worked at a prestigious New York steakhouse for over 40 years as a server, using this experience of putting guests first to enhance the experience at his eponymous restaurants. Zweiner's main focus is on the quality of the meat and the customer experience. Meat is dry-aged for 28 days in a custom humidity controlled warehouse, before being imported by air each week. Only Prime Grade USDA beef is served at the restaurant, which is ranked highest 3% of its kind and some of the finest in the world. With dry-aging and maturation enhancing the meat’s flavor, it’s then cut into luxuriously thick slices before being cooked on a grill at a temperature of 900°C. The surface of each steak is fragrant and crisp, with the meat retaining its moisture inside. The signature T-bone steak an opportunity to enjoy both the sirloin and fillet cuts at the same time, as well as classic accompaniments like mashed potatoes and creamed spinach. Over 1,000 bottles of wine from across the world are offered to guests to pair with their meal. Inside the spacious dining room, 140 tables, 18 counter seats and two 10-person private dining rooms are available for guests. Dark wood panelling and ambient lighting creating a noble, luxurious atmosphere - the perfect environment to enjoy fine steaks. Ideal for celebrations, family get-togethers, dates, and entertaining. 〈Group Restaurant Information〉 Wolfgang's Steakhouse Signature Aoyama Wolfgang's Steakhouse Osaka Wolfgang's Steakhouse Fukuoka Wolfgang’s Steakhouse TEPPAN Wolfgang's Steakhouse Marunouchi Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa
nearestStations: A 4-minute walk from Roppongi Station, Exit 3 (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

245473.longDescription:
At Yakiniku Queue, a top-notch restaurant befitting the vibrant, mature neighborhood of Roppongi, Chef Sadayuki Nagashima, known as a meat specialist, thrills the taste buds of food lovers by offering his favorite Kobe beef carefully selected for its freshness and prepared in the most suitable way to bring out the most of the best beef of the day.  

Chef Nagashima honed his culinary skills at Yoroniku in Omotesando, which has now become a synonym for popular yakiniku restaurants. Finding it enjoyable to serve dishes fresh from the kitchen and directly feel how guests are reacting, he opened his own restaurant, Yakiniku Queue, in 2022 to unlock the delightful potential of the cuisine.  The restaurant’s name “Queue” is taken from his nickname as an apprentice at Yoroniku, but the word that also means ‘tail’ in French is selected to represent his desire to make the restaurant so popular that a long, tail-like queue will form in front.  

If you choose a prix-fixe menu, you will be served with yakiniku meat all grilled to perfection by staff right in front of you. The full-course meal starts with appetizers, such as namul and kimchi, followed by very lightly grilled (almost undercooked) beef, Wagyu beef tongue, salt-seasoned Kobe beef, and Kobe beef enriched with yakiniku sauce, and ends with a dish of your choice from 15 varieties of dishes, including Pyongyang Cold Noodles, Keema Curry, and Pasta Bolognese. Developed by Chef Nagashima with another chef experienced in Western and Korean cuisine, the prix-fixe menu goes beyond the boundaries of yakiniku cuisine, pursuing excellence in the quality of beef. They go as far as picking out Kobe cow meat for its tender, low-melting fat that will not sit heavy on the stomach.

The wine list curated by the sommelier, mainly from Bordeaux, Bourgogne, and Napa Valley, offers a great selection of 80 red, white, and sparkling wines that go well with Japanese yakiniku. 
In addition, a combination of Kutani, Arita, and Hasami ware and distinctive Spanish dishware adds a unique touch to the tables. The luxurious interior full of artworks brings in the vibes of Roppongi. The main dining space is furnished with four dining tables, with four seats each, divided by see-through curtains and high-back sofas to provide a semi-private dining experience. The restaurant also has two private dining rooms, between which the spacious room seating up to 10 guests is soundproof, and they are perfect for families with children. It is also equipped with a large screen for karaoke parties. Its high-class yakiniku cuisine, attentive service, and sophisticated atmosphere befitting the night vibes of Roppongi make the restaurant an ideal destination for different occasions.

244648.longDescription:
"Yakitori & Wine Moto" is a 3-minute walk from Roppongi Crossing, and its clean, white facade stands out from its surroundings. "Moto" has recently garnered popularity for its new take on yakitori culture that focuses on fermented food and natural wine, in addition to skewered chicken. 

The foundations of the restaurant's unique concept are in its boundless respect for the traditional Japanese dish of yakitori. The restaurant expands on the concept by implementing fermentation, another Japanese culinary tradition. By focusing on more than the chicken itself, it is creating its own new style of yakitori. Menu development has been aided by ideas from two of the minds behind modern Vietnamese restaurant "An Di": prominent Japanese wine taster Motohiro Okoshi, and Chihiro Naito who previously worked his way up to the rank of sous-chef at world gourmet guide award French restaurant "L’Effervescence" in Omotesando.

Yuta Hasebe, the chef at "Yakitori & Wine Moto", has over 10 years of experience cooking Italian at the likes of Le Acacie. He has implemented fermentation techniques and an Italian flair into Moto's entrees, appetizers, and sauces. By approaching yakitori from a different vector, accenting dishes with strong umami and acidic tones, he brings out the best of the restaurant's signature dish, yakitori, in courses that keep diners interested in what's coming next.

He artfully selects chicken from all corners of Japan, from sources including breeds like Akita's Hinai Jidori , Ibaraki's Kasumi Jidori , Kyoto's Kyobeni Jidori and Aichi's Kinsodori, in order to allow diners to enjoy the distinct flavors each different cut has to offer. He selects chicken like a sushi chef selects fish, picking the best breeds at the best times and preparing each piece of meat in the way most suited to its unique characteristics.

The vast lineup of natural wines and Japanese sake selected by Okoshi make for perfect dining companions. The stars of the show are the natural wine. Carefully selected from across the globe, they are well known for being easier on the body, but more importantly at Moto, they play an integral role in the dining experience. The various wine comes in a variety of vessels, including both glasses and decanters as the situation demands, and are expertly paired with the menu's plethora of skewered delights.

The subdued, modern Japanese decor sets the stage for 9 counter seats overlooking the grill and 14 table seats. The restaurant also offers one private dining area that seats six guests. 245063.longDescription:
World-renowned chef Masaharu Morimoto presents his signature cuisine at atelier morimoto XEX on Seijoki Street in Roppongi. With teppanyaki counters, a sushi counter, and lounges for after-meal drinks, this versatile restaurant attracts not only local food lovers but also visitors from around the world.

The restaurant features eclectic Western and Japanese cuisine based on the signature cuisine of chef Morimoto, known as the successful owner of innovative Japanese restaurants in the U.S., and even more renowned as the third generation Iron Chef of Japanese cuisine from the popular Japanese show. Diners can enjoy exquisite dishes in a generous space that was once open only to members of the XEX Group.

Guests are invited to discover the chef’s excellent sushi, featuring the highest-quality ingredients such as oma maguro (tuna) at the sushi counter, as well as Kobe beef and Japanese Kuroge wagyu beef steaks expertly grilled and sliced in front of the guests at the teppanyaki counters. Dining is also available at the bar, in the lounge, and private dining rooms, making the restaurant the perfect place to dine incognito and grab a bite and a drink. The drink menu offers 180 wines, 25 types of sake, and a wide selection of cocktails and whiskies.

Inside the restaurant, a bar area and a sushi counter greet guests on the first floor, while teppanyaki counters await on the basement floor, and private dining rooms and a lounge area are available on the second floor. The sushi counter, made of solid plain wood, seats up to 11 guests, while semi-circular teppanyaki counters seat up to 22. In addition, the lounge area accommodates 20 guests comfortably. 

With leather sofas, armchairs, and lighting inspired by the bubbles of sparkling wine, the interior offers a luxurious, elegant atmosphere befitting a secret hideaway for adults. The entire space can be booked out for exclusive use, and it’s also possible to grab a late-night bite. Guests are invited to enjoy excellent food in a luxurious, tranquil, and private setting at atelier morimoto XEX for occasions such as business dinners, date nights, and anniversaries.


* The counter and table seats for teppanyaki dining are on the first basement floor, which is accessed by the spiral staircase inside the restaurant.

* To book a private room with a teppanyaki counter seating from 4 to 10 guests on the second floor (Booking fees: ¥20,000 including consumption tax), or a semi-private room with a low horigotatsu table seating from 4 to 8 guests in the sushi dining area on the first floor, please contact the restaurant through the inquiry form.

245556.longDescription:
Perched on the third floor of a building near Roppongi Station, muho enchants guests with dishes where traditional Japanese natural ingredients and their stories are woven together by Chef Takashi Ikeda, who trained at top restaurants overseas. His distinguished career is built on a strong foundation of hands-on training at prestigious restaurants, such as Restaurant Geranium in Copenhagen, Denmark, Aska in New York City, the U.S., and Mugaritz in San Sebastián, Spain. Positive and determined, the young Ikeda went abroad and got himself apprenticed to renowned chefs by handing out résumés in person.

After returning to Japan, he focused on Japanese ingredients. In July 2025, he opened muho, named after a four-character compound word, Teni Muho, which means “perfect beauty with no trace of artifice.” This eulogy fits the chef’s simple yet creative, one-of-a-kind dishes that celebrate wild ingredients from local land and sea. The seafood is sourced mainly from his home prefecture of Kumamoto but also from around the Kyushu region. The pasture-raised mutton is supplied from Aso, Kumamoto, known for producing Aka Beef, and the venison and other precious game meats that are only available once in a few years are purchased from trusted hunters. In addition, Chef Ikeda himself collects ingredients from the wild, including fruits like wild grapes, bayberries, Japanese figs, and Siberian gooseberries (the original species of kiwifruits) and spices like Japanese spicebush and mountain pepper (both belonging to the laurel family) , native wild pepper, and Japanese cinnamon. These rare ingredients not commonly available in regular markets are transformed into about 12-course meals, from appetizer to dessert, with a deep respect for ancestral knowledge.

The sake list also features Japanese labels, such as Ubusuna, brewed from horse-cultivated Edo Higo rice and traditional “Kimoto” yeast by Hananoka Sake Brewery in Kumamoto. There is also a non-alcoholic pairing menu featuring homemade drinks with natural ingredients. The black interior design is highlighted by a red dahlia crafted from Arita ware and accentuated by artisan-made plates reminiscent of natural landscapes on the counter (seating up to eight guests). Perfect for various occasions, from private to business, muho awaits guests with unique gastronomic experiences. Please enjoy Chef Ikeda’s special dishes to your heart’s content.

244975.longDescription:
Found on the 2nd floor of a building near Roppongi Station, chef Seiji Shirato opened this eponymous restaurant under his family name in 2019, after studying at the French restaurant Kamatsuda in Azabu-jūban. 

Shirato, who also worked the line in Japanese and Chinese restaurants in Tokyo, interweaves elements of different cuisines in his fine, multi-course menus. The chef favours carefully selected produce from all over Japan -- seafood from Toyosu Market, vegetables from NOTO Taka Farm in Ishikawa, and ducks from Kyoto or Nanatani. Furthermore, only the highest grade of meat from across Japan is prepared for guests, such as sika deer from Hokkaido. 

The restaurant’s specialty is a classic French soup de poisson, prepared using nodoguro (blackthroat seabass) from regions such as Kyushu, Nagasaki, Shimane and Ishikawa, chosen at its peak. "It is not available in other restaurant; I think you can only taste it here," he says.

Along with the restaurant’s carefully selected dishes, a pairing is recommended to complement the flavours of the food, typically consisting of seven to eight types of beverage. As well as wines and sake, botrytized and orange wines are also available, with the ability for guests to combine drinks in a freeform, borderless style. In addition, tea pairings with organic and decaffeinated domestic teas are also popular.

Named for a type of white clay, the restaurant features an open kitchen with a pristine plastered white wall, and a single counter with 8 seats.  Arita-ware and other pottery styles, and glassware such as Yoshinuma Glass and Sugahara Glass, decorate dishes and drinks, enhancing the experience.

243876.longDescription:
ÉdiTioN Koji Shimomura is a world gourmet guide awarded French cuisine restaurant located on the ground floor of a skyscraper directly connected to Roppongi-itchome station.

Chef Shimomura, who trained at a three-starred restaurant in France, currently organizes several international cooking events. While using traditional French cooking techniques, he creates elegant dishes whose tastes do not depend on the excessive fat and sugar contained in butter and cream. His specialty dish is seaweed-flavored cold oysters lightly cooked with seawater, served with citrus and seawater gelee.

From the tables and chairs to the cutlery, everything inside the restaurant was picked out by the chef himself. The interior shows his strong determination in creating the atmosphere that best matches the sophisticated French cuisine he prepares.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

"Yakitori Tokoshima", provides only 17 counter seats, a place you can enjoy wonderful Yakitori(grilled chicken) made with the freshest ingredients. The owner chef Mr. Tokoshima has been certificated for handling chicken. He purchases whole chickens and scrapes by himself so that he is able to serve the meal, meat, offal and even the rare part with the best condition. The ingredient is delivered directly from farmers in Ibaraki Prefecture. With seasonal vegetables delivered from agricultural producer in Tochigi Prefecture, making you taste the real delicacy. Yakitori is grilled one by one, carefully handled on the charcoal fire. The flavors are simple, salt, pepper or special sauce. Mr. Tokoshima's exquisite grilling makes chickens so tasty and juicy. The chef hopes that guest enjoy his own-style of cooking and experience Yakitori at the best timing. Not to mention 40 kinds of sake carefully selected, paring to Yakitori. 244488.longDescription:
"Daikanyama Sushi Takeuchi" opened in 2017, serving Tokyo style sushi in a location a bit away from the boutique streets. The owner-chef, Jun Takeuchi, aims at a sushi that is a little different from the standard Tokyo style. In his own words, "I don't want to get caught up in the traditional notions of sushi chefs - if it is good, I want to offer it as much as I can".

Mr. Takeuchi first decided to become a sushi chef after visiting Bolivia as a college student. When he saw how sushi was enjoyed by people in countries far from Japan, he became convinced of its global popularity.  After graduating, he entered a cooking school and spent 10 years training in Ginza and 4 in Daikanyama. Wanting people to be able to relax while eating instead of feeling nervous or on edge, he established his restaurant in Daikanyama after searching for a suitable location.

He is very particular about the fish, and sources tuna wholesale from Tsukiji Fish Market - a place he has a long history with - and mackerel from Kagoshima and Izumi. The restaurant offers an entertaining and ever-changing chef's course, with tempura and dishes made with vegetables sent from Mr. Takeuchi's hometown of Shimane. Mr. Takeuchi, wanting his guests to enjoy diverse experiences, also sources the dishes and tools himself, with over 10 varieties of unique items from places such as Imari, Karatsu, and Oribe. The sign at the entrance and the colorful flowers on the inside of the restaurant were designed by a trusted artist. With around 10 types of Japanese sake specially chosen to suit the season, there is a great pairing for Mr. Takeuchi's sushi, which is appetizing just by appearance.

At the L-shaped counter (which seats 8), Mr. Takeuchi's gentle personality radiates everywhere - treating every guest with kindness. "Daikanyama Sushi Takeuchi" is a place where you can take a load off your shoulders and relax in a space full of the warmth of wood, letting you savor every dish.
nearestStations: A 15-minute walk from Daikanyama Station(Tokyu Toyoko Line)

244387.longDescription: ””Paul Bocuse”” is a legendary grand maison in Lyon, France. ””Maison Paul Bocuse in Daikanyama, Tokyo””, is a rare restaurant in Japan that offers the authentic French cuisine that has long attracted gourmets from around the world. Opened in 2007, the restaurant is managed in Japan by Hiramatsu, a leader in the Japanese restaurant scene. The chef is Shugo Fujihisa. At the age of 20, he pursued a career in French cuisine, and at 28, he traveled alone to France. He trained at various grand maisons across the country, learning about regional cuisine and the local gastronomy there. After returning to Japan, he joined Hiramatsu and worked at “Le Baerenthal” in Sapporo. In 2010, he became the sous-chef at “Jardin Paul Bocuse” in Kanazawa, where he served as the head chef for 12 years. From 2024, he will showcase his culinary skills as the head chef at “Maison Paul Bocuse” in Daikanyama. The menu also includes many of Paul Bocuse's specialties, such as "Truffle soup dedicated to V.G.E. at the Elysée Palace in 1975" and "Sea bass in pie with sauce cholon," allowing guests to enjoy the same famous dishes as in his home country. The restaurant offers a wide selection of wines directly imported from chateaus and domaines around France, selected to match the cuisine at Maison Paul Bocuse. The restaurant is divided into dining, salon, bar, and other spaces, and is also equipped with private rooms for small groups. The restaurant is decorated with Venetian chandeliers and Tiffany stained glass throughout and has an Art Nouveau atmosphere, making it the perfect place to enjoy fine cuisine. We hope that you will experience the true essence of French cuisine again at this grand maison. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.

244790.longDescription: "Ristorante ASO" is a five-minute walk from Daikanyama Station in Tokyo. with its beautiful seasonal garden and yellow exterior walls, is an Italian restaurant by Hiramatsu Corporation, set in a classic Western-style building built in the early Showa period. Chef Taku Takashina's cuisine is classic modern Italian cuisine that incorporates the essence of French cuisine with traditional Italian and regional dishes. Based on Hiramatsu's philosophy that "Cooking is an art of the moment to present one's sensibility," Takashina says, "I aim to leave guests with a strong memory of what they have eaten. This commitment is also evident in the procurement of ingredients. He meets and talks directly with producers to understand their feelings before making the most of the ingredients. In particular, he sources first-class Italian products, including porcini, white truffles, and prosciutto ham. In addition, "Cold Pasta with Caviar" and "Karasu Spaghetti" are the signature dishes of "ASO" brand restaurants, and have been loved for a long time as specialties. A wide selection of French and Italian wines are available, and for non-alcoholic drinks, "ASO's special tomato juice" made from Hokkaido tomatoes with high sugar content is available. The juice has an excellent balance of sweetness and acidity, and is the pride of the restaurant and has made many gourmets' mouths water. The restaurant also actively holds events in which wine producers, talented musicians, and other guests are invited to enjoy the special menu. The restaurant is brightly lit at lunch time with sunlight streaming in through large windows, and has a main dining room on the first floor and private rooms on the second floor. The restaurant also has a party salon in the back of the main dining room, where diners can enjoy their meals in a relaxed and elegant setting that is hard to believe that it is in Tokyo. It is the perfect place for a dinner with family and friends, a date, a business meeting, an anniversary, or any other important occasion. ■Please click here to see the "Hiramatsu Standard" for hygiene management and safety measures implemented by HIRAMATSU INC.

244250.longDescription: In March 2015, Restaurant Bacar was regretfully closed. Sincere, opened in April 2016 by Shinsuke Ishii who was a chef at Restaurant Bacar – which became known as a restaurant hard to reserve – almost instantly became so popular that it was impossible to get a reservation and has fascinated many fans. On 2018, it has received world gourmet guide award. Chef Ishii has experienced working under French masters at restaurants such as Yotsuya's Hotel de Mikuni and Minami Aoyama’s La Branche, and honed his skills at world gourmet guide awarded French restaurants. His playful presentation of dishes from his Restaurant Bacar days is not lost, but the true essence is classic French cuisine. The signature dish Taiyaki (traditionally a fish-shaped pancake filled with sweet bean paste) was inspired by the local fish pie. The day’s dishes are presented to guests on the menu like a story, with courses offered to evoke the feelings of each season and the suppliers. In addition, the ambiance that Chef Ishii gives off is the stage that completes the total Sincere atmosphere. The concept of the restaurant is “a playful yet sophisticated atmosphere with some depth”. From the stone floors to the fabric of the sofa, the color of the brass on the door to the cutlery on the table, you can see unity; creating a calm and chic atmosphere. While placing importance on the appearance of the restaurant, Chef Ishii also wanted to make sure that most of the seats were faced to the kitchen. “To create an enjoyable atmosphere where all guests can feel united is the true charm of the restaurant”, says Chef Ishii. Because of the relaxed atmosphere, the restaurant is perfect for casual business entertainment, dates, anniversaries, dinner with colleagues, and various other occasions. We offer you a Chef Ishii-style “Omotenashi (hospitality)” as you enjoy watching his performance in the kitchen. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 Featured Article: ""Sincere""

244826.longDescription:
A 5-minute walk from Onarimon Station in Tokyo, “Onarimon Haru” is a Japanese restaurant located in a business district frequented by businessmen. Chef Haruyuki Ogawa trained at famous Japanese restaurants such as “Ginza Suzaku” and Daimon “Kurogi”, and opened his own restaurant “Onarimon Haru” in March 2019.

Ingredients are purchased from Toyosu market, starting from tuna broker "Yamayuki", and rice from Sado "Iwakubi Shoryu Tanada". The most important thing is "timing". "There is only a moment when it tastes good. There are some points that can be called delicious," said chef Ogawa, while looking for the best timing to use the ingredients. Restaurant’s specialty is "Sesame dressing", which offers freshly roasted and ground sesame. The high aroma makes even gourmets impress. Depending on the season, you can enjoy the "earthen-pot rice" as you visit, such as white rice, takikomi rice (mixed rice), or ojiya (rice porridge) after white rice. Chef Ogawa finds about 10 kinds of Japanese sake every season.

There are 7 counter seats, 2 rooms with 4 table seats and 6 horikotatsu seats. You can enjoy the restaurant for various occasions, from privates to business use, such as on a date or dinner gathering. You will be able to relax and enjoy the essence of Japanese cuisine created from careful work.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2023

14033.longDescription:
5 minutes' walk from Shibuya station in Tokyo, ABASQUE Itsas eta Mendi is located at one of the corners of Shibuya 2 chome intersection. "ABASQUE" is a coined word that combines "Aba" meaning offal in French and the gastronomic ground "Basque" between France and Spain. 

Chef Shibata who practiced in Europe for many years produces a new-style Basque cuisine unique in Tokyo based on the local traditional cuisine featuring the tastes from seas and mountains at Basque. Mr. Oyama is a senior sommelier, picking a variety of wines mainly from France and Spain for those rare labels of Basque's. Chef's selected course is subject to change in a monthly basis and a pairing course is formed with wines handpicked by sommelier Oyama.

The interior is unified with colour of white and brown, floor is one step lower than the entrance, all these elements with a dull lighting form a clam space for adults. Assorted dessert or whole cake (must be reserved at least 3 days ago) can be prepared for your dating. Kids and baby cars are welcome in lunch time. In the serene corner of Shibuya, "ABASQUE" is the place for you to enjoy tasty Basque cuisine.

244053.longDescription: ”LATURE” is a French restaurant located in the basement of Aoyama Gakuin University, not far from Omotesando Station, and is now attracting attention in the area. Owner-chef Takuto Murota worked at ”Tateru Yoshino” before becoming chef at Shibuya's "deco" in 2010, and opened "LATURE" in 2016. The name of the restaurant was coined by Chef Murota and means "drop of nature. The name expresses his passion to provide the best hospitality to his guests by expressing his respect and appreciation for nature through French cuisine. Chef Murota's well known as a master of gibier, and holds a hunting license himself. His cuisine is based on traditional, classic French cuisine, but developed with soft nuances using seasonal Japanese ingredients. In spring, he serves wild plants; in summer, sweetfish; and in fall and winter, his specialties are gibier dishes. Their nourishing and affectionate dishes strongly move the hearts of the eaters. The restaurant provides a casual and relaxed atmosphere, making sure not to appear too formal and stilted. It offers table seats, semi-private rooms, and a chef's table counter in front of the open kitchen, from where guests can see and experience Chef Murota's great sense of presence as he carefully prepares his blessings from nature. (English language enabled) This is a perfect venue for a casual date or dinner among foodies, where guests can enjoy traditional French cuisine and experience the true essence of LATURE. ※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Please be aware that the service charge, the room fee and Tax are charged in addition to your bill. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can accommodate a party of 6 to 8 people. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? Photos are allowed in the restaurant.

244013.longDescription:
French restaurant Monolith, located just off Aoyama-dori —the road leading from Shibuya to Omotesando— a perfect venue for welcoming matured guests. When you go through the entrance door, you will see a short corridor leading you into the dining hall and away from the hustle and bustle of the street. The restaurant interior features moderate colors, providing the atmosphere of a French family-run restaurant.

After training at A Tes Souhaits in Aoyama, Chef Go Ishii refined his techniques further in France with Georges Blanc, Jean Bardet, and Bernard Robin. After returning to Japan, he gained world gourmet guide award as the head chef of the Monna Lisa, in Marunouchi.

 Chef Ishii is a veteran chef with a brilliant track record, having won the second prize at Le Tetangier Concours Japon two years in a row and being selected as a "great restaurant" by the international gourmet guide.Chef Ishii focuses on creating course menus featuring dishes that incorporate an abundance of seasonal vegetables. Amongst these, his monthly menu Menu Neo Monolith showcases many Japanese ingredients with dishes full of seasonal specialties from Japan, attracting many regular guests who look forward to a new experience.

We would like to recommend this restaurant to all guests wishing to experience and appreciate the full joy of seasonal flavors and the staff's attentive hospitality. Monolith is perfect for business meetings, or for enjoying some precious time with close friends and relatives, or with those especially loved ones — a perfect venue that will greatly satisfy not only the guests, but also the hosts.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

recommendations.comment: 一晩経ったいまでも、昨日の記憶をどう整理して素晴らしさの表現に代えようか、時間がかかるほど彩が溢れてきます。お店に一歩入った瞬間から、静謐と心遣い、お店の明かり、テーブルクロスの張り、調度品の距離感が醸す空気に息を飲み、心を奪われました。スタッフの皆様がお話になる日本語の美しさ、問いかけの柔らかさ、当然ドリンクのセレクションに驚きました。綿密なストーリーのあるメニュー、食器となる台座と料理との距離感、色彩のコンビネーション、視覚が刺激される間は食材の味覚を思いつくことも出来ず、口に入れた瞬間に双方が結びつくという類まれな経験をしました。鮎の作品は、プレートのブラックを受けて既に全体が光沢を放っていましたが、一枚一枚剥いで食すと、全てが完全に調理を受けた存在であり、確実な味を持っていました。完全なピースが完全に融合する、プログレスの提示を最後まで切れることなく楽しませて頂きました。ひとつひとつの食材も新鮮で美しく、また味が良くなければ、創造しえない世界なのだろう、と帰路で話しながら、多くの嗜好と思考を刺激されました。それでもまだ昨日の時間のためにかけてくださった労力と配慮に対して、必要十分な表現をみつけることが出来ません。ただ心から感謝申し上げ、季節に応じて訪れたいお店を知ることが出来た幸せを噛みしめております。有難うございました。

245548.longDescription:
About six minutes’ walk along Miyamasuzaka Street from Shibuya Station, Sushi Ikki is nestled in a quiet neighborhood, offering exquisite sushi crafted by Chef Takafumi Kiyonaga with a keen sensitivity. Pursuing a career in the culinary industry, the young Kiyonaga trained at Japanese restaurants, such as Komakata Dozeu Asakusa Honten and Uoshin Shimokitazawa. Meanwhile, an encounter with a popular sushi chef opened doors to the world of sushi for him. To follow this new career path, he got himself apprenticed to renowned sushi chefs in Shinjuku and Ginza. Then, in 2020, he opened his own restaurant, Sushi Ikki, in Chitose Funabashi, making it an instant success with his skillfully created delicacies and nigiri sushi. In 2025, the restaurant was relocated to Shibuya, for which the chef had special feelings, but the creative flair of the chef keeps sushi lovers coming again and again to the new location.

Chef Kiyonaga’s culinary journey keeps evolving as he continues to refine his sensitivity based on his years of experience in the art of Japanese cuisine and his ability to infuse creativity into his Edomae-style sushi. The seafood is directly sourced from top-class fishermen, fishmongers, and wholesalers around Japan, such as Hiroki Hasegawa, a wholesaler “Sakana-bito ” at Nagai Fishing Port in Yokosuka, Kanagawa; Junichi Fujimoto, a fisherman in Imabari, Ehime; Yamasaki Sengyo “Shitateya Yusuke” in Kagoshima; and Kenji Akiyama, a freediving sea urchin fisherman at Yura Port in Awaji Island, Hyogo. These fish and shellfish are featured in the almost 20-course prix-fixe menu where six to seven small dishes and 10 to 11 pieces of nigiri sushi are served in turn. The final piece of sushi is Dried Gourd Rolls, which enjoy year-round popularity. Another popular item is the Grilled Sesame Tofu. Though it is not commonly found on the sushi restaurant menu, Chef Kiyonaga often made it during his apprenticeship.

The wine list offers about 50 options from Burgundy and other renowned regions, including many Grand Cru vintages, such as Champagne Salon, while the sake list consists of 20 labels, including Jokigen from Yamagata. The interior inspired by townhouses in Kyoto is decorated with seasonal flowers arranged by Ikenobo ikebana artists. On the hinoki cypress wood counter, nine Chosen Karatsu ware plates are set for nigiri sushi. With a private dining room with an L-shaped hinoki counter (seating up to six guests) in addition to the main dining room, Sushi Ikki is suitable for various occasions, from private to corporate events. Enjoy the sushi and delicacies crafted by the highly sensitive Chef Kiyonaga.

244284.longDescription:
Tucked away quietly in the Shiodome area of Tokyo, surrounded by office buildings and with few dining options nearby, Restaurant Sugita offers matured steak made from purebred Tajima beef. With no signage, an unpublished phone number, and no listings on gourmet websites, it remains a true hidden gem known only to a select few. The restaurant has been featured in the global steakhouse rankings published by a London-based company for three consecutive years, and in 2025, it finally earned a place in the Global 101 Ranking.
(*Reference: https://www.worldbeststeaks.com/)

Owner Yasushi Sugita trained for seven years at the now-closed but once-renowned French restaurant Jean Moulin in Kobe, beloved among food connoisseurs. He inherited the legacy of his predecessor, who founded the original steakhouse in Kitashinchi, Osaka in 1961. In 2017, Sugita relocated the restaurant to Tokyo, carrying with him over 60 years of expertise in beef cuisine.

Sourcing organic and safe ingredients from all over Japan, including Tajima and Kobe beef, the restaurant crafts dishes rich in deep umami flavors unique to Japan. The finest cuts of meat are matured at 0°C in a specialized refrigeration unit, enhancing their tenderness, aroma, and depth of flavor through a method known as ice-temperature aging.

The “Wagyu Steak Course” allows diners to enjoy purebred Tajima beef and premium branded wagyu from across Japan, with an optional add-on of the restaurant’s original premium beef cutlet sandwich. For those seeking variety, the “Chef’s Recommended Course” features small portions of various premium beef cuts and includes the signature original premium beef cutlet sandwich as a specialty item.

It’s no surprise that many guests return repeatedly; courses are often tailored based on the guest’s past visits. Wine and non-alcoholic pairings are available, including rare bottles that are hard to find elsewhere. With jazz flowing through the dimly lit interior and dishes served on one-of-a-kind antique tableware, the refined space provides the perfect ambiance to savor the finest meat in Japan, elevating the entire dining experience.

245505.longDescription:
Sushi Kagura is tucked in a back alley, just a few steps from the hustle and bustle of Shinbashi Station. With just nine seats at the counter, the restaurant is always packed with sushi lovers eager to taste the superb sushi and see how it is conjured up by Chef Sho Mochizuki. He has devoted his whole career to making sushi. He first honed sushi-making skills at a renowned sushi restaurant, Ginza Kyubei, for 12 years, not only at its branch in Keio Plaza Hotel Tokyo but also at the main location in Ginza. Then, he served as manager at Sushi Onikai in Kamimeguro and at Sushi Onikai Tasuichi in Nakameguro before he opened his own restaurant. Launched in 2021 with nigiri sushi that delights even the taste buds of the God of Sushi, Sushi Kagura has made it into a world-renowned restaurant guide. 

The chef’s selection prix-fixe menu consists of about 20 dishes, ranging from soup to Japanese omelet. The meal starts with appetizers, followed by 10 pieces of nigiri sushi. The sushi rice is seasoned with a mix of red vinegar, rice vinegar, and apple cider vinegar to add a mild sour note. The wasabi is sourced from Wasabiji Ozawa in Shizuoka run by a wasabi farmer who was a high school classmate of Chef Mochizuki. The lean, medium-fatty, fatty, and other tuna cuts are selected from the specialty sushi toppings of Ishiji, a popular wholesaler in Toyosu Market, and sliced and brought to room temperature as soon as they are delivered.  In addition, before the tuna nigiri sushi is served, hot dishes are served, such as chawanmushi (Japanese steamed egg custard), to warm up the taste buds so that they can taste the sweetness of the tuna fat better. Sliced boiled octopus is also popular for its tenderness, which results from freezing the meat at minus 60 degrees Celsius to break down the fibers before cooking.

Sushi Kagura always has a selection of 12 to 13 brands of sake, selected by Chef Mochizuki from around Japan, including Tanigawadake from Gunma and Houken from Hiroshima. The drink menu also offers a great selection of champagnes and red and white wines to meet the preferences of guests. While the entire restaurant is clean in white tones, the dining room is dimly lit and cozy, with jazz music playing softly in the background. It is perfect for various occasions, from intimate family meals, friend gatherings, and dates to business dinners with guests from around the globe.

244522.longDescription:
A four-minute walk from Meguro Station on the JR Yamanote Line, Cellar Fête is a must-visit for meat lovers from all over the world, run by a talented chef who knows best about French meat dishes, such as steak tartare and French aged beef, in Japan.

Chef Takeshi Saita started his career 30 years ago as an opening team member of Taillevent Robuchon in Ebisu. In 2004, he went to France and joined the kitchen team of La Maison Courtine in the 14th arrondissement of Paris. He also worked at Le Severo, a restaurant known for serving the best aged beef in Paris, for four and a half years. Moreover, he cut and trimmed meat at the 16th arrondissement branch of Hugo Desnoyer, the best butcher’s shop in Paris, as well as Rungis International Market, known as a mecca for chefs in the capital of gastronomy. After 11 years’ energetic work in Paris, he returned to Japan and became the chef of Hugo Desnoyer Ebisu in Ebisu. Then, he opened Cellar Fête in May 2018.  The restaurant’s name is a coined word combining ‘Cellar’ (wine cellar) and ‘Fête’ (which means ‘festival’ in French), expressing the chef’s desire to create a festive setting where guests can enjoy the bistro cuisine he explored in his earlier career in France.

The specialty of Cellar Fête is undeniably Tartare of Raw Beef. Although beef tartare is the national dish of France popular among local food lovers, the one created by Chef Saita, who has worked at the top three locations in the ranking of the best tartare restaurants in Paris published by the French magazine, Le Figaro Magazine, is so amazing that you cannot miss it.  The main course features the chef’s selection of natural beef, coming from cattle raised on nutritious grass pastures with plenty of exercise, fresh water, and sunshine.  To get the best beef comparable to the type he sourced in France, the chef makes regular trips to Hokkaido and Iwate to make his own choice of beef raised in a natural environment. He also carefully controls water activity and heat while cooking it.

Guests can choose wines from the wine cellar stocked with a great selection of wines, including many natural wines from French producers with whom the chef has built family-like relationships. 


The main dining area with large windows that create a sense of spaciousness has table seating for 22 guests in addition to 6 counter seats, while the private dining room seats up to 10 guests. The walls and furniture in orange shades add a touch of warmth, making the dining experience with your close friends, coworkers, or family all the more homey and pleasant.  Please enjoy natural beef and wine in that festive mood at Cellar Fête!


Please note that it may take time to serve your order because all the food is prepared by a single chef. Please sit back and enjoy your wine while waiting.
Cellar Fête is the perfect place to entertain clients. Please contact the restaurant for details.
The restaurant may not be able to accommodate allergies or preferences at the last minute. So, please ask in advance if you have any concerns.

244727.longDescription:
“Ranmaru” is a sushi restaurant located in a quiet residential area near Fudomae Station in Meguro, Tokyo. According to the desire of the master of “Sushi Rinda”, located in front of Fudo-mae, "I wanted to make a shop where young craftsmen could make sushi". As a result, “Ranmaru” opened as a sister-restaurant, originally serving Uwajima udon and sushi. Today, chef Yukichika Shimazu, at the young age of 25, is in charge of restaurant. 

The rice for the sushi is Koshihikari from Niigata. The rice is cooked in a pot under pressure, trapping moisture in the rice grains, and is mixed with a blend of rice vinegar and red vinegar with a small amount of sugar. The best seafood of the day is purchased through any means necessary, including shipping it directly from local fishing ports, as well as Toyosu market. The special Futomaki roll, "Ranmaru rolled sushi", that is served at the end, uses plenty of tuna, from lean to medium fatty meat. Another popular dish is the "Ranmaru special rolled sushi", in which sea urchin and salmon roe are placed on top of the "Ranmaru Rolled Sushi".

There are around 10 types of sake, including seasonal sake, carefully selected from all over Japan. Champagne and wine are also available. In addition, there is a variety of Uwajima mandarin orange juice from Ehime prefecture that is made at the home of Yuta Kono, the chef of “Sushi Rinda”. You can enjoy it as a soft drink or as a dessert.

The restaurant has 10 counter seats. The counter, coated with Japanese cypress, is set at a high position as a remnant of its past as an udon restaurant, so it is a perfect position for taking photos of sushi. Conversations with chef Shimazu naturally becomes lively when dining here. We would like you to enjoy the youthful “Ranmaru” for your private use with your fellow sushi lovers and family members, as well as for dates and entertaining.

"Sushi Rinda" is 10-minute walk from Meguro Station, situated close to Meguro Fudoson Temple. The location, a short walk from the station, will excite the gourmand spirit in you that delights in going to enjoy sushi.
 In 2024, to coincide with its 10th anniversary, it was redesigned and made even more powerful.

244204.longDescription:
In such a big city like Shinjuku, it is surprisingly hard to find a quiet restaurant like "Chiso Fufu". Located in Shinjuku 3-Chome, "Chiso Fufu" is the place where you can forget about the hustle and bustle outside of the restaurant and enjoy the Japanese cuisine. Inside of the restaurant, the sophisticated wooden interior makes the space very elegant. It is a Japanese restaurant where customers can spend relaxing time with friends and family. 

Chef Katsumi Hattori is an experienced chef who worked at Hotel Apex Toya (now The Windsor Hotel Toya Resort and Spa), Hotel New Otani and Japanese Cuisine Kamogawa for 25 years. According to the chef, people in the old days used to say “embrace the season with your heart", and he tries to cook while keeping that in his mind. This idea is where the name of the restaurant came from, "the wind that brings different seasons" and "enjoys the seasonal food". The menu is changed every two weeks according to the Solar terms that are a more detailed transition of the season. 


The course begins with "Ichiban-dashi (first brewing of soup stock)" that is seasoned with sake and salt.  The ingredients for the main course is purchased every day from Tsukiji fish market. Serving the seasonal vegetables, the best taste of the season is presented. "Chiso Fufu" serves unique Japanese cuisine that does not follow the traditional format in Japanese cuisine, for example, it does not serve the essence of Japanese cuisine, "the bowl". The restaurant has about 15 different kinds of sake, 5 different kinds of champagne and 8 different kinds of white wine to match with the seasonal Japanese cuisine. Furthermore, there is not only counter-seat but also private room and box sofa seat where customers can use for a casual gathering. Please enjoy spending luxurious time while enjoying the seasonal ingredients in this Japanese restaurant.

244664.longDescription:
Edomae sushi restaurant "Nishi" is located near Tokyo's Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden. Tatsuhiro Nishi, also the owner of the branch sushi restaurants "Takumi Tatsuhiro" and "Sushi Band", opened this restaurant that mainly serve lunch with the intention of focusing on natural wines, “Atsukan” (warmed Japanese sake), and sushi.

After building up experience working at a Kanazawa Japanese restaurant and a Tokyo sushi restaurant, Nishi went on to work at the renowned Yotsuya sushi restaurant "Sushi-sho" before opening his own restaurant. He first opened "Takumi Tatsuhiro" in 2012, followed by its sister restaurant "Sushi Band" in 2017. Finally, in 2019, he opened his third restaurant "Nishi", named after himself, across from "Takumi Tatsuhiro". The restaurant is mainly open during the day and only accept reservations at night if you reserve the entire restaurant for 6 to 8 people.

The ingredients are sourced from the same producers used by "Takumi Tatsuhiro", and rather than serving side dishes and nigiri sushi alternately, the restaurant's set course focuses on nigiri, with 12 kinds of nigiri as well as rolled sushi, egg, and steamed dishes. The seafood is sourced from nearby Toyosu or shipped directly from locations all around Japan, including Hokkaido, Ishikawa, and Kyushu. The sushi rice is Hanamizuki rice from Nishi's native Ishikawa. The sushi vinegar is a blend of Kyoto Io Jozu red Fuji vinegar and rice vinegar—a Tatsuhiro brand original. The wine selection consists of naturally made wines from Japan, Italy, and the United States, with three to four varieties of red and white respectively available by the glass. The selection of 12-13 seasonal Japanese sake is best enjoyed warm, and can even be warmed to your preferred temperature.

With eight counter seats, the lounge style interior creates a sense of playfulness. The design makes liberal use of Japanese cypress, while the arch-shaped wall constructed of roof tiles serves as an accent. The restaurant's exterior sports a chic, predominantly black design. During the cherry blossom season, small windows allow diners to enjoy the view of the flowers from one area of the restaurant. A great choice for a sushi lunch with your coworkers, family or friends. Enjoy superior time at the restaurant's relaxed atmosphere together with luxurious sushi and sake.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Shinjuku Ghoenmae, Exit 2(Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line)

243774.longDescription: Shinjuku Kappo Nakajima serves innovative new dishes while offering traditional Japanese cuisine made with seasonal ingredients. The current owner Sadaharu Nakajima's grandfather Teijiro Nakajima was the first head chef of Hoshigaoka Saryo, the exclusive high-class restaurant that was opened in 1925 and run by Rosanjin Kitaoji. Teijiro's son branched off and opened Nakajima in Shinjuku. The current owner Sadaharu is his heir, and his hereditary culinary talent is evident in the food. Sadaharu Nakajima and his restaurant has received a great deal of exposure on television, in print, and in other media. Their specialty dish is the Owan. The owner lavishes his greatest skill on this soup dish, which he considers the embodiment of Japanese cuisine. All the dishes are prepared with great care, and seasoned to precise standards. This renowned restaurant is a short walk from Shinjiku station but has a relaxed atmosphere that is very different from the bustle of the rest of Shinjuku. This is a perfect place for entertaining guests with delicious Japanese food. * Nakajima does not accept lunch reservation, queuing at lunch time is the only possible way to enjoy their lunch menu. ------------------------------------------------------------------ Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? No room charge is required for our private dining room. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? Our private dining room can be reserved for a party of 2 to 12 people. ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? We offer both the table and chair (Western style) and the Horigotatsu style (a low table over a recessed floor where you can sit in the same way you would sit in a western style chair). ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? We ask you to remove shoes in our Horigotatsu private dining room. ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customizations for vegetarian, vegan or low calories. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We do not offer children's menus. This is only possible when children can eat the same course as adults. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? 244189.longDescription: "Takumi Tatsuhiro" is an Edomae-style sushi restaurant located near Shinjuku Gyoen in Tokyo. Following the tradition of the famous sushi restaurant "Sushi Sho", customers can enjoy the unique style of enjoying side dishes in between sushi. Before opening his own sushi restaurant in August 2012, chef Tatsuhiro Nishi has gained a lot of experiences in Japanese restaurant in Kanazawa and several sushi restaurants in Tokyo, including "Sushisho" in Yotsuya. He not only gets his ingredients from Tsukiji, but also directly from Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Ishikawa. It is very important that the vineger rice balance with the seafood, the chef uses the "Hana Mizuki" rice from Ishikawa Prefecture, which is also his hometown. The chef visited the rice field, which is in a mountain that is surrounded by abundant nature, and talked with the producers before purchasing the rice. And for the sushi vinegar, the chef uses the blend of Fuji vinegar's red vinegar and rice vinegar from Kyoto's "Iio Jozo Vinegar Brewery". The vinegar brings out the flavor of the rice that matches with the seafood and creates a great combination. The chef serves the "omakase" course with the ten appetizers in between the 12 sushis, this tempo prevents customers from getting tired and full while satisfied with the course. There are ten seats at the main counter. The interior is decorated with beautiful polished wood which gives customers a comfortable environment. This restaurant is not only suitable for sushi dates and with a group of people, but also alone. There is a private room (up to 6 guests) where customers can use to bring important guests. From June 2017, one-minute walk from "Takumi Tatsuhiro", their other sushi restaurant "Sushi Band" is opened.

244259.longDescription: Tsunahachi, a long-established tempura restaurant, was established in Shinjuku in 1924 (Taisho 13). While valuing the best performance and heartfelt hospitality by its skilled chefs, Tsunahachi has sometimes innovated the tempura industry with innovative approaches. Tsunohatsu-an" was established in 1991 as a place to provide the best service and taste, and was relocated to the same Shinjuku location in 2022. The restaurant consists of not only counter seats – the charm of tempura restaurants – but also table seats that can seat up to 30 people for private parties and completely private rooms, creating a space for customers to have a slow, leisurely experience. The ingredients used range from specially ordered refined sesame seed oil and fresh seafood purchased at Tsukiji market in the morning, fresh vegetables delivered directly from contracted farms such as Ebihara Farm. Those who stand in the kitchen are the most skilled of the chefs in Tsunahachi. Each tempura dish, deep-fried and presented at the perfect timing, is the result of the finest ingredients and skills – a true work of art. There are always about 10 kinds of sake and a wide variety of wine available, making it possible to enjoy pairing tempura with sake and wine.. The hospitality of the female staff wearing kimonos makes customers feel at home, as the entire experience goes above and beyond the concept of “highest quality tempura at a reasonable cost”. ​​ The fine service of women serving in kimono is also comfortable and gives us a satisfying feeling over the concept of "extremely fine tempura at a casual price". Access to restaurant is a convenient 3-minute walk from Shinjuku-Sanchome Station, making it a reliable restaurant for all occasions, from business use such as business entertainment and dinners, to family use such as celebrations and memorial services, and even for guests from overseas. *Private rooms are available for private and large parties. Private room reservation begins with 2~25 guests, private parties with X~Y guests. For details, please fill out a request in this inquiry form. You can also contact us by e-mail at info@pocket-concierge.jp
