245499.longDescription:
Within walking distance from Shibuya Station, Luna e Gatto is an Italian restaurant in Shinsencho, which is also known as Ura-Shibuya.  To delight the taste buds of guests, Chef Keisuke Yamanaka, who honed his culinary skills at a renowned restaurant in Nishi Azabu, brings out best in ingredients that captivate his senses.

Chef Yamanaka worked at DAL-MATTO (currently known as P-MATTO), a renowned Italian restaurant, in Nishi Azabu for 17 years, including 10 years as Chef, and opened his own restaurant, Luna e Gatto, in July 2024.   The restaurant’s name, Luna e Gatto, which means the moon and cat in Italian, is taken from his memory of seeing a cat looking up at the full moon in Venice, Italy.  This name also reflects his commitment to creating a restaurant where guests can feel at home like a cat sitting comfortably in a cozy corner.

The chef’s selection menu offers seven courses, starting with an amuse bouche, followed by cold appetizers, a specialty dish, a cold pasta, an entrée, and a refreshing gelato and concluding with a hot pasta.  The specialty dish features jumbo mushrooms from Hasegawa Nosan in Shizuoka Prefecture. Chef Yamanaka came upon these jumbo mushrooms during his apprenticeship and immediately fell in love with them for their thick meat and robust flavor that would harmonize with even the most substantial, flavorful fillings, such as foie gras terrine and minced chicken. Since his first encounter with this ingredient, he has aspired to feature it in a specialty dish for his restaurant someday. In this sense, these jumbo mushrooms are imperative in describing Luna e Gatto. They are prepared in different ways, depending on the season – sometimes wrapped in pie or filo dough and sometimes used as dishes for gratins. Another of the restaurant’s signature dishes, pasta, featuring seasonal produce and served in both cold and hot forms before and after the entrée, makes the full-course menu worth it. Guests can also add another pasta course if they want.

The alcohol menu offers about 30 selections of wine, including natural wine, mainly from Italy, as well as Italian bottled beer, such as Peroni Nastro Azzurro, and Houou Biden Fruit Wine from Kobayashi Shuzo in Tochigi.  The soft drink menu includes Organic Japanese Black Tea from Marushichi Seicha. The dining area is discreet, complemented by an indigo blue plaster wall. Boasting a warm wood counter (seating up to six guests) as well as a small two-seat counter at the far end, the restaurant can be used for various purposes, such as chatting with fellow diners, meeting someone new, and indulging in an exclusive date night. Please enjoy the exquisite dishes prepared by Chef Yamanaka in a laid-back setting at Luna e Gatto.
nearestStations: 4 minutes walk from Shinsen Station on the Keio Inokashira Line

243700.longDescription:
“81” is widely recognized as a space where gastronomy transcends its boundaries and merges with art. Chef Kenji Nagashima, who trained at the legendary three-star restaurant “El Bulli” in Spain, founded the restaurant in 2012 to embody his own vision, earning one star from a world-renowned gourmet guide the following year. Having established a strong reputation both in Japan and internationally, he reopened “81” in Shirokane on December 1, 2025, marking the beginning of a renewed chapter.  

 

Nagashima’s concept is “More than a restaurant.” It defines the venue not simply as a place to dine, but as a living laboratory where art, ideas, and culture intersect. Executive Chef Paco La Monica, whose career spans leading kitchens such as “Noma” in Copenhagen, “Gaggan” in Bangkok, and “KOKS” in the Faroe Islands, brings a sensibility that moves fluidly between Italian culinary tradition and Japanese kaiseki. His perspective resonates with Nagashima’s philosophy, giving rise to a new expression of gastronomy. Brand engagement is directed by Alessio Gorny, who unites art, events, and hospitality, elevating the space and the guest experience into a seamless narrative. 
 
Upon entering, guests are first welcomed into a reception-gallery space featuring seasonal exhibitions that evolve in dialogue with the menu. Each season unfolds as a cohesive story, where the exhibition and cuisine respond to one another. The cuisine is presented as a seasonal course featuring ingredients at their peak, products connected to meaningful relationships, producers, and regions, and a diverse range of elements. Pairings are designed to complement the culinary worldview, stimulating not only the palate but also the intellect. Guests are then guided to an intimate 12-seat chef’s table, where a “vertical journey” between floors allows cuisine and art to actively interact, giving rise to an experience that could never be created independently. Tableware and cutlery used since the restaurant’s founding further embody its philosophy.  
 
The exterior is deliberately left untouched, creating a striking contrast with the immersive interior world. For those with an artistic mindset and for guests who seek experience itself as a form of meaning, “81” is not merely a restaurant, but a cultural platform for the future—where dining becomes a ritual and creativity is shared.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Shirokanedai Station

244450.longDescription:
""Akiyama"" opened in 2018 near 'Kitasato Hospital' in the Shirokane-takanawa area of Tokyo’s Minato Ward. Running by the owner-chef Hideto Akiyama, who found himself getting more and more interested in fish after working at an izakaya, a type of Japanese-style pub, that centered its menu on fish and other seafood. From there, he went on to spend 5 years training at “Sushi Shin,” a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, neighborhood. After working with fine-quality fish and polishing up his culinary skills, he decided to push his skillset even further by spending 4 years building up experience and diving deeper into Japanese-style cooking at a world gourmet guide award Japanese cuisine restaurant called “Higuchi,” located in the Jingumae area of Tokyo.

When the Chef Akiyama decided to open up a place of his own, he knew he wanted to have a small eatery that was not like a typical sushi restaurant or classic Japanese-style restaurant that served Kaiseki cuisine and the like. Chef Akiyama says that “My goal was to start a restaurant where guests could casually stop by on the regular and enjoy delicious food in an easygoing atmosphere. I wanted to offer great food and drinks without tying myself down to one particular style of cooking.” He travels to Tsukiji fish market each day to pick up fresh, seasonal ingredients for his omakase (chef’s choice) courses. He mainly centers on seafood for these courses and puts together sashimi and flame-broiled dishes, as well as boiled foods and seasonal vegetables. Each dish in this special course meal is served one by one in small portion sizes. When it comes to Oshinogi dishes, which are small appetizers served during a course meal, he puts together a changing selection of seasonal specials, including sushi rolls, hand-rolled sushi, pressed sushi sticks, and bamboo leaf rice cakes. Each course is finished off with handmade soba, freshly cooked rice, and other exquisite ingredients. The food here is simply wholesome and profoundly delicious, without the slightest bit of ostentatiousness. Guests will also be happy to find that the size of each meal is tailored to their appetite. And for drinks, they offer a seasonal variety of specially selected Japanese sake to pair with each meal.

Inside guests will find a stylish dining space with a mortar counter and vivid indigo blue walls with Japanese paper. Dishware includes items from the Edo and Heian periods decorated with calligraphy and more, which adds to an already chic dining experience. As for seating, there are only 7 seats at the counter. ""Akiyama"" welcomes guests with friendly banter and an immersive dining space where friends and couples, as well as guests dining alone and travelers from abroad,  can all enjoy their meal together.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245067.longDescription:
Hidden on a quiet back alley in Shirogane, Rama serves chef Katsuhiro Aoki’s innovative cuisine, an innovative hybrid of traditional Italian recipes and Japanese influences served to guests over the counter.

Chef Aoki graduated from Ecole Tsuji Tokyo’s Master College for Italian and French cuisine and joined Guccina, a long-established Italian trattoria in Sangenjaya to hone his culinary skills. After being promoted to sous chef, he left the restaurant for Italy, where he learned authentic Italian cuisine at renowned restaurants, such as Trattoria Baldini, Vecchia Bettola, and Osteria S. Nicola in Florence, Ristorante alla Madonna in Venice, and Ristorante Tullio in Rome. After returning to Japan, he worked as chef at Ristorante Felicita in Omotesando and HirraRi in Sangenjaya, and then became main chef at Rama when it opened in 2019.

Chef Aoki serves an innovative spin on Italian cuisine by combining the authentic Italian techniques he learned in Italy with Japanese influences. For example, soy sauce and miso is made from dried tomatoes, while Japanese stock is derived from dried marlin instead of dried bonito flakes. The seafood and vegetables are delivered fresh, most directly from fishing ports and farms. White fish is filleted on the spot via the Shinkei-jime method to keep the meat fresh and delivered from Hakodate, Hokkaido, while the vegetables are sourced from Kamakura.

The prix-fixe menu combines Italian dishes such as acqua pazza, carpaccio, and pasta, with sushi featuring sushi rice seasoned with sherry wine vinegar and homemade soy sauce made from dried tomatoes. The sushi conjured up by the chef right in front of you is unmissable.

The dining room is designed with inspiration from traditional Japanese tearooms. At the chef’s table, awaits an R-shaped counter with eight seats, where guests are warmly welcomed and invited to enjoy watching their food being prepared by the talented chef. 

The restaurant invites guests to enjoy innovative Italian cuisine presented by chef Aoki with friends, family, a partner, or fellow epicures.

244985.longDescription:
Close to the Ebisu 3-chome intersection and a short walk from Hiroo Station and Ebisu Stations, the location of this yakitori restaurant is subtly given away by a sign in the shape of an egg. Here, the rare parts of the chicken are exquisitely grilled at high heat over Kishu Binchotan charcoal, producing flavor to impress even the most discerning of epicures. 

After graduating from university, chef-owner Shiro Izawa started his training at the long-established yakitori restaurant Sakuraya in Hatchobori, before working at the Yotsuya branch of the Tsukiji Miyagawa Honten. In 2000, he opened Shirokane Toritama Honkan. 

Earning a reputation for perfectly grilled yakitori, the restaurant gained a reputation for its flavor in the blink of an eye, and it gained popularity both in Japan and abroad as it opened in Hong Kong, Singapore, Bangkok, Malaysia and two stores in Guangzhou, as well as Shirokane Toritama Bekkan and Shirokane Toritama Kagurazaka, where Izawa sent his apprentices.

"I think we are the first time to grill rare parts of chicken", says Izawa. There are over 30 kinds of rare parts that can be enjoyed, such as kinchaku, intestines, azuki (kidney), and more. They are grilled on Kishu Binchotan charcoal and flavored individually. There are even some parts that Izawa named by himself.

Izawa’s sourcing of ingredients is also perfect. He is confident in his purchasing power, as he is connected to a chicken producer and a vegetable vendor in Tsukiji Market that he has known since he was young. The hens' tail (misaki), which is prepared with garlic butter, is chewy and has been featured in overseas press. Classic oyakodon (chicken and egg over rice) is seasoned with shuyu, amazake and Kumamoto's akazake, is a popular dish that was introduced in a recipe book on television. 

The chef is also particular about sake. The restaurant offers around 25 kinds of hard-to-find Japanese sakes like Yamagata Juyondai and Niigata Higan. As for the sake cups, they use Reikan Hanabi glasses made of Marumotaki earthenware, which emit fireworks when cold sake is poured, adding a sense of fun.

Inside the restaurant, which is unified in monochrome and the sounds of jazz, the 20-seat U-shape counter surrounds the grill. Shirokane Toritama Honkan is perfect for parties and dates with family, friends, and colleagues, where guests can enjoy yakitori unique to the restaurant, along with favorite drinks.

244798.longDescription:
In a quiet residential area about an 8-minute walk from Shirokane-Takanawa Station in Tokyo, the noren curtain lit by warm lights of a 1-star sushi restaurant “Sushi Matsuura" welcomes visitors. Osamu Matsuura, the young chef, moved from working at a fisheries company to becoming a sushi chef. In addition to working at several sushi restaurants, he was also responsible for launching new restaurants in Hawaii and Los Angeles for the "Sushi Ginza Onodera" chain, thus honing his skills on the world stage. After returning to Japan, he worked at "Sushi Masuda" (now closed) in Omotesando and was then in charge of a private-room counter in Ebisu’s "Sushi Kurusu", attracting many fans. He launched his own restaurant in September 2019 where he has been providing highly satisfying omakase course with the hope that young people will also enjoy authentic Edomae-style sushi.

"Sushi Matsuura" uses the finest ingredients that are purchased from Toyosu market every morning and employs aging techniques that require time and effort to bring out the umami of the seafood. The preparation techniques and creative talent the chef learned from famous restaurants shine. The rice used for sushi is an original blend prepared by a rice meister. Koshihikari and Akita Komachi varieties from Yamagata are cooked al dente in a hagama traditional rice pot. Two types of red vinegar made from Junmai Daiginjo sake lees from Wakayama of different ages are blended and only salt added to bring out the intrinsic flavor of rice. The house specialty is the conger eel nigiri sushi, and the restaurant has access to top-grade conger eels all year round thanks to the relationship of trust it has built with its buyers. Sake-steamed belt fish is also popular. Chef Matsuura goes to buy sake himself, and he always prepares about 10 kinds, such as carefully selected Junmai and Junmai Ginjo varieties known for their outstanding rice flavor. "Sushi Matsuura" stocks different types of sake each time rather than a selection of well-known brands for guests to enjoy.

The clean and bright wood-themed interior is filled with warmth reflecting Chef Matsuura’s character. At the L-shaped counter with eight to nine seats, you can enjoy conversing with the chef in true Edomae-style fashion while enjoying sushi and sake. This restaurant is suitable for a wide range of occasions, such as gatherings of family and friends, as well as for dates and business entertaining. It is recommended as a sushi restaurant to spend time with your loved ones and for showing hospitality to overseas guests.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

244671.longDescription:
Located a 10-minute walk from Shirokanedai Station. Sushi Mizuno stands unobtrusively in a quiet residential neighborhood. Yoshiyuki Mizuno, the owner-chef, spent 20 years training at a long-established sushi restaurant in Nihonbashi before opening Sushi Shibadaimon Mizuno in Daimon, Tokyo. Seeking a new stage, he relocated it to a back street in Shirokane in 2018.
“I want people to savor Edo-style sushi done right while they enjoy the location with its 'A sushi restaurant here?' sense of novelty,” says Chef Mizuno. The seafood is sourced from Toyosu Market. He uses the same suppliers as the restaurant where he learned his craft. Their long-term relationship and trust enables him to source fine seafood. He uses only red vinegar and salt to enable a traditional flavor for the sushi rice. The rice is a flavorful variety from Yamagata called Tsuyahime, which is aged in an ice house. He then combines two varieties of red vinegar, aged for 8 years, to create sushi rice with a clean flavor, pleasing to the palate. The prepared sushi rice is place in a specially made straw carrier to help controlling the temperature. “Nigiri-zushi is the leading part in Edo-style sushi. I place a lot of importance on customers’ enjoyment of the sushi,” says Chef Mizuno, and as he adds on, guests can enjoy his perfectly prepared nigiri-zushi here. In addition, the sake is personally chosen by Mizuno himself. There is a selection of 7 to 8 varieties of sake that are chosen to match with the sushi and other Japanese side dishes.
The interior features beautiful Japanese carpentry such as a Japanese cypress counter and wickerwork ceiling, with only 7 counter-seat, which can also be reserved for private party. The copper framed lantern placed at the entrance was created by a Kyoto artisan, and Chef Mizuno’s ideas are reflected on everything, from the interior furnishings to the kitchen utensils. “This restaurant is by no means exclusive, please feel free to make casual reservations,” says Chef Mizuno. Guests can enjoy classic Edo-style sushi in an unpretentious atmosphere at this secluded restaurant.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Shirokanedai Station (Toei Mita Line)

244422.longDescription:
"Sushi Nagashima," a sushi restaurant located on a street near Kitasato University in the center of the high-class Tokyo residential area of ​Shirokane, opened in 2017.

The Owner-chef Tomoharu Arai’s story up until he became an independent chef is somewhat unique. After working from the age of 15 as a fisherman in Nagashima, Kagoshima for 3 years, he moved to Tokyo. He graduated from a culinary academy and went on to work for 4 years at a traditional Japanese restaurant in Tokyo and 6 years at a sushi restaurant in Nihonbashi. After that, following two years at the Ginza branch of "Sushi Ginza Onodera," he worked for 2 and a half years in Hawaii. And after serving as a proprietor there, he worked at a restaurant in New York before returning to Japan. Wanting to “create a warm and homely restaurant which puts the customer first”, he established "Sushi Nagashima" in this neighborhood with its calm atmosphere. The name of the restaurant is taken from the place name of Nagashima where he got his start, and it evokes the very warm-hearted personality of Mr. Arai.

The courses provided alternate between snacks and sushi, based around 6 to 7 snack dishes and about 15 sushi dishes. Three types of tuna, purchased mainly from "Yamayuki" in Tsukiji, are served as standard – lean red “Akami”, medium-fatty “chu-toro,2 and fatty “o-toro”. Sea urchin is purchased from various areas, such as Kyushu and Hokkaido, depending on the season, and served in “Gunkan” (battleship) or “nigiri” (fish on rice) style. With the expertise of former fishermen, Mr. Arai matches these exquisite ingredients with a very particular kind of vinegared rice made by blending two types of rice and red vinegar made by Yokoi Vinegar. The sweetness of each and every grain of rice and the rich taste of red vinegar are harmoniously combined with the conscientiously prepared Edo-mae sushi toppings.

"I don’t want it to be a sushi restaurant where you’re nervous about eating, but rather a place where you can relax and enjoy yourself," says Mr. Arai. The interior has a Japanese cypress counter with spacious seating for seven, and it is very comfortable. It’s ideal for casual entertaining or a business dinner, for a sushi date or whenever you want to enjoy blissful sushi with that important someone.

245307.longDescription:
Nestled in a tranquil residential neighborhood of Shirokane, Tokyo, TATSUMI is accessed by stairs outside the building. As you pass through the door at the top of the stairs, you will be greeted with a refined, understated interior.
TATSUMI was opened in 2021 by a renowned chef, Tatsumi Watanabe, who honed his skills as a sous-chef at Il Teatrino da Salone in Hibiya and as a chef at K+ (Kagero Plus), an Italian restaurant in Nishi-Azabu affiliated with Restaurant l'equateur. Now, with his own restaurant, he creates his ideal Italian cuisine, putting his heart and soul into each dish.
 
“I try to create simple, plain dishes,” says Chef Watanabe. “So, I take care not to arrange dishes merely for decoration or add any unnecessary frills.” He is also particular about ingredients, sourcing precious vegetables from Osaka and seafood fresh from the sea in Fukuoka. Carefully selected from around Japan, they taste even better and richer when combined with the chef’s creative flair. Especially, “Consommé of Shamo Chicken from Okukuji, Ibaraki,” a popular dish made from shamo breast, has such a deep, rich flavor that it can tempt the appetite. Another signature dish, Raviolone (which means “big ravioli”), is topped with a whole egg yolk from Tokushima. Once you cut into the egg, the yolk runs out, captivating the palate of all those who taste it.
 Chef Watanabe’s hearty dishes are enhanced when paired with wines selected by Sommelier Yuji Tsutsumi. With some 400 bottles in stock, mostly from Bourgogne, the restaurant also offers pairing options. The drink menu also includes Italian old vintages, popular Japanese whiskies, and soft drinks.
 
The restaurant’s interior is as simple as its dishes, without any extra frills. Only the walls are adorned with viridian green accents, a favorite of the chef. The food is also simply presented in lustrous white ceramics, served from the open kitchen at the stylish counter (seating up to eight guests).
Enjoy Chef Watanabe’s dishes prepared with heart and soul with your family, significant other, friends, or colleagues in the cozy atmosphere of the restaurant TATSUMI.

243765.longDescription:
Located near the Ebisu 3-chome intersection, Taira is a sushi restaurant housed in a renovated traditional Japanese home, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere.
Though modest in scale, the space feels refined and unconfined, creating a calm and elegant setting.

The Edomae-style sushi showcases the natural flavors of seasonal ingredients. The sushi rice is prepared with both red and white vinegar, selected and used according to each topping to achieve the ideal balance.
Its signature dish, the kinmedai battera (pressed sushi), is known for a flavor that cannot be found elsewhere and is also popular as a take-home gift.

The counter seating offers ample depth and comfort, and the entire restaurant can be reserved for private use. A private room is available for up to eight guests. It is a perfect option for occasions such as business gathering and special anniversaries.

The experienced chef at Wagyu Yakiniku KIM offers quality meat and suggests KIM's original ways to enjoy Yakiniku. The restaurant is at good location just three minutes on foot from Shirokane-takanawa Station. 

The recommended way to enjoy Yakiniku is to change sauces for different cuts. For example,  thick cuts with a pinch of salt, and soft cuts with citrus-based sauce or herbs. One of the attraction of Wagyu Yakiniku KIM is to compare the tastes of a variety of cuts with specific sauces. In addition, the main attraction of Wagyu Yakiniku KIM is the specially stocked-in Japanese Black Beef that is rare and particularly higher in quality among A5-level Wagyu Beef. The must-try gem at Wagyu Yakiniku KIM is the newly classic item, the Rare Hamburg Steak. Roughly yet thinly sliced meat is made into a ball of patty, then grilled crispy outside and rare and juicy inside. 

The restaurant with a relaxed atmosphere features private room for parties up to six and is perfect for casual dining, entertainment and for get-togethers with yakiniku grill fans. You'd only have to know this premier Yakiniku in Shirokane-Takanawa area to be a true gourmet foodie.

Located in a tranquil residential area a five-minute walk from Shiroganedai Station, CIRPAS is helmed by Chef Takashi Yoshida, who learned the essence and art of French cuisine in Japan and France.

Yoshida boasts a distinguished career working at pomme d’Adam in Marunouchi Hotel for four years, before going to France to hone his culinary skills at Dominique Bouchet in Paris, and coming back to Japan to work at Pierre Gagnaire in Akasaka. Then, in 2015, he was offered the position of sous chef of Dominique Bouchet Tokyo in Ginza by Dominique Bouchet, with whom he apprenticed in Paris. He continued working at new restaurants opened by Dominique Bouchet until March 2021, when he stepped down from his executive chef position. He made his name even better known with George, an online cooking channel launched on the world’s largest video platform in 2020. His professional culinary skills and humorous way of talking made the channel an immediate smash hit, attracting 600,000 subscribers.

In November 2022, Yoshida finally opened his long-awaited restaurant, CIRPAS, to present his gastronomic philosophy. The restaurant’s name, CIRPAS, is coined from two words, “circulation” and “passion,” to represent the chef’s ambition to create dishes with innovative originality and passion as well as a respect for French classics.

CIRPAS offers prix fixe meals of around 11 courses. The seafood, vegetables, and meats featured on the menu are sourced from hunters and farmers with whom the chef has established strong personal relationships, allowing their philosophies and enthusiasm to be conveyed through the dishes. These ingredients are prepared using different cooking methods, such as charcoal grilling and hot iron plate cooking, to explore the different textures of the ingredients.

The wine selection includes options from France and other countries around the world. We recommend unique pairings, including Japanese sake. Non-alcoholic pairings, based on seasonal fruits and teas, are also available.

The interior is modern and chic with grey colors. On the marble countertop (with eight stools), the dishes are served in original tableware created by Kamachi Toho in Arita, Saga. Also equipped with a private dining room seating up to four guests, CIRPAS can be used for various occasions, either personal or business-related. Please treat your palate with the exquisite dishes and immerse yourself in the unique gastronomic world of CIRPAS.
nearestStations: 4-minute walk from Shirokanedai Station (Exit 2) on Namboku Line

244066.longDescription:
REQUINQUER is a small, single detached French restaurant located in a small alley just off the Ichou Namiki and Platinum Dori, a mere 3 minutes walk from Shirokanedai Station. ""REQUINQUER"" means ""to perk up"" in French and is intended to convey the desire for guests to enjoy the food, wine and conversation to be had and leave with smiles on their faces. It is a venue where guests can relax and calm while enjoying traditional French cuisine prepared with seasonal ingredients.

After training in the art of preparing French cuisine at venue such as the Keio Plaza Hotel in Shinjuku and Restaurant ALADDIN in Hiroo, chef Soichi Furuya served for five years as Chef at BISTROT DE LA CITE, also located in Hiroo, before opening REQUINQUER in Shirokanedai in 2009. He has been won award for his second consecutive year in the world gourmet guide Tokyo 2016. The spirited chef continues to charm connoisseurs with his sincere, down-to-earth cuisine prepared using fresh seasonal ingredients. The restaurant also features a selection of approximately 100 carefully-selected labels of wine, with an emphasis on French imports.

With its warm, orange-themed interior, the venue features a casual atmosphere with an open kitchen on the first floor and a relaxing dining space with tables on the second floor. Easy to visit for everything from everyday dining to dates, it is also possible to rent out the entire venue for private gatherings, after-parties, convocations and other such events, making it a versatile spot for almost all occasions.

244482.longDescription:
""Restaurant L'allium,"" which has taken over the former site of old French restaurant ""OZAWA"" in Shirokane-dai, opened in 2018. The owner-chef, Yoshiaki Shindo, practiced French cuisine under ""French Kaiseki Shukouju"" (presently closed) in Motomachi, Yokohama, went on to ""L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon"" in Roppongi, ""Bon Pinard"" in Moto-Azabu, and returned as the sous chef of ""L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon"" in 2007. In the following year 2008, ""L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon"" received world gourmet guide award, and after becoming at chef at ""Gentil H"", it received world gourmet guide award in the first year.

The concept is ""modern grande Maison"". What chef Shindo aims for is the stability of Grande Maison (a term used in Japan for the highest–class French restaurants), and a relaxing atmosphere that isn't too tense. ""In a time in which authentic Grande Maison is starting to disappear, I want to pass on the 30 years of history that my great senior Ozawa chef has built up, and provide the finest service,"" he states with a sense of determination. He focuses his dishes on valuing the ingredients in season and bringing out their natural flavors to the fullest. He selects ingredients from all over Japan, and in regards to the vegetables, there are many that he buys directly from the producers, based on their varieties. Mr. Shindo's specialty is a dish of black abalone from Shimane prefecture, that is slowly steamed for 8 hours to create the perfect softness. It is a dish that has lasted since the ""Gentil H"" days, with many guests visiting just to have a taste of it. Many guests visit the restaurant for this reason. The wine selection is centered on Burgundy and Champagne.

The interior, inspired by concert halls, are made for sounds to echo against the wood. The movements of the guests create sounds that become one—the music of the restaurant. There are counter seats by the open kitchen, 16~20 table seats, and a luxurious carpeted private room (for 2-6 people). We would like you to dine with the silverware of Christofle, passed down from ""OZAWA,"" and ponder on the possibilities that ""modern grande Maison"" holds, along with the history of ""OZAWA.""

Shirokanedai Kobayashi is a Japanese restaurant located only ten-minute walk from the Tokyo Metro Shirokanedai Station or a five-minute walk from Yebisu Garden Place and Westin Hotel. The owner-chef, with 22 years of experience in Japanese cuisine in Kobe, who never compromise when it comes to food, will greet diners kindly along with the proprietress. 

The restaurant only serves Omakase Course that changes monthly. From the delicate soup stock to dishes prepared to elevate flavors of the ingredients that are only available in Kansai region, the course itself is unforgettable. With a variety of sake and Japanese wines available, diners can also enjoy pairings between food and drink.

Counter seating is available for diners who would like to enjoy watching the preparation works by the owner-chef. This Japanese restaurant will surely be the top choice on the reservation list for business dining and group outings.

243827.longDescription:
Wami Daisuke has been open since 2010. Its unique location - a detached house tucked away in a back alley - gives it a special ambience.

There are only four private rooms. Each has a warm and tranquil atmosphere with wood as the main design element.

Due to the limited number of guests they can accommodate, they strive to ensure that you and your companions are the focus of your visit. By respecting your space and time, they provide attentive care and a comfortable, welcoming service.

It is a place where you can spend quality time with your loved ones in a private and exclusive space that is made all the more special by its location at the back of an alley.

244817.longDescription:
Minutes from Suehiromachi Station in Tokyo, yakiniku restaurant Namaiki opened in 2014 as a sister site of the legendary Yoroniku in Minami Aoyama, a place where meat lovers will be drawn to a noren (curtain) inscribed with “肉(Meat)” that sets the agenda for a memorable evening. 

As the name of the restaurant is prefixed with “Nama (raw)”, attention to detail to the quality of produce takes precedence above all else. Lean, high quality meat sashimi melts on the tongue, and beef sushi has a deep flavor, with the rich, sweet flavor of the beef blending with the rice. Yukhoe, a kind of steak tartare, is exquisitely balanced, with egg yolk and a balanced sauce elevating the flavour of the meat. 

For yakiniku, specially-trained staff offer diners a way of tasting each part in a Yoroniku style. For example, beef tongue is thinly sliced from the marbled beef core and salted with kelp; misuji (top blade) comes with dashi and grated daikon; zabton (chuck flap) is dipping in a special sauce and entwined with egg yolk. Each dish is a delight, and exquisitely prepared by a professional staff. 

Meanwhile, a wide variety of drinks such as wine, beer, sake, and shochu are available to guests to enjoy with their meal.

As guests pass through the noren and ascend the stairs to the second floor, the interior is casual but chic and calm. There are a total of 93 seats at the counter and large tables, and private rooms for up to 24 people. Ideal for occasions with friends, parties, dates, and more.

244831.longDescription:
“Ishibashi” is located in a quiet town 6-minute walk from Edogawabashi Station. It is a 1-star eel restaurant where the third and fourth generations are in the grill, the proprietress cooks rice with carefully-selected rice, and the young proprietress selects and serves sake, continuing the traditional family business.

It was founded by the first generation Ryo Nemoto in 1910, around the end of Meiji period. After the war, it was relocated from Nakanohashi to its current location. Today, the fourth generation owner, Kazunori Nemoto, serves as president of the restaurant. His teacher was his father Mitsuaki Nemoto, the third generation. He trained under Mr. Mitsuaki since he was 20 years old, and now he is the fourth generation, keeping up with the third generation to preserve the taste of “Ishibashi” that he is proud of.

Eel changes its state every day. Different eel, from Shizuoka or from Kyushu, was purchased in the best condition on the day with the trust of the connoisseur who was familiar with the condition. The sauce, known as "the life of eel shop", has been passed down since the establishment, and the pickle is another specialty. Nuka-doko (bed of salted rice bran), a secret recipe of “Ishibashi”, has a history longer, more than 100 years, than the sauce. The "100-year assorted pickles", where you can taste all the pickles pickled in nuka-doko, is also a popular menu item.

"Please enjoy side dishes and alcohol until we serve the eel," says young proprietress Ayuko Nemoto. It takes less than 1 hour to grill the eel, meanwhile please enjoy the sake selected by Ms. Ayuko, who is also a Kikizake-shi (sake sommelier). The Japanese sake is selected to go well with à la carte dishes or course meals upon request from customers. There are always 20 to 30 kinds of seasonal sake and changes every 2 weeks. With a wide range of contacts with breweries, there are many rare sakes that you can meet only once, so it is a lineup that even sake connoisseurs will appreciate. The restaurant is also particular about tea and serves tea from Kagurazaka Meicha “Rakuzan”, that they have known since the first generation.

It is a tasteful restaurant with a brick wall that withstands air raids at the entrance. The "box" of Wajimanuri was used with great care and some of them were inherited from the first generation. The box with the long history is sometimes served, and you can enjoy a joint performance of traditional Japanese culture with eel cuisine, a craft of food and dinnerware. There are 3 tatami rooms, 3 tables, and around 40 seats. On weekdays you can enjoy business activities such as business entertainment, and on weekends you can enjoy the “Ishibashi” space and traditional taste for your private time such as with family, friends and dates. English menu is also available, so why not use it as a place to entertain overseas guests?

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2023
nearestStations: A 6-minute walk from Edogawabashi Station, Exit 4 (Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line)

recommendations.comment: コース全般を通してとても良い内容でした。

小部屋に少し早めに入れて頂き寒く無くてそのサ－ビスに感謝でした。コースでしたが中井さんのサ－ビスも心地よく「待つ』という時間が気になりませんでした。鰻は他のお店とはやや違って茶色がかり、よく蒸してよく焼いていると感じました。見た目と違って脂っこくなく、おお！これぞ江戸風という鰻です。肝吸いと名物のおしんこ、漬物が鰻にはまっていますね。静かなお部屋でしつらいもそして器も良い江戸の情緒を感じました。またコースの中の美味３珍？といいましたか？玉手箱という素敵な箱の蓋を取った時の煙が出たときの遊び心は素晴らしい演出ですし、ほかにも小技が効いていて感激しました。またその中の実山椒だし巻き卵は今迄のだし巻き卵の中で秀逸でした。
また行きたいお店が増えました。感謝です
素敵な器、お部屋で美味しく頂きました。
料理も接客も大満足でした。

Excellent foods and service!
Will definitely come back.

I would like to express my deepest gratitude to the team for welcoming us into their restaurant. I felt I was transported to a time that doesn’t exist but yet here we were enjoying this amazing meal on exquisite tableware. Thank you for the eel, the great service and of course, the beautiful sake selected for us.
we could spend quality time at here.
美味しく、楽しいひとときでした
料理は勿論ですが、お店の方も気さくで素晴らしい対応でした。大変満足でした。
とても美味しかったです。また、個室でご配慮頂き、落ち着いた環境の中で過ごすことが出来ました。
良い雰囲気で楽しく会食できました。機会があればまた行きたいです。
個室を用意してくださりとても落ち着いて食事ができました。コースはお腹にもちょうど良くとても満足致しました。また伺いたいと思います！
食事はもちろん、スタッフの対応、お店の雰囲気が良かったです。

母が高齢なためコース料理が食べきれないので1人だけ単品注文をお願いしたり、また別の1人が30分遅れるなどのわがままを快く受けてくださりとても助かりました。

お店の建物もとても素敵でお部屋も和室に螺鈿細工のテーブルに椅子が置いてあり高齢者にはとても有り難かったです。

鰻も柔らかさとパリっと焼けた香ばしさがあってタレとの相性もとても私好みであっという間にたいらげてしまいました。

テーブル席の予定でしたがお座敷が空いていてそちらの部屋にしていただきました。
個室はとても広くて落ち着いて、食事もとても美味しくいただきました。
素敵なひと時を過ごすことができました。
ありがとうございました。
コースのお料理は全て美味しく、量も適度で、お部屋の居心地もよく、スタッフの方の応対も適切で理想的な食事を楽しむことができました。同行の友人も大満足でした。また伺わせていただきます。ありがとうございました。
本当に美味しかったです。また伺います。

La Barrique Tokyo provides you the dining experience in a renovated 70-year-old Japanese house. White table cloths in a Japanese house complete with fusuma sliding doors creates a unique dining space. In addition to table seating, private rooms, business dining party, are also available.

Guests can choose from three courses or prefix Italian presented in Japanese taste. The restaurant's specialty is squid ink risotto. This creamy and fragrant dish features large-grained rice and cream concentrated with rich, umami, seafood flavors, together with the tartness of tomato. The wine menu offers 700 wines collection by bottle or over twenty different wines by glass to pair with your dishes.

As one of the city's leading ristoranti, La Barrique Tokyo is always extolled by renowned restaurant journalists.

244060.longDescription:
Kaiseki Fuji is in a quiet residential district 10 to 15 minutes walk from JR Shinagawa station and only 5 minutes on foot from Takanawadai Station on the Asakusa Line. This Kyoto-style Kaiseki and sushi venue allows guests to experience both sushi and the traditional tea ceremony's Kaiseki cuisine in one place. The venue's young head chef, Yasuhiro Fujii, makes good use of his years of experience of working at Japanese cuisine and sushi restaurants in Ginza and Ebisu by opening "Kaiseki Fuji" in the autumn of 2015.

The Tea Kaiseki-style cuisine is served as reservation-only course meal in both the lunch and dinner service.The handmade "nigiri" sushi served as a finishing touch in all courses are made mainly with seasonal fish topping shipped directly from Nagasaki combined with exquisite sushi rice made of either red vinegar or rice vinegar. Courses of 10,000 yen and over features a  handmade traditional Japanese sweets with freshly-whisked, fragrant powdered "matcha" green tea. There is also, of course, a rich selection of carefully-selected Japanese sake that excellently pair with  Kaiseki cuisine and sushi. 

The traditional Japanese-style interior features tatami flooring as well as traditional beautiful wooden sunken counter seating and separate private-room seating in addition. Behind the counter is a traditional Japanese tearoom. This is a space where guests can fully enjoy a meaningful time with delicious Kaiseki cuisine while chatting with the head chef over the counter. 

Located not far from the Grand Prince Hotel Takanawa and the Sheraton Miyako Hotel Tokyo, the traditional Japanese style with tatami mats and sunken seating, is perfect for entertaining guests from overseas and is also an excellent place for dining receptions and group outings. It is also rare among traditional Japanese restaurants to be open on Sundays, a welcoming service. With cuisine prized by its patrons, it is no wonder that over 9 out of 10 guests are repeated regulars.

245554.longDescription:
About five minutes’ walk from Shinagawa Station, L’ARBRE is located on the second floor of a building in a quiet residential area, bringing one-of-a-kind French cuisine to Shinagawa’s restaurant scene. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Masaki Kikuchi. As a young man aspiring to become a chef, he first worked at the main restaurant of Sheraton Grande Tokyo Bay Hotel in Urayasu, Chiba and then joined AUXAMIS WORLD, which had 10 restaurants in Tokyo at that time. He worked at AUXAMIS TOKYO in Marunouchi and Brasserie AUX AMIS Tokyo Skytree Solamachi in Oshiage and made two trips to France to hone his culinary skills before venturing into self-employment.
In November 2024, he opened L’ARBRE, embarking on a culinary journey of creating ideal dishes in his own style.

The restaurant’s name, L’ARBRE, means “the tree” in French, derived from a Chinese character meaning “tree” from the chef’s given name. It also reflects his commitment to bringing excitement and energy to the lives of guests like trees producing oxygen which we need to live. The chef’s philosophy is to create “new classics” that highlight the natural flavors of “produits” (products), not through processing but through traditional French culinary techniques, such as “cuisson” (cooking) and “assaisonnement” (seasoning). With a commitment to direct sourcing, the chef purchases fish and shellfish from fishermen around Japan, including Kagoshima, Hagi, Kochi, Shizuoka, the Naruto Strait, and Hakodate. In addition, he sources rare ingredients that are not commonly available in regular markets, such as shorthorn Kazuno Beef from Kazuno, Akita. It is amazing to see how these precious ingredients turn into 13-course feasts.

The homemade caviar is made from sturgeons which are delivered alive from Ibaraki and seasoned with just enough salt to enhance the natural flavor. Their nutritious meat is also transformed into an amuse-bouche, along with their jellied skin. The menu also includes popular specialties, such as Pâté en Croûte filled with three different types of flavorful meat and Consommé Soup prepared through a long, meticulous process of boiling native chicken, wild duck, and Yamagata beef for five days. To complement these foods, the wine list offers about 100 labels, mainly from France but also from California and the New World. The alcoholic and non-alcoholic drink pairings curated by the sommelier are also highly recommended.

The main dining room inspired by sukiya-style architecture overlooks a terrace where a weeping Japanese maple tree, Ryusen, stands as a symbol of the restaurant. With counter seating (for up to eight guests) and private table seating (for up to four guests), the restaurant caters to various occasions, from private to business. Please enjoy the new classic French cuisine featuring precious Japanese ingredients at L’ARBRE.
nearestStations: 5 minutes walk from Shinagawa Station

245275.longDescription:
品川駅へのアクセスも程よい高輪台駅から徒歩5分のところに店を構えるのが『鮨 梢（こずえ）』。「鮨は大人のエンターテイメント」だという親方の梢 ひろし（こずえ ひろし）氏が、つけ場をステージとし、渾身の握りパフォーマンスを見せる劇場型の鮨店だ。

梢氏は、『赤坂 菊乃井』をはじめ都内の名だたる日本料理店や鮨店などで修業を重ね、北九州にある実家の鮨店で腕を磨いた後、独立。2021年10月に『鮨 梢』を開店した。
コースは、つまみ5〜7品に続き、握りが15〜16貫ほど提供される。握りを数多く味わって欲しいという思いから、酢飯は小さめ。淡い色の赤酢に、石川県産の米を使う。鮨のスタイルはフグを握ったりと江戸前のみならず、北九州での経験も活かした仕立てを楽しむことができる。魚介は、梢氏が毎日豊洲市場に足を運び目利き。マグロは人気の専門仲卸「やま幸」から仕入れる。また、日本料理店での経験を活かしたつまみも充実し好評だ。
日本酒は山口「貴」、広島「宝剣」といった西日本のものも含め、全国の銘酒を。ワインは、梢氏が好むブルゴーニュやシャンパーニュを中心に、常時50本ほどワインセラーに置かれる。

レンガ造りのビルの入り口から店内に入ると、そこは異空間。黒で統一されたインテリアに宙に浮かぶ木曽ヒノキ一枚板のフロートカウンター（7席）。そこにスポットライトを浴びた梢氏が登場し、カウンター前のお客様にパフォーマンスを見せ料理を提供する。まさに劇場型の『鮨 梢』を家族や友人、同僚やカップルなどと訪れ、梢氏のつまみから握りまでのパフォーマンスに酔いしれていただきたい。	Sushi Kozue is a 5-minute walk from Takanawadai Station, which is within easy reach of Shinagawa Station. This is a theatrical type of sushi restaurant where the master chef, Hiroshi Kozue, uses the counter as a stage to show his spirited and powerful nigiri performance, saying, "Sushi is entertainment for grown ups".

Kozue trained at many famous Japanese and sushi restaurants in Tokyo, including Kikunoi in Akasaka, and also honed his skills at his family's sushi restaurant in Kitakyushu before going independent. He opened Sushi Kozue in October 2021.
The course consists of five to seven side dishes followed by 15 to 16 pieces of nigiri. The vinegared rice is prepared in small portions with the wish that diners enjoy many pieces of nigiri. Light colored red vinegar is used with rice produced in Ishikawa Prefecture. The style of sushi is not limited to Edomae, such as fugu (blowfish) nigiri, but also includes preparations based on his experience in Kitakyushu. Chef Kozue visits the Toyosu Market every day to pick out the seafood. The tuna is sourced from the popular Yamayuki wholesaler. In addition, the side dishes which reflect his experience in Japanese cuisine are highly regarded.
The sake list has offerings from all over Japan, including some from western Japan such as "Taka" from Yamaguchi and "Hoken" from Hiroshima. There are always about 50 bottles of wine in the cellar, mainly from Burgundy and Champagne, regions that are the favorites of Chef Kozue.

You step into a different world when you enter the brick building. The interior is decorated in black with a counter (7 seats) made of a single piece of Kiso cypress floating in midair. Chef Kozue emerges there in the spotlight, theatrically serving the customers in front of the counter. Bring your family, friends, co-workers, or couples to the theatrical Sushi Kozue and enjoy Chef Kozue's performance in everything from nibbles to nigiri.

245586.longDescription: Opened in September 2025, Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa is perched on the 29th floor, the top floor of NEWoMan TAKANAWA, in TAKANAWA GATEWAY CITY, directly connected to JR Takanawa Gateway Station. Originating from Manhattan, New York, the popular steakhouse is known for its unparalleled steaks, a testament to its commitment to quality and mastery of aging and broiling techniques. Opening its first location in 2004 in the United States, Wolfgang’s Steakhouse made its debut in Japan in 2014. The steakhouse made itself known to the world with its highly prized beef, rated among the top few percent of American beef by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). The highest-grade Prime beef is dry-aged in a dedicated aging room for 28 days to intensify its flavor and tenderness, and then cut thick, cooked in an oven at 900°C , and served on a heated plate. The menu offers a variety of steaks, ranging from the signature Steak, a combination of sirloin and filet mignon, to New York Sirloin, Filet Mignon, and Rib Eye Steak . The menu also includes exclusive specialties, such as Italian Veal Chop, grilled over an open flame, Tajima Ota Gyu Steak Tartar, Burrata And Cherry Tomato Salad, and Fresh Dover Sole. In addition, the wine cellar boasts over 1,000 bottles from around the world to meet the different tastes of guests. The steakhouse is located in the LUFTBAUM area on the 29th floor, the uppermost level of NEWoMan TAKANAWA, filled with over 500 plants to create a city retreat in the sky about 150 meters above the ground. Surrounded by plantings that change with the seasons and soundscapes that shift depending on the location, the venue has a main dining area (seating up to 126 guests), 3 private dining rooms (seating up to 26 guests in total), and a bar lounge (seating up to 29 guests). It can cater to various occasions, including family gatherings, friend meet-ups, date nights, and dinners with guests from around the world. Please enjoy the unparalleled steaks and stunning skyline views at Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Takanawa. 〈Group Restaurant Information〉 Wolfgang's Steakhouse Signature Aoyama Wolfgang's Steakhouse Roppongi Wolfgang's Steakhouse Osaka Wolfgang's Steakhouse Fukuoka Wolfgang’s Steakhouse TEPPAN Wolfgang's Steakhouse Marunouchi

244687.localizedAddress: Yanagi Koji Minamikado 1F, 3-13-7, Tamagawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
244687.longDescription:
Italian restaurant Ristorante i-lunga is located close to Futako-Tamagawa Station in Setagaya, Tokyo. The owner-chef Junichiro Horie showing his respect for both traditional Italian cooking techniques he employs and Japanese ingredients and producers.

Tokyo-born owner-chef Horie left for Italy at the age of 25. In 2002, after being the opening chef of Ristorante Pisterna in the Piedmont region, he became the first Japanese chef to be awarded by the world gourmet guide in Italy, a crowning achievement. He spent 9 years in Italy before returning to Japan in 2007 to open La Gradisca in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo. The renowned restaurant unfortunately closed its doors when Horie moved to Nara in 2009, where he opened Ristorante i-lunga in front of the gates of Todaiji Temple. He relocated the restaurant to Futako-Tamagawa, Tokyo, in 2019. ""I was born and raised in Setagaya, and studied at Komazawa University, which is also in Setagaya,"" explains Horie. ""When I began thinking of returning to Tokyo, I chose Setagaya because it's a nice location with the Tama River nearby, and it's my home.""

Owner-chef Horie pays respect to Italy, Italian ingredients, and Italian cooking, while teaming up with Japanese producers to add a spice of originality to his dishes. Some of his innovations include providing chopsticks for foreign guests and his use of ""umami"", or savory flavor. With the children's taste training program ""A Week of Flavor"" gaining traction in Japan and France, the fifth basic taste umami has become increasingly recognized internationally. Owner-chef Horie uses soup stock made from kelp and shiitake mushrooms to add an extra layer of flavor to his Italian cuisine. His specialty is Agnolotti del Plin. A local dish from Piedmont, with no doubt, this dish is the very soul of the region. ""It was difficult for me, a foreigner, to master this simple, unfussy style of cooking, but I'm proud to have received recognition from Italians,"" remarks owner-chef Horie. The restaurant also offers a wide selection of wines—mostly natural wines from Italy. Along with Grand Vin and Super Tuscan old vintage varieties, wine pairing is also available. 

The restaurant's building itself is constructed of wood, uncommon in Japan. Located on the bottom floor, the restaurant's striking design—with its thick wooden beams and pillars—will capture your attention. The cozy interior offers table seating for up to 14 people. The wooden decor and lighting creates a natural atmosphere, perfect for enjoying a moment of luxury. English and Italian speaking staffs are also available. A great choice for a relaxing sit-down meal with family, friends, or foodies, or even a meal out with foreign guests.

244816.longDescription:
A 7-minute walk from Yoyogi-Hachiman Station, “Kyoto Cuisine Aun” is located in Tomigaya, a town for adults, also known as "Oku Shibuya", which is slightly different from bustling Shibuya. Meticulous attention is paid to the "dashi" (soup stock). You can enjoy carefully prepared dishes made with the high-quality ingredients same as the one used at other long-established restaurants, at a reasonable price, is due to the thought of the owner Eiji Onoyama, who says, "I want you to enjoy authentic Japanese cuisine without any worries". He trained for 10 years at the long-established 3-star restaurant “Kikunoi Honten” in Kyoto and 8 years at the 2-star restaurant “Akasaka Kikunoi”. After that, he worked for a 1-star Japanese restaurant in California called “Kenzo Napa” for 1 and half year, and then went independent after he returned to Japan. In December 2018, he opened “Kyoto Cuisine Aun”.

What chef Onoyama cherishes the most is soup stock. He uses the "Kurawarijiri kelp" delivered from Okui Kaisei-do that is laid in the storehouse after harvesting and the freshly shaved bonito flakes from Makurazaki that is said to be the highest quality bonito flakes and carefully draw the soup stock. The soup made with seasonal ingredients and the finest soup stock has a special taste. The "Takikomi gohan (mixed rice)" that is cooked with the "Shigaraki Unseigama", carefully made by the craftsman, is a standard dish where you can fully enjoy the dashi that the chef is proud of. The ingredients used in the Omakase Course are mainly fresh seafood delivered daily from Toyosu Market and "traditional Kyoto vegetables". The plating is simple to bring out the ingredients. In addition to Japanese seasonal ingredients, such as pufferfish in winter and conger pike in summer, you can also enjoy the "Course with softshelled turtle and seasonal ingredients" from "Hattori Nakamura Turtle Farm" in Lake Hamana all year round. There are always 10 kinds of seasonal sake from all over Japan.

The restaurant has a warm atmosphere with the warmth of wood and only 12 seats at the L-shaped counter. There is no difference in level, so you can see chef Onoyama's hands well, and conversation with customers naturally bounces. The “Kyoto Cuisine Aun” dining experience is a great place to dine and date with family, friends and colleagues, and to entertain overseas guests. Please enjoy the essence of Japanese cuisine that permeates the quiet area of Tomigaya.

New address: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza D 2F, 5-10-7 Toranomon, Minato-ku, Tokyo Helmed by Chef Hiroyasu Kawate, Florilège is a widely acclaimed restaurant that has received two stars from an international restaurant guide. Chef Kawate accumulated experience by working at Le Bourguignon, a one-star restaurant in Roppongi, and by serving as a sous chef at Quintessence, a three-star restaurant in Gotenyama. His experience has made him a globally influential player in the restaurant industry. In Autumn 2023, he made a fresh start in Azabudai Hills, opening his third restaurant after closing his restaurant in Gaienmae. Having worked on sustainability for years, Chef Kawate has embraced the concept of plant-based eating at his new restaurant, which features vegetables (plants) indigenous to Japan, instead of using meat or fish as the centerpiece of meals. For the entree, guests are also offered two options, either meat or vegetables. Moreover, the drink menu offers a diverse range of pairing options, including not only wines but also other alcoholic beverages and mocktails. The restaurant’s interior is designed in table d’hôte style based on Chef Kawate’s long-planned concept for the restaurant. The large table that everyone can gather around as if they were invited to a family dinner serves various occasions and makes the experience even more enjoyable. ※ Awarded 2 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

244745.longDescription:
“Kyo Ryori Tomura”, not far from Tokyo Metro Toranomon Station, is located in a quiet alley in the city center. It is decorated with noren that features the restaurant’s name and gives it a calm and welcoming appearance, raising the expectations of the guests who visit.

The owner, Kimio Tomura, has been a chef for over 40 years. “Kyo Ryori Tomura” opened in 1992 and moved from Akasaka to its current location in 2007. From season to season, the restaurant serves the best dishes that can only be eaten at that particular time. For instance, Bamboo in spring; abalone, sweetfish and natural eel in summer; soft-shelled turtle in autumn; and crab and wild game such as bear and duck in winter. Regular customers come to the restaurant looking for seasonal dishes. Bamboo is purchased directly from a farmer with whom they have a long relationship in Tsukahara, Kyoto; sweetfish that are called "golden sweetfish" is purchased in Akaishikawa in Shirakami mountain range; and wild game is purchased directly from hunters in Shirakami. Owner Tomura believes that by building a relationship of trust through years of interaction with the producers, he can gain a deep understanding of the environment in which the ingredients grow and how to use them to bring out the most delicious full flavours of the food. Even though the same dish is served at the same time every year, it is gradually improved and evolved. That is the depth of the cuisine that this long-established restaurant is truly proud of.

Rich ingredients are brought by Japan's beautiful four seasons. In order to serve them to perfection to their guests, owner Tomura takes care to express how good each ingredient is. Minimal modification brings out the best of their flavours. Sake is limited to brands which compliment but do not interfere with taste of the best dishes to ensure that his wish to fully enjoy the ingredients prepared in the best possible way can be fulfilled.

The quiet restaurant has 6 counter seats and 2 private rooms (4 and 8 people). The impressive L-shaped counter is 70 cm wide and is made of majestic Bishu cypress (Bishuhinoki) which is no longer available. It is perfect for dining with family, friends and colleagues, and it is possible to accommodate guests from overseas with owner Tomura and other English-speaking staff. You will want to enjoy the Japanese cuisine of each of the four seasons with a calm mind.

[Regarding reservations]
After you register on the "waiting list", Pocket Concierge will contact you once there are seats available.

[About Cancellation]
We do not provide refunds for cancellations including changes in the number of people after the reservation is confirmed. We appreciate your understanding in advance.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Toranomon Station, Exit 4 (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line)

245226.longDescription:
Okamoto, a kappo (Japanese cuisine) restaurant housed in a building directly adjacent to Exit 2 of Kamiyacho Subway Station near Tokyo Tower, is helmed by Chef Hidetsugu Okamoto, who trained at Serabi (presently known as Nihon Ryori C'est la vie in Okayama and then served as a chef at Wakuden, an old-established Japanese restaurant in Kyoto, and a three-star restaurant in Tokyo. Eventually, he opened his own restaurant, Ginza Okamoto, in 2012 and relocated it to the current location in Kamiyacho in 2017. Okamoto is a highly rated restaurant, as indicated by the two stars consecutively awarded to it in the world’s leading restaurant guide since 2013.

In Okamoto, guests seated at the counter can enjoy watching the chef’s masterful culinary skills. With immense care and excellent skills, he breathes life into each ingredient and brings out their full flavors to turn them into masterpiece dishes right in front of guests. The artistic Japanese dishes conjured up by the acclaimed chef in the vibrant open kitchen are definitely one of the attractive features of Okamoto. The innovative yet simple dishes grounded in traditional Japanese cuisine and infused with the chef’s ingenious creativity are full of the rich flavors of the ingredients.
The vegetables used at the restaurant, mainly delicious and nutritious Kyoto vegetables, are carefully selected as they play an important role in Japanese cuisine. Meanwhile, “Soba Noodles with Dried Mullet Roe,” the restaurant’s signature dish featuring buckwheat noodles and topped with plenty of roughly shaved mullet roe as well as buckwheat grains to add crispness and an appetizing flavor, tingle the taste buds. “Mackerel Sushi,” which features fatty mackerel caught in autumn and winter and stored by flash freezing to make it available year-round, also enjoys great popularity. In addition, different brands of rice, grown in Niigata and Kyoto, are used depending on the dish. The sake list offers a wide selection of Japanese sake, mostly consisting of refreshing dry ones from Niigata.

The interior is designed in Japanese and Western style and furnished with a nine-seat counter from which guests can enjoy watching the chef working right before their eyes. With a private room (furnished with an L-shaped counter seating up to five people), the restaurant is worth visiting every season to savor seasonal dishes.
The restaurant is perfect for anniversary celebrations, business dinners, and intimate meals with your family. Please enjoy the great dining experience at Okamoto while savoring with all five senses the delicious dishes made by one of the most talented chefs who trained both in the Kansai and Kanto regions.


※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025
nearestStations: A 0-minutes walk from Exit 2 of Kamiyacho Station on the Hibiya Line

243862.longDescription:
10min’s walk from Shin Okachimachi Station in Tokyo, there is a casual Japanese restaurant “Minoya” among the Shopping district. A hidden home of vegetable’s cooking which only those in the know, know. 

The course meals consist solely of 30 varieties of seasonal vegetables, with numerous carefully prepared dishes served in small portions. The broth used in the dishes is a vegetable dashi stock developed exclusively by Minoya for vegetable dashi. It is a gentle and smooth broth that brings out the flavor of the vegetables without using any animal ingredients, so both vegans and non-vegetarians can enjoy vegetable broth to their heart's content. You can fully fill your stomach without worrying digestion or calories, welcomed by women and foreigner guests. The course recipes are all original and change every month, so many customers visit repeatedly. Carefully selected Japanese Sake, homemade sour and beer cocktails, and other various drinks available on your choice relieve with the vegetable-main courses.

Counter seats and table seats available on your choice. Best suggestion for casual dinner, dating, or health dinner for women. Also welcoming family dinner with children. Nearby Ueno and Asakusa area, please come and taste the new charming of vegetables.

A two-minute walk from Shintomicho Station or a four-minute walk from Tsukiji Station, the Italian restaurant PRIMO PASSO is easy to access on the way home from work.  Helmed by Chef Tomoyuki Fujioka, who knows the true charm of pasta, the restaurant offers pastas and other local dishes tailored to Japanese tastes.

Born to a family that runs a sushi restaurant in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, Chef Fujioka loved pasta so much that he decided to pursue a career in Italian cuisine. After a two-year apprenticeship in Japan, he went to Italy at the age of 25 and honed his culinary skills at authentic Italian restaurants, such as Mimi alla Ferrovia, Oasis Sapori Antichi, and Quattro Passi, for four years.  He then returned to Japan and opened PRIMO PASSO in May 2023. The restaurant’s name, which means the first step in Italian, was chosen to pay tribute to his training ground as a pasta chef: Quattro Passi (which means ‘four steps’ in Italian).

Featured in five out of the 12 prix-fixe courses, pastas are signature dishes of PRIMO PASSO. The exquisite dishes are conjured up with different types of pasta, such as capellini, linguine, and tagliolini, by the Italian-trained chef who knows the true appeal of pasta. Even the Cappuccino has pasta in it. However, no matter how many pasta dishes you have, you will never grow tired of them because each dish is reinterpreted with different Japanese ingredients to create different flavors.  In addition, they are complemented by Tokachi Herb Beef, which is elaborately cooked to be crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, and tender Prosciutto sliced with a Berkel hand crank slicer. The dishes can be further enhanced by pairing them with drinks selected from the pairing menu, including wines from different regions, original limoncello, and Japanese sake.

PRIMO PASSO boasts a Japanese-style interior with a lattice ceiling, a solid wood countertop, and wood accents. Behind the eight-seat counter is an eye-catching open kitchen. A delightful surprise is that sets of chopsticks are offered in addition to other pieces of cutlery. You can enjoy intimate meals with your family or friends in the private room (seating up to six guests) or sit with your date or gourmet friends at the counter.  Suitable for different occasions, PRIMO PASSO is worth a visit. Please enjoy the exquisite full-course meal prepared by the chef who specializes in pasta.


*Awarded one star in the 2025 edition of the World Gourmet Guide Tokyo.

Tsukiji in Tokyo is the gathering point of Japan’s finest ingredients, and behind the Tsukiji Hongan-Ji temple that is just a little ways from the market, you will find the world gourmet guide award restaurant “Sushi Keita,” which opened its doors in September 2017. The restaurant is run by Chef Keita Aoyama, who came from Hokkaido originally and went on to Tokyo after working at ""Sushi Sai Wakichi,"" a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Sapporo. Once in Tokyo, he went on to further his skills at famed Ginza establishments, including ""Sushi Mizutani"" for 2 and a half years and ""Sushi Taichi"" for 3 and a half years, before venturing out to run his own restaurant at age 30.

Chef Aoyama has a deep familiarity of Tsukiji market that grew hold after he first made his way to Tokyo, which of course made it a natural choice of location when the time came to open his own restaurant. He says that “I didn’t want it to be the type of sushi restaurant that people could only come to for celebrations and special occasions, but rather an everyday kind of place that you could come to whenever you felt like it.” With that sentiment in mind, he focused on creating a relaxing environment where each and every guest could enjoy their meal without any stress or pretension in the air. Chef Aoyama has a lighthearted personality, which is complemented by the friendly demeanor of the restaurant’s proprietress who takes care of everything on the hospitality end. These two personalities come together to create a warm and comfortable dining atmosphere, so even first time patrons can enjoy their fill of sushi without the slightest bit of awkwardness or apprehension.

Chef Aoyama blends his own personal style together with his hard-earned experience of working at several noted restaurants preparing Edomae sushi, otherwise known as “Tokyo-style” sushi. And at the same time, he still has his sights on achieving even greater heights. He has a keen awareness for balanced flavors and moderates aging, vinegar marinades and other such measures to ensure that the inherent flavor of each ingredient can shine through unhindered. Chef Aoyama also focuses his attention on getting the best possible temperature for each dish he puts out for guests. For example, he handpicks each squid at the start of the day before boiling it to perfection, and each conger eel is steamed under his watchful eye to make sure the temperature is just right. Some of his specialties include Hamaguri (Asian hard clam), Kohada (dotted gizzard shad), and mackerel, which all require delicate handling and preparation. For his sushi rice, he works with Akazu, which is red vinegar made from sake lees. This combination of rice and vinegar creates a splendid union of acidity, fragrance, and savory umami flavor that delight the taste buds.

※ Awarded 1 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025

245533.longDescription:
Located in Tsukiji Outer Market, Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Honten was founded in 2004 by a third-generation fish broker, Motonobu Ishikawa, and the chef of Aozora Sushi Sandaime to offer authentic Edomae sushi in their hometown of Tsukiji. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Ryuichi Tsuruya, who learned thoroughly about Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime while honing his skills at its branches. Committed to “not compromising on the quality of ingredients and offering the best sushi at ‘Tsukiji’ prices,” he personally sources ingredients from Toyosu Market every morning and turns them into Tsuruya-style delicacies and “Tsukiji sushi” by using Edomae sushi-making techniques and taking inspiration from everyday moments.

The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu offers three options, each consisting of one or two delicacies and about ten pieces of nigiri sushi. The exquisite sushi toppings are complemented by sushi rice seasoned with red vinegar to bring out their savory aromas and flavors. In particular, it is worth noting that tuna selected by Hiroki Fujita, also known as the Charisma of Tuna, from Fujita Suisan is available at the restaurant. It was the passion of a former chef of Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Marunouchi that persuaded the wholesaler favored not only by sushi chefs but also by sushi lovers to sell the exceptional fish to the restaurant.

The alcoholic drink menu offers an excellent selection of sake from around Japan, including Hitakami from Miyagi and Kamonishiki from Niigata, as well as Tokyo Craft Pale Ale, which is sourced in barrels. The soft drink menu also offers a wide range of options, such as Hebesu (citrus fruit juice from Hyuga, Miyazaki) with soda. With counter and table seating (the former seating up to 18 guests)  and a private dining room with a horigotatsu table (seating up to four guests), the spacious restaurant is alive with the laughter of guests. In addition, English-speaking staff are always available, which makes the restaurant popular among international guests. Please visit Tsukiji Aozora Sandaime Honten for various occasions, from private to business, and indulge in “Tsukiji sushi,” which reinterprets authentic Edomae sushi in a casual way.

245249.longDescription:
About a 7-8 minute walk from Shibuya Station. Nestled in a hidden spot along Orchard Road, in the area known as Oku-Shibuya, with the hustle and bustle of Shibuya in the background, is the restaurant Ajiyuta. As the name suggests, the owner, Hiroki Ajiyuta, began his culinary journey at the age of 20, drawn to the world of sushi by the energy of the counter. At the age of 25, he began honing his skills under a master sushi chef, including working at world-renowned restaurants, and in 2021, he opened Ajiyuta.

Focusing on the highest quality fish sourced from around the country, no effort is spared in preparation to bring out the maximum flavor and combine it with a unique blend of shari (sushi rice) to create sushi that meets our satisfaction. While maintaining traditional Edo-style sushi techniques, modern approaches and added care are incorporated to create our original sushi.
The restaurant offers an omakase course of approximately 15 to 20 items, focusing not only on providing the most delicious experience for the present moment, but also on sustainability by using fish that will still be available in 100 years. One of the key elements of our commitment is salt. The restaurant uses 'Shimama-su' from Okinawa to dehydrate the fish, 'Maldon Sea Salt' from the UK to season the sushi, and 'Guérande Salt' from France for the vinegared rice. Depending on the ingredients and preparation, we also use a variety of smoked salts. Chef Ajuta is equally meticulous in sourcing our fish, not leaving it to the wholesalers, but selecting only the best ingredients that we personally approve every day.
On the beverage side, the restaurant has partnered with a renowned sommelier to offer carefully selected Japanese sakes and wines that are not easily accessible, ensuring that each bottle and glass is perfectly paired with Ajiyuta's sushi. Of course, you can also enjoy pairing sushi with sake or wine to experience a harmonious marriage of flavors. The restaurant views pairing as something that enhances our guests' valuable time, and we hope you will enjoy the connections between the conversation, the chef, the food, and the drinks.

The interior is a comfortable space with a Japanese aesthetic, designed by someone who has worked on two-star French restaurants. The solid Kiso Hinoki (Japanese cypress) counter and the eye-catching granite serving area create a striking atmosphere. With 8 counter seats and a private room for four, Ajiyuta can accommodate a variety of situations.
Ajiyuta invites you to forget the hustle and bustle of Shibuya and enjoy the serene yet warm atmosphere of Ajiyuta with family, friends, colleagues or as a couple, while enjoying our carefully crafted sushi, sake and wine.
nearestStations: A 7-minutes on foot from Shibuya Station

244904.longDescription:
Located on the first floor, Kai is a two-minute walk from Yoyogi-Uehara Station. 

Named for a kind of rowing oar, Kai means “to go out onto the ocean" — and this maritime association hints at the quality of the nigiri diners can expect. Since opening in July 2013, the restaurant has drawn sushi connoisseurs from across the country, as well as a local clientele. 

Seafood is sourced from Toyosu market, with tuna procured from renowned wholesaler Yamayuki, a figure trusted by some of Japan’s best restaurants. Owner Naruhiko Yamamoto says, "when I became independent, I wanted to use local ingredients from Fukui." To that end, aged Koshihikari rice from Fukui Prefecture forms the base of his sushi, which is then paired to a blend of fragrant red vinegar and rice vinegar. 

A single omakase menu is offered, consisting of 20 dishes. In addition to 13-14 kinds of sushi, diners can expect popular side dishes such as delicate chawanmushi (a savory steamed egg custard) made with fresh clams and sea urchin, and crisp croquettes filled with seasonal seafood such as scallops, oysters, shrimp, and crab. 

As for Japanese sake, Hanagaki from Nambu Brewery in the owner's hometown is available throughout the year, as well as a seasonally changing selection of around 10 varieties.

Crossing a series of stepping stones, guests enter a tastefully decorated dining room, with an 8-seat gingko counter taking pride of place. A small private room seating up for four diners is ideal for dinner parties, dates, and occasions with family, friends, and colleagues.

244040.longDescription:
Yoyogi-Uehara Station is located 5 minutes from Shinjuku Station on the Odakyu Line. This area in Tokyo has many great restaurants where celebrities secretly visit. Among those restaurants, one of the popular Japanese cuisine restaurant is Kappo Ichika. The food on offer at this restaurant is made with a variety of ingredients, including fresh seafood, vegetables, and Japanese beef sourced from Tsukiji, and our highest recommendation is for the Seasonal Selection Course Menu, featuring a superb range of dishes carefully selected by the restaurant owner. 

In addition, guests can enjoy those delicious dishes accompanied by a carefully-picked selection of Japanese sake served in traditionally Japanese Edo Kiriko cut glasses. From the selection menu, the most popular dish is the "wafers filled with Japanese beef and shira-ae mashed tofu and green vegetables salad." Typically wafers are served as confectionery; however, at this restaurant the wafers are filled with a salad made of mashed tofu and seasonal greens, mixed with diced Japanese beef and an original homemade sauce. This is a superb must-eat dish that will allow all guests to rejoice in the changes of its delicious flavors and textures. 

The restaurant offers 11 counter seats, where guests can enjoy the chef’s skills right in front of their eyes, as well as two private rooms. The private rooms can be found outside of the main building where the counter seats are located, on the second floor of a separate building known in Japan as hanare (outbuilding). There is no age restriction for children, and the food is prepared in a kitchen dedicated to the hanare. If you are using a semi-private room where up to four people can be seated around a table, then smoking is permitted. If you wish to use a private room with seating for up to eight people, you can have a Japanese-style room with a traditional kotatsu table placed over a hole on the ground, offering a private space where the guests can relax in great comfort. 

Compared to other Japanese cuisine restaurants in Ginza and Roppongi, Kappo Ichika offers food at reasonable prices, so it is worth a visit if you are visiting Tokyo.

244906.longDescription:
Kiwa is located in a residential area, a five-minute walk from the east exit of Yoyogi-Uehara Station. Since opening in 2020, this restaurant has quickly gained a following among locals and tempura devotees. 

Owner Shinichi Tomori is a genuine tempura chef, having worked for 12 years at Tempura Yamanoue Roppongi in Tokyo. The name “Kiwa” denotes joy, a sentiment that Tomori hopes to impart among each of his guests. 

Ingredients for the tempura are carefully selected in season. In spring, edible wild plants from Niigata arrive each morning and in summer, seafood is sourced from nearby Toyosu market at its peak. In addition to tempura over rice and tencha (tempura over rice in tea), a refreshing dish of cold Inaniwa udon noodles is served as the last dish in summer. In autumn, chestnuts, matsutake mushrooms and ginkgo nuts are at their best, while in winter, pufferfish dishes are served to reflect the change of seasons. 

The Tomori-style of tempura favoured by the restaurant prefers the use of 100% Taihaku sesame oil instead of a blended frying oil, a method that ensures a light, crisp tempura. As an accompaniment, grilled salt from Tomori’s hometown in Okinawa is recommended. Meanwhile, dipping sauce for the popular tempura over rice is made by combining mirin, sake, soy sauce, and bonito soup stock, without any additional sugar. 

For its signature dish, fresh sea urchin is deftly deep-fried with shiso leaves mixed with Japanese mustard. Another dish of sweet potato washed with white wine and served with sherry is a dish that also serves as an homage to Tempura Yamanoue. From March to June, shrimp from Okinawa, directly delivered from farms, are a must-try.

The restaurant focuses on natural wine and offers two to three types of sake per season. Among them, the owner’s favorite sake, Denshu by Aomori Nishida Shuzo, is available year round, and the limited Sotogahama is also available.

A relaxed, stylish design showcases eye-catching details, such as glass walls and an entrance garden covered with pebbles. Guests are seated at a 10-person counter, or one of two tables designed for small parties. "We hope that customers who are experts in tempura and those who have never tried tempura before enjoy it," Tomori says. 

The restaurant is ideal for a dinner with family or friends, a date, or business gatherings.
