244452.longDescription:
Doing what you love to earn a livelihood. The owner-chef Shusaku Toba has pride in his calling and brings innovation to the Japanese restaurant industry as a spirited, energetic chef. After working at Italian restaurant ""DIRITTO"" in Kagurazaka and world gourmet guide award innovative restaurant ""Florilege"" in Azabudai, he took positions as sous chef at ""Tacubo"" in Daikanyama and chef at ""Gris"" in Yoyogiuehara before finally opening ""sio"" in the same place in 2018. The restaurant's name comes both from Japanese ""sio"" (salt) used in cooking as well as the acronym for ""Shuusaku Itsumo Oishii (Shusaku is always delicious),"" a most charming meaning. From this small, 16-seat restaurant arises a culinary reformation of a new age.

After his years rich with experience, Mr. Toba has arrived at the idea of a ""support-format committed restaurant."" By bringing together all the people who are involved in a restaurant—food producers, cutlery makers, interior designers, music creators—he aims to improve everyone's business and create a large movement. Mr. Toba has only one thought for ""sio"": to make unquestionably delicious food with his own hands and bring joy to his customers and other cooks. That's all. The chef's choice course is similar to ""Gris"" but more evolved, and while it is subtle and artistic, it focuses strongly on flavor and cheerfully transcends the boundaries of French cuisine with no regard for limits or genres.

Accompanying Mr. Toba's subtle cuisine are 6-7 types of tea pairings which do not hinder the food. Not concerned with providing the best match, the aim is simply to allow one to enjoy the variations of tea by providing tea pairings only to be found at ""sio,"" such as Taiwanese ""Tohobijin,"" blue tea, or carbonated jasmine tea. Wine is also offered, with 16 types including much natural French wine are available, and pairings are made just as with the teas. With his eloquence and diversity lending to his power as a chef, Mr. Toba's ""sio"" will pull forward the restaurant industry and become a flagship restaurant for reform.

244042.longDescription:
Kyobashi Moto, a sake lover's hideout where sake and food are enjoyed as a marriage, will make a new start in March 2023 as "Moto Tokyo" in Yaesu, Tokyo.
The restaurant is located in Yaesu, the gateway to Tokyo and the nexus of various mobility systems, including the Shinkansen bullet train, which connects all of Japan.

Mariko Taniguchi, the proprietress, will offer a lineup of sake supported by a wide range of customers, and Yugo Sakuma, the head chef, who has honed his skills at Japanese restaurants in Ginza and Kyoto, will continue to offer dishes that make full use of seasonal ingredients. This popular restaurant is known as a "hideout for sake lovers" where they can enjoy the marriage of sake and cuisine.

The dishes are "dishes that go well with sake" and are healthier for the body, with less salt and fat, and with the natural flavors of the ingredients being used to bring out the umami. A popular menu item is the "Sake-no-Azaki-Hassun. It is served on a single plate with a small selection of snacks that go well with sake. The restaurant also does not skimp on the ingredients and cooking methods, such as nigiri tuna selected from all over Japan, sashimi made from fish that has been laid down to maximize its flavor, morning duck processed early in the morning, and rare and highly valued brand-name wagyu beef. There are about 80 varieties of sake to choose from. The proprietress says, "We select sake breweries and brewers who are active as a small group, such as young breweries, young people in their 20s and 30s who are changing generations, and family-run businesses, and we would like to convey their dramas as well. The restaurant offers a wide selection of sakes with a wide range of tastes, from refreshing to robust, to suit the cuisine of the day and the tastes of the guests.
The restaurant has six seats at the counter and two private rooms (for 4-6 people). We hope you will take the time to enjoy the marriage of seasonal cuisine and sake in a variety of situations, such as dinner with family, friends, or business associates, a date, or when entertaining guests from overseas.

、ゆっくりといただきました。

244988.longDescription:
A 12-minute walk from Toritsu-daigaku Station transports guests to Yakumo Saryo, nestled in a tranquil part of residential Meguro. 

Entering through the gate of a house bordered by hedges and stone walls, guests are welcomed by a white split curtain imprinted with a coat of arms. This is a Japanese restaurant designed as an escape from  the everyday chaos of Tokyo, a balm for the body and mind where guests are encouraged to feel the waves of modernity and the tradition of Japan.

In order to provide an ultimate dining experience to guests, Yakumo Saryo is committed to two ideals: Food that stimulates all five senses, and the culinary art that makes this ambition possible. The cuisine of Yakumo Saryo follows the traditional concept of holistic cookery, which places high value on intrinsic wealth. The restaurant’s ingredients and tableware are carefully selected by combing Japan for producers, intermediate buyers, and craftsmen. In summer, seared pike conger, grilled over charcoal, enjoys immense popularity; meanwhile in winter, deep-fried puffer fish captures the season, as well as the hearts and palates of guests. However, the carefully selected wine, sake, and tea pairings are where the true genius of this restaurant lies, for here it celebrates a unique marriage of food and drink.

Moreover, Yakumo Saryo incorporates traditional crafts of the future, utilizing the craftsmanship to create utensils. This includes ceramics, iron, tin, copper, lacquer, glass, wood, bamboo, and other materials. Yakumo Saryo explores the new possibilities inherent in each material, combining them to enhance texture and allure, further accentuating the charm of the cuisine.

The restaurant’s dining spaces are defined by white plastered walls and a blend of modernity and tradition, offering 10 counter seats and 14 garden seats. In addition, a private room seating up to eight people is offered. Dinner is available only for guests introduced to reserve their table to dine, and only four private rooms are open for dinner service. Floor-to-ceiling windows allow warm sunlight to flood dining spaces with natural light while offering beautiful views of the garden, which is particularly splendid during the plum blossom season. Each dish is served on original pieces and Japanese ceramics crafted by artists. Wrapped in the aesthetics of Japan, Yakumo Saryo is the perfect place to enjoy meals with your friends, partner, or companions from abroad in a luxurious, comfortable setting, where guests will forget the passage of time.

The owner trained at Kagaman, a world gourmet guide award restaurant in Osaka, also at various establishments in Tokyo. The shop revolves around counter seating and serves both locals and gourmands traveling from far away.

Committed to the dashi broth, the basis of Japanese cuisine, the restaurant serves impactful and creative dishes that you will never tire of. The truffle rice that comes out at the end is already a classic must-eat. Rice cooked in a stone pot is prepared in front of you with shaving truffles on it, what a bold performance! Dear Haramasa Tokyo Team,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to express my utmost satisfaction and appreciation for the exceptional Omakase dining experience I recently had at your esteemed restaurant.

From the moment I stepped foot into Haramasa, I was captivated by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The staff greeted me with genuine smiles and displayed the highest level of professionalism throughout my entire visit. It was evident that the team at Haramasa takes great pride in their work and is dedicated to providing an unforgettable dining experience.

I had the pleasure of entrusting myself to the talented hands of your skilled chef, and I must say that the Omakase meal surpassed all my expectations. Each dish was a true masterpiece, showcasing the finest ingredients and meticulous attention to detail. The flavors were simply divine, and the presentation was a feast for the eyes. I could tell that every element of the meal had been thoughtfully curated to create a harmonious and unforgettable gastronomic journey.

Moreover, I would like to commend the chef for their outstanding artistry and culinary expertise. Not only were they incredibly skilled, but their passion and dedication were palpable throughout the entire dining experience. Their meticulous techniques and personalized touches made each dish a unique delight. It was evident that the chef took great pride in their craft and was committed to ensuring that every guest had a memorable dining experience.

Equally remarkable was the impeccable service provided by the entire staff. The waitstaff were attentive, knowledgeable, and accommodating, making me feel welcome and valued as a guest. Their attentiveness to every detail and their ability to anticipate my needs truly enhanced the overall experience.

I would like to extend my deepest gratitude to the entire team at Haramasa Tokyo for their commitment to excellence and for creating an extraordinary dining experience. It is evident that your dedication and passion for gastronomy have resulted in a truly exceptional restaurant.

I will cherish the memories of my visit to Haramasa Tokyo and will undoubtedly recommend it to friends, family, and colleagues. Please convey my heartfelt appreciation and congratulations to the chef and the entire staff for their outstanding work.

Thank you once again for an unforgettable dining experience. I look forward to returning to Haramasa Tokyo in the near future.

Warmest regards,
HAN SONGRU

A six-minute walk from Yotsuya-Sanchome Station  takes you to a ground-floor restaurant, Niku Kaiseki Rinzen, run by Owner-Chef Naohiro Takami. Enchanted by Tajima beef, he strives to unlock the full potential of the premium beef through the magic of kaiseki cuisine. Also known as a meat enthusiast, he loves meat so much that he has traveled around Japan in search of the best Wagyu beef. On this journey, he was captivated by Tajima beef for its lean and tender meat melting in the mouth with a hint of fresh aftertaste. Inspired to allow as many people as possible to enjoy the best beef in the best way, he opened his own restaurant, Niku Kaiseki Rinzen, in 2021.

The restaurant features Tajima and Kobe beef, directly sourced from Ota Bokujo by Tajima Beef Otaya, a Kobe-based producer and wholesaler of beef products. To highlight the flavor of the meat, all the other ingredients are carefully selected, including sweet cones from Cone Lab in Ibaraki; brand rice “Gin no Mikazuki” from Gero, Gifu; sea urchins “Hamanaka Ogawa Uni,” and kelp (kombu) from Hokkaido. The prix-fixe menu consists of 10 courses of kaiseki cuisine, from appetizer to dessert, featuring different cuts of Tajima beef prepared in various ways, such as steamed, deep-fried, raw, and grilled. Among them, Tajima Beef Sirloin Yukhoe Topped with Caviar (to be wrapped in the thin, hand-sliced sirloin) is so popular that it is served year-round. Slowly cooked over low heat, Charcoal-Grilled Beef is another regular favorite among the frequent diners.

The wine cellar boasts about 100 wines from around the world, mainly from France and the USA but also from Japan, Italy, and Australia. The drink menu also offers a wide selection of options, including sake, highballs, and homemade lemon sours, to satisfy different customer tastes. Meanwhile, the soft lighting and classical music playing in the background create a chic ambience. With three semi-private dining rooms with dining tables and chairs and a private dining room with a chef’s counter, the restaurant suits various occasions, ranging from personal celebrations to business gatherings. So indulge in the exquisite Japanese meat kaiseki cuisine prepared by a Japanese chef at Niku Kaiseki Rinzen.

244009.longDescription:
Sushi Wa-sabi is in a favorable location, a 30-second walk from the Yotsuya-sanchome Station on Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line. For owner Sho Mizuta, sushi has been a lifelong passion, rooted in the childhood memories of eagerly visiting his favorite sushi shop on special days. He describes those moments as his true “starting point.”
The specialty at Sushi Wasabi lies in its expertly crafted shime dishes—fish delicately marinated in vinegar, a traditional Edo-style technique that enhances both flavor and aroma. Equal care is given to the rice, the foundation of every piece of sushi. Timed perfectly to the transition from appetizers to sushi, the rice is cooked in a traditional hagama pot. By blending two varieties of rice—one rich in umami and the other with less stickiness—the chef achieves a texture that gently melts in the mouth. To further refine the flavor, four types of vinegar are combined, including rice vinegar made with five to eight times the usual amount of rice and red vinegar aged for over ten years.

The restaurant offers just nine counter seats, creating an intimate yet casual setting. Unlike the often-intimidating image of Tokyo’s high-end sushi restaurants, Sushi Wasabi is known for its warm, relaxed atmosphere and the chef’s engaging conversation. Whether gathering with friends for a casual dinner or enjoying a thoughtfully balanced progression of appetizers and sushi paired with sake, guests will find both comfort and delight. It’s a place where you can stop by alone, even late at night, yet still experience a truly special sushi meal—one filled with flavor, tradition, and heartfelt hospitality.
nearestStations: Yotsuya-sanchome Station, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line

244506.longDescription:
"Unico-co" is an Italian restaurant that specializes in "uni", or sea urchin, established in an area of the capital where there is fierce competition between unique restaurants. Their sea urchin variety course, which includes an appetizer, pasta, and main dish, has created quite a stir, and the restaurant is now visited by fans from both Japan and abroad.

Chef Hironobu Tsujita entered Tsuji Culinary Institute at the age of 31, and after graduation, he studied cuisine and wine at Tokyo's "Osteria Vincero" and also became a qualified sommelier. Later, after training at a restaurant in Perugia, Italy, he opened Osteria T in Tokyo in 2012 at the age of 35. As a result of holding a "Sea Urchin Matsuri" summer event at the restaurant, he began to look more into sea urchins and opened Unico-co in 2016. Unico-co was relocated with new interior on November, 2018.

"What led me to open the restaurant was the feeling that while there are people who like sea urchins, not many people know about them," says Mr. Tsujita. Consequently, at "unico-co" he offers a course made using seasonal sea urchins purchased from trusted suppliers all over Japan, so you can enjoy new ways of eating sea urchin and the different flavors of various production areas. More than 12 kinds of sea urchins are used, and in the third dish of the course, he prepares all of them on a single plate for comparison. Other popular specialties are the rich sea urchin pasta and "Unico-co Tournedos Rossini," a sublime intermingling of beef tenderloin, foie gras, truffles, caviar, and sea urchin.

To drink, there is about 380 Italian wine carefully selected by Mr. Tsujita. There is also a pairing menu in accordance with the food. And when comparing the different varieties of sea urchin, an original label of "unico-co" sake is on offer so you can enjoy the marriage of sea urchins and sake.

The interior of "Unico-co" is a Mediterranean-style design based on white and blue, and has 6 seats at the counter and table seating for 9. In addition to people visiting to celebrate anniversaries, it brings together lovers of inimitable sea urchins from not only Japan but also overseas, and it is bustling every day. "My aim is to be the best in the world for sea urchin," says Mr. Tsujita. He would like you to experience new delicious flavors at a restaurant with an insatiable passion for sea urchin.

"Jour de Marche", a french restaurant hidden in the residential area about 3 minutes' walk from Akebonobashi Station on Toei Shinjuku Line, Tokyo. Chef's selected course with a hidden story-line is your only option. With the abundant use of seasonal ingredients, delicate and colorful French is provided. Live cooking can been seen at the modern and relaxing dining space from the semi-open kitchen. Both lunch and dinner can be reserved on Pocket Concierge, for your dating, causal dining with families and more.

244531.longDescription: Located on the third floor of the Hibiya district landmark-Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, ""Nanzenji Hyotei Hibiya"". It is a new branch of Hyotei, the well-known and long-established luxury world gourmet guide award restaurant in Kyoto. With the goal of accomadating as many guests as possible, including younger generations, this restaurant is highly recommended for who prefer to experience Kyoto cuisine in Tokyo, 15th-generation chef Yoshihiro Takahashi brings a novel take on traditional Japanese cooking. Yoshihiro is the eldest son of Eiichi Takahashi, the 14th-generation chef of Hyotei, which is a veteran restaurant specializing in Kyoto dishes and founded over 450 years ago. After graduating from university in Tokyo, Yoshihiro apprenticed for 3 years at the famous dual-starred kaiseki restaurant ""Tsuruko"" in Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture, returning to Kyoto in 1999, where he diligently studied under his father before taking the reins as the 15th-generation master in 2015. He is active both within Japan and abroad, including collaborative work with French master chef Alain Ducasse, while preserving the traditions and reputation of classic Kyoto kaiseki cuisine handed down over the generations. Opening in 2018, ""Nanzenji Hyotei Hibiya"" features Hyotei classics such as the famous soft-boiled ""Hyotei Egg"" kaiseki dish as well as seasonally-available breakfast rice porridges. The difference here from the original location, however, is that Chef Takahashi himself can be seen working behind the counter. The inclusion of special seating, from which guests can witness the chef at work before their eyes, is proof that Chef Takahashi, who readily answers the questions of his guests, has no small number of fans. The main focus of the Hibiya location is traditional Japanese kaiseki cuisine. Ingredients carefully selected both from the Kyoto area and from Japan as a whole are utilized to prepare both lunchtime and dinnertime kaiseki course meals. Casual, simplified kaiseki-style course meals are also available at lunchtime. Guests are invited to enjoy a pairing with a Kyoto sake or one of the many wines on offer. With details such as its entrance walkway and bamboo-themed interior, space overflows with the same elegant charm as the original Hyotei. The L-shaped counter, with seating for 12, is designed to give the impression of enjoying kaiseki cuisine on tatami matting, and the table seating also features a stylish tatami theme. Individual rooms seating 6 and tatami rooms seating 4 are also available. Chef Takahashi offers traditional flavor prepared with imagination, flexibility, and kindness. The venue is as accessible to Kyoto cuisine novices as it is to connoisseurs coming to experience the dishes of the 15th generation. It is the perfect place to gaze at the green landscape outside in the daytime or spend an evening enjoying Kyoto cuisine at the counter against the backdrop of the city lights with that special someone. ＝＝＝＝＝＝ Nanzenji Hyotei Hibiya is located in Tokyo. Please note that this restaurant is a sister restaurant of Hyotei in Kyoto. For reservations at Hyotei, please click here. ＝＝＝＝＝＝

243688.localizedAddress: 7F Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, 1-1-2, Yurakucho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
243688.longDescription: Anyone who loves Japanese cuisine knows Seiji Yamamoto. The chef Mr. Yamamoto is ranked in the Top 10 in the World's Top 100 chefs. His world gourmet guide award Japanese restaurant, "Nihonryori RyuGin" represents the very essence of Japanese cuisine. The restaurant has maintained its three-star rating in the international gourmet guide and has also received the highest score for "outstanding restaurant in all" in a gastronomic guidebook with a network of 15 countries, and has been voted "Best Restaurant in Asia" and "World Best Restaurant" making it one of the most famous Japanese restaurants. Yamamoto explains his conviction. "I prepare Japanese dishes that showcase the splendor of Japanese ingredients to my guests, sharing with them the notion of "Wa" [the Japanese concept of harmony] and expressing the rich abundance of Japanese produce to create an environment where people can come together with a mutual love of food to enjoy delicious cuisine". He opened "Nihonryori RyuGin" in 2003 in a back street in Roppongi. 15 years later, he moved and opened "RyuGin Honten" on the 7th floor of "Tokyo Midtown Hibiya" on August 21, 2018. "Nihonryori RyuGin" exclusively serves an "omakase" set menu (Blessings of the Season), featuring dishes specially selected by the chef. Traditional recipes are carefully followed to ensure each dish is served at the correct temperature, preserving its aromas and umami. The unique cooking here magnificently epitomizes the wealth that nature has to offer in Japan. "There is no greater delight than tasting Japan's most treasured culinary ingredients in their most natural state". The dining at "Tokyo Midtown Hibiya" is designed to convey an intense feeling of Japanese tradition and culture. Whether at a table, in a semi-private room or private room (maximum 8 persons), you are invited to savor hospitality infused with "Wa," through cooking that is instilled with the charms and attractions of Japan, resonating with your five senses to bring you a delicious taste experience. Enjoy the culinary creations of Chef Yamamoto, skillfully evoking the changing seasons of Japan. [Information] "Nihonryori RyuGin" moved from Roppongi to "Tokyo Midtown Hibiya," and opened on August 21, 2018. ※ Awarded 3 star on world-renowned gourmet guide Tokyo 2025 * Reservation is required to be made in-person. Any reservation from a travel agent or different guest is not acceptable. 【Nearby Hotels】 * With taxi within less than 10 minutes ■ Imperial Hotel Tokyo ■ The Peninsula Tokyo ■ The Palace Hotel Tokyo ----------------------------------------------------------------- Frequently Asked Questions ■ Do you have a private dining room? Private dining room(s) are available. ■ Is there a charge to book a private dining room? Additional 15% service fee is charged. ■ How many people can the private room(s) accommodate? 1 private dining room: up to 8 people are welcome. 2 semi-private dining rooms: up to 4 or 6 people are welcome ■ What is the arrangement in the private dining room(s)? The private dining room offers table(s) and chairs (Western style). ■ Are shoes allowed in the private dining room(s)? Shoes are allowed in the private dining room(s). ■ Can the course be customized for vegetarian, vegan or low calories? Unfortunately, we are not able to offer any customizations for vegetarian, vegan, low calories or a la carte option. ■ Are children welcome? If so, is a separate menu for children available? We welcome children over 10 years of age or children who can enjoy our standard course offer for adults. We require that each guest including children participates in the standard course offers as we do not offer a special menu for children. ■ Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible? We are wheelchair accessible and we will be happy to assist as needed. ■ Are menus available in other languages? English menu is available. ■ Does anyone in the restaurant speak other languages? We have staff that speaks English. ■ Can I make a reservation for 1 person? We accept reservations starting from 1 person. ■ Is there a dress code? Our dress code is Elegant Casual. Please note that reservations with guests with T-shirts, shorts or sandals for gentlemen will not be honored, and we ask guests to be responsible for its cancellation fee.

また、サービス・店内の調度品や雰囲気もとてもすばらしく、快適な時間を過ごすことができました。
本日も美味しい時間を有難うございました。過去にも頂いた料理は更に進化し、初めて頂いた料理と共に改めてその美味しさに驚きました。コロナ禍において何かと不自由な時間が続いていますが、龍吟・山本シェフをはじめスタッフの皆さんが作って頂いた時間と空間が、我々にとって何よりの活力になります。季節がうつろいで行くタイミングでまた訪問させて頂きますので、宜しくお願いします。御馳走さまでした。

本日も有難うございました。晩秋～初冬の旬の食材の、食感、香り、うま味、そしてそれらの組合せによる変化を堪能させて頂きました。この数日間、東京はめっきり寒くなりましたが、一品目の暖かいすっぽんスープですっかり心身ともにリラックスでき、器やペアリングのちょっとした変化も楽しませて頂きました。お料理だけではなく給仕を頂くスタッフの皆様の暖かな接客にも訪問毎ではありますが感心、勉強させて頂いております。当分、外食の機会は減るような状況ではありますが、自分にとって大切なお店での贅沢な、幸せな時間を社会のルールを守りながら、今後も楽しませて頂こうと思いますので次回も楽しみにしております。

　龍吟のホームページで見覚えのある、凜とした佇まいのお店の入り口の引き戸に実際に手をあてた時の高揚感は格別のもので、待合室では番の梟が静かに迎えてくれたのには大変驚きました。

本日は大変お世話になりました。
お料理、サービス共に大感激でした。
一緒に行かせていただいた者は、和食の道に進んだばかりの若い料理人です。
一流と言われる名店を訪れるに至り、少しでも何かを盗んで来ようと、フロアーの方々に様々な質問をしてしまい大変お手間を取らせたことと思います。
山本シェフの手の込んだお料理、器の選び、細やかなサービス、どれを取っても彼には衝撃的だったようです。
失礼ながら、いつかは自分も山本シェフに負けないような料理人になりたいとまで言っておりました。
場違いなような私達2人でしたが、また季節が変わる頃に是非お邪魔させていただきたいと思っています。
ありがとうございました。ごちそうさまでした。
長々と失礼いたしました。

○雰囲気 空間は広過ぎず、座席の間隔や位置も適切。照明は最初少し暗めかとも感じましたが、落ち着いた雰囲気で会話や食事にも良かったと思います。
○器 陶器のものも良かったですが、塗りのものが温かみがあり、色彩も楽しめました。
○料理 素材が良いことは勿論ですが、奇をてらわず、それでいて味覚のアンサンブルが新鮮。火の通し加減も絶妙。
○飲み物 料理に合わせワイングラスで供されたボトル入りのお茶は、アルコールが無理な人にとっても料理とのマリアージュを楽しめるものでした。
○サービス 食べ手のペースに合わせ、会話の邪魔にもならぬよう、良いタイミングで料理が供されていたと思います。
○その他 食材の産地の説明があまりないのは、敢えて先入観を抱かせるのを防ぐ意図でしょうか。個人的には気にはなりませんが、知りたい方も多いのではないかと思いました。外国の方は産地やブランドに興味があるのでは。

244343.localizedAddress: TOKYO MIDTOWN HIBIYA 3F, 1-1-2, Yurakucho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
244343.longDescription:
Tokyo Midtown Hibiya was born in March 2018 in a space with lush greenery adjacent to Hibiya Park, an oasis in the heart of Tokyo. With an abundant history and culture, Hibiya is a great location for shopping complex where quality stores from both Japan and overseas are gathered together. Among all the shops, the most eye-catching is "Restaurant TOYO Tokyo", a popular restaurant from Paris that it is difficult to make reservations, and this is their first time to open a branch in Japan.

After working at "Jean Moulin", a French Restaurant in Kobe, the owner chef Toyomitsu Nakayama went to France to work not only at French restaurants but also at Japanese restaurants in Paris. He was then recognized by the world-famous Japanese designer Kenzo Takada and now also works as Takada's personal chef. He opened "Restaurant TOYO Tokyo" in Paris in 2009 and established his reputation through his original French-and-Japanese cooking style that derived from his unique training experiences.

A portrait of Chef Nakayama painted by Takada is displayed inside the restaurant just like the one in "Restaurant TOYO Tokyo" in France. "Restaurant TOYO Tokyo" in Hibiya even has the same ambiance as the one in Paris. There are 8 counter seats and 14 table seats including the ones in the private rooms that can fit up to 6 people. The restaurant implements the "Counter French" style which is a trend in France. Sometimes the chefs will place a hot plate on the counter and perform the cooking right in front of the customers' eyes, and this "live" sensation is enjoyable. Paris and Tokyo are two cities known for being "food capitals". Be sure to experience the miraculous French cuisine created from the fusion of the two cultures of these two capitals.
nearestStations: ■Direct link from Hibiya Station (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, Hibiya Line, Toei Subway Mita Line)
■Direct link from Yurakucho Station (5-minutes walk)

recommendations.comment: 大変美味しくいただきました。ご馳走様でした。

和風で丁度よい味、量で満足でした。
Great food, perfect service, nice place to be. Will certainly come back again!
スタッフのみなさんも非常に親切で楽しいひと時を過ごすことができました！もちろん料理も大満足でした！
Excellent food and service
未体験の創作メニューは面白く美味しいもので、品数も多く大変満足感の高いランチになりました。
ワインペアリングは完璧でした。
美味しい
Service was very good, and some of the dishes were very creative and good.

雰囲気の良いお店で、妻の誕生日のお祝いの旨前もってお伝えしていたので、落ち着いた席にご案内いただきました。それぞれの料理に合わせた器、料理とお酒のマリアージュ、どちらもとても満足しました。
また、サービススタッフ、ソムリエ、シェフ、みなさんの笑顔での接客に、素敵な時間を過ごせました。
デザートへ合わせた、北海道のジン、絶品でした。帰ってから、色々な方にお勧めしてしまいました。

楽しい時間をありがとうございました。
初めての食事でしたが、お料理、ワイン、サービスも満足しました。次回は2人で伺いたいと思います。
工夫の凝らされた一皿一皿にきめ細かいサービス｡締めのヴィヤベースカレーも素晴らしかったです。
コース内容がきちんと考えられており、どれも美味しくいただくことができた。また、お店の方も人柄がいい方が多く、会話も楽しむことができた。値段以上に満足することができ、また食べに行きたいと思ったため。

初TOYOさんが1名いましたが、とても満足されていました。　私は羊をいただきました。本当に美味しかったです。　また、伺いたいと思っています。
ご馳走様でした。

最後のメッセージプレートもいただいて、おいしくご飯をいただきました。
コロナ禍でもお客さんがちゃんと入っていて、安心しました。
これからも頑張ってください。
多彩なまたとてもおいしい料理を堪能させて頂き有り難うございました。

ふきのとう、いちご等旬の食材を使っての料理、春を感じました。
５皿のコース、ひとつひとつに意味があり、とても詩的に思いました。
美味しい時間をありがとうございました。また近いうちに伺いたいです。
和食のように楽しめるフレンチ。TOYOならではの唯一無二の食体験、今回も大変満足しました。穴子のグリエ、旬の野菜とミモレット。同行の友人とカウンターフレンチをゆっくりくつろぐことができました。
おいしかったです
旬や和食材の使い方、火入れ具合、盛り付け、ペアリングのドリンク、サービス、其々にワクワクして楽しく過ごしました。
料理も美味しく、見た目も美しかったので、話も盛り上がりました。
All dishes displayed like an art and the taste was so delicious. We enjoyed the dinner. Definitely, we will comeback TOYO Hibiya again. Thank you :)
料理の内容が素晴らしかったですまた伺います

まず、料理がとても美味しかったです。素材を活かされていたし、それに合わせたソースなどがとても美味しかったです。
また、目の前で料理されるので、エンターテインメント性がありました。
ワインも美味しく頂きました。
今度はフルコースを食べてみたいです。
ごちそうさまでした。

モダンフレンチの料理がどれもとても美味しく、ペアリングのワインも料理に合っていて良かったです。
スタッフの皆様も若々しく親切で良い時間を過ごすことができました。また是非来たいと思います。
誠実さの伝わるお店でした。カウンターからキッチンが見えること、スタッフのみなさんが食材について説明できること、絶妙のタイミングでのサービング。お味ももちろん。あちこちから、美味しいの言葉が聞こえてきました。こんな美味しいものがあるのだなと感動のひと時でした。ありがとうございました。

料理の味、サービス共に大変満足しました。
ワインも美味しく頂きました。
また利用させて頂きます。

昨日は大変お世話様になりました。
お料理はどれも美しく、美味しく、堪能いたしました。
シェフのお人柄も素晴らしく、いろいろなご配慮をいただき嬉しかったです。
同行した友人がお正月の来客にお出しする料理のヒントを得たようでとても喜んでくれました。
次回はもう少し時間をかけ、ワインも楽しみたいと思います。
ご馳走様でした。
エントランスを入った空間から・料理・ワイン・デザートに至るまでシェフのコンセプトを五感で感じることのできる洗練されたひと時を体験することができる。一皿ひと皿に旬を創意された演出が常に新鮮であり、新たな刺激と発見がある。季節を変えて再訪を続けたい希少な逸店です。

事前のお願いや前日のベジへ料理対応や当日も！
本当に素晴らしいと思います。
お料理も大満足です！
お肉やお魚が美味しいのはもちろんですが、野菜がしっかりしていて、いいアクセントになっていました。食感や温度や色など楽しむことができ、シェフやソムリエや盛り付けスタッフの方々も笑顔とお話が素敵でした。急な予約にもかかわらず、素晴らしいサービスとコースにも感動しました。ありがとうございます。

お料理が素晴らしく、また、スタッフの方のサービスが丁寧＆全員フレンドリー、それでいて、キビキビとしたオペレーション～お店全体の雰囲気もとてもよかったです。
また、ワインのペアリングも興味深く最高でした。ごちそうさまでした。またお邪魔いたします。
多彩な食材を使った和とフレンチの素敵な融合を楽しむことができました。
とても美味しい料理とソムリエの対応が良かったです。
素材の味が生かされている優しい味わいがありとても美味しいお料理でした。カウンターでの盛り付けを目の前で見ながらいただき、待っている間も楽しませてもらいました。最後は口の中で調理されているかのように、色々な味を楽しむことができたので押し付けられる味ではなくでもしっかりと下準備されている美味しさを感じることができました。また機会があれば伺いたいです。
どのdishも洗練されて美しく、私達の期待を裏切らない。素晴らしい記念日になりました。ワインも料理とのマッチングが申し分無く楽しめました。また、別の季節に参ります。

お店の方々が気持ち良く、キビキビと動いていらっしゃり、見ていて清々しい気がしました。
過度過ぎないサービスが良く、もちろん味も良かったです。
初めて食べました。今まで食べたことがない新鮮な食材で家族が驚いていました。ありがとうございました。また伺うときを楽しみにしています。
good food and very good service
料理はイノベーティブ、かつ食材の力が最高に引き出されていて、感動しました。接客もくつろげ、カウンターでシェフとの会話も楽しかったです。

1品1品繊細で素晴らしい味でした。
文句の付けようがありません！
一緒に行った人間も大満足でした。
また伺いたいと思いました。
和食でシンプルな食し方しかした事ない食材を独特なチーズといただくなど初めての体験でした。成人になった娘と少し大人なお食事が出来て幸せな時間でした。

食材の味が活かされていて、とても美味しかったです。贅沢なランチを楽しめました！
次回ディナーを楽しみにしております。

料理をしている様子を間近に見ることができて、お料理をされる皆さんと親しく会話できるスタイルは新鮮でとても楽しかったです。

またカウンターで間近にお料理をしているお客さんに先にお料理を配膳して、テーブル席はあとからという順番もうれしかったです。もし逆だったら、待たされている感じが印象に残って、残念な感じになっていたと思います。

お料理を担当されるシェフがお休みがないことは心配です。
大変おいしかったのと、職人さんとの会話を楽しみながら食事ができたので、また行きたいと思いました。
珍しい旬の食材を巧みに調理いただき、味覚と視覚の両方で料理を楽しめました。
一人でお邪魔しましたが楽しく食事をすることができました。味はもちろんですが、スタッフの方々の心配りもいつもながら素晴らしいです。

ゆったりとお食事をさせていただきました。
お料理も、盛り付けも、ロケーションも、スタッフの方の対応も、大変満足致しました。
また機会を作って是非お伺いしたいと思いました。
人ごみでにぎわっているビルなのに、入店すると、まったく別の空間が広がっていて素敵でした。お料理はどれも丁寧、かつ、色彩豊かで、味わい深いものでした。海外のお客さんも訪れていましたが、フロアの方も、シェフの方も、臆することなく対応しており、ホスピタリティが溢れる素晴らしいお店でした。また機会をつくって利用したいと思います。ごちそうさまでした。
料理の素材、調理方法、プレゼンテーションも素晴らしかったですが、サービスもよく、カウンター席でシェフといろいろ話すことができたのも、非常に楽しかったです。また再訪したいと思います。
シェフの方をはじめ、スタッフ皆様がとても感じがよく料理も美味しく家族で楽しい時間を過ごすことができました。是非、近いうちに伺いたいと思っております。
シェフと会話をしながら楽しくお食事させていただきました。ひとつひとつのお料理の内容にも満足です。若手のスタッフの方々のサービスや対応がぎこちないのが少し残念でした。

お料理のひとつ、ひとつに心がこもって美味しいのは勿論、五感で心身に記録される様が感動しました。
偶然にも世界のTOYOシェフに、お目にかかれて光栄でした！そんなシェフがお皿をさげている店内は威張ってなくて心地よく居る事ができました。お料理だけでなく、人が人して時間を気持ち良く過ごせる空間でした！またぜひ、行きたいお店です！

また、ゆっくりお邪魔したいです。
今度は中山さんが来日しているときに伺いたいと思っています。
ありがとうございましました。

先日は、美味しいお料理を頂きまして有難うございました。
フレンチなら ソースがメインなのに 、素材の持つ旨味が一つ一つ生かされていて美味しく頂きました。
器も 素敵でした。

上手く説明が出来なくて 申し訳御座いません。
今回は、父が是非行きたいと 言う事で来店いたしました。その父が、満足していましたので、、、、

また 機会がありましたら 来店したいです。ありがとうございました。

アミューズから始まり、それぞれの季節の香りが感じられてとても美味しかったです。
盛りつけの心配りが素敵でした。又機会を見つけてお伺いしたいです。

大学時代の友人との食事会に利用させていただきました。
素敵なお料理を堪能しつつ、でも決して肩肘が張った感じではない居心地のいい空間で、お喋りも楽しめました。スタッフの方にも自然な気配りをしていただき、とても満足しました。また東京近郊に行くことがあったら利用させていただきたいです。

お料理は美味しくて、かつ美しく、ボリュームもちょうど良かったです。
マネージャーの気配り、サービスもとても素晴らしく、大変楽しいひとときを過ごすことができました。また、お伺いしたいお店です。

私はメインにカレーを選択、今までで食べた中で一番おいしいカレーでした。魚介の風味濃厚で、絶品。母はメインは豚肉を選択しましたが、これもまた初めての味付けと喜んでいました。
デザートのパルフェもコースでよくデザートはあまり印象に残らないことが多いのですが個々のデザートは料理を食べた後でも美味しくもう一度同じ物を食べたいです。温度感最高。

スタッフの皆様のサービス料理とも、とても満足いたしました。
特にデザート時にサプライズでハッピバースデーをスタッフの
皆様で歌っていただき、妻も大変喜んでおりました。
機会があればまた利用させていただきます。

とても美味しかったです。
カウンターの中の笑顔もとても良かったです。
また、寄らせて頂きます。
お料理の内容や盛り付けなど、全てに力を入れていらっしゃる感じがいたしました！

244688.longDescription:
--
~ Dear guest from Mitsuki ~
We accept reservations from "2 persons". When applying for a waiting list, please apply for a minimum of two people.
Thank you very much for your understanding.
--
“Mitsuki" is located near "Suehiroonsen-cho," in front of Tottori Station, which is surrounded by hot springs for people to relax. It is a 2-star Japanese restaurant that serves dishes based on Kyoto cuisine using only carefully-selected ingredients.

Chef Yuki Mitsui, who trained for about 13 years in a Japanese restaurant in Tokyo, became independent in 2013, opening "Mitsuki" in his home town in Tottori Prefecture. It can be said that the restaurant is like a members-only Japanese restaurant where high-class customers dine. Another secret to its popularity is the restaurant's hospitably with an emphasis on satisfying customer requests.

The dishes at "Mitsuki" are based on Kyoto cuisine, learned during Chef Mitsui's training, and using carefully selected ingredients. Seafood is sourced from all over Japan such as Hamasaka Fishing Port in Hyogo, Iwaya Fishing Port in Awaji, Toyosu Market in Tokyo, etc., drawing on their experience and connections. You can enjoy seasonal local ingredients, such as natural ayu from Chiyokawa in Tottori, snapping turtle, wild edible plants and matsutake mushrooms. For meat, diners can request filet cutlets of Tottori Japanese beef, shabu-shabu, or local wild boar in winter. Ichiban-dashi stock, which is the basis of Kyoto cuisine, consists of Rishiri kelp, that has been matured for 2 years, and dried, pure bonito shavings. The rice at the end of the course is cooked in an earthenware pot just before it is served, at the guests preferred timing.

For Japanese sake, warm Tottori "Bentenmusume" is recommended. There are around 10 kinds of chilled sake from all over Japan such as "Treasure Sword" from Hiroshima, "Suigei" from Kochi, and "Yoshio" and "Shinsei" from Akita. They also have half bottles of white wine and champagne, and a wide variety of plum wine, highballs and shochu.

Inside, there is a cypress wood counter that seats 9 and private rooms with seating for 6. The paintings, calligraphy and utensils are decorated by Kitaro Uchisihma, a poet and potter who is the great-grandfather of the Mitsui clan. They also have old baccarat from young contemporary artists such as Daiki Kosaka and Kyo-yaki from the first Chikusen Miura creating a comfortable space that stimulates the five senses.

This is a comfortable restaurant where you can spend time dining with family and friends, dates and business meetings. "Mitsuki" is a Japanese restaurant that is loved by the locals, where you can take your time enjoying the taste of the chef's creations.
nearestStations: JR Sanin Main Line (Toyooka - Yonago) Tottori
A 10-minute walk from Tottori Station, North Exit (JR Inbi Line)

244679.longDescription: Iwase Town is a port in Toyama that has flourished by Kitamae-Bune since the Edo period. “Cave Yunoki”, is located at the Mori Family's Dozougun, one of the many splendid buildings of Kaisen Donya that are reminiscent of the prosperity of those days. It is a famous restaurant which received the award in a well-known gourmet guide for Toyama Ishikawa (Kanazawa) 2016 and 2021. Chef Eijyu Yunoki studied French cuisine in Toyama Prefecture for 3 years and honed his skills at a French restaurant in Tokyo after moving there. After returning to his hometown and working as a hotel chef for several years, he has been working at his current restaurant since 2009. Chef Yunoki, who knows all the ingredients of Toyama, where he was born and raised, including fresh seafood called "Kitokito fish". 90% of the ingredients used are locally produced, purchased directly from fishermen or other merchants. "We respect high quality ingredients from Toyama and aim for natural cuisine" says Chef Yunoki. While their dishes are based on French cuisine, the ingredients and amazing techniques are taken from different genres and brought together beautifully to create dishes full of originality. They have everything from game meat that is carefully baked in a special kiln to special seasonal ingredients from Toyama. The sake line-up is also inspired by Toyama, and you can enjoy a wonderful combination of sake and ingredients grown in the same location, paired with the food. The spacious interior, which is a renovated 100-year-old warehouse (Cave), has beautiful beams and pillars on the ceiling, giving guests a profound feeling of history together with the comfort of being invited to the living room of a friend. In addition, Iwase is also a town with many creative artisans, and the fact that it incorporates many of the works of local glass artists, ceramic artists, wood carvers, etc. is a characteristic of “Cave Yunoki”, and all the dishes, containers, and space create a value that can only be experienced here. The dinner is limited to one group per day, so there are many guests who come from outside the prefecture for family anniversaries and entertainment. Enjoy the ever-evolving Toyama Cuisine of Chef Yunoki to your heart's content. * We accept reservations for 2 people if the total price is over 50,000 yen, please use the following inquiry form to make a reservation.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Higashi Iwase (Toyama Light Rail)

244951.longDescription:
Toyama City is famous as a tourist spot. Taking advantage of the region's abundant natural resources, the sushi restaurant Gejo can be found in the town of Higashi-Iwase, about ten minutes by car from Toyama Station. 

Not overtly Japanese from the outside, guests can feel the warmth of the interior as they enter the restaurant. It’s the first hint of the novel, fresh approach to the traditional sushi restaurant that chef Takahiro Gejo aims for, and his individualistic ideas are evident in his personal history. After training at local French restaurant Cave Yunoki and sushi restaurant Sushijin in Toyama, he went abroad, visiting France, Italy, Spain and mainland Europe, and worked as a private chef in Bulgaria. After returning to Japan, his full repertoire of skills were put on display at Gejo, which opened in January 2020.  "Deliver what you encounter in the world with its deliciousness", was the Gejo-style, which emphasises simplicity, working to enhance each ingredient’s inherent flavour. The restaurant sources its ingredients mostly from Toyama, except for wasabi from Azumino, Nagano, and caviar from Takachiho, Miyazaki. Guests are invited to enjoy the rare parts of tuna as it is purchased from an acquaintance of a pole-and-line fisherman. 

Above all, Gejo’s true worth is his free ideas, which are unbound by style or genre. For example, from spring to early summer, he serves vinegared rice with red vinegar and grilled rosy seabass in fish broth in the style of classic French soup de poisson, and he also serves bear bone soup with shabu-shabu, leaving guests in anticipation of the following dishes, let alone the nigiri.   The restaurant serves wine from Burgundy and Piedmont, and Domaine wines produced by Japanese makers. The main Japanese sake favoured and offered to guests is Masuizumi produced by Masuda Shuzo in Toyama Prefecture; dishes made with sake lees from Masuizumi are also available. 

The tableware that frames and colors the cuisine are Etchu Seto-yaki ware, as well as many of the works of artists active in Toyama and Iwase, each full of the region’s charms. With only 8 coveted seats at the counter, Gejo is ideal for occasions with family, friends, colleagues and fellow gourmets, a unique slice of Toyama’s gastronomic offering.
nearestStations: A 10-minute walk from Higashi-Iwase Station (Toyama Light Rail)

244609.longDescription:
A two-star “Oryouri Fujii” is a Japanese cuisine restaurant located in Gofuku, 10-minute drive from Toyama Station.  Hironori Fujii, the owner, serves dishes inspired by his love of the local area, featuring Toyama mountain delicacies and delicious seafood. 

After graduating from high school, Chef Fujii spent a year studying Japanese cuisine at the “Ecole Tsuji Tokyo”, the national cookery school in Tokyo. He learned his trade for five years at ""Zeniya""which is a world gourmet guide award washoku restaurant in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, and then went to work at ""Mashita"" in Kyoto’s Gion in for another 6 years, under the supervision of the owner, who was from the main restaurant of the ""Shofukuro"" chain in Shiga. After that, he returned to his hometown Toyama and opened his own restaurant “Oryori Fujii” in 2011. The restaurant has strong regional ties and is highly regarded by the locals, as well as being listed in world gourmet guide.

 “My ethos is to create food that blends the well-established traditions of Japanese cuisine with contemporary techniques, reflecting the changes of the four seasons,” says Chef fujii. He wants his guests to enjoy what he describes as Toyama's “treasure trove"" of food, with dishes that feature produce of the earth and ingredients purchased directly from the producers. His aim is to serve dishes that consist almost entirely of produce from Toyama. He puts a particular emphasis on the “dashi” (soup stock) he uses since this is the base ingredient for all his cooking. The key ingredients are: kelp (Chef fujii uses high-grade aromatic Rishiri kelp from Hokkaido); bonito flakes (he uses high quality dried fermented tuna, “katsuobushi,” from Makurazaki in Kagoshima - the flakes are shaved daily to ensure the best dashi); water (he uses well water from Manjusen's brewery). He adds seasonal ingredients and serves these together with the dashi as a soup dish which can be enjoyed all year round. 

The fine quality of Toyama's water means it is also well-known for its sake and liquor. Fujii serves a wide range of sake from Toyama breweries; there are 20 varieties available, each one from a different brewery to ensure as representative a selection as possible. In terms of non-local varieties, the restaurant serves sake from the Manjusen, the Iwase storehouse in the restaurant area. It also serves wine from “SAYS FARM” in Himi, Toyama, as well as shochu and plum wine from Toyama. Inside the restaurant, where you can experience the food being prepared in front of you, and a tatami room with tables and chairs which are suitable for a wide range of occasions, from dates to dinners with friends and family. There is also a completely separate private room (4-6 seats), recommended for important occasions such as entertaining or a meeting.

Chef Fujii  feels a deep affection for the region and is devoted to using ingredients from the local area. He is now preparing a new phase of growth. His restaurant will relocate to the “Iwase area” with its early Edo period buildings in the northern part of Toyama, this quiet port town redolent of old Japan. 

Overall this is a restaurant that sets its sights on being a high-class venue. It has its eyes firmly set on the future, with the unending pursuit of its ideals to convey the best that Japanese culture has to offer.
nearestStations: A 10-minutes walk from Toyama Light Rail or Higashi-Iwase Station on the JR Hokuriku Main Line or Hokuriku Shinkansen

245245.longDescription:
Facing the Sea of Japan, Toyama Prefecture is rich in marine products and has a number of fishing ports along Toyama Bay, including Himi Fishing Port. Located in a quiet area near the center of the prefecture’s capital, Kitokito Hagiwara is only a seven-minute walk from Marunouchi Station on the Toyama City Tram Line. The restaurant opened at a location in front of Toyama Station in 2011 and was relocated to its current location in 2019. The premises house a tea house that was relocated from a long-established traditional Japanese restaurant (Kincharyo) that opened in Sakuragi-cho, Toyama City, in 1929.

Kitokito Hagiwara is helmed by Chef Yutaka Hagiwara. Born in Toyama and raised in a family that ran a fish shop, he grew up on high-quality fresh seafood. He started his career outside the culinary field but later switched to the restaurant industry as he enjoys seeing people eating and enjoying his seafood like the customers from fish shop. Motivated by the smiles of his pleased guests, he led his restaurant to be awarded one star in the world’s leading restaurant guide.
Kitokito Hagiwara serves highly elaborate dishes to allow diners to thoroughly enjoy the seasonal ingredients of Toyama. Not only the ingredients but also the tableware and furnishings are locally sourced in Toyama. The water used for cooking is also locally sourced from a spring in Kamiichi. This soft water brings out the best flavor of kelp in the dashi stock. The first brewed dashi stock is made from bonito and tuna. The chef’s specialty is trout sushi, a local dish in Toyama that he gives a twist to by adding trout roe and tangle shavings between the trout and sushi rice. It is highly recommended. Another popular dish is a soybean milk hotpot featuring so-called Ikeda Beef from Ikeda Farm in Toyama, garnished with early onions and watercress. After their meals, guests move to the tea house on the premises where they are offered matcha tea and sweets made by Chef Hagiwara.
The beverage menu offers some 10 labels of local Japanese sake, including those from SAYS FARM in Himi, Toyama. Diners can also enjoy a marriage of food and Japanese sake sourced from Toyama, which is well supplied with snowmelt from the Tateyama Mountains throughout the year and has a number of distinguished sake breweries that draw water from selected exquisite water systems.

The interior of the restaurant, which was converted from a large mansion, has a modern design with warm wood accents. With an eight-seat counter and two private rooms, Kitokito Hagiwara is perfect for celebrating anniversaries and family events, entertaining guests from outside the prefecture, and enjoying local flavors.
The word “kitokito” included in the restaurant’s name means “fresh” in Toyama dialect and is often used to refer to fresh seafood. Please enjoy the freshest seafood of Toyama at Kitokito Hagiwara.
nearestStations: A 7-minutes on foot from Marunouchi Station on the local train from JR Toyama Station

245498.longDescription:
Just take a short 10-minute streetcar ride from Toyama Station to Kokusai-Kaigijo-Mae Station, and you will find the Japanese restaurant “Dai” in a quiet neighborhood nearby the station. Helmed by Owner-Chef Daisuke Murai, who knows Toyama like the back of his hand, the restaurant celebrates the charms of the region with exquisite dishes highlighting the bounty of the land and sea.

Owner-Chef Murai first trained at Japanese restaurants in Kanazawa and Kyoto. Then, in 2001, he returned to his hometown and opened a Japanese tavern, Sakana Kobo Dai, in front of Toyama Station. It was a smash hit for its casual dishes featuring local, seasonal ingredients. Over two decades after the opening of his first restaurant, he opened a detached Japanese restaurant, Dai, in 2023 to embody his vision of a Japanese restaurant.

Dai specializes in full-course meals, each consisting of 11 to 12 courses from appetizers to desserts and finishing with a cup of weak green tea. The menu mainly features local ingredients, including locally grown rice. The stock is also made from ingredients familiar to local taste buds, such as extremely soft spring water from Mt. Joyama, which is suitable for making stock, and Rausu Kombu kelp from Hokkaido, where many migrant workers from Toyama work in kelp forests. In spring, bamboo shoots from Kurokawa, Imizu City, are featured in meals, and so are edible wild plants picked by Chef Murai himself. In summer, wild sweetfish from the Jinzu River is slowly grilled over charcoal in front of guests at the counter. In autumn, soba noodles are handmade with buckwheat flour from Yamada Village and served with wild nameko mushrooms from Nanto City. In winter, Himi’s winter yellowtail from the Bay of Toyama is featured as a specialty. These diverse seasonal ingredients are the reason why Toyama is called a “treasure trove of food.” Meanwhile, the drink menu offers some 50 options of sake, mainly from Toyama, and a wide selection of wines, not only from France and Italy but also from Toyama, to meet the different tastes and preferences of guests.

The interior is designed entirely in Japanese style, adorned with seasonal flower arrangements by Owner-Chef Murai. The main dining room has a spacious 10-seat counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood, and the two private rooms off the main dining room can seat up to 10 and four guests, respectively. Although the restaurant is now sought after by foodies from inside and outside Japan, Owner-Chef Murai continues on his quest for deliciousness, as he says, through a series of trials and errors on the way to perfection. So visit Dai every season and embark on a culinary journey with the chef who continues to pursue greater heights to discover the seasonal flavors of Toyama.
nearestStations: 1 minute walk from Toyama Chitetsu Toyama City Line Kokusai Kaigijo-mae Station

245551.longDescription:
Situated in Himi City, Toyama Prefecture, at the bottom of the Noto Peninsula, the sushi restaurant, Naruki, is blessed with an abundance of produce from the land and sea of Noto and Toyama Bay. Helmed by Chef Naruki Takimoto, the restaurant offers amazing delicacies and nigiri sushi featuring local ingredients favored by culinary professionals. Hailing from Himi, Toyama, known as a treasure trove of fresh ingredients, he initially pursued a career in the music industry and moved to the UK for job opportunities. However, his encounter with a sushi chef in the country changed his career path. Impressed by the rhythmical movements of the chef’s hands conjuring up sushi behind the counter like a live performer, he apprenticed under the chef. After six years of apprenticeship, he returned to Japan and further honed his skills at Ginza Kyubey Ginza Honten for seven years, Sushi Namba Hibiya for two years, and a Japanese restaurant for one year. Then, in July 2022, he opened his own restaurant, Naruki, in his hometown.

The chef’s choice prix-fixe dinner consists of about 20 courses, starting with delicacies, such as sashimi and grilled and simmered dishes, followed by 10 pieces of nigiri sushi, rolled sushi, Japanese omelet, and miso soup. The sushi menu proudly features fish and shellfish sourced from local catches and prepared in Edomae style. The sushi rice is made from a mix of naturally cultivated varieties, including Sasashigure locally sourced from Nagasaka in Himi and Shitsuhara in Noto, and seasoned with a ruby-colored blend of two different types of rice vinegar from Imakawa Suzo, a long-established vinegar brewery, in Kanazawa. The first piece of sushi is topped with squid to highlight the flavor of the sushi rice. The fourth piece of sushi featuring small horse mackerel from local waters off the coast of Himi is a specialty of the restaurant that shines like the fourth batter in a baseball lineup. Fresh from the sea, the horse mackerel is elevated from a common sushi topping to an excellent treat that melts in the mouth. In addition, Japanese rock oysters and oval squid are also offered in summer. The wide variety of fish and shellfish available throughout the year is why Himi, Toyama, is called a treasure trove of fresh ingredients. These fresh seasonal ingredients are all must-tries! They are complemented by about 70 different varieties of sake, mainly from Toyama Prefecture but also from the Hokuriku region, including Akebono and Hatsuarashi from Takazawa Sake Brewery in Himi. The wines from Says Farm Winery in Himi also offer a perfect marriage of local food and drink.

Once you enter through the striking black lattice façade, you will find a spacious interior (with an area of 165 sq. meters) where time passes leisurely. With a 7m-long counter made of solid Kiso hinoki cypress wood (seating up to eight guests) and two private dining rooms with tables (for six guests each). Naruki is suitable for various occasions, from family and friend gatherings to corporate meals, date nights, and dinners with guests from abroad. Please enjoy seasonal ingredients and flavors from Himi, Toyama.
nearestStations: 25 minutes walk from Himi Station

245570.longDescription:
About 30 minutes’ drive from Toyama City, Shikiryori Yu is located in Uozu City, Toyama Prefecture, bordered by the 1,000-meter-deep Toyama Bay and the 3,000-meter-high Tateyama Mountain Range. Helmed by Chef Fumiaki Umino, the restaurant offers kaiseki cuisine inspired by seasonal flavors and local ingredients, including seafood, meat, vegetables, fruits, and spring water. Hailing from Uozu City, Chef Umino studied at Kyoto Culinary Art College and trained at a renowned Japanese auberge “Yamabana Heihachi Jaya” and a bistro “Gion Plum” in Kyoto. Subsequently he returned to his hometown of Uozu and further honed his culinary skills at Japanese Cuisine Kazumino before venturing into self-employment. Then, he opened an izakaya kappo restaurant, Shokusai-An Yu, in Uozu City in 2009. His exquisite Kyoto-style dishes made the restaurant a popular destination. It was even featured in a global gourmet guide in 2016. However, at that time, he discovered the charm of local ingredients through study meetings with fellow chefs and decided to convert his restaurant into Japanese kaiseki with a focus on local ingredients. He made a new start with the restaurant Shikiryori Yu in 2017. The menu showcasing the charm of local ingredients which even local diners did not know made the restaurant a smash hit and won one star from the above-mentioned gourmet guide in 2021.

The curated prix-fixe menu offers 11 courses of kaiseki cuisine, including appetizer; soup; sashimi; grilled, simmered, steamed, and vinegared dishes; rice; and dessert. The menu features locally sourced seasonal ingredients – firefly squid, Japanese glass shrimp, mozuku seaweed, freshly picked bamboo shoots, and other edible wild plants in spring; Japanese rock oysters and sea eel as well as asparagus, corn, tomatoes, and other vegetables from the towns of Nyuzen and Asahi in summer; wild mushrooms, hen of the woods, and other mountain vegetables as well as red snow crab, ocean pout, and other seafood in autumn; and yellowtail, crab, amadai, and longtooth grouper in winter. The seasonal menu also includes wild bear meat, which is hunted and processed by experienced, skilled hunters in the Kurobe and Yao regions. The fish is bought alive from the market and bled out and killed by Chef Umino at the restaurant using the shinkeijime technique. The rare fishes, such as hammerhead shark and tidepool gunnel, are also purchased, and prepared by grilling, simmering, or frying, depending on their condition. In addition, cutlets (commonly made for special occasions in the local area) are featured on the menu, such as those made with Kurobe Meisui Pork, Tateyama Pasture-raised Wagyu Beef, or Taniguchi Beef (from Farm Taniguchi in Nyuzen Town) – all of which are served with the restaurant’s exclusive homemade cutlet sauce.

The drink menu offers about 15 labels of sake, including locally brewed varieties, such as Masuizumi, Kachikoma, and Hayashi from Toyama, Honami from Uozu (brewed by the city’s only sake brewery, Uozu Shuzo), and Shiraiwa’s Iwa from Tateyama, as well as wines from Kanata Winery in Uozu and Says Farm in Himi and non-alcoholic sparkling wines from Celeble in Toyama. The interior is clean and elegant with mortar walls and a counter made from a single piece of ginkgo wood (seating up to eight guests). In addition to the counter, there are two tables (each seating up to four guests) and two horigotatsu-style private dining rooms (one seating up to four guests and the other up to six guests). This makes the restaurant perfect for various occasions, from private to business, such as family and friend gatherings, corporate meals, date nights, and dinners with business partners and clients from abroad. Explore the lesser-known charm of Uozu, Toyama, at Shikiryori Yu.
nearestStations: 3 minutes walk from the main exit of Uozu Station

244525.longDescription:
Toyama Bay. Nutrient-rich water flows down from the Tateyama mountain range and into the submarine valley of the bay, creating the perfect natural environment for fish to grow up. ""Sushi Daimon,"" established by Taro Daimon, stands near the station in Uozu, a port town looking out over Toyama Bay. Growing up in the vicinity of such bounteous waters, Chef Daimon dreamed of becoming a sushi chef with his own restaurant even from an early age. He got his first job working part-time at a sushi restaurant when he was still in high school, then went on to gain experience at a traditional Japanese restaurant, before moving to Otaru, Hokkaido at the age of 22. There, he landed the opportunity to train at a long-established sushi restaurant for four years, after which he further honed his skills at Sushi Zen in Sapporo. During the years away from his hometown, Daimon began thinking about making sushi in Toyama and resolved to establish a sushi restaurant worthy of the location. After returning to Toyama, he opened ""Sushi Daimon"" in 2012. At last, Chef Daimon's dream of owning his own sushi restaurant had come true. Moreover, by 2016, Sushi Daimon had grown to the point where the chef's ability earnt the restaurant international acclaim, as it was awarded in the world gourmet guide that very same year.

Dishes at ""Sushi Daimon"" incorporate plenty of fresh seafood that has just been unloaded at Uozu fishing port, such as Japanese Spanish mackerel, tilefish, rosy seabass, and glass shrimp. Luxury ingredients that Chef Daimon first encountered when he was training, such as tuna and sea urchin, are procured from Hokkaido and Tsukiji Fish Market. Chef Daimon says, ""I can get almost everything that I need from Toyama Bay, but sometimes you just have to go to Tsukiji,"" as he always pays attention to the seasonal tastes from around Japan. Furthermore, he makes every effort to coax out the maximum flavor of the carefully chosen fish in every dish he serves. For the sushi rice, Chef Daimon uses Koshihikari rice produced in Uozu that has been allowed to age for one year. It goes perfectly with the fish that have grown up in the same environment, and Chef Daimon prepares it with a blend of three kinds of red vinegar made with sake lees combined with salt and sugar. The glaze used on some of the sushi (made by boiling down a mixture of soy sauce, mirin, sake, kelp, and bonito flakes) has a flavor that combines exquisitely with the sushi and contributes to the popularity of ""Sushi Daimon"". There is a good selection of Japanese local sake from Toyama to enjoy with a meal, including Hayashi, Kachikoma, and Hokuyo.

""Sushi Daimon"" is arranged with 7 seats at the counter, and seating for a further eight people in a private tatami-matted room. The counter itself is made from a single piece of Hinoki cypress. Diners at the restaurant will find their place laid with a pair of bespoke Yoshino cedar chopsticks, designed to be easy to use. From couples to families, ""Sushi Daimon"" is the perfect place to be, whatever the occasion. ""I aim to have people come to the restaurant simply to try my sushi,"" says Chef Daimon with a twinkle in his eye, and, once you've tried the sushi that he makes, you're sure to want to come again and again.

244652.longDescription:
On a quiet corner in the back streets of downtown Toyama, a sign with glowing light leads you to the Japanese restaurant Fukuya. In this secluded location, they serve relaxing, high quality meals made with local Toyama ingredients. It has received world gourmet guide award.

Owner-chef Joji Oya worked at Nishiazabu’s Kasumicho Suetomi (now closed), and then spent six and a half years helping at his family’s soba restaurant before going independent. He opened Fukuya in 2015.

Owner-chef Oya has a predilection for ingredients from his hometown Toyama. 80% of the ingredients he uses are from Toyama, including fresh seafood caught in Toyama Bay, which his known as one of Japan’s foremost fishing grounds. He also expands his cuisine by sourcing special ingredients like organic vegetables and local game meats through his connections with the vendors. Taking advantage of Toyama’s many natural blessings, owner-chef Oya even serves mushrooms picked by himself, these uniqueness makes the appealing part of Fukuya.

The 10-dish menu starts from appetizer to dessert, with other dishes recommended by the chef. With his cooking, Oya aims to provide “food that calms the mind and provides energy for tomorrow.” In order to do so, he avoids excessive seasoning, brings out the best in the ingredients and makes the most of each ingredient.

Without over exaggeration and paying attention to overall balance, guests will not loose their appetites during the beautiful meal. There are 13-15 varieties of sake available, mainly from local brands in Toyama. The sake collection are light and refined, in order to taking over the tastes of the cuisine. The wines are also lighter style, and are selected to pair with Fukuya’s dishes.
For seating, there is a counter for 8 guests as well as tables, and it can be reserved for private parties with up to 20 guests.

There are also private rooms available for families with children. Furthermore, on the third floor of the same building, a banquet space can accommodate 30-35 people. (With additional charges)

It is a place for special occasions like family celebrations and birthdays, or as a special treat for oneself. With the elegant atmosphere in Fukuya, please enjoy essential excellence of Japanese cuisine.

244660.longDescription: "Tempura Takano (Tempura Koizumi Takano)" is a 1-starred tempura restaurant where you can enjoy freshly fried tempura using ingredients in season from Toyama. The chef, Tomoo Takano, showcases his skills at a counter with a live feel. Mr. Takano, who is from Osaka, trained for about 16 years at the venerated tempura restaurant "Ippo" in his hometown of Osaka before going independent, opening "Tempura Takano (Tempura Koizumi Takano)" in 2013. He chose the location of Toyama based on the recommendation of a former senior co-worker who had opened a restaurant earlier in Kanazawa and pays tribute to him by including his name, "Koizumi", in the name of the restaurant. The tempura here is fried individually with care in 100% safflower oil, using rigorously selected ingredients in season, primarily sourced from Toyama, and is finished with a light, thin batter in the Kansai style. The firefly squid in early spring and the white shrimp are customer favorites, and the Toyama-grown rice, cooked in a pot, is regarded highly. Mr. Takano says "I want our guests to savor the freshly fried tempura as close to me as possible." The counter, which makes this wish possible, provides premium seating. There is also a wide variety of drinks, with around 15 varieties of Japanese sake mostly focused on microbrews from Toyama, but also including Japanese sake from outside the prefecture. The wine starts with SAYS FARM, in Himi, Toyama, and ranges to the Kenzo Estate in California as well as French wine. The interior has a relaxed ambiance with an extremely luxurious feel. There are nine seats at the counter so do savor the live experience slowly, listening to the sound of the tempura being fried. Small parties such as family and friends, or co-workers, are recommended. An English menu is available, so tourists visiting Toyama from overseas should feel comfortable dropping by. 【SNS】 Click here to view the restaurant's Instagram.
nearestStations: A 3-minute walk from Toyama Station, Exit North(JR Hokuriku Line)

245147.longDescription:
This acclaimed two-star destination restaurant is nestled in the mountains above Toyama Prefecture, relocated from Toyama City to its current location in December 2020. The restaurant was built with an accommodation facility in a cleared area of 7,500 m2 overlooking the Toga River.

Toga Village, where L'évo is located, is surrounded by 1,000-meter-high peaks and steep canyons blanketed with greenery. The village is also close to the historic villages of Gokayama known for their houses with steeply pitched thatched roofs inscribed in the World Heritage list. The village is a 90-minute drive from Toyama City or Kanazawa City, and a 40-minute drive from the nearest railroad station (JR Johana Station). Overnight guests can request a pickup service from JR Ecchu Yatsuo Station. While a significant trip from the city, the vistas and mountain breeze alone make a visit to the restaurant unforgettable.

L'évo is helmed by chef Eiji Taniguchi, who was born in Osaka and trained at three-star restaurants in Japan and France. He opened L'évo in the southern area of Toyama City in 2014. The restaurant was awarded one star, and he himself won the Chef Award of the Year, the highest accolade in the Japanese edition of a world-renowned restaurant guide, in 2017.

L'évo offers French cuisine that celebrates the bounty of the region. Flanked by the Sea of Japan and the mountains, Toyama Prefecture is blessed with a bounty from the land and sea. The restaurant’s specialty, L'évo Chicken, made with chicken thighs exclusively grown for chef Taniguchi and sake rice originally used to brew the local Japanese sake “Masuizumi,” is still on the menu. Entrées also highlight local game meat, such as wild bear and sika deer meat; meanwhile, fresh fish and shellfish are delivered from a local market near Yokata Fishing Port each day, selected by the chef or another staff member. The tableware and cutlery are also produced by local artists.

The wine list offers a wide selection of Japanese wines, including white wines from a Japanese sake brewery known for Masuizumi and wines from Says Farm in Himi, as well as imported wines, mainly from France and Italy. In addition to wines, guests can also explore a variety of Japanese sake, including Masuizumi and Kachikoma. Both alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks pairings are available.

The restaurant has a graceful and modern interior with a counter seating up to four guests, three tables (each seating up to four guests), and two private rooms seating up to four and six guests respectively. The dining space is connected to the kitchen so that diners can sit and watch the chef and his team working. Though it should be noted that guests must be 12 years or older (old enough to have a full-course meal) to dine at the restaurant, L'évo can be booked out for special events, as well as anniversaries and gourmet gatherings to enjoy chef Taniguchi’s cuisine. In addition, English- and Chinese-speaking staff are on hand to assist guests from abroad.

Worth a special journey, L'évo offers seasonal delights reflective of the surrounding landscape, allowing guests to feel closer to nature, and to appreciate the significance and charm of the region through chef Taniguchi’s graceful dishes.
nearestStations: A 40-minutes by car from Etchu-Yatsuo Station on the JR Takayama Line and Johana Station on the JR Johana Line

245426.longDescription:
Five to six minutes by car from Toyama Station. A two-minute walk from Yasunoya Station on the Toyama Chitetsu Railway, which runs through Toyama City. Ebitei Bekkan boasts a perfect location, located along a river known for being a cherry blossom viewing spot and close to Yasunoya Kotohira Shrine. The owner, Kentaro Mura, entertains customers with food that give full expression to the charms of Toyama and other parts of the Hokuriku region.

Mura is the fourth generation owner of a venerable Japanese restaurant. He took over the family business after apprenticing at Tokushima Aoyagi, which is renowned for Japanese cuisine. In 2016, when the opening of the Hokuriku Shinkansen line drew attention to the food of Toyama, the restaurant was awarded two stars and closed temporarily in 2018 in search of further advancement. He studied at a famous restaurant in Tokyo and reconsidered his cooking style. When the time was finally ripen in October 2022, the restaurant relocated and opened as Ebitei Bekkan.

From appetizers to rice to finish off the meal, many of the dishes are made with ample local ingredients from the Hokuriku region. From 5:30AM each morning, Chef Mura participates in ocean-front auctions held at Shinminato and Himi ports among other sites. After his sourcing runs, he returns to the restaurant and begins prepping soba buckwheat noodles. It takes an hour by car to collect the two types of spring water used for cooking. Rice is cooked with soft water. The rice served is koshihikari rice from Oyabe City in Toyama Prefecture, which is paired with accompaniments that change with the seasons. Also, different broth as well as water is used for each dish. Medium-hard water is used for the soups, and Rishiri kombu and Makurazaki bonito flakes are used for the broths. Rausu kombu and Makurazaki dried bonito flakes are used in the simmered dishes.

Joining sake from within Toyama prefecture, such as Kachikoma and Masuizumi as well as Tateyama for warmed sake, are Denshu from Aomori and other selected sake from outside the prefecture. There is also a selection of whiskies produced by Wakatsuru Shuzo in Toyama.
Chef Mura has also obtained a sommelier certification during his apprenticeship. There is a many kinds of wines, including those from SAYS FARM.
Non-alcoholic options include plum juice produced by a local winery, Japanese tea, and Taiwanese tea, all presented in wine glasses to entertain guests.

The reception area is on the first floor of a stylish building that catches the eye from the street. The dining room on the second floor has six counter seats (seven may be seated if fully reserved) and two private rooms (for four and six guests). English-speaking staff are on hand to serve international guests. Please try the restaurant for a variety of settings, from private occasions with family and friends or as a couple, to client entertainment and other business situations.
nearestStations: From JR Toyama Station, take the Toyama Local Railway City Tram in the direction of Toyama University and get off at the Anoyacho stop. 2-minute walk / 6-minute drive.

244106.longDescription:
In Iwade city, Wakayama prefecture, there is a restaurant run by a couple coexisting with nature. Using vegetable and herbs harvested from their own farm, serving creative Italian to guests. Departing from the urban and staying with a accommodation and select shop, two-star "Villa AiDA" is attracting gourmands from within Japan and overseas. While seeing fields and sea, enjoy the nature and time staying with Mr. and Ms. Kobayashi.
 
Chef's selected course only for both lunch and dinner. Using organic vegetable coming from farms nearby and the AiDA farm next to the restaurant imaging European historic establishment, guests are served with creative dishes prepared by Chef Kobayashi. "There is a special flavor hidden in the vegetable and herbs harvested on the same day morning" says Kobayashi. Vegetables, fruits, meat and fish, ingredients coming from the mountains and seas at Wakayama, also game meats and vegetable from friends and farmers around, you can taste the origins of all the ingredients used in "Villa AiDA". Wines chosen are also showing the pure flavor of grapes used. 

English, French and Italian service available, overseas guests can enjoy with confidence. Forget those restaurants at urban district and spend a meaningful time in nature, it will be an irreplaceable experience to enrich your life.

244347.longDescription:
Tanabe-shi is located in the southwest part of Wakayama prefecture, surrounded by abundant nature. In this area, blessed with the fruits of the mountains and the sea, "Shizen Mukuan" opened in 2016. It uses only local ingredients from the southern Kii Peninsula, and has a reputation for creating once-in-a-lifetime cuisine, flexibly adjusting the ingredients and recipe according to requests from customers. It is located about a 10-minute walk from JR Kii Tanabe, the nearest station, but it has fans who travel from all over the country to eat food only available at this restaurant.

The owner-chef Toshimasu Kumoi has pioneered routes to purchase stock from local suppliers and has introduced a lot of local ingredients that are not yet widely known. They include agricultural products such as Tanabe almonds and ‘Fuji ume’, a processed food made from Nankobai plums, as well as seasonal marine products cultivated in the abundant ocean, such as Frog crab, Red Eye Puffer fish, or whitebait and Bigfin Reef Squid eggs from Tanabe. Rare and luxurious seafood, such as wild eel, Slipper lobster and Spider crab, also appear according to the time and budget. And when it comes to meat, again they stick strictly to local products such as brand pork and beef. 

Ingredients and methods used in cooking the food are adjusted according to the customer. For example, in the spring they offer things such as horsetail picked by the guests themselves with locally reared wild boar in a sukiyaki dish or baked whole bamboo shoots grown in Tanabe. Also, they ask guests to break almonds themselves, to bake pork on magnolia leaves at the table, and other enjoyable little experiences. They also have locally produced beer and sake, so you can enjoy the exquisite compatibility of different fruits of the earth.

The warm, wooden-based interior has 7 counter seats and 8 table seats. Mr. Kumoi says, “The word Mukuan in the name of the restaurant does not mean the literal ‘end of suffering’, but I chose a name that conveys my hope that you can forget about it when you come to the restaurant." If you’re looking for wonderful cuisine and hospitality that lets you forget about everything, this a restaurant worth going out of your way to visit.

珍しい食材が多く楽しい。これらの珍しい食材全てがおいしいものではないと想像するが、それをおいしく仕上げるのが、一流料理人の大将の腕なのだとお察しする。
盛り付けは、この地方を体現しているかのような、素朴な美しさ。

いただいたのは13000円のコース。
振り返ってみると、いのししの焼き物以外のすべてのメニューに味わったことのない食材が含まれているし、いのししも食べたことないおいしさだった、というすごさ。

圧巻なのが、人の好みなどはさまざまな中、1人1人のとって最高のもの出したいという大将の情熱。
例えば、いのししの焼き物をいただいたときのこと。
大将、脂がおいしいのだが、女性は概して脂を嫌う傾向にある、こちらが一見の女性客でネット予約、どんな人かわからなかったので、相当悩んだ末脂は取り除いたとのこと。
１つ１つのメニューの出し方について、そんな感じでこちらの立場を考え相当悩んでくださったようす。感激。こちらからすれば、そんなに悩むなら電話をくださればいいのにと思ったが、ネットで予約する人は概して電話を嫌がるので、、とのこと。

1人1人オーダーメイドのコースなので事前に電話で打ち合わせたい旨に関してはHPを読んで把握していた。一方で、私はHPを見て、それぞれの知らない希少食材がどんな味なのか想像つかなかったし、食べたことない食材は何でも食べてみたい。これまでのレビューを拝見して、どのコースでも満足しそうと思ったので、特に電話せず、紀南ならではの食材、珍しい食材をいただきたいです、とのみコメントしていた。
一方で大将からすれば、珍しい食材といっても人によって何が珍しいと感じるかはさまざまだし、よくわからなかったとのこと。言われてみればたしかに。しかも例えば、このイノシシの焼き物ひとつひとつとっても、脂を付けたままがいいか取り除いた方がいいか、薄切りがいいか厚切りがいいか、味噌漬けの味付けは好みか別の味付けの方がいいか、そんなことまで電話してれば配慮してくださるそう。HPに書いてあったオーダーメイドは、それほどのレベル。
事前に電話を、とHPに書いてあった意味がよくわかった。まさかそこまで一人一人の客のことを思いやっている大将だったとは。。感嘆と、必要以上に大将を悩ませてしまった申し訳なさと、電話していればもっと好みに合った満足な食事になったのではという後悔と。。

244792.longDescription:
Situated a 15-minute drive from JR Wakayama Station and a 6-minute walk from the nearest Miyamae Station is a French restaurant that attracts guests not only from within Wakayama Prefecture but also from all over Japan. A one-star “hotel de yoshino” is located on the top floor of Wakayama Big Ai, a 12-story commercial complex run by public-private company associated with Wakayama Prefecture. There are no tall buildings nearby, so it stands out distinctly from its surroundings.

“hotel de yoshino” is a restaurant named after Tateru Yoshino, one of Japan’s leading chefs. Chef Yoshino opened “STELLA MARIS“ in Paris and was rewarded with a star in 2006. “hotel de yoshino” is one of the restaurants run by Chef Yoshino in Japan. Based on the concept of terroir (earth) cuisine, the restaurant elevates rich ingredients gathered from Wakayama and neighboring areas into traditional French cuisine.

The cuisine of “hotel de yoshino” features a classic style that is faithful the traditions of French cuisine. Wakayama is blessed with a diverse range of delicious bounties from the Seto Inland Sea and the Pacific Ocean, as well as its mountains, such as wild game caught locally. The specialty of Chef Teshima is Iwagaki oyster cuisine that can only be savored in Wakayama. Another superb dish is his game meat tart (wrapped in a pie crust) accompanied by an exquisite sauce made by reducing meat juices and red wine that reflects on the plate like a shiny mirror. Chef Teshima’s outstanding culinary skill attracts fans from all over Japan. The restaurant always cellars more than 300 fine wines from France and around the world. There is also a plentiful selection of local sake and craft beer. As for non-alcoholic selections, mandarin orange juice and herb teas native to Wakayama offer special appeal.

The restaurant is open and spacious with 35 tables and private rooms for parties of two to six guests. Works of modern art stand out in the bright white interior. The spacing between tables is ample and generous, with large windows overlooking the city of Wakayama. Dinner with a good vantage point for taking in the night scenery is also not to be missed. “hotel de yoshino” is perfect not only for dates and anniversary celebrations, but also for family gatherings and for entertaining overseas guests. Enjoy the essence of the ever-evolving classical French cuisine that not only represents Wakayama, but also Japan itself, here in Wakayama’s “hotel de yoshino”.

A 1-minute walk from Teheideshima Bus Stop, Wakayama Bus from Wakayamashi Station(Nankai Main Line) or 20-minute taxi from Wakayamashi Station
