245439.longDescription:
Dewaya was founded in 1929 in front of Mazawa Station, a terminal on the Yamagata Kotsu Sanzan Line, in Nishikawa Town in central Yamagata Prefecture to provide food and lodging for travelers taking a train to the sacred Dewa Sanzan mountains. The long-established restaurant is now run by Haruki Sato, the fourth-generation owner who was born in 1988. Guests are asked to take off their shoes as they make their way through the historic entrance, reminiscent of the early days of the restaurant, to the dining room with a chef’s table. Limited to one group of guests at a time, the room is warm with plaster walls and locally sourced natural stone and wood.

The menu features seasonal ingredients from the mountains, including edible wild plants in the spring, river fish and summer mushrooms in the summer, meaty and flavorful mushrooms in the autumn, and game meat, salt-preserved foods, and snow-preserved carrots and turnips in the winter. The dishes born from life in the mountainous region and mountain delicacies only found here tickle the taste buds of guests. The chef’s table, which is limited to one group at a time, represents the owner’s commitment to serving dishes fresh from the mountains. The ingredients vary from day to day, depending on the season and the conditions of the mountains. As wild ingredients are blessings from nature, it is wise to treasure the best of each day.

At Dewaya, different Japanese sake and wines are offered to match each dish and each guest’s preference and are chosen from a great selection of locally brewed sake from around Japan, including Dewazakura, and wines mainly from France but also from around the world. Some options are served by the glass to match each course. The restaurant also offers homemade non-alcoholic drinks such as wild grape juice and perilla juice.

Renovated in 2023, the dining room with a chef’s table has a discreet eight-seat counter made of ancient zelkova with a pleasant feel and large windows that provide relaxing views of the courtyard that changes with the seasons.

Dewaya is accessible mainly by public transportation. Just rent a car or take an express bus from JR Yamagata Station or take a base-fare taxi ride from the nearest bus stop (Nishikawa Bus Stop) for the last part of the journey. The restaurant attracts families, groups of friends, and travelers from outside the prefecture with its unique local dishes featuring edible wild plants and mushrooms. Exclusively booked for one group at a time, the restaurant accommodates children of any age. It also offers a children’s menu if requested in advance. It is advisable to check the menu in advance as it may include natural ingredients your child cannot eat. There is also a simple English menu for foreign guests.

The dishes at Dewaya feature edible wild plants and other mountain products in tribute to the art of living with the blessings of the mountains. Such wholesome dishes will surely add an exclusive touch of color to your journey.
nearestStations: 40 minutes by car from Yamagata Station on the JR Ou Main Line, Senzan Line, or Aterazawa Line. Or, take a highway bus bound for Shonai from JR Yamagata Station, get off at Nishikawa IC stop, and drive 5 minutes. *Pick up and drop off available with advance reservation.

245318.longDescription:
A 10-minute drive from JR Yamagata Station takes you to Restaurant Pas Mal set in a discreet neighborhood. Take a step inside, and you will be greeted by a chic black countertop contrasted with a pop color painting. Behind the counter is an open kitchen, where the restaurant’s owner-chef is seen busily at work.

Hailing from Yamagata Prefecture, Chef Yusuke Murayama entered the culinary industry directly after graduating from high school. He trained at restaurants in Yamagata and Tokyo and then returned to his home prefecture of Yamagata to open Bistro Pas Mal in Tendo, Yamagata, at the age of 25. It was relocated to the current location and renamed Restaurant Pas Mal in 2017. The restaurant offers French dishes based on classic techniques. Especially, Chef Murayama is obsessed with sauces, where the essence of French cuisine lies. In addition, knowing about his home prefecture of Yamagata like the back of his hand, the chef incorporates local ingredients into his French dishes.
The ingredients are mostly sourced from Yamagata Prefecture, including edible wild plants locally picked in spring, game meat (e.g., wild boar and duck meat) delivered in autumn and winter from local hunters on friendly terms with the chef, locally bred lamb, and fish from Sakata such as Japanese Spanish mackerel and cherry salmon. Vegetables are supplied from Verdure italiane di Kahoku, an association in the Kahoku region (a town in Yamagata Prefecture) for research and production of Italian vegetables, which grows Western vegetables, such as white asparagus, in summer and Treviso in winter. Thus, local ingredients are featured, rather than truffles, caviar, or foie gras.
The drink menu offers a variety of wines not only from France but also from Yamagata, which has as many as almost 20 wineries, and Japanese sake from local breweries in Yamagata, including those to be paired with dishes. The pairing menu is flexible enough to allow diners to choose the number of glasses of drinks, depending on the number of courses served, and the amount of each glass. The food is mostly served on refined white porcelain plates crafted by Mr. Takahiro Yahagi, a local ceramic artist, as well as being presented on discreet plates to highlight the beautiful colors of the ingredients. The tables are served by the chef’s younger brother, Tatsuaki, who works harmoniously with the chef.

Inside the restaurant, the first floor is shaded in black tones to add an urban touch to the interior, making a contrast with the second floor in bright white tones. The first floor dining room boasts a seven-seat counter, while the second floor dining room has three tables seating up to 12 guests in total, though the number of guests at one time is limited to 10. The restaurant is perfect for family dinners, anniversary celebrations, and dates but also attracts food lovers, many of whom come alone to enjoy French dishes crafted by Chef Murayama. The majority of diners come from outside the prefecture. The restaurant cannot cater for children under about 12 years old who cannot eat the same meals as adults unless it is exclusively booked. Please enjoy the classic French dishes only available in Yamagata at Restaurant Pas Mal.
nearestStations: 20 minutes walk from the east exit of Yamagata Station

244353.longDescription: Yamaguchi prefecture is a famous ingredient treasury nestled between mountains and ocean. It was also elected as CNN's "Japan's 34 most beautiful places" with "Motonosumi-Inari Torii gates" (※). This is where you will find “le-sorcier,” a famous French restaurant and the most exclusive dining spot in the Chugoku region, since its location and contact information are closely-guarded secret. Lunch and dinner are both restricted to a single party, and chefs from around the world sing the praises of this hidden gem, known only to those “in the know.” The Owner-Chef Keiichi Hashimoto came to Tokyo after he graduated from culinary school in Osaka to study in various French restaurants in Tokyo and has worked as chefs in many places. In July of 2015, he returned to his hometown in Shunan-city, Yamaguchi, where he opened “le-sorcier,” which was recognized in the 2018 world-famous gourmand guide as the top culinary spot of western Yamaguchi prefecture. Furthermore, Mr. Keiichi Hashimoto is awarded as the Japan's "remarkable chef", like Alain Ducasse and Alfonso Iaccarino in Europe. He gets his inspiration from the ingredients and tools he uses, assembling them one by one as puzzle pieces, and serves the dish that has the landscape. Over 70 percent of the ingredients are sourced directly from the Yamaguchi area, considering elements such as the terroir of the land and using organic and pesticide-free fruits and vegetables, along with the bounty of the Seto Inland Sea and the ocean surrounding Japan, Atou wagyu, and the Kuro-Kashiwa chickens whose breed was named a natural monument of Japan. The dishes Chef Hashimoto creates, based on his steadfast commitment to making French cuisine by using ingredients that are close to home, has attracted attention even from European media, and his thoroughly original gastronomical delights have charmed many gourmets. Opening the door to “le-sorcier,” which belies the existence of a restaurant beyond, there is one single table that can seat up to 6 people during lunch, or 4 for dinner. While it may strike some as unusual, it also gives the impression of being invited into the chef’s own personal domain. Chef Hashimoto says, “I want people to experience the charm of the region while being enveloped in all the activity related to creating their meals.” It is worth traveling from both near and far to experience the new expression of cuisine made with Yamaguchi ingredients in this restaurant. (※) Motonosumi-Inari Torii gates : Japan's 34 most beautiful places

244751.longDescription: The restaurant is approximately 20 minutes’ walk from Yamaguchi Shimonoseki Station. Located in a perfect location overlooking the sea, chef Kenichi Takatsu offers innovative cuisine overflowing with the charm of Shimonoseki. Chef Takatsu, from Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, wanted to be a chef and learned cooking at a restaurant in Fukuoka. After that, he went to Canada and learned English while working at a Western-style restaurant. After returning to Japan, he not only worked at “Trattoria ALBERI” in Shimonoseki, but also at Karato Market to learn about seafood. He went abroad again, and this time he experienced working at a famous and prosperous store, “Basta Pasta”, in New York. As he returned to Japan, he went back to Fukuoka and worked as a sous-chef at “La Maison de la Nature Goh”. In 2017, he opened his own restaurant, “Restaurant Takatsu” in his hometown of Shimonoseki. Chef Takatsu uses local ingredients to create dishes that are free from any genre. It is a cuisine that uses the ingredients without adding too much, pulling too much and destroying the flavor. For example, in summer, chilled lettuce is served with blue cheese sauce and Delaware. In winter, blackened nappa cabbage from Shimonoseki is served with blue cheese sauce, walnuts and parmigiano, and also Chef Takatsu’s favorite blueback, such as sardine and mackerel, are smoked, served with grilled skin, eggplant from Shimonoseki with smoked garlic, pickled garlic puree, red onion pickles, and so on. The wine that goes well with the creative dishes varies from France, South Africa, Australia and Japan. There are always 5 ~ 6 types of red, white and sparkling wine by the glass. There are also several kinds of sake such as local sake from Yamaguchi Prefecture. The building “Restaurant Takatsu” is located is a Western-style building of a former whaling company that was built in the Taisho era. The chef renovated the building with his sensibilities while keeping the ceiling and pillars of the building, which is designated as a national tangible cultural asset. The counter, which is limited to 9 seats, is made of mortar mixed with ink to create an uneven look, and then ground with a sander to match a retro building. “Restaurant Takatsu” with a nostalgic feeling is recommended as a place for family, friends, dates and wine parties. Please enjoy the innovative cuisine of chef Takatsu, whose charm lies in Shimonoseki. For details on parking lot in the neighborhood, please check on the restaurant website.

244833.longDescription:
Terroir Ai to Ibukuro is located in Hokuto City, Yamanashi Prefecture, in what used to be a posting station on the Sakukoshu Highway. It is a French restaurant that operates in a 170-year-old house and is open only once a day.

The chef is Shinsaku Suzuki. He studied Japanese cuisine in restaurants starting at the age of 15, and then switched to French cooking. After working at several French restaurants, including Restaurant J in Omotesando run by Masahito Ueki, he opened Restaurant Ai to Ibukuro with his wife Emi in 2011 at Sangenjaya in Tokyo. Four years later, in 2017, wishing to live in harmony with nature, he relocated and opened a new restaurant called Terroir Ai to Ibukuro in Yatsugatake, where a former vegetable supplier was located.

The name of the restaurant — Terroir Ai to Ibukuro — comes from a European proverb: "Love comes through your stomach." It was born from chef Suzuki's thought that "how wonderful it would be to grow love by eating delicious food with your loved one!" 

The terrier of Hokuto City is special and valued by the restaurant. Hokuto City has three springs that are considered among the 100 best water sources. It has all kinds of sake breweries and is a very rich area for vegetables, fish, and livestock. Chef Suzuki sometimes goes to Yatsugatake to collect wild vegetables and mushrooms, or hunt deer and ducks. Beef is mainly distributed from Shiga. The specialty from the Sangenjaya era is the seasonal vegetable soup. Among them, the brown mushroom soup during the winter is the most popular. 

There are about 100 kinds of wine, including natural wines from France and options from neighboring areas such as Yamanashi and Nagano. Non-alcoholic pairings are also available, like an original cordial drink made from Yatsugatake herb tea.

Diners will be surprised by the large roof from the entrance, and will see a historic space that has remained unchanged for 170 years. Huge wooden beams of this sort are rarely seen today, and the seats are made using natural materials such as local wood and soil. You will feel at ease in the tasteful space, with a wood stove, bare beams, and earth walls painted with natural materials.A pleasant breeze will pass from the open tatami room to the audience. Please visit this restaurant for birthday, anniversary, or dinner with loved ones.
nearestStations: 20 minutes by car from Kobuchizawa Station (JR Chuo Main Line (Tokyo-Shiojiri), JR Koumi Line (Yatsugatake Kogen Line))

245607.longDescription:
Marked by a long noren curtain in holy white, “Sushi Hinomoto” is located on the first floor of a building about two minutes’ walk from Daimon Station. Guests are welcomed with exquisite sushi crafted by Chef Hayato Wada, who aspires to introduce authentic Japanese sushi culture to the world, as indicated by the restaurant’s name (“Hinomoto” means “Japan” in archaic Japanese). After apprenticeships at popular sushi restaurants, such as Ginza Kyubei and Ginza Iwa,  he took over the kitchen of Sushi Tokami in Ginza as the third-generation chef. Subsequently, he brought his delicate craftsmanship to Singapore, where he continued to delight in the taste buds of foodies from around the world. Then, he returned with success to set up his own business in Japan. Eventually, he became the chef of “Sushi Hinomoto” when it opened in October 2025.

Following the themes of back to basics and innovation, “Sushi Hinomoto” combines traditional sushi-making techniques with Chef Wada’s creative twists to create next-generation sushi. Its essence lies in the prix-fixe menu, which starts with Precious Tuna Handroll, followed by 3 to 5 delicacies and 14 to 15 pieces of nigiri sushi, and ends with soup and Japanese egg omelet. The eye-catching golden sushi rice is made with rice sourced from Hokkaido, cooked with ultra-soft water from Kagoshima, and seasoned with a rice vinegar blend in a brilliant gold color. It matches particularly well with the restaurant’s specialties, bluefin tuna and sea urchin, sourced from Toyosu Market. Selected from the high-quality cuts of upper tuna belly, the Sunazuri Otoro is especially popular for its rich marbling, beefy flavor, and melt-in-the-mouth tenderness. The double-layer stacked Sea Urchin Battleship Roll is also popular for its generous portion size, keeping diners coming back for more.

Pivotal to the story of the multi-course menu, the delicacies prepared using all the five Japanese culinary techniques of cutting, simmering, grilling, steaming, and deep-frying, and also going well with sake. The drink menu offers about 20 varieties of rare sake, such as Kagura from Kyoto, as well as sweet potato shochu from Kagoshima. If you are not sure which drink to choose, try the pairing menu to follow a curated sequence of drinks starting with champagne, followed by sake, sweet potato shochu, and sake pairings. Transitioning from dry to sweet, they create perfect harmony with the dishes.

Inspired by the main shrine of Ise Jingu, the restaurant looks sublime. With charcoal-painted walls and an indigo-dyed whitewood counter (8 seats), crafted using a traditional Japanese dyeing technique called aizome, the interior is also designed with inspirations from Japanese culture. The divine atmosphere is further enhanced by the iconic golden sushi rice on the crystal serving plates that makes a striking contrast with the indigo countertop. Please enjoy the Hinomoto sushi rooted in Japanese culinary tradition, as well as Japanese culture, in the solemn setting of “Sushi Hinomoto”, which makes any occasion memorable, regardless of whether it is personal or business.

245600.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of a building about five minutes’ walk from Yotsuya-Sanchome Station, “Takumi Makoto”, a sushi restaurant, offers exquisite sushi and Japanese dishes crafted by experienced chef Makoto Shimura. He began his career at Tsuji Culinary Institute and then apprenticed himself to Chef Keiji Nakazawa at Sushi Takumi in Yotsuya. After mastering the artistry of Sushi Takumi-style Edomae sushi, he set up his own business and opened “Takumi Makoto” in Shinjuku in February 2017. It was relocated to Yotsuya, a neighborhood full of memories of Chef Nakazawa, in July 2024, and reinforced its reputation as a popular destination for sushi lovers exploring culinary delights.

The prix-fixe menu offers 13 to 14 nibbles and about 13 pieces of nigiri sushi, which are served alternately like in Sushi Takumi. The sushi rice is made with aged Hitomebore rice from Iwate Prefecture, seasoned with red or white vinegar, depending on the topping. All the sushi is served in small portions so that guests can enjoy a variety of seasonal and specialty fish, such as bluefin tuna sourced from Yamayuki, a popular intermediate wholesaler at Toyosu Market. In addition to fish, the restaurant also offers Horse Meat Sushi. Featuring fresh horse meat sourced from the chef’s home prefecture of Yamanashi and marinated in a special sauce, it is a specialty that combines the culinary artistry of Sushi Takumi with the creativity of Chef Shimura. Stuffed Horsehair Crab, also known as Horsehair Crab Shortcake for its resemblance to a cut of shortcake, is also loved by many foodies. Another must-try is Sardine Wrapped in Nori Seaweed. The combination of the savory flavor of the fatty sardine and the refreshing aroma of the nori seaweed is so amazing that even those who do not like silver-skinned fish can enjoy it.

“Takumi Makoto” offers about 20 varieties of refined sake from around Japan, including Shichiken from the chef’s home prefecture of Yamanashi, Dan from the nearest brewery to his birthplace in the prefecture, Hitakami from Miyagi, Okunokami from Higashi Murayama, Tokyo, and KID from Wakayama. Among them, Seikyo, a Hiroshima-brewed Junmai sparking sake given a name that shares the same Chinese characters as the restaurant, is recommended as the first drink of the meal. The drink menu also offers wines and whiskeys, mainly from Yamanashi, such as Grace Koshu white wine and Suntory Hakushu whisky. The interior is warm and cozy with wood accents, and the black Arita ware serving plates on the L-shaped hinoki cypress wood counter (seating up to seven guests) boost expectations for sushi. Please enjoy a delightful dining experience, delicious sushi and delicacies, and friendly conversations with Chef Shimura at “Takumi Makoto”, which makes any occasion unforgettable, regardless of whether it is personal or business.

245606.longDescription:
Situated on the first basement floor near Akasaka-Mitsuke Station, “Sushi Itsumi” is the second location of Sushi Kuriyagawa, a popular sushi restaurant, in Ebisu. Opened in September 2019 by Koichi Kuruyagawa, t he owner-chef of Sushi Kuriyagawa, to provide his apprentices with a stage to demonstrate their honed skills, “Sushi Itsumi” is helmed by Chef Kozo Gomi an experienced sushi chef and an old friend of Chef Kuriyagawa, who was entrusted to take care of young apprentices and oversee the restaurant named after his family name.

“Sushi Itsumi” offers authentic Edomae-style sushi crafted with traditional Japanese culinary techniques, such as simmering, boiling, marinating, and pickling, handed down from Sushi Kuriyagawa. The sushi rice is made with Kinuhikari rice from Shiga, selected for its moderate stickiness and ability to absorb vinegar, and a red vinegar blend with a rounded flavor, and served at body temperature to bring out the best flavors of wild fish and shellfish on top of it. The colorful Nigiri Sushi with Fatty Tuna, Sea Urchin, and Caviar is a signature dish of the restaurant. In addition, infused with playful twists, the delicacies of the restaurant are not just side dishes―heaty enough to satisfy the appetite, they could be standout stars on their own. Especially, Risotto with Karinto-style Deep-fried Abalone and Liver Sauce and the eye-catching Sushi Restaurant’s TKG (scattered sushi topped with meringue and egg yolk) delight the eyes and taste buds of guests.

The drink menu offers 10 varieties of refined sake from around Japan, such as Zaku from Mie, Kokuryu from Fukui, and Dassai from Yamaguchi. They are served in small bottles of 180-ml so that guests can enjoy different pairings. The restaurant also offers wines, shochu, and cocktails to meet the different tastes of guests. With an eight-seat counter and tables seating up to six guests as well as a private dining room furnished with a six-seater round table, “Sushi Itsumi” caters to various needs. In addition, though it features high-quality ingredients from the same suppliers as Sushi Kuriyagawa, such as tuna from Yamayuki, a popular intermediate wholesaler, at Toyosu Market, “Sushi Itsumi” offers sushi and delicacies at more reasonable prices. Please enjoy dishes that continue to evolve as the young apprentices develop their skills and confidence.

245599.longDescription:
About five minutes’ walk from Iidabashi Station, “Kifu” is located on the first floor of the building “kif”, in a back alley near Zenkoku-ji Temple, which is also known as Bishamon-sama of Kagurazaka.  Helmed by Chef Yuki Sato, the sushi restaurant offers refined Edomae-style sushi that suits the Edo vibe of the Kagurazaka district. Hailing from Akita, Sato moved to Tokyo to develop his career as a sushi chef. After apprenticeships at Ginza Rin Nishimura and Ginza Sushi Ichi Ginza Honten, he became the chef of “Kifu” when the restaurant opened in September 2020. Since then, he has developed his style of sushi and cuisine by adding his own twist to traditional Edomae cuisine.

The restaurant’s name, “Kifu”, which means the passage of time and the flow of time in archaic Japanese, reflects the chef’s commitment to creating a pleasant place where time slows down and developing himself step by step over time. Featuring high-quality, seasonal ingredients, such as bluefin tuna sourced from Hicho, a popular intermediate wholesaler, at Toyosu Market, Special Conger Eels caught in the Tsushima Strait and delivered exclusively to noted restaurants through another popular intermediate wholesaler, Ueken, and red sea bream and white tilefish caught by Junichi Fujimoto, a fisherman from Imabari, Ehime, who has earned the trust and loyalty of renowned chefs, the menu offers a multi-course meal consisting of 6 to 7 nibbles, 12 to 13 pieces of nigiri sushi, Japanese egg omelet, miso soup, and dessert. The first sushi is topped with squid so that guests can enjoy the rich flavor of the sushi rice of “Kifu”
. It is made with Yumeobako rice sourced from a contract farm in Akita, cooked in a broad-brimmed rice-cooking pot, and seasoned with a blend of Junmai Fuji vinegar and red vinegar from Iio Brewery in Kyoto. Carefully produced in the farm run by the family of the chef’s former classmate, the Yumeobako rice is characterized by its large grain size and rich flavor. Featuring iburigakko (smoked, pickled radish) produced by the same farm, Iburigakko Torotaku Handroll is a popular specialty of “Kifu”, known for its smoky flavor and irresistible crunch.

The drink menu offers about 10 varieties of refined sake from around Japan, including Mansaku no Hana and Ama no To from Akita, as well as KENZO ESTATE wines, highballs, and other drinks to meet the different tastes of guests. The modern black doors of the building create a stunning contrast with the interior of the restaurant designed in a wabi-sabi style inspired by traditional Japanese tea houses. The black Oribe ware sushi serving plates from Tajimi, Gifu, also contrast elegantly with the L-shaped counter made of plain hemlock wood (seating up to eight guests). Please enjoy an elegant dining experience with exquisite seasonal flavors in a refined setting that befits the historic Kagurazaka district.

245561.longDescription:
A six-minute walk from Sakuragicho Station in Yokohama City, Kanagawa Prefecture, Noge no Onikai opened on the second floor of a building in Nogecho in December 2021 as the third location of Sushi Onikai, a popular, hard-to-book sushi restaurant. At Noge no Onikai, specially selected young sushi chefs create Kuzushi zushi by combining traditional Edomae sushi-making techniques with their original twists.

The chef’s choice menu offers 15 pieces of sushi, three delicacies, and one soup curated based on the concept of authentic sushi at reasonable prices. The menu items are decided through monthly tastings, selected from suggestions offered by kitchen staff across all locations of Sushi Onikai. A particular emphasis is placed not only on the sushi toppings and delicacies prepared with fish and shellfish scrutinized by experts with a discerning eye, but also on the sushi rice made with top-quality rice from Mihama Town, Fukui Prefecture, and red vinegar brewed by Yokoi Vinegar Brewing. Mixed with vinegar in a large wooden bowl in front of guests just before service, the sushi rice is served fresh without any toppings at first, and then served with sushi toppings to help guests discover how to enjoy the flavor that evolves with time like a connoisseur. Known as the specialty of the restaurant, Prawn Tempura Wrapped with Nori Seaweed is created under the supervision of the chef of Tempura Miyashiro, an affiliated restaurant awarded one star in a world-renowned restaurant guide. The crispy prawn tempura placed on a bed of sushi rice and wrapped with a crisp sheet of nori seaweed is handed across the counter. Some of the year-round menu items are also popular, such as Bluefin Tuna Hand Roll featuring three different cuts of tuna (fatty, medium fatty, and lean tuna) and flavorful flash-smoked seafood.

The drink menu offers a great selection of sake, shochu, and beer as well as wines curated by Wine Sommelier and Italian Wine Ambassador Yoshihiro Nagase, who also joined monthly menu tastings to select Italian wines to pair with the sushi and delicacies of Sushi Onikai. Stepping through the inconspicuous entrance with noren curtains, guests are welcomed by an eye-catching plain wood counter (seating up to eight guests) in the modern dining area. Enjoy authentic sushi in a casual setting at the secluded sushi restaurant, Noge no Onikai.

245558.longDescription:
Perched on the third floor of Azabudai Hills Tower Plaza with direct access to Tokyo Metro Kamiyacho Station, Izakaya Uchiyama was opened by Masahiro Uchiyama, the CEO of a company that runs many popular restaurants, such as Nakame no Teppen, Sushi Onikai, Tempura Miyashiro, and Sushi Tsukiuda. Named after his own name, Izakaya Uchiyama is his vision of the ideal izakaya for grown-ups. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Tomoaki Shimada, used to work as a kitchen assistant in a hotel restaurant but became the Executive Chef of Nakame no Teppen Honten in Nakameguro. He also engaged in the opening of Izakaya Uchiyama before becoming its Executive Chef.

Known for its diverse presentations, Izakaya Uchiyama emphasizes appetizing visuals, cooking meat, fish, and vegetables to charred perfection in the charcoal-fired oven like a pizza oven at the kitchen and topping dishes with a pile of fluffy bonito flakes freshly shaved with a bonito shaver. The prix-fixe menu offers 10 courses, starting with two seasonal amuse-bouche courses, followed by a platter of five appetizers, sashimi, oven-cooked meat, fish, and vegetables, and specialty of the day, and ending with seasonal clay pot rice and fishhead soup. Among them, Noriten (bite-sized nori tempura topped with seasonal fish or the like), is a signature dish served as an amuse-bouche. Handed across the counter, this specialty item captures the hearts of many guests.

The drink menu offers a permanent selection of 10 sakes and a seasonal selection of limited-time sakes, as well as about 20 wines, all served by the bottle, to complement the diverse food offerings and satisfy the different tastes of guests. Boasting a main dining area with an L-shaped counter (seating up to 19 guests), a chic private dining room (seating up to eight guests) with black walls, and a semi-private dining room (seating up to four guests), the restaurant caters to various occasions, combining vibrant pub ambience with refined kappo cuisine. Please enjoy the exquisite dishes in a sophisticated setting at Izakaya Uchiyama.

245559.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of a building about six minutes’ walk from Tokyo Metro Higashi-ginza Station, Yakitori Hirano is a refined restaurant helmed by Owner-Chef Ikuji Hirano, who has mastered the art of yakitori (Japanese chicken skewers). Starting his career with Toriyoshi Seo, a renowned restaurant, in Azabu Juban, he served as the chef of Yakitori Seo on the first basement floor of The Tokyo Station Hotel for eight years and then opened Yakitori Hiranoin February 2022. His yakitori cuisine, featuring traditional Edo-style techniques, made his restaurant an instant success and secured its place as an unparalleled yakitori restaurant with unwavering popularity.

The secret to Chef Hirano’s cooking lies in his mastery of traditional techniques and his continuous pursuit of future excellence. He elevates his yakitori cuisine to new heights by mastering the traditional Edomae yakitori technique of grilling chicken over high charcoal heat at close range, making no compromise on the freshness of chicken, and pursuing the perfection of cutting and skewering. The prix-fixe menu offers three seasonal delicacies, salad, 10 chicken skewers, rice, and dessert (Egg Pudding). Carefully selected for its freshness, the Kai Shingen chicken from Yamanashi is grilled to charred perfection over Owari Binchotan charcoal from the Chita Peninsula, Aichi, known for its high heat output, and finished with a secret sauce continuously replenished for years. The rice course can be chosen from Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl, Chicken Soboro Rice Bowl, Inaniwa Udon (thin Japanese udon noodles), and Chicken Soup Rice. Served in an eggshell, Egg Pudding is especially popular for its creamy, velvety texture.

Sitting on the luxury hinoki cypress-wood counter (seating up to 12 guests) surrounding the stove, guests can indulge in exquisite yakitori cuisine while enjoying the sound of charcoal cracking. There is also a private dining room (seating up to six guests) with a large monitor. On arrival, guests are welcomed with a glass of sakebrewed by Nishi Sake Brewery in Kagoshima to refresh their palate before starting meals. Enjoy the exquisite yakitori that lends itself to various occasions, either for business or pleasure, at Yakitori Hirano.

Secluded on the second floor of a building about a six-minute walk from Tokyo Metro Higashi-ginza Station, Yakitori Hirano Tonari was opened as the second location of Yakitori Hirano by Owner-Chef Ikuji Hirano, a master of yakitori (Japanese chicken skewers), in a building adjoining the main location in July 2025. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Makoto Kuwata, Hirano’s top apprentice involved in the opening of Yakitori Hirano. Featuring the same ingredients prepared in the same way as for Yakitori Hirano in 30 seconds’ walk distance, Yakitori Hirano Tonari also offers yakitori cuisine elevated to new heights.

The keys are the traditional Edomae yakitori technique of grilling chicken over high charcoal heat at close range, no compromise on the freshness of chicken, and the perfection of cutting and skewering. The prix-fixe menu starts with three seasonal delicacies, followed by salad, 10 chicken skewers, and rice, and ends with a perfect pairing of slightly sweet, salty yokan (Japanese sweet bean jelly) and matcha tea. Carefully selected for its freshness, the Kai Shingen chicken from Yamanashi is grilled to charred perfection over Owari Binchotan charcoal from the Chita Peninsula, Aichi, known for its high heat output, and finished with a secret sauce continuously replenished for years. To guests’ delight, the rice course can be chosen from Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl, Chicken Soboro Rice Bowl, Inaniwa Udon (thin Japanese udon noodles), and Chicken Soup Rice. Meanwhile, the wine list showcases a perfect marriage of wine and yakitori by offering a selection of wines that go well with grilled chicken, such as Domaine Jux Réserve Riesling from Alsace, France.

The restaurant offers counter seating (for up to six guests) where diners can indulge in exquisite yakitori cuisine while enjoying the sound of charcoal cracking, as well as round table seating (for four people) where guests can enjoy conversations in an intimate setting. On arrival, guests are welcomed with a glass of sake, just like at the main location. Brewed by Nishi Sake Brewery in Kagoshima, it is intended to refresh the palate before starting meals. Enjoy the perfectly grilled, exquisite yakitori that lends itself to various occasions, either for business or pleasure, at Yakitori Hirano Tonari.

245594.longDescription:
Perched on the fifth floor of Izumi Garden Tower with direct access to Tokyo Metro Roppongi-itchome Station, BLT STEAK ROPPONGI is an American steakhouse that has enjoyed remarkable popularity since it opened in September 2014. Known as a sophisticated social hub with New York vibes in Roppongi, where business, art, and nightlife intertwine, it is part of the BLT Steak chain, which has opened more than 15 locations around the world under its various brands, such as BLT Steak, BLT Prime, and BLT Burger, since it opened its flagship location in New York in 2004. They are also recognized for their outstanding service and hospitality.

The Roppongi location is helmed by Chef Kotaro Habuchi. After starting his career with a Japanese restaurant in Roppongi, he worked in Western, Portuguese, and Oceanian restaurants and eventually joined BLT STEAK ROPPONGI. Captivated by the simple yet profound charm of steak, he continued to hone his meat processing and cooking skills, while offering delightful dining experiences that connect people through cuisine, ambience, and service at the restaurant.

BLT STEAK ROPPONGI offers modern steakhouse cuisine combining classic flavors with bistro fare. Faithful to authentic American steakhouse culture, the menu features dry-aged USDA Prime beef. Its robust flavor, enhanced by dry-aging and sealed in by broiling over a high heat of 800°C, enchants the taste buds of steak lovers. In particular, Dry Aging Prime T-bone Steak, cut from the highest quality beef and seasoned and cooked with meticulous care, and Seafood Platter are must-try specialties. In addition, Popover, a signature bread of BLT, has enjoyed high popularity since the restaurant chain’s founding. To create a perfect harmony with its meat, the steakhouse offers a wide selection of wines, not only from Napa, California, but also from around the U.S., Italy, and France. The drink menu also includes a great selection of bourbons and cocktails to complete the authentic American dining experience.

The interior and open terrace evoke an elegant resort vibe. Stepping into the entrance hall, guests are ushered through a bar area and a waiting hall to the spacious main dining area with a 6m-high ceiling. The restaurant also boasts four private dining rooms (seating up to 4 to 8 guests), which can be combined to seat up to 16 guests, a dining lounge (seating up to 30 guests) on the slip-level floor with a view of the lower floor, and a dedicated bar area with relaxing sofas. Together, they make the steakhouse a perfect venue for both business and pleasure dining. Indulge in the sophisticated New York vibe while enjoying premium steakhouse cuisine and exceptional service in an elegant setting filled with music at BLT STEAK ROPPONGI.

245563.longDescription:
Perched on the fourth floor of Tokyo Metro Toranomon Hills Station Tower with direct access to Toranomon Hills Station, Sushi Onikai Kakeniwas opened in 2024 as an affiliate of Sushi Onikai, a popular, hard-to-book sushi restaurant. At Sushi Onikai Kakeni on the fourth floor of the skyscraper, talented young sushi chefs create Kuzushi zushi by combining traditional Edomae sushi-making techniques with their original twists.

The chef’s choice menu offers 15 pieces of sushi, three delicacies, and one soup. The menu items are decided through monthly tastings, selected from suggestions offered by kitchen staff across all locations of Sushi Onikai based on the concept of authentic sushi at reasonable prices. The sushi toppings and delicacies are prepared with fish and shellfish scrutinized by experts with a discerning eye. The sushi rice is made with top-quality rice from Mihama Town, Fukui Prefecture, mixed with red vinegar from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing in a large wooden bowl in front of guests just before service. The sushi rice is served fresh without any toppings at first and then served with sushi toppings so that diners can enjoy the flavor that evolves with time.

Known as the specialty of the restaurant, Prawn Tempura Wrapped with Nori Seaweed is created under the supervision of the chef of Tempura Miyashiro, an affiliated restaurant awarded one star in a world-renowned restaurant guide. The crispy prawn tempura placed on a bed of sushi rice and wrapped with a crisp sheet of nori seaweed is handed across the counter. Some of the year-round menu items are also popular, such as Bluefin Tuna Hand Roll featuring three different cuts of tuna (fatty, medium fatty, and lean tuna) and flavorful flash-smoked seafood. The drink menu offers a great selection of sake, shochu, and beer as well as wines curated by Wine Sommelier and Italian Wine Ambassador Yoshihiro Nagase, who also joined monthly menu tastings to select Italian wines to pair with the sushi and delicacies of Sushi Onikai.

The interior is all blue-colored, including the ceiling, walls, and chairs. On the L-shaped plain wood counter (seating up to 12 guests), serving plates, also colored deep blue, highlight the sushi on them. Please enjoy the Kuzushi zushi in a casual setting in the spacious dining area with views of Tokyo Tower.
nearestStations: Directly connected to Toranomon Hills Station

245377.longDescription:
One of Kyoto’s most iconic landmarks, the Togetsukyo Bridge stretches gracefully across the Katsura River. At its foot stands MUNI KYOTO, a small luxury hotel, with Restaurant MUNI on the lower ground floor. 
Within easy reach of Arashiyama Station on the Keifuku Line, and JR Saga-Arashiyama Station, the hotel sits in quiet harmony with its natural surroundings—an understated prelude to the experience ahead.

At Restaurant MUNI, guests are invited to experience MUNI French KAISEKI – French cuisine shaped by the philosophy of Japanese kaiseki. The course follows the seasons and Japan’s twenty-four seasonal phases, with dishes that highlight ingredients at their peak. Grounded in classical French technique, the cuisine remains closely attuned to Kyoto’s natural rhythms, expressing each season with clarity and precision. 
Every element—from temperature and aroma to texture and finish—is carefully considered to engage all five senses. The course reflects the refined aesthetics of Japanese cuisine, while allowing room for creativity beyond convention. Signature meat dishes feature selections from Sakaeya, known for its meticulous aging and preparation, bringing out the full character of each ingredient. 
As the course progresses, each dish reveals a distinct expression, unfolding with quiet continuity. To complement the cuisine, pairings are selected from a wine cellar of over 1,000 bottles, thoughtfully chosen by the sommelier to suit both the menu and individual preferences. Centered on French wines, the selection also includes sake and non-alcoholic options, offering a broader range of pairing possibilities.

Defined by deep reds and warm browns, the dining room offers a calm and contemporary setting. Facing the inner courtyard known as the “Garden of Light,” it draws in natural daylight from above, creating a quiet sense of openness despite its location below ground. Carefully selected tableware and glassware complete the experience, each chosen as an integral part of the presentation.
Within this serene space, cuisine and aesthetics are brought into quiet balance.
Rooted in Kyoto yet open in perspective, Restaurant MUNI presents a distinctive expression of French gastronomy—refined, thoughtful, and unmistakably its own.

245557.longDescription:
Perched on the third floor of Azabudai Hills Tower Plaza with direct access to Exit 5 of Kamiyacho Station, Azabudai Sui Inaba is an affiliated restaurant conceptualized by Masanobu Inaba, the chef of Ginza Inaba, to reflect his culinary philosophy of featuring seasonal ingredients and tableware that enhances the presentation of dishes and paying attention to every aspect of time and space in the dining experience, ranging from the timing of serving each dish to the temperature of the day and the appetite of each guest to offer exceptional hospitality.

The kitchen is helmed by Chef Atsushi Fukuda, who worked as chef at Japanese Kaiseki restaurants in Nishiazabu and Azabu-Juban before he took up his current position at Azabudai Sui Inaba when it opened in December 2024. With a thorough knowledge of Japanese Kaiseki cuisine, he follows Chef Inaba’s culinary philosophy of paying homage to traditions while also reinterpreting them through his own lens to create outside-the-box dishes.

The unconventional flavors of Ginza Inaba are served in a casual setting at Azabudai Sui Inaba. Its six-course prix-fixe menu, beginning with starters, appetizers, and amuse-bouche, followed by sashimi, simmered dish, and main dish, showcases the natural flavors of seasonal ingredients. In particular, the amuse-bouche, Truffe Soba Noodles, is a luxurious dish featuring nihachi soba (made of 80% buckwheat flour and 20% wheat flour) topped with a pile of sliced truffes. This highly rated dish becomes even more flavorful and satisfying when mixed with quail egg yolk.

The drink menu is also extensive, offering eight varieties of sake, ranging from rare limited editions to affordable options, 10 varieties of shochu, including rice, barley, and potato, as well as a variety of beers, wines by the glass, umeshu plum wines, whiskies, and soft drinks. The interior is understated with natural wood accents. The dining area offers counter seating (for 11 guests) and table seating (for 10 guests) to accommodate various group sizes, from small to large, which makes the restaurant the perfect venue for different occasions, ranging from family and friend gatherings to after-work meals with colleagues, date nights, and business dinners with international clients. Please enjoy the out-of-the-ordinary flavors of Azabudai Sui Inaba!

245581.longDescription:
Four minutes’ walk from Ginza Station, Ginza En Tamura on the 10th floor of Sakura Marks Ginza 612 behind GINZA SIX is the third Japanese restaurant conceptualized by Masanobu Inaba, the chef of Ginza Inaba. As indicated by its name, Ginza En Tamura offers Japanese dishes cooked over charcoal embers, wood fire, or straw flames (‘En’ means ‘flame’ in Japanese). Each dish showcases the grilling mastery of Chef Katsuhiro Tamura, who used to work as the right-hand man of Chef Inaba at Conrad Tokyo in Shiodome and then served as Sous Chef at Janu Tokyo in Azabudai. Subsequently, singled out to lead the kitchen of the new restaurant opened by Chef Inaba, he became the chef of Ginza En Tamura when it opened in August 2025.

Embracing live-fire cooking, Chef Tamura transforms seasonal ingredients into exquisite dishes that transcend culinary boundaries while being rooted in Japanese culinary arts. This Tamura style is also reflected in the 10-course prix-fixe menu (dinner), which starts with amuse-bouche and appetizers, followed by sashimi, grilled fish, entrée, soup, main dish (meat), and ends with rice and dessert. Among them, the second course, Nigiri Sushi with Lightly Wood-fired Marinated Tuna, is especially popular for its lingering wood-fired aroma and its perfect combination of sushi rice and marinated tuna lightly grilled to bring out its rich flavor and umami. The Wood-fired Wagyu Beef, cut into bite-size chunks and served on a skewer with homemade brioche, is also highly rated.

The wine cellar houses about 120 bottles of exquisite wine, including reds, whites, and sparkling options, mainly from France but also from the USA, Italy, and Japan, and the sake list offers about 20 labels from around Japan, including seasonal limited editions. If you are not sure which drink to choose, try the wine, sake, wine and sake, or soft drink pairing menu curated by Manager Atsushi Sato, a qualified sake sommelier and wine expert, to complement the dishes and satisfy the guests’ palate.

The restaurant’s black-themed interior beautifully contrasts with the eye-catching wood-fired oven made of white Oya stone. The wood fire that keeps burning until the last guest leaves is also an essential element of the interior design. In addition to this cozy main dining area with counter seating (for eight guests) surrounded by chic black walls, the restaurant has two private dining rooms (seating up to 2 and 6 guests) with wine-red accents reminiscent of red wine. Please enjoy the Japanese dishes crafted by Chef Tamura, a master of live-fire cooking, at Ginza En Tamura, which lends itself to various occasions, from business to pleasure.

245604.longDescription:
About 10 minutes’ walk from Shibuya Station, Sushi Rizaki Shibuya is nestled in Kamiyamacho, a tranquil neighborhood known as Oku-Shibuya. The restaurant opened in March 2026 as the fifth branch of Sushi Rizaki, a popular, hard-to-book restaurant, in its birthplace, following the Aoyama, Ebisu, and Nishiazabu locations. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Naoki Shiotani, who has carried on the art of sushi making from Sushi Rizaki. He learned the basics of Japanese cuisine at Kikunoi Honten in Kyoto and went on to a French culinary career at Tsubaki in Nishiazabu before he knocked on the door of Sushi Rizaki to become a sushi chef who could perform culinary miracles in front of guests. Highly regarded for his sushi-making skills based on his mastery of culinary arts, he was entrusted to helm the third location of Sushi Rizaki in Ebisu in 2021, and its fourth location in Nishiazabu in 2023, and made them both popular destinations for sushi lovers. Subsequently, he became the chef of the fifth location that opened on the former site of the main location after its relocation to Tomigaya, Shibuya, leading the way in exploring premium taste and performance with affordable prices for Sushi Rizaki.

The prix-fixe menu consists of two parts. In the first part, 5 nibbles and 5 pieces of nigiri sushi are served alternatively. Then, in the second part, 3 to 4 nibbles and 6 to 7 pieces of nigiri sushi are also served alternatively.  They feature carefully selected premium ingredients, such as Mazuma wasabi grown by Koichi Tashiro from Gotemba, Shizuoka. The sushi rice is made with a blend of two rice varieties of different grain sizes and textures: Tohoku No. 194 and Emi no Kizuna. They are cooked to fall-apart perfection and seasoned with a mix of three vinegars: the spirit vinegar Hakuju and the red vinegar Kohaku from Yokoi Vinegar Brewing and Chidorisu from Murayama Zousu. The latter part begins with highlights of nigiri sushi – lean, medium-fatty, and fatty tuna. To bring out the best in these premium sushi toppings sourced from Hicho, a popular intermediate wholesaler, at Toyosu Market, the rice is cooked to order and mixed with vinegar at the right time by calculating backwards to get it to the right temperature and moisture level for the signature sushi toppings when they are consumed.

The sake list offers about 20 labels, including seasonal limited editions and permanent options, such as Juyondai from Yamagata and Aramasa from Akita. The wine list also offers a wide selection of wines, including reds, whites, and sparkling options from French vineyards and Kenzo Estate in the Napa Valley. If you are not sure which drink to choose, you can also ask for recommendations to pair with specific sushi or to match your preference. Each nigiri sushi is served on traditional plain wood serving plates on the L-shaped hinoki wood counter (seating up to 10 guests). Please enjoy the unsurpassed sushi of Sushi Rizak that lends itself to various occasions, from business to pleasure. With English and Chinese speaking staff, the restaurant is also recommended for entertaining international guests.

245588.longDescription:
Located on the second floor of a building in Ginza 5-chome, a short walk from Tokyo Metro Higashi-ginza Station, “Ginza Unagi no Miyau” opened in December 2024 to bring Nagoya-style eel, a specialty of “Miyau Joshin”, a long-established eel restaurant founded in Nagoya in 1946, to Ginza. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Hisashi Nakamura. Having devoted his entire career to Japanese eel cuisine, he is a charismatic chef with a loyal following. His masterful grilling technique is also known as “Nakamura-style” among eel enthusiasts. He uses a Nagoya-style eel knife to cut eels and grills them over charcoal without steaming.

The eels split open and skewered by the chef himself are a rare breed called Blue Eels. In particular, domestically raised tender females are featured, carefully selected from top-quality young eels growing to as large as 300 g within one year from their birth (known as “3.5P”). The standard prix-fixe menu, Unaju Kaiseki, offers seven dishes, including Unaju (eel rice box), Shiroyaki (grilled eel without sauce), deep-fried eel, and Uzaku (eel and cucumber salad). Eels are kept alive until an order is placed and then slit open and grilled to perfection, crispy outside and tender inside. In particular, Unaju is a luxurious dish with a perfect combination of freshly sliced, grilled-to-order eel and freshly cooked rice. The eel is first grilled without sauce and then dipped twice in sauce made with the chef’s secret recipe and grilled again before resting on top of special rice, which is sourced from Uonuma, Niigata, and cooked with a traditional broad-brimmed rice cooking pot. Shiroyaki is another specialty dish that showcases the chef’s grilling mastery and the natural flavor of eel. It is served with spices, such as homemade wine salt, yuzu pepper, plum sauce, raw Japanese pepper, and marinated wasabi stem. The food menu also includes a wide selection of eel dishes, ranging from classic specialties of Japanese eel cuisine, such as Umaki (eel omelet) and Uzaku (eel and cucumber salad), to creative dishes, such as Unagi Ham (tightly rolled eel that looks like ham) and Unagi Chanja (Korean-style salted eel).

The wine list, carefully curated by Restaurant Manager Yasuhiro Kasahara, who is also a qualified sommelier, offers 40 to 50 labels (mainly champagnes, reds, and whites from France) that complement the flavor of eel. The drink menu also offers about 10 varieties of sake, including seasonal limited editions. The interior is designed in classic Japanese style with warm wood accents, while the jet-black tables add a luxurious touch. The dining area with four tables spaced apart and the four private dining rooms with soft sunlight streaming through the paper screen windows make the restaurant the perfect venue for all occasions, from business to pleasure. With English, Chinese, and Korean menus available, the restaurant is also recommended for entertaining international guests.

245605.longDescription:
Tucked in a back alley in Nishi-Azabu, five minutes’ walk from Nogizaka Station or nine minutes’ walk from Roppongi Station, “Washoku no Mori Yuki” is helmed by Chef Tatsuyuki Yaguchi, who has devoted his entire career to the art of Japanese cuisine. He first honed his culinary skills at renowned Japanese restaurants in Tokyo, and then he opened a restaurant that shares a Chinese character in his name in December 2022. Since then, the restaurant has been enjoying great popularity for its beautiful and delicious dishes.

The 11-course prix-fixe menu is built around classic Japanese Kaiseki cuisine, starting with appetizers, soup, and mukozuke (side dish), followed by simmered, steamed, vinegared, and grilled dishes, and ending with rice with miso soup and dessert. The main course is Sukiyaki Hotpot with White Miso Broth. Served in a personal iron pot, this specialty dish features a broth made with flavorful white miso from Nagano Prefecture and thick slices of lean A5-rank Kuroge Wagyu beef. The rice course features Yukitsubaki, a premium brand of Uonuma Koshihikari rice, in winter and Yumepirika, a premium rice brand from Hokkaido, in summer. Served in an earthen pot with an egg from Yamagata, soy sauce from Nara, and other accompaniments carefully selected from around Japan, it is a testament to the chef’s passion for culinary exploration. The Hiryuzu (deep-fried tofu with vegetables) is also popular for its hearty chunks of vegetables and its fluffy texture achieved by the unique method of deep-frying and broiling the tofu from Kanagawa with the vegetables. It also features precious seasonal ingredients, such as bamboo shoots and matsutake mushrooms.

The sake list curated by Chef Yaguchi, who is a qualified sake sommelier, offers about 30 labels, including Kaze no Mori from Nara and Kachikoma from Toyama. They all go well with the dishes inspired by Kyoto Kaiseki cuisine, precisely because it is perfectly paired with sake. The restaurant features a warm wooden interior, which is small yet spacious with only counter seating available (for six guests), and Akahada ware plates crafted by Onishi Rakusai, a Living National Treasure, to complement the presentation of food. Please enjoy the seasonal flavors that lend themselves well to all occasions, ranging from family and friend gatherings to after-work meals with colleagues, date nights, and dinners with international guests.

244746.longDescription:
“Sushi Onikai” is located on the 2nd floor of a 100-year-old renovated house, just a 5 minute walk from Nakameguro Station in Tokyo. The entrance is marked with a small nameplate and when guests take off their shoes and go up to the second floor, they are greeted by a modern space that is very different from the external appearance of the building. It is run by two chefs, Kazuki Sakamoto and Sho Mochizuki, who both showcase their sushi-making skills at the restaurant.

“Sushi Onikai” is the sister restaurant of the famous “Sushi Tsukiuda” in Meguro. After gaining some experience working at a hotel in Tokyo, Chef Sakamoto moved to “Sushi Tsukiuda” where he has been learning and honing his craft since it opened. After training at “Ginza Kyubei” for 12 years, Chef Mochizuki moved to “Sushi Tsukiuda”. In November 2019, when “Sushi Onikai” opened, the two chefs, who had achieved a level of equal status at “Sushi Tsukiuda”, both began working there together.

Chef Sakamoto and Chef Mochizuki’s ‘Kusushi Sushi’ dishes are full of ideas and are very popular with their guests. They are made with some elements of the traditional Edomae techniques. One example of their method is used for their marinated lean tuna. The fish, which comes from Ireland, is first cut and pre-treated with boiling water, and then dipped in soy sauce and finally served with konowata (trepang salted entrails). Their yellowtail is marinated with salt for 3 hours, and served with senmaizuke to finish. Their “Gunkanmaki with simmered monkfish liver”, is made by simmering the liver for 30 minutes and rolling it with narazuke (pickles in sake lees). The Koshihikari rice comes from Fukui and red vinegar is used for their sushi rice. In addition, there is also a restaurant called “Tempura Miyashiro” on the 1st floor of the same building, 

There are 5 types of wine selected by sommelier Yoshihiro Nagase, who is the previous winner of the best sommelier contest in Italy (JETCUP). There are around 15 types of wine available, including dry varieties which have refreshing mineral tastes. There are also 5 ~ 6 kinds of sake that pair well with the sushi.

The stylish and refined interior features antique-style chairs, modern Japanese lamps and one L-shaped counter with 10 seats which helps to create a unified space. The utensils are unique, having been made by artists from all over Japan. The creative and delicious ‘Kuzushi Sushi’, prepared by Sakamoto-san and Mochizuki-san at Sushi Onikai, can be enjoyed on private occasions such as with family, friends and on dates.

245601.longDescription:
About three minutes’ walk from Azabu-juban Station, “Yakitori Shinoda Azabu Juban” is located on the second floor of a building in a quiet back alley. The secluded restaurant tantalizes the taste buds of food connoisseurs with its Yakitori Kaiseki meals―a competitive combination of perfectly seasoned and grilled Hinai Jidori yakitori (chicken skewers) and elaborate Japanese kaiseki dishes featuring carefully selected ingredients. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Katsuhisa Kato, who honed his culinary skills at several Japanese and sushi restaurants in Tokyo before joining “Yakitori Shinoda Azabu Juban”. Committed to making each dish rival those of dedicated specialty restaurants, just like the elaborate chicken skewers worthy of a yakitori restaurant, he carefully selects the best ingredients and sake by visiting producers and breweries in person in pursuit of the ultimate menu.

Opened in 2013 with the ambition of becoming Japan’s most luxury yakitori restaurant, Yakitori Shinoda Azabu Juban exclusively features Hinai Jidori chicken, one of Japan’s three great chicken varieties. Known for its rich umami flavor, it is simply seasoned with salt from Hamada, Shimane, or drizzled with a secret sauce and grilled to perfection over either of the two types of Binchotan charcoal from Kishu or Kochi, depending on the cut of chicken. The first skewer of the prix-fixe menu is Dakimi (chicken breast wrapped in chicken skin). Crispy outside and tender and juicy inside, it is a signature dish that showcases the chef’s craftsmanship. Including this, all chicken skewers are small so that guests can enjoy a variety of flavors and textures, ranging from Chicken White Liver, seasoned with flavorful Henko First-press Sesame Oil from Yamada Sesame Oil Manufacture in Kyoto, to Chicken Skin and Burdock (crispy chicken skin with burdock chips deep-fried over low heat), Kinkan (the rare cut of unlaid egg yolk), and Chicken Offal Assortment (consisting of four kinds of offal―chicken kidneys, entrails, hearts, and ovaries).

The Rice with Raw Egg features Milky Queen rice from Minami-uonuma, Niigata. It is freshly milled and cooked according to each guest’s arrival time, served with an Araucana egg, also known as the blue egg of happiness, and three-year-old Kappo Soy Sauce from “Kuramoto Odaya”, a long-established soy sauce brewery, in Ibaraki Prefecture. The key to enjoying this dish is to lightly beat the egg 7 to 8 times and drizzle the soy sauce over the rice. This way, the rich flavor of the egg yolk is highlighted in contrast with the mild flavor of the egg white. Another prix-fixe menu, Yakitori Kaiseki, is also full of elaborate dishes. For example, Homemade 100% Buckwheat Soba Noodles is made from buckwheat grains sourced from Mashiko Town, Haga District, Tochigi Prefecture, and home-milled with a stone mill. The optional Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl features Benibana Eggs from Yamagata Prefecture, while Bite-sized Hamburg Steak features Masuda Wagyu Beef from Misato-machi, Takasaki City, Gunma Prefecture. Original Curry is crafted with minced Hinai Jidori chicken and a blend of more than 20 spices, and Homemade Egg Sandwich is prepared with homemade white bread exclusively made with fresh cream and milk. The meal ends with authentic seasonal desserts, such as Kashiwa Mochi (oak leaf-wrapped rice cake), Mont Blanc, and Strawberry Daifuku (rice cake filled with red bean and strawberry).

The drinks menu offers a wide range of options to meet the different tastes of guests, including about 20 varieties of sake from around Japan, such as Kokuryu from Fukui and Aramasa from Akita, a selection of wines from Burgundy and Japan, shochu, and soft drinks, such as Salty Cider and premium bottled Royal Blue Tea. The main dining area, with an L-shaped solid hinoki wood counter (seating up to 10 guests), and two private dining rooms (seating up to 10 and 4 guests) are filled with the savory aroma of grilled chicken, thanks to powerful ventilation. Please enjoy the premium full-course yakitori meal that lends itself to various occasions, whether business or casual, in the comfortable setting of Yakitori Shinoda Azabu Juban.

About six minutes’ walk from Shibuya Station, “Tokusen Takasakadori Katsudori” opened in July 2025 in the Dogenzaka district, a short distance from the hustle and bustle of the station area. The yakitori restaurant enchants the taste buds of food connoisseurs with its multi-course meals that combine yakitori (chicken skewers) and creative cuisine featuring carefully selected premium cuts of mythical Takasaka chicken. The kitchen is helmed by Grill Chef Nobuaki Taniguchi. Before taking up the position of chef at this new concept restaurant, the grill master with 20 years of experience in yakitori cuisine at affiliated restaurants apprenticed himself to Owner-chef Hirokazu Kaneda at “Ebisu Torihiro”, as well as Mamoru Tatemori, a legendary chef who had made Takasaka chicken famous as yakitori, to learn how to handle premium Takasaka chicken.

The 15-course Premium Takasaka Chicken Meal starts with clear Soup served in a teacup with premium Takasaka chicken, followed by Chicken Liver Pâté sandwiched in a meringue made with hojicha tea. The third course is Premium Takasaka Chicken Breast grilled whole, according to each guest’s arrival time, and then sliced before served. The Takasaka chicken is aged at low temperature for 10 days after slaughter to bring out the maximum flavor and grilled to salmon pink perfection without burnt spots. This elaborate specialty is followed by the first skewer course: White Chicken Liver. Raised on specially formulated feed for as long as 130 days, premium Takasaka chicken is all fatty with white liver, which is rich and creamy like foie gras but not overly heavy. This is no doubt another specialty of the restaurant. It is followed by skewered Red Chicken Thigh, Chicken Hearts, and two Seasonal Vegetables. Next comes Mini Hotpot with Chicken Meatballs, followed by more skewers, such as Chicken Wing Tips, Chicken Heart Root, Seasonal Vegetables, Chicken Breast with Skin grilled to perfection that highlights the grill chef’s craftsmanship, and Minced Chicken finished with cured, shaved egg yolk reminiscent of shaved mullet roe. The rice course can be chosen from two options: Rice Bowl with Chinese Chives and Chicken Soboro and Dry Curry and Rice. The former option can be enjoyed in three ways: first, savor it as it is; next, enjoy it with egg yolk; and finally, pour dashi broth over it. The latter option also comes with egg yolk, and another helping is accompanied by a thick sauce made from kombu kelp broth. The dessert is Homemade Pudding with Pecorino Romano cheese and Taiwanese Maqaw pepper. These luxury ingredients enhance the flavor of the premium Takasaka chicken eggs while complementing each other.

The wine list, curated by the sommelier, offers about 30 labels of white, red, and orange wines, mainly from France. In addition, the drinks menu offers a range of options to complement yakitori cuisine, including precious sake, shochu, whisky, and fresh orange juice. In the main dining area that combines Japanese aesthetics with a touch of luxury, the substantial grill station with an L-shaped counter (seating up to 12 guests) serves as a special stage for the grill chef. There is also private dining room seating for up to four guests. The tables are set with rustic saucers, small plates, and cruets created by Ceramic Artist Taeko Kajihara from Saga. With many English-speaking staff, the restaurant is also recommended for meals with international guests. Indulge in the premium Takasaka chicken that lends itself to various occasions, whether business or casual, at Tokusen Takasakadori Katsudori.

245614.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of a building about six minutes’ walk from Higashi-shinjuku Station, or about 10 minutes’ walk from Shinjuku Station, “Sushi Uta” offers authentic Edomae-style sushi that tantalizes the taste buds of sushi lovers. Set in Kabuki-cho, an entertainment district that attracts tourists from Japan and abroad, the restaurant is helmed by Owner-chef Uta Ehara. After seven years of apprenticeship at a popular sushi restaurant in Roppongi, he opened his own restaurant, “Sushi Uta”, in January 2026.

The chef’s choice prix-fixe menu, supervised by the renowned Chef Hidefumi Namba from “Sushi Namba” in Hibiya, offers 5 to 6 delicacies and 10 pieces of nigiri sushi that showcase the craftsmanship of Chef Namba and the unique artistry of Chef Ehara. The meal starts with a series of delicacies, among which the starter, Seared Fatty Tuna and Botan Shrimp, wrapped in a sheet of Gokujou Kontobi (black nori with spots of green nori from Maruyama Nori) with a spread of shrimp tomalley and handed over to guests, is an exceptional masterpiece that packs a punch. The last delicacy, Chawanmushi with Hairy Crab (cup-steamed egg custard hotchpotch with hairy crab meat), is accompanied by hairy crab bisque, which can be enjoyed as it is or added to the chawanmushi to enhance the flavor of the crab. Then, it is followed by a series of sushi courses that feature premium Uonuma Koshihikari rice and one of the finest rice vinegars from the renowned Yokoi Vinegar Brewery. The first sushi is topped with Fatty Tuna from “Yamayuki”, a popular tuna wholesaler, at Toyosu Market. Serving the highest fat sushi as a starter is another bold move of Chef Ehara to pack a punch. The second sushi is Gizzard Shad marinated with a blend of vinegar and Citrus sudachi to add a refreshing sour note.

The sake list, curated to complement each sushi, offers five labels, including Hidakami Yasuke from Miyagi Prefecture. The drinks menu also offers a variety of options that go well with sushi, ranging from cocktails such as AKAYANE Ginger Spirit featuring sweet potato shochu from Sata Souji Shoten in Kagoshima Prefecture to non-alcoholic beverages such as Red Grape Juice and White Grape Juice crafted from 100% wine grapes by Pfalzer Traubensaft in Germany and the bottled Japanese tea CHIRAN from Marushichi Seicha. Secluded from the hustle and bustle of the street, the restaurant boasts a sophisticated interior with an I-shaped hinoki wood counter (seating up to eight guests). It is also adorned with smoke-fired blackware plates crafted by Ceramic Artist Gen Onodera. Hidden away from the competitive sushi scene of Tokyo, Sushi Uta is the ideal place to enjoy authentic Edomae-style sushi in a relaxing setting. Please enjoy the hidden gem for various occasions, whether business or casual.
nearestStations: 6-minute walk from Higashi-Shinjuku Station

245616.longDescription:
“Kaishokuan Nakatake” is a Japanese restaurant quietly nestled in the residential neighborhood of Shinsakae, Naka Ward, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture. The invite-only restaurant whose address and phone number are not disclosed has now opened its doors through Pocket Concierge. The luxurious dining experience that celebrates quality ingredients and culinary artistry is only offered to select guests through a password-protected entry system. Chef Masayuki Nakatake started his culinary career at a sushi restaurant at the age of 16 and shifted his focus to Japanese cuisine when he set up his own business at the age of 21. In 2019, he opened “Kaishokuan Nakatake,” which he runs with Co-Proprietor Mai Nakamura, and in 2021, he also opened “Bettei Nakatake En” in Aoi, Higashi Ward, Nagoya City, captivating food enthusiasts with unique dishes only found at “Nakatake” in Nagoya.
 
The nine-course chef’s choice menu offers two appetizers, soup, sashimi, simmered, grilled, and fried dishes, rice, and dessert. The ingredients are all high quality, sourced directly from renowned origins around Japan, such as eels from the Nagara River in Gifu Prefecture, ark shells from Yuriage in Miyagi Prefecture, and rice and puffer fish from the local Mikawa region. The menu also features ingredients rarely used in classic Japanese cooking, such as caviar. In addition, it is inspired by seasonal flavors. For example, in spring, bamboo shoots collected by skilled bamboo shoot hunters in Kyoto are grilled over charcoal, while the Wagyu beef shabu-shabu hot pot is accompanied by Japanese pepper blossoms. In summer, wild sweet fish from the Kuzuryu River in Fukui Prefecture is prepared live and grilled over charcoal right in front of guests. In autumn, matsutake mushrooms from the Shinshu region are cooked with rice in small pots or steamed in earthenware teapots. In winter, puffer fish and snow crab from the Mikawa region are crafted into sashimi or cooked in small pots along with rice and various other ingredients, some grilled over Binchotan charcoal from the Kishu region and some simmered into broth and served as a specialty.

These dishes are complemented by a gorgeous selection of drinks. The wine list offers eight prestige champagnes, such as Salon and Louis Roederer Cristal, eight red and white French wines, and hard-to-find Japanese wines from Obuse Winery in Nagano, Says Farm in Toyama, and Azucca e Azucco, known as the first winery in Aichi (Toyota City), to satisfy the tastes of guests from Japan and abroad in search of sought-after Japanese wines. Meanwhile, the sake list includes Nakatake Original, brewed by Houraisen Ginjo Kobo (Sekiya Brewery in Toyota City) to drink at mealtimes, as well as renowned sake varieties, such as Juyondai from Yamagata, Jikon from Mie, Aramasa from Akita. Renovated from an old private house, the restaurant’s façade looks elegant and sophisticated, and the interior, where shoes are taken off before entering, boasts Taisho Romanticism vibes. The solid wood counter and bench (seating up to eight guests) create an intimate setting encouraging conversation between guests sitting next to each other. International guests are also welcomed and served by Proprietor Nakamura, who is fluent in English. Please visit “Kaishokuan Nakatake” for various occasions, whether business or leisure, and enjoy the exquisite dishes to your heart’s content.

245620.longDescription:
Housed in a historical building in Ningyocho, an old neighborhood known for its small-town charm and Edo food culture, “Ningyocho Sushi Kaki” is a sushi restaurant opened in 2025 by Chef Yoshiharu Kakinuma, former head chef of “Sushi Yoshitake” in Ginza. The sushi master with a wealth of experience, including as a head chef abroad, showcases Edomae-style sushi craftsmanship in the historic heart of Tokyo.

A testament to the expertise of the former head chef of the three-starred “Sushi Shikon” in Hong Kong, each sushi piece highlights the harmony between the toppings made from carefully selected fish and shellfish from Suruga Bay, Sagami Bay, and Toyosu, and the rice seasoned with aged red vinegar, as this is where the aesthetic of “Ningyocho Sushi Kaki” comes in.

The dining area is plain and simple with a nine-meter-long hinoki wood counter. The refined dining experience is further enhanced by the attentive hospitality of Co-Proprietor Minako Kakinuma and complemented by a rare selection of sake, such as Juyondai and Aramasa, and a range of champagnes of different vintages from Salon and Delamotte. The restaurant has English-speaking staff to assist international guests, and it caters to various other occasions, from celebratory feasts to quiet dinners for two. Please indulge in the authentic Edomae-style sushi, the pride of Tokyo cuisine, at “Ningyocho Sushi Kaki.”

245627.longDescription:
Located in Kagurazaka, a district of Tokyo filled with quirky restaurants, “CRAZY BRAVO” has gained immense popularity for its unique cuisine based on Italian regional traditions but with twists not found anywhere else.

The kitchen is helmed by Chef Masayuki Shibata. Graduating from Tsuji Culinary Institute, he began his culinary career at restaurants in Tokyo before he joined “Don Bravo,” a popular Italian restaurant in Kokuryo, Tokyo, at its inception. He continued to hone his culinary skills while working as Sous Chef at the restaurant. Then, in 2017, he moved to Italy, where he further refined his expertise at starred restaurants such as the renowned “Arnolfo” in Tuscany, and “Le Api Osteria” in Milan. After returning to Japan in 2020, he started working at “CRAZY PIZZA,” a sister restaurant of “Don Bravo,” and became Chef at “CRAZY PIZZA at SQUARE” in Kagurazaka in February 2022. It was reopened as “CRAZY BRAVO” in August 2025 after refurbishment with the aim of offering a first-rate culinary experience in a casual setting, reflecting the chef’s culinary philosophy.

Featuring ingredients from local markets, which Chef Shibata visits every day to get fresh, seasonal seafood, fruits, and vegetables, as well as mountain delicacies (edible wild plants) from his home prefecture of Akita, he creates unique dishes based on traditional Italian regional recipes he learned while working in the country but infused with his own flair and a Japanese sense of seasons. The elaborate, authentic Italian dishes that rival those of high-end restaurants are served in a casual setting at “CRAZY BRAVO.”

The delightful dining experience is elevated even further with sommelier-curated alcoholic and non-alcoholic pairings, just like at “Don Bravo.” The different types of wines, not only from Italy but also from other parts of the world, are also available by the glass. In addition, the drink menu offers a wide selection of craft beers, spirits, whiskeys, and digestifs.

Designed by Architect Taichi Kuma, the white-themed dining area with a high ceiling has an eight-seater counter and five tables. The serene atmosphere is enhanced by the gentle sunlight streaming through the large windows during the daytime and the contrast between the illuminated white interior and the darkness outside the windows after sunset.
 
Catering to various occasions, from anniversary celebrations to exclusive gatherings and family meals with children, “CRAZY BRAVO” is recommended for those who want to enjoy authentic Italian cuisine in a casual setting.

245613.longDescription:
Located across the way from Osaka Castle Park, about six minutes’ walk from Osaka Metro Tanimachi 4-chome Station, “Barin” is a teppanyaki (iron plate grill) restaurant on the 19th floor of the luxury hotel “PATINA OSAKA” overlooking the main tower of Osaka Castle. At this restaurant, diners can enjoy the natural flavors of top-quality ingredients, such as premium Kuroge Wagyu beef, abalone, spiny lobster, and seafood, with local specialties from the Osaka area. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Toru Aso, who has devoted himself entirely to teppanyaki cuisine. Captivated by the cuisine since his recruitment at the “Hilton Osaka” hotel in 1992, he has honed his grilling skills for over three decades at renowned hotel restaurants in the Kansai Region. Subsequently, he became the chef of “Barin” in “PATINA OSAKA” when it opened its doors in January 2025. Since then, he has captured the taste buds and hearts of diners and brought smiles to their faces with his proven skills.

The restaurant’s name, “Barin,” comes from the anecdote that Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the legendary samurai warlord of Osaka Castle, adorned his helmet with 29 iris leaves (also known as “barin”). Chef Aso cooks carefully selected ingredients on the teppanyaki iron plate with skillful movements like a samurai who has honed his sword technique. The signature prix-fixe menu “BARIN” takes diners on the ultimate culinary journey through 10 courses featuring seasonal ingredients carefully selected by the chef. For example, the early summer menu offers premium dishes, such as Pureed Soup of White Asparagus, Parboiled Conger Spike Sushi, Deep-fried Young Ayu Fish, Horse Crab, Live Spiny Lobster, and Chef Aso’s Recommended Matsuzaka Beef Fillet (60g). The restaurant is also characterized by featuring local specialties from the Osaka area, such as Baba Eggplants, Osaka Shirona, onions from Awaji Island, and unrefined soy sauce from Nara Prefecture. The drink menu offers 30 varieties of fine sake from around Japan and a wide selection of wines, 10 varieties by the glass and many more by the bottle. The wine pairings, sake pairings, and wine and sake pairings are also worth trying.

The interior inspired by the Golden Tea Room of Osaka Castle built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi boasts gold leaf art walls, which unfold like a picture scroll to depict the history of Osaka from the Naniwa Palace period through the Warring States period to the present day. With counter and table seating (for 10 and 15 guests, respectively) and a private dining room (seating up to six guests), “Barin” is versatile for various occasions, from business to casual. Please enjoy stunning views and teppanyaki cuisine artfully cooked over fire to bring out the natural flavors of ingredients at “Barin.”
