245611.longDescription:
About six minutes’ walk from Osaka Metro Tanimachi 4-chome Station, “IÑAKI” is the main dining room of the luxury hotel “PATINA OSAKA” on the 19th floor with views of Osaka Castle across the way. There, diners can enjoy refined dishes influenced by the flavors of Basque Country, Spain, known as one of the world’s best gastronomic destinations.

As implied by its name, which means ‘fiery’ in the Basque language, “IÑAKI” specializes in charcoal grill cuisine that highlights the flavors and aromas of ingredients. At the center of the open kitchen is a charcoal-fired Josper oven. Commonly used in commercial kitchens in Basque Country, it adds robust flavor and tender juiciness to each ingredient. With this oven, the chef cooks up delicious dishes against the backdrop of flickering and cracking charcoal fires. Charcoal-grilled specialties are also featured on the “IÑAKI” six-course dinner menu, such as duck and seafood grills, as well as optional Dry-aged Beef Tomahawk Grill featuring premium cuts. This signature dinner menu usually starts with tapas featuring cured ham from Spain, and ends with seafood paella and desserts. The dry-aged beef and cured ham are kept in a dedicated cellar. Next to that is a wine cellar with Grand Cru wines, including champagnes, reds, and whites carefully selected by the sommelier. His suggested wine pairings are also worth trying.

Another highlight of the restaurant is the panoramic view of the city skyline with the iconic Osaka Castle. In particular, the Osaka Castle Park below offers beautiful views that change with the seasons – cherry blossoms in spring, fresh greenery in summer, golden foliage in autumn, and snowy serenity in winter. Enjoying grandstand views of the seasonal scenery from the 19th floor while indulging in delicious Basque cuisine is a true jewel that will forever shine in your memory. The spacious dining area with table seating (for up to 100 guests) and two private dining rooms (seating up to 8 and 12 guests) make the restaurant a versatile choice for various occasions, from business dinners with international clients to private gatherings with families and friends, after-work meals with colleagues, and date nights with partners. Embark on a gastronomic adventure at “IÑAKI” and discover the flavors of Basque cuisine!

About six minutes’ walk from Osaka Metro Tanimachi 4-chome Station, “P72” is housed in the luxury hotel “PATINA OSAKA” right in front of Osaka Castle Park. Located on the first floor of the hotel, the signature restaurant with a sense of unity with nature is helmed by Chef Keita Kobayashi, who aspired to be a chef as an elementary school student while watching a cooking contest show on TV. In 2014, he joined “ANA Crown Plaza Hotel Kobe,” where he honed his culinary skills in different genres, from banquet to all-day dining and Italian cuisine. Subsequently, he served as Sous Chef in the main kitchen of “CONRAD OSAKA,” and then became the chef of “P72” in “PATINA OSAKA” when it opened in January 2025. Each of his dishes, created with fresh, in-season ingredients, tells a story about the producers and the land behind them and celebrates the rhythm of nature.

Named after the 72 micro-seasons of the traditional Japanese calendar, “P72” takes guests on a delicate culinary journey through the seasons. Around 70 percent of the menu is dedicated to healthy and environmentally friendly vegetarian options, featuring organic produce grown by local farmers under contracts. In addition, herbs grown in the outdoor herb garden and the indoor hydroponic garden flooded with natural light from the windows elevate the direct farm-to-table dining experience of the restaurant. The exploration of seasonal variations continues with the popular afternoon tea menu. For example, the early summer afternoon tea menu features sweets made with melons and mangoes, savories with seasonal vegetables, and charcuteries with homemade herbs. The five-course signature dinner menu “P72” also features delicious seasonal dishes that celebrate the bounty of nature. For example, the early summer dinner menu starts with Domestic Green Asparagus with Soy Milk and White Miso Foam, followed by Shiitake Mushroom Soup, Risotto with Domestic Saffron and Kombu Stock, and Tamba Black Chicken Roast (or Dry-aged Kuroge Wagyu Beef Rump Roast), and ends with Vacherin with Tonka Beans and Honey.

Stepping through the entrance, guests are welcomed by a 52-meter-long artwork reminiscent of tree roots floating in the air. With a spacious dining area with table seating (for up to 46 guests) and terrace seating (for up to 38 guests), wrapped in greenery and sunshine, where guests can enjoy lunch or afternoon tea with their dogs, the restaurant is versatile for various occasions. Please enjoy a health-conscious dining experience with your family, partner, friends, or colleagues at the signature restaurant of “PATINA OSAKA” that embodies the hotel’s concepts of sustainability and well-being.

245621.longDescription:
About three minutes’ walk from Tokyo Metro Omotesando Station, “HISASHI SUSHI” is an Edomae sushi restaurant on the first floor of a sleek building harmonizing with the stylish vibes of the street. The restaurant opened its doors in April 2026 as a branch of “Udatsu Sushi,” a popular sushi restaurant in Nakameguro.

“HISASHI SUSHI,” a new brand by Chef Udatsu, features the same style of nigiri sushi crafted with the same ingredients from the same sources as “Udatsu Sushi,” but offers an a-la-carte ordering system, which, unlike the ordering system of “Udatsu Sushi,” allows diners to choose delicacies and nigiri sushi they like from the menu, as is currently in vogue. Prix-fixe meals are also offered at reasonable prices so that diners can relax and enjoy their dining experience. The prix-fixe dinner consists of three delicacies and eight pieces of nigiri sushi. In addition, Vege Roll (maki sushi with a mix of chopped seasonal vegetables) is served between the delicacies and the nigiri sushi, like at “Udatsu Sushi,” to cleanse the palate.

Another common feature of the two restaurants is that they both highlight ingredients from Itoshima City, Fukuoka Prefecture. Fresh vegetables, fish, and shellfish are delivered directly from farmers and fishermen in Itoshima. Seasonings, such as Mitsuru Soy Sauce and Mataichi Salt, are also sourced from Itoshima. In addition, seawater delivered by fishermen from Itoshima is boiled down for one day to make homemade salt. It is mixed with Fuji rice vinegar from Iio Jozo in Kyoto and Agave Powder, a natural sweetener with a mild sweetness, and added to organic Hinohikari rice from Ryumon, Kikuchi City, Kumamoto Prefecture, to make sushi rice. Moreover, eggs from Itoshima are used to make Dashimaki Tamago (rolled omelet) and Chawanmushi (cup-steamed egg custard hotchpotch). All these dishes celebrate the bounty of Itoshima by capturing the essence of the region’s flavors that have charmed Chef Udatsu.

The sake list features Homase from the Ubusuna series by Hananoka Shuzo in Kumamoto Prefecture, brewed from an indigenous rice variety grown with the same water as the tributary of the Kikuchi River system that provides water for cultivating the rice used to make sushi rice. The drink menu also offers four types of Clase Azul, a tequila that goes along with sea urchin, aged for different lengths of time. The main counter made of lava stone from Mt. Aso (seating up to eight guests) and the U-shaped counter made of Kiso Hinoki wood (seating up to 11 guests) are beautifully arranged, making the restaurant suitable for various occasions from casual to business. Please relax and enjoy sophisticated Edomae-style sushi in a casual setting at “HISASHI SUSHI.”

244658.longDescription:
Set on the western foothills of Mt. Hakusan, one of Japan’s three sacred mountains, "ENNU Shiramine Hakusanroku Auberge" lies in Shiramine, a remote mountain community near the borders of Fukui and Gifu Prefectures. Surrounded by dramatic peaks and nourished by the headwaters of the Tedori River, this is a place where the grandeur and challenges of nature coexist, creating a landscape unlike anywhere else in Ishikawa Prefecture.
The story of "ENNU Shiramine Hakusanroku Auberge" began in the heart of Kanazawa, where "Restaurant Enn" earned a devoted following after opening in 2015. Drawn by the unique character of Shiramine and the powerful natural environment surrounding Mt. Hakusan, Chef Shoji Nishiyama chose to leave the city and relocate to Hakusan City. What was once an area with virtually no connection to destination dining became the setting for a new chapter—one that allows guests to experience the culture, landscape, and ingredients of the Hakusan foothills in their purest form.
Located approximately 1.5 kilometers from the historic center of Shiramine, a designated Important Preservation District for Traditional Buildings, the auberge is surrounded by a village renowned for its distinctive architecture and some of the deepest snowfall in the region. Here, visitors encounter a way of life shaped by the mountains and preserved across generations.

The name "Enn" is derived from the French pronunciation of the letter “N,” representing Chef Nishiyama, Nihon (Japan), nature, and nouveau (new). Following the move to Shiramine, the restaurant adopted the name "ENNU." Inspired by the Finnish word enn, meaning meaningful connections between people, the new name reflects a wish to cherish existing relationships while creating new ones, much like the enduring flow of the Tedori River.
Born in Aichi Prefecture, Chef Shoji Nishiyama has led kitchens at restaurants, hotels, and auberges across Japan, including Nagoya, Hakuba, Toyama, and Hokkaido. A pivotal moment in his career came while serving as head chef of the main dining room at The Windsor Hotel Toya Resort & Spa, internationally recognized as the venue of the 2008 Hokkaido Toyako Summit. There, he developed a deep appreciation for working directly with producers and for expressing the character of a region through its ingredients. In 2013, his appointment as head chef at the predecessor of "Restaurant Enn" marked the beginning of his culinary journey in Ishikawa.
At "ENNU," Chef Nishiyama presents a distinctive style of French-inspired mountain cuisine shaped by the bounty of the Hakusan region. His cooking reflects not only the landscapes surrounding Mt. Hakusan, but also the diverse character of Ishikawa, a prefecture where mountains, rivers, and sea are closely intertwined.
The menu showcases ingredients nurtured by abundant snowmelt, including wild mountain vegetables, seasonal mushrooms, wild char from the crystal-clear streams of Shiramine, fresh wasabi, and Hakusan Lamb raised on natural mountain pastures. These carefully selected ingredients are treated with restraint and respect, allowing their natural flavors to shine. Many dishes are prepared over wood fires fueled by timber sourced from Shiramine, imparting depth, aroma, and a tangible connection to the surrounding landscape.
Accompanying the cuisine is a thoughtfully curated selection of French and Japanese wines chosen for their balance and compatibility with the menu. Original cocktails infused with wild plants gathered around the property, along with house-made non-alcoholic pairings, further capture the essence of the mountains and seasons.
The restaurant’s connection to local producers extends beyond its ingredients. Bespoke ceramics, porcelain, and steak knives commissioned from artisans throughout Ishikawa Prefecture bring warmth and craftsmanship to the table, enhancing the dialogue between cuisine and place.

At the heart of the dining room stands a striking single-piece wooden counter with just eight seats. Combined with the semi-open kitchen, the intimate setting allows guests to observe the culinary artistry up close while gazing out over the surrounding mountains. The result is a tranquil dining experience that feels deeply connected to the natural world.
Whether gathering with family and friends, sharing a special meal with colleagues, or travelling in search of memorable regional cuisine, "ENNU Shiramine Hakusanroku Auberge" offers a rare opportunity to discover the spirit of the Hakusan foothills. Please indulge in Chef Shoji Nishiyama’s mountain-inspired cuisine and experience the landscapes, traditions, and stories of Shiramine through every thoughtfully crafted dish.

245634.longDescription:
Set on a quiet street about five-minute walk through shopping districts from Tenjinbashi Suji 6-chome Station in Osaka City, “Sushidokoro Shin” is a sushi restaurant helmed by Chef Tetsuji Kobayashi. Hailing from Kumamoto, Kyushu, he started his career as a sushi chef in Fukuoka and continued to hone his culinary skills in Los Angeles, the U.S. After returning to Japan, he further developed his skills at sushi restaurants in Minami and Kita-Shinchi, Osaka. Eventually, he opened his own restaurant, “Sushidokoro Shin,” in 2011 and relocated it to its current location in 2014. With a discerning eye and a creative flair, he has conquered the palates of sushi lovers with sushi that blends classic Edomae techniques with Kansai culinary traditions, welcoming a steady stream of guests to his secluded restaurant.

The chef’s choice menu offers 7 nibbles and about 12 pieces of sushi, which are served alternatively. The ingredients are all high quality, mostly sourced from “Hondaya,” an intermediate fish wholesaler in Amakusa, Kumamoto, with which the chef has built a long-term relationship and trust, but also from other intermediate wholesalers around Japan, some based in the Seto Inland Sea and others in Toyosu Market. The sushi rice is made from Hinohikari rice, exclusively grown for sushi in Oita, and seasoned with different varieties of Edomae Sushi Vinegar from Kisaichi Brewing in Chiba: white rice vinegar for summer and two different blends of red and white rice vinegar, depending on the sushi topping, for winter. The rich flavor enhanced by a mild touch of natural salt, Umi no Sei, from Izu Oshima Island, and the temperature gradations highlight the umami tastes of sushi toppings. Another aspect that makes the restaurant stand out is its original menu that changes with the seasons. For example, in summer, guests are offered Pressed Sushi with Horsehair Crab, nigiri sushi topped with a slice of swordtip squid so large that it almost completely covers the sushi rice, Confit of Sweetfish, and Seasonal Chawanmushi (Japanese steamed egg custard) made with plenty of vegetables to cleanse the palate.

The sake list offers about 12 selections from around Japan, including Hitakami from Miyagi, Nabeshima from Saga, Juyondai from Yamagata, Hiroki from Fukushima, and Kuheiji from Aichi. In particular, Kuzuryu from Kokuryu Brewery in Fukui, served cold with precious puffer fish fins, is immensely popular. The drink menu also includes Grand Cru wines, such as Kenzo Estate Asatsuyu from Napa, prestigious champagnes, such as Dom Pérignon and Drappier, and soft drinks, such as Yuzu Citrus Cider and Nose Ginger Ale from Osaka, to satisfy the different tastes of guests. The interior boasts an L-shaped hinoki cypress counter (seating up to eight guests) and subtle green walls, creating an atmosphere reminiscent of stepping into a quiet forest. The chopstick rests and ginger plates made by Baccarat and small plates created by renowned ceramic artists, such as Morimitsu Hosokawa from Kumamoto, Munehiko Maruta from Saga, and Kai Tsujimura from Nara, also reveal the chef’s keen eye for aesthetics. The sophisticated ambience and exquisite delicacies and nigiri sushi crafted with expert craftsmanship make “Sushidokoro Shin” a perfect place to discover the true pleasure of sushi.

245623.longDescription:
Opened in April 2026 as a branch of the popular “Sushi Masashi” nearby, “Bettei Sushi Masashi” is helmed by Chef Hayato Tajima, who has been apprenticed to Masashi Yamaguchi, the owner of the flagship location, since they met in Kyoto. At that time, the young Tajima worked at “Sushi Wakon” in the Four Seasons Hotel Kyoto under the supervision of the then Executive Chef Yamaguchi. Later, Tajima went on to serve as the second-in-command at “Sushi Masashi” and was appointed Chef at its Kita-Aoyama branch when it opened.

“Bettei Sushi Masashi” offers more classic sushi using ingredients from the same suppliers as “Sushi Masashi,” such as bluefin tuna from “Yamayuki” and fish and shellfish from “Asahi Suisan,” “Dainaka,” and other popular wholesalers. They are elaborately transformed into traditional sushi using Edomae techniques. The authentic craftsmanship is also showcased in the chef's choice menu of approximately 22 items. Guests are first offered approximately 8 classic delicacies that match sake, such as grilled fish and sashimi, followed by approximately 12 pieces of nigiri sushi. The sushi rice is made from a blend of Koshihikari from Minakami, Gunma, and Koshihikari from Yamagata, which are sieved by hand to obtain consistent grain size, and seasoned with a blend of lightly aged red vinegar and rice vinegar and a pinch of natural salt from Noto to enhance sweetness. As it falls apart in your mouth, the sushi rice perfectly harmonizes with each topping, from five seasonal toppings to different tuna cuts – marinated lean, medium fatty, and fatty tuna. Mehari Zushi (sushi rice ball wrapped in pickled mustard leaves) served between delicacies is also popular for its fresh flavor.

The drink menu offers eight labels of fine, seasonal sake, including Zaku from Mie and Hiroki from Fukushima, and a carefully curated selection of wines, mostly red Burgundy that pairs well with tuna. Guests can also ask the sommelier to choose a bottle that matches their preferences. The white-themed interior boasts a deep, straight counter made of solid hinoki cypress wood (seating up to 10 guests), adorned with antiques for a classic atmosphere. Offering a delightful dining experience at reasonable prices with high-quality ingredients and high-end furnishings comparable to those found in its flagship location, “Bettei Sushi Masashi” lends itself to various occasions, from business dinners with international guests to private events, such as family and friend gatherings, after-work meals with colleagues, and date nights. Please enjoy traditional Edomae sushi in a casual setting at this exceptional restaurant.

245622.longDescription:
Located on the first floor of a building, five minutes’ walk from Fujisakigu-mae Station, at the center of Kumamoto City, Kumamoto Prefecture, “Chisou Maru” welcomes guests with exquisite dishes created by Executive Chef Yoshihiro Maruyama to celebrate the natural bounty of Kumamoto. He started his career at a Japanese restaurant in his hometown of Fukuoka and honed his culinary skills at renowned restaurants such as “Kaishoku Michiba” and “Rokusan Tei” in Ginza and “Warayaki Mikan” and “Akasaka Komikan” in Fukuoka. He also served as the director and chef of “Ruri-AN” in Kumamoto. Then, in June 2025, he opened his own restaurant, “Chisou Maru,” which shares a Chinese character in his name.

It was an encounter with an intermediate fish wholesaler “Hondaya” in Amakusa, Kumamoto, that brought the Fukuoka-born chef to settle and open a restaurant in Kumamoto. The seafood from the popular intermediate wholesaler trusted by renowned chefs around Japan and fresh vegetables from local farmers are transformed into exquisite dishes to treat the taste buds, as represented by the restaurant’s name (“Chisou” means “making every effort to gather the best ingredients to entertain guests” in Japanese). The sushi is prepared by Sushi Chef Shuzo Iwashita, especially appointed by Executive Chef Maruyama, who believes that sushi is the best way to savor the gizzard shad of Amakusa. The duo has been joined by a restaurant pastry chef, Karen Kugiyama, to create a full-course menu.

The Chef’s choice menu offers 10 courses filled with seasonal flavors. To start the meal, guests are offered a seasonal leaf to crush and smell as they embark on a gastronomic journey into the world of “Chisou Maru.” The first course is a vegetable dish, followed by sashimi, and next come three pieces of sushi crafted by Sushi Chef Iwashita. The meat dish is accompanied by a sauce served in a Japanese tea bowl for thin tea to add a touch of elegance. Both the sushi rice and steamed rice are made from estate-grown “Minami Nishiki” rice. A bowl of steamed rice is accompanied by homemade cod roe, simmered small fish, and nori seaweed from Mikuniya, a famous nori manufacturer, in Hiroshima. Last but not the least, the meal ends with two authentic desserts created by Pastry Chef Kugiyama to captivate the taste buds and hearts of guests.

The drink menu offers about eight wines, including Chardonnay from Kikuka Winery in Kumamoto, 13 to 15 sake labels, including Ubusuna from Hananoka Brewery in Kumamoto, and selections of shochu, mostly from local breweries, including the limited rice shochu, Hyaku, brewed by Takahashi Shuzo in Hitoyoshi, Kumamoto, in collaboration with a Kumamoto-born writer, Kundo Koyama, to complement the locally sourced dishes.

The restaurant’s façade is also striking, showcasing craftsmanship with a high-gloss polished plaster wall framed by plaster cornices like a picture frame. Take a step inside, and you will be greeted by a traditional Japanese cooking stove and an eye-catching cedar counter (seating up to 10 guests). The setting is further elevated by the sushi serving boards crafted by Nara-born ceramic artist Kai Tsujimura and tableware created by Kanazawa-born artist Kiyoko Morioka and other local artists. Tailored to suit various occasions, from business to pleasure, “Chisou Maru” is the perfect place to discover the charm of Kumamoto.

244982.longDescription:
Located on the third floor of Intercity AIR, directly connected to Tameike-Sanno Station in Tokyo, "Lawry's The Prime Rib, Akasaka" is the Japanese outpost of the prime rib specialty restaurant that has been cherished in Beverly Hills, since 1938. After making its first appearance in Japan in Akasaka in 2001, the restaurant later relocated to Ebisu before returning to Akasaka in 2017. The restaurant's long history spans generations, with guests who once visited the original Lawry's The Prime Rib now dining at its locations around the world with their grandchildren.

"Lawry's The Prime Rib" is Japan's only restaurant specializing exclusively in prime rib (thick-cut roast beef). Carefully selected 36-month-old Black Angus beef is used, with lean ribeye chosen for its balance of flavor and texture. The beef is marinated with "Lawry's Seasoned Salt," a proprietary blend of 17 spices and herbs created by founder Lawrence L. Frank, then rested for more than a day before being slow-roasted at a low temperature for three to four hours. Served tableside from the restaurant's signature silver cart and carved to each guest's preferred size and doneness, the prime rib offers a notably juicy dining experience.
The restaurant's signature "Original Spinning Bowl Salad" was also devised by Lawrence L. Frank. Prepared before guests' eyes, fresh vegetables are tossed in a spinning bowl while dressing is poured from above, creating a presentation that continues to be popular with diners. The wine selection focuses primarily on American labels, with approximately 100 red wines and 50 white wines available to pair with Lawry's generous cuisine.

With seven-meter-high ceilings, the dining room provides an open and dynamic atmosphere inspired by classic American dining. Soft lighting and luxurious interiors further enhance the anticipation of the restaurant's signature prime rib. In addition to 220 seats in the main dining area, three private dining rooms are available for a variety of occasions. Whether for meals with colleagues, gatherings with friends, dates, business entertainment, or family celebrations, guests can enjoy the restaurant in a range of settings. Please enjoy a memorable time with the traditional prime rib and wine at "Lawry's The Prime Rib, Akasaka."
nearestStations: Directly connected to Exit 14 of Tameike-Sanno Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line

245630.longDescription:
About 10-minutes’ walk from Roppongi Station, "TOSAGE" is an Italian restaurant tucked away in the tranquil neighborhood of Motoazabu, housed in a modern building reminiscent of a European apartment residence. The kitchen is led by chef Ryo Tosaka, who was born in Niigata Prefecture, a region renowned for its rice production. After honing his skills for 12 years at "OGGI DAL-MATTO", including three years as head chef, he opened "TOSAGE" in January 2022. The restaurant’s name combines DOSAGE, the crucial step of adding a finishing liqueur known as the “liqueur d’expédition” in the Champagne-making process, with the chef’s surname, Tosaka. Through dishes that highlight the natural flavors of seasonal ingredients, Chef Tosaka expresses his own culinary vision, transforming each creation into a memorable plate.

The omakase course (a chef-curated dining experience) begins with amuse-bouches, followed by a seafood appetizer, risotto, charcoal-grilled dry-aged Yamagata beef fillet, and six varieties of pasta served in 20-gram portions, allowing guests to choose as many as they wish. The meal concludes with gelato, tiramisu, and coffee.
Vegetables are sourced from a contracted farm in Yachimata, Chiba Prefecture, while fresh seafood is procured from trusted suppliers at Toyosu Market, including tuna from the specialist wholesaler Hinaga. For the risotto, Chef Tosaka uses Tosaka Rice, a variety of Koshihikari cultivated by his family in Niigata Prefecture. Its rounded grains blend seamlessly with cheese and other ingredients, enhancing their flavors. The Yamagata beef, prized for its balanced marbling and lean meat, is grilled over premium binchotan charcoal to achieve a crisp exterior and tender interior, then accompanied by Shiroi Diamond, a natural salt produced in Murakami, Niigata Prefecture, which accentuates the beef’s natural sweetness.
The restaurant’s culinary identity is reflected in its pasta selection. In addition to three handmade pasta dishes, including the signature “Tajarin with Fermented Butter and Black Truffle,” guests can enjoy six specialty pasta offerings and select their preferred number of courses.

The wine list focuses on labels from Italy and France, with sommelier-selected pairing options available. Guests will also find a wide range of beverages, including sake, shochu, house-made limoncello, and soft drinks such as Unshu mandarin orange juice and Shinshu peach juice.
Inside, the stylish dining room is finished in shades of gray. At the spacious open kitchen, the eight-seat counter allows guests to watch the chefs preparing dishes directly in front of them, creating an immersive dining experience. Table settings feature cutlery from YAMACO of Tsubame City, Niigata Prefecture, along with Arita ware and Hermès tableware. A private dining room accommodating up to four guests is also available, making the restaurant suitable for both private gatherings and business occasions. Experience Italian cuisine shaped by the creativity and sensibility of Chef Tosaka in this distinctive dining destination.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from Roppongi Station

245631.longDescription:
Located on the 5th floor of the West Walk in Roppongi Hills, one of Tokyo’s famous landmarks buildings, “Roppongi Adesso” is an Italian restaurant that entered a new chapter when it was renamed from “Dal-Matto Roppongi Hills” in April 2026. While continuing to welcome many guests, the restaurant presents Italian cuisine that evolves with the times.  The kitchen is led by Takumi Tominaga, a chef from Fukuoka Prefecture who refined his skills through years of training in Italian cuisine. After serving as sous-chef at Nishiazabu OGGI, he was appointed head chef of “Roppongi Adesso.”

The name “Adesso”, meaning “now” in Italian, reflects the restaurant’s desire to serve seasonal ingredients sourced from across Japan, served at their peak flavor. A popular dinner option is the “STANDARD Course”, which begins with a selection of house-made breads and an assortment of eight appetizers, followed by the day’s specialty dish, chilled pasta, low-temperature roasted Yonezawa pork from Yamagata, a warm pasta dish, seasonal dolce created by a dedicated pastry chef, and coffee or tea. The restaurant’s signature chilled pasta, “Seasonal Fruit Chilled Pasta”, highlights the flavors of each season. Strawberries are featured in spring, cherries exclusively in June, peaches in summer, and pears in autumn. Prepared with generous amounts of seasonal fruit, it is presented almost like a dessert. The roasted Yonezawa pork can be upgraded to A5-grade Yamagata beef bistecca for an additional charge. Another specialty, the warm pasta “Shinshu Wagyu Rich Bolognese”, is available in portions of 20g, 40g, or 60g depending on appetite.

The wine list spans all 20 regions of Italy, from north to south, offering selections to suit a variety of tastes. Wine pairing sets featuring sparkling, white, and red wines are also available. In addition, guests can choose from a range of beverages including Dassai sake from Yamaguchi, highballs, and teas selected to accompany dessert. The bright and open dining room includes nine tables accommodating up to four guests each, an eight-seat counter, three semi-private box-seat rooms for up to five guests, and one fully private room with corner bench seating for up to five guests. English- and Chinese-language menus are available, making the restaurant accessible to international visitors. Discover Italian cuisine that reflects the ingredients of the season and the spirit of “now” at “Roppongi Adesso.”

245648.longDescription:
Located 8-minutes’ walk from Mita Station, in front of the East Gate of Keio University, "Chugokuhanten Mita" opened in 1984 as the second branch of "Chugokuhanten", which was founded in 1975. Specializing in Chinese cuisine, wok chefs, dim sum chefs, and roast meat chefs who have honed their skills in Shanghai, Beijing, Guangdong, and Hong Kong, work together to present authentic Chinese dishes.

The culinary style of "Chugokuhanten" combines traditional Chinese cuisine with occasional new ideas, developed to suit Japanese tastes. The menu features a mix of classic and contemporary dishes, from appetizers to meat and seafood courses. Included in every course is the signature “Peking Duck,” carefully prepared by the restaurant’s roast meat chef and finished with a crisp, aromatic skin using a proprietary method. Unique to the Mita location, this dish can be upgraded with additions such as caviar, sea urchin, or Shanghai crab miso. From September, a seasonal Shanghai crab menu is offered, featuring carefully selected Shanghai crabs sourced through the restaurant’s own suppliers and shelled before serving. Special dishes made with white truffles are also available.

Wine selected by the restaurant’s dedicated sommelier includes around 80 varieties, primarily from France and the United States. A wide selection of Champagne is also available, including labels such as Taittinger and Perrier-Jouët, with which the restaurant regularly hosts collaborative events. Guests can also explore a diverse range of directly imported Shaoxing wines and Chinese teas.
The restaurant’s interior is minimally decorated with Chinese furnishings, accommodating up to 120 guests, with six private dining rooms and a dining area that can be freely arranged using partitions. 245632.longDescription:
Approximately 9-minutes’ walk from Hatsudai Station or Hatagaya Station, "UNE IMMERSION" is a French restaurant located on the ground floor of a building in Honmachi, Shibuya Ward, an area with a nostalgic downtown atmosphere. Tucked away in a residential neighborhood, the restaurant is led by chef Mutsuki Hayata, who transforms his inspirations and refined sensibilities into dishes that express his own culinary style. After serving as sous-chef at "Le Sputnik" in Roppongi and later as chef at "L’Art et la Manière" in Ginza, he went on to establish his own restaurant, opening "UNE IMMERSION" in December 2023.

The name "UNE IMMERSION" means “immersion” in French. Limited to just four parties per day, the restaurant offers a tranquil setting where guests can fully focus on their meal. The name also reflects Chef Hayata’s desire to immerse himself completely in the cooking process, handling every step personally to create memorable dishes. The seasonal omakase course captures attention from the very first plate. “Rose of sumiika and turnip”, presents turnip and sumiika (golden cuttlefish) marinated with salt and lime as delicate petals, accented by a vibrant sauce made from turnip leaves and parsley. Another memorable ingredient is koi (carp), whose flavor captivated the chef and appears in preparations such as soup, nage, and ravioli. Signature dishes also include the “Homemade Charcuterie Platter,” featuring small portions of pâté de campagne, foie gras terrine, and lamb sausage, as well as game dishes such as lamb from Boya Farm in Hokkaido.

Even the restaurant’s rustic pain de Lodève is baked in-house. Believing that dedicating time and effort to sourcing ingredients and preparation is the minimum courtesy owed to guests, Chef Hayata devotes himself fully to every stage leading up to each service. The wine selection focuses primarily on Japanese wines, including Tarujuku Koshu from Ikeda Winery in Katsunuma, Yamanashi, and wines from Inishie no Sato Budoshu in Shiojiri, Nagano. Pairing courses are also available, designed to complement the chef’s vision for each dish. The dining room features just two tables with a total of six seats, offering a relaxed and intimate atmosphere. Leave the bustle of the city behind and immerse yourself in cuisine shaped by the sensibilities of Chef Mutsuki Hayata.
nearestStations: 9-minute walk from Hatagaya Station on the Keio Line

245583.longDescription:
Around 10-minutes’ walk from Roppongi Station and Azabu-juban Station, "cépages - de la nuit" is a French restaurant located in the tranquil neighborhood of Motoazabu. The restaurant is the successor to "cépages," which gained popularity in Maebashi, Gunma Prefecture before relocating and reopening as "cépages - de la nuit" in May 2026.
Leading the kitchen is chef Kazuki Ishibashi. After training for eight and a half years at "Apicius" in Yurakucho, he served as a section chef at "L’Effervescence" in Nishiazabu, later working at restaurants in Tokyo before becoming chef of "cépages." At the restaurant’s new location in Motoazabu, he continues to present dishes that reflect his own sensibility.

The name cépages means grape varieties in French, reflecting the restaurant's wish to be a place where guests can enjoy excellent wine and cuisine. The omakase course, consisting of around 10 dishes from amuse-bouche to dessert, is available with wine pairings selected to highlight the character of Chef Ishibashi's cuisine. One example is the signature dish, "Foie Gras and Yaki Manju", an interpretation of yaki manju (a grilled sweet bun specialty of Gunma Prefecture) paired with foie gras terrine and boka (brown sugar syrup) from Kochi Prefecture. The dish is served with Château d’Yquem, a botrytized sweet wine from Bordeaux, presented in an antique Lobmeyr glass. Guests can experience the harmony created by the interplay of food and wine. Another popular dish is a tartine topped with Jamon Minakami, dry-cured ham from Minakami, Gunma Prefecture, and burrata cheese.

The shorter course of around five dishes introduces a different approach. Guests first select a bottle of wine, and Chef Ishibashi creates dishes to match it. Demonstrating his skill in shaping flavors and textures spontaneously according to the wine, he offers pairings with added depth and nuance.
The restaurant features a six-seat main counter dining area and a fully private room accommodating up to six guests. The interior is a stylish space furnished solely with striking paintings by Teppei Takeda. Suitable for both private gatherings and business occasions, "cépages - de la nuit" offers a dining experience centered on wine, shared with companions who appreciate its appeal.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from Exit 1B of Roppongi Station on the Hibiya Line and Oedo Line

245650.longDescription:
Located about 5-minutes’ walk from Tamachi Station, "Chuugokuhanten Kurawan" occupies a renovated warehouse with a distinctive atmosphere. Part of the original Chuugokuhanten founded in 1975, the Shibaura location has served authentic Chinese cuisine since 2012. Led by a chef invited from Shanghai, and deeply familiar with the group's culinary traditions, a team of skilled Chinese chefs prepares a range of classic dishes.

The restaurant's specialty is "Peking Duck," which has been served by Chuugokuhanten since its founding. Prepared with great care by a dedicated roasting specialist and meticulously carved to serve only the crisp skin, it remains a signature dish. Another house specialty, "Braised Shark Fin with Superior Broth Sauce," features shredded shark fin shaped into a patty, lightly seared, then simmered in superior broth sauce before being served piping hot in a clay pot. Also unique to the restaurant is "Glass Noodles with Mullet Roe and Caviar," in which glass noodles, dressed with scallion oil, are topped with generous portions of karasumi (dried mullet roe) and caviar. Unique to the restaurant is the inclusion of a pastry chef within the culinary team. Available year-round, "Crystal Almond Tofu" layers house-made almond tofu with apricot sauce and almond liqueur jelly, while pieces of pink grapefruit create the appearance of goldfish swimming through the dessert. Reflecting an interior inspired by Shanghai during the era of the French Concession, traditional Chinese cuisine and original desserts come together in harmony.

The restaurant offers a selection of imported Shaoxing wines, ranging from 3-year-aged to 60-year -aged vintages, alongside dessert-style Shaoxing wine and premium baijiu. Guests can also choose from a variety of other wines, including Champagne and red and white wines, as well as non-alcoholic beer, sparkling drinks, gin and tonic, cocktails, and Chinese teas. The modern, open dining room is complemented by private rooms on the mezzanine and third floor, while the first floor is also available for private events. With facilities suited to a wide range of occasions, this versatility is one of the reasons the restaurant has been embraced by the local community. Please savor traditional Chinese cuisine alongside desserts created by its dedicated pastry chef.

245640.longDescription:
Located on the 41st floor of "Midland Square", the striking skyscraper near Nagoya Station, "Chuugokuhanten Reiho" opened in 2017 as the first restaurant outside Tokyo by the "Chuugokuhanten" group, which has continued expanding in Tokyo since its founding in 1975. The kitchen is led by Hong Kong-born chef Lee Wai Fan. The restaurant's name, Reiho, reflects the idea of welcoming guests with humility and grace, inspired by a Japanese proverb comparing maturity to rice ears that bow lower as they ripen.

The cuisine centers on Shanghai-style Cantonese cooking, combining the Shanghai foundation of "Chuugokuhanten" with Chef Lee's expertise in Cantonese cuisine. A signature dish is "Peking Duck", which has been served at "Chuugokuhanten" for many years. Prepared by a dedicated roast chef, only the crisp skin, fried in the Cantonese style, is served, wrapped tableside in a special Chinese crepe. Other signature dishes include "Rich Shark Fin Pot-Stew", simmered with Shanghai-style soy sauce, and "Shanghai Crab" (available seasonally from September), carefully shelled before serving. Exclusive menu items at "Chuugokuhanten Reiho" include "Kuwana Clam Stew" and "Mikawa Bay Swimming Crab Marinated in Shaoxing Wine", both featuring local ingredients. Chef Lee also showcases dishes using dried seafood and preserved ingredients, including "Steamed Soup" prepared with dried abalone sourced in Guangzhou and painstakingly rehydrated over time.

To accompany the cuisine, guests can choose from ten varieties of Chinese tea and seasonal freshly squeezed juices, as well as wine and Shaoxing wine pairing menus selected by the restaurant's dedicated sommelier. The dining room offers panoramic views from the 41st floor, with red pearwood-toned flooring and walls providing elegant accents. In addition to generously spaced table seating, seven private dining rooms are available. Paintings, antiques, and other furnishings throughout the restaurant reflect Chinese culture. Standing at the gateway to Nagoya, "Chuugokuhanten Reiho" offers the flavors of "Chuugokuhanten" together with sweeping views from the 41st floor.

245653.longDescription:
Located about an 8-minute walk from either Honmachi Station or Yodoyabashi Station in Osaka, "Vivacchus" occupies the basement level of an office building. The restaurant was opened in April 2012 by Akiko Masaki, who traveled to Italy and obtained sommelier certification there, with the aim of sharing the appeal of Italian cuisine and a wide range of Italian wines. Leading the kitchen is chef Tamotsu Yoshizawa, who has worked alongside Masaki since the restaurant’s opening. Together, they create dishes centered on pairings of Italian cuisine and wine.

The standard six-course "Qualita Course" begins with an amuse-bouche and appetizer, followed by house-made bread, pasta, a main dish, risotto, and dessert. The main course can be upgraded for an additional charge to the restaurant’s specialty, “Braised Domestic Pork Back Ribs.” Domestic pork back ribs (bone-in ribs from the back) are slowly braised with aromatic vegetables and red wine until tender enough to cut without a knife. Served with two sauces, a refreshing herb sauce and a mustard-based sauce accented with spices, the tender pork develops additional depth of flavor while remaining designed with wine pairing in mind.

Nearly all of the wines are Italian selections chosen by Akiko Masaki. The collection covers wines from all 20 wine-producing regions of Italy. More than 100 bottles are available, including a selection of Champagne and other French wines. By the glass, around 15 options are offered, ranging from sparkling, white, red, and rosé wines to dessert wines, allowing for a wide variety of pairings. Complementing chef Tamotsu Yoshizawa’s cuisine, which incorporates seasonal organic vegetables and balances gentle flavors with depth of umami, the wine selection focuses on soft, smooth expressions from across Italy’s diverse wine landscape.

Tucked away on the basement floor of a building in the business district, the restaurant opens into a spacious interior with high ceilings and a modern, luxurious design featuring abundant wood elements. The dining room offers four tables seating four guests each, while three private rooms can accommodate up to 16 guests. 245665.longDescription:
About a seven-minute walk from the East Exit of Ebisu Station, "Sushi Amakawa" offers authentic Edomae sushi in one of Tokyo’s most vibrant dining districts. The owner personally visits Toyosu Market to select the finest seasonal seafood available each day. Respecting traditional Edomae techniques while incorporating new methods, each piece of sushi is carefully prepared and served one by one. With the aim of making authentic Edomae sushi more approachable, the restaurant also offers a lunch course consisting exclusively of nigiri sushi. 

Every course begins with seasonal vegetables before the sushi. This opening dish reflects the owner’s wish for guests to start their meal with something nourishing. The omakase course features the restaurant’s signature dish, “Charcoal-Grilled Toro.” Grilling maguro (tuna) toro directly over an open flame brings out the natural sweetness and rich flavor of its fat. 

The restaurant features an L-shaped counter crafted from light-colored wood, along with a fully private room accommodating two to four guests. In this refined setting, guests can experience authentic Edomae sushi for both casual lunches and special occasions.
nearestStations: 7-minute walk from JR Ebisu Station
7-minute walk from Hiroo Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)

245642.longDescription:
Located about a 10-minute walk from Ichigaya Station, “Chugokuhanten Ichigaya” occupies the basement floor of a building in a quiet neighborhood just off the lively Yasukuni-dori Avenue, which connects the city's entertainment and business districts. Established in 1988, the restaurant serves authentic Chinese cuisine crafted by a chef invited from Shanghai, carrying on the culinary traditions that have made Chugokuhanten a respected name since its founding in 1975.

The restaurant specializes in classic Shanghai cuisine, highlighting an abundance of seasonal ingredients that reflect the changing seasons. Carefully selected produce and seafood sourced from Toyosu Market and, at times, mainland China are transformed into the distinctive flavors of Chugokuhanten, refined to suit Japanese tastes.
Every dinner course features signature dishes such as “Peking Duck” and premium shark fin specialties. The restaurant’s celebrated “Peking Duck” is meticulously prepared by a dedicated roast chef, who carefully carves only the crisp skin before serving. Its fragrant, crackling texture has made it one of the restaurant’s enduring specialties since opening. Another signature dish, “Sweet and Sour Pork with Black Vinegar,” is prepared without any vegetables, using only deep-fried pork loin, coated in a sauce made with Zhenjiang vinegar, a traditional Chinese black vinegar. The contrast between the aromatic exterior and the rich flavor of the pork leaves a lasting impression.
During winter, guests can enjoy Shanghai hairy crab, flown live from China and steamed before being carefully removed from the shell and served, allowing diners to savor its delicate flavor without the inconvenience of shelling it themselves.

The beverage selection includes five varieties of Shaoxing wine ranging from three to thirty years of aging, as well as Huadiao wine presented in decorative jars and Natsuno Sake, made without caramel coloring. Guests can also choose from French wines and whiskies such as Yamazaki, Taketsuru, and Ao. Chinese and Taiwanese teas are equally well represented, including Jasmine Tea, Pu-erh Tea, Keemun Tea, and Alishan Ginseng Tea.
Warm wood accents, paired with collections of Chinese art and antiques, create a sophisticated and welcoming atmosphere. The dining room features thirteen tables along with ten private rooms, making the restaurant suitable for a wide range of occasions, from meals with family and friends to date nights, business dinners, and hosting international guests. At “Chugokuhanten Ichigaya,” guests can discover classic Chinese cuisine that beautifully showcases the seasons in an elegant setting.
nearestStations: 10-minute walk from JR Ichigaya Station
5-minute walk from Exit A4 of Ichigaya Station (Tokyo Metro)

245641.longDescription:
Located on the 5th floor of Palace Hotel Tokyo in Marunouchi, Chiyoda, "Chuugokuhanten Kohakukyu" opened in 2012. A team of Cantonese chefs from China presents the authentic Chinese cuisine of the Chuugokuhanten Group, which has been supported since its founding in 1975. Dishes feature seafood, vegetables, and other ingredients sourced throughout Japan and prepared using traditional Chinese culinary techniques. Alongside classic preparations, the menu also incorporates more adventurous ideas. Although located within a luxury hotel, the restaurant maintains a lively and approachable atmosphere reminiscent of a neighborhood Chinese restaurant, creating a welcoming experience for guests.

In addition to specialties of the Chuugokuhanten Group, such as “Peking Duck” prepared by a dedicated roast chef, shark fin dishes, and seasonal Shanghai crab available during winter, "Chuugokuhanten Kohakukyu" also offers dishes unique to the restaurant that showcase seasonal ingredients in a manner similar to Japanese cuisine. Examples include “Braised Beef Cheek with Aged Black Garlic and Honey Sauce,” “Sazae (turban shell) and Winter Melon with Ise-Shima Aosa Seaweed Sauce,” and “Chicken with Fermented Bean Curd and Basil Sauce.” These dishes express the restaurant’s distinctive approach, sometimes pairing traditional Chinese techniques with Japanese ingredients, and at other times incorporating traditional Japanese seasonings into familiar Chinese ingredients.

A dedicated sommelier curates the wine selection, while Shaoxing wine aged from three to thirty years is also available. Guests can additionally choose from a wide range of non-alcoholic sparkling beverages, beer, mocktails, and Chinese teas. The dining room is decorated with traditional furnishings, including jade and agate tableware and vases, evoking the atmosphere of classic China while complementing the artwork displayed throughout the hotel. The main dining area features 19 spacious tables, and five private rooms are available for both private and business occasions. Here, guests can experience authentic Chinese cuisine together with polished service.
nearestStations: 5-minute walk from Otemachi Station Exit C13b
